docs.title: groundfield
docs.text:
Numerical field computation for grounding systems.

groundfield is an open-source Python package that computes the electric field of earthing systems in layered soil: electrodes of any shape, the conductors that connect them (PEN conductors, cable screens, measurement leads) with their inductive coupling and earth return, and the current and potential distribution that follows from a fault or a test current. This page says what the package computes, shows a first example and points you to the part of the documentation you need.

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text: Engineers and researchers who plan, assess or measure earthing systems in medium- and low-voltage networks and need numbers they can trace back to physics: the earthing impedance of interconnected systems, the influence of soil layering and of the measurement set-up, touch and step voltages, and the frequency response below 1 kHz. You should know the engineering side (EN 50522, IEEE Std 80); the documentation explains the code and the numerical methods.

docs.title: What it computes
docs.text:
Quantity Typical use Input, cluster and electrode impedance \(Z(f)\) earthing resistance, fault and test-current loops Potential \(\varphi(\mathbf{r}, f)\) in and on the soil potential profiles, earth potential rise (EPR) Touch and step voltage, EN 50522 limits safety assessment, including fault-current spectra Current sharing between electrodes and conductors PEN and cable-screen currents, split factors rho-f model \(Z(\rho, f)\) reduced models for groundinsight (BusType)

The physics is the quasi-static conduction problem \(\nabla\cdot(\sigma\nabla\varphi) = 0\) in horizontally layered soil: current is conserved in the soil of conductivity \(\sigma\), and the potential \(\varphi\) follows from the currents the electrodes leak. It is coupled to the conductor network by Kirchhoff's laws and, for conductors with inductance, by the Neumann inductance with a Carson or Sommerfeld earth-return correction. The frequency range is limited to \(f < 1\,\mathrm{kHz}\) on purpose: it keeps the model identifiable from measurements.

The field solution is a reference, not the end product: every solve is instrumented so that a reduced, interpretable equivalent model (the rho-f model of an earthing system) can be derived from it and handed to groundinsight.

docs.title: A first example
docs.text:
The earthing impedance and the earth potential rise of a 20 m × 20 m grid in two-layer soil, for an earth-fault current of 100 A:

import groundfield as gf

soil = gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=100.0, rho_2=300.0, h_1=2.0)        # Ω·m, Ω·m, m
world = gf.create_world(soil=soil)
gf.create_electrode(world, "grid_mesh", name="grid", corner=(-10.0, -10.0, 0.5), size=(20.0, 20.0), n_x=4, n_y=4)
gf.create_source(world, attached_to="grid", magnitude=100.0)       # A

result = world.solve(gf.create_engine(frequencies=[50.0]))
print(f"Z = {result.input_impedance()[0].real:.2f} Ω")            # Z = 4.80 Ω
print(f"EPR = {abs(result.electrode_potentials['grid'][0]):.0f} V")  # EPR = 480 V

A World holds the physics (soil, electrodes, conductors, sources), an Engine the numerics (backend, frequencies, discretisation). Coordinates are in metres with the depth \(z\) positive downwards. The quickstart continues this example with touch voltages, a potential profile and a plot.

docs.title: How a computation runs
docs.text:
soil model ──┐
geometry  ───┼──▶ World ──▶ Engine.solve ──▶ FieldResult ──┬──▶ potentials, impedances,
conductors ──┤                (backend,                     │    touch / step voltages
sources  ────┘                 frequencies,                 └──▶ rho-f fit ──▶ groundinsight
                               kernel)                               (BusType JSON)

The same world can be solved by several engines, which is how results are cross-checked. The default engine image covers homogeneous and two-layer soil; mom, mom_sommerfeld and the experimental fem cover what it cannot (choosing an engine, concepts).

docs.title: Software family
docs.text:
groundmeas  ──▶  groundinsight  ◀──  groundfield
(measurements)   (reduced network    (field model,
                  model)              PDE reference)

groundfield is the field-model member of the family. It exports reduced models as groundinsight BusType formulas (JSON file or live object, see IO and groundinsight), where they can be reconciled with measurements from groundmeas.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to groundfield are documented in this file. The format is based on Keep a Changelog.

These are concise release notes. The full narrative of every review and audit pass (findings, measurements, decisions) is kept verbatim in the audit history; work that is planned but not scheduled is on the roadmap. Up to 0.15.0 both stood in this file; they moved in 2026.11.0, and the release notes of 0.1.0 to 0.15.0 were condensed. The complete text as published is in the history of this file (for example at the tag v0.15.0).

Versioning. From 2026.11.0 on, the project uses Calendar Versioning with the scheme YYYY.MM.MICRO in its PEP 440 form: the month has no leading zero and there is no hyphen, MICRO counts the earlier releases of the same month, and tags carry a v prefix. 2026.11.0 is the first release of November 2026, 2026.11.1 the second one, 2027.1.0 the first release of January 2027. Releases up to 0.15.0 followed Semantic Versioning.

Deprecation policy. A calendar version carries no compatibility promise; compatibility follows this policy instead:

  • A deprecated name, parameter or behaviour keeps working and emits a DeprecationWarning that names its replacement and the earliest release in which it may be removed.
  • It is removed no earlier than two releases and six months after the release that announced the deprecation (announced in 2026.11.0: removed in 2027.5.0 at the earliest).
  • Every deprecation is listed under Deprecated in the release that announces it, every removal under Removed in the release that performs it.

Categories. Each release lists its changes under Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed and Security. An entry marked ⚠ changes numerical results; from 2026.11.0 on, every release that moves numbers opens with a Numbers that change block (what moves, by how much, for whom, and how to get the old numbers back), and every Fixed entry names the test that fails on the previous release. Finding identifiers (F01–F57 of review pass 9, 10.01–10.95 of review pass 10) refer to the audit history.

Contributing. Add your entry under the matching category of the [Unreleased] block; python scripts/release.py calver turns that block into the section ## [YYYY.M.MICRO] - YYYY-MM-DD of the new release.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• BusType formulas are parsed, never executed (10.01). evaluate_spec passed impedance_formula to sympy.sympify, so a crafted BusType file ran code or exhausted memory. An allow-list parser (groundfield.io._formula) builds the expression from the syntax tree, every node unevaluated, computes its numbers itself in bounded floating point and evaluates it with its own numeric function instead of lambdify, with bounds on length, nodes, depth, number size, work and the product of nested exponents (64); formulas are validated on load (EvaluateSpecError), and crafted documents raise ValueError (metadata nested deeper than MAX_METADATA_DEPTH, fields of the wrong type), so every other entry point works on what the loader accepts (audit A3SG-04). (A first version still let SymPy expand symbolic exp and fractional powers of large powers: 67- to 75-character formulas ran longer than 60 s; second adversarial audit, A2G-01 to A2G-03.) Every formula the 0.15.0 exporter wrote still loads with the same value. The attack corpus tests/data/formula_corpus.json (119 accepted, 122 rejected) is shared with groundinsight's guard. Tests: tests/test_formula_security.py.
  • Result files from untrusted sources (audit A1-01). load_result decodes only the array types the encoder writes, checks shapes and sizes before allocating and bounds the nesting depth; a number beyond the float range raises ValueError (audit A2S-04). Tests: tests/test_result_metadata_codec.py.
  • Overpass requests (10.05). Validated parameters (no query injection through timeout_s), https only, a capped response (16 MiB by default), error payloads raise and are not cached, atomic cache files, every element checked before caching; payloads nested deeper than an Overpass result, ids beyond 64 bits and oversized integer coordinates raise OverpassError (audit A2G-05). Tests: tests/test_overpass_ingest.py.
  • Wheel contents (10.02). The wheel installed scripts/release.py and the release command like groundinsight 0.3.0 does, so installing both overwrote one with the other; it now ships only groundfield. Test: tests/test_packaging.py::test_wheel_contents.
  • Supply chain (10.03, 10.04). Workflows with minimal permissions and actions pinned to commit SHAs (Dependabot keeps them current), no persisted credentials, tag names only through environment variables, the release gated by the full CI; locked dependencies updated until pip-audit reports no known advisory (last: tornado 6.6.1 for CVE-2026-126347, a dependency of the Jupyter tools in the dev and docs groups, not of the package).
  • Documentation site (10.08). MathJax 3.2.2 is vendored with the site and pinned by checksums, and no Google Fonts are loaded: the site requests no third-party resource. Test: tests/test_docs_assets.py.
  • VTK export (10.10). A newline in world.name can no longer break the file header; coordinates are written as double. Tests: tests/test_io_vtk.py::test_world_name_cannot_break_the_header, tests/test_io_vtk.py::test_points_are_double_precision_at_utm_scale.
  • Release tool (10.09). scripts/release.py runs git in the repository root, validates everything (also against the remote) before it writes and restores the files if the commit fails. Tests: tests/test_release_script.py.
  • FIPS builds (10.07). The penetration-mask hash uses md5(usedforsecurity=False); the digests and stored masks are unchanged. Test: tests/test_generator_reproducibility.py::test_mask_works_where_md5_is_blocked_for_security.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
Solver and kernels

  • Exact line-source kernel (10.28, 10.33): Engine(kernel="line" | "point") and create_engine(kernel=...); segments are uniform line currents in the reaction matrix, in FieldResult.potential and in solve_mutual_*. Results record metadata["kernel"]; PointSource gains an optional direction. Test: tests/test_line_kernel.py.
  • Backend registry (10.74): groundfield.solver.registry (register_backend, get_backend, available_backends, BackendCapabilities), a capability check before every solve (BackendCapabilityError, BackendCapabilityWarning), backend options Engine(options={...}) with MomSommerfeldOptions and FemOptions, and Engine.sommerfeld_assembly. Tests: tests/test_backend_registry.py, tests/test_engine_options.py.
  • Junction nodes (10.38): create_junction(world, position=...), a leakage-free network node for conductor ends, source terminals and measurement instruments; potentials in metadata["junction_potentials"]. Test: tests/test_junction_nodes.py.
  • solve_mutual_matrix(..., offdiag="galerkin" | "probe") (10.34): reciprocal off-diagonal entries that reproduce a network solve of the joined clusters, the default of every call (user decision Q15); ProbePointsIgnoredWarning when probe points are passed without offdiag="probe". Test: tests/test_mutual_matrix.py.
  • Per-engine resource limit (10.06; user decision Q17): Engine(max_segments=...) and create_engine(max_segments=...) set the hard limit of leakage segments and nodal unknowns for one engine (default diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT, 20 000), honoured by every segment backend, solve_mutual_* and the diagnostics, recorded in metadata["max_segments"]. Test: tests/test_resource_limit.py.
  • Per-engine size notice (10.06; user decision Q31): Engine(warn_segments=...) and create_engine(warn_segments=...) set the size at which a solve reports that it may take minutes (default diagnostics.SOFT_LIMIT, 5 000, read at solve time), counted like max_segments (leakage segments and nodal unknowns) and honoured by the solve's pre-flight warning, check_segment_resolution and diagnose() (report.context["warn_segments"]); kept by JSON, copies and the provenance. It is not checked against max_segments: a notice above the hard limit never appears. Tests: tests/test_resource_limit.py::test_warn_segments_is_a_validated_engine_field and four siblings.
  • Concrete shells on every electrode kind (10.12–10.14): concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m on rods, rings and meshes, with the conversions concrete_shell_coefficient, shell_coefficient_from_resistance and shell_resistance_from_coefficient. Test: tests/test_concrete_shell_coefficient.py.
  • Geometry queries (10.79): every electrode provides segments, segment_count, wire_polylines, bounds, total_length and min_feature_length. Test: tests/test_electrode_geometry.py.
  • Optional fast extra: with numba the two-layer series and the far field of the line kernel run compiled, bit-identical to numpy.

Results, diagnostics and files

  • FieldResult.input_impedance(source) and FieldResult.sources (10.18): the driving-point impedance (φ_attached − φ_return) / I a measurement or a fault sees, and the sources as solved. Test: tests/test_input_impedance.py.
  • Metadata and provenance (10.74, 10.77, F22): every result carries a metadata core (backend, kernel, versions, segment count, series controls, solve time) and metadata["provenance"] with world_fingerprint. Test: tests/test_result_persistence.py.
  • Versioned result files (10.77, F23): groundfield.io.save_result and load_result (standard JSON, schema version, atomic write). Test: tests/test_result_persistence.py.
  • FieldResult.to_dataframe() (10.69, 10.72) and read_csv_with_provenance(path) (10.73). Tests: tests/test_result_dataframe.py, tests/test_io_csv.py.
  • diagnose(world, engine=None, result=None) (10.70) returns a DiagnosticsReport (thin wires, resolution, segment budget, close or crossing wires, inert settings, series truncation); World.check() (10.66) validates source terminals and conductor ends; check_segment_budget and ResourceLimitError (10.06); find_close_wires, find_close_conductors, segment_distance (10.44); expected_segments(...)["nodal_unknowns"], the size of the dense nodal system the guard checks (audit A2S-02); groundfield.solver.PointKernelInterfaceWarning (10.28); groundfield.solver.InterfaceContactWarning and the diagnose() category interface_contact (a free rod end within one wire radius of an interface; a rod split at the interface is not reported; audit A3S-05); groundfield.world.RESERVED_NAME_PREFIXES. Tests: tests/test_diagnostics_report.py, tests/test_source_validation.py, tests/test_conductor_proximity.py, tests/test_cross_layer_point_form.py.

Coupling

  • Skin effect, opt-in (10.37): Conductor(resistance_model="skin") and create_conductor(resistance_model=...); exact solid-round internal impedance (solid_round_internal_impedance). Tests: tests/test_skin_effect.py, tests/test_inductive_solver_integration.py.
  • Earth-return builders (10.20, 10.46, 10.60): image="none" | "additive" | "antiparallel" on the inductance and correction builders, touching="exact", per-segment internal inductance, multi-frequency builders build_sommerfeld_correction_matrices / build_carson_correction_matrices, and the tabulated Sommerfeld assembly (Engine(sommerfeld_assembly= "tabulated" | "exact"), tabulated by default). Tests: tests/test_sommerfeld_accuracy.py, tests/test_sommerfeld_tabulated.py.
  • LayeredEarth.interface_depths and LayeredEarth.layer_of(depth).
  • coupling.carson.carson_mixed_mutual_correction (10.20, audit A2C-1): the earth-return coupling of an overhead and a buried wire (Carson's J and the remainder of the buried wire's attenuation, Ametani et al. 2009). Test: tests/test_carson_validity_domain.py.

Safety, fits and export

  • EN 50522:2022 (F51, 10.42, 10.52): permissible_prospective_touch_voltage_en50522 (Annex B.4) and touch_voltage_spectrum (true RMS over a fault spectrum). Tests: tests/test_safety.py.
  • Touch-voltage options (10.21, 10.22): touch_voltage(anchor=), touch_voltage_envelope(anchor=, interior=False | "meshes" | True, corners=True, return_points=), step_voltage(world=), UniformCurrentFieldWarning. Tests: tests/test_touch_voltage_footprint.py, tests/test_touch_voltage_envelope.py, tests/test_touch_voltage_envelope_corners.py.
  • Touch points (10.21; user decision Q3): touch_voltage_at_part(result, world, position=, bonded_to=, distance=1.0, ...), the touch voltage of an accessible metal part above ground (a station door, a mast, a fence post, a service connection box) bonded to an electrode or a PEN junction, with the feet on the 1 m circle around it, optionally only in given directions or outside given outlines (exclude); also gf.safety.touch_voltage_at_part. How-to Assess touch voltages. Test: tests/test_touch_voltage_at_part.py.
  • Effective resistivity (10.84; user decisions Q6, Q36): effective_resistivity(soil, *, preset="lv_network", w0=None, beta=None, h_ref=10.0), ρ_eff = ρ₁^(1−w)·ρ₂^w with w = w0·(h₁/h_ref)^(−β) limited to [0, 1], exact for homogeneous soil and equal layers, canonical stacks reduced, an error for three or more distinct layers; bit-identical to the AP1 / AP2 scripts inside their calibration range. The weights come from a preset per electrode class, groundfield.soil.EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS, with the values of the AP2 hand-over (2026-10-20, AP1 catalogue computed with groundfield 0.14.0): "lv_network" (0.13, 0.8; the default, the AP1 calibration over all LV networks), "station" (0.06, 1.3; the station electrode alone) and "lv_group_<g>_p<pp>" for the four LV network groups (perimeter equivalent n_U = Σ building perimeter / 40 m, thresholds 20 / 100 / 250) and 5 / 10 / 20 / 40 % foundation electrodes (q50 fit per group). An explicit w0 or beta replaces that weight only; an unknown name raises ValueError naming the closest presets. For the AP1 station in the 39 AP1 soils, R = c·ρ_eff misses the field solution by a median 1.8 % (over all 39 soils, the homogeneous ones at zero; 2.1 % over the 36 two-layer soils) and at most 15.7 % with "station", against 5.0 % / 35.9 % with "lv_network" and 11.9 % / 41.9 % over ρ₁; the hand-over's 1.7 % / 15.7 % appear to be this metric with the 0.14.0 point kernel at 1.5 m segments, which gives 1.71 % / 15.69 % (the hand-over does not name its metric). Tests: tests/test_effective_resistivity.py.
  • Impedance quantity (10.18, 10.19): quantity="input" | "cluster" | "electrode" and source= on sweep, convergence_study and the rho-f helpers. Test: tests/test_impedance_quantity.py.
  • Passivity (10.40, 10.41): check_passivity and PassivityReport; the BusType export checks passivity, records it in metadata["passivity"] and raises with require_passive=True (NonPassiveFitWarning, NonPassiveFitError). Tests: tests/test_passivity.py, tests/test_io_groundinsight.py.
  • Fit quality (10.27, 10.41): RhoFStandardFit.k0, .max_relative, .weights, .quantity, VectorFitResult.rms_relative, vector_fit(rms_tol=), RhoFStandardQualityWarning, VectorFitQualityWarning; BusType documents record the coefficients, the fit quality and the fitted quantity. Tests: tests/test_rho_f_standard.py, tests/test_vector_fitting.py.
  • sweep(n_jobs=...) (10.64) runs a process pool, bit-identical to the serial sweep. Test: tests/test_sweep.py.
  • Plots (10.73): component="real" | "imag" | "abs" | "phase" on the potential plots. Test: tests/test_plotting.py.

Engines and validation

  • Engine benchmark suite (10.76): tests/benchmarks (B1–B13) with analytic or independent reference values and one tolerance table per backend (pytest tests/benchmarks --run-benchmark).
  • compare_engines (10.71, 10.76): an explicit tolerance table (EngineComparison.rows), complex impedances at every frequency, component_floor, and a note when two engines run the same computation. Tests: tests/test_compare_engines.py, tests/test_engine_aliases.py.
  • mom_sommerfeld (10.47, 10.61): convergence and kernel-tabulation reports in the metadata. Test: tests/test_mom_sommerfeld.py.
  • FemReductionWarning, ExperimentalBackendWarning and ComplexImageFit.max_error (10.23, 10.49).

Generators

  • Network plan (10.78): NetworkPlan and materialise_plan; TnNetworkGenerator.plan() and LvNetworkLayout.plan(). Test: tests/test_network_plan.py.
  • Simulated earth tester (10.17): measured_impedance(result, probe=None, source=None) (three-pole reading) with the terminals meas_H and meas_S. Test: tests/test_measurement_loop.py.
  • Footprints (10.54): foundation_outline="ombr" | "polygon" | "spec", exclude_building_tags with NON_SERVICE_BUILDING_TAGS, rng= on build() and plan() (10.53); BuildingFootprint.mean_width_m() and .is_degenerate(), geo.mean_width, geo.MIN_OUTLINE_WIDTH_M and geo.MAX_PAYLOAD_DEPTH (audit A2G-05, A2G-06). Tests: tests/test_footprint_foundations.py, tests/test_overpass_ingest.py, tests/test_geo_footprint.py.

API

  • Typed factories (10.68): one overload per electrode kind, Literal option types (ElectrodeKind, SourceKind, KernelKind, ...) and “did you mean …?” errors. Test: tests/test_api_factories.py.
  • Namespaces (10.72): gf.plot, gf.safety and gf.fit; the flat names keep working. Test: tests/test_package_namespace.py.
  • groundfield.utils: suggest, did_you_mean, warn_deprecated, warn_inert, InertConfigurationWarning, REMOVAL_VERSION.
  • The package ships a py.typed marker (10.02).
  • WireSegments.wires, .wire_index, .n_wires (the straight wire of every segment); geometry.primitives.COLLINEAR_ROUNDOFF_ULPS; build_inductance_matrix(conductors=...).
  • Conductor.is_shield; build_inductance_matrix(shields=...).
  • FieldResult.metadata["wire_owners"].
  • Impressed voltage sources (10.51). A VoltageSource holds attached_to at \(U\) above return_to (or remote earth) and is solved by every backend on the shared pipeline — image, image_2layer (also for electrodes through the layer interface), mom, mom_sommerfeld — with conductors, inductive coupling and several frequencies: one current unknown and one constraint row per source in the nodal system (modified nodal analysis). Several voltage and current sources superpose; 0 V is an ideal short. The result reports the solved current in SourceRecord.current (new field SourceRecord.voltage, new column voltage_v of to_dataframe("sources")), input_impedance() is \(U/I\), and sweep, the rho-f helpers, split_factor and touch_voltage_spectrum accept the source. New registry capability BackendCapabilities.voltage_sources. Validated against the 1 A current-source solve scaled by \(U/Z_\text{in}\) in every backend, two- and three-layer soil, the cross-layer path and inductive conductors at 0 / 50 / 1000 Hz (at most 1.4e-15 relative), against solve_mutual_matrix for a two-terminal source, the hand-inverted transfer matrix for three sources, Dwight's rod (−0.012 %) and the hemispherical far field. Tests: tests/test_voltage_sources.py.
  • Internal impedance of a voltage source (user decision D1). VoltageSource.internal_resistance_ohm (Ω) and internal_inductance_h (H), both ≥ 0 and 0 by default (the ideal source, unchanged bit for bit), and VoltageSource.internal_impedance(f); create_source(..., internal_resistance_ohm=, internal_inductance_h=). \(Z_q = R + j\omega L\) is the diagonal entry of the source's constraint row, \(\varphi_a - \varphi_r + Z_q I = U\), in every backend that solves voltage sources (image, image_2layer with the cross-layer path, mom, mom_sommerfeld), with conductors, inductive coupling and sweeps; a galvanic world whose source has an inductance is solved per frequency on the complex path in the image family (its owner-level system; ×1.00 … ×1.09) and with one factorisation of the segment system plus a V × V system per frequency in mom / mom_sommerfeld (audit W2R2-02). For R ≫ Z_E a current source is the better model: the potentials and input_impedance() lose about log10(R/Z_E) digits (2.7e-6 at 1e12 Ω on a 36 Ω rod); R and L are 0 or at least 2.2e-308 (audit W2R2-10). SourceRecord.internal_resistance_ohm / internal_inductance_h / internal_impedance(f) and the columns of to_dataframe("sources"); input_impedance() of a voltage source is the impedance the source sees, \(U/I - Z_q\). Validated against the junction + lumped_series_resistance_ohm pattern (≤ 7.2e-16) and the 1 A solve with \(I = U/(Z_q + Z_\text{in})\) at 0 / 50 / 1000 Hz in every backend, three earth models and the cross-layer path (≤ 4.0e-15), the transfer matrix of three sources and solve_mutual_matrix (≤ 3.4e-16). Tests: tests/test_voltage_source_impedance.py.
  • Worlds that mix projected and local coordinates are reported (user decision D5, audit W2B-04). diagnose() has the category coordinates: a warning when points lie both within 10 km of the origin and beyond 1000 km from it (electrodes at UTM coordinates and a node or electrode given near (0, 0)), naming both groups and the conductors between them; information for a world wider than 100 km that does not mix. Such a world is solved as given, its two groups some 33 000 km apart: a return rod given at local (80, 15) m for an outline at UTM coordinates raised Z_in by 0.43 %, a PEN cable to a cabinet at local coordinates became a 33 118 km conductor (7494 + j25396 Ω instead of 5.39 + j0.19 Ω at 50 Hz with carson_series; sommerfeld did not finish), and nothing said so. Its solve (image family, mom, mom_sommerfeld, solve_mutual_*) now warns once with the new groundfield.diagnostics.MixedCoordinatesWarning before anything is discretised; a world wholly in projected or wholly in local coordinates is never warned about at the solve, and diagnose() reports one wider than 100 km as information (audit W2R2-06). Test: tests/test_mixed_coordinates.py.

  • mom and mom_sommerfeld (and the deprecated alias bem) solve concrete-encased electrodes (concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m, ADR-0012). Each segment adds its radial shell resistance C/Δs to the diagonal of the point-matching system, and the shell drop to its potential. With one owner per segment the image family solves the same system (agreement 7e-16); a ring rises by exactly C/(2πr) in one, two and three layers (1e-14). Up to 2026.11 both raised BackendCapabilityError; since wave 4 fem solves shells as well (its axisymmetric model as a surface conductance, its 3-D model as a radial resistance per length). mom is thereby the per-segment reference for encased foundations: against it the image family's point kernel lies +0.35 … +0.69 % high for grids in 5 cm of wet concrete and up to +18.8 % for stars. Test: tests/test_concrete_shells_mom_family.py.

  • The line kernel's near/far switch is continuous (user decision D2, audits W2B-01/-02): pairs between six and 7.5 segment lengths blend the exact and the far value with a C¹ weight — direct pairs, surface and Tagg/Sunde images, the images of the cross-layer correction and field points (SWITCH_FACTOR in groundfield.solver._line_kernel). Results no longer depend on where a world stands beyond round-off: 1e-13 over local shifts, ≤ 5e-11 at UTM coordinates, as the point kernel (audit W3A-04) (tests/test_line_kernel_switch.py).

  • Far Tagg/Sunde images carry the quadrupole term of the segment average, and the far form of segment pairs the radius term of the reduced kernel; the term is tapered off between 60 and 120 segment lengths of the pair's vertical distance and left out below 1e-9 of a unit point term (10.28; tests/test_two_layer_far_images.py).
  • The layered correction of the cross-layer path is evaluated in line form (its exact image expansion, ADR-0007 amendment; tests/test_cross_layer_line_form.py).
  • penetration_depth(soil, frequencies) and PenetrationDepth: the complex penetration depth \(p\) and equivalent resistivity \(j\omega\mu_0p^2\) of a soil with any number of layers, for the complex-depth (Dubanton / Deri) earth-return formulas of cables and overhead lines (PenetrationDepth.mutual_impedance). Exact for homogeneous soil; over the 39 AP1 soils, 50 Hz … 1 kHz, 0.1 … 1000 m within a median of 2.2 % of the exact layered earth return (at most 28 / 33 % overhead / buried; the formula's own error in homogeneous soil: median 2.4 %, at most 13 %; three and four layers up to 46 / 77 % at 1 km, 1 kHz, audit W3B-08).
  • coupling.sommerfeld_inductance.per_metre_mutual_impedance: the exact layered earth-return impedance per metre of two infinite parallel wires (within 5e-8 of Carson and of the two-layer Pollaczek integral; against an independent integral within 6e-8 of the earth-return correction up to 300 m and 7e-7 at 1 km for buried pairs, audit W3B-08).
  • BusType documents record the effective-resistivity preset (rho_preset=... of the exporters, metadata["rho_preset"], BusTypeSpec.rho_preset); evaluate_spec(..., rho_preset=...) and the new bustype_from_spec(spec, rho_preset=...) emit RhoPresetMismatchWarning when the bus uses another preset (user decision Q39).

  • diagnose() reports inductive conductors that lie beside each other closer than touching over more than ten touching distances and 5 % of the shorter one (category overlap, warning).

  • bustype_rho_preset(bus_type): the effective-resistivity preset recorded on a live groundinsight.BusType, also one read back from the groundinsight database (audit W3B-06).

  • PlannedBranch.axis_offset_m: horizontal offset of a branch from the line between its end points; the TN generator lays service drops in a row with it (user decision D9). Plans without it keep their geometry.

  • Engine.image_far_field ("quadrupole", the default, or "point"): the form of the far images of the line kernel in two-layer soil (the author's decision of 2026-11-15). "point" keeps the Tagg/Sunde images and the images of the cross-layer correction beyond the near-pair reach as point sources and leaves out their dense far-field term; the near image pairs (within 7.5 segment lengths, a segment's own images included) stay Galerkin integrals on both paths, and so do the continuous switch and the transverse distance of near image pairs — it is therefore not the result before wave 3 (within the upper layer up to 2.3e-4 from it). Networks move by 3e-6 … 4.3e-4 against the default (16 house grids 0.4 m above a 1000/10 Ω·m interface), a wire near the interface by 4e-4, surface potentials by up to 0.8 %; a 40-house network in 1000/30 Ω·m with h₁ = 1.5 m, whose transformer rods reach below h₁, solves in 0.49 of the default's time (0.91 of the solve before wave 3). Any other value raises ValueError, also in solve_image_2layer(far_field=...). Recorded in metadata["series"]["far_field"] and used by FieldResult.potential and solve_mutual_*; create_engine(image_far_field=...). Test: tests/test_image_far_field_option.py.

  • ⚠ fem is a conforming finite-element model (user decisions Q37, Q40; ADR-0016). The equivalent-hemisphere reduction is gone. Axisymmetric model (no new dependency): rods on one vertical axis and horizontal rings centred on it are solved as the solid bodies they are (cylinder with flat end faces, torus), in any number of horizontal layers, bare or with a concrete shell, each electrode one port; linear triangles on a graded tensor mesh conforming to every electrode surface and layer interface, an O-grid around the ring wire, the monopole Dirichlet-to-Neumann condition on a box 1000 lengths away, the port conductance matrix extrapolated from two nested levels; within about 1e-4 of independent references at 0.2 … 2 s per solve. Three-dimensional model for every other world (strips, polylines, stars, meshes, grids, rods and rings side by side, several clusters with their transfer resistances, galvanic distributed conductors with every leaking piece a port): smoothed line sources with an analytic radius correction in an isotropic tetrahedral mesh refined towards them, partially penalised immersed layer interfaces, conjugate gradients with an algebraic multigrid, two nested levels extrapolated; within 2e-3 of the axisymmetric model for rods and rings in one to three layers away from interfaces; wires that do not meet but run beside each other are kept at least 1.5 source radii apart by a smaller source radius, wires end to end at least 5, and refused closer than 3.3 radii of the thickest bare wire of the world, axis to axis (11 end to end); wires that meet at 10° or more are one conductor (audits W4B-01, W4B-02, W4R2B-03, W4R2A-01, W4R3B-01, W4R3B-02, W4R3B-05); the AP1 station in the corner soils of the AP1 grid lies between image_2layer (+0.7 … +3.0 %) and mom (−0.4 … −0.9 %), at 1.5 … 3 minutes and 4.1 … 4.3 GB per solve. It needs the optional extra fem3d (scikit-fem, BSD-3; pyamg, MIT; pip install "groundfield[fem3d]", decision D6) and raises ImportError naming it otherwise. Both models run the network of the shared pipeline: concrete shells, junctions, two-terminal and voltage sources, lumped and distributed conductors, inductive branches and the skin effect at every frequency, and the coordinate check of decision D5. FemOptions: model ("auto", "axisymmetric", "3d"), refinement, extrapolate, max_nodes, source_radius, growth, concrete_resistivity, max_nodes_3d, max_ports_3d (100: more ports are refused before meshing; raise it to solve such a world on purpose, audit W4B-08); metadata fem_port_resistance, fem_ports, fem_error_estimate (3-D model also fem_error_estimate_transfer for the transfer entries, audit W4R2B-05), fem_mesh, fem_model and more. Against the concrete resolved as a volume (Q40) a junction of encased wires acts like a few cm of wire, at most about \(2\,r_b\), sign not settled (not converged; audit W4B-05); the generators' house mesh changes by about 1 % or less, so no correction rule is applied. Tests: tests/test_fem.py, tests/test_fem_3d.py.

  • PlannedBranch.axis_offset_normal_xy: the unit plan vector along which axis_offset_m moves a branch; the TN generator records the common normal of a row of drops that are not exactly parallel (placement jitter; audit W3R2B-01). Plans without it keep their geometry.

  • InterfaceContactWarning (and the diagnose() category interface_contact) also for horizontal wires next to a contrasting layer interface (audits W4A-07, W4B-02, W4R2A-04, W4R3A-02): every electrode but a rod and the leaking pieces of galvanic distributed conductors, within the reach where the thin wire deviates from the solid wire by more than about 1 % in five ring geometries with the layer beyond on either side — 3.9 wire radii over a layer 33 times more conductive (+3.6 % at 2 radii, +8.6 % at 1.5, +89 % when the interface cuts the wire), 1.9 … 2.3 radii under a layer 10 … 1000 times more resistive, a wire the interface cuts from a contrast of 1.3, nothing below. Emitted by the image family, mom, mom_sommerfeld, solve_mutual_* and the 3-D fem, which also warns for rod ends at an interface (audit W4R2A-03); the axisymmetric fem resolves the wire and diagnose() with an fem engine reports nothing for a world it takes (audit W4R2A-05). No generated network and no world of the AP1 soils is reported. Test: tests/test_wire_interface_contact.py.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
Versioning, packaging and tooling

  • Calendar versioning and release tool (10.09): python scripts/release.py calver [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--dry-run] or set X.Y.Z; it updates the three version files and the changelog, commits and tags, and never pushes.
  • Package metadata (10.11): PEP 621 [project] table, SPDX licence, classifiers for Python 3.12–3.14, poetry-core>=2.2.0,<3.0.0.
  • Development standards (10.80, 10.94, 10.95): ruff format and lint (NumPy docstring convention), mypy, pre-commit, CI for lint, types, tests on Python 3.12–3.14 and a strict docs build on pull requests; tests are organised by feature and carry a finding marker.

Solver

  • ⚠ Default kernel (10.28): Engine.kernel defaults to None, the backend's preferred kernel: "line" for the image family, also through the deprecated alias cim. A 16-house solve takes 2.7× (with numba) or 5.7× (without) the time of the point kernel.
  • ⚠ Two-terminal sources (10.16, 10.75, F01/F30): image, image_2layer, mom and mom_sommerfeld inject +I at attached_to and −I at return_to; fem still returns the current through remote earth and warns.
  • ⚠ Floating passive clusters (10.29) in the image family, the mom family and solve_mutual_*.
  • ⚠ Cross-layer electrodes (10.15, F02), slivers and segment counts (10.32), post-solve series controls (10.25), solve_mutual_matrix diagonal (10.26): see Numbers that change. Cross-layer solves no longer report an image series they did not evaluate (10.50, F43).
  • ⚠ Concrete shells (10.12–10.14): the solver sees a shell only as the per-length coefficient C; concrete_model="lumped" and "distributed" put C on every encased wire, the cross-braces of a mesh foundation included (DIN 18014; user decision Q20).
  • solve_mutual_matrix / solve_mutual_field (10.34): resolve and check the backend like Engine.solve; a backend outside the image family raises BackendCapabilityError.
  • Errors (10.74, audit A1-08): worlds a backend cannot represent raise BackendCapabilityError (a ValueError and NotImplementedError) before the solve, also from the backend functions; code that caught TypeError from image_2layer or mom must catch BackendCapabilityError or ValueError.
  • Engine validation (audit A1-02, A1-04): Engine.model_copy(update=...) and attribute assignments are validated; create_engine forwards only the arguments it is given.
  • mom, bem, mom_sommerfeld (10.31, 10.75): documented and reported (metadata["solver"] == "point_matching") as one point-matching scheme; they share one solve pipeline and the depth advisories of the image family.
  • ⚠ cim (10.30) reads the length-weighted node potential; ⚠ layer stacks (10.48) are merged to their canonical form in every backend (TwoLayerSoil(ρ, ρ, h) is homogeneous soil, audit A2S-07); ⚠ fem (10.23, 10.49) is experimental, warns where its reduction does not model the world or ignores the skin model, and raises for electrodes below its hemisphere's layer, for clusters below a top layer that holds most of the hemisphere (audit A2E-2) and for driven polyline and star electrodes.
  • ⚠ fem and more conductive layers (10.23; user decision Q23): fem raises BackendCapabilityError when a layer that no electrode of a cluster touches and that conducts better than every layer the electrodes touch lies above the hemisphere radius a_eq, or below the hemisphere but above the electrodes' horizontal half-extent with no more resistive layer in between. The hemisphere then puts the current into that layer, and fem misplaces it: −97 … +30 % against image_2layer, mom and an independent ring series, mostly far too low — rods, strips and rings below a more conductive top layer from 22 mm thickness, rings whose hemisphere reaches a more conductive lower layer (−92 % for a 10 m ring at 0.8 m over 1000/30 Ω·m at h₁ = 2 m), −78 … +1 % for rings and strips with the layer below the hemisphere but within the half-extent, +30 % for a ring within its wire radius below a more conductive top layer. The half-extent part was added by the coordinator after the audit of the decision streams (D2A-03: the error is continuous across a_eq, −67.9 % on both sides for the 10 m ring), for the author's review. Up to now these worlds only warned (FemReductionWarning). The rule is structural, independent of the size of the contrast (100/120 Ω·m raises as well, where fem was −7 … +5 % off), on the canonical layer stack: a horizontal wire touches the layers that hold its axis (an axis on an interface touches both, to 1e-9 m), a rod the layers its axis passes through (an end on an interface does not count, as in the thin-wire model of the integral engines: a rod head on a conductive top layer raises, −92.9 % before); only the rule of an electrode below its hemisphere also counts a wire within its radius of a layer. More resistive layers keep the warning (−3 … +48 % spanned, −17 … +16 % within the half-extent, +16 … +46 % for a conductive layer behind a more resistive one). The message names the cluster, the layer, the electrodes' ρ, a_eq, the measured range and only backends whose own checks accept the world (or the finer segment_length or larger max_segments with which they would). Tests: tests/test_fem.py::test_fem_rejects_a_more_conductive_layer_its_hemisphere_spans, ::test_fem_rejects_a_more_conductive_layer_within_the_electrode_extent, ::test_fem_a_resistive_layer_in_between_keeps_the_warning, ::test_fem_partial_contact_with_a_more_conductive_layer_raises, ::test_fem_a_rod_head_on_the_interface_does_not_touch_the_layer_above, ::test_fem_names_only_a_backend_that_solves_the_world and siblings.
  • ⚠ fem within the range of its formulas and in the soil (10.23; audit of the decision streams): a driven strip deeper than half its length, a driven ring deeper than its diameter and any driven MeshElectrode raise BackendCapabilityError: Dwight's strip series diverges there (+369 % and +6120 % for a 1.88 m strip at 5 m and 9.8 m, silent before), the ring formula stays within −0.8 … +1.2 % of the exact thin ring down to one diameter and falls off beyond (−3.6 … −7.1 % at 2 D), and the mesh formula is +118 … +262 % at every depth. Electrodes and galvanic conductors at or above the soil surface, in the surface plane or reaching above it raise ValueError as in every other backend (a ring 0.5 m in the air was solved like a ring 1 mm deep); a rod with its head at z = 0 stays valid, and a strip whose end depths differ by round-off is a horizontal wire. Tests: tests/test_fem.py::test_fem_rejects_an_electrode_deeper_than_its_formula_reaches, ::test_fem_solves_a_ring_down_to_its_diameter, ::test_fem_rejects_a_driven_mesh_electrode, ::test_fem_rejects_an_electrode_above_the_surface_like_every_backend, ::test_fem_refuses_a_galvanic_conductor_out_of_the_soil, ::test_fem_round_off_in_a_strip_does_not_change_the_verdict.
  • A world without a current source (10.66, audit A2S-05) raises the same ValueError in every backend and entry point (fem solved it to zeros).
  • compare_engines (10.71) compares complex impedances at every frequency; comparisons that passed before may now fail.
  • Warnings (10.70): one warning per cause instead of per electrode; pre-flight warnings point at the caller's line; ShallowSegmentWarning follows the kernel (audit F08).

Coupling

  • ⚠ Inductive assembly (10.20, 10.46): carson_series on the anti-parallel image, sommerfeld on the image-free matrix, exact touching pairs by default (touching="quadrature" reproduces 0.15.0), Carson's P and Q with the a² term and the asymptote only above a = 15. carson_series keeps Carson's per-metre formula for near-parallel, near-horizontal pairs on one side of the surface; a pair across the surface has no anti-parallel baseline and couples through the transmitted field, and oblique, inclined and vertical segments get the Sommerfeld correction of a homogeneous earth (at the 8.1° boundary the result steps by the error of the per-metre model, 12 % for two 1 km leads at 1 kHz). Wires closer than the sum of their radii are evaluated as touching wires, close non-parallel pairs semi-analytically, and sommerfeld integrates segments longer than a quarter skin depth piecewise (audit A2C-1, A2C-2).
  • ⚠ references.pollaczek (10.45) is exact for two layers, also for conductors below the first interface and pairs in different layers.
  • One earth-return assembly for all frequencies (10.60): bit-identical per frequency; a 30-house Carson network 16.4 s → 3.3 s.
  • ⚠ Tabulated Sommerfeld assembly by default (10.60; user decision Q16): one table of the spectral integral per pair of depth groups and frequency; blocks of fewer than 64 sub-segment pairs keep the per-pair rule, which stays available as sommerfeld_assembly="exact". Test: tests/test_sommerfeld_assembly_default.py.
  • perfect_mirror across the soil surface (10.46; user decision Q27): a solve with earth_inductive_model="perfect_mirror" emits one UserWarning when inductive conductor segments lie on both sides of the soil surface, naming the number of such pairs and the conductors and pointing to "sommerfeld": the additive mirror image has no physical basis for an overhead/buried pair (2.28 / 2.77 times the mutual reactance of sommerfeld at 50 Hz / 1 kHz for a lead 1 m above a PEN 0.7 m deep).   • ⚠ Generated conductors end at the foundation point nearest to them (user decision Q41). Every conductor that TnNetworkGenerator and the layout builder route to a foundation ends at the point of that foundation nearest to the conductor, for every foundation form (rectangles at any orientation, building outlines, a substation's or cabinet's foundation): a service drop is the shortest connection in plan between its feeding cable and the building's foundation wires (their closest pair); a cable leaving a site with a foundation starts at the foundation's point nearest to its next node; the conductor is attached to the wire that holds the point (PlannedBranch.start_contact / end_contact, a PlannedContact). Ties go to the lowest wire index, then to the smallest arc position along the wire, so a cable parallel to the side facing it meets that side at the corner where its wire starts. A building that a cable crosses is joined to it and fed by it, without a drop: a cable of its feeding path, every trunk of RadialTrunkTopology (a building in a substation slot has no cable of its own, and a trunk beyond its tap source runs on past it), and in the star topology the main that crosses it, whose cabinet then feeds it instead of its nearest one (the nearest of the cabinets whose mains cross it, ties to the lower index; 1 of 50 and 3 of 150 houses of the default grids); a main that does not feed the building stays unjoined. Where the foundation touches the cable at a node (a cabinet on a wire), a crossing of the cable through the foundation elsewhere is the joint; otherwise the joint lies 1 cm from the node. A drop whose closest pair lies at such a joint starts there on the cable, and no drop runs along a cable farther than one minimum section (1 cm): a drop from a node that would run along a trunk or another main — both ends of a section within 1 cm of the drop's line — starts where it leaves it; the one overlap left is that 1 cm, where a foundation touches the end node of its cable from beyond and is tapped 1 cm before the node. A drop may pass over other buildings' foundations, 0.2 m above their wires (see the known limitations). The layout builder keeps its taps on the layout polyline, clipped at the projection of a site's foundation contact onto it, so no tap on the first or last segment lies inside a site foundation, also next to a rotated, polygon or offset one (corners inside the foundation of the substation or a cabinet are part of that site, see the layout entry under Fixed). Up to then every conductor ended at the connection point of the site's anchor — a corner of a rectangular foundation (meshes since audit A2G-04, rings since Q38), the first vertex of a building outline: 47 of 282 drops of a ring-house test set ran along a side of their own foundation and 45 crossed it (audits D3A-02, D3B-03). With the cabinets per building group (user decisions Q22, Q35; quiet machine) 1000 / 8000 star houses take 0.92 / 14.3 s, radial with max_feeder_length_m=1e5 0.98 / 17.2 s (the default 500 m: 8 000 radial houses 2.6 s). The mutual of two long close conductors (1 km, 1 m / 0.1 m apart) moved by 2.6e-5 … 4.0e-5 at 50 Hz and 3.4e-6 … 1.5e-5 at 1 kHz and is now within 1.3e-10 of an independent reference (audit W3B-10).

  • carson_series: a tilted near-parallel pair that comes close within its overlap is tiled per stretch (audit W1R3-07): a lumped pair and its pieces add up within 8e-6 of the loop reactance (5.2e-2 apart at 4e-2 rad); other pairs keep their entries; generated networks move by up to 3e-7 (the 10-house star with sites 2.8e-7, the 80-house radial network 3.4e-8; audit W3B-07).

  • Generated TN networks: service drops that leave one tap in one direction (the drops of houses behind each other, radial taps and the substation drops of the star) lie side by side at the touching distance of the PEN, sorted by length and centred on their former axis, so that only neighbours touch (user decision D9 of 2026-11-15). Before, they lay on one axis and the inductance matrix read every pair as touching; diagnose() reported them as overlaps (5-house radial network: 10 pairs, 200 houses: 247). The drops of one node form a row when their start points lie within the touching distance d_t of each other and the shorter drop's end lies within d_t of the longer drop's line; drops that are not exactly parallel (placement jitter) lie along one common normal, each at least d_t from the others, and a drop that would overlap a drop of a row joins it, also a drop of a tap 1 … 4 cm away on the same trunk (from 2 cm of jitter; audit W3R2B-01). A drop of a row starts up to (n − 1)/2 touching distances off its tap (2 cm in a row of five). No generated network reports an overlap with jitter_m 0 … 0.1 m (star and radial, 5 … 200 houses).

  • TnNetworkGenerator.build() right after plan() on the same generator (no rng=, nothing drawn from generator.rng since, the same configuration) gives the world of that plan; before, it drew a second realisation, another world with placement jitter. Successive calls still draw successive realisations (audit W3R2B).
  • bustype_rho_preset returns None when the last line of the description is not exactly groundfield rho_preset: <known preset> (before, a blank name raised ValueError; audit W3R2B-06).

  • PenetrationDepth compares by value and is hashable; its arrays are read-only copies (audit W3B-11).

  • ⚠ Every fem number changes (golden fem_rod_hom −4.65 %, fem_rod_two_layer_deep −4.57 %: Dwight's rod ignored the head depth); FemOptions: n_radial, n_axial, z_far_factor removed (2026.11 names), r_far_factor measures a box in characteristic lengths (default 1000), far_field="dirichlet" grounds the box; fem's point sources count against Engine.max_segments. Benchmark B1 checks fem against Weber's disc (was the hemisphere).

  • FemOptions.max_nodes defaults to 2 million (was 4 million, about 16 GB; the axisymmetric model needs about 4 GB per million nodes, audit W4A-05); fem with extrapolate=False reports fem_error_estimate = NaN (was 0.0, W4A-02); the common axis of the axisymmetric fem has a tolerance of 1e-3 of the smallest wire radius or gap (was 1e-9 of the world size, so a rod 1 µm off a ring's axis went to the 3-D model, W4A-08); metadata["fem_peak_memory_gb"] of the 3-D model is what the solve added (new fem_process_peak_memory_gb: the process peak; W4B-09).

  • The fem page: the validation rows next to and on an interface and the engine columns re-measured after the wave-3 changes of the image family and the refined ring block (audit W4A-01): image_2layer reads a ring 1 cm above a 1000 / 30 Ω·m interface +3.46 … +3.57 % above fem (the page said +5.2 … +5.4 %), the ring on an interface within 1.2e-5 of the solid-torus boundary elements; boundary elements as a second method for B2, B3 and the bonded ring with a central rod (W4A-11); benchmarks B8 and B10 exclude fem for its cost, with the 3-D result measured once (reciprocal to round-off; B10 +0.6 / +0.8 % above mom).

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text:
Every name below keeps working, emits a DeprecationWarning that names its replacement, and is removed in 2027.5.0 at the earliest.

Deprecated Replacement backend cim (10.76) image (auto-dispatch; cim already ran image_2layer, whose default kernel is now "line", see Numbers that change) backend bem (10.76) mom (identical point-matching system) backend image_nlayer (10.76) image (auto-dispatch by soil) Engine.tolerance, Engine.max_iterations (10.51) none, they have no effect Engine.sommerfeld_lambda_max_factor, sommerfeld_epsabs, sommerfeld_epsrel, sommerfeld_max_osc_panels (10.74) Engine(options={"mom_sommerfeld": {...}}) or MomSommerfeldOptions World.solve(snapshot_sources=False) (10.72) none, every entry point takes the snapshot World.concrete_shell_corrections (10.12–10.14) concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m of the electrodes HomogeneousSoil(resistivity=...), SoilLayer(resistivity=...) (10.69) rho SoilLayer(thickness=...) (10.69) h module groundfield.generators.ortsnetz_builder (10.69) groundfield.generators.layout OrtsnetzLayout LvNetworkLayout KvsPlacement, KvsConfig CabinetPlacement, CabinetConfig StarKvsTopology, kind="star_kvs" StarCabinetTopology, kind="star_cabinet" TnNetworkConfig.kvs, TnNetworkConfig.source_magnitude_A TnNetworkConfig.cabinets, TnNetworkConfig.source_magnitude_a CabinetConfig.quote_per_100_buildings CabinetConfig.count_per_100_buildings RadialTrunkTopology.slots_per_kvs, .kvs_spacing_m, .plan_feeder_kvs_positions() .slots_per_cabinet, .cabinet_spacing_m, .plan_feeder_cabinet_positions() LvNetworkLayout.add_kvs(), .kvs_placements .add_cabinet(), .cabinet_placements from_osm(kvs_lat_lons=, kvs_xys=), to_world(kvs_grounding=) cabinet_lat_lons=, cabinet_xys=, cabinet_grounding= source_magnitude_A= of to_world, measured_grounding_impedance, verify_current_balance, and the *_A result keys of verify_current_balance source_magnitude_a= and *_a keys HomogeneousSoilSpec.resistivity, SoilLayerSpec.resistivity, SoilLayerSpec.thickness_m rho, rho, h FoundationElectrodeSpec(concrete_model="distributed") (user decisions Q21, Q38) none, drop the argument: the field has no effect — both values put the same concrete shell on every wire, and every rectangle without cross-braces (style="ring", or "mesh" with n_x = n_y = 1) is one owner per side at every orientation, which is what "distributed" did (the default "lumped", silent so that 0.15.0 files keep loading, made an axis-aligned one a single grid-mesh owner up to user decision Q38, see Changed); warns also from JSON, from a model_copy that sets it and from copy.replace on Python ≥ 3.13. Test: tests/test_foundation_owners.py

Configurations and worlds written by 0.15.0 still load. solve_cim and solve_bem warn and delegate; their results carry the metadata of the backend that ran. fem is registered as experimental (ExperimentalBackendWarning).

  • groundfield.solver.fem.equivalent_hemisphere_radius and solve_fem(n_radial=…, n_axial=…, z_far_factor=…) (0.15.0 names; no effect; removal no earlier than 2027.5). FemReductionWarning is kept and never emitted.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• From the wheel (10.02, 10.11): the console scripts release and generate-third-party-licenses, the top-level scripts package and the unused polars dependency (groundinsight 0.3.0 still installs it with the groundinsight extra); run the tools from a checkout (python scripts/release.py ...).
  • Release tool options (10.09): the major / minor / patch bumps and --no-push, --allow-dirty, --allow-empty-changelog.
  • Metadata of cim results (10.76): cim_fit_used, cim_n_images, cim_rms, reduces_to, n_layers, h, rhos.
  • Private names (10.75, 10.79, 10.81): solver.image._potential_kernel, _segment_z_extent, the _discretize_* helpers, _grid_segments and the electrode classes and PointSource that solver.image re-imported; image_2layer._two_layer_potential_kernel; the module solver.field_study; Engine._stub_result and _dispatch; _layered.cylindrical_radius and _split_layer_thicknesses; mom._carson_skin_metadata, bem._build_Z_collocation, cim._cim_self_kernel_factory, _galerkin_solve of bem and mom_sommerfeld, the private Pollaczek kernels of coupling.sommerfeld_inductance and the helpers the solver modules re-imported from each other. Import public names from groundfield or groundfield.geometry.
  • gf.annotations (a leaked __future__ object, 10.72).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
Inputs that solved silently

  • Source references (10.66): misspelled attached_to / return_to, a source on a conductor, a source returning to its own node, no current source, magnitude 0 and dangling conductor ends raise with the closest names. Tests: tests/test_source_validation.py.
  • VoltageSource solved to zero (10.51): up to 0.15.0 every backend dropped it with a warning and the world solved to zero potentials; it is solved now (see Added). Test: tests/test_source_validation.py::test_voltage_source_solves_and_fixes_the_feeding_potential.
  • HARD_LIMIT only warned (10.06): worlds beyond the segment limit, or whose dense nodal system with every conductor sub-piece exceeds it (audit A2S-02: a 100 m PEN in 2000 pieces was predicted at 12 segments), raise ResourceLimitError before any allocation. Test: tests/test_diagnostics_report.py::test_world_beyond_the_hard_limit_is_rejected_before_any_allocation.
  • Conductors (10.43, 10.67): non-positive or non-finite cross sections and resistivities raise; a cross section above 1e-2 m² warns (mm² given?); an ideal conductor with discretize_segment_length raises. Tests: tests/test_conductor_validation.py.
  • Soils and geometry (10.67): infinite resistivities and thicknesses, malformed MultiLayerSoil stacks and degenerate electrode geometry raise when built. Tests: tests/test_soil_models.py, tests/test_electrode_validation.py.
  • Inert settings (10.51, F57): non-default boundary conditions, soil permittivity and engine settings that no backend reads warn. Tests: tests/test_boundary_conditions.py, tests/test_engine_options.py, tests/test_soil_specs.py.
  • Engine assignments and copies (audit A1-02, A1-04): engine.frequencies = [] and a raw options dict were accepted, and deprecated flat names in model_copy were ignored. Tests: tests/test_engine_validation.py.
  • Names used twice in a loaded or edited world (10.66, audit A2S-06) failed with a singular matrix or merged an electrode and a junction, and names with the solver's internal prefixes __layer_ / __cond_ broke the solve (audit A3S-03); World.check() and the add_* methods reject both. Tests: tests/test_source_validation.py::test_check_reports_names_used_twice, tests/test_source_validation.py::test_check_rejects_a_name_with_a_reserved_prefix.

Solver

  • Reciprocity (10.28, 10.29): transfer impedances of the mom family (were up to 1.46 Ω apart) and of the line kernel across the interface (were 1.1–4.7 % non-reciprocal) are reciprocal. Tests: tests/test_mom_family.py::test_two_port_transfer_impedance_is_reciprocal, tests/test_reciprocity.py.
  • cim is bit-identical to image_2layer (10.30) of the same release, default line kernel included (against 0.15.0 both move, see Numbers that change). Test: tests/test_cim.py::test_cim_is_bit_identical_to_image_2layer_for_unequal_segments.
  • Layer stacks (10.48): physically two-layer or homogeneous MultiLayerSoil stacks no longer raise. Tests: tests/test_layer_stack.py, tests/test_layer_stack_dispatch.py.
  • ⚠ Interface slivers and contact (10.32, audit A2S-01): a rod tip just below h₁ no longer raises or shorts the mom solve, and the contact with the layer it reaches is kept: the first fix dropped cuts shorter than the wire diameter, so a 4.5 m rod in 1000/30 Ω·m jumped from 195.0 to 128.6 Ω between 15.9 and 16.1 mm of tip penetration (audit A2S-01). The diagonal of a piece at the interface clamped its closed-form image terms at h₁/200, so a ring lying at h₁ = 5 m read −5.29 Ω with the default engine and contact values were 10–32 % low (audit A3S-01); it is evaluated at the wire radius. Tests: tests/test_interface_slivers.py, tests/test_cross_layer_line_kernel.py::test_ring_resistance_is_continuous_through_a_deep_interface.
  • ⚠ Point form next to the interface (10.28): on the cross-layer path a horizontal wire next to h₁ gave wrong, even negative impedances with kernel="point" and the mom family (−14 % … −552 %, also in 0.15.0) or a bare ValueError; it raises BackendCapabilityError naming the line kernel, and one within 0.6 segment lengths warns (PointKernelInterfaceWarning), on both sides of the interface (a ring 1 mm above h₁ read −945 Ω; audit A3S-02). Test: tests/test_cross_layer_point_form.py.
  • ⚠ Field of equal-resistivity layers (10.48, audit A3S-04): FieldResult.potential and solve_mutual_field of TwoLayerSoil(ρ, ρ, h) were up to 21 % off next to wires below h; they read the canonical stack and equal the homogeneous field. Test: tests/test_layer_stack.py::test_field_of_an_equal_resistivity_stack_is_the_homogeneous_field.
  • Floating clusters in solve_mutual_* (10.29, audit A2S-03): one factorisation for all excitations (256 bonded nodes 199.9 s → 5.6 s, results equal to 1e-12). Test: tests/test_mutual_matrix.py::test_shared_factorisation_equals_one_floating_solve_per_anchor.
  • mom family above ground (10.75): a segment crossing the surface raises instead of being solved as buried. Test: tests/test_point_matching_pipeline.py::test_mom_family_rejects_a_segment_partly_above_the_surface.
  • mom_sommerfeld budget (10.47): a binding oscillation budget counts as non-convergence. Test: tests/test_mom_sommerfeld.py::test_kernel_warns_or_converges_when_the_oscillation_budget_binds.
  • fem warnings (10.23, audit F01): interfaces above or beside the electrode are reported. Tests: tests/test_fem.py.
  • ⚠ fem below a thin top layer (10.23, audit A2E-2): a 3 m rod below h₁ = 0.4 m in 1000/30 Ω·m read 31.1 Ω against 10.5 Ω (mom) with a warning; it raises, and driven polyline and star electrodes raise BackendCapabilityError instead of a bare TypeError; fem warns that it ignores resistance_model="skin" (audit A2C-4). Tests: tests/test_fem.py, tests/test_backend_registry.py::test_a_backend_that_ignores_the_skin_model_says_so.
  • fit_complex_images (10.49) no longer reports convergence for a fit that misses Γ₁. Test: tests/test_cim.py::test_fit_converged_flag_bounds_the_maximum_error.
  • compare_engines (10.71, audit F03) sees the reactance, every frequency, non-finite results and a zero of one engine. Tests: tests/test_compare_engines.py.
  • Resolution check (F53, F54): polyline and star electrodes are checked. Test: tests/test_diagnostics_report.py::test_resolution_check_covers_star_and_polyline.
  • expected_segments for layer stacks (10.79, audit A2S-07) cuts where the backends cut. Test: tests/test_diagnostics.py::test_expected_segments_matches_the_solve_for_every_layer_stack.
  • convergence_study (A1-02, audit A2S-08) shows each warning once and rejects non-finite segment lengths. Tests: tests/test_convergence.py.
  • Line-kernel cost (10.28): one long segment no longer slows down the whole near-pair search (16 houses: 29 s and 1.7 GiB before). Test: tests/test_line_kernel_near_pairs.py.
  • Engine knobs (10.74): fem options are reachable, options for another backend warn, Engine.solve keeps the caller's sources (10.72). Tests: tests/test_engine_options.py, tests/test_solve_entry_points.py.
  • Memory (10.56, 10.57, 10.59, 10.62, 10.65): see Changed. Tests: tests/test_kernel_performance.py.

Coupling

  • ⚠ carson_series baseline (10.20, F32). Test: tests/test_inductive_solver_integration.py::test_carson_series_reactance_matches_carson.
  • ⚠ carson_series across the surface and outside its domain (10.20, audit A2C-1): an overhead wire over a buried one was coupled through an image above ground (mutual reactance 35.9 % low for a lead 1 m above a PEN at 0.7 m, 1 kHz), and oblique pairs got the per-metre value once per segment pair, which grew with the number of segments (two 1 km leads at 9°: 20× the Sommerfeld coupling). Tests: tests/test_carson_validity_domain.py.
  • ⚠ Wires lying side by side (10.46): coincident or overlapping parallel conductors had no finite mutual inductance (two coincident 50 m leads read 1.87 H), which made a two-house network with drops along the PEN main non-passive. Where a point of one wire lies beside the other closer than r_a + r_b, the touching distance is used, pointwise inside the Neumann integral and independent of the order of the conductors (a first version switched whole pairs from the row segment's view: +38.7 % depending on the order, indefinite matrices; audit A3C-1, A3C-2); a thinner wire inside a thicker one couples at the thicker radius (core in a shield: the loop was +36 %, audit A3C-5). Tests: tests/test_interpenetrating_wires.py.
  • ⚠ Close non-parallel pairs (10.46): nearly parallel, crossing, skew and T-junction pairs were integrated with a 16 × 16 rule that does not resolve 1/r (+12 % at 10 cm, up to +250 % at 1 cm, −13 % for T-junctions); they are integrated semi-analytically, to 5e-11 for directions that differ by more than 1e-6 rad (1.0e-9 at 1e-8 rad); filaments from one vertex at tiny angles were up to 16 % off (audit A3C-4). Tests: tests/test_neumann_close_pairs.py, tests/test_neumann_touching.py.
  • ⚠ carson_series and the segment order (10.20, audit round 3): a near-parallel pair was projected on the axis of its first segment, so the order of the segments moved entries by up to 3.1 % of the largest one; such pairs are projected on the bisector (two 1 km leads 2 m apart: +2e-5 at 0.5° … +6.4e-3 at 8°). Test: tests/test_carson_validity_domain.py::test_carson_tiling_does_not_depend_on_the_segment_order.
  • ⚠ Long segments under sommerfeld (10.24, audit A2C-2): one 16 × 16 rule over a segment much longer than the skin depth put a lumped 3 km PEN's earth-return resistance +13.4 % high at 1 kHz (+34.9 % at 5 km), without a warning; the lumped 3 km PEN now matches its refined chain to 1e-4, and the composite rule stays within 5.9e-4 (resistance) and 2.4e-4 (reactance) of a refined rule up to 3 km, with a step of 3.5e-4 at a quarter skin depth (audit A3C-4). Tests: tests/test_sommerfeld_long_segments.py.
  • Cost of the exact touching-pair rule (10.46, audit A2C-5): the coaxial closed forms are evaluated in one vectorised call per segment, bit for bit (2 km PEN solve 2.2–2.6 s → 1.1–1.4 s). Tests: tests/test_neumann_touching.py.
  • ⚠ Sommerfeld kernel (10.35, 10.36) for three or more layers, conductors below h₁ and distant pairs; SommerfeldResolutionWarning instead of silent truncation. Tests: tests/test_sommerfeld_accuracy.py.
  • ⚠ earth_return_correction_layered sign (10.46, F50). Test: tests/test_sommerfeld_accuracy.py::test_layered_point_kernel_has_the_exact_sign.
  • ⚠ Carson P and Q (10.46): the a⁻⁷ term of the Q asymptote, the small-a series and the θ = 0 quadrature. Tests: tests/test_carson_pq.py.
  • ⚠ Lumped and single-segment conductors (10.24): the Neumann inductance of a lumped conductor and the leakage of a one-piece galvanic conductor. Tests: tests/test_inductive_solver_integration.py::test_neumann_is_honoured_on_lumped_and_single_segment_conductors, tests/test_conductors_distributed.py::test_a_single_segment_galvanic_conductor_leaks.
  • Conductors at the surface (10.46, F52): crossing or lying in the surface plane is solved under sommerfeld and raises with the image models. Tests: tests/test_inductive_solver_integration.py::test_sommerfeld_accepts_a_surface_crossing_conductor.
  • segment_distance with a point segment (10.44, audit F04). Test: tests/test_conductor_proximity.py::test_segment_distance_with_point_segments.
  • Docstrings (10.95): invalid escape sequences and control characters. Tests: tests/test_coupling_conventions.py, tests/test_source_escapes.py.

Safety, fits and export

  • ⚠ Touch voltage at the electrode centre (F13, 10.21), also for rotated foundations (audit H4). Tests: tests/test_touch_voltage_footprint.py::test_grid_envelope_covers_the_one_metre_offset_curve, tests/test_touch_voltage_footprint.py::test_touch_voltage_of_a_rotated_foundation_matches_the_unrotated_one.
  • Uniform-current caveat (10.22): touch and step voltages near grids, meshes, stars, strips and bonded clusters from the image family warn. Test: tests/test_touch_voltage_footprint.py::test_uniform_current_backend_warns_once_per_call_near_a_grid.
  • EN 50522 anchors (F44, 10.42): checked against literals of EN 50522:2022 Table B.4 (values unchanged); docstrings cite the 2022 edition. Test: tests/test_safety.py::test_en50522_docstrings_cite_the_current_edition.
  • touch_voltage_spectrum (10.52, audit L4) rejects a frequency given twice. Test: tests/test_safety.py::test_touch_voltage_spectrum_rejects_a_frequency_given_twice.
  • Vector fit with a 0 Hz sample (10.41): no collapse to Z ≈ 0. Test: tests/test_vector_fitting.py::test_dc_sample_with_imaginary_part_does_not_collapse_the_fit.
  • Export errors and metadata (10.84, 10.27, 10.19): an actionable error without rho_at_fit, the running version in the BusType metadata, every non-finite number of a BusType document as null (audit A2G-08). Tests: tests/test_io_groundinsight.py::test_vector_fit_without_rho_at_fit_raises_an_actionable_error, tests/test_io_groundinsight.py::test_metadata_of_hand_built_fits_is_strict_json, tests/test_io_groundinsight.py::test_unknown_fit_quality_and_samples_are_written_as_null.
  • Result JSON (10.77): float keys, infinities and numpy values in the metadata survive the round trip; result files honour the umask (audit A1-05). Tests: tests/test_result_persistence.py.

Generators

  • ⚠ Measurement leads (10.17, 10.55, F48): leads no longer short-circuit the instrument and run at their depth. Tests: tests/test_measurement_loop.py::test_resistive_leads_do_not_change_the_reading, tests/test_measurement.py::test_buried_lead_runs_at_its_depth.
  • ⚠ Concrete shells (10.12–10.14, F08): the lumped shell outside TN service drops, rod current through the foundation's shell, substation and cabinet shells, and the layout builder. Tests: tests/test_concrete_one_mechanism.py.
  • ⚠ PEN joints and depth (10.38): joints no longer leak, PenConfig.depth_m acts. Tests: tests/test_pen_junctions.py, tests/test_pen_depth.py.
  • ⚠ Foundations (10.39, 10.54, F28): rotated meshes without the clamp, layout foundations from the footprint, no shift of the random draws, degenerate footprints get a minimum foundation. Tests: tests/test_rotated_foundations.py, tests/test_footprint_foundations.py.
  • ⚠ Mesh foundations depended on their orientation and on an absent shell (10.12, 10.39, audit A2G-04): the same bare mesh gave 4.796 Ω at 0° and 4.738 Ω at 30°, and a shell with ρ_c = ρ_soil lowered the largest touch voltage of a 10 m mesh from 232.3 to 221.2 V (100 A). Tests: tests/test_foundation_owners.py.
  • ⚠ Overlapping PEN cables (10.38): service drops ran from the cabinet back along the main, coaxial with it, which made an inductive 2-house network non-passive (Im Z_in −0.633 Ω at 1 kHz); drops now tap their feeding cable and run along no cable farther than one minimum section (1 cm; "along": both ends of a cable section within 1 cm of the drop's line — a test to 1 µm let a drop 2 µm beside a trunk run 60 m along it, audit R5A-01), and conductors lying side by side are touching wires (10.46). Tests: tests/test_pen_routing.py, tests/test_interpenetrating_wires.py, tests/test_foundation_contact.py::test_a_drop_beside_a_trunk_leaves_it_at_its_end.
  • Outlines without area (10.05, 10.54, audit A2G-06) crashed the generators; they are skipped on ingest and widened with a warning by the generators, and polygon foundations of outlines narrower than 1 m are widened like the OMBR ones (audit A3SG-07). Tests: tests/test_geo_footprint.py, tests/test_footprint_foundations.py.
  • Integer fields of a resolved config (10.53) hold int. Test: tests/test_generators_base.py::test_resolved_integer_fields_hold_integers.
  • Reproducibility (10.53, F07): resolved configs replay their realisation; masks ignore the footprint order. Tests: tests/test_generator_reproducibility.py.
  • ManhattanGridPlacement(jitter_m=<distribution>) (10.55, F47). Test: tests/test_placement.py::test_manhattan_grid_jitter_accepts_a_distribution.
  • Malformed Overpass payloads (10.05, audit M1, A2G-05) raise OverpassError before caching, also deeply nested ones (RecursionError before), on every Python version: the client checks the nesting right after decoding, because Python 3.14 may decode 100 000 levels where 3.12 and 3.13 raise (release CI). Tests: tests/test_overpass_ingest.py.
  • Layouts and generator configs pickled with 0.15.0 (10.69, audit A2G-07) still load and build. Tests: tests/test_generator_pickles.py, tests/test_generator_naming.py::test_layout_pickled_with_v0150_still_builds.
  • FoundationElectrodeSpec rejects non-positive size_m / size_xy_m, and a drawn side that is not positive raises when the site is built; four strips had accepted a negative side and built the mirrored rectangle (10 m × −1 m gave the 9.47312 Ω of 10 m × 1 m; audit D3A-01). Tests: tests/test_foundation_owners.py::test_a_non_positive_side_is_rejected, ::test_a_drawn_negative_side_is_rejected_when_the_site_is_built.
  • diagnose() leaves out the pairs of wires that a generated foundation bonds to its anchor (_bond_ conductors) where they meet at a shared corner or crossing: an encased 10 m ring / 2 × 2 mesh reported 4 / 9 proximity findings at its own corners (warnings with the point kernel; audit D3A-04); real proximity inside one foundation — the opposite sides of a narrow encased ring, the wires of a fine mesh — and unbonded strips with look-alike names are still reported (audit R4A-04). Tests: tests/test_diagnostics.py::test_diagnose_does_not_flag_the_wires_of_one_foundation, ::test_diagnose_still_flags_the_close_opposite_sides_of_a_narrow_encased_ring, ::test_diagnose_flags_the_parallel_wires_of_a_fine_encased_mesh, ::test_diagnose_still_flags_unbonded_strips_whose_names_look_like_one_foundation.
