  5. Discriminator — setting concrete_rho_ohm_m on any non-foundation electrode is silently a no-op (the field doesn't exist on those primitives). Setting it on FoundationElectrodeSpec and choosing style="ring" with orientation_deg != 0 (the rotated-strip path) and style="mesh" (the GridMeshElectrode path) both produce the same lumped correction for a square footprint to within 1 ‰.
  6. JSON round-trip — a config with stochastic concrete_rho_ohm_m=Discrete(...) round-trips through model_dump_json / model_validate_json and reproduces the same draws under a fixed seed.
  7. Stochastic-moisture sweep — a 1 000-sample Monte Carlo over concrete_rho_ohm_m=Discrete(values=[50, 150, 500, 2000]) reproduces the analytical mean of \(R_\text{shell,total}\) to within 1 % statistical noise.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Foundation electrodes generated from the OSM path (ADR-0011) now reflect their real Streifenfundament environment, closing one of the largest physical gaps in the generator pipeline.
  • The dry-concrete worst case becomes computable without leaving the 1-kHz quasi-static regime.
  • Stochastic moisture maps cleanly onto the existing Distribution framework — Monte Carlo over concrete_rho_ohm_m is one line of config.
  • The lumped path adds zero solver risk: existing distributed- conductor machinery already handles arbitrary bond impedances.

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• The distributed path touches the diagonal-augmentation hooks of every layered backend (image, image_2layer, image_nlayer, optionally mom_sommerfeld). Each backend gets one new conditional branch; the test programme covers the cross-engine agreement.
  • The shell-thickness t becomes a new modelling decision the user has to make. We document the typical range (50–200 mm) and default to 50 mm so a "I just set \(\rho_c\) and want it to work" experience exists.
  • StripElectrode and Conductor each gain one optional field; JSON files written before this ADR continue to round-trip but carry None defaults.

docs.title: Neutral
docs.text:
• The Sunde-shell decomposition is well-known textbook physics (Sunde 1968 §4.4, Tagg 1964 ch. 7). Implementing it does not expand groundfield's modelling envelope, only fills a gap.
  • ADR-0007 (cross-layer electrodes) is orthogonal: a foundation at 0.8 m with a 5 cm shell stays entirely inside a typical \(h_1 \ge 1\,\text{m}\) upper layer, so the cross-layer machinery is not exercised by the concrete shell itself.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Sunde, E. D. (1968). Earth Conduction Effects in Transmission Systems, Dover. §4.4 — wire in concrete in conducting earth (the closed-form cylindrical-shell formula used here).
  • Tagg, G. F. (1964). Earth Resistances, George Newnes. Ch. 7 — foundation earth electrodes, contact-resistance contribution.
  • DIN 18014:2023-06. Fundamenterder — Planung, Ausführung und Dokumentation. DIN, Berlin. Defines the geometric envelope (depth, perimeter, conductor cross section) the Sunde shell wraps.
  • Banton, O. et al. (2017). Electrical resistivity of concrete: a function of moisture content and ageing. Cement and Concrete Research 95, 60–69. Empirical basis for the four-state moisture bands recommended above.
  • ADR-0003 — distributed conductor model. The V1 path reuses the per-conductor distributed framework introduced there.
  • ADR-0011 — OSM building footprints. This ADR completes the OSM-driven generator pipeline by giving the generated foundations the right electrical boundary condition.

docs.title: Amendment 2026.11 — one mechanism: the shell coefficient on the wires (review pass 10)
docs.text:
Findings 10.12, 10.13 and 10.14.

The two variants of this ADR reached the solver on different roads, and only one of them did. Variant 1 (lumped) recorded the total shell resistance in World.concrete_shell_corrections, which only TnNetworkGenerator turned into a series resistance on the PEN service drop; Engine.solve of any other world, solve_mutual_matrix, solve_mutual_field and the layout builder ignored it but kept the inflated wire radius \(r_b\). For the AP1 catalogue, whose foundation matrix comes from solve_mutual_matrix, the concrete therefore lowered the foundation impedance at low soil resistivity instead of raising it (10.12). Spreading a site's lumped resistance over rods and braces mis-assigned their current (10.13), and the layout builder dropped the shell (10.14).

Decision:

  1. One representation. Every electrode kind has the field concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m, \(C = \frac{\rho_c}{2\pi}\ln\frac{r_b}{r_a}\) in Ω·m. The image family and solve_mutual_* add \(C/\Delta s\) to the diagonal of every segment — variant 2 of this ADR, now for every electrode kind. Under the uniform current of an owner of length \(L\) this is exactly the lumped series resistance \(C/L\) of variant 1, so the two variants coincide by construction and the 2 % acceptance criterion is met exactly (tests/test_concrete_shell_coefficient.py, tests/test_concrete_one_mechanism.py).
  2. Generators. Both concrete_model settings put \(C\) and the radius \(r_b\) on every wire of an encased foundation, the cross-braces of a mesh foundation included (user decision Q20, below); rods stay bare; no shell resistance on PEN drops; substation and cabinet electrodes get \(C\) when their specification is encased. concrete_model has no effect: every rectangle without cross-braces is one owner per side (user decision Q38, below); the field is deprecated (user decision Q21, below).
  3. Registry deprecated. World.concrete_shell_corrections is read by no solver and warns at solve (removal no earlier than 2027.5).
  4. Conversion helpers in groundfield.geometry.electrodes: concrete_shell_coefficient, shell_coefficient_from_resistance, shell_resistance_from_coefficient.
  5. Capability. Backends outside the image family reject electrodes with a shell (BackendCapabilityError). Since the release scope of 2026-11-14 mom and mom_sommerfeld add the same term per segment to their point-matching systems, \(C/\Delta s\) on the diagonal and the shell drop on the segment potential; with one owner per segment the image family solves the same system (agreement \(7\cdot10^{-16}\)), and an encased ring rises by exactly \(C/(2\pi r)\) in every soil. fem is the backend left that rejects shells (concrete shells).

The API additions and Variant 1 sections above describe the mechanism of 0.15.0 and are superseded by this amendment.

docs.title: User decision Q20 (2026.11): the cross-braces are encased
docs.text: A foundation earth electrode per DIN 18014 lies in the concrete together with its connections. The first version of this amendment, on the 2026.11 development line and never released, kept the cross-braces of a mesh foundation bare (\(r_a\), no \(C\)), like the rods (finding 10.13); in 0.15.0 they had the radius \(r_b\) but no \(C\) (and with "lumped" no wire had \(C\)). Since the user decision Q20 every wire of an encased foundation carries \(r_b\) and \(C\), and the lumped shell resistance of the foundation is \(C\) over its whole encased length. Bare braces were a bare electrode inside the concrete: the foundation could not exceed the spreading resistance of its braces alone, however dry the concrete. For the generators' default house mesh (10 m, 2 × 2 cells, 0.8 m, \(r_a\) = 5 mm, \(t\) = 5 cm) in 100 Ω·m encasing the braces changes \(Z\) by +1.5 / +47 / +307 % at \(\rho_c\) = 150 / 1 000 / 5 000 Ω·m against the bare braces of the development line. Against 0.15.0, default engine of each version, the same house moves by +6.6 / +68 / +399 % ("distributed") and +23 / +157 / +782 % ("lumped", whose shell Engine.solve did not read in 0.15.0). Engine.solve and a hand assembly of the wires from solve_mutual_matrix agree to 4e-16; the assembly uses the same kernel and owner model, so it checks the generator's wiring of \(r_b\) and \(C\), not the numbers. An independent thin-wire boundary-element solution (audit D2B) reproduces the numbers to 0.02 percentage points for the same owner model; with one current per segment (the moment-method reference) the change is +49.2 / +318.5 % with the line kernel and +49.6 / +321.2 % with mom (audit W2B-06) instead of +46.9 / +307 % at 1 000 / 5 000 Ω·m, a model uncertainty of the owner model that lies in the bare-brace reference (1.6 / 2.8 % high there, 1.5 / 2.7 % with the point kernel against mom; at most 0.6 % for encased meshes) (tests/test_concrete_one_mechanism.py; tables on the concrete-shell page). Ring and building-outline foundations, among them the AP1 catalogue, do not change by the brace rule.

docs.title: User decision Q21 (2026.11): concrete_model is deprecated
docs.text: Since item 2 the field no longer selected a shell model; it only chose one owner ("lumped", one grid mesh) or one per side ("distributed") for an axis-aligned rectangle without cross-braces (style="ring", or "mesh" with n_x = n_y = 1), and user decision Q38 (below) took that choice away as well. The field is deprecated like the flat sommerfeld_* fields of the engine: "distributed" keeps loading and emits a DeprecationWarning at the user's line; the default "lumped" — also in the configuration JSON and pickles of 0.15.0 — is accepted silently; a model_copy validates an update of the field like the constructor (another value raises, audit D2B-04; only that field, so a subclass with fields of its own copies as before, audit R2B-05) and warns only when it sets the deprecated value, also through copy.replace on Python ≥ 3.13 (audit R2B-06), so the copies made by the generators do not repeat the warning. Assigning the attribute and unpickling do not validate and do not warn. Removal no earlier than 2027.5 (tests/test_foundation_owners.py).

docs.title: User decision Q38 (2026.11): one owner per side, already in 2026.11.0
docs.text:
Every rectangle without cross-braces (style="ring", or "mesh" with n_x = n_y = 1) is one strip per side, bonded to the local \(-y\) side, at every orientation and for both values of concrete_model, which therefore has no effect; the warning of "distributed" says so. Up to the decision the default "lumped" made an axis-aligned one — also one at a multiple of 90°, which was built as the axis-aligned rectangle with swapped sides — a single GridMeshElectrode (rectangles at other angles were one strip per side for both values; audit D3B-04). Rationale: of the two owner models, one per side is the closer one to one current per segment (at the largest decreases of the scope 0.23 … 0.90 % high against 0.55 … 2.16 % for one owner; over the whole scope at most 1.4 % high, 150 m × 3 m bare in 30 / 200 Ω·m, against up to 2.2 % — 2.16 % for 16 m × 1 m in a 0.2 m shell of 30 Ω·m over 1 000 / 30 Ω·m at 0.25 m segments, audits D3B-01, R4B-05), it does not depend on the orientation, and it is what rotated rectangles and, wire by wire, meshes already were. Polygon outlines (one closed polyline), meshes with cross-braces and RingElectrodeSpec circles are unchanged.

Size of the change for an axis-aligned rectangle built with the default value. The input impedance per side is never higher than with one owner: the bonded owners carry the split of the current among the sides that dissipates least (the owner matrix is symmetric and positive definite), and the single owner's split is one of those they can take; for a square nothing changes. Over the 39 soils of the AP1 grid, for a 5 mm wire at 0.8 m, bare or in concrete of 30 to 1 000 Ω·m up to 0.2 m thick, it is lower by less than 1 % up to aspect ratio 4 (short side at least 1 m, sides up to 80 m) and 2 % up to aspect ratio 50 (short side at least 1 m, sides up to 150 m); bare or with the default 5 cm shell by less than 0.4 % and 1 %. The largest decreases found are −0.686 / −1.529 % and −0.320 / −0.907 % (4 m × 1 m and 16 m × 1 m in 0.2 m of wet concrete over 1 000 / 30 Ω·m; 80 m × 20 m and 150 m × 7.75 m in 30 / 200 Ω·m): the scan of audit R2B-01 (13 524 owner matrices, every value of \(\rho_c\)), re-run for the decision, with no positive value beyond round-off, and Engine.solve and the owner algebra agree. The same numbers bounded the difference between the two values of the field before the decision, as one owner over one per side minus one: the first version of decision Q21 quoted 0.16 % and 0.67 %, measured on six rings; the second 0.7 % and 1.6 %, the maxima of a coarser scan, without a shortest side for aspect ratio 4 (2 m × 0.5 m changes by −1.01 %). The largest values belong to the 0.2 m shell, whose outer radius of 0.205 m is not thin against the default 0.5 m segments (ratio 2.4, below the thin-wire limit of 5): there an independent solution that averages the potential over the wire surface gives −0.594 / −1.447 % instead of −0.686 / −1.529 % (the same at 0.25, 0.125 and 0.083 m segments), and the comparison of each model with one current per segment on the concrete-shell page is not converged.

Consequences: the AP1 station (4 m × 4 m ring with three rods) changes by −0.0009 … −0.0026 % over the 39 AP1 soils, its houses (building outlines) not at all; the golden case mutual_foundations_lumped_concrete equals mutual_foundations_distributed_concrete (its passive foundation carries equalising currents: \(Z_G\) 5.2e-4; the field at its edges +5.5 / −4.7 % — +5.9 / −5.1 % with the golden engine's 2 m segments and the point kernel, a segmentation effect (audit R4B-13) —, 1.6 % of the largest value of the case's field, the golden harness's norm-wise measure, audit D3B-02). The electrode named after the foundation is the \(-y\) side, so its current and grounding_impedance refer to that side (as for rotated rectangles and meshes); cluster quantities (cluster_impedance, input_impedance, solve_mutual_matrix, the touch-voltage helpers, which take the whole foundation) keep their meaning. Its connection point, where conductors attached by name start, moves from the centre of the rectangle to the corner at the start of the \(-y\) side; the generators' cables and service drops end at the point of the foundation nearest to each conductor instead (user decision Q41, ADR-0009 amendment 2026.11), so that corner is no longer where they meet the house. fem reduces the four strips as a cluster of four electrodes (see the fem page). Tests: tests/test_foundation_owners.py (# user decision Q38).

docs.title: ADR-0013: Calendar versioning
docs.text: Status Accepted Date 2026-11-07 Deciders Project maintainers Scope version numbers of groundfield (pyproject.toml, groundfield.__version__, CITATION.cff), the release tool scripts/release.py, the changelog, the deprecation policy and the versioned documentation

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Up to 0.15.0 groundfield used semantic-versioning numbers below 1.0: sixteen releases in about six months, most of them minor releases that changed numerical results. The numbers said little:

  • Compatibility was never the question a user of a reference model asks; the question is which results changed. A 0.x minor release could move an impedance by tens of per cent, a patch release could fix a security problem without touching a number. The version number carried neither fact.
  • Dating matters for a dissertation and its catalogue of computed networks: a result has to be traceable to the code that produced it, and "computed with 2026.11.0" places it in time; "computed with 0.15.0" needs a lookup.
  • Review pass 10 asked for one release with everything (physics fixes, performance, architecture, documentation) and for an explicit list of numbers-changing releases. A 1.0.0 would have promised a stability that a research code under active validation does not offer.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Version scheme YYYY.M.MICRO in PEP 440 canonical form: year, month without leading zero, and MICRO = the number of earlier final releases in that month (the first release of November 2026 is 2026.11.0; a second one would be 2026.11.1; January 2027 starts at 2027.1.0). Pre-releases append aN, bN or rcN; post- and development releases .postN / .devN. A deleted tag never reuses a number.
  2. One release tool. python scripts/release.py calver [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--dry-run] computes the next version; python scripts/release.py set X sets an explicit one (also to finalise a pre-release). The tool runs every check before it writes anything: repository root, clean tree, a branch checked out, the three version sources agree, the new version is valid and above the current one, its tag does not exist, [Unreleased] of the changelog is not empty, no unmerged changelog.d/ fragment remains. It writes the three version sources and the changelog heading, commits and tags — and never pushes. The tool is not installed with the package (finding 10.02); it runs from a checkout.
  3. Numbers instead of semantics. Every release that moves computed numbers carries a ⚠ "Numbers that change" block in its release notes (quantity, magnitude, who is affected), and the changelog keeps a table of all numbers-changing releases. Every result records the producing version in metadata["provenance"].
  4. Deprecation policy. A deprecated name keeps working, emits a DeprecationWarning naming the replacement and the earliest removal version, and is removed no earlier than two releases and six months after the release that announced it: names deprecated in 2026.11.0 go in 2027.5 at the earliest.
  5. Versioned documentation. The documentation is published per release with mike (one documentation version per calendar release, latest for the newest release, dev for the main branch).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive. A version number dates a result; the changelog answers the question users ask (which numbers moved); the release tool cannot leave half-bumped version files behind; removal dates of deprecated names are computable from the announcing version.

Negative. The version no longer signals compatibility; users must read the ⚠ block of the release notes. Tools that compare versions numerically must not assume MAJOR < 1 semantics; 2026.11.0 sorts above 0.15.0 under PEP 440, so upgrades work.

Neutral. The first calendar release follows 0.15.0 directly; there is no 1.0.0. Pass-5's guard against a hard-coded version in the project instructions is kept by the release tool.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Python Packaging Authority. PEP 440 — Version Identification and Dependency Specification.
  • Keep a Changelog, version 1.1.0 (format of CHANGELOG.md).
  • Calendar versioning, https://calver.org (scheme catalogue).
  • Review pass 10 (2026-11-07), decision questions 1 and 11, findings 10.02, 10.09 and 10.93.

docs.title: ADR-0014: Backend registry and shared solve pipeline
docs.text: Status Accepted Date 2026-11-07 Deciders Project maintainers Scope groundfield.solver.registry, Engine.solve, Engine.options, the private modules solver._pipeline, _discretize, _topology, _inductive, _kernels, _series, _guards, result provenance and persistence (groundfield.io.results)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Review pass 10 (findings 10.74, 10.75, 10.77, 10.79, 10.81) found the solver grown by copying:

  • Engine.solve was an eight-branch if chain. Backends declared nothing about what they could solve; an unsupported world failed deep inside a backend, or worse, solved with a silent simplification (return_to ignored, distributed conductors reduced).
  • The solve pipeline — discretise, inject the sources, build clusters and branches, assemble the inductive block, solve the nodal system, build the result — existed in seven copies (991 duplicate lines). The Tagg/Sunde series existed in four or five copies with two truncation policies, the injection loop seven times, the point kernel five times. This is how the length-weighted read-back fix of 0.11 missed cim and how the post-solve series kept a cap of 100 terms.
  • solver/image.py (2 500 lines) served as a private library for the other backends (63 private cross-module imports).
  • Of 32 metadata keys only two were common to all backends; results carried no provenance and had no versioned file format.
  • Backend settings were flat Engine fields (sommerfeld_*), accepted silently for every backend; the fem knobs were unreachable.

docs.title: Registry
docs.text:
groundfield.solver.registry is the authority on backend names: register_backend(name, solve_fn, capabilities=..., options_model=..., deprecated_alias_of=..., experimental=..., forward=...).

  • Capabilities (BackendCapabilities): soil layer counts, conductor models, concrete shells, two-terminal sources, junctions, voltage sources (amendment below), source kernels. Engine.solve checks a world before the backend runs. Hard mismatches (layer count, concrete shells, an explicitly requested kernel, junctions, voltage sources) raise BackendCapabilityError — a subclass of ValueError and NotImplementedError, so earlier except clauses keep working — and name a backend that can solve the world; soft ones (a conductor model the backend reduces, return_to ignored) warn with BackendCapabilityWarning.
  • Names. Unknown names raise with the closest registered name. Deprecated names (cim, bem, image_nlayer) warn with the replacement and the removal version; an experimental backend (fem) warns once per process. Only the requested name is checked: the forwarding of image to image_2layer for a two-layer soil stays silent. Alias chains are not allowed.
  • Options. Backend settings live in Engine.options, keyed by backend name and validated by the backend's options model (MomSommerfeldOptions, FemOptions); misspelled names raise with a suggestion, options for another backend warn. The flat sommerfeld_* fields of 0.15.0 are deprecated aliases. The image-series controls (image_max_terms, image_series_tol) stay common Engine fields because every layered backend and the post-solve evaluation read them.
  • Metadata core. Engine.solve writes backend, effective_backend, kernel, groundfield_version, frequencies, n_segments, soil_kind, earth_inductive_model, solve_time_s, series and provenance into every result (CORE_METADATA_KEYS).
  • Third-party backends register a solve function with the same contract, solve_fn(world, engine, **options) -> FieldResult, without editing Engine.solve.

docs.title: Shared pipeline
docs.text:
groundfield.solver._pipeline implements the solve once:

discretise → inject → build_topology → assemble_branches → solve → build_result

A backend supplies a Green's-function object (the ImageGreen protocol: prepare(segments, arrays) -> kernel, metadata(solution)) and, for the point-matching family, the segment-level solve and read-back (_PointMatchingGreen). The steps are shared by image, image_2layer, mom and mom_sommerfeld, so a fix in one step — two-terminal sources, junction nodes, the inductive branch block, the burial-depth guards — reaches every backend at once. fem, which solves a different model, is registered but not on the pipeline. Around the pipeline:

  • _kernels holds every kernel of the closed-form family (point and line kernel, field evaluation, row-block and memory budget), _series the one ImageSeries object of the Tagg/Sunde series used by the solver, FieldResult.potential and solve_mutual_*.
  • Geometry queries that were isinstance ladders are methods of the electrode classes (segments, segment_count, wire_polylines, bounds, total_length, min_feature_length).
  • image.py keeps re-exports of the moved private names for one release cycle.

docs.title: Provenance and persistence
docs.text: Every result records metadata["provenance"]: package and dependency versions, platform, the engine configuration and a SHA-256 fingerprint of the world as built, plus the solve time stamp. save_result / load_result write and read a versioned envelope (groundfield.result, schema version 1) with a lossless metadata codec (complex numbers, arrays, non-finite values); a newer schema raises.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive. One place for each piece of physics; capability errors at the call site instead of wrong numbers; results that can be traced and reloaded; a new backend is a registration plus a Green's-function object. The refactor was verified against the golden-value suite: bit-identical, except for the round-off of the reordered two-layer series summation (at most \(7.3\cdot 10^{-16}\) relative).

Negative. The private module structure is new; external scripts that imported private helpers from groundfield.solver.image may need the re-exports (kept) or the electrode methods. The two-layer owner split of cross-layer electrodes (ADR-0007 amendment 2026.11) is a composed path inside image_2layer until the pipeline offers a split/merge hook.

Neutral. Backend names and results are unchanged; deprecated names keep working until 2027.5 at the earliest (ADR-0013).

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Review pass 10 (2026-11-07), findings 10.74–10.77, 10.79, 10.81, decision question 9.
  • ADR-0002 (engine family) and its amendment 2026.11.

docs.title: Amendment 2026.11 — impressed voltage sources in the pipeline (finding 10.51)
docs.text:
VoltageSource was a data model only: up to 0.15.0 every backend dropped it with a warning and solved to zero potentials, the release preparation made it raise. Decision (scope of the 2026.11 release, 2026-11-14): the shared pipeline solves it by modified nodal analysis. Step 2 lists the voltage sources next to the impressed currents (_pipeline.impressed_voltages); step 5 appends, after the branch block, one unknown per voltage source — its current \(I_v\), entering Kirchhoff's current law at attached_to (\(-I_v\) on the left-hand side) and return_to (\(+I_v\)) — and one row \(\varphi_a - \varphi_r = U\) (\(\varphi_r = 0\) for remote earth). The image family and the point-matching family call the same helpers (_topology._voltage_source_entries), so the cross-layer path, inductive branches, frequency sweeps and junction terminals need no code of their own. A voltage-source terminal is a driven node: its cluster does not float. A world without voltage sources assembles the same matrix as before, bit for bit (golden suite strict against the base). The backend reports the solved currents in FieldResult.sources (SourceRecord.current, with the impressed SourceRecord.voltage); input_impedance() is \(U/I\).

World.check rejects what makes the system singular: a voltage source with both terminals in one ideally bonded cluster, and voltage sources that close a loop through ideal bonds or remote earth (union-find over clusters with remote earth as one more node). A voltage source of 0 V is an ideal short and allowed. The capability voltage_sources is declared by image, image_2layer, mom and mom_sommerfeld; fem raises BackendCapabilityError. solve_mutual_* ignore the sources of the world, as before. Validation (tests/test_voltage_sources.py): the voltage solve equals the 1 A current-source solve scaled by \(U/Z_\text{in}\) in every backend, two- and three-layer soil, the cross-layer path and inductive conductors at 0, 50 and 1000 Hz (at most \(1.4\cdot 10^{-15}\) relative); a two-terminal source equals \(U/(Z_{11}+Z_{22}-Z_{12}-Z_{21})\) of solve_mutual_matrix, three voltage sources the hand-inverted transfer matrix of three 1 A solves, a rod Dwight's formula (−0.012 %) and its far field the hemispherical \(\rho I/(2\pi r)\).

docs.title: Amendment 2026.11 — internal impedance of a voltage source (user decision D1)
docs.text:
Decision of 2026-11-15: a VoltageSource carries an internal series impedance \(Z_q(f) = R + j\omega L\) as two fields, internal_resistance_ohm and internal_inductance_h (both ≥ 0, default 0: the ideal source, which assembles the matrix of the first amendment entry for entry). \(Z_q\) is the one diagonal entry of the source's constraint row, \(\varphi_a - \varphi_r + Z_q I_v = U\), with \(I_v\) flowing from the source into attached_to (the terminal voltage is \(U - Z_q I_v\)). The pipeline evaluates it per angular frequency (ImpressedVoltage.terminals(cluster_id, omega)); _voltage_source_entries writes \(\operatorname{Re} Z_q\) into the real matrix and _source_reactance_entries adds \(j\operatorname{Im} Z_q\) to its complex copy. A real (galvanic) system with a non-zero \(\omega L\) therefore takes the complex path rather than being refused. The image family solves its owner-level system once per frequency (cheap: ×1.00 … ×1.09 the R-only solve at 1 … 20 frequencies on a 1 488-segment station, homogeneous and two-layer). The point-matching family would factorise its segment-level system once per frequency — ×2.0 / ×8.1 / ×28 the R-only solve at 1 / 5 / 20 frequencies on 1 488 segments (audit W2R2-02) — so it keeps the one real factorisation instead: \(j\omega L\) enters only the diagonal of the V source rows, the real block \(A_{11}\) (the world with its voltage sources open) is factorised once with the V + 2 right-hand sides \([\operatorname{Re} b_1, \operatorname{Im} b_1, A_{12}]\), and each frequency solves the V × V Schur complement \((A_{22} - A_{21} A_{11}^{-1} A_{12} + j\omega L)\,x_2 = b_2 - A_{21} A_{11}^{-1} b_1\) (_point_matching_source_sweep; exact, the Woodbury update the auditor proposed). Measured on the same world (best of three): ×1.06 / ×1.04 / ×1.02, and the results agree with the per-frequency path to 3.3 · 10⁻¹⁵ and with the scaled 1 A solve to 1.3 · 10⁻¹⁵. A solve at \(f = 0\) alone remains the R-only solve, bit for bit; inside a sweep the \(f = 0\) entry agrees with it to round-off. The same two helpers serve the image family (including the cross-layer path) and the point-matching family, so image, image_2layer, mom and mom_sommerfeld honour \(Z_q\) with conductors, inductive coupling and frequency sweeps; fem keeps refusing voltage sources.

input_impedance() of a voltage source is the impedance the source sees, \(U/I - Z_q\), without its own \(Z_q\); SourceRecord carries \(R\) and \(L\) so a result read back from a file computes it alone. Records and sources written before have 0 / 0: in JSON by the field defaults, in pickles since audit W2R2-01 through a __setstate__ that fills the two fields. A non-zero \(R\) or \(L\) below the smallest normal float is rejected (audit W2R2-10). World.check treats a source with \(R > 0\) as no edge of the loop check — two such sources in parallel, or a ring with one of them, are solvable — while an inductance alone keeps the source an edge, because \(Z_q\) vanishes at \(f = 0\) and World.check does not know the engine's frequencies. A source short-circuited by an ideal bond stays rejected also with \(Z_q\) (its current \(U/Z_q\) would circulate through the bond and the source, none through the soil — the wording of the message since audit W2R2-04). Validation (tests/test_voltage_source_impedance.py): the solve equals the junction + lumped_series_resistance_ohm pattern for a resistance, and the 1 A current-source solve with \(I = U/(Z_q + Z_\text{in})\) at 0, 50 and 1000 Hz in every backend, with inductive conductors (three earth models) and on the cross-layer path; several sources satisfy \((Z_T + \operatorname{diag} Z_q)\,\mathbf I = \mathbf U\) with the transfer matrix of 1 A solves, a two-terminal source \(U/(Z_q + Z_{11}+Z_{22}-Z_{12}-Z_{21})\) of solve_mutual_matrix.

docs.title: ADR-0015: Exact line-source kernel as the default of the image family
docs.text: Status Accepted Date 2026-11-07 Deciders Project maintainers Scope Engine.kernel; the reaction matrix and the field evaluation of image, image_2layer (and the deprecated names that run them), solve_mutual_matrix, solve_mutual_field, FieldResult.potential; PointSource.direction

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Up to 0.15.0 the image family placed the current of every wire segment at the segment midpoint (point kernel) and used the collocation self term \(2\ln(L/a)/L\) on the diagonal. Review pass 10 (finding 10.28) showed that this kernel converges to a biased limit:

  • Per row of the reaction matrix the self term is \(+0.61/L\) too large and the two collinear neighbours \(-0.77/L\) too small; the row sum errs by about \(-0.23/L\) for every segment length \(L\). Because the row sum itself scales like \(1/L\), the relative error of the resistance does not vanish under refinement: rods, rings and strips converge 0.9–1.9 % below the exact solution of the uniform-current model. A convergence study cannot see it.
  • Field points near a wire see point sources: the surface potential spikes at every segment midpoint and is several per cent off above a wire at typical segment lengths (finding 10.33).
  • Near a layer interface the point form of the interface image needs segments much shorter than the distance to the interface (−46 % for a ring 5 cm below \(h_1\) at ds = 0.5 m).
  • The kernel error has the opposite sign of the uniform-current ansatz error, so for impedances the two partly cancel — which made the old numbers look closer to some references than they were.

The review proposed the exact line-source kernel as an opt-in with a default decision at 1.0. The user decided to make it the default in this release, with kernel="point" reproducing the old numbers.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Engine.kernel takes None (default), "line" or "point". None lets the backend choose its preferred kernel: "line" for the image family, the backend's own kernel ("point") for every other backend. An explicit "line" on a backend without it raises BackendCapabilityError. The request is carried in the value, so an engine rebuilt from JSON or from a result's provenance block runs like the original; metadata["kernel"] records the kernel that ran.
  2. Galerkin form. The line kernel is the segment-averaged potential of uniform line currents with the reduced kernel \(1/\sqrt{r^2 + a^2}\) — the Galerkin pairing dual to the uniform-current ansatz, symmetric, and exact for a straight wire at any segment length. A Galerkin self term with collocated exact mutual terms was rejected: it biases every interior row by about \(-0.6/L\), worse than the point kernel.
  3. Evaluation. Pairs within six segment lengths are integrated exactly (closed form for parallel pairs, graded Gauss–Legendre with the exact inner line potential otherwise); farther pairs use the point form plus the quadrupole term of the segment average, remainder \(O((L/R)^4)\). The Tagg/Sunde images use the point form unless closer than six segment lengths. On the cross-layer path pairs in different layers carry the transmitted resistivity \(2\rho_1\rho_2/(\rho_1+\rho_2)\) and the interface image is a Galerkin integral for near pairs, which keeps the matrix reciprocal.
  4. Field evaluation. Line-kernel results store the unit tangent of every source segment (PointSource.direction), and FieldResult.potential evaluates exact line potentials near the segments. Results without directions (written by 0.15.0) are evaluated with the point kernel.
  5. The mom family keeps the point kernel. Its point-matching scheme is defined with point sources; cross-checks between image and mom pin kernel="point" so that they compare current models on one kernel.
  6. Cost control. The far-field term over all pairs is the expensive part. It is compiled with numba when available (optional extra fast, bit-identical blocks) and runs in NumPy otherwise; kernel="point" remains the opt-out.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Numbers change. Grounding resistances of single electrodes rise by about 1–2 % at typical segment lengths (the point kernel's bias); network quantities move less — the input impedance of a synthetic 30-house network by +0.35 % (performance page). The generated kernel check of the validation page shows the size per geometry and segment length; the release notes list the moved golden cases. What remains against the true thin-wire solution is the uniform-current ansatz itself (about +0.9 % for the 3 m rod of benchmark B2, larger near grid corners for field quantities, see the image engine page).

Cost. The Engine.kernel documentation gives the measured factor for a 16-house solve (\(N\) = 1920): 2.7 with numba, 5.7 without; the performance page puts it into the context of whole studies.

Accuracy statements become clean. With the kernel error removed, the remaining deviations of the image family are attributable to the current model, which mom checks — the separation the validation page relies on.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Keep the point kernel as default, line opt-in (the review's proposal). Rejected: every study would carry a known, invisible 1–2 % bias by default.
  • Far-field cut-off (no quadrupole term beyond some distance): about 1.5 times the point-kernel cost at about \(10^{-4}\) accuracy instead of a few \(10^{-6}\). Not taken; the numba path makes the full form affordable.
  • Quadrupole terms for every Tagg/Sunde image: at most 0.05 % gain on a straight strip in two-layer soil for about twice the series assembly cost. Not taken in 2026.11.0 at first; taken in wave 3 with a taper (amendment below).

docs.title: Amendment 2026.11 (wave 3) — a continuous switch, far images, the cross-layer path
docs.text:
User decision D2 of 2026-11-15, audits W2B-01/-02, finding 10.28.

  1. Continuous switch. Decision 3 switched from the exact integral to the far form at six segment lengths in one step. The pairs six segments apart on a straight wire, and in two-layer soil every segment's own Tagg/Sunde image when an image distance equals six segment lengths, sit exactly there, so the round-off of the coordinates decided their form: the same world at different positions spread by up to 4.4e-7 (a 12 m strip) and 2.6e-5 (two layers) in the impedance. Pairs between six and 7.5 segment lengths now take a C¹ blend of the exact and the far value, for direct pairs, every image, the images of the cross-layer correction and field points. The spread is at most 1e-13 over local positions and the UTM solves lie as close to the local ones as with the point kernel (3e-11). Alternatives: a margin on the distance (a new knife-edge at another distance, which a chosen \(h_1\) hits again) and a far form exact to round-off at six segment lengths (about ten more multipole orders); the blend costs the integrals of the pairs in the band (+24 % solve time in homogeneous soil).
  2. Far form. The far form of segment pairs carries the radius term \(-a^2/(2R^3)\) of the reduced kernel \(1/\sqrt{R^2 + a^2}\) that every exact pair uses; without it the far form was \(a^2/(2R^2)\) away from the exact pairs it joins, which made straight wires converge non-monotonically at the 1e-6 level.
  3. Far Tagg/Sunde images carry the quadrupole term (the alternative above). On every image it cost 2.2 … 3.9 times the solve of 16 house grids; the term is therefore tapered off between 60 and 120 segment lengths of vertical distance between observer and image (at most \(1/(6\cdot 60^2)\) of the image's point value, for a vertical wire and its collinear image; \(1/(8\cdot 60^2)\) for horizontal wires; the order of the far form's remainder at the switch), a property of the pair, and images beyond every observer are skipped: 1.2 … 1.5 times, the impedance within 1e-6 of the term on every image. Gain: the strip of the alternative within 7.7e-7 instead of 5.1e-4, monotone in the segment length; its surface potential within 8e-6 instead of 0.94 %; house grids 3e-6 … 1.8e-4.
  4. The cross-layer path (ADR-0007) treats the images of its layered correction alike (ADR-0007, amendment wave 3).

docs.title: Amendment 2026.11 (wave 3, audit W3A) — image pairs, the cost of the far images, a point-form option
docs.text:
The author's decision of 2026-11-15 and audit W3A (stream fw3xl).

  1. Image pairs. Decision 2 applied the reduced kernel to every pair, images included, and point 2 of the wave-3 amendment gave the far form of images the radius term. An image line that passes a wire at a transverse distance \(\rho_\perp \ge a\) acts with its axis value (the average of \(\ln\lvert x - y\rvert\) over a circle of radius \(a\) is \(\ln\max(\rho, a)\)), so the reduced kernel left out \(a^2/(2d^2)\) of an image \(d\) away: a ring 1 cm above a 1000 / 30 Ω·m interface read +1.60 % against its exact thin ring (audit W3A-02, finding of w4axi). The line potential of an image at a point of the observer now uses \(\max(\rho_\perp, a)\), which is the reduced kernel for a collinear image (a rod against its own image, where it is exact); an image within one wire radius of its own segment blends into the reduced kernel of the direct pair it nearly coincides with, so that a wire on the interface is the same on both sides; the far form of images has no radius term; the image corrections are symmetrised (the pointwise rule differs between the two orders of a skew pair). The ring is within 0.004 % now, a rod through the interface within 1.4e-6 of its exact two-owner value. The soil-surface image keeps the reduced kernel (homogeneous results unchanged; with the transverse distance a house grid at 0.8 m would move by 4e-7, at 0.1 m by 1.7e-5 — an open decision).
  2. Cost of the far images. Every image the longest segment of the world reached was evaluated on every pair (audit W3A-01: eight 9.4 m pieces among 1920 segments multiplied the far-image work by 5.6), and the image density of a high contrast made a 40-house network in 1000 / 30 Ω·m with \(h_1\) = 1.5 m (82 images within the taper) 4.4 times the solve of the base. An image is now evaluated on the pairs whose longer segment reaches it (bit-identical), the far-image part of the reaction matrix on its upper half (it is symmetric), with one division per evaluation and the taper and tolerance tests left out where they hold for a whole block (round-off). That network takes 1.8 times the solve before wave 3 with numba (3.6 times without; 4.2 and 9.7 before the audit), 16 house grids with eight long pieces 1.5 times (2.8 before; performance page). Rejected: tabulating the far term per image family in the horizontal distance (an interpolation error instead of round-off) and multi-threading (the base is single-threaded, parameter sweeps run processes in parallel).
  3. Option. Engine.image_far_field = "point" keeps the far images in point form: the dense far-field term is left out, the near image pairs (within 7.5 segment lengths, a segment's own images included) stay Galerkin integrals on the series and the cross-layer path alike, and the continuous switch and the transverse distance stay. It is not the result before wave 3: within the upper layer up to 2.3e-4 from it (the blend of D2). The quadrupole form stays the default. The point form moves networks by 3e-6 … 4.3e-4 (16 house grids 0.4 m above a 1000 / 10 Ω·m interface), a straight wire near the interface by 4e-4 and the surface potential above it by up to 0.8 %, and takes 0.49 of the default's time on the 40-house network (0.91 times the solve before wave 3; the network solves on the cross-layer path). A common Engine field next to image_max_terms / image_series_tol rather than a backend option, because solve_mutual_* and FieldResult.potential read it too; any other value raises ValueError (audit W3R2A-02).

Audit W3R2A-01 (round 2): the option first kept, on the cross-layer path, the line form of the interface image only, as before wave 3. The own surface and transmitted images of a segment below the interface were then point sources, so a 75 m strip below a 0.5 m top layer read −1.0e-3 at a segment length of 2.5 m and −58 % at 37.5 m, and a network with a 75 m conductor in two pieces +1.1 % against the default. Every image of the layered correction now keeps its near pairs, and a segment's own images follow the switch of every pair (exact within six segment lengths, blended to 7.5, point beyond — the self pair of the series path): the strip within 1.1e-5 at every segment length, the network within 4e-6. Below thin top layers this costs the near image pairs the option had saved: 1.5 … 2.4 times the solve before wave 3 instead of 1.2 (still 0.51 … 0.94 of the default's time). The auditor's variant (every self image at every distance) and the default's tapered diagonal agree with it to 2e-6 on networks and cost up to 14 % more. 4. Wires within a fraction of a radius of the interface (audit W3R2A-03). The image of a wire within \(a/20\) of the interface blends into the reduced kernel of the direct pair over a tenth of the wire radius (before: over one radius, whose blended distance peaked at \(a/\sqrt 2\) and gave a ring 1.75 mm above a 1000 / 30 Ω·m interface +22 %). Z then moves through \(\pm a\) of the interface with wiggles of at most 0.17 % against its direction (strips and rings in 1000 / 30 and 30 / 1000 Ω·m; before up to 24 %).

docs.title: ADR-0016: A conforming finite-element model in fem
docs.text: Status Accepted — part A (axisymmetric model) and part B (three-dimensional model, user decision Q40 on the shell overlap) 2026-11-15 Date 2026-11-15 Deciders Project maintainers (user decision Q37 of 2026-11-14) Scope groundfield.solver.fem (now a package), the fem entry of the backend registry, FemOptions, the optional fem3d extra

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Up to 2026.11 fem replaced every galvanic cluster by one equivalent hemisphere — the hemisphere with the closed-form resistance of the electrodes in homogeneous soil of the top-layer resistivity — and solved the volume problem of that hemisphere. In homogeneous soil that reproduces Dwight's formula by construction; in layered soil it describes another geometry. Every audit round of the release found new limit cases (an interface 1 cm below a deep ring read +191 … +308 % without a message, a rod reaching 1 µm … 8 cm into a more conductive top layer −44 … −78 % with a warning, a ring lying exactly on an interface −21 … +30 %), and the reduction had grown a dozen structural rules (review pass 10, 10.23; user decision Q23; audits D2A, R2A). User decision Q37 stops adding rules and replaces the reduction by a conforming model; the scope decision of 2026-11-15 adds the full 3-D model to the release (part B, with the overlap of concrete shells at junctions, user decision Q40).

fem stays a reference backend (grey-box principle): the integral engines are the production engines, fem checks them with a method that shares nothing with them but the network solve.

docs.title: 1. Physical model: the electrodes as they are
docs.text:
The quasi-static field \(-\nabla\cdot(\sigma(z)\nabla\varphi) = 0\) in the soil, no current into the air, \(\varphi \to 0\) far away. Every electrode is a perfect conductor at its own potential — a port: a rod is the solid cylinder of its wire_radius with flat end faces, a ring the solid torus of its wire_radius. The port conductance matrix \(G\) (currents leaked for the port potentials, symmetric positive definite) is the earth part of the solve; nothing is reduced or averaged.

A concrete shell (ADR-0012) keeps its meaning: the soil sees the shell surface \(r_b\) (wire_radius) and every metre of wire adds the radial resistance \(C\) = concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m. fem applies it locally, as the surface conductance \(g = 1/(2\pi r_b C)\) between the metal potential and the soil at every point of the electrode surface, so the current may redistribute along the electrode. For a cylindrical shell that is exact (Sunde's decomposition) and needs neither \(\rho_c\) nor \(r_a\), which the electrode does not carry; resolving the concrete as a volume is left to part B, where the overlap at junctions (Q40) needs it.

docs.title: 2. Axisymmetric discretisation (part A)
docs.text:
A world whose electrodes are rods on one vertical axis and horizontal rings centred on it is a body of revolution and reduces to the meridian half-plane \((s, z)\) with the weight \(2\pi s\):

  • Graded tensor mesh. Lines \(s = s_i\) and \(z = z_j\) through every feature — rod surfaces and end faces, layer interfaces, soil surface, axis, truncation box — graded geometrically away from them (\(h(x) = \min_f(h_f + g|x - x_f|)\), \(g = 0.2\)). The rod's end edges are re-entrant corners of the conductor; with a spacing of \(0.002\,a\) there (a few dozen lines more) the convergence stays of second order even for a rod tip lying on an interface. Linear triangles, the weight integrated exactly.
  • O-grid for the ring wire. A square block of up to three wire radii around the wire cross section is filled by an O-grid conforming to the tensor lines on its boundary and inscribed in the circle of the wire (32 nodes at level 0). The block keeps clear of the surface, the axis, the other electrodes and every interface more than \(1.05\,a\) from the wire axis; a nearer interface (a ring on it, or within its radius) is cut into the block's elements, so every element lies in one layer. Such a block is finer: the gap between the wire and the interface, and the narrow wedge where the interface cuts the wire near its edge, make the field vary over \(\sqrt{2a\,|d - a|}\) (\(0.14\,a\) at \(d = 1.01\,a\)). With the default block the levels converged at first order and not monotonically there (up to −6.0e-3 next to a layer 33 times more conductive, the error estimate below the error in 7 of 14 cases, audit W4A-01); refined to 64 intervals the default lay within 3.3e-4 at contrast 33 (stream fw4axi), but beyond it the levels converged at first order again (touching a 1000 times more conductive layer −1.6e-2, estimate 1.1e-2; audit W4R2A-02). A refinement alone does not resolve this: the field is singular where the interface cuts the wire at a narrow angle or touches it, on a scale that shrinks with the contrast. The block's O-grid is graded towards those points in angle and radius (32 intervals, cells of 1e-3 wire radii), which resolves them at fewer nodes: within 5.1e-5 of the boundary elements up to a contrast of 1000, the estimate above the error in all 113 cases of the audit's sweep (evidence e05 of stream fw4r2a).
  • Truncation. A box at r_far_factor (1000) characteristic lengths — the electrodes' size, or the depth of the deepest interface times the layer contrast if larger (a resistive bottom keeps the current in the layers above it over that distance) — carries the Robin condition \(\partial_n\varphi = -(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r/r^2)\varphi\), the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of the monopole far field on any boundary. The graded mesh reaches the box with a few dozen extra lines.
  • Ports. The surface nodes of a bare electrode are one unknown; the port conductance matrix is the Schur complement of the stiffness matrix onto the ports (one sparse LU factorisation for all ports).
  • Refinement and extrapolation. Level \(\ell\) bisects every interval of the level-0 lines \(\ell\) times. The tensor part of the spaces is nested, the O-grid of a ring is not (its layers move with the level, the inscribed polygon grows): one level converges at second order and, in every case tested away from interfaces, from below — observed, not guaranteed (audit W4A-09). The default solves levels 0 and 1 and extrapolates the port conductance matrix with the observed second order (Richardson); the relative difference between the extrapolated and the finer level is reported as metadata["fem_error_estimate"] (about the finer level's error, 0.88 … 0.99 of it in 36 cases of auditor W4A and 0.94 … 1.07 in 60 cases of a ring at an interface, audit W4R2A-02; NaN with extrapolate=False, audit W4A-02).
  • Resource guard. FemOptions.max_nodes (2 million nodes of the finer mesh, about 8 GB: the axisymmetric solve needs about 4 GB per million nodes, 0.82 / 3.15 / 5.15 GB at 0.20 / 0.80 / 1.22 million measured with /usr/bin/time -l, evidence e02 of stream fw4axi; audit W4A-05) against a prediction from the mesh lines before anything is assembled. The prediction counts the O-grid exactly and bounds the cut of an interface, so it errs high (audit W4A-10).

Every other world — electrodes other than rods and rings, a rod or ring off the common axis, galvanic distributed conductors (their leakage runs along their route), touching electrodes, a ring wire that reaches within 5 % of its radius to the soil surface (the solid torus must fit) and a ring without room for its mesh block (within about a wire radius, diagonally, of a rod's end edge; audit W4A-03) — goes to the three-dimensional model of section 5 under the default FemOptions.model = "auto". With model = "axisymmetric" it is refused with BackendCapabilityError, naming the backends that solve it. (Part A alone, before part B, refused every such world.) The common axis has a tolerance of 1e-3 of the smallest wire radius or surface gap between two electrodes (at least 1e-12 of the world's size): the resistance is even in the offset \(\delta\), so the axisymmetric reading is off by \(\kappa(\delta/L)^2\) with \(|\kappa| \le\) 6e-4 for \(L\) the wire radius and \(\le\) 1.1e-2 for \(L\) the gap (image and mom, three worlds), below 1e-6. Up to audit W4A-08 it was 1e-9 of the world's size (3 nm): a rod 1 µm off a ring's axis went to the 3-D model (40.7 s, 2.35 GB, −1.43e-3).

docs.title: 3. Network and results on the shared pipeline
docs.text: The soil model delivers an EarthPorts record (solver/fem/_ports.py): the port conductance matrix, the display segments of the electrodes (the segments the integral backends would use at the engine's segment_length) and the current each of them leaks for 1 V on each port. solver/fem/_network.py runs the pipeline of the integral backends (ADR-0014) with one pseudo-segment per port and \(Z = R = G^{-1}\) as the multi-port matrix: lumped and isolated distributed conductors, inductive branches with their earth-return models, the skin effect, junctions, return_to and voltage sources are honoured as there, at every frequency of the engine. The result carries point sources with the model's leakage distribution, so FieldResult.potential and the touch-voltage helpers work (homogeneous and two-layer soil, as for the other backends). The solve runs the coordinate check of user decision D5.

docs.title: 4. Package layout (the interface for part B)
docs.text:
solver/fem/
  __init__.py       solve_fem (dispatch), public names, module docstring
  _mesh.py          graded lines, tensor grid, O-grid, interface cut (2-D)
  _assembly.py      axisymmetric P1 assembly, far field, shells, port Schur complement
  _axisymmetric.py  world -> coaxial electrodes -> EarthPorts (part A)
  _ports.py         EarthPorts: the interface of any soil model to the network
  _network.py       EarthPorts + world -> FieldResult on the shared pipeline
  _guards.py        refusals shared by every model, the remedy text
  _legacy.py        equivalent_hemisphere_radius (deprecated), FemReductionWarning

Part B adds its 3-D model as further modules (for example _mesh3d.py, _assembly3d.py, _solid.py) whose entry point returns an EarthPorts for any world, and extends the dispatch in solve_fem (axisymmetric where possible, 3-D otherwise); _network.py, _ports.py and _guards.py are shared unchanged.

docs.title: 5. Three-dimensional model (part B)
docs.text:
Every world that the axisymmetric model cannot hold — strips, polylines, stars, meshes and grids, rods and rings side by side, several clusters, galvanic distributed conductors — is solved in three dimensions. FemOptions.model = "auto" (default) keeps the axisymmetric model where it applies (bit for bit) and takes the 3-D model otherwise; "3d" forces it, "axisymmetric" refuses every other world. Modules: _wires3d.py (wires, radius correction), _mesh3d.py (mesh), _assembly3d.py (stiffness, immersed elements, sources, port solve), _solid.py (world → EarthPorts).

  • Electrodes as smoothed line sources with an analytic radius correction. A resolved wire surface (radius 5 mm in a domain of kilometres) cannot be meshed affordably in 3-D, and the brief asked for embedded line sources. Every wire axis (a ring as a polygon of 1° chords) carries the current density \(j(s)\), spread over the disc of radius \(R\) perpendicular to the axis with the bump \(\eta = \frac{3}{\pi R^2}(1 - r^2/R^2)^2\); the wire sees the \(\eta\)-weighted disc average \(\Pi(s)\). What lies inside the disc is added analytically as a radial resistance per length, \(U - \Pi = (C + \Delta C)\,j\), with the shell coefficient \(C\) of ADR-0012 and the correction \(\Delta C\) = the difference between the reduced thin-wire kernel of radius \(a\) and that of the smoothed source (energy radius \(0.5442\,R\)), integrated in closed form over what the mesh does not resolve: the observer's own wire whole (its polyline as far as it has turned by at most 90° along the wire, by a weight falling linearly to 0 at 150°, and every piece on its axis line that belongs to its port or to a wire that meets it — the next piece of a galvanic conductor, the surface image of a rod reaching the surface); of the rest of its electrode (the own polyline beyond, by the rest of the weight), of a wire of another port that meets the observer's wire (their surfaces touch: a rod on a ring, a T-joint, a crossing; one conductor), fading out with the surface gap where two wires have just stopped touching, and of every other surface image only the part within \(1.5\,R\) of the point; any other wire of another port nothing, since it carries its own current (audit W4R2B-03). An exact-parallel test of folded arms switched at a tilt of 1e-6 rad (audit W4R2B-02), a test of the direction within 120° counted a meander's arm whole after a full turn and made a V jump at 120°, a meeting distance of the smaller radius made two crossing strips jump where their surfaces still overlapped, and a collinear rod of another electrode counted whole across an end gap (audits W4R3B-01, -03, -04); the axis distance from the cross product keeps long oblique pieces whole (W4R2B-01). Beyond that the disc average of a smoothed line is its line field (2-D mean-value property of the radial bump), so the mesh is exact there: for two parallel wires the exact correction is below \(10^{-3}\) of the self term from \(1.5\,R\) on (evidence f01 of stream fw4fem3d). The first version counted the surface images and every wire within \(20\,R\), with the observer's current: shallow wires read up to +1.9e-3 high and two rings 10 cm apart +4.6e-3, above their error estimate (audit W4B-01). Far inside a straight wire \(\Delta C\) is Sunde's \(\frac{\rho}{2\pi}\ln(r_\eta/a)\). The result depends little on \(R\) (evidence e07 of stream w4fem3d, re-measured as f05 of stream fw4fem3d: a 3 m rod and a ring at \(R\) = 4, 6 and 10 cm against part A). Default \(R\) = 6 cm. Wires that do not meet but run beside each other (side by side within 30° of parallel, a folded arm, a wire within reach of another over its whole length) are kept at least \(1.5\,R\) apart, two wires end to end in line with a gap at least \(5\,R\): \(R\) becomes their axis distance over 1.5 (end to end: their gap over 5) for the whole world, and below 2.2 radii of the thickest bare wire of the world the solve is refused before meshing (BackendCapabilityError, naming the distance and the integral engines). Wires that meet at 10° or more (junctions, corners, a V or a branch of 10 … 30°) and crossings at more than 30° are left alone; wires that meet at less than 10°, nearly parallel or touching along their length, run beside each other (audits W4R2B-03, W4R2A-01, W4R3B-01, W4R3B-02, and the coordinator's decisions on them; up to then two coaxial rings 7.5 cm apart read +4.35e-3 in a port entry, two rings diagonal to each other, surface gaps 1.3 … 3.8 mm, +11 … +14 %, two stacked rods 1 cm apart +1.6e-2, and a V narrower than 30° was refused). An encased wire meets others by its outer shell radius \(r_b\), what the soil sees: two encased wires of different ports whose shells touch are one conductor in the radius correction, and their separate port entries are not resolved.
  • Isotropic mesh, deterministic bisection. A coarse grid of \(8 \times 8 \times 4\) cubes (six Kuhn tetrahedra each) on the box is refined by conforming longest-edge bisection (own implementation with ties broken by node numbers; scikit-fem's adaptive refinement asserts on some backgrounds) until every element is below \(1.5\,(R/2 + g\max(0, d - R))\), \(d\) the distance from the nearest wire, \(g = 0.5\). A graded tensor grid, the first design, carries the fine lines of the layer interfaces and electrodes to the box as slabs thousands of times wider than thick: the multigrid needed 345 iterations for a 5 m slab and did not converge for a 0.3 m one; the isotropic mesh needs 16 … 115 (up to 115 with immersed layer interfaces).
  • Layer interfaces as partially penalised immersed elements. No interface is a mesh plane (a plane through the isotropic mesh would cut the large far elements into slivers). A tetrahedron that one interface cuts gets the immersed shape functions of Li, Lin & Wu (2003) / Kafafy et al. (2005) — linear on either side, continuous, with continuous normal flux — and the faces the interface crosses get the symmetric consistency and penalty terms of Lin, Lin & Zhang (2015); nodes within 30 % of their shortest edge of a plane (and a quarter of the thinner layer) are moved onto it so no cut leaves a sliver. The scheme reproduces a layered field exactly (to 3e-14; without the face terms −1.6e-4 … −6.4e-4 on the same cube, e01 / e08 of stream w4fem3d). A laminate mean (arithmetic along, harmonic across the layers) is a non-conforming average of first order; it is kept only for elements more than four times larger than the thinner layer they cut (far from the electrodes, where the field varies on scales far above the layer).
  • Solve. The disc averages couple every node of a disc with every other, so the coupling \(A^\mathsf T D A\) is never formed: conjugate gradients on \(K + A^\mathsf T D A\) with the smoothed-aggregation multigrid of \(K\) (pyamg) as preconditioner, one solve per port (\(G\) is quadratic in the solution, so its error is the square of the solver's). A direct sparse factorisation (SuperLU, scipy.sparse.linalg.splu) needed 93 s at 155 000 nodes (COLAMD ordering) and had not finished after 15 minutes at 68 000 nodes with the MMD ordering. pyamg draws the start vectors of its spectral-radius estimates from numpy's global random state; the hierarchy is set up under a fixed seed and the user's state is restored, so results are bit-identical whatever the user's seed and the user's stream is not advanced (audit W4B-07). The iterations grow with the layer contrast (16 … 115 up to the contrast 33 of AP1, 384 … 530 at 100 and 1 225 … 1 264 at 333 for a rod through the interface); at 1 000 they do not converge in 3 000 iterations, and the solve raises BackendCapabilityError naming the contrast, the axisymmetric model where it takes the world, and the integral engines; the tested range is up to about 300 (audit W4B-03; without a layer contrast the refusal names its circumstances instead, audit W4R2B-06). The multigrid of \(K + \operatorname{diag}(A^\mathsf T D A)\) gives the same counts (evidence f02 of stream fw4fem3d).
  • Levels and extrapolation. The finer level is the red refinement of the coarser one (nested); \(G\) is extrapolated with the second order as in part A. The levels are not yet asymptotic for every geometry (error ratios \(r\) = 3.3 … 4.4 for rods and 3.0 … 3.4 for rings), so the extrapolated value carries up to 2e-3. It errs by \(e_1(4 - r)/3\), the reported estimate is \(e_1(r - 1)/3\) (3 … 5e-3): a bound while \(r \ge 2.5\), 2.1 … 4.4 times the error for rings. The same level difference of the transfer entries is reported as metadata["fem_error_estimate_transfer"] (audit W4R2B-05: the estimate covered the diagonal only; where the model holds it is 1.06 … 6.3 times the error of the transfer entries, also for wires end to end at the gap of \(5\,R\) the rule keeps: the error of their transfer entry falls with \(R\) / gap, and factor 3 left 1.15 … 1.18 times the estimate for 8 mm rods 10 … 18 cm apart). This holds away from layer interfaces and other wires — the model keeps wires that run beside each other at least \(1.5\,R\) apart, and two coaxial rings 4.5 … 10 cm apart lie within 1.8e-3 of the solid tori in every port entry. Next to a strongly contrasting interface the thin-wire error applies, which the levels do not see (a ring 1.5 cm above a 1000 / 30 Ω·m interface lies between the exact thin ring and the solid torus, its levels on either side of the torus; audit W4B-02). Resolved concrete converges at first order (\(r \approx 2\)): there the estimate is no bound.
  • Thin wire next to an interface. The smoothed line source shares the thin-wire limit of the integral engines next to a contrasting interface (+9.2e-3 against the solid torus for a ring 3 radii above a 1000 / 30 Ω·m interface, beyond its estimate; evidence f10 of stream fw4fem3d, audit W4B-02). The dispatch therefore emits InterfaceContactWarning for a horizontal wire within the reach of an interface (3.9 radii at a contrast of 33, audit W4R2A-04; the table of the reach is in the warnings reference) before the 3-D model runs, as the integral engines do (audit W4A-07); the axisymmetric model resolves the wire and does not warn. The 3-D model's own guard refuses bare wires closer than about 2.8 radii (the disc of the source must lie in one layer).
  • Ports and network. Every electrode is one port, every leaking piece of a galvanic distributed conductor one more; _network.solve_network takes the pipeline's topology of those pieces, the rest is section 3.
  • Concrete (user decision Q40). By default each encased wire carries its shell coefficient \(C\) (the model of the image family and mom). With FemOptions.concrete_resistivity = \(\rho_c\) the concrete is resolved: a square prism of conformal radius \(r_b\) (side \(r_b/0.59017\)) around every straight axis-aligned encased wire, the metal radius following from \(C = \frac{\rho_c}{2\pi}\ln(r_b/r_a)\), the prism faces as immersed interfaces, so overlapping shells at corners, T-joints and crossings share their concrete. The square keeps the resistance to the soil, but in the shell-dominated limit its concrete is 3.8 % less resistive than the circular shell: the concrete is set by the square's inner conformal radius, \(0.914\,r_b\) (audit W4B-04; one side cannot match both radii, so the prism is not resized). Together with the first order of the prism faces and edges the resolved concrete reads the conductance per metre 2.8 … 4.6 % high at the default levels, so it measures differences on one mesh. Against the per-wire shells a junction acts like a few cm of wire, at most about \(2\,r_b\), sign not settled — the junction numbers are not converged (one refinement of the prism faces moved the corner by about 5 cm; evidence e09, e11 of stream w4fem3d, audit W4B-05) — and the house mesh of the generators changes by about 1 % or less (0.35 … 0.85 % with every sign aligned after the fix of W4B-01, evidence f12 of stream fw4fem3d). The per-wire shells keep their place as the default (no correction rule). A cover so thin that the smoothed source the prism allows does not reach beyond the metal (energy radius at most 1.2 metal radii: a 5 mm bar with 5 mm cover) is refused before meshing, naming concrete_resistivity=None (audit W4R2B-04; up to then a bare ValueError after meshing).
  • Resource guard. Before anything is meshed: the display segments against Engine.max_segments, the number of ports against FemOptions.max_ports_3d (default 100; every port is one conjugate-gradient solve per level, 0.93 … 0.96 s per port and level at 583 000 nodes, auditor W4B and evidence f14 of stream fw4fem3d; audit W4B-08) and FemOptions.max_nodes_3d (2 million nodes of the finer mesh; the solve adds about 2.9 GB per million, evidence f15) against a prediction; the exact count again before the finer level. metadata["fem_peak_memory_gb"] is what the solve added to the peak resident memory of the process, fem_process_peak_memory_gb that peak (audit W4B-09).
  • Face pairing. The immersed elements' face terms pair the faces by their sorted node triples (numpy.lexsort); a packed integer key aliased above \(2^{21}\) nodes (audit W4B-06).
  • Dependencies (decision D6). scikit-fem (BSD-3: the Kuhn background MeshTet.init_tensor, the red refinement) and pyamg (MIT), as the optional fem3d extra; import groundfield imports neither. Without the extra a world that needs the 3-D model raises ImportError naming the extra. No GPL or LGPL mesher (gmsh, TetGen, CGAL, netgen) is used: the design needs no resolved surface, so nothing beyond permissive packages was required.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Every fem number changes (both stored golden cases by −4.6 %; the benchmark tables of the fem page). fem agrees with independent references to about 1e-4 (within 5.1e-5 for a ring wire within 1.05 radii of an interface, up to a contrast of 1000) at a cost of a second per solve (fem page).
  • fem solves every world again: the axisymmetric model where it applies (about 1e-4), the 3-D model otherwise (with the optional fem3d extra; about 2e-3 away from layer interfaces, wires that run beside each other kept at least \(1.5\,R\) apart, which refines the mesh or refuses the closest pairs); without the extra the 3-D worlds raise ImportError.
  • fem gains concrete shells, junctions, two-terminal and voltage sources and every conductor model (registry capabilities).
  • FemOptions changes: refinement, extrapolate, r_far_factor (default 1000), far_field, max_nodes; for the 3-D model model, source_radius, growth, concrete_resistivity, max_nodes_3d, max_ports_3d. The 2026.11 fields n_radial, n_axial, z_far_factor are gone; as keyword arguments of solve_fem (0.15.0) they warn and have no effect. equivalent_hemisphere_radius is deprecated; FemReductionWarning is kept and never emitted.
  • The 3-D model shares the thin-wire assumption of the integral engines (uniform current around the wire, no end faces); it is independent of them in everything else (the layering, the surface, the far field, the current distribution along the wires). Its accuracy (about 2e-3 away from interfaces and other wires, the wires beside each other at least \(1.5\,R\) apart, levels not yet asymptotic for every geometry; next to a strongly contrasting interface the thin-wire error of the integral engines) is a reference for the integral engines' biases of 0.4 … 3 %, not for effects below 1e-3; differences of two concrete models on the same mesh (Q40) are finer than that.
  • No stored number changes with part B: the golden fem cases are axisymmetric and stay on part A bit for bit.
  • fem stays experimental until the audits of the release have passed.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Thin-wire line sources in the mesh with a radius correction (Peaceman-type well index). Cheaper meshes, but the correction depends on the mesh, and the end faces and the contact with an interface — the configurations where the reduction failed — are exactly what a line source cannot represent. A resolved surface costs only logarithmically many lines on a graded mesh.
  • Extending the spherical-shell mesh of the reduction. It conforms to a hemisphere, not to rods and rings.
  • An unstructured mesher. Not needed in 2-D; in 3-D the smoothed-source formulation needs no surface-fitted mesh, and the bisection mesh of section 5 is built with scikit-fem's tensor grid and an own refinement (decision D6: no GPL / LGPL mesher).
  • 3-D alternatives tried and dropped (stream w4fem3d). A graded tensor grid (slab anisotropy, multigrid stalls); quadratic elements on the bisection mesh (the multigrid did not converge in 500 iterations); laminate interfaces (first order); a mesh cut along the interface planes (slivers where thin layers cross the far elements); plain immersed elements without face terms (not consistent: −1.6e-4 … −6.4e-4 on a layered cube that the penalised form reproduces exactly); a fixed source quadrature coarser than the finer mesh (the finite elements resolve the individual points: the rod's level 2 overshot by +0.6 %); forming \(K + A^\mathsf T D A\) for the multigrid (3.4 GB instead of 1.8 GB at 600 000 nodes). Singularity subtraction with the analytic segment potential (Gjerde et al. 2019) would make the method a moment method with a finite-element correction in homogeneous soil.
  • Resolving the concrete as a volume. Needs the concrete resistivity and the metal radius, which the electrode does not carry; for a cylindrical shell it is equivalent to the surface conductance.
  • Infinite elements or a mapped layer at the truncation. The monopole Robin condition on a box a thousand electrode lengths away moves the result by less than 1e-5 and needs no special elements.

docs.title: Audit history
docs.text:
groundfield is a reference model: its numbers feed a catalogue of real low-voltage networks, rho-f models for groundinsight and touch-voltage assessments. A number that changes therefore needs a recorded reason. Since May 2026 the code has been reviewed in ten numbered review passes and one physics and numerics audit. Each pass produced findings, each fix a regression test, and the releases below shipped them.

Up to 0.15.0 the full narrative of every pass stood in the changelog. Since 2026.11.0 the changelog holds concise release notes, and the narratives are kept here, verbatim, one page per pass.

Pass Date Reviewed Fixes released in Finding identifiers Pass 1 2026-05-10 development state between 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 not labelled (backlog) none Pass 2 2026-05-10 not stated not labelled (backlog) none Pass 3 2026-05-12 not stated not labelled (backlog) none Pass 4 2026-05-12 not stated 0.5.0 none Pass 5 2026-05-13 not stated 0.5.0 none Pass 6 2026-05-14 0.5.0 0.6.0 (one fix) none Pass 7 2026-05-18 three days after 0.6.0 0.7.0 none Pass 8 2026-05-25 ten days after 0.6.0 recorded in the 0.7.0 notes none Audit of 2026-07-08 2026-07-08 0.10.0 0.11.0 work packages WP-A to WP-F Pass 9 2026-07-28 0.14.0 0.14.1 and 0.15.0 F01–F57 Pass 10 2026-11-07 0.15.0 2026.11.0 10.01–10.95

docs.title: Reading the pages
docs.text:
• A page reproduces what was written at the time. File paths, test modules, notebook numbers and API names refer to the code of that time; later releases renamed or removed some of them (see the changelog).
  • Passes 1 to 8 recorded their findings as a backlog of work to do. Not every backlog entry was implemented, and later passes re-listed what was still open, so the same finding can appear on several pages.
  • Where a later pass found a published statement to be wrong, the page carries a correction box above the original text; the text itself is not changed. Pass 9 has such a box (the corrections of finding 10.82), and so has the pass-10 page for statements of the work-stream fragments that later audits found wrong.
  • Roadmap candidates of a pass are ideas, not commitments; the current plan is on the roadmap.

docs.title: Finding identifiers
docs.text:
• Passes 1 to 8 name findings by their subject only.
  • The audit of 2026-07-08 groups its fixes into work packages WP-A to WP-F and quotes the audit's own finding labels (such as P4 and P5) in passing.
  • Pass 9 numbers its findings F01 to F57.
  • Pass 10 numbers its findings 10.01 to 10.95 and keeps the pass-9 number where a finding was already known (for example F01/F30 with 10.16).
  • The adversarial audits of the release preparation of 2026.11.0 number their findings per audit and round (for example A2G-04, D3A-02, R6A-01, W1A-02, W3R2B-08); the pass-10 page records them with the streams that fixed them.
  • From 2026.11.0 on, regression tests carry the marker @pytest.mark.finding("10.NN"); pytest --finding 10.28 runs the tests of one finding.
