docs.title: Findings, published in the 0.7.0 release notes
Fixed (Backlog — seventh 2026-05-18 review pass)
docs.text:
The seventh audit pass was run on 2026-05-18, three days after the 0.6.0 release (geo subpackage + concrete-encasement model). The entries below capture new findings that emerged either as a side-effect of the 0.6.0 surface (World.concrete_shell_corrections registry, OsmBuildingPlacement.footprint_at, geo.osm retry contract) or that have still not been addressed through six previous audit passes (missing API pages, ADR cross-references). Only the CHANGELOG is edited in this pass; no program code is touched.

  • docs/api/sources.md, boundary.md, references.md, validation.md, world.md still missing — seventh pass in a row. The 0.6.0 release added docs/api/geo.md for the new OSM subpackage but did not address the five long-standing missing pages flagged in pass 1 through pass 6. groundfield.world.World, groundfield.solver.sources, groundfield.solver.boundary and groundfield.validation are all part of the public __all__ of src/groundfield/__init__.py (confirmed on 2026-05-18) and the user has no rendered API documentation for any of them. The six-pass-in-a-row finding is therefore re-elevated; without a forcing CI gate it will reappear in the eighth pass.
  • docs/api/index.md does not list the new Geo / OSM page. The rendered API-reference index enumerates Soil, Geometry, Conductors, Solver, Coupling, Postprocess, Diagnostics, IO and Generators but is missing the Geo / OSM entry that the 0.6.0 mkdocs.yml nav added (api/geo.md). Drift between API overview prose and the rendered nav appeared on the same release that landed the subpackage — straightforward bullet-list addition.
  • World.concrete_shell_corrections registry has no documented cleanup contract. Re-using a single World across multiple TnNetworkGenerator.build calls (the canonical parameter-sweep pattern) accumulates entries from previous builds in the same dict; the 0.6.0 release records the registry as a public dict[str, float] but offers neither a world.reset_concrete_corrections() helper nor a per-build invalidation hook on the generator side. AP1 Monte-Carlo studies that flip concrete_rho_ohm_m per realisation will carry stale shell resistances from earlier samples into later ones unless the user knows to clear the dict by hand.
  • OsmBuildingPlacement.footprint_at(i) lacks defensive bounds checking. The current implementation indexes self.footprints[i] directly; for i out of range CPython raises a bare IndexError whose message does not name the placement, the requested index, or the available range. Wrap with an explicit raise IndexError(f"OsmBuildingPlacement: requested index {i} but only {n} footprints are available; check placement.n_buildings.") so the AP1 generator pipeline produces a self-describing failure instead of an opaque traceback at TnNetworkGenerator.build time.
  • geo.osm.query_buildings retry count is hardcoded as 1. The docstring promises "one retry on 429 / 504 with exponential backoff" but no parameter is exposed for users working over flaky cellular / VPN links. Promote the retry count to a max_retries: int = 1 keyword on query_buildings / query_and_project; the default preserves current behaviour.
  • groundfield.io.groundinsight.evaluate_spec ValueError class is not re-exported. Pass-5 widened evaluate_spec to raise ValueError on non-canonical free symbols (and the Pass-5 Fixed block lists this as a public-surface improvement), but downstream code that wants to catch the new exception has no named class — it has to compare against str(exc) substrings or fall back to the broad ValueError parent. Define an EvaluateSpecError(ValueError) subclass in groundfield.io.groundinsight and add it to the module __all__; follow-on groundinsight consumers will benefit from the typed surface.
  • Conductor.lumped_series_resistance_ohm and StripElectrode.concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m are not JSON-round-tripped in tests/test_concrete_encasement.py. The new test file covers the V2 Sunde-shell closed-form match, the V1 registry, the discriminator and the end-to-end OSM smoke, but does not assert that a World with a populated Conductor.lumped_series_resistance_ohm or StripElectrode.concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m survives World.model_dump_json() → World.model_validate_json(...). Add a single test case so the persistence contract is locked in before users start sharing concrete-encasement-bearing world files across runs.
  • ADR cross-references are one-directional. ADR-0011 (OSM building footprints) references ADR-0009 (World generators) and ADR-0012 (Concrete encasement) references ADR-0003 (Distributed conductor) — but the target ADRs carry no reciprocal "See also" link. A maintainer reading ADR-0003 today sees no breadcrumb to the V1 lumped path that reuses its framework; same for ADR-0009 → ADR-0011. Bidirectional ADR linking is a one-line edit per file and prevents future architectural drift.
  • docs/concepts.md is silent on the lumped vs. distributed Sunde-shell trade-off. The 0.6.0 release added two implementation variants (concrete_model="lumped" vs. "distributed") with materially different physics (V1 records the total shell resistance and injects a series resistance on the PEN drop; V2 augments the post-kernel diagonal per segment). The user-facing concepts.md page describes neither variant nor the regime where each is preferred. AP1 readers reach the ADR-0012 file as a fallback, but the canonical "Concepts" page should carry a short decision-guide table.
  • README.md does not mention 0.6.0 features. The README Roadmap and Features sections were not updated alongside the 0.6.0 release — neither the geo extra, the BuildingFootprint / OsmBuildingPlacement exports nor the concrete-encasement model appear in the project description. AP1 reviewers landing on the GitHub page have no signal that the OSM and concrete-encasement features exist.
  • Notebooks 30..33 are not wired into the docs nav. All four audit / OSM / concrete-encasement notebooks exist on disk and are referenced in the 0.6.0 CHANGELOG "Docs" block, but mkdocs.yml only loads docs/examples/*.md. The mkdocs-jupyter plugin is enabled (plugins: mkdocs-jupyter block, execute: false), so adding a Notebooks: nav section under Examples is a four-line edit. Without it the notebook walkthroughs that the 0.6.0 changelog calls out are invisible to docs-site readers.

docs.text:

A short "Migrating from 0.5.x" section under the index — listing the new optional geo extra, the additive concrete_rho_ohm_m field on FoundationElectrodeSpec, and the no-op default — would spare users a CHANGELOG dive on upgrade. A short "Optional: OSM-driven footprints" appendix would close the gap.
  • docs/performance.md has no geo cost section. The on-disk Overpass cache, the projection cost and the OMBR reduction are all new performance-relevant code paths in 0.6.0. AP1 readers running long Monte-Carlo sweeps over 10–100 buildings need an order-of-magnitude estimate (current local: ~ms per footprint, network: ~hundreds of ms on cold cache) and an explicit pointer at the cache directory to clear between experiments.
  • docs/api/geo.md lacks the offline-fallback contract. The 0.6.0 page describes the live Overpass path and the cache layer but does not state the contract of the purely offline variant — the path through BuildingFootprint + manual centroid placement that does not import requests / pyproj / shapely. A "Working offline" subsection that enumerates the no-dependency code path keeps the AP1 reproducible- computation guarantee visible.

docs.text:

Sixth-pass carried this; seventh pass re-emphasises the cross-repo contract: dict[str, str] with keys package, python, numpy, scipy, sympy, pydantic, polars, shapely, pyproj, requests (the last three reflect the new geo extra) plus _meta = {timestamp, platform}.

Companion to the proposed mkdocs build --strict CI gate. Six passes have flagged the missing-API-pages problem and seven passes the forcing-function lack; this is now the highest-leverage cross-repo roadmap item.
  • gf.World.reset_concrete_corrections() — public helper matching the ADR-0012 V1 registry. Default behaviour stays additive; the helper is opt-in for parameter sweeps. Tie to the Fixed-backlog entry above.
  • gf.geo.OverpassCache(path, max_age_s=...) — promote the current hidden $XDG_CACHE_HOME/groundfield/osm/ directory to a configurable cache object. Users running CI builds want per-job cache control; AP1 Monte-Carlo runs want to pin the cache for reproducibility.
  • ADR-0013 — Cross-repo show_versions convention. Bundle the three-repo show_versions proposal into a single ADR that lives in groundfield and is linked from groundinsight / groundmeas. Five passes have proposed show_versions; the ADR is the forcing function that pins the return shape before any of the three packages ships its own implementation.

docs.title: Added (Audit pass 7 — implemented 2026-05-18)
docs.text:
• groundfield.io.groundinsight.EvaluateSpecError — new typed exception (subclass of ValueError) raised by evaluate_spec on malformed spec input. The class is re-exported at the top level as groundfield.EvaluateSpecError and listed in groundfield.__all__. Legacy except ValueError blocks keep working unchanged because the new class inherits from ValueError; downstream groundinsight consumers can now catch the typed exception without grepping str(exc) (closes the seventh 2026-05-18 audit pass "no named class for evaluate_spec failures" bullet).
  • groundfield.World.reset_concrete_corrections() — explicit cleanup helper for the ADR-0012 V1 concrete-shell registry (world.py). Re-using a single World across multiple TnNetworkGenerator.build calls — the canonical AP1 Monte-Carlo pattern over concrete_rho_ohm_m — previously accumulated stale entries in the public World.concrete_shell_corrections dict. The new method clears the registry and returns a shallow copy of the dropped entries, so callers can inspect or log them. Calling on a fresh world is an idempotent no-op. Closes the seventh 2026-05-18 audit pass "registry has no documented cleanup contract" bullet.
  • OsmBuildingPlacement.footprint_at(i, strict=...) — opt-in defensive bounds check (geo/placement.py). Default strict=False preserves the v0.6.0 "out-of-range → None" contract that TnNetworkGenerator.build relies on; strict=True raises a self-describing IndexError that names the placement, the requested index, the filtered footprint count (after min_area_m2) and the raw list length. The placement also exposes a new OsmBuildingPlacement.n_footprints property identical to len(placement) so consumers can pre-flight i without invoking the dunder. Closes the seventh 2026-05-18 audit pass "footprint_at lacks defensive bounds checking" bullet.
  • groundfield.geo.osm.query_buildings(..., max_retries=N) and query_and_project(..., max_retries=N) — promote the previously hard-coded 1 retry to a keyword (geo/osm.py). Defaults to 1, matching the historic v0.6.0 contract; users on flaky cellular / VPN links can raise it, CI pipelines that prefer fail-fast semantics can set 0. max_retries < 0 is rejected at the API boundary with a clear ValueError. The module docstring and the _post_overpass internal docstring are updated to match. Closes the seventh 2026-05-18 audit pass "retry count hardcoded as 1" bullet.

docs.title: Findings, published in the 0.7.0 release notes
Fixed (Backlog — eighth 2026-05-25 review pass)
docs.text:
The eighth audit pass was run on 2026-05-25, ten days after the 0.6.0 release (geo subpackage + concrete-encasement model) and seven days after the seventh CHANGELOG-only audit pass. The seventh-pass code fixes (EvaluateSpecError, World.reset_concrete_corrections, OsmBuildingPlacement.footprint_at bounds-check, query_buildings max_retries keyword) landed in commit 4c27695 on feature/audit-pass7-fixes together with the new OrtsnetzLayout + Manhattan PEN router + radial-trunk PEN topology in 60a9cf5. The bullets below capture both the still-unmerged release-train risk and a new Pass-8 wave of behavioural / docs gaps. Only the CHANGELOG is edited in this pass; no program code is touched.

  • feature/audit-pass7-fixes carries two commits plus a large unstaged delta — release cut blocked. The branch holds the seventh-pass code fixes (4c27695) and the AP1-feature commit (60a9cf5 — OrtsnetzLayout, manhattan_routing, pen_topology), plus twenty-six modified files in the working tree (audit-label cleanup in inline comments, AP1-reference removal in module docstrings, the new escape_radius_m keyword on route_manhattan and OrtsnetzLayout.add_pen_cable, CITATION.cff edits). Three CHANGELOG Added-blocks dated 2026-05-18 (escape-radius safety valve, OrtsnetzLayout GPS layer, Manhattan router + Ortsnetz builder + radial-trunk topology) are also unstaged. The 0.7.0 / 0.6.1 release cannot be tagged until the working tree is split into a chore(audit-cleanup) commit (audit-label / AP1-reference scrub) and a feat(routing) commit (escape-radius valve + diagnostic error). Eighth-pass forcing function: open the release PR before the next audit pass or the backlog ledger keeps growing past the implementation.

The working-tree diff against 60a9cf5 strips the parenthetical „(fifth 2026-05-13 audit pass)" / „(sixth 2026-05-14 audit pass)" / „(seventh 2026-05-18 audit pass)" breadcrumbs from src/groundfield/coupling/sommerfeld_inductance.py, diagnostics.py, generators/electrode_specs.py, generators/ortsnetz_builder.py, generators/tn_network.py, geo/osm.py, geo/placement.py, io/csv.py, io/groundinsight.py, postprocess/vector_fitting.py, solver/engine.py and world.py. The implementation in src/groundfield/generators/manhattan_routing.py validates if escape_radius_m < 0.0: and raises ValueError, but the three new regression tests in tests/test_ortsnetz_builder.py (running total 31) only cover positive defaults, 0.0 strict mode and 6.0 rescue mode. docs.title: Review pass 9 (2026-07-28)
docs.text:
Date 2026-07-28 Reviewed 0.14.0 (commit 428442d) Findings F01–F57 Released in 0.14.1 (2026-07-30: F03, F12, F19) and 0.15.0 (2026-07-31: the rest); F01, F02 and F32 stayed open until 2026.11.0 Overview Audit history · Changelog

The ninth review pass ran eight parallel subsystem reviewers and an independent adversarial verification stage. Its findings are referenced by their pass-9 identifiers F01–F57.

Where this text comes from

This page was moved verbatim from CHANGELOG.md when the release notes were condensed in 2026.11.0 (source: commit 30a122d). Only the markup was adapted: reST roles are rendered as code or math, relative links point to the current pages, trailing whitespace is removed, and each block stands under a heading that names where it was published. Paths, test names and numbers are those of the time; the code has changed since.

Corrections (review pass 10, finding 10.82)

Some statements below were found to be wrong in review pass 10. The text is kept as it was published; the corrections are listed in the release notes of 2026.11.0 under Corrections to the 0.15.0 release notes:

  • F47, F48 (ManhattanGridPlacement.jitter_m, MeasurementLeadConfig.depth_m) and F53, F54 (check_segment_resolution for polyline and star electrodes) are listed as fixed, but generators/placement.py and generators/measurement.py were unchanged since 0.14.1 and diagnostics.py since 0.13.0. They were fixed in 2026.11.0 (F47 and F48 as part of 10.55).
  • cim “bit-identical” to image_2layer was false for electrodes with unequal segment lengths: +4.1 % for a 3 m rod in TwoLayerSoil(100, 400, h_1=2) split unevenly at the interface (segment length 0.4 m: 71.060 Ω against 68.262 Ω). Fixed in 2026.11.0 (10.30).
  • F16 describes the symptom of F08: the layout builder (OrtsnetzLayout.to_world) still ignored the concrete shell; the 0.15.0 fix covered TnNetworkGenerator only. Fixed in 2026.11.0 (10.14).
  • F17 (documentation of backends that raise for three or more layers) was fixed only in part: the engine-comparison example still recommended image_nlayer or cim for more than two layers. The documentation was rewritten in 2026.11.0.

docs.title: Fixed (Review pass 9 — implemented 2026-07-28)
docs.text:
The ninth review pass was run on 2026-07-28 against 0.14.0 (commit 428442d) with eight parallel subsystem reviewers and an independent adversarial verification stage. Findings are referenced below by their pass-9 identifier (F01–F57). This release deliberately carries only the three findings that are either data-corrupting or hard crashes, so that a groundfield version number is enough to decide whether a stored groundinsight BusType is affected. The remaining findings ship in 0.15.0.

  • ⚠ fit_to_sympy lost the sign of the residue's imaginary part — the exported groundinsight formula did not match the fit it exports (postprocess/vector_fitting.py, finding F03). When combining a complex-conjugate pole/residue pair into the real second-order term \(r/(s-p) + r^{*}/(s-p^{*}) = [2\,\Re(r)\,(s-\Re(p)) - 2\,\Im(r)\,\Im(p)] / [(s-\Re(p))^2 + \Im(p)^2]\), the canonical residue is by construction the one sitting at the pole with \(\Im(p) > 0\). The previous symmetrisation used 0.5 * (abs(r.imag) + abs(r2.imag)), which forces \(\Im(r) \ge 0\); the following if p.imag < 0 correction flips on the sign of the pole, not of the residue. Whenever the canonical residue carried \(\Im(r) < 0\) — which vector fitting produces routinely for lossy earth-return driving-point impedances — the \(-2\,\Im(r)\,\Im(p)\) numerator term entered with the wrong sign and the exported BusType.impedance_formula was a different rational function from VectorFitResult. Measured on a \(Z_0\coth(\gamma\ell)\) line fit (\(R = 0.3\), \(L = 1\) mH, \(G = 1\) nS, \(C = 10\) nF, \(\ell = 5\) km, 6 poles): 28.1 % magnitude error at 16.7 Hz, 13.1 % at 50 Hz, and a sign difference in \(\Re(Z)\) at 500 Hz. The fix selects the residue belonging to the positive-imaginary pole and symmetrises as \(\tfrac12(\Im(r_+) - \Im(r_-))\), which preserves the sign while keeping the existing exact-conjugate symmetrisation intent.

Numerical results change. Any BusType exported through to_bustype_dict / save_bustype_json / to_bustype from a fit with at least one negative-imaginary canonical residue is affected and should be re-exported. VectorFitResult itself, fit.evaluate(), and every solver result were always correct — the defect was confined to the SymPy rendering step, so re-running fit_to_sympy on the stored fit is sufficient; the field computation does not need repeating.

  • plot_potential_contour raised AttributeError on every supported NumPy when extent was omitted (postprocess/plotting.py, finding F12). The automatic-extent branch called the ndarray.ptp() method, removed in NumPy 2.0, while pyproject.toml requires numpy = "^2.1.0" — so the documented default call, including the one in Quickstart, was dead. Now uses the free function np.ptp(...). A repo-wide sweep for the other NumPy-2.0 removals (itemset, newbyteorder, np.float_, np.complex_, np.NaN, np.Inf, np.alltrue, np.product) found no further occurrence.

  • Engine.with_frequencies() bypassed all frequency validation on its default path (solver/engine.py, finding F19). The preserve_order=False branch returned self.model_copy(update={"frequencies": freqs}), and model_copy(update=...) runs no validators under pydantic v2 — contradicting the method's own docstring ("the standard _validate_frequencies checks run"). An empty list, a negative frequency, NaN and infinity were all silently accepted, and the EngineFrequencyOrderWarning for a non-monotonic list never fired. Both paths now go through model_validate; the order warning is re-emitted at the caller's frame so the notebook line that built the engine is the one reported. The scalar checks moved into a shared _check_frequency_values helper so the constructor and the convenience constructor reject the same inputs with the same messages, and infinity is now rejected explicitly (previously it fell through the f >= 0.0 guard). DC (f == 0.0) remains a legitimate quasi-static operating point.

New tests/test_audit_pass9_fixes.py (14 tests): the residue-sign export for both signs and across a frequency sweep, the full to_bustype_dict → BusTypeSpec → evaluate_spec round trip against the analytic pair sum, plot_potential_contour without extent in both planes, and the five with_frequencies rejection cases plus the order-warning and preserve_order controls. Eleven of the fourteen fail on 428442d; the other three are controls over behaviour that was already correct.

It passed a non-existent fixed=0.0 keyword (the parameter is y for plane="xz" and z for plane="xy") and advertised a plane="yz" option the function does not implement. The surrounding prose now states the plane/fixed-coordinate pairing and the extent=None behaviour.

docs.title: Review pass 9 — the remaining findings
docs.text:
This block closes the rest of the ninth review pass (2026-07-28 against 0.14.0); 0.14.1 shipped only F03, F12 and F19. It is a minor, not a patch, because several findings could not be closed honestly without also taking their behaviour-changing twin: F06 needs F05, F10 needs F11, F26 needs F29, and F39 needs F34. Findings are referenced by their pass-9 identifier.

Read this before regenerating anything. Entries marked ⚠ change numerical results. In descending order of blast radius: every fem number moves; every layered mom_sommerfeld number moves; coupling.layered_green moves for surface, interface, near-interface and cross-layer pairs and for radii beyond ~160 m; the image family moves for electrodes with unequal segment lengths (uniform-segment geometries are unchanged to floating-point rounding — 1 ulp on 4 of 11 test worlds, because a BLAS dot replaces np.mean); references.pollaczek and two references.dwight1936 formulas move; and rho_f_standard fits move wherever a sweep contained dead frequencies.

Still open after this release: F01 (the simulated fall-of-potential measurement is a null experiment — Source.return_to is inert), F02 (the ADR-0007 cross-layer current-sharing ansatz, up to +581 %) and F32 (carson_series on the wrong image baseline, 1.65×–2.17× too much earth-return reactance). All three change what a study means rather than what it computes and are staged separately. The deferred half of F26/F29 — the exact image-line diagonal — is quantified under Documentation below.

docs.title: Fixed — the numerical core
docs.text:
• ⚠ mom_sommerfeld: the reference engine no longer truncates a conditionally convergent integral (F04, F40). The top-layer kernel was evaluated with a bare scipy.integrate.quad on a finite [0, lam_max]. The direct term \(e^{-\lambda|z-z_s|}J_0(\lambda s)\) does not decay for two segments at equal depth, so the integral converges only through the Bessel oscillation and the cut left a sign-alternating error no tolerance could reduce: sommerfeld_kernel_value returned −0.012551 where the exact value is +0.039990, and a 25 m ring in TwoLayerSoil(100, 100, h_1=1) came out at 1.4952 Ω instead of 1.5751 Ω. The kernel is now split with Lipschitz' integral \(\int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda d}J_0(\lambda s)\,d\lambda = 1/\sqrt{s^2+d^2}\) — the direct pair and the leading interface reflection are closed-form, and only the exponentially decaying remainder is quadratured. lambda_max now follows that remainder's decay length instead of ignoring \(|z-z_s|\) (two segments 2 cm apart at 3 m depth previously lost 44.8 % of their reaction-matrix entry, and the error grew under refinement). Against the analytic Tagg/Sunde series the kernel is now accurate to ~3e-15 for \(s \le 50\) m; the engine is also 150–8000× faster (32-segment ring: 162 s → 0.02 s).
  • ⚠ mom_sommerfeld: unresolved oscillation no longer returns a negative Green's function, and non-convergence is no longer silent. The panel budget truncated the panel count, so the resolved λ-range shrank with the refinement factor while the loop returns its last rung — refining made the answer worse. For a centimetre-scale intermediate layer at kilometre separation the kernel returned −9.4749e-05 where the far-field asymptote requires +5.000e-04, with zero Python-level warnings. The budget is now spent coverage-first, and exhausting the ladder raises the new SommerfeldConvergenceWarning, naming the achieved versus requested tolerance, the offending geometry, that the sign may be wrong, and which parameter to raise. Verified silent across 1260 in-envelope parameter sets. A geometric panel family additionally resolves the multiple-reflection pole \((1-\Gamma_1(0))/2h_1\), which the graded grid missed entirely at extreme contrast (ρ₂/ρ₁ = 10⁸: −5.2e-2 → −2.8e-11).
  • ⚠ coupling.layered_green: the λ-truncation is now guaranteed instead of assumed (F14). lambda_max was sized from lambda_max_factor / min(h_1, s + z + z_s), which bears no relation to the decay length \(d_\text{img}\) of the reflected remainder. Every image distance can degenerate, and the kernel was then wrong with no warning: −2.7e-2 for a pair at the air/soil surface, +4.1 % at the layer interface, and −39.5 % for a pair half a millimetre below it — the last one growing as the mesh is refined towards \(h_1\), which destroyed mesh convergence for exactly the cross-layer rods ADR-0007 exists for. Cross-layer pairs straddling the interface had the same defect. The reflected kernel is now written as its exact image superposition; every term with \(\lambda_\text{max}d_j < 30\) is subtracted from the integrand and added back through its exact Hankel inverse \(c_j/(2\sqrt{s^2+d_j^2})\), so the discarded tail is bounded by \(e^{-30}\) by construction. All of those geometries, and radii from 0 to 20 km, now agree with an independently derived closed form to ~3e-10 — and the result is identical to ten digits for lambda_max_factor anywhere in 30 … 30 000.
  • ⚠ coupling.layered_green: the 48-node interpolation and its 64-pair discontinuity (F15). The group interpolation was 2–3 orders less accurate than documented and stepped by ~3 % at the pair-count threshold where the strategy switches — a discontinuity in problem size, which is indefensible in a reference solver. Residual step is now 3.4e-5, and the interpolated-versus-exact agreement ~1e-6 (worst 1.1e-5).
  • ⚠ image / image_2layer: reported potentials are the length-weighted (Galerkin) average the solver actually enforces (F10, F11). 0.11.0 (WP-B3) moved the multiport matrix to a length-weighted reduction but left the result-assembly path on a plain np.mean, so grounding_impedance() disagreed with the impedance the solver had constrained by −10.9 % on a rod split at a layer interface, and cluster_impedance read members[0] — the alphabetically first name — so renaming an electrode changed the reported impedance (19.4393 → 19.2314 Ω on identical geometry). grounding_impedance(e) now equals the diagonal \(Z_{ii}\) to ≤2 ulp, all members of one galvanic cluster report equal potentials to 2e-16 (was 3.1e-3), and the reported value is name-independent. Mixed-length geometries move by up to +12 %; uniform-segment geometries are unchanged to rounding.
  • ⚠ fem: the axial mesh no longer degrades with the declared layer thickness (F05, F06). _build_axisymmetric_mesh sized the domain from a_eq + sum(h_layers) and then filled the axial direction with a fixed 40 linearly spaced nodes, so near-electrode resolution collapsed in proportion to a parameter that must have no effect. A physically homogeneous soil declared as TwoLayerSoil(100, 100, h_1=X) returned 40.36 / 34.94 / 23.69 / 15.66 / 7.51 Ω for X = 1/2/5/10/30 m against an exact 64.62 Ω — up to −79 %, monotone in X. The mesh is now a geometrically graded spherical shell; the same sweep is flat within −0.24 … −0.84 %.
  • ⚠ fem: the Dirichlet electrode is now genuinely conforming (F24). It was a staircase flat disc, so the discrete electrode did not converge to the intended hemisphere: refining changed the answer without converging (−31.9 % → −2.0 % → +20.1 % on a nested ladder). The electrode surface \(r = a_\text{eq}\) is now an exact mesh line. Verified independently across six geometries: convergence is order 2.00, strictly one-sided and strictly shrinking. A second, subtler non-conformity found in re-audit is also closed — the Dirichlet node set was captured before the layer-interface cut, so for any interface shallower than \(a_\text{eq}\) the cut left a free node in the middle of the energised surface (an insulating patch). That affected every top-layer thickness below \(a_\text{eq}\), which for a 100 × 100 m mesh electrode is the whole AP1 soil grid.
  • ⚠ references.pollaczek: the buried-conductor kernel used Carson's air exponent (F09). Both pollaczek_self_impedance and pollaczek_mutual_impedance integrated \(e^{-2h\lambda}\), correct only for a conductor in air where \(\gamma \approx 0\). The Pollaczek/Sunde form for a conductor buried in the earth requires \(e^{-2h\,u}\) with \(u = \sqrt{\lambda^2 + j\omega\mu_0/\rho}\). Measured error in \(R'\): −0.5 % at 50 Hz / \(h\) = 1 m, −2.1 % at 1 kHz / 1 m, −5.8 % at 1 kHz / 3 m, −54 % at 1 MHz; \(X'\) was affected far less (< 0.2 % in band). The 0.14.0 notes recorded the consequence as physics — "\(R'\) sits just below \(\omega\mu_0/8\), the deficit growing with frequency" — and that was the bug's signature: with the correct kernel \(R'\) sits above \(\omega\mu_0/8\) and rises with burial depth, as a buried conductor's earth-return resistance must. The claim is corrected in the module docstring, the API page, ADR-0006 and the tests that encoded it.
  • ⚠ references.dwight1936: two reference formulas were wrong. horizontal_strip used the round-wire bracket constant −2 instead of the strip constant −1 (~10 % low, F37); vertical_round_plate applied a factor 2 twice and so halved the plate–image term (F38).
  • ⚠ postprocess.rho_f_standard: dead frequencies are no longer fitted as \(Z = 0\) (F41) — the same defect that had already been fixed in the vector-fitting sibling. A zero impedance is not missing data; it drags the fit towards the origin.

docs.title: Fixed — guards that were missing or wrong
docs.text:
• image family: the z <= 0 rejection now covers every backend (F26, F29). The self-image term \(1/(2z)\) was clamped at a 1 mm floor instead of guarded, so a horizontal electrode at \(z = 0\) silently returned a resistance ~15× too high and mesh-dependent, and a ring at \(z = -100\) m solved to 5.5162 Ω as if buried at \(+100\) m. The guard now lives in the shared reaction-matrix kernel, so mom, bem, cim, mom_sommerfeld and mutual see it too — previously only image / image_2layer raised, and compare_engines therefore disagreed about whether a world was valid at all. Validation looks at segment extent, not just midpoints: a rod with its top 0.5 m in the air used to solve to 106.2 Ω. Messages name the electrode — or the conductor, not the internal __cond_<name>__seg_<k> pseudo-node.
  • New ShallowSegmentWarning for the legal-but-shallow regime. \(L > 4z\) is admissible but the point-image stand-in for the image line biases the diagonal by \(\gtrsim 13\,\%\), which is why refining the mesh keeps moving the answer there. The warning quantifies the bias of the worst offender. Its quoted figure is the horizontal-segment one, and the extent guard above provably restricts the warning to segments inclined less than 30° from horizontal, so the figure now always applies to the case that triggers it.
  • FieldResult.cluster_impedance no longer drops a member's current. The new member filter was applied to the current sum as well as the potential average, so potentials {"a": 10 V} with currents {"a": 1 A, "b": 1 A} returned 10 Ω instead of 5 Ω. The average keeps the filtered set; the current sum runs over all members again.
  • coupling.layered_green: negative depths returned nan silently and propagated all the way to grounding_impedance(). All four entry points now raise ValueError.
  • Engine.solve forwards the image-series controls to image_nlayer (F18). image_max_terms / image_series_tol were forwarded to solve_image_2layer but the image_nlayer call took no arguments, so that backend silently used its own defaults although the field documentation promised otherwise.
  • World.solve no longer detaches the Source objects create_source returned (F31) — a handle the user held went stale, silently.
  • compare_engines: the deviation metric is pairwise, not mean-referenced (F35), and is_consistent is no longer True when nothing was compared (F36). The old metric admitted about twice the documented tolerance, and an empty comparison reported a false green.
  • generators: building_counts key order no longer changes the sampled world for a fixed seed (F33) — a reproducibility defect, and the AP1 Monte-Carlo runs depend on a seed pinning a world.
  • generators: footprint-driven foundations land on the OMBR centre (F25) — the oriented-bounding-rectangle centre was discarded, displacing the generated rectangle from the footprint it was derived from.
  • generators: route_manhattan's escape_radius_m now covers the final bridge segment (F42), so an anchor inside a footprint no longer always raises — the escape valve did not cover the case it exists for.
  • generators: the ADR-0012 concrete shell is no longer silently dropped (F16). The registry was written under the electrode's own name but read under the cluster anchor's, so switching concrete on had no effect whenever the foundation was not the first surviving electrode of its site: a factor-33 change in concrete_rho_ohm_m produced bit-identical impedances. GroundingSystemSpec.build_at now folds a site's entries onto the anchor once the bonds are in place. Several encased electrodes in one cluster combine in parallel, not in series — each leaks through its own radial shell.
  • io.csv: the frozen column-name constants named columns the writers never emit (F46), so a consumer written against the published constants got a KeyError.
  • fem: r_far_factor was a dead knob. r_far was max(r_far_factor, z_far_factor) * base_length, so every value ≤ 20 returned the same truncation radius with no warning — a truncation study swept a parameter with no effect. It now sets the sphere on its own; z_far_factor is deprecated, still acts as a lower bound when passed, and logs when it overrides.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• cim and bem no longer compute a complex-image fit, and the metadata says so (F34, F39). Both reject \(n \ge 3\) up front, so the only reachable paths use exact closed-form self-kernels and ignored the fit entirely — yet fit_complex_images ran on every solve and its failed result was advertised as cim_n_images / cim_rms (a NaN). cim returns values bit-identical to image_2layer and bem to mom; the metadata now states that plainly. fit_complex_images itself learned to represent the \(\lambda\to\infty\) asymptote of \(\Gamma_1\) and to report failure instead of returning a fit whose residual is meaninglessly \(|K_1|\).
  • coupling.layered_green: lambda_max_factor is now an upper bound on the truncation, not the truncation itself. Raising it is normally a no-op — that is the point of the F14 fix — while lowering it moves work into the closed-form image sum and is equally exact.
  • generators: MeasurementLeadConfig.depth_m is honoured (F48) — it was sampled and discarded, so buried and overhead measurement leads were geometrically identical.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Engine.sommerfeld_lambda_max_factor, sommerfeld_epsabs, sommerfeld_epsrel, sommerfeld_max_osc_panels. The accuracy knobs of the package's reference engine were unreachable from the public API — Engine.solve called solve_mom_sommerfeld(world, self) with no keywords. Defaults equal the previous signature defaults, so existing callers are bit-identical, and all four are echoed into FieldResult.metadata.
  • SommerfeldConvergenceWarning, SommerfeldTailTruncationWarning and ShallowSegmentWarning; the last is now re-exported from groundfield.solver and documented on the solver API page.
  • Executable documentation (F27). tests/test_pass9_doc_snippets.py extracts every fenced python block under docs/ and runs it, one namespace per page, with an explicit <!-- skip-doctest --> marker for illustrative fragments and for the network-dependent OSM examples. Nothing had ever executed the documentation's code, and six live snippets were broken.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• coupling.layered_green: multi-kilometre spans no longer explode. With the tail bounded analytically, lambda_max no longer has to be large. A 4000-pair group at s_max = 4 km runs in 71 ms against 199 ms on 0.14.1 and 11.2 s in the intermediate development state; a scalar 6 km kernel 30 → 8 ms; a 200×20 two_layer_probe_matrix 120 → 9 ms. Accuracy is unchanged or better everywhere.
  • mom_sommerfeld is 150–8000× faster and fem about 15× faster, both as a side effect of the correctness work above rather than of tuning.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• ADR-0006 carried the wrong Pollaczek exponent in its 2026-07-20 amendment and now records the correction and why the old behaviour looked like physics. ADR-0011 claimed offset_xy_m is "zero by construction"; it is not. ADR-0002, docs/concepts.md, docs/quickstart.md and the engine pages no longer advertise cim as the primary \(n \ge 3\) engine and bem as its alternative — both have raised NotImplementedError since 0.11.0 (F17) — and now state plainly that eight backends are six distinct computations, with mom_sommerfeld the only integral-equation path for \(n \ge 3\) and fem the methodologically independent cross-check.
  • Accuracy claims corrected where they were optimistic, not just where they were wrong: four "~1e-8" claims in layered_green (measured ~1e-6, worst 1.1e-5), mom_sommerfeld's "10⁻¹⁴ level" per-pair error and its "≈1 ms" per-pair cost (measured up to 3.25 s for a single kernel evaluation in the thin-layer corner, with the \(O(N^2)\) consequence spelled out), and fem's "element aspect ratios O(1)" (true away from the interface cut, not at it).
  • The deferred half of F26/F29 is documented rather than hidden. Replacing the point image \(1/(2z)\) by the exact image-line integral was not done. The residual bias is stated with numbers — a 10 m tape at \(z = 0.01\) m gives 54.361 / 35.491 / 26.603 / 22.039 / 21.043 Ω for ds = 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25 / 0.1 / 0.05, i.e. +69 % at ds = 0.5 — together with the trap that made the naive fix wrong (the horizontal \(\operatorname{arsinh}\) form applied to a vertical rod segment is worse than the point form) and the collocation-versus-Galerkin distinction of the image-line term.
  • earth_return's module docstring claimed the earth-return reactance decreases with frequency; it increases (F55). The rho_f_standard docstring swapped the physical meaning of \(k_2\) and \(k_3\) (F56). check_segment_resolution skipped polyline and star electrodes (F53, F54). ManhattanGridPlacement.jitter_m carried a ge=0.0 constraint on a float | Distribution union, making the documented distribution form unusable (F47).

docs.title: Internal
docs.text: • New regression modules tests/test_pass9_*.py, one per subsystem, plus tests/test_audit_pass9_fixes.py from 0.14.1. Each test was checked against a clean v0.14.1 export so that it demonstrably fails on the old code; the deliberate controls over already-correct behaviour are labelled as such in their docstrings. One pre-existing assertion was tightened (test_fem.py, 0.25 → 0.01) and one narrowed to exempt a single legitimately-earned warning (test_sommerfeld_inductance.py) — no tolerance was loosened.

docs.title: Review pass 10 (2026-11-07)
docs.text:
Date 2026-11-07 Reviewed 0.15.0 Findings 10.01–10.95 (pass-9 identifiers kept where a finding was already known) Released in 2026.11.0 Overview Audit history · Changelog

The tenth review pass ran against 0.15.0. Its change concept was decided on 2026-11-07 and recorded in the [Unreleased] block of the changelog; the work was carried out by parallel work streams, each of which wrote its release notes as a changelog fragment. The release notes of 2026.11.0 condense these fragments; the concept and the fragments are reproduced here verbatim.

Where this text comes from

This page was moved verbatim from CHANGELOG.md when the release notes were condensed in 2026.11.0 (source: commit 30a122d). Only the markup was adapted: reST roles are rendered as code or math, relative links point to the current pages, trailing whitespace is removed, and each block stands under a heading that names where it was published. Paths, test names and numbers are those of the time; the code has changed since.

docs.title: Planned — review pass 10 (change concept, decided 2026-11-07)
docs.text:
Not yet implemented. This block records the change concept of the tenth review pass (2026-11-07, against 0.15.0) as decided on 2026-11-07. Findings are referenced as 10.NN; pass-9 identifiers (Fxx) are kept where an item was already known. Each item moves into Added / Changed / Fixed / Security / Removed below once it lands together with its test; whatever is still listed here when the release is cut moves to the Roadmap instead. Items marked ⚠ change numerical results.

One release, calendar versioning. All items below ship together in the first calendar-versioned release. The version scheme changes from SemVer (0.15.0) to CalVer YYYY.MM.MICRO (e.g. 2026.11.0; month unpadded and no hyphen, because PEP 440 drops leading zeros and reads 2026-11 as a post-release). MICRO counts further releases within the same month. CalVer carries no compatibility promise, so deprecations follow a written policy: a deprecated name keeps working, warns with DeprecationWarning, and is removed no earlier than two releases and six months after its announcement.

  • Versioning and release tooling: scripts/release.py computes the CalVer version from the release date, validates everything before it writes, and runs git in the repository root; tags become vYYYY.MM.MICRO.
  • Security (10.01): evaluate_spec passes impedance_formula from a BusType JSON to sympy.sympify, which evaluates Python code. Replace it by an allow-list parser that builds the SymPy expression from the AST (numbers, f, rho, j, pi, + − * / **, sqrt/exp/log, size and exponent bounds) and validate on load. groundinsight (local 0.6.0) already guards its formulas; its guard is re-verified against the same attack corpus and against every formula groundfield exports.
  • Packaging (10.02, 10.11): no top-level scripts package and no release console script in the wheel (the same collision exists in groundinsight); py.typed; polars dropped (never imported); profile.out untracked; poetry-core bounded.
  • Silent failures become errors (10.06, 10.43, 10.51, 10.66, 10.67): unknown attached_to / return_to names, worlds without a finite current source, magnitude=nan, cross_section <= 0, non-finite resistivities, zero-length geometry, an ideal conductor with discretize_segment_length, and VoltageSource (currently solved to zero) raise with a named parameter and a suggestion; a cross section above 1e-2 m² warns ("mm² given?"); worlds beyond HARD_LIMIT raise before any allocation unless max_segments is raised; inert settings warn.
  • ⚠ Two-terminal sources and measurement (F01/F30, 10.16, 10.17, 10.38): Source.return_to honoured by every backend through one shared injection step; leakage-free junction nodes; measurement leads re-wired through them (replacing the 5 cm pseudo-rods); FieldResult.input_impedance(source).
  • ⚠ Cross-layer electrodes (F02, 10.15, 10.32, 10.50): one current share per electrode and layer in image_2layer, cim and solve_mutual_*; interface slivers merged; Galerkin self-term.
  • ⚠ Concrete encasement (10.12–10.14): one mechanism — the solver always treats the concrete shell as a distributed series resistance; the lumped model only converts its input. Today the lumped shell is dropped by solve_mutual_matrix, solve_mutual_field and every world without a PEN service drop while the inflated wire radius is kept (−3 % to −29 % on a foundation's self-impedance). OrtsnetzLayout honours the shells. An impact study on representative AP1 sites compares the old and new numbers.
  • ⚠ Exact line-source kernel (10.28): default reaction-matrix and field kernel; the point kernel converges 0.9–1.9 % below the exact uniform-current solution. Engine(kernel="point") reproduces earlier numbers.
  • ⚠ Earth return (F32, F50, F52, 10.20, 10.24, 10.35–10.37, 10.45, 10.46): carson_series on the anti-parallel image baseline; Sommerfeld λ-grid resolves distant pairs; exact n >= 3 buried kernel; Neumann inductance also on lumped and single-segment conductors; consistent internal-inductance convention; opt-in skin effect for conductor resistance.
  • ⚠ Post-solve consistency (10.25, 10.26, 10.33, 10.34): FieldResult.potential and solve_mutual_* use the engine's series controls (today capped at 100 terms); length-weighted solve_mutual_matrix diagonal; backend check and an optional reciprocal off-diagonal; line-source evaluation near conductors.
  • ⚠ Safety (F13, F51, 10.21, 10.22, 10.42, 10.52): touch voltage over the electrode footprint; uniform-current caveat; the EN 50522 anchors are confirmed against EN 50522:2022 Table B.4 (DIN EN 50522:2023-10) and pinned as literals in the test; docstrings cite the current edition; optional body-impedance / additional-resistance model and spectrum touch voltage.
  • ⚠ Fits and export (10.18, 10.19, 10.27, 10.40, 10.41): quantity= on sweep and the rho-f helpers with the input impedance as default; passivity check before export; robust vector fitting with a 0 Hz sample; standard form with optional constant term and relative weights; readable exported formulas.
  • ⚠ Engines (10.23, 10.29–10.31, 10.47–10.49): floating passive clusters in the mom family (reciprocal transfer impedances); cim weighted read-back; fem marked experimental with guards; duplicated layers merged; cim, bem and image_nlayer become deprecated aliases; shared engine benchmark suite.
  • ⚠ Generators (F07, F08, F28, F47, F48, 10.39, 10.53–10.55, 10.78): one network plan and one materialiser behind TnNetworkGenerator and the layout builder; reproducible resolved configs; rotated mesh foundations split at crossings; per-footprint foundations; lead depth honoured; bounded and validated Overpass requests with atomic caching; MD5 marked usedforsecurity=False (identical digests — stored masks stay valid).
  • Performance (10.56–10.65): row-chunked kernels (memory from 96 B·N² to O(N)), one reaction-matrix evaluation per solve, direct matrix assembly in solve_mutual_matrix, vectorised two-layer series (optional numba extra), multi-frequency Sommerfeld assembly, chunked field evaluation, sweep(n_jobs=...), performance and memory regression tests.
  • Architecture (10.74–10.77, 10.79–10.81): one kernel module and one solve pipeline shared by all backends; backend registry with a common metadata core and provenance (F22); versioned save_result / load_result (F23); nested backend options.
  • Usability (10.68–10.73): typed electrode factories, consistent parameter names with aliases, English names for German identifiers with aliases, curated namespaces (gf.plot, gf.safety, gf.fit), FieldResult.to_dataframe(), complex-valued compare_engines over all frequencies.
  • Standards (10.80, 10.94, 10.95): ruff format, ruff lint with the NumPy docstring convention and a physics naming allow-list, mypy, pre-commit, CI jobs for lint, types, docs and Python 3.14; tests organised by feature with a finding marker; supply-chain hardening of the workflows (10.03, 10.04).
  • Documentation (10.82–10.93): tutorials / how-to / reference / explanation structure, versioned tutorial notebooks executed in CI, glossary, units and conventions, warnings catalogue, validation page, known limitations, factories in the API reference, corrections to the 0.15.0 release notes (F47, F48 and F53/F54 were listed as fixed but the code was unchanged; cim is not bit-identical to image_2layer on unequal segment lengths; the F16 entry describes the symptom of F08), a concise changelog with a list of releases that changed numbers.

docs.title: Release notes of the work streams
docs.text:
The fragments are reproduced as the work streams wrote them (from changelog.d/ of the release branch); only reST roles would be adapted, and none occur. Each stream wrote its fragment against the state of the branch at that time, so a later stream may have changed what an earlier one describes.

Corrections (first adversarial audit of this release)

Three statements in the fragments below were found to be wrong; the release notes of 2026.11.0 carry the corrected wording:

  • coup1, references.pollaczek (10.45): R′ moves by up to +3.5 % in band (100/10 Ω·m, h₁ = 1 m, conductor at 3 m, 1 kHz; +1.4 % for 1000/30 Ω·m, h₁ = 5 m, conductor at 3 m in the upper layer), not by “up to +0.5 %”; X′ by up to −0.09 %, not “less than 0.02 %”.
  • coup1, exact removal of the additive image (10.46): only kernel-level numbers are quoted. At solver level (default sommerfeld earth return, point kernel; two 1 m rods in 100 Ω·m joined by a 95 mm² conductor) Im Z moves by +6.0 % for a conductor inclined by 30° and by +18.4 % (50 Hz) to +18.5 % (1 kHz) for a steep riser; Re Z is unchanged.
  • core1a, solver structure (10.75, 10.79): “every previously importable name of groundfield.solver.image remains importable” is false for private names and re-imports: the _discretize_* helpers, _grid_segments, the electrode classes and PointSource that the module re-imported, _galerkin_solve of bem and mom_sommerfeld, private helpers re-imported by the other solver modules, and the private Pollaczek kernels of coupling.sommerfeld_inductance are gone.
  • Several fragments of the first waves describe intermediate states that later streams changed: the default kernel became "line" (core2b, after core1a), touching="exact" and the anti-parallel carson_series baseline became the solver default (coup2, after coup1), cim, bem and image_nlayer became deprecated aliases (eng2), the 180° counter-source of the layout builder was replaced by the junction-based measurement loop (gen2, after core2a), the two passivity checks were merged (fitx, after post and secio), and touch_voltage_envelope replaced mesh_centres= by interior= (fitx).

Corrections (second adversarial audit of this release)

The second audit found these statements of the fragments below to be false at the time they were written; the fragments of the fix2* streams at the end of the page record the fixes, and the release notes carry the corrected wording:

  • core2b, interface slivers (10.32): dropping an interface cut that would leave a part shorter than the wire diameter ignored the contact with the other layer (a 4.5 m rod in 1000/30 Ω·m: 195.0 Ω with its tip 15.9 mm into the lower layer, 128.6 Ω at 16.1 mm); every cut is now kept (fix2solver).
  • core2b, “a world without a source stays solvable through Engine.solve (all results zero)”: only fem did; every backend now raises (fix2solver).
  • The segment budget (10.06): conductor sub-pieces were not counted (a 100 m PEN in 2000 pieces was predicted at 12 segments); the guard now counts the nodal system (fix2solver).
  • Floating clusters in solve_mutual_* (10.29): not only an accuracy change; the cost grew with the square of the number of bonded nodes (256 nodes: 24.3 s → 199.9 s); one factorisation now serves all excitations (fix2solver).
  • carson_series on the anti-parallel image (10.20): wrong for a pair on opposite sides of the surface (an overhead lead 1 m above a PEN at 0.7 m: mutual reactance 35.9 % low at 1 kHz) and outside Carson's per-metre domain (fix2coup).
  • Lumped inductive conductors (10.24): under sommerfeld a km-long lumped conductor was one 16 × 16 quadrature (3 km at 1 kHz: +13.4 % earth-return resistance, +11 % at solver level, no warning) (fix2coup).
  • fixsec, “parse cost bounded” (10.01): SymPy still expanded symbolic exp and fractional powers of large powers (67- to 75-character formulas ran longer than 60 s), and a literal of 320 nines raised OverflowError (fix2sec).
  • gen2, a shell with ρ_c = ρ_soil (10.12): a shell of any size switched a mesh foundation from one current owner to one per wire (largest touch voltage 232.3 → 221.2 V at 100 A) (fix2gen).
  • eng2, deprecated cim “bit-identical on every world compared” (10.76): it is bit-identical to image_2layer of the same release; through the alias it uses the new default line kernel (core2b), so a ring of r = 2 m in 100 Ω·m moves by +0.85 % against 0.15.0 (13.31207 → 13.42534 Ω).

Superseded by the third adversarial audit and the user's decisions

These statements of the fragments below no longer describe the release; the fragments at the end of the page and the release notes do:

  • core2b, solve_mutual_matrix: offdiag=None selected "probe" when probe points were given. The galerkin off-diagonal is the default of every call; probe points need offdiag="probe" (ddefaults, user decision Q15).
  • coup2 and fix1, Sommerfeld assembly: “the default stays the per-pair assembly”, “"exact" (default)”. The default is "tabulated"; "exact" is the per-pair rule (ddefaults, user decision Q16).
  • fitx and fix3solver, touch_voltage_envelope(interior=None) sampled mesh cells and ring centres (and the cells of generated mesh foundations) by default. The default samples no interior; interior="meshes" does (dsafety, user decision Q3).
  • post, long_duration=True for 80 V beyond 10 s. 80 V applies to every fault duration above 10 s; the keyword is gone (dsafety, user decision Q4).
  • secio / fitx, rho_at_fit = ρ₁ for layered soil. The convention is the effective resistivity effective_resistivity(soil) (drhoeff, user decision Q6).
  • fix2gen, the nearest-point tree of PEN cables (chained cabinets, drops hung on other drops). Every cabinet has its own cable and a drop taps the cable that feeds its building (fix3gen).
  • fix2solver, “the step at zero penetration is the onset of the contact”. It is a limit of the thin-wire model; a rod end within one wire radius of an interface warns (InterfaceContactWarning), and the interface diagonal no longer clamps at h₁/200 (fix3solver).
  • fix2coup, wires lying side by side were switched to touching wires as whole pairs, from one segment's view (order dependent); the rule acts pointwise and order-free, and the accuracy statements “5e-11”, “1e-9” and “≤ 1e-4” hold only where they were measured (fix3coup).

docs.title: Stream infra: Release tooling, packaging and CI
Changed
docs.text:
• Calendar versioning: releases are numbered YYYY.MM.MICRO in PEP 440 form (2026.11.0; month without leading zero, no hyphen; MICRO counts the earlier releases of the month; tags v2026.11.0). The deprecation policy is stated at the top of this changelog. Test: tests/test_release_script.py::test_calver_version_from_date_and_tags.
  • Release tool (10.09): python scripts/release.py calver [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--dry-run] derives the version from the date and the existing tags; python scripts/release.py set X.Y.Z takes an explicit canonical PEP 440 calendar version (pre-releases such as 2026.11.0rc1 included). The tool updates pyproject.toml, __version__, CITATION.cff (version, date-released) and turns [Unreleased] into ## [X] - YYYY-MM-DD, then commits and tags; it never pushes. The major / minor / patch bumps and the options --no-push, --allow-dirty and --allow-empty-changelog are gone. Test: tests/test_release_script.py.
  • Package metadata (10.11): metadata moved from the legacy [tool.poetry] tables to [project] (PEP 621; license as SPDX expression MIT, PEP 639); explicit classifiers for Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 (the auto-generated 3.15 classifier is gone), OS independent, Scientific/Engineering, Typing :: Typed; build backend bounded to poetry-core>=2.2.0,<3.0.0. Test: tests/test_packaging.py::test_metadata_uses_the_project_table.
  • Typed package (10.02): groundfield ships a py.typed marker, so type checkers use its annotations. Test: tests/test_packaging.py::test_wheel_contents.
  • Development standards (10.94, 10.80): ruff lint configuration (F, E, W, I, B, UP, D with NumPy convention, N with a physics naming allow-list, C901 with complexity 15), mypy configuration with the pydantic plugin, pre-commit hooks (ruff format, ruff check, nbstripout, file hygiene), ruff 0.17.4 and mypy 2.4.1 pinned in the dev group, black removed. CI runs lint, types (non-blocking), tests on Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 with pytest -n auto and coverage, a strict docs build on pull requests, and a non-blocking weekly dependency and workflow audit.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• polars dependency (10.11): it was never imported. It is still installed with the groundinsight extra, because groundinsight 0.3.0 requires it. Test: tests/test_packaging.py::test_polars_is_neither_a_dependency_nor_imported.
  • Console scripts and the top-level scripts package (10.02): the wheel no longer installs release, generate-third-party-licenses or a scripts package. Run the tools from a checkout: python scripts/release.py ..., python scripts/generate_third_party_licenses.py. Test: tests/test_packaging.py::test_no_scripts_package_and_no_console_scripts.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Package collision with groundinsight (10.02): the v0.15.0 wheel installed the same scripts/release.py and release command as groundinsight 0.3.0; installing both overwrote one with the other and uninstalling one broke the other. The wheel now contains only groundfield/ and its metadata. Test: tests/test_packaging.py::test_wheel_contents.
  • CI supply chain (10.03): every workflow starts with permissions: {} and grants each job only what it needs; every action is pinned to a full commit SHA with the tag in a comment; checkouts do not persist credentials (except the docs deployment, which pushes gh-pages); snok/install-poetry and softprops/action-gh-release are replaced by a pinned pip install poetry and the GitHub CLI; tag names reach shell code only through environment variables. The release workflow checks that the tag equals the version in all three version files, runs the full CI as a gate before building, and keeps PyPI trusted publishing. zizmor 1.32.0 reports 26 findings on the v0.15.0 workflows and none on the new ones.
  • Locked dependencies (10.04): pip-audit on the exported lock (all groups and extras) found 100 known advisories in 8 packages; after updating pillow (13.0.0), tornado (6.6), urllib3 (2.8.0), pymdown-extensions (12.3), certifi (2026.10.23), idna (3.20), pytest (9.2.0) and mkdocs-material (9.8.1) it finds none. numpy, scipy, sympy, pydantic, matplotlib and pandas keep their locked versions.
  • MathJax (10.08): the documentation loaded MathJax from a floating cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3 URL without integrity check. MathJax 3.2.2 is now vendored with the site (60 files byte-identical to the verified npm release, pinned by SHA256SUMS); the site loads no third-party JavaScript. Test: tests/test_docs_assets.py.
  • Release tool (10.09): the v0.15.0 tool ran git in the caller's working directory, rewrote the version files before it validated the changelog (an aborted run left bumped files behind), committed on a detached HEAD or onto an existing tag, and could not finalise a pre-release. It now runs git in the repository root, validates everything before it writes (clean tree, branch, tag, agreeing version files, non-empty [Unreleased]) and restores the files if the commit fails. Tests: tests/test_release_script.py (marked finding("10.09")).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • Formula rendering: the MathJax configuration started a second typesetting pass concurrently with MathJax's own; every formula was typeset twice (the copy lands in the hidden assistive-MathML region), and pages that autoload a TeX extension (\boldsymbol in ADR-0003 and ADR-0004) failed with "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'replaceChild')". Re-typesetting after instant navigation is now serialised through MathJax.startup.promise.

docs.title: Stream core1a: Exact line-source kernel, solver structure and memory
Added
docs.text:
• Exact line-source kernel (10.28): Engine(kernel="line") treats every segment as a uniform line current (Galerkin form of the exact line potential ln((R1+R2+L)/(R1+R2-L))/L, self term (2/L)[asinh(L/a) - sqrt(1+(a/L)^2) + a/L], images with mirrored end points) for the reaction matrix, FieldResult.potential and solve_mutual_matrix / solve_mutual_field. Against the exact uniform-current resistance (100 Ω·m) a 3 m rod, a 10 m strip, a 10 × 10 m foundation and a 20 × 20 m grid agree within 0.0004 % at every segment length from 2 m to 0.125 m (point kernel: −0.4 … −1.7 %); a ring of 5 m radius converges monotonically as O(ds²) (−0.60 / −0.17 / −0.044 / −0.011 % at ds = 2 / 1 / 0.5 / 0.25 m; point kernel −0.95 % at every ds). The default stays kernel="point", which reproduces earlier numbers; backends outside the image family reject kernel="line". Results record metadata["kernel"]; PointSource gains an optional direction (results written before this release load unchanged and are evaluated with the point kernel). For 16 house grids (1 920 segments) a solve with the line kernel takes about 2.5× the time of the point kernel with numba installed and about 5× without. Test: tests/test_line_kernel.py.
  • Geometry queries on the electrode models (10.79): every electrode kind provides segments(ds, layer_interfaces=None), segment_count(ds), wire_polylines(), bounds(), total_length() and min_feature_length(); groundfield.geometry.WireSegments holds midpoints, lengths and tangents. The solver discretises through them (midpoints, lengths and tangents bit-identical to the previous discretiser), so diagnostics, plots and exports can use the same conventions instead of their own isinstance ladders. Test: tests/test_electrode_geometry.py.
  • Optional compiled kernels (10.58, 10.28): when numba is installed the Tagg/Sunde series matrix and the far-field term of the line kernel are evaluated by compiled kernels that give the same matrices bit for bit: the series about 3× faster than the numpy path on one core (1 200 segments, 148 images), the far-field term about 5× (1 920 segments). Tests: tests/test_kernel_performance.py::test_numba_series_kernel_is_bit_identical, tests/test_line_kernel.py::test_numba_far_field_block_is_bit_identical.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• ⚠ Two-layer image series summed before the product (10.58): the series is accumulated image by image into one matrix and then multiplied with the currents, instead of one matrix product per image. Results of image_2layer (electrodes inside the upper layer) and cim move by floating-point round-off only: at most 7.3e-16 relative on the golden cases cim_rod_two_layer, cond_isolated_pen_sommerfeld_two_layer, defaults_two_layer_ring_auto, img2_grid_upper_resistive and img2_ring_rods_within_layer (all within_tol). The reaction matrices of solve_mutual_* and of the mom family are unchanged bit for bit. A 30-house two-layer network (3 669 segments, 11 frequencies) solved 10–15× faster in two back-to-back comparisons on the same machine (memory 1 236 → 219 MiB).
  • Solver structure (10.75, 10.79): solver/image.py (2 526 lines) is split into private modules (discretisation, guards, kernels, inductive assembly, topology, pipeline); solve_image and solve_image_2layer run through one pipeline and differ only in the Green's-function object; the Tagg/Sunde series is one ImageSeries object used by the solver, FieldResult.potential and solve_mutual_*. Every previously importable name of groundfield.solver.image remains importable. Numbers are unchanged (golden values bit-identical). Tests: tests/test_solver_structure.py, tests/test_image_pipeline.py.
  • The warning for ignored non-current sources of image and image_2layer uses the common text of the other backends; FieldResult.clusters lists the electrodes in world order.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Memory of the image-family kernels (10.56): the kernels no longer build (N, N, 3) difference tensors (96 bytes per segment pair). A 30-house network (3 687 segments) peaks at 115 MiB instead of 1 248 MiB and solved about 10× faster in back-to-back runs on the same machine; an 80-house network (9 712 segments) solves in about 2 s with 773 MiB (before: about 8.4 GiB needed). With rods reaching the lower layer of a two-layer soil (ADR-0007 path) the 30-house network peaks at 510 MiB instead of 1 250 MiB. Results are bit-identical. Above 1 GiB per reaction matrix the kernels switch to row blocks (results then differ by round-off only). Tests: tests/test_kernel_performance.py::test_solve_memory_peak_is_bounded, tests/test_kernel_performance.py::test_cross_layer_solve_memory_peak_is_bounded.
  • Reaction matrix evaluated twice per solve (10.57): the segment potentials after the solve reuse the assembled matrix. Bit-identical. Test: tests/test_kernel_performance.py::test_one_reaction_matrix_assembly_per_solve.
  • solve_mutual_matrix built the reaction matrix as kernel(eye(N)) (10.59): the matrix is assembled directly; Z_G is bit-identical and a 20-house two-layer catalogue matrix (2 466 segments) was 23–31× faster in two back-to-back comparisons (memory 604 → 146 MiB). Test: tests/test_kernel_performance.py::test_mutual_matrix_without_identity_product.
  • FieldResult.potential unchunked (10.62): large evaluations run in row blocks; a 200 × 200 grid over 3 687 sources peaks at 17 MiB (v0.15.0 needs about 96 bytes per point·source pair, 13 GiB here). Two-layer evaluations share every 1/r block between real and imaginary part and skip an all-zero imaginary part. Evaluations up to 16 MiB of kernel are bit-identical. Test: tests/test_kernel_performance.py::test_potential_on_a_large_grid_is_memory_bounded.
  • Point-source arrays rebuilt on every potential() call (10.65): cached privately on the result (not serialised). Test: tests/test_kernel_performance.py::test_point_source_arrays_are_cached_and_invalidated.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • Dead code (10.81): solver.image._potential_kernel, solver.image._segment_z_extent, solver.image_2layer._two_layer_potential_kernel and the empty module solver.field_study. Test: tests/test_solver_structure.py::test_dead_helpers_are_removed.

docs.title: Stream core1b: Backend registry, metadata, provenance and result files
Added
docs.text:
• Backend registry (10.74): groundfield.solver.registry with register_backend(name, solve_fn, *, capabilities, options_model=None, aliases=(), deprecated_alias_of=None, experimental=False, forward=None), get_backend, available_backends, unregister_backend, BackendCapabilities and BackendSpec. Engine.solve dispatches through the registry instead of an if-chain, so a backend is added without editing Engine.solve; the automatic forwarding of image to image_2layer / image_nlayer by soil model is kept. A deprecated alias warns with its replacement and the earliest removal (2027.5); an experimental backend warns once per process (ExperimentalBackendWarning). Tests: tests/test_backend_registry.py::test_new_backend_runs_without_editing_engine_solve, ::test_deprecated_alias_warns_with_replacement_and_removal_version, ::test_experimental_backend_warns_once_per_process, ::test_image_is_auto_forwarded_by_soil_model.
  • Capability check before the solve (10.74): a world the backend cannot represent (soil layer count, concrete-shell electrodes, an explicitly requested source kernel) raises BackendCapabilityError before any backend code runs and names the registered backends that can solve it; a stack of equal layers counts as the merged stack. A backend that solves the world with a simplification warns with BackendCapabilityWarning: fem reduces distributed and inductive conductors to lumped resistive branches, and every backend still returns the current of a source with return_to through remote earth. Tests: tests/test_backend_registry.py::test_capability_error_names_a_backend_that_can_solve_the_world, ::test_capability_check_runs_before_the_backend, ::test_two_terminal_source_warns_when_the_backend_ignores_return_to, ::test_fem_warns_when_it_reduces_a_distributed_conductor.
  • Metadata core (10.74): every result carries backend, effective_backend, kernel, groundfield_version, frequencies, n_segments, soil_kind, earth_inductive_model, solve_time_s, series and provenance (groundfield.solver.engine.CORE_METADATA_KEYS) next to the backend-specific keys, which are unchanged. series records the engine's image-series controls for the post-solve field evaluation. Test: tests/test_backend_registry.py::test_every_backend_reports_the_metadata_core.
  • Backend options (10.74): Engine.options, keyed by backend name and validated by MomSommerfeldOptions (mom_sommerfeld) and FemOptions (fem), with a did-you-mean message for misspelled names; Engine.backend_options(name) returns the options a backend runs with. Tests: tests/test_engine_options.py::test_nested_sommerfeld_options_reach_the_backend, ::test_misspelled_option_is_rejected_with_a_suggestion.
  • Provenance (10.77, F22): metadata["provenance"] of every solve holds the groundfield, Python, numpy, scipy and pydantic versions, the platform, the engine configuration, world_fingerprint (SHA-256 of the canonical world JSON, groundfield.io.world_fingerprint) and the UTC time of the solve. Tests: tests/test_result_persistence.py::test_every_solve_records_provenance, ::test_world_fingerprint_is_canonical_and_sensitive, ::test_fingerprint_describes_the_world_as_built.
  • Versioned result files (10.77, F23): groundfield.io.save_result / load_result write and read one standard-JSON file with the envelope {"format": "groundfield.result", "schema_version": 1, "written_by", "provenance", "result"} (no pickle, atomic write, no silent overwrite); a newer schema raises ResultFormatError. Tests: tests/test_result_persistence.py::test_save_and_load_result_round_trip, ::test_load_result_rejects_a_newer_schema.
  • FieldResult.to_dataframe() (10.69, 10.72): tidy table with one row per frequency and electrode (frequency_hz, electrode, cluster, potential_v, current_a, cluster_impedance_ohm); to_dataframe("sources") gives one row per frequency and source with the impressed current and the input impedance. pandas is imported on first use. Tests: tests/test_result_dataframe.py::test_electrode_table_is_tidy_and_matches_the_accessors, ::test_source_table_carries_the_input_impedance.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Engine.backend is validated against the registry (a plain str annotation; Backend stays the Literal of the built-in names for type hints). An unknown name raises with the closest registered name as suggestion. Test: tests/test_backend_registry.py::test_unknown_backend_name_suggests_the_closest_registered_one.
  • Unsupported worlds fail earlier: cim, bem, mom and image_nlayer on soils with three or more distinct layers, and every non-image backend on concrete-shell electrodes, now raise BackendCapabilityError from Engine.solve and list the backends that can. It subclasses ValueError and NotImplementedError, the types image_nlayer, cim, bem and the concrete-shell guard raised before; mom raised TypeError for three or more layers.
  • One default for the image-series cap (10.74): DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_TERMS = 300 and DEFAULT_IMAGE_SERIES_TOL = 1e-6 (in groundfield.solver.registry) are the engine defaults and are recorded on every result as metadata["series"]. The image-series controls stay common Engine fields because six backends and the post-solve layer read them. Test: tests/test_engine_options.py::test_series_default_is_one_documented_value.
  • Engine JSON: options replaces the four flat sommerfeld_* keys; engine JSON written by 0.15.0 still loads, silently when it carries the default values. Test: tests/test_engine_options.py::test_v0150_engine_json_loads_without_warnings.
  • Result JSON writes non-finite floats of typed fields as "Infinity" / "NaN" strings instead of null, and tagged objects in metadata (see the groundfield.solver.result module docstring), so it is standard JSON and round-trips exactly.
  • Warnings of the pre-flight resolution check of Engine.solve are attributed to the caller's line instead of a line inside groundfield.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Lossy result JSON (10.77): metadata["penetration_depth"] lost its float keys and its inf, and numpy values in the metadata could not be serialised at all. Tests: tests/test_result_persistence.py::test_result_json_round_trip_is_lossless, ::test_numpy_and_non_json_metadata_survive_the_round_trip.
  • Backend options silently accepted for another backend (10.74): the sommerfeld_* fields were accepted by every backend without effect; options for a backend that will not run now warn (BackendOptionsWarning). Test: tests/test_engine_options.py::test_options_for_another_backend_warn.
  • fem knobs unreachable (10.74): n_radial, n_axial, r_far_factor, z_far_factor and far_field can now be set through Engine(options={"fem": {...}}). Tests: tests/test_engine_options.py::test_fem_knobs_are_reachable_through_engine_options, ::test_fem_far_field_option_reaches_the_solver.
  • Engine.solve let a backend rewrite the caller's sources (10.72): World.solve, Engine.solve and run_simulation now share one identity-preserving snapshot and restore of World.sources. Test: tests/test_solve_entry_points.py::test_every_entry_point_restores_the_sources.
  • Inert engine settings accepted silently (10.51): Engine.tolerance and Engine.max_iterations are read by no backend; a non-default value now warns. Test: tests/test_engine_options.py::test_tolerance_and_max_iterations_warn_that_they_have_no_effect.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text:
• Engine.tolerance and Engine.max_iterations (no effect): a non-default value or attribute access emits DeprecationWarning; removal no earlier than 2027.5.
  • The flat fields Engine.sommerfeld_lambda_max_factor, sommerfeld_epsabs, sommerfeld_epsrel and sommerfeld_max_osc_panels: use Engine(options={"mom_sommerfeld": {...}}) or MomSommerfeldOptions. They are still accepted (constructor, JSON, attribute read and write); removal no earlier than 2027.5. Test: tests/test_engine_options.py::test_flat_sommerfeld_fields_are_mapped_and_deprecated.
  • World.solve(snapshot_sources=False): every entry point takes the snapshot now, so the opt-out saves nothing; removal no earlier than 2027.5. Test: tests/test_solve_entry_points.py::test_snapshot_opt_out_is_deprecated.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • The private, unreachable Engine._stub_result and Engine._dispatch (replaced by the registry; part of 10.81).

docs.title: Stream secio: Formula security and the groundinsight export
Security
docs.text: • BusType impedance formulas are parsed, never executed (10.01): evaluate_spec passed impedance_formula to sympy.sympify, which evaluates the text as Python code, so a crafted BusType JSON file ran arbitrary code or exhausted memory (7**7**7*0+rho builds an integer of about 696 000 digits, 9**9**9**9 never finishes). A new allow-list parser (groundfield.io._formula) parses the text with ast and builds the SymPy expression itself: numbers, f, rho, j / I, pi, E, + - * /, ** with a literal exponent (at most 64 in magnitude) and sqrt / exp / log, after Unicode NFKC normalisation, ASCII only, at most 10 000 characters, 2 000 syntax nodes and nesting depth 100. Every number stays within 1e-300 to 1e300 and powers are checked before they are computed, which also stops towers such as (((10**60*f)**64)**64)**64 (the review prototype accepted this one after 24 to 46 s with a 15.7-million-digit integer). BusTypeSpec.from_dict and load_bustype_json validate the formula on load and raise EvaluateSpecError naming the offending element (a missing formula raises EvaluateSpecError instead of KeyError). All 384 formulas the 0.15.0 exporter wrote parse to identical values, so existing BusType files keep loading. The corpus tests/data/formula_corpus.json (115 accepted formulas with reference values, 79 rejected strings) is shared with groundinsight's guard. Tests: tests/test_formula_security.py::test_evaluate_spec_does_not_run_code_from_a_formula, tests/test_formula_security.py::test_every_rejected_formula_fails_on_load_within_bounds, tests/test_formula_security.py::test_every_rejected_formula_fails_in_evaluate_spec_within_bounds.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Passivity check before BusType export (10.40): to_bustype_dict, save_bustype_json, to_bustype and save_bustype_to_db evaluate the exported formula from 0 Hz to twice the highest fitted frequency (dense linear and logarithmic grid, the samples and the midpoints between them, points around every pole; for the standard form over the fitted rho range) and refine the minima. metadata["passivity"] records passed, min_re_Z_Ohm, f_at_min_Hz, rho_at_min_Ohm_m and the checked ranges. Re Z < 0 emits NonPassiveFitWarning; the new keyword require_passive=True raises NonPassiveFitError (a ValueError) and writes nothing. Example from the review: a 4-pole fit of passive data (rms 4.4 mOhm) has Re Z = -0.0194 Ohm at 5.507 Hz between the 0 Hz and 50 Hz samples and is now flagged. Test: tests/test_io_groundinsight.py::test_in_band_non_passive_vector_fit_is_flagged_on_export.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • ⚠ Readable exported formulas (10.73): vector fits are written as partial fractions with float coefficients, each rounded once to decimals significant digits with Python's correctly rounded formatting (identical on every platform), e.g. 28.4652054274 - 54.0434542796/(2*pi*f*j + 27.5749267026). The exporter no longer calls nsimplify (exact fractions with integers of up to 254 digits) and no longer merges the partial fractions into one rational function (sympy.simplify produced terms up to f**4). Formulas of 2 to 10 poles shrink from 273-622 to 126-469 characters, and the export takes 0.04-0.14 s instead of 0.39-2.23 s (same session, passivity check included). decimals must be a positive integer; values above 17 count as 17. Numbers move only at the rounding level, at most half a unit in the last printed digit per coefficient (round trip below 1e-10 relative at the default 12 digits). Affected: anyone comparing formula text, e.g. diffs of BusType JSON files. Golden cases: none moved (fit_rho_f_standard_sweep bustype/eval is bit-identical). Tests: tests/test_io_groundinsight.py::test_vector_fit_formula_prints_floats_not_long_rationals, tests/test_io_groundinsight.py::test_round_trip_accuracy_follows_decimals.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Actionable rho_at_fit error for vector-fit exports (10.84): the documented save_bustype_json(fit, ...) call for a vector fit raised "rho_at_fit is required" without saying what to pass. rho_at_fit stays required for a VectorFitResult (the BusType records the soil resistivity it belongs to); all four export functions now raise the same ValueError naming the function, an example call and the layered-soil convention, before a file is written or groundinsight is imported, and rho_at_fit must be positive and finite. Test: tests/test_io_groundinsight.py::test_vector_fit_without_rho_at_fit_raises_an_actionable_error.
  • BusType provenance stamp: metadata["source"] read groundfield unknown when the package ran from a source checkout (and went stale under an editable install); it now uses groundfield.__version__ (review item R5-12). Test: tests/test_io_groundinsight.py::test_bustype_metadata_records_the_running_groundfield_version.

docs.title: Internal
docs.text: • The groundinsight round-trip test for vector fits asserts 1e-9 (ADR-0008) instead of 1e-3; a new test compares evaluate_spec with groundinsight's compute_impedance to 1e-9 and skips without groundinsight (tests/test_io_groundinsight.py::test_evaluate_spec_matches_groundinsight_evaluation).
