docs.title: Stream drhoeff: User decision Q6: effective resistivity
Added
docs.text: • effective_resistivity (10.84, user decision Q6): the effective resistivity of a homogeneous or two-layer soil in Ω·m, ρ_eff = ρ₁^(1−w) · ρ₂^w with w = w0 · (h₁ / h_ref)^(−β), h_ref = 10 m and the AP1 calibration w0 = 0.13, β = 0.8 (group-specific values as w0=, beta=, h_ref=). gf.effective_resistivity(soil) (also groundfield.soil.effective_resistivity, or with the keywords rho_1, rho_2, h_1) returns ρ itself for homogeneous soil and for stacks of equal layers, without round-off (the plain formula gives 200.00000000000003 Ω·m for 200 / 200 Ω·m, h₁ = 10 m); reduces a MultiLayerSoil to its canonical stack (equal adjacent layers merged, as the layered backends do, 10.48) and raises ValueError for three or more distinct layers; limits w to [0, 1], so ρ_eff stays between ρ₁ and ρ₂ (the unlimited formula leaves that interval below h₁ = 0.78 m: 17.9 Ω·m for 100 / 30 Ω·m at h₁ = 0.5 m; with the limit such a thin upper layer gives ρ₂). Inside the calibration range of the AP1 catalogue (h₁ = 5 … 30 m, ρ₁ = 30 … 1000 Ω·m, ρ₂ = 30 … 200 Ω·m) the value is bit-identical to the AP1 / AP2 scripts' r1 ** (1 - w) * r2 ** w and agrees with a 50-digit evaluation to 1.6e-16. Test: tests/test_effective_resistivity.py.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • ⚠ The rho of a BusType in layered soil is the effective resistivity (10.84, user decision Q6): rho_at_fit of a vector fit and the rho samples of a standard form fitted in layered soil are ρ_eff of the soil they were computed in, effective_resistivity(soil), the specific_earth_resistance the AP2 network model gives a groundinsight bus. This replaces the upper-layer resistivity ρ₁ that the 10.84 entry of this release cycle had made the convention; on the AP1 grid ρ_eff differs from ρ₁ by −54.8 % (1000 over 30 Ω·m, h₁ = 5 m) to +53.6 % (30 over 200 Ω·m, h₁ = 5 m). The error message for a missing rho_at_fit, the docstrings of the four exporters, the IO and Soil references, ADR-0008 and tutorial T05 state it. Every BusType document records the convention as metadata["rho_definition"] = "effective_resistivity" (documents of 0.15.0 have no such entry). No function computes a different number: the exporter writes the rho it is given. Affected: BusTypes exported in layered soil with ρ₁ as rho. A compact electrode in the upper layer follows ρ₁ more closely than ρ_eff of the AP1 networks: the station of the IO example (2 m ring and 3 m rod) swept over ρ₁ fits the standard form to 13.4 / 8.3 / 3.6 % over ρ_eff and to 3.9 / 1.9 / 0.6 % over ρ₁ for h₁ = 5 / 10 / 30 m; check max_relative. Golden cases: none. Tests: tests/test_io_groundinsight.py::test_rho_at_fit_convention_for_layered_soil_is_the_effective_resistivity, ::test_bustype_metadata_records_the_rho_definition, ::test_layered_soil_exports_pair_with_an_effective_resistivity_bus.

docs.title: Stream ddefaults: User decisions Q15 to Q17: galerkin, tabulated Sommerfeld, resource limit
Added
docs.text: • Per-engine resource limit Engine.max_segments (10.06, user decision Q17): the hard problem-size limit of the segment backends — the number of leakage segments and the number of unknowns of the dense nodal system — is set per engine: Engine(max_segments=...) (also a create_engine parameter) raises or lowers it for one engine, a positive integer; None (default) takes the module constant groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT (20 000), read at solve time, so the constants stay the defaults. Every segment backend (the image family, mom, mom_sommerfeld), solve_mutual_matrix and solve_mutual_field refuse a larger world with ResourceLimitError before anything of that size is allocated; check_segment_budget, expected_segments (new key "limit"), check_segment_resolution and diagnose (report.context["max_segments"]) check against the same limit, and the messages name the setting to change. The limit is recorded in the new core metadata key FieldResult.metadata["max_segments"] (the engine block of the provenance keeps the request itself). SOFT_LIMIT (5 000, the size above which the solve reports that it may take minutes) stays a module constant. Tests: tests/test_resource_limit.py.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• ⚠ solve_mutual_matrix uses the galerkin off-diagonal for every call (10.34, user decision Q15): offdiag="galerkin" (the reaction of the leakage distributions: reciprocal, and the matrix with which (Y_L + Z_G⁻¹)u = i reproduces the solve of the clusters joined by branches) is the default whatever the call; offdiag="probe" (the potential at one probe point per cluster, the definition of releases up to 0.15.0) stays available. A call that passes probe_points without offdiag="probe" — every 0.15.0 call, the AP1 catalogue pipeline among them — returns the galerkin matrix; the points are ignored, not validated, with the new groundfield.solver.mutual.ProbePointsIgnoredWarning, which names offdiag="probe" as the way back. This supersedes the selection rule added earlier in this release cycle (offdiag=None choosing "probe" when probe points were given; None is no longer accepted). The diagonal does not move. On an AP1-like site (station ring and three rods, twelve polygon foundations, ds = 2 m, five soils) the symmetrised probe matrix missed the input impedance of the joined network by −0.15 … −0.88 % and single off-diagonal entries by up to 41 % (median 0.15 … 1.1 %); the galerkin matrix reproduces it to 7e-13. On the AP1 catalogue path (group-2 site, 7 corner soils × 4 penetrations) |Z_ons| at 50 Hz moves by −0.05 … +0.29 % at penetrations up to 20 % and by +0.25 … +2.67 % at 40 % (largest at ρ₁ = 1000 Ω·m), the ONS current share at 50 Hz by up to +2.7 %. Who is affected: every Z_G built with probe points, the AP1 catalogue. Golden cases: mutual_foundations_lumped_concrete, mutual_foundations_distributed_concrete, mutual_three_rods_crosslayer, line_mutual_two_layer (Z_G norm-wise 7.7e-4 … 8.8e-4, single off-diagonal entries 0.48 … 5.9 %). Tests: tests/test_mutual_matrix.py::test_galerkin_is_the_default_whatever_the_call, ::test_ignored_probe_points_are_not_validated, ::test_offdiag_selection_and_validation.
  • ⚠ Tabulated Sommerfeld assembly by default (10.60, user decision Q16): Engine.sommerfeld_assembly defaults to "tabulated" (one table of the spectral integral per pair of depth groups and frequency); "exact" (one quadrature per segment pair, the default up to 0.15.0) stays available. The image family, mom, mom_sommerfeld and solve_mutual_* follow the setting alike; engine JSON without the field (0.15.0) gets the new default. Blocks of fewer than 64 sub-segment pairs keep the per-pair rule, so small inductive worlds do not move. On a TN network with an inductive PEN (TnNetworkGenerator, homogeneous 100 Ω·m, ds = 1 m, four frequencies 50 … 1000 Hz) the input impedance of the tabulated solve lies within 2e-10 of two independent refined references (per-pair rule with 200 instead of 24 interpolation nodes; tables of 400 instead of 100 nodes; both with a refined λ grid), which agree with each other to 2e-10, while the per-pair rule is 1.2e-8 off (8 houses); CPU time 1.0 s instead of 16.6 s (8 houses, 78 inductive branches) and 12.2 s instead of 306 s (30 houses, 338 inductive branches; input impedance equal to 1.1e-8, the tabulated one 1.8e-11 from the 400-node tables). The correction matrices of small conductor sets in twelve critical geometries (buried, overhead, 1 cm below the surface, in the surface plane, crossing the surface or a layer interface, two- and three-layer earth, 250 m segments, 10 and 1000 Ω·m; 50 Hz and 1 kHz) are finite, symmetric and free of warnings; against a reference refined in S(ρ) and in the λ grid the tabulated rule is closer than the per-pair rule in ten of them (1.5e-7 … 1.1e-5 against 4.2e-6 … 7.6e-5 of the largest entry) and equal in two (the surface plane, where both use the per-pair rule, and a riser through h₁, 4.3e-6). Who is affected: inductive conductors under earth_inductive_model="sommerfeld" (the default) with blocks of at least 64 sub-segment pairs; numbers move by about 1e-8 … 2.4e-6. Golden case: cond_lumped_long_pen_sommerfeld (≤ 2.4e-6; against the refined per-pair reference the tabulated result is 4.2e-7 off, the per-pair rule 2.0e-6). Tests: tests/test_sommerfeld_assembly_default.py.

docs.title: Decisions on the questions left open (2026-11-08)
docs.text:
After the third adversarial audit and the user's decisions Q1–Q19, the release preparation left 17 questions to the author, each with a recommendation. The author followed every recommendation. The table records the question, the decision and where it went; the work streams d2solver, d2gen and d2soil below implemented the decisions that change code.

Q Question Decision Where 20 Encase the cross-braces of mesh foundation electrodes in the concrete shell, as DIN 18014 lays the foundation earth electrode with its connections in the concrete? yes streams d2gen, f2gen 21 Deprecate FoundationElectrodeSpec.concrete_model, which only chooses one or four current owners of a ring foundation (≤ 0.06 % apart up to aspect ratio 4)? yes; the measured difference is larger (< 1 % / < 2 % up to aspect ratio 4 / 50, see the box below; for the author's review) streams d2gen, f2gen, f3gen 22 Keep the PEN routing of TnNetworkGenerator (an own cable per cabinet, a service drop taps the cable that feeds its building)? Place cabinets per building group in the future? routing kept; cabinets per building group moved into 2026.11.0 (user decision of 2026-11-14, stream w1gen; a wide group's cabinet on the ray through its far-end building since audit W1B-01, stream fw1gen; the 20 m step of the rule stays, user decision D7, stream fw1r2gen) changelog 23 fem whose equivalent hemisphere puts current into a more conductive layer that the electrodes do not touch (−38 … −98 %): error instead of warning? error; extended after the audit to a more conductive layer within the electrodes' horizontal half-extent (coordinator, for the author's review) streams d2solver, f2solver, f3solver 24 Point-form guard near a layer interface: keep the conservative thresholds (warning within 0.6 segment lengths, error within 0.387)? kept known limitations 25 Accept the step of carson_series at the 8.1° boundary of its validity domain as a documented limit? accepted known limitations, earth return 26 Accept that the simulated in-line fall-of-potential reading moves because the leads now couple as wires lying side by side (Im Z_meas 0.063 → 0.054 Ω at 50 Hz)? accepted release notes, 10.46 27 Warn when perfect_mirror couples conductors on opposite sides of the soil surface through its additive image? warning streams d2solver, f2solver, f3solver 28 Count powers of numbers (10**40) in the rule on nested exponents of the formula parser, as groundinsight does? yes; already the rule ((f*10**40)**2 is rejected, tests/test_formula_security.py::test_exponents_of_nested_powers_multiply_to_at_most_max_pow) no change 29 Only document that printing a parsed formula or passing it to lambdify lets SymPy evaluate parts of an untrusted formula again? documented IO reference 30 One current per wire line for grids and stars in the image family (−3 … −5 %)? moved into 2026.11.0 (user decision of 2026-11-14, stream w1sol): grids one owner per wire line (−1.2 … −5.5 %), building outlines per side (Q44); a star alone does not change (equal arm currents), its remaining error is on the roadmap changelog 31 Make the soft size notice (5 000 segments) adjustable per engine as well? yes stream d2solver 32 Read a thin conductor inside a thicker one as a concentric cable only with an explicit marker? moved into 2026.11.0 (user decision of 2026-11-14, stream w1sol): marker conductor_type="cable_shield" changelog 33 No internal inductance of a solid wire for cable shields (100 m coaxial pair 31.97 instead of 26.97 µH)? moved into 2026.11.0 together with 32: 26.97 µH; sub-pieces add up since audit W1A-02 (stream fw1sol), also tilted against each other since audits W1R2-01, W1R3-01 and W1R3-02 (streams fw1r2sol, fw1r3) changelog 34 Tighten the rule for segments up to a quarter skin depth under sommerfeld (step of 3.5e-4 at δ/4)? a later release (2026-11-08); moved into 2026.11.0 by the user decision of 2026-11-14 done in 2026.11.0 (streams w3perf, fw3perf): exact one-dimensional self rule and graded close-pair rule; with the λ grid of audit W3B-01 the self correction is within 1.1e-9 of a refined rule from 1 m and 0.01 δ to 3 km at 50 Hz and 1 kHz for the soils tested (up to 3.4e-9 in high-contrast soils, audit W3R2B-08), no step (was 4.8e-4, step 3.5e-4); close pairs within about 4e-8 (were up to 1.5e-3); five golden cases move by up to 4.9e-7 (changelog) 35 Radial trunk: a building in a substation slot taps its feeder's trunk instead of getting its own line from the substation? moved into 2026.11.0 together with 22 (stream w1gen) changelog 36 Presets of the effective-resistivity weights per electrode class, with the values of the AP2 hand-over? yes streams d2soil, f2gen

The audits of the decision streams left four more questions, answered on the same day; the author again followed the recommendations and chose the next release for 37 and 39, this release for 38, and for 40 a quantification only once a 3-D volume reference exists. The earlier wording of 37 pointed to a "conforming axisymmetric" roadmap item that did not exist yet. With the user decision of 2026-11-14, 37 and 39 moved into 2026.11.0, and the 3-D model of wave 4 gave the reference that 40 waited for; the rows say where each was done.

Q Question Decision Where 37 Stop adding rules to the equivalent-hemisphere reduction of fem, in which every audit round found new limit cases (an interface 1 cm below a deep ring +191 … +308 % without a message; a rod reaching 1 µm … 8 cm into a more conductive top layer −44 … −78 %, warning only)? yes; no further rules, replaced by a conforming axisymmetric model (rod on the axis, ring, ring with central rod; other electrodes refused until a full 3-D method exists); planned for a later release on 2026-11-08, moved into 2026.11.0 with the full 3-D model by the user decision of 2026-11-14 implemented in 2026.11 (streams w4axi, w4fem3d; fixes of audits W4A / W4B in fw4axi, fw4fem3d): conforming axisymmetric model of rods on one axis and rings around it (about 1e-4; rings next to a conductive layer 3.3e-4 since W4A-01), and a three-dimensional conforming model for every other world — strips, grids, meshes, several clusters, galvanic distributed conductors — within 2e-3 of the axisymmetric model away from interfaces and other wires (W4B-01/-02) and between image_2layer and mom at the AP1 station; the 3-D port limit is the option FemOptions.max_ports_3d (stream fw4int); the equivalent-hemisphere reduction is gone (changelog) 38 Which owner model stays when concrete_model is removed: one current per rectangle without cross-braces (up to 2.2 % above the reference with one current per segment) or one per side (up to 0.9 %; short side at least 1 m)? one per side, already in 2026.11.0: concrete_model has no effect stream d3gen 39 Record the effective-resistivity preset in the BusType document (for example metadata["rho_preset"]), so that a bus paired with the wrong preset is detectable? yes, in a later release (2026-11-08); moved into 2026.11.0 by the user decision of 2026-11-14 done in 2026.11.0 (streams w3perf, fw3perf, fw3r2b): rho_preset of the exporters, metadata["rho_preset"], BusTypeSpec.rho_preset, the last line of the description of the live BusType and of its database entry (bustype_rho_preset; audit W3B-06), RhoPresetMismatchWarning from evaluate_spec / bustype_from_spec; a document holds a known preset name or null, and only an exact preset line of a description is replaced (audit W3R2B-06); older documents load with None (changelog) 40 Quantify the overlap of the concrete shells at the corners and crossings of encased foundations? only once a 3-D volume reference is available quantified in 2026.11 (stream w4fem3d, audit W4B-05) against the concrete resolved as a volume in the 3-D fem model: a junction acts like a few cm of wire, at most about 2 r_b, sign not settled (not converged); the generators' house mesh changes by about 1 % or less (0.35 … 0.85 % re-measured after W4B-01); no correction rule (concrete shells)

The audits of stream d3gen (D3A-02, D3A-03, D3B-03, D3B-04) found that the generators attach PEN conductors at the connection point of a foundation's anchor, which is a corner for rectangular foundations in this release (meshes since audit A2G-04, rings since Q38; the centre of one grid mesh in 0.15.0) and the first vertex for building outlines; the author decided on 2026-11-14:

Q Question Decision Where 41 Where do the conductors the generators route to a foundation end: at the centre as in 0.15.0, at the corner of the anchor side, or at the point of the foundation nearest to the conductor? at the nearest point, for every foundation form (rectangles, building outlines, the substation's foundation), already in 2026.11.0 streams f4gen, f5gen, f6gen (audits D3A, D3B, R4A, R4B, R5A, R5B, R6A); rings and strips since Q43 and layout cables clipped at every site they pass since audits R6A-01, W1B-03, W1B-04 (streams w1gen, fw1gen) (changelog)

The hand-over of 2026-11-14 left three questions; the author answered them the same evening and decided to integrate (almost) every open roadmap item into 2026.11.0 before the release — everything scheduled for the next release, the items left open, and the full 3-D FEM; out of scope stay the BranchType export to groundinsight, the import of measurement setups from groundmeas, the AP1 reference-case library and scaling the LU solve to 10 000 segments.

Q Question Decision Where 42 Route service drops around foundations (street geometry) instead of the shortest connection? no, keep the shortest connection no code change; known limitations, roadmap (row of the TN generator) 43 Apply the nearest-point rule of Q41 also to sites earthed by a RingElectrodeSpec circle or a strip (the default substations)? yes done in 2026.11.0 (stream w1gen): every conductor routed to such a site ends at the point of the electrode nearest to it (a circle exactly), rods keep their head (changelog) 44 One current per straight wire for building outlines? yes, together with Q30 (one current per wire line in the solver) done in 2026.11.0 (stream w1sol); straight runs at projected coordinates since audits W1A-01 and W1R2-05 (streams fw1sol, fw1r2sol), in linear time since audit W1R3-03 (stream fw1r3) (changelog)

The decisions D1–D9 taken while these items were implemented are listed in Decisions of 2026-11-15, before the sections of the four waves at the end of this page.

Correction to question 38 (audit D3B-01)

The 0.9 % of question 38 was measured at the cases where the owner change is largest. Over the whole scope of the owner texts (short side at least 1 m, aspect ratio up to 50, sides up to 150 m, the AP1 soils) one owner per side is at most 1.4 % above one current per segment (150 m × 3 m bare in 30 over 200 Ω·m: +1.34 %) and one owner per rectangle up to 2.2 % (16 m × 1 m in a 0.2 m shell of 30 Ω·m over 1000 / 30 Ω·m: +2.106 / +2.160 % at 0.5 / 0.25 m segments); one per side is closer everywhere, so the decision stands.

Corrections (adversarial audits of the decision streams)

Two adversarial audits of the three decision streams below (D2A / D2B, fixed by the streams f2solver and f2gen; R2A / R2B, fixed by f3solver and f3gen) corrected these statements; the release notes describe the release:

  • d2solver, Q23: the rule also covers a more conductive layer below the hemisphere but within the electrodes' horizontal half-extent when no more resistive layer lies in between (the error is continuous across a_eq, −67.9 % on both sides for a 10 m ring over 1000/30 Ω·m; an extension by the coordinator, for the author's review). A horizontal wire touches the layers that hold its axis (within its wire radius only for the rule of an electrode below its hemisphere); a rod end on an interface does not touch the layer beyond. fem misplaces the current by −97 … +30 % in the rejected worlds (mostly far too low); more resistive spanned layers are −3 … +48 % off, not +3 … +45 %; none of the rejected worlds was silent before, they warned. fem also refuses strips deeper than half their length, rings deeper than their diameter, driven MeshElectrodes and electrodes and galvanic conductors out of the soil, and names only backends whose own checks accept the world.
  • d2gen, Q20: the brace table is measured against the bare braces of the development line, which were never released; in 0.15.0 the braces had the shell radius without the shell resistance, and against the 0.15.0 "distributed" model the brace rule alone is +5.9 / +66 / +393 % at ρ_c = 150 / 1000 / 5000 Ω·m. The hand assembly that reproduces the solve is a check of the generator with the same kernel and owner model, not an independent method (an independent boundary- element model confirms the numbers; with one current per segment the brace effect is +49.2 / +318.5 % instead of +46.9 / +307 %).
  • d2gen, Q21: concrete_model changes the impedance of an axis-aligned rectangle without cross-braces (also style="mesh" with n_x = n_y = 1) by less than 1 % up to aspect ratio 4 and 2 % up to 50 over the AP1 soils (short side at least 1 m; 5 mm wire at 0.8 m, bare or in concrete of 30 … 1000 Ω·m up to 0.2 m thick; largest values found 0.69 / 1.55 %), not by at most 0.16 % / 0.67 %, and the premise of question 21 (≤ 0.06 %) holds only for bare rings in homogeneous soil (0.09 % / 0.33 % measured): flagged for the author's review.
  • d2soil, Q36: the medians 1.8 % / 5.0 % are over all 39 AP1 soils with the homogeneous ones at zero (2.1 % / 5.5 % over the 36 two-layer soils); that the hand-over's 1.7 % / 15.7 % are this metric is an inference (groundfield 0.14.0 itself at 1.5 m segments reproduces them).

docs.title: Stream d2solver: User decisions Q23, Q27, Q31: fem and more conductive layers, perfect_mirror across the surface, per-engine size notice
Changed
docs.text:
• ⚠ fem (experimental) raises BackendCapabilityError when the equivalent hemisphere of a cluster spans a layer that no electrode of the cluster touches and that conducts better than every layer the electrodes touch (user decision Q23, finding 10.23). The hemisphere injects the current straight into that layer and the result is too low: −97 … +5 % against image_2layer and mom in the measured cases (rods, strips and rings below a more conductive top layer from 22 mm thickness, rings above a more conductive lower layer; −92 % for a 10 m ring at 0.8 m over 1000/30 Ω·m at h₁ = 2 m). Up to now a FemReductionWarning or silent. The rule is structural (near-equal 100/120 Ω·m raises as well), uses the canonical layer stack, and an electrode exactly on an interface touches both layers; the message names the cluster, the layer, the electrodes' ρ, a_eq, the measured range and a backend that solves the world. More resistive spanned layers keep the warning (+3 … +45 %). Tests: tests/test_fem.py::test_fem_rejects_a_more_conductive_layer_its_hemisphere_spans and four siblings.
  • earth_inductive_model="perfect_mirror" emits one UserWarning per solve when inductive conductor segments lie on both sides of the soil surface, naming the number of such pairs and the conductors and pointing to "sommerfeld" (user decision Q27, finding 10.46): its additive image has no physical basis for an overhead/buried pair (2.28 / 2.77 times the mutual reactance of sommerfeld at 50 Hz / 1 kHz for a lead 1 m above a PEN 0.7 m deep). Numbers do not change. Tests: tests/test_inductive_solver_integration.py::test_perfect_mirror_warns_for_inductive_pairs_across_the_surface and siblings.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Engine.warn_segments (int | None, default None = diagnostics.SOFT_LIMIT, 5 000, read at solve time): the size of the soft notice "solve time may run from seconds to minutes" per engine, counted like max_segments (segments and nodal unknowns); honoured by the solve's pre-flight warning, check_segment_resolution and diagnose() (report.context["warn_segments"]). Not checked against max_segments (a notice above the hard limit never appears). Booleans rejected; kept by JSON, copies and the provenance (user decision Q31, finding 10.06). Tests: tests/test_resource_limit.py::test_warn_segments_is_a_validated_engine_field and four siblings.

docs.title: Stream d2gen: User decisions Q20, Q21: encased mesh braces, concrete_model deprecated
Changed
docs.text:
• ⚠ Mesh foundations: the cross-braces are encased (user decision Q20). A foundation earth electrode per DIN 18014 lies in the concrete together with its connections, so every wire of an encased FoundationElectrodeSpec(style="mesh") — the perimeter and the cross-braces — carries the outer radius \(r_b = r_a + t\) and the shell coefficient \(C\); up to now the braces stayed bare, and a foundation could not exceed the spreading resistance of its braces alone however dry the concrete. Without a shell nothing changes. See Numbers that change. Tests: tests/test_concrete_one_mechanism.py::test_mesh_braces_are_encased, ::test_encased_mesh_equals_the_assembly_of_its_wires, ::test_shell_of_a_mesh_foundation_spans_every_wire.
  • groundfield.generators.materialise.concrete_shell takes encased_length_m (the keyword perimeter_m of the earlier 2026.11 work is gone) and reports the shell resistance \(C/L\) over every encased wire.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text: • FoundationElectrodeSpec.concrete_model (user decision Q21). The field no longer selects a shell model; it only chooses one current owner ("lumped", the default) or one per side ("distributed") for an axis-aligned style="ring" rectangle, at most 0.16 % apart up to aspect ratio 4 and 0.67 % up to 50 over the soils of the AP1 grid, bare or in concrete of 30 to 1 000 Ω·m (0.06 % / 0.3 % for a bare ring in homogeneous soil). "distributed" keeps working and emits a DeprecationWarning at the user's line (constructor, model_validate, JSON, model_copy that sets it); "lumped" and the configuration JSON and pickles of 0.15.0 load silently; the generators do not repeat the warning. Drop the argument; removal no earlier than 2027.5. Tests: tests/test_foundation_owners.py.

docs.title: Stream d2soil: User decision Q36: effective-resistivity presets per electrode class
Added
docs.text: • Effective-resistivity presets per electrode class (user decision Q36). gf.effective_resistivity(soil, preset=...) takes the weights \((w_0, \beta)\) from the read-only mapping groundfield.soil.EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS, with the values of the AP2 hand-over (2026-10-20, AP1 catalogue computed with groundfield 0.14.0): "lv_network" (0.13, 0.8; the default, the AP1 calibration), "station" (0.06, 1.3; the station electrode alone) and "lv_group_<g>_p<pp>" for the four LV network groups (perimeter equivalent \(n_U\), thresholds 20 / 100 / 250) and 5 / 10 / 20 / 40 % foundation electrodes (method A, q50). An explicit w0 or beta replaces that weight only; an unknown name raises ValueError naming the closest presets. For the AP1 station in the 39 AP1 soils, \(R = c\,\rho_\text{eff}\) misses the field solution by a median 1.8 % and at most 15.7 % with "station" (hand-over: 1.7 %, 15.7 %), against 5.0 % and 35.9 % with "lv_network". Tests: tests/test_effective_resistivity.py (presets section, test_the_station_preset_reproduces_the_handover_for_the_ap1_station, test_the_documented_tables_hold_the_presets).

The IO reference example fits the station over \(\rho_\text{eff}\) with preset="station" (max_relative 7.48 % instead of 13.41 %); Soil reference, ADR-0008 (amendment item 5) and glossary describe the presets and that a BusType and its bus must use the same one.
