The models are quasi-static and validated for \(f < 1\,\mathrm{kHz}\): displacement currents in the soil and wave propagation along the conductors are neglected. Higher frequencies are accepted but outside the validated range.
  • A fault-current spectrum is combined as a true RMS value, \(U_\text{rms} = \sqrt{\sum_k \lvert\underline{U}_k\rvert^2}\) (touch_voltage_spectrum).

docs.title: Potentials, currents and signs
docs.text:
• Potential reference. Every potential is measured against remote earth, \(\varphi \to 0\) far from all electrodes. The soil surface is insulating (no current into the air).
  • Source current. A CurrentSource with magnitude \(I > 0\) and phase_deg \(= 0\) drives \(+I\) into the node attached_to and takes it back at return_to (or at remote earth).
  • Electrode currents. FieldResult.electrode_currents[name] is the current an electrode leaks into the soil: positive at the feeding earth, negative at the electrode that collects the current of a two-terminal source. With one source of \(+1\) A the potentials of the fed earthing system are positive (earth potential rise).
  • Impedances. Input, cluster and electrode impedance are defined in the quickstart; for a passive earthing system their real parts are positive.
  • Touch and step voltage. \(U_T = U_E - \varphi(\text{feet})\) and \(U_S = \varphi(\mathbf{r}_1) - \varphi(\mathbf{r}_1 + 1\,\mathrm{m}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}})\), complex phasors in V for the given source current; compare magnitudes with the permissible values.
  • When comparing with another tool or a measurement, check its sign convention for injected currents and node potentials.

docs.title: Material defaults
docs.text: Parameter Default Note wire radius of electrodes and conductors 5 mm wire_radius=0.005 conductor resistivity \(1.68\cdot10^{-8}\,\Omega\,\mathrm{m}\) copper relative permittivity of the soil stored, not used quasi-static model (InertConfigurationWarning when changed) magnetic permeability \(\mu_0 = 4\pi\cdot10^{-7}\,\mathrm{H/m}\) soil and conductors non-magnetic

docs.title: Warnings and errors
docs.text:
This page explains every warning and error that groundfield emits: when it appears, what it means for your result, and what to do. Look a message up here when a solve or a post-processing call warns; the how-to guide Read and act on warnings shows the workflow, and Known limitations gives the size of each limit behind a warning.

groundfield warns when a result is valid but limited, and raises when it cannot produce a meaningful result. Every warning class below is a subclass of UserWarning (except DeprecationWarning), so it can be filtered by category:

import warnings

import groundfield as gf

with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter("error", gf.UniformCurrentFieldWarning)   # make it fatal
    warnings.simplefilter("ignore", gf.ExperimentalBackendWarning)  # or silence it
    ...  # solve and post-process here

Warnings are attributed to the line of your code that caused them, not to the inside of the package; warnings that the package's own internal calls would trigger (for example a generator using an old keyword) are not shown, because you cannot act on them. Python shows a DeprecationWarning by default only for code in __main__ and in notebooks; run tests with -W error::DeprecationWarning to find deprecated names early. The page lists every warning and exception class defined in src/groundfield, then the plain UserWarnings, then the built-in exceptions with a fixed meaning.

Class Kind Typical cause BackendCapabilityError error the engine cannot represent the world BackendCapabilityWarning warning a documented simplification of a custom backend ExperimentalBackendWarning warning first solve with fem BackendOptionsWarning warning options for a backend that does not run ProbePointsIgnoredWarning warning probe_points of 0.15.0 code EngineFrequencyOrderWarning warning frequencies not increasing ShallowSegmentWarning warning point kernel, segment long against its depth PointKernelInterfaceWarning warning point kernel, wire next to the layer interface InterfaceContactWarning warning rod end or wire at a layer interface SeriesTruncationWarning warning image series cut at its cap SommerfeldConvergenceWarning warning layered quadrature not converged FemReductionWarning warning never emitted since 2026.11 ComplexImageFitWarning warning direct call of the old complex-image fit SommerfeldResolutionWarning warning Hankel quadrature out of nodes SommerfeldTailTruncationWarning warning tail of the reflected kernel not bounded DeprecationWarning warning deprecated name, keyword or alias InertConfigurationWarning warning a setting no backend reads CrossSectionUnitWarning warning cross section given in mm² DiagnosticsWarning warning the findings of diagnose(...).warn() MixedCoordinatesWarning warning projected and local coordinates mixed ResourceLimitError error too many segments, nodes or ports UniformCurrentFieldWarning warning image-family field values near grids and stars VectorFitQualityWarning warning vector fit misses its rms tolerance VectorFitConvergenceWarning warning poles still moving VectorFitUnderdeterminedWarning warning more poles than samples RhoFStandardQualityWarning warning standard form misses a sample NonPassiveFitWarning / NonPassiveFitError warning / error exported formula not passive RhoPresetMismatchWarning warning BusType fitted over another preset EvaluateSpecError error BusType document or formula rejected ResultFormatError error not a readable result file OverpassError error failed Overpass query

docs.title: BackendCapabilityError
docs.text:
gf.BackendCapabilityError, subclass of ValueError and NotImplementedError.

When: raised by Engine.solve before any numerics when the backend cannot represent the world: a number of soil layers it does not support (three or more distinct layers for every engine but mom_sommerfeld and fem), an explicitly requested kernel the backend does not implement (kernel="line" for the mom family), a world outside the axisymmetric model of fem with FemOptions.model="axisymmetric", a world the 3-D model of fem refuses before meshing (see the fem engine page), or a horizontal wire so close to the layer interface, on either side of it, that the point form cannot evaluate it (see PointKernelInterfaceWarning). solve_mutual_matrix and solve_mutual_field raise it for a backend outside the image family and for three or more layers. A backend registered by the user that declares no support for concrete shells, junctions or voltage sources raises it for such worlds; every built-in backend supports them.

What it means: nothing was computed. The message names the backends that can solve the world.

What to do: choose one of them (see the backend registry); three or more distinct layers need mom_sommerfeld.

docs.title: BackendCapabilityWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.solver.BackendCapabilityWarning.

When: emitted when the backend solves the world with a documented simplification: a backend without two-terminal sources returns the current of a source with return_to through remote earth.

What it means: the conductor network or the return terminal is simplified. No built-in backend emits it since 2026.11.

What to do: use an image or MoM backend when the conductor network or the return terminal matters.

Audit trail

Up to 2026.11 fem also treated distributed and inductive conductors as lumped resistive branches, with this warning.

docs.title: ExperimentalBackendWarning
docs.text:
gf.ExperimentalBackendWarning.

When: emitted once per process on the first solve with an experimental backend (fem).

What it means: fem is a reference backend whose model, options and results may still change between releases; its measured accuracy is on the fem engine page.

What to do: nothing; filter the category once you have read the limits of fem.

docs.title: BackendOptionsWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.solver.BackendOptionsWarning.

When: emitted when Engine.options configures a backend that will not run (for example options={"fem": ...} with backend="mom").

What it means: the options are ignored.

What to do: remove them or select that backend.

docs.title: ProbePointsIgnoredWarning
docs.text:
gf.ProbePointsIgnoredWarning (also groundfield.solver).

When: emitted by solve_mutual_matrix when it is given probe_points but computes the galerkin off-diagonal, the default of every call since 2026.11.

What it means: a call written for 0.15.0 (the AP1 pipeline, for example) keeps running and now returns the reciprocal galerkin matrix, which reproduces the solve of the clusters joined by branches; the probe matrix missed it by −0.15 … −0.88 % on an AP1-like site.

What to do: drop probe_points, or pass offdiag="probe" to keep the 0.15.0 definition.

Audit trail

Up to 0.15.0 probe points selected the potential at those points as the off-diagonal.

docs.title: EngineFrequencyOrderWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.solver.engine.EngineFrequencyOrderWarning.

When: emitted when Engine.frequencies is not strictly increasing.

What it means: the order is kept, and every result list follows it.

What to do: sort the list, or state the intent with engine.with_frequencies(..., preserve_order=True).

docs.title: ShallowSegmentWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.solver.ShallowSegmentWarning.

When: emitted for the point kernel only (kernel="point" and the mom family) when a leakage segment is longer than about four times its depth.

What it means: the self term uses the point image at distance \(2z\) instead of the image line, which overestimates it by more than 13 % and biases the impedance high. The message quantifies the worst case.

What to do: shorter segments, or the exact line kernel of the image family (the default), which has no such bias.

docs.title: PointKernelInterfaceWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.solver.PointKernelInterfaceWarning.

When: emitted for the point form (kernel="point" of the image family and of solve_mutual_*, the mom family) when a horizontal wire lies within 0.6 segment lengths of the layer interface \(h_1\), on either side of it. Closer than 0.387 segment lengths, or where the rule would reach above the surface, the solve raises BackendCapabilityError instead.

What it means: the impedance is biased low. With an electrode that reaches the interface (the cross-layer path) the three-point rule of the diagonal samples the layered correction where it varies quickly; with every wire above \(h_1\) the diagonal takes the image of a segment in the interface as a point source \(2\lvert z - h_1\rvert\) away, while its image line runs much closer to the wire. Measured: 3–17 % low on the cross-layer path, −2.5 % and −0.4 % for a ring 0.2 m above \(h_1\) (1000/30 and 30/1000 Ω·m, ds = 0.5 m).

What to do: the exact line kernel of the image family (the default), or segments shorter than the distance of the wire to the interface.

Audit trail

The refusal below 0.387 segment lengths follows audit A3S-02: a ring 1 µm above \(h_1\) read −1931 Ω where the line kernel gives 4.18 Ω.

docs.title: InterfaceContactWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.solver.InterfaceContactWarning.

When: emitted by every segment backend (the image family, mom, mom_sommerfeld), by solve_mutual_* and by the three-dimensional fem (both rules, once per rule and solve) where the thin-wire model, which carries the current on the wire axis, deviates from the solid wire next to a layer interface:

  • Rod ends: a rod head or tip within one wire radius of a layer interface. An end that meets the end of another rod — a rod split at the interface into two pieces, the usual way to give each layer its own piece — has no free end face and is not reported.
  • Horizontal wires: every electrode but a rod, and the leaking pieces of a galvanic distributed conductor, whose axis lies within the reach of a contrasting interface (table below). A piece of a galvanic distributed conductor counts as horizontal while its slope \(\lvert e_z\rvert\) is at most 0.1 (5.7°).

What it means: the result carries the thin-wire error next to the interface. The thin-wire model has no end face: a rod that ends exactly at the interface is a wire entirely on one side of it, and one that reaches past it by a fraction of its radius touches the other layer through a short part only, while the solid rod with a flat end is continuous in between. Against an axisymmetric model of the solid rod (4.5 m, \(a\) = 8 mm, 1000/30 Ω·m) the thin wire reads +21 % with its tip at the interface, +7 % 1 mm above it, −4.6 % 1 mm below it, and within a few per cent beyond two radii, as anywhere else. Next to a more conductive layer the current of a horizontal wire crowds to its near side, which a current on the axis cannot follow: against the solid torus a ring of \(a\) = 5 mm over a layer 33 times more conductive reads +0.59 % at 4 radii, +1.2 % at 3, +3.6 % at 2, +8.6 % at 1.5 and +32 % at 1.1 radii, and +89 % when the interface cuts the wire; under a more resistive layer up to +2.6 %.

Reach of the interface, wire axis to interface plane, in wire radii \(a\):

contrast of the layers more conductive beyond more resistive beyond 1.4 1.0 \(a\) 1.0 \(a\) 2 1.3 \(a\) (1.14 \(a\)) 3 1.9 \(a\) 1.3 \(a\) 5.5 2.7 \(a\) (1.60 \(a\)) 10 3.3 \(a\) 1.9 \(a\) 18 3.7 \(a\) (2.05 \(a\)) 33 3.9 \(a\) 2.2 \(a\) 100 4.1 \(a\) 2.2 \(a\) 1000 4.3 \(a\) 2.3 \(a\)

Log-linear in between, values in brackets interpolated; held beyond 1000, and at 1.0 \(a\) down to a contrast of 1.3; 1.0 \(a\): only a wire that the interface cuts. Below a contrast of 1.3 nothing is reported. The table is measured on rings with \(r_0/a \ge 18\); a thicker wire on a smaller ring is not covered. No generated network and no world of the AP1 soils (\(h_1\) = 5 or 30 m) comes within reach.

diagnose() reports both under interface_contact; with an fem engine it reports neither for a world that the axisymmetric model takes, which resolves rod end faces and ring wires.

What to do: keep rod ends and horizontal wires a few wire radii from a contrasting interface; bracket a rod end by moving it by ±2 wire radii; check a ring with fem's axisymmetric model (FemOptions.model="axisymmetric"), which solves the wire as the solid torus and does not warn.

How the reach was measured, and audit trail

The three-dimensional fem is a thin wire without end faces too: a rod tip on 1000/30 Ω·m reads +43 % there against the solid rod, with an error estimate of 6e-3 (audit W4R2A-03, since which it warns for rod ends). It shares the horizontal-wire limit as well (its smoothed line source lies between the thin wire and the torus). The horizontal-wire rule dates from 2026.11 (audits W4A-07, W4B-02, W4R2A-04 and W4R3A-02).

The solid torus is the axisymmetric fem; a Hankel thin ring plus the exact 2-D proximity correction agrees with it to 5e-4. The +2.6 % under a more resistive layer is a 55 mm wire on a 1 m ring at 1.01 radii, contrast 1000.

The reach is the distance of the wire axis from the interface inside which the thin wire (converged in its segment length) is 1 % or more off: the largest of five ring geometries (\(r_0/a\) = 18 … 400: rings of 0.5 … 5 m at 0.3 … 2 m depth, \(a\) = 5 … 55 mm; the more conductive layer below the wire, for the 2 m ring also above it; the more resistive layer below and above every one; a 55 mm wire on a 1 m ring is the widest at every contrast), rounded up to 0.1 \(a\), plus 0.1 \(a\) for the contrasts between the nodes — the resistive side from the converged thin wire, the conductive side from the thin wire at one segment length, its node at 1000 raised to 4.3 \(a\) so that the converged distances lie inside.

Checked at the nodes and between them (conductive 1.3 … 1.9, 2.5, 4, 7, 14, 25, 50, 300; resistive 2, 5.5, 18, 300): of 2348 conductive distances (the thin wire at one segment length) and 2470 resistive ones (converged in it) none with the thin wire 1 % or more off lies outside the reach, the largest errors outside it are +0.94 % and +0.93 %; converged, the thick wire's conductive 1 % distances lie 0.004 … 0.17 \(a\) inside the reach (the node at 1000 is 4.3 \(a\) for the 4.15 \(a\) at 300). Below a contrast of 1.3 a cut wire is at most +0.96 % off at 1.3 and +1.06 % at 1.35 (the thick wire cut 0.5 \(a\) below its axis by a more resistive layer above it).

Up to audit W4R2A-04 the table came from four geometries (0.2 … 0.4 \(a\) short of the thick wire on the 1 m ring) and started at a contrast of 2, below which a cut wire read up to −1.46 %; up to audit W4R3A-02 its resistive side was measured above the wire for the thin ring only (the thick wire 1 % off up to 0.74 \(a\) beyond it: +1.75 % at 1.3 \(a\) under a 33 times more resistive layer, unreported) and it started at 1.4 (+1.16 % there).

A steeper piece of a galvanic distributed conductor passes the reach of an interface over at most \(2\,\mathrm{reach}/\lvert e_z\rvert\) wire radii of its length, like a rod through an interface, and is not reported (a step at the cutoff, kept). That diagnose() reports nothing for a world of the axisymmetric fem is audit W4R2A-05.

docs.title: SeriesTruncationWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.solver.image_2layer.SeriesTruncationWarning (also in groundfield.solver.mom and groundfield.solver.mom_sommerfeld).

When: emitted when the Tagg/Sunde image series reaches Engine.image_max_terms before its tail bound \(\lvert K\rvert^{n+1}/(1-\lvert K\rvert)\) falls below image_series_tol, typically at very high layer contrast (\(\lvert K\rvert \to 1\)).

What it means: the image series is cut before its tolerance; the result is not converged in the series.

What to do: raise image_max_terms (the default 300 covers \(\lvert K\rvert = 0.94\)).

docs.title: SommerfeldConvergenceWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.solver.mom_sommerfeld.SommerfeldConvergenceWarning.

When: emitted when the quadrature of the reflected part of the layered Green's function does not converge to epsrel. The message names the worst pair and the cause.

What it means: the value may even have the wrong sign.

What to do: raise max_osc_panels in Engine(options={"mom_sommerfeld": {...}}) for kilometre separations with thin layers; at a layer contrast \(\lvert K\rvert \to 1\) in two-layer soil use image_2layer.

docs.title: FemReductionWarning
docs.text:
gf.FemReductionWarning.

When: never emitted since 2026.11: fem solves a conforming finite-element model (user decision Q37) instead of the equivalent-hemisphere reduction.

What it means: the class is kept importable for filters of older code.

What to do: none needed; remove filters for this category when convenient. The conforming model and its guards are on the fem engine page.

Audit trail: the reduction up to 2026.11

Up to 2026.11 it was emitted once per fem solve, listing the reasons, when the reduction did not represent the world: several electrodes in a cluster (mutual resistance neglected; −35 % for a ring with three rods, −55 … −75 % for two bonded rods of which one reaches into a conductive top layer), several clusters (no coupling between them), or a layer interface within the hemisphere radius or the electrode's horizontal extent over a layer that the electrodes touch or that conducts no better than theirs (−3 … +48 % measured for a spanned layer, −17 … +16 % for one within the extent; −44 … −78 % for a rod that reaches 1 µm … 8 cm into a conductive top layer, −21 … +30 % for a ring lying exactly on the interface; −10 … +46 % for a more conductive layer within the extent behind one that conducts no better than the electrodes', audit R2A-09). A layer that no electrode touches, that conducts better than the electrodes' layer and whose top lies above the hemisphere radius or the horizontal half-extent (below the hemisphere: with no such shielding layer in between) was no warning but a BackendCapabilityError (user decision Q23 and audit D2A-03: fem misplaced the current, mostly far too low), as were electrodes touching a layer the hemisphere does not reach, a strip deeper than half its length, a ring deeper than its diameter and a driven MeshElectrode (the closed forms outside their range).

docs.title: ComplexImageFitWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.solver.cim.ComplexImageFitWarning.

When: emitted only by a direct call of groundfield.solver.cim.fit_complex_images when the complex-image fit misses its tolerance. The cim backend no longer fits (it is a deprecated alias of image).

What it means: the fitted images do not reproduce the layered kernel to the requested tolerance.

What to do: do not use the fit as a Green's function.

docs.title: SommerfeldResolutionWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.coupling.layered_green.SommerfeldResolutionWarning (also raised by coupling.sommerfeld_inductance).

When: emitted when the Hankel quadrature cannot place enough nodes per oscillation of \(J_0(\lambda s)\) within its node budget — for example a conductor longer than the spectral range of the earth-return quadrature (see Known limitations).

What it means: the result would not be converged.

What to do: lower lambda_max_factor (no accuracy is lost: the truncated tail is added in closed form) or reduce the distance range of the group.

docs.title: SommerfeldTailTruncationWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.coupling.layered_green.SommerfeldTailTruncationWarning.

When: emitted when the reflected kernel needs more closed-form image terms than its budget to bound the truncated tail of the quadrature (a very wide range of horizontal distances in one group, typically pairs near the surface or the layer interface).

What it means: the value is then not bounded by the documented tolerance.

What to do: lower lambda_max_factor (fewer image terms are then needed) or reduce the horizontal distance range of the group.

docs.title: DeprecationWarning
docs.text:
When: emitted for every deprecated name, keyword, JSON key or backend alias.

What it means: the name still works; the message names the replacement and the earliest removal (2027.5).

What to do: see Deprecations.

docs.title: InertConfigurationWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.utils.InertConfigurationWarning.

When: emitted when a public setting is stored but read by no backend: a non-default BoundaryConditions field or a soil relative_permittivity (also in the generator soil specs).

What it means: the setting has no effect. Every backend uses the quasi-static conduction-current model with remote earth as reference.

What to do: remove the setting.

docs.title: CrossSectionUnitWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.conductors.CrossSectionUnitWarning.

When: emitted for a conductor cross_section above 10⁻² m².

What it means: almost always a value in mm² (50 instead of 50e-6), which would make the conductor a near-ideal short.

What to do: give the cross section in m².

docs.title: DiagnosticsWarning
docs.text:
gf.DiagnosticsWarning.

When: emitted by diagnose(...).warn(): one aggregated warning with all findings, one line per cause (mixed coordinates, thin-wire ratio, resolution, problem size, close or interpenetrating wires, overlapping inductive conductors, rod ends and horizontal wires next to a layer interface, inert settings, series truncation).

What it means: the solve emits the discretisation findings as individual warnings; this class collects them before a solve.

What to do: follow the advice in each line; see Diagnostics.

docs.title: MixedCoordinatesWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.diagnostics.MixedCoordinatesWarning.

When: emitted once per solve by the image family, mom, mom_sommerfeld, fem and solve_mutual_*, before anything is discretised, when points of the world lie both within 10 km of the origin and beyond 1000 km from it (horizontal distance): electrodes at projected (UTM, Gauss–Krüger) coordinates and a node or electrode near (0, 0), almost always given in the wrong system by mistake.

What it means: the world is solved as given, its two groups some 33 000 km apart; the message names both groups and the conductors between them. Measured with a 12 m × 7 m outline and a 3 m rod at UTM coordinates: a return rod given at local (80, 15) m raises \(Z_{in}\) by 0.43 %; a PEN cable to a cabinet at local coordinates is 33 118 km long, \(Z_{in}\) = 7494 + j25 396 Ω instead of 5.39 + j0.19 Ω at 50 Hz with carson_series, and the default sommerfeld earth return does not finish.

What to do: give every point in one coordinate system; to stop such a solve at once, warnings.simplefilter("error", MixedCoordinatesWarning). diagnose() reports the same world under coordinates (a warning), and a world wider than 100 km that does not mix as information. A world wholly in projected or wholly in local coordinates never warns.

Audit trail

The warning and the check of fem at the solve date from 2026.11 (user decision D5); the measurements are those of audit W2B-04.

docs.title: ResourceLimitError
docs.text:
gf.ResourceLimitError, subclass of ValueError.

When: raised before any allocation when the predicted number of segments, or of unknowns of the dense nodal system, exceeds the engine's limit Engine.max_segments (default groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT, 20 000), by every segment backend and by solve_mutual_matrix / solve_mutual_field. fem checks the display segments that carry the point sources of its result against Engine.max_segments too, and limits its mesh by FemOptions.max_nodes (axisymmetric, about 4 GB per million nodes) and max_nodes_3d (3-D; the solve adds about 2.9 GB per million nodes, 3.0 … 3.1 GB with the process), estimated before anything is assembled, and the ports of its 3-D model by max_ports_3d (100), checked before meshing.

What it means: nothing was allocated. The usual cause is a geometry given in millimetres, a very small segment_length or a conductor discretize_segment_length in millimetres.

What to do: check units and segment lengths; to solve a large world on purpose, raise the limit of the engine, Engine(max_segments=...) (or the FemOptions limit). Below that limit, a world at or above the engine's notice size (Engine(warn_segments=...), default SOFT_LIMIT = 5 000) only emits the UserWarning "budget: ..." that the solve may take minutes; the notice comes from Engine.solve (with any backend), not from solve_mutual_matrix / solve_mutual_field. Both sizes count the segments of the integral engines.

docs.title: UniformCurrentFieldWarning
docs.text:
gf.UniformCurrentFieldWarning.

When: emitted once per call by touch_voltage, step_voltage, touch_voltage_envelope, touch_voltage_at_part and touch_voltage_spectrum when a result of the image family (one uniform current per straight wire of an electrode) is evaluated within 5 m (NEAR_FIELD_DISTANCE_M) of a grid, mesh, star, strip, open polyline or bonded multi-electrode cluster. Without the world the point sources of the result stand in for the wires.

What it means: the real current crowds to edges and tips, so the field values there are impedance-grade, not field-grade (against mom: a 20 m grid corner +6 % in the touch voltage 1 m outside and −8 % in the step from 1 m to 2 m outside; see Known limitations).

What to do: re-solve with backend="mom" for those quantities.

docs.title: VectorFitQualityWarning
docs.text:
gf.VectorFitQualityWarning.

When: emitted when the relative rms error of a vector fit exceeds rms_tol (1 %), or when the imaginary part of a 0 Hz sample had to be discarded.

What it means: the fitted model misses the samples by more than the tolerance.

What to do: inspect rms_relative; try another n_poles, more samples or weighting="inverse_magnitude".

docs.title: VectorFitConvergenceWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.fit.VectorFitConvergenceWarning.

When: emitted when the poles still move by more than 1 % after n_iter relocation steps.

What it means: the poles are not converged.

What to do: more iterations, another n_poles, or a different weighting.

docs.title: VectorFitUnderdeterminedWarning
docs.text:
groundfield.fit.VectorFitUnderdeterminedWarning.

When: emitted when n_poles is not smaller than the number of samples.

What it means: the fit only interpolates.

What to do: fewer poles or more frequencies.

docs.title: RhoFStandardQualityWarning
docs.text:
gf.RhoFStandardQualityWarning.

When: emitted when the standard-form fit misses a sample by more than max_relative_tol (5 %).

What it means: the fixed ansatz cannot represent the sampled \(Z(\rho, f)\).

What to do: check max_relative, restrict the \(\rho\) range, or fit per \(\rho\) with vector fitting.

docs.title: NonPassiveFitWarning / NonPassiveFitError
docs.text:
gf.NonPassiveFitWarning, gf.NonPassiveFitError (subclass of ValueError).

When: emitted (or raised, with require_passive=True) when the exported impedance formula has \(\operatorname{Re}Z < 0\) somewhere between 0 Hz and twice the highest fitted frequency.

What it means: the formula is not passive there; the message names the frequency (and \(\rho\)) of the most negative value.

What to do: refit (fewer poles, different weighting) before exporting.

docs.title: RhoPresetMismatchWarning
docs.text:
gf.RhoPresetMismatchWarning (also groundfield.io).

When: emitted by evaluate_spec and bustype_from_spec when the caller names the preset of its bus (rho_preset=...) and the document records a different one in metadata["rho_preset"].

What it means: the rho of the bus then means another resistivity than the rho of the formula (see the effective resistivity in Known limitations).

What to do: evaluate the BusType with the preset it was fitted over, or refit it over the preset of your bus.

Audit trail

The preset record is user decision Q39.

docs.title: EvaluateSpecError
docs.text:
gf.EvaluateSpecError, subclass of ValueError.

When: raised by evaluate_spec, load_bustype_json and BusTypeSpec.from_dict when a BusType document or its formula is rejected: not a BusTypeSpec, empty formula, unknown symbol, or a formula outside the allowed grammar or its size bounds.

What it means: the parser never evaluates the text; its own groundfield.io._formula.FormulaError arrives wrapped in this class.

What to do: regenerate the document with save_bustype_json, or fix the formula by hand.

docs.title: ResultFormatError
docs.text:
gf.ResultFormatError, subclass of ValueError.

When: raised by load_result for a file that is not a readable result file: wrong format, a newer schema_version, invalid JSON or UTF-8, or metadata outside what the writer produces.

What it means: the file is not loaded.

What to do: load it with the groundfield version that wrote it (written_by), or regenerate it.

gf.OverpassError, subclass of RuntimeError.

What it means: the answer is not cached.

What to do: retry later, reduce the radius, or work from a cached / stored answer.

docs.title: Top-level namespace
docs.text:
import groundfield as gf loads the data model, the factories and the engine. Everything else is imported on first use, so the import stays light (no pandas, matplotlib or most of scipy until a function needs them). Every name of groundfield.__all__ is available under its flat name (gf.touch_voltage) and is the same object as the one of its home module (groundfield.postprocess.safety.touch_voltage), documented once, on the page of that module. The post-processing API is also grouped in curated namespaces:

Namespace Content Page gf.plot potential maps and profiles, world geometry, current sharing, sweeps, convergence Postprocess gf.safety touch and step voltage, touch points (touch_voltage_at_part), EN 50522 permissible touch voltage Postprocess gf.fit rho-f models: vector fitting and the research standard form Postprocess gf.io BusType export to groundinsight, CSV, VTK, result files IO, Result files 
import groundfield as gf
from groundfield.references import dwight1936

world = gf.create_world(soil=gf.HomogeneousSoil(rho=100.0))
gf.create_electrode(world, "rod", name="g1", position=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), length=3.0)
gf.create_source(world, attached_to="g1", magnitude=1.0)
result = gf.create_engine(frequencies=[50.0]).solve(world)

Z = result.input_impedance()[0]                      # 35.99 Ω
R_dwight = dwight1936.rod(rho=100.0, length=3.0, radius=0.005)
assert abs(Z.real - R_dwight) / R_dwight < 1e-3      # Dwight (1936): 35.99 Ω
assert gf.safety.touch_voltage is gf.touch_voltage   # same function, two names

docs.title: What counts as public
docs.text: The public API is the __all__ list of groundfield and of every module whose dotted path has no part that starts with an underscore. tests/test_docs_api_coverage.py checks that each of these names is rendered on one of the pages above and has a docstring summary, that every public function documents its parameters and its return value, and that every public method has a docstring. Modules with a leading underscore (groundfield.solver._kernels, …) are internal and are not documented here.

__version__ = '2026.11.0'

Version of the installed package (calendar versioning since 2026.11, ADR-0013).

docs.title: Boundary conditions
docs.text: BoundaryConditions records the boundary conditions of the field problem on the World. Every backend implements the same set — remote earth as the potential reference and an insulating soil surface — so the fields exist for documentation and forward compatibility only. A non-default value is stored but read by no backend and warns with InertConfigurationWarning.

docs.title: Mathematical and physical context
docs.text:
Below 1 kHz the displacement current in the soil is negligible, the leakage current density follows Ohm's law \(\mathbf{J} = -\sigma abla\varphi\), and charge conservation \( abla\cdot\mathbf{J} = 0\) gives

\[ abla\cdot igl(\sigma(\mathbf{r})\, abla\varphi(\mathbf{r}) igr) = 0 , \]

Laplace's equation \( abla^2\varphi = 0\) inside every homogeneous layer. The injected currents are not a volume source; they enter through the electrode surfaces. A well-posed problem needs three conditions, which are the three fields of this model:

Field Value used by every backend Meaning far_field "dirichlet" \(\varphi o 0\) for \(\lvert\mathbf{r} vert o \infty\): remote earth is the reference of every potential surface "neumann" \(\partial\varphi/\partial z = 0\) at \(z = 0\): no current into the air; realised by the mirror image at \(z o -z\) reference_node None the datum is remote earth

At an interface between layers \(\varphi\) and the normal current density \(\sigma\,\partial_n\varphi\) are continuous; the layered Green's functions of the solvers satisfy these conditions, not this model.

Validity. Linear, isotropic, piecewise homogeneous soil in the quasi-static regime. The inductive coupling of conductors (and its earth-return correction) is a separate branch impedance of the conductor network, not part of this electrostatic-type boundary-value problem.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import warnings

import groundfield as gf
from groundfield.utils import InertConfigurationWarning

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    boundary = gf.BoundaryConditions(surface="dirichlet")   # stored, not used
assert [w.category for w in caught] == [InertConfigurationWarning]
world = gf.create_world(soil=gf.HomogeneousSoil(rho=100.0), boundary=boundary)

World.set_boundary_conditions(...) stores a changed value as well and warns with a plain UserWarning, also when a value is set back to the default.

docs.title: boundary
docs.text:
Boundary conditions for the field computation.

The boundary configuration bundles the assumptions imposed at the boundary of the computational domain:

  • far_field: behaviour at infinity (Dirichlet \(\varphi = 0\), Neumann \(\partial_n \varphi = 0\)). For grounding systems, Dirichlet at infinity is the standard assumption ("remote earth").
  • surface: condition at the soil surface (\(z = 0\)). Default is Neumann (no current flow into the air).
  • reference_node: optional reference node that fixes the zero point of the potential.
Implementation status

No backend reads these fields (checked for image, image_2layer, image_nlayer, cim, mom, mom_sommerfeld, bem and fem: a world with every field set to a non-default value solves bit-identically, see tests/test_boundary_conditions.py). Every backend imposes the defaults implicitly:

  • far_field = "dirichlet" through the \(1/r\) decay of the Green's function (the potential vanishes at remote earth);
  • surface = "neumann" through the air-side image charge at \(z \to -z\) (the fem backend through its natural boundary condition);
  • reference_node is never consulted; all potentials are reported relative to remote earth (\(\varphi \to 0\) at infinity).

The fields are accepted and round-trip through serialisation for forward compatibility. Setting a non-default value warns with InertConfigurationWarning — when the model is constructed (directly, via groundfield.create_world() or from a world JSON) and in groundfield.world.World.set_boundary_conditions().

docs.text:

Attributes:

Name Type Description far_field Literal['dirichlet', 'neumann']

Condition at infinity. "dirichlet" (default): φ → 0 at remote earth. Not read by any backend.

surface Literal['neumann', 'dirichlet']

Condition at the soil surface z = 0. "neumann" (default): no current flows into the air. Not read by any backend.

reference_node str | None

Name of an electrode whose potential would define zero. Not read by any backend: potentials are always relative to remote earth.

When a field is set to a value other than the implemented default (see the module docstring).

docs.title: Conductors
docs.text: A Conductor connects two nodes of the network (electrodes or junctions) or two points: a PEN conductor of a low-voltage network, a cable screen, a bare bonding wire, an overhead earth wire or a measurement lead. Unlike an electrode it is not an equipotential body: it has a series impedance, and depending on its settings it carries inductance and leaks current into the soil along its length.

docs.title: Mathematical and physical context
docs.text:
A conductor of length \(\ell\), wire radius \(a\), material resistivity \(\rho_\text{mat}\) and cross section \(A\) is a branch of the nodal system with

\[ Z_b(\omega) = R + j\omega L_\text{Neumann} + \Delta Z_\text{earth}(\omega), \qquad R = \rho_\text{mat}\,\ell / A , \]

where \(L_\text{Neumann}\) (self and mutual, from the segment geometry) and the earth-return correction \(\Delta Z_\text{earth}\) (Carson or Sommerfeld) are assembled in Coupling when the conductor sets inductance_model="neumann". The settings that decide the model:

Field Values Meaning cross_section None (default) ideal connection: both end nodes form one galvanic cluster float (m²) or "from_radius" (\(\pi a^2\)) finite resistance \(R = \rho_\text{mat}\ell/A\) lumped_series_resistance_ohm Ω replaces the geometric \(R\) discretize_segment_length m distributed conductor: a chain of branches with this segment length (needs a finite resistance) coupling_to_soil "isolated" (default), "galvanic" insulated cable, or bare wire that leaks along its length like an electrode inductance_model None (default), "neumann" resistive branch only, or Neumann inductance with the engine's earth-return model (Engine.earth_inductive_model) resistance_model "dc" (default), "skin" \(R\) at every frequency, or the exact internal impedance of a solid round wire (Bessel functions)

Units. Lengths and radii in m, cross_section in m² (95 mm² is 95e-6), resistivity in Ω·m (copper 1.68e-8, the default). A cross section above MAX_PLAUSIBLE_CROSS_SECTION (10⁻² m²) warns with CrossSectionUnitWarning, because a value given in mm² would otherwise be a silent near-ideal short.

Skin effect. With resistance_model="skin" the internal impedance per unit length is

\[ Z'_\text{int} = \frac{k\,\rho_\text{mat}}{2\pi a}\,\frac{I_0(ka)}{I_1(ka)}, \qquad k = \sqrt{j\omega\mu_0/\rho_\text{mat}} \]

(Schelkunoff 1934), which tends to \(\rho_\text{mat}/(\pi a^2) + j\omega\mu_0/(8\pi)\) at low frequency. Below 1 kHz the effect matters only for thick conductors: the skin depth of copper at 1 kHz is about 2 mm.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import groundfield as gf

world = gf.create_world(soil=gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=100.0, rho_2=500.0, h_1=1.0))
gf.create_electrode(world, "ring", name="g1", center=(0.0, 0.0, 0.8), radius=3.0)
gf.create_electrode(world, "ring", name="g2", center=(40.0, 0.0, 0.8), radius=3.0)

pen = gf.create_conductor(
    world, name="pen_1", start="g1", end="g2",
    conductor_type="pen",
    cross_section=95e-6,             # 95 mm² in m²
    discretize_segment_length=2.0,   # distributed: about 20 inductive segments
    inductance_model="neumann",      # with the engine's earth-return model
)
assert abs(pen.length - 40.0) < 1e-12   # m, from (3, 0, 0.8) on g1 to (43, 0, 0.8) on g2
assert abs(pen.series_resistance - 1.68e-8 * 40.0 / 95e-6) < 1e-15   # 7.1 mΩ

The conductor object is geometry and material only; the earth-return model is chosen on the engine (earth_inductive_model, default "sommerfeld"), so the same world can be solved with different earth-return models. The theory is on the earth return page.

find_close_wires and find_close_conductors report pairs of wires that are closer than the thin-wire model allows (interpenetrating, crossing or very close); diagnose runs them before a solve.

docs.title: conductors
docs.text:
Conductors, PEN, and cable shields.

Subpackage for all current-carrying elements above and inside the soil that are not electrodes themselves but still take part in the current distribution:

  • overhead lines (phase conductor, earth wire),
  • cables (phase + shield, concentric or three-core),
  • PEN conductors in TN low-voltage networks,
  • auxiliary electrodes for grounding measurements.
Contents

Conductor Single conductor segment with end-point coordinates and a type tag ("pen", "cable_shield", "bare_copper", "overhead", "generic"), its series resistance and — with resistance_model="skin" — its frequency-dependent internal impedance. ConductorType, ResistanceModel Literal unions of the supported type tags and resistance models. CrossSectionUnitWarning Raised for cross sections that look like mm² entered as m². solid_round_internal_impedance Exact internal impedance per unit length of a solid round wire (skin effect). find_close_wires, find_close_conductors, WireProximity Detection of close, interpenetrating and crossing wire pairs.

Notes

Carson corrections for the earth-return path are not computed here; they enter via groundfield.coupling. This keeps the conductor model purely geometric and material-based, so it can be combined with different earth-return models.

docs.title: ConductorType module-attribute
docs.text:
ConductorType = Literal['pen', 'cable_shield', 'bare_copper', 'overhead', 'generic']

Kind of a conductor (Conductor.conductor_type).

  • "pen": PEN conductor of a low-voltage network;
  • "cable_shield": cable shield, a thin-walled tube around its core (user decisions Q32 / Q33);
  • "bare_copper": bare copper wire;
  • "overhead": overhead line or earth wire;
  • "generic": fallback.

docs.title: MAX_PLAUSIBLE_CROSS_SECTION module-attribute
docs.text:
MAX_PLAUSIBLE_CROSS_SECTION = 0.01

Largest cross section in m² accepted without a warning (100 cm²).

Real conductors stay far below it; a value in mm² does not.

docs.title: ResistanceModel module-attribute
docs.text:
ResistanceModel = Literal['dc', 'skin']

Series-resistance model of a conductor (Conductor.resistance_model).

  • "dc": rho * L / A at every frequency (the default);
  • "skin": the exact internal impedance of a solid round wire (Bessel solution).

docs.title: Conductor
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Wire segment between two points.

Attributes:

Name Type Description name str

Unique name within the World.

start, end

Start and end point (x, y, z) in metres. z > 0 puts the conductor inside the soil, z < 0 above ground.

start_electrode, end_electrode

Optional name of the electrode anchored at start / end. If both are set, the solver inserts this conductor as a branch in the nodal analysis: ideal (cross_section=None) → hard cluster constraint, finite section → branch with \(R_\text{ser} = \rho L / A\).

conductor_type ConductorType

Type tag from ConductorType. "cable_shield" marks the shield of a concentric cable, a thin-walled tube (user decisions Q32 and Q33 of 2026.11): with inductance_model="neumann" a thinner conductor drawn on its axis, inside it, is its core and couples to it at the shield radius (the geometric mean distance of a point inside a tube), and its self inductance carries no internal inductance of a solid wire. Two conductors of other types on one axis are separate conductors that touch. The other tags only select plot styles.

wire_radius float

Wire radius in metres. Default 5 mm. Used for the geometric thin-wire approximation in the segment self-action and as a fallback for cross_section when the latter is given as "from_radius".

resistivity float

Material resistivity in \(\Omega\,\mathrm{m}\). Default: copper (1.68e-8).

cross_section float | Literal['from_radius'] | None

Conductor cross section in \(\mathrm{m}^2\). None (default) means ideal galvanic short — the conductor is a zero-impedance bridge. A finite value enables the nodal-analysis branch model with \(R_\text{ser} = \rho_\text{mat}\, L / A\). The string "from_radius" is a convenience shortcut for \(A = \pi r_\text{wire}^2\).

docs.title: effective_cross_section property
docs.text:
effective_cross_section: float | None

Resolved cross section in \(\mathrm{m}^2\) or None.

Returns:

Type Description float or None

None when cross_section is None (ideal-galvanic mode). Otherwise the explicit cross section in m² ("from_radius" resolved to \(\pi\, r_\text{wire}^2\)).

docs.title: is_distributed property
docs.text:
is_distributed: bool

True iff the conductor is split into sub-segments.

A distributed conductor has a finite discretize_segment_length — the solver builds one longitudinal segment per sub-piece. False keeps the conductor lumped (single branch between the two end electrodes).

docs.title: is_shield property
docs.text:
is_shield: bool

Whether the conductor is a cable shield ("cable_shield").

A shield is a thin-walled tube: no internal inductance of a solid wire, and a thinner conductor on its axis is its core (user decisions Q32 and Q33 of 2026.11).

docs.title: length property
docs.text:
length: float

Euclidean length of the conductor in m.

docs.title: n_segments property
docs.text:
n_segments: int

Number of segments produced by the discretiser.

Returns 1 for a lumped conductor. Otherwise \(n = \lceil L / \Delta s \rceil\) with \(L\) the Euclidean length and $\Delta s = $ discretize_segment_length, with the round-off allowance of the electrode wires (_segment_count()): a conductor that exceeds a whole number of pieces only through the round-off of its end points gets no extra piece. Up to the calendar release the count had no allowance, so a 60 m counterpoise in 10 m pieces got 7 instead of 6 at projected (UTM) coordinates, where its computed length is 60.0000000012 m.

docs.title: series_resistance property
docs.text:
series_resistance: float

Series DC resistance \(R_\text{ser}\) in Ω.

Resolution order:

  1. If lumped_series_resistance_ohm is set (ADR-0012 V1 concrete-shell path or any user-supplied lumped override), return that value verbatim.
  2. Otherwise compute the geometric formula \(R = \rho_\text{mat}\, L / A\) from resistivity, length and effective_cross_section.
  3. If cross_section is None, the conductor is in the ideal-galvanic-short branch and the series resistance is 0.0.

Returns:

Type Description float

Total series resistance in Ω consumed by the solver's distributed-conductor model (ADR-0003).

docs.title: internal_impedance_per_length
docs.text:
internal_impedance_per_length(frequency: float | ndarray) -> complex | np.ndarray

Internal series impedance per unit length in Ω/m.

The conductor's own longitudinal impedance \(Z'_\text{int} = R'(f) + j\omega L'_\text{int}(f)\), excluding the external (thin-wire / earth-return) inductance of groundfield.coupling.

  • resistance_model="dc": \(R' = R_\text{ser}/L\) and the uniform-current internal inductance \(\mu_0/(8\pi)\) — the convention of groundfield.coupling.inductance.thin_wire_self_inductance() with include_internal=True; a "cable_shield" (a thin-walled tube) has none (user decision Q33). An ideal conductor has \(R' = 0\).
  • resistance_model="skin": the exact solid-round Bessel solution for the radius \(\sqrt{A/\pi}\) of the conducting cross section (solid_round_internal_impedance()).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default frequency float | ndarray

Frequency in Hz (scalar or array, >= 0).

required

Returns:

Type Description complex or ndarray

Internal impedance per unit length in Ω/m.

Source code in src/groundfield/conductors/conductor.py 
def internal_impedance_per_length(
    self, frequency: float | np.ndarray
) -> complex | np.ndarray:
    r"""Internal series impedance per unit length in Ω/m.

    The conductor's own longitudinal impedance $Z'_\text{int} =
    R'(f) + j\omega L'_\text{int}(f)$, excluding the external
    (thin-wire / earth-return) inductance of
    :mod:`groundfield.coupling`.

    - ``resistance_model="dc"``: $R' = R_\text{ser}/L$ and the
      uniform-current internal inductance $\mu_0/(8\pi)$ — the
      convention of
      :func:`groundfield.coupling.inductance.thin_wire_self_inductance`
      with ``include_internal=True``; a ``"cable_shield"`` (a
      thin-walled tube) has none (user decision Q33). An ideal
      conductor has $R' = 0$.
    - ``resistance_model="skin"``: the exact solid-round Bessel
      solution for the radius $\sqrt{A/\pi}$ of the conducting
      cross section
      (:func:`~groundfield.conductors.skin.solid_round_internal_impedance`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    frequency
        Frequency in Hz (scalar or array, ``>= 0``).

    Returns
    -------
    complex or np.ndarray
        Internal impedance per unit length in Ω/m.
    """
    f = np.asarray(frequency, dtype=float)
    if np.any(f < 0.0) or not np.all(np.isfinite(f)):
        raise ValueError("frequency must be finite and >= 0")
    if self.resistance_model == "skin":
        area = self.effective_cross_section
        assert area is not None  # guaranteed by the validator
        return solid_round_internal_impedance(
            frequency,
            radius=math.sqrt(area / math.pi),
            resistivity=self.resistivity,
        )
    length = self.length
    r_per_m = self.series_resistance / length if length > 0.0 else 0.0
    l_int = 0.0 if self.is_shield else _MU_0 / (8.0 * math.pi)
    z = r_per_m + 1j * 2.0 * math.pi * f * l_int
    if np.ndim(frequency) == 0:
        return complex(z)
    return z

docs.title: is_ideal
docs.text:
is_ideal(threshold: float = _IDEAL_RESISTANCE_THRESHOLD) -> bool

Return True when the conductor acts as a galvanic short.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default threshold float

Resistance threshold in Ω. Conductors at or below this value are treated as ideal by the solver. Default 1e-6 Ω.

_IDEAL_RESISTANCE_THRESHOLD Source code in src/groundfield/conductors/conductor.py 
def is_ideal(self, threshold: float = _IDEAL_RESISTANCE_THRESHOLD) -> bool:
    """Return ``True`` when the conductor acts as a galvanic short.

    Parameters
    ----------
    threshold
        Resistance threshold in Ω. Conductors at or below this
        value are treated as ideal by the solver. Default
        ``1e-6 Ω``.
    """
    if self.cross_section is None:
        return True
    return self.series_resistance <= threshold

docs.title: skin_correction_per_length
docs.text:
skin_correction_per_length(frequency: float | ndarray) -> complex | np.ndarray

Skin-effect correction to the DC convention, in Ω/m.

\(\Delta Z' = Z'_\text{int}(f) - [R'_\text{dc} + j\omega\mu_0/(8\pi)]\): what a solver that assembles \(R_\text{dc}\) and the DC internal inductance (include_internal=True) has to add per metre of branch length. Zero for resistance_model="dc".

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default frequency float | ndarray

Frequency in Hz (scalar or array, >= 0).

required

Returns:

Type Description complex or ndarray

Correction per unit length in Ω/m.

Source code in src/groundfield/conductors/conductor.py 
def skin_correction_per_length(
    self, frequency: float | np.ndarray
) -> complex | np.ndarray:
    r"""Skin-effect correction to the DC convention, in Ω/m.

    $\Delta Z' = Z'_\text{int}(f) - [R'_\text{dc} + j\omega\mu_0/(8\pi)]$:
    what a solver that assembles $R_\text{dc}$ and the DC internal
    inductance (``include_internal=True``) has to add per metre of
    branch length. Zero for ``resistance_model="dc"``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    frequency
        Frequency in Hz (scalar or array, ``>= 0``).

    Returns
    -------
    complex or np.ndarray
        Correction per unit length in Ω/m.
    """
    f = np.asarray(frequency, dtype=float)
    if np.any(f < 0.0) or not np.all(np.isfinite(f)):
        raise ValueError("frequency must be finite and >= 0")
    if self.resistance_model == "dc":
        return 0j if np.ndim(frequency) == 0 else np.zeros(f.shape, dtype=complex)
    area = self.effective_cross_section
    assert area is not None
    z = self.internal_impedance_per_length(frequency)
    z_dc = self.resistivity / area + 1j * 2.0 * math.pi * f * _MU_0 / (
        8.0 * math.pi
    )
    if np.ndim(frequency) == 0:
        return complex(z - z_dc)
    return z - z_dc

docs.title: CrossSectionUnitWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

A conductor cross section is implausibly large for m².

Conductor.cross_section is in m². A value above MAX_PLAUSIBLE_CROSS_SECTION almost always means the value was given in mm² (50 instead of 50e-6), which turns the conductor into an ideal short (series resistance in the nΩ range). Silence with warnings.simplefilter("ignore", CrossSectionUnitWarning) when a huge cross section is intended (e.g. a deliberate near-ideal bond).

def find_close_conductors(
    conductors: Iterable[Conductor],
    *,
    rel_threshold: float = 5.0,
    abs_threshold: float = 0.0,
    include_junctions: bool = False,
) -> list[WireProximity]:
    """:func:`find_close_wires` for :class:`~groundfield.conductors.Conductor` objects.

    Every conductor is one straight wire from ``start`` to ``end`` with
    its ``wire_radius``; pairs are reported by conductor name.

    Parameters
    ----------
    conductors
        Conductors, e.g. ``world.conductors``.
    rel_threshold, abs_threshold, include_junctions
        See :func:`find_close_wires`.

    Returns
    -------
    list of WireProximity
        Close / interpenetrating / crossing conductor pairs, worst
        first.
    """
    conds = list(conductors)
    if len(conds) < 2:
        return []
    ep = np.array([[c.start, c.end] for c in conds], dtype=float)
    radii = np.array([c.wire_radius for c in conds], dtype=float)
    names = [c.name for c in conds]
    return find_close_wires(
        ep,
        radii,
        names,
        rel_threshold=rel_threshold,
        abs_threshold=abs_threshold,
        include_junctions=include_junctions,
    )

def find_close_wires(
    endpoints: np.ndarray,
    radii: Sequence[float] | np.ndarray,
    names: Sequence[str],
    *,
    rel_threshold: float = 5.0,
    abs_threshold: float = 0.0,
    include_junctions: bool = False,
) -> list[WireProximity]:
    r"""Find segment pairs of different owners that are too close.

    Parameters
    ----------
    endpoints
        Segment end points, shape ``(K, 2, 3)``, in m.
    radii
        Wire radius of every segment in m, shape ``(K,)``.
    names
        Owner name of every segment (conductor or electrode name),
        length ``K``. Segments of one owner are never paired.
    rel_threshold
        A pair is reported when its axis distance is below
        ``rel_threshold * (a_i + a_j)`` (default 5: e.g. 8 cm for two
        8 mm rods, where the point-source kernel is already +24 % off).
    abs_threshold
        Additional absolute threshold in m (default 0); the larger of
        the two applies.
    include_junctions
        Also report pairs that only meet at a shared end point (default
        ``False``: such junctions are connections by design).

    Returns
    -------
    list of WireProximity
        Sorted by ascending clearance (worst first).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``endpoints`` does not have shape ``(K, 2, 3)``, if ``radii`` or
        ``names`` does not have one entry per segment, if an end point or
        radius is not finite or a radius is negative, or if a threshold is
        negative.
    """
    ep = np.asarray(endpoints, dtype=float)
    if ep.ndim != 3 or ep.shape[1:] != (2, 3):
        raise ValueError(f"endpoints must have shape (K, 2, 3), got {ep.shape}")
    K = ep.shape[0]
    rad = np.asarray(radii, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    if rad.shape != (K,) or len(names) != K:
        raise ValueError("radii and names must have one entry per segment")
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(ep)) or not np.all(np.isfinite(rad)) or np.any(rad < 0):
        raise ValueError("endpoints and radii must be finite, radii >= 0")
    if rel_threshold < 0.0 or abs_threshold < 0.0:
        raise ValueError("thresholds must be non-negative")
    if K < 2:
        return []
    p1 = ep[:, 0]
    p2 = ep[:, 1]
    mid = 0.5 * (p1 + p2)
    half = 0.5 * np.linalg.norm(p2 - p1, axis=1)
    thr = np.maximum(rel_threshold * 2.0 * rad.max(), abs_threshold)
    reach = 2.0 * half.max() + thr
    from scipy.spatial import cKDTree  # lazy: keep `import groundfield` light

    tree = cKDTree(mid)
    pairs = tree.query_pairs(r=float(reach), output_type="ndarray")
    if pairs.size == 0:
        return []
    names_arr = np.asarray(list(names), dtype=object)
    keep = names_arr[pairs[:, 0]] != names_arr[pairs[:, 1]]
    pairs = pairs[keep]
    if pairs.size == 0:
        return []
    i, j = pairs[:, 0], pairs[:, 1]
    # cheap pre-filter: midpoint distance minus both half lengths
    gap = np.linalg.norm(mid[i] - mid[j], axis=1) - half[i] - half[j]
    pair_thr = np.maximum(rel_threshold * (rad[i] + rad[j]), abs_threshold)
    sel = gap <= pair_thr
    i, j, pair_thr = i[sel], j[sel], pair_thr[sel]
    if i.size == 0:
        return []
    dist, s, t = segment_distance(p1[i], p2[i], p1[j], p2[j])
    hit = dist < pair_thr
    scale = np.maximum(np.abs(ep[i]).max(axis=(1, 2)), np.abs(ep[j]).max(axis=(1, 2)))
    inside = dist < _closer_than_touching(rad[i] + rad[j], scale)
    out: list[WireProximity] = []
    for k in np.nonzero(hit)[0]:
        ia, ib = int(i[k]), int(j[k])
        length = max(2.0 * half[ia], 2.0 * half[ib], 1e-12)
        tol = _TOUCH_REL * length
        at_end_a = s[k] <= 1e-9 or s[k] >= 1.0 - 1e-9
        at_end_b = t[k] <= 1e-9 or t[k] >= 1.0 - 1e-9
        if dist[k] <= tol and at_end_a and at_end_b:
            if not include_junctions:
                continue  # shared end point: a junction by design
            kind: ProximityKind = "junction"
        elif dist[k] <= tol:
            kind = "touching" if (at_end_a or at_end_b) else "crossing"
        elif inside[k]:
            kind = "interpenetrating"
        else:
            kind = "close"
        pa = p1[ia] + s[k] * (p2[ia] - p1[ia])
        pb = p1[ib] + t[k] * (p2[ib] - p1[ib])
        out.append(
            WireProximity(
                kind=kind,
                name_a=str(names_arr[ia]),
                name_b=str(names_arr[ib]),
                index_a=ia,
                index_b=ib,
                distance=float(dist[k]),
                clearance=float(dist[k] - rad[ia] - rad[ib]),
                point_a=(float(pa[0]), float(pa[1]), float(pa[2])),
                point_b=(float(pb[0]), float(pb[1]), float(pb[2])),
            )
        )
    out.sort(key=lambda p: p.clearance)
    return out

segment_distance(p1_a: ndarray, p2_a: ndarray, p1_b: ndarray, p2_b: ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

Minimum distance between straight segments (vectorised).

Closest points \(p_a(s) = p_{1,a} + s\,d_a\) and \(p_b(t) = p_{1,b} + t\,d_b\) with \(s, t \in [0, 1]\), by the standard clamped two-segment algorithm (Ericson 2005, sec. 5.1.9). Parallel segments and zero-length segments (points) are handled explicitly: the distance of a point to a segment is that of its orthogonal projection, clamped to the segment (audit of review pass 10, F04: a point-like second segment was measured from the start of the first one).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default p1_a ndarray

End points, arrays of shape (K, 3) (or (3,)) in m.

required p2_a ndarray

End points, arrays of shape (K, 3) (or (3,)) in m.

required p1_b ndarray

End points, arrays of shape (K, 3) (or (3,)) in m.

required p2_b ndarray

End points, arrays of shape (K, 3) (or (3,)) in m.

required

Returns:

Type Description distance, s, t : np.ndarray

Distance in m and the segment parameters of the closest points, each of shape (K,).

Source code in src/groundfield/conductors/proximity.py 
def segment_distance(
    p1_a: np.ndarray,
    p2_a: np.ndarray,
    p1_b: np.ndarray,
    p2_b: np.ndarray,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    r"""Minimum distance between straight segments (vectorised).

    Closest points $p_a(s) = p_{1,a} + s\,d_a$ and
    $p_b(t) = p_{1,b} + t\,d_b$ with $s, t \in [0, 1]$, by the standard
    clamped two-segment algorithm (Ericson 2005, sec. 5.1.9). Parallel
    segments and zero-length segments (points) are handled explicitly:
    the distance of a point to a segment is that of its orthogonal
    projection, clamped to the segment (audit of review pass 10, F04:
    a point-like second segment was measured from the start of the
    first one).

    Parameters
    ----------
    p1_a, p2_a, p1_b, p2_b
        End points, arrays of shape ``(K, 3)`` (or ``(3,)``) in m.

    Returns
    -------
    distance, s, t : np.ndarray
        Distance in m and the segment parameters of the closest points,
        each of shape ``(K,)``.
    """
    p1_a = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(p1_a, dtype=float))
    p2_a = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(p2_a, dtype=float))
    p1_b = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(p1_b, dtype=float))
    p2_b = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(p2_b, dtype=float))
    d1 = p2_a - p1_a
    d2 = p2_b - p1_b
    r = p1_a - p1_b
    a = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", d1, d1)
    e = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", d2, d2)
    f = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", d2, r)
    c = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", d1, r)
    b = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", d1, d2)
    denom = a * e - b * b
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        s = np.where(
            denom > 1e-14 * np.maximum(a * e, 1e-300),
            np.clip((b * f - c * e) / denom, 0.0, 1.0),
            0.0,
        )
        t = (b * s + f) / np.where(e > 0.0, e, 1.0)
        # clamp t and recompute s where needed
        t_lo = t < 0.0
        t_hi = t > 1.0
        t = np.clip(t, 0.0, 1.0)
        s = np.where(t_lo, np.clip(-c / np.where(a > 0.0, a, 1.0), 0.0, 1.0), s)
        s = np.where(t_hi, np.clip((b - c) / np.where(a > 0.0, a, 1.0), 0.0, 1.0), s)
        # Degenerate segments: a point against a segment is the clamped
        # projection; two points are their distance.
        scale = np.maximum(np.maximum(a, e), 1e-300)
        point_a = a <= 1e-24 * scale
        point_b = e <= 1e-24 * scale
        s = np.where(point_b, np.clip(-c / np.where(a > 0.0, a, 1.0), 0.0, 1.0), s)
        t = np.where(point_b, 0.0, t)
        s = np.where(point_a, 0.0, s)
        t = np.where(
            point_a & ~point_b, np.clip(f / np.where(e > 0.0, e, 1.0), 0.0, 1.0), t
        )
    ca = p1_a + s[:, None] * d1
    cb = p1_b + t[:, None] * d2
    dist = np.linalg.norm(ca - cb, axis=1)
    return dist, s, t

def solid_round_internal_impedance(
    frequency: float | np.ndarray,
    *,
    radius: float,
    resistivity: float,
) -> complex | np.ndarray:
    r"""Internal series impedance per unit length of a solid round wire.

    Parameters
    ----------
    frequency
        Frequency in Hz (scalar or array, ``>= 0``).
    radius
        Conductor radius $a$ in m (the radius of a solid conductor with
        the same conducting cross section, $a = \sqrt{A/\pi}$).
    resistivity
        Conductor resistivity $\rho$ in Ω·m.

    Returns
    -------
    complex or np.ndarray
        $Z'_\text{int} = R'(f) + j\omega L'_\text{int}(f)$ in Ω/m;
        at ``frequency == 0`` the DC resistance $\rho/(\pi a^2)$.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``radius`` or ``resistivity`` is not positive and finite, or
        if a frequency is negative or not finite.
    """
    if not (radius > 0.0 and math.isfinite(radius)):
        raise ValueError(f"radius must be positive and finite, got {radius}")
    if not (resistivity > 0.0 and math.isfinite(resistivity)):
        raise ValueError(f"resistivity must be positive and finite, got {resistivity}")
    f = np.asarray(frequency, dtype=float)
    if np.any(f < 0.0) or not np.all(np.isfinite(f)):
        raise ValueError("frequency must be finite and >= 0")
    r_dc = resistivity / (math.pi * radius * radius)
    omega = 2.0 * math.pi * f
    k = np.sqrt(1j * omega * MU_0 / resistivity)
    z = k * radius
    out = np.full(f.shape, r_dc, dtype=complex)
    small = np.abs(z) < _SERIES_LIMIT
    if np.any(small):
        z2 = z[small] ** 2
        # Z' = r_dc * (k a / 2) * I0/I1 = r_dc * (1 + z^2/8 - z^4/192 + z^6/3072)
        out[small] = r_dc * (1.0 + z2 / 8.0 - z2 * z2 / 192.0 + z2**3 / 3072.0)
    big = ~small
    if np.any(big):
        # Imported here: ``import groundfield`` must not load scipy.special.
        from scipy.special import ive

        zb = z[big]
        out[big] = (
            k[big] * resistivity / (2.0 * math.pi * radius) * ive(0, zb) / ive(1, zb)
        )
    if np.ndim(frequency) == 0:
        return complex(out[()])
    return out

docs.title: Coupling
docs.text: The coupling package collects the coupling relations the solvers consume: the Neumann partial inductances between conductor segments (inductance, ADR-0004), the earth-return correction of that inductance — Carson's per-metre series for long parallel wires over homogeneous earth (carson, ADR-0005) and the geometric Sommerfeld/Pollaczek integral for any geometry and any number of layers (sommerfeld_inductance, ADR-0006) — and the scalar Green's function of two-layer soil for electrodes through the layer interface (layered_green, ADR-0007). There is no capacitive coupling: below 1 kHz it is negligible for buried conductors.

docs.title: Mathematical and physical context
docs.text:
Conductors with inductance_model="neumann" are split into segments whose series impedance matrix is

\[ \mathbf{Z}_b(\omega) = \mathbf{R} + j\omega\,\mathbf{L} + \Delta\mathbf{Z}_\text{earth}(\omega), \qquad L_{ij} = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\Gamma_i}\!\int_{\Gamma_j} \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{l}_i\cdot\mathrm{d}\mathbf{l}_j}{\lvert\mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{r}_j\rvert}, \]

the Neumann double-line integral (closed forms for parallel and touching segments, Gauss–Legendre otherwise) plus the internal inductance \(\mu_0\ell/(8\pi)\) on the diagonal. The earth enters twice: as an image term in \(\mathbf{L}\) and as the frequency-dependent correction \(\Delta\mathbf{Z}_\text{earth}\); the two are only meaningful together, which is why every builder takes the same image= convention ("none": free space; "additive": perfect magnetic mirror; "antiparallel": perfect electric conductor).

Carson (1926). For a long straight wire above homogeneous earth of conductivity \(\sigma\), against the antiparallel image,

\[ \Delta Z_\text{Carson} = \frac{\omega\mu_0}{\pi}\bigl[P(a,\theta) + jQ(a,\theta)\bigr], \qquad a = D\sqrt{\omega\mu_0\sigma} = \frac{\sqrt{2}\,D}{\delta}, \]

with \(D = 2h\) (self) or the image distance of a pair (mutual) and \(\delta = \sqrt{2/(\omega\mu_0\sigma)}\) the skin depth in the soil. \(P, Q\) are evaluated by Carson's series (\(a \le 0.25\)), quadrature (\(0.25 < a \le 15\)) and the asymptotic expansion (\(a > 15\)). The correction is per metre and scaled by the segment-pair length, so it is exact only for long parallel wires; for a layered soil the upper-layer resistivity is used with a warning.

Sommerfeld / Pollaczek. The quasi-static vector-potential Green's function of the layered half-space,

\[ G(\rho, z, z') = \delta_{kj}\,\frac{e^{-\gamma_k R}}{R} + \int_0^\infty \lambda\,F_{kj}(\lambda; z, z')\,J_0(\lambda\rho)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda, \qquad \gamma_k^2 = j\omega\mu_0\sigma_k , \]

is integrated over every segment pair (time convention \(e^{+j\omega t}\)). It handles short and non-parallel wires, buried and overhead conductors and any number of layers, and is the default (Engine.earth_inductive_model="sommerfeld"). In the long-wire limit it gives the Pollaczek line impedance with the earth-return resistance \(R' \approx \omega\mu_0/8\).

docs.title: Choosing the earth-return model
docs.text:
earth_inductive_model Use for Limits "sommerfeld" (default) quantitative \(Z(f)\) of buried and overhead conductors, layered soil, short or bent conductors cost grows with the number of segment pairs; the default tabulated assembly (Engine.sommerfeld_assembly) shares one table per pair of depth groups, "exact" integrates every pair "carson_series" fast scoping of long parallel conductors over homogeneous soil per-metre approximation; layered soil uses \(\rho_1\) (warning); rejects segments in the surface plane "perfect_mirror" diagnostic baseline only frequency-independent image, far from the physics of buried conductors below 1 kHz

The theory, the validation against Carson's and Pollaczek's line impedances, and the history of these models are on the earth return page.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The per-metre impedance of a conductor buried 0.7 m deep (wire radius 5 mm, internal inductance included via \(\mathrm{GMR} = a\,e^{-1/4}\)), from the closed-form references the solver is validated against:

import math

from groundfield.references import earth_return, pollaczek

gmr = 0.005 * math.exp(-0.25)
for f in (50.0, 1000.0):
    z_carson = earth_return.carson_self_impedance(100.0, f, gmr=gmr)       # Ω/m
    z_buried = pollaczek.pollaczek_self_impedance(100.0, 100.0, 5.0, f, depth=0.7, gmr=gmr)
    z_layered = pollaczek.pollaczek_self_impedance(100.0, 1000.0, 5.0, f, depth=0.7, gmr=gmr)
    # homogeneous soil: the buried (Pollaczek) and Carson line impedances agree
    assert abs(z_buried - z_carson) / abs(z_carson) < 1e-3
    # earth-return resistance omega*mu0/8: 49.3 mOhm/km at 50 Hz
    assert abs(z_carson.real - earth_return.carson_earth_return_resistance(f)) < 1e-12
    # 1000 Ohm m below 5 m of 100 Ohm m soil: about 9 % more reactance
    assert 1.08 < z_layered.imag / z_buried.imag < 1.10

docs.title: inductance
docs.text:
Self- and mutual-inductance helpers for distributed conductors.

This module implements the inductance physics described in ADR-0004. It provides three public functions:

  • thin_wire_self_inductance() — closed-form self-inductance of a straight thin-wire segment of length \(\ell\) and radius \(a\) (Grover 1946): \(L_\text{self} = (\mu_0\,\ell)/(2\pi) \bigl[\ln(2\ell/a) - 1\bigr]\).
  • parallel_segments_mutual() — closed-form mutual inductance of two parallel coaxial segments of equal length \(\ell\) at perpendicular distance \(d\).
  • neumann_mutual() — generic Neumann double-line integral via two-point Gauss–Legendre quadrature, valid for any 3-D segment-pair geometry.

Earth-image contributions are handled by the caller: for a perfect-mirror earth the caller adds the integral against the mirror image of the source segment (see perfect_mirror_self_pair_inductance() and the assembly logic in build_inductance_matrix()).

Conventions

Image convention (image=). The earth image of a segment \((p_1 \to p_2)\) is the segment \((p_1' \to p_2')\) with \(z \to -z\) (the \(z\)-axis points into the soil). Its Neumann integral against a partner carries the orientation through the dot product, so the mirrored-endpoint image is the image in a perfect magnetic conductor (horizontal currents co-directed, vertical currents reversed). Three conventions are offered:

  • "none" — free space, \(L = L_\text{dir}\). The exact quasi-static baseline of the Sommerfeld earth-return correction (groundfield.coupling.sommerfeld_inductance): at DC the soil is magnetically transparent.
  • "additive" — \(L = L_\text{dir} + L_\text{img}\), the ADR-0004 "perfect mirror" (historic default, use_image=True).
  • "antiparallel" — \(L = L_\text{dir} - L_\text{img}\), the perfect-electric-conductor image (horizontal currents reversed). This is the baseline against which Carson's correction \(\Delta Z = (\omega\mu_0/\pi)(P + jQ)\) is defined (groundfield.coupling.carson). A perfect conductor screens the soil: a pair on opposite sides of the surface has \(L = 0\) (since audit round 2 of the calendar release; the mirrored-endpoint image of a buried partner lands above ground and gave \(\ln(D_\text{mirror}/D) < 0\)), and its whole coupling is in the earth-return correction.

An earth-return correction matrix is only meaningful together with the image convention of the inductance matrix it is added to; the correction builders therefore take the same image= argument.

Internal inductance (include_internal=). The diagonal (partial self) term is the external thin-wire inductance plus, by default, the DC internal inductance of a solid round conductor, \(\mu_0 \ell/(8\pi)\). Every function of this package that returns a self term uses this one convention, controlled by include_internal (default True; the solver passes False for the conductors of conductor_type="cable_shield", thin-walled tubes, user decision Q33). A per-unit-length reference that includes the internal flux uses the geometric mean radius \(\mathrm{GMR} = a\,e^{-1/4}\); with include_internal=False the matching reference uses \(\mathrm{GMR} = a\). The frequency dependence of the internal impedance (skin effect) is provided by groundfield.conductors.Conductor.internal_impedance_per_length() as a correction relative to this DC convention.

Wires lying beside each other. Where a point of one wire lies beside another wire (its foot on that wire's axis falls inside the wire) closer than the sum of the radii \(r_i + r_j\) — two conductors in one trench, a service drop routed back along its PEN main, coincident leads, wires leaving a junction or crossing at a small angle — the distance from the other axis is taken as \(r_i + r_j\) (touching wires) inside the Neumann integral of build_inductance_matrix(), or as the radius of the thicker wire where the thinner one runs inside it and the thicker one is marked as a cable shield (shields=; a core inside a cable shield couples as a filament inside a thin tube). The marker is explicit since the user decision Q32 of 2026.11: two unmarked wires on one axis are separate conductors that touch. For parallel wires the rule refers to whole conductors (conductors=, one label per conductor, as the solver passes them; audit W1A-02 of the calendar release): a thinner wire inside a cable shield couples at the shield radius at every axial offset (exact for a filament on the axis of a thin tube), and a point lies beside another conductor when its foot falls inside that conductor, so the sub-pieces of two conductors lying beside each other add up to the lumped pair (a 100 m coax in 1 m pieces read 2.2 % low before). Pieces tilted against each other by more than the closed form's tolerance of about 4.5e-5 rad, at any angle and whatever their length, get the same two readings with the stretches inside, beside and away from the partner found exactly (audits W1R2-01, W1R3-01, W1R3-02; a core tilted by 4.5e-5 rad read 7.4 % low in 0.25 m pieces, with a step at the tolerance; until W1R3 the rule stopped where the lateral distance changed by more than the touching distance along a piece, or at \(|\cos\varphi| = 0.99\), and a core crossing its shield's axis read -8.6e-5 of the loop off the lumped pair in 10 m pieces, two wires leaving a junction stepped by 1.5e-3 at 8.1°). The filament integral diverges for coincident axes (two coincident 50 m leads read +587j Ω at 50 Hz) and exceeds the self inductance once the wires are closer than about their radius (an indefinite matrix, a TN network with drops along its PEN main had a negative input reactance). The rule acts pointwise and on both one-sided integrals, so the value is continuous in the geometry and independent of the order and direction of the segments (audit round 3 of the calendar release; the whole-pair switch of audit round 2 depended on which segment was the row). Chain neighbours and bends turning by less than 90° keep their closed forms.

Close pairs. Nearly parallel wires close together whose directions differ by more than the closed form's tolerance, crossing and skew pairs are integrated semi-analytically with touching="exact"; the 16x16 rule was +12 % at 10 cm and up to +250 % at 1 cm for two 5 m segments (audit round 2 of the calendar release).

Touching segments (touching=). The Neumann integrand is log-singular for segments that share an end point (bends, chain neighbours) or lie on one axis. "exact" (the default since the calendar release 2026.11) uses the closed forms (Grover 1946: two filaments meeting at a point; coaxial filaments with a gap), accurate to machine precision; a straight wire split into any number of segments keeps the self inductance of the unsplit wire. "quadrature" (the default up to 0.15.0, kept to reproduce old numbers) integrates such pairs with the 16x16 Gauss–Legendre rule, which is accurate to about -0.3 % ... +0.8 % for them (review pass 10, finding 10.46). The closed forms of all coaxial pairs of a segment are evaluated in one vectorised call — a straight conductor of \(M\) sub-segments has \(M(M-1)/2\) of them — bit-identical with the scalar routine (audit round 2 of the calendar release, A2C-5).

References
  • Grover, F. W. (1946). Inductance Calculations: Working Formulas and Tables. Dover (reprint 2004).
  • Sunde, E. D. (1968). Earth Conduction Effects in Transmission Systems. Dover, ch. 7.
  • Paul, C. R. (2010). Inductance: Loop and Partial. Wiley.
