docs.title: build_carson_correction_matrices
docs.text:
build_carson_correction_matrices(seg_endpoints: ndarray, wire_radii: ndarray, *, omegas, sigma_earth: float, image: ImageConvention = 'antiparallel') -> np.ndarray

Carson earth-return correction matrices for several frequencies.

Multi-frequency form of build_carson_correction_matrix(): the frequency-independent tiling geometry (pair classification, axial overlaps, Carson heights) is built once and every frequency only evaluates the per-metre Carson values. Entry k equals build_carson_correction_matrix(..., omega=omegas[k]) bit for bit.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default seg_endpoints ndarray

Array of shape (M, 2, 3) (m), as in build_inductance_matrix().

required wire_radii ndarray

Per-branch wire radii in m, shape (M,).

required omegas

Angular frequencies in rad/s (sequence of floats); entries <= 0 give zero matrices.

required sigma_earth float

Earth conductivity in S/m.

required image ImageConvention

Image convention of the inductance matrix this correction is added to (see build_carson_correction_matrix()).

'antiparallel'

Returns:

Name Type Description dZ np.ndarray, shape (n_f, M, M), dtype complex

Correction matrices in Ω.

Source code in src/groundfield/coupling/inductance.py 
def build_carson_correction_matrices(
    seg_endpoints: np.ndarray,  # shape (M, 2, 3)
    wire_radii: np.ndarray,  # shape (M,)
    *,
    omegas,
    sigma_earth: float,
    image: ImageConvention = "antiparallel",
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Carson earth-return correction matrices for several frequencies.

    Multi-frequency form of :func:`build_carson_correction_matrix`: the
    frequency-independent tiling geometry (pair classification, axial
    overlaps, Carson heights) is built once and every frequency only
    evaluates the per-metre Carson values. Entry ``k`` equals
    ``build_carson_correction_matrix(..., omega=omegas[k])`` bit for
    bit.

    Parameters
    ----------
    seg_endpoints
        Array of shape ``(M, 2, 3)`` (m), as in
        :func:`build_inductance_matrix`.
    wire_radii
        Per-branch wire radii in m, shape ``(M,)``.
    omegas
        Angular frequencies in rad/s (sequence of floats); entries
        ``<= 0`` give zero matrices.
    sigma_earth
        Earth conductivity in S/m.
    image
        Image convention of the inductance matrix this correction is
        added to (see :func:`build_carson_correction_matrix`).

    Returns
    -------
    dZ : np.ndarray, shape (n_f, M, M), dtype complex
        Correction matrices in Ω.
    """
    mode = _resolve_image(image, None)
    omegas = [float(om) for om in np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(omegas, dtype=float))]
    from groundfield.coupling.carson import (
        carson_mixed_mutual_correction,
        carson_mutual_correction,
    )

    M = seg_endpoints.shape[0]
    out = np.zeros((len(omegas), M, M), dtype=complex)
    if M == 0 or sigma_earth <= 0.0 or all(om <= 0.0 for om in omegas):
        return out
    radii = np.asarray(wire_radii, dtype=float)
    heights, lengths, horizontal, entries, fallback = _carson_pair_plan(
        seg_endpoints, radii
    )
    p1 = seg_endpoints[:, 0, :].astype(float, copy=False)
    p2 = seg_endpoints[:, 1, :].astype(float, copy=False)
    above = _overhead(p1, p2)
    opposite = above[:, None] != above[None, :]
    fallback_values = (
        _carson_fallback_values(seg_endpoints, radii, fallback, omegas, sigma_earth)
        if fallback
        else {}
    )
    M_conv = None
    if mode != "antiparallel":
        # Carson's correction is defined against the anti-parallel
        # image: L_anti = L_dir - L_img on one side of the surface, 0
        # across it. Moving it onto an inductance matrix with another
        # image convention, dZ -> dZ - scale jw M_conv:
        #   additive: L_add - L_anti = 2 L_img  |  L_dir + L_img (across)
        #   none:     L_dir - L_anti =   L_img  |  L_dir         (across)
        M_conv = _image_inductance_matrix(seg_endpoints, wire_radii=radii)
        if opposite.any():
            L_dir = _direct_mutual_matrix(seg_endpoints, radii)
            if mode == "additive":
                M_conv[opposite] = 0.5 * (L_dir[opposite] + M_conv[opposite])
            else:
                M_conv[opposite] = L_dir[opposite]
    for k, omega in enumerate(omegas):
        if omega <= 0.0:
            continue
        dZ = out[k]
        for i in range(M):
            if not horizontal[i]:
                continue  # inclined / vertical: Sommerfeld (fallback)
            # Diagonal: self correction (parallel-to-self ⇒ θ = 0),
            # per-unit-length value times this branch's length.
            dz_per_m = carson_mutual_correction(
                omega=omega,
                height_i=heights[i],
                height_j=heights[i],
                horizontal_distance=0.0,
                sigma_earth=sigma_earth,
            )
            dZ[i, i] = dz_per_m * lengths[i]
        for i, j, d_h, factor, sign in entries:
            if opposite[i, j]:
                # Overhead wire parallel to a buried one: the field
                # transmitted into the soil (no PEC baseline across the
                # surface; audit A2C-1).
                h_air, d_soil = (
                    (heights[i], heights[j]) if above[i] else (heights[j], heights[i])
                )
                dz_per_m = carson_mixed_mutual_correction(
                    omega, h_air, d_soil, d_h, sigma_earth
                )
            else:
                dz_per_m = carson_mutual_correction(
                    omega=omega,
                    height_i=heights[i],
                    height_j=heights[j],
                    horizontal_distance=d_h,
                    sigma_earth=sigma_earth,
                )
            # += : a tilted pair has one entry per node of its stretch
            dZ[i, j] += sign * dz_per_m * factor
            dZ[j, i] = dZ[i, j]
        for (i, j), vals in fallback_values.items():
            dZ[i, j] = dZ[j, i] = vals[k]
        if M_conv is not None:
            scale = 2.0 if mode == "additive" else 1.0
            dZ -= scale * 1j * omega * M_conv
    return out

docs.title: build_carson_correction_matrix
docs.text:
build_carson_correction_matrix(seg_endpoints: ndarray, wire_radii: ndarray, *, omega: float, sigma_earth: float, image: ImageConvention = 'antiparallel') -> np.ndarray

Assemble the dense Carson earth-return correction matrix.

Returns the per-segment-pair impedance correction \(\Delta Z^{(i,j)}_\text{Carson}(\omega)\) described in ADR-0005. The output has the same shape as build_inductance_matrix() but is complex and frequency-dependent — it is therefore rebuilt at every frequency by the solver (or built for all frequencies at once with build_carson_correction_matrices()).

Image baseline (review pass 10, findings 10.20 / F32)

Carson's correction \((\omega\mu_0/\pi)(P + jQ)\) is defined against the anti-parallel (perfect-electric-conductor) image: the complete series impedance is \(Z = j\omega L_\text{antiparallel} + \Delta Z_\text{Carson}\) with \(L_\text{antiparallel}\) from build_inductance_matrix(image="antiparallel"). The image argument names the image convention of the inductance matrix the returned correction is added to; for "additive" / "none" the matrix is shifted by \(-2j\omega L_\text{img}\) / \(-j\omega L_\text{img}\) so that the sum is the same physical impedance. The default "antiparallel" returns the plain Carson correction (bit-identical to earlier releases). The docstring of earlier releases said the correction goes "on top of the perfect-mirror (additive) Neumann matrix" — that pairing double-counts the image and gives 1.66–2.25× the earth-return reactance on 100 m – 1 km lines.

Tiling convention (audit 2026-07-08, WP-C3)

Carson's correction is an infinite-wire, per-unit-length concept. To make the assembled matrix consistent — and, crucially, convergent under mesh refinement — the per-pair entries tile the per-unit-length values without double counting:

  • Diagonal dZ[i, i]: self correction per metre × segment length. Summed over a refined straight wire this reproduces the full z'_self · ℓ exactly, independent of the segment count.
  • Collinear pairs (same axis, negligible perpendicular offset): zero. The infinite-wire self value on the diagonal already contains the interaction with the rest of the same wire.
  • Near-parallel pairs on distinct axes (|cosφ| > 0.99) of near-horizontal segments: mutual correction per metre at the perpendicular horizontal axis separation, weighted by the axial overlap length of the two segment intervals — measured along the bisector of the two axes for a pair that is not exactly parallel, so that the order of the segments does not matter (audit round 3 of the calendar release; on the first segment's axis the entries moved by up to 3.1 % of the largest one). Non-overlapping (e.g. staggered or end-to-end) pairs contribute zero. Two different conductors that overlap on one axis are wires lying side by side: the mutual at the distance of touching wires \(r_i + r_j\) (they used to get none).
  • Pairs on opposite sides of the surface (an overhead wire parallel to a buried one): the field transmitted into the soil, carson_mixed_mutual_correction() — the anti-parallel baseline of such a pair is zero (audit round 2 of the calendar release, A2C-1; the buried wire used to be treated as an overhead wire at height \(|z|\) on the mirrored-endpoint image: -36 % mutual reactance for a lead 1 m above a PEN at 0.7 m, 1 kHz).
  • Outside Carson's domain — oblique pairs (1e-9 < |cosφ| ≤ 0.99) and every pair and self term of a segment inclined by more than 8.1 deg: the exact quasi-static Sommerfeld correction of a homogeneous earth of the same conductivity (tabulated assembly), moved onto the anti-parallel baseline. Up to audit round 2 oblique pairs got the projected geometric-mean heuristic \(\sqrt{\ell_i\ell_j}\,|\cos\varphi|\) per segment pair, which grows with the number of segments (a probe lead turning 8.1 deg against the feed lead changed the reading 17.6-fold). At the domain boundary the result steps from the per-metre tiling to the Sommerfeld value, by the model error of the tiling there (two 1 km leads 2 m apart, 1 kHz: 13 %). Orthogonal pairs contribute zero by symmetry.
Earth-conductivity sign convention

In groundfield the \(z\)-axis points into the soil. A wire above ground has \(z < 0\) and height = -z > 0. A wire just below the surface has \(z > 0\) and we use height = z as the Sunde-equivalent depth (Carson's \(h\)).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default seg_endpoints ndarray

Array of shape (M, 2, 3) in m — same layout as build_inductance_matrix().

required wire_radii ndarray

Per-branch wire radii in metres (only used as a regulariser for a wire exactly at the surface; the Carson kernel itself does not depend on the radius).

required omega float

Angular frequency in rad/s.

required sigma_earth float

Earth conductivity in S/m.

required image ImageConvention

Image convention of the inductance matrix the correction is added to: "antiparallel" (default, Carson's own baseline), "additive" or "none".

'antiparallel'

Returns:

Name Type Description dZ np.ndarray, shape (M, M), dtype complex

Symmetric Carson correction matrix in \(\Omega\).

Source code in src/groundfield/coupling/inductance.py 
def build_carson_correction_matrix(
    seg_endpoints: np.ndarray,  # shape (M, 2, 3)
    wire_radii: np.ndarray,  # shape (M,)
    *,
    omega: float,
    sigma_earth: float,
    image: ImageConvention = "antiparallel",
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Assemble the dense Carson earth-return correction matrix.

    Returns the per-segment-pair impedance correction
    $\\Delta Z^{(i,j)}_\\text{Carson}(\\omega)$ described in ADR-0005.
    The output has the same shape as :func:`build_inductance_matrix`
    but is **complex** and **frequency-dependent** — it is therefore
    rebuilt at every frequency by the solver (or built for all
    frequencies at once with :func:`build_carson_correction_matrices`).

    Image baseline (review pass 10, findings 10.20 / F32)
    -----------------------------------------------------
    Carson's correction $(\\omega\\mu_0/\\pi)(P + jQ)$ is defined
    against the **anti-parallel** (perfect-electric-conductor) image:
    the complete series impedance is
    $Z = j\\omega L_\\text{antiparallel} + \\Delta Z_\\text{Carson}$
    with $L_\\text{antiparallel}$ from
    ``build_inductance_matrix(image="antiparallel")``. The ``image``
    argument names the image convention of the inductance matrix the
    returned correction is **added to**; for ``"additive"`` /
    ``"none"`` the matrix is shifted by $-2j\\omega L_\\text{img}$ /
    $-j\\omega L_\\text{img}$ so that the sum is the same physical
    impedance. The default ``"antiparallel"`` returns the plain Carson
    correction (bit-identical to earlier releases). The docstring of
    earlier releases said the correction goes "on top of the
    perfect-mirror (additive) Neumann matrix" — that pairing
    double-counts the image and gives 1.66–2.25× the earth-return
    reactance on 100 m – 1 km lines.

    Tiling convention (audit 2026-07-08, WP-C3)
    -------------------------------------------
    Carson's correction is an *infinite-wire, per-unit-length*
    concept. To make the assembled matrix consistent — and, crucially,
    **convergent under mesh refinement** — the per-pair entries tile
    the per-unit-length values without double counting:

    - **Diagonal** ``dZ[i, i]``: self correction per metre × segment
      length. Summed over a refined straight wire this reproduces the
      full ``z'_self · ℓ`` exactly, independent of the segment count.
    - **Collinear pairs** (same axis, negligible perpendicular
      offset): **zero.** The infinite-wire self value on the diagonal
      already contains the interaction with the rest of the same
      wire.
    - **Near-parallel pairs on distinct axes** (``|cosφ| > 0.99``) of
      near-horizontal segments: mutual correction per metre at the
      **perpendicular** horizontal axis separation, weighted by the
      **axial overlap length** of the two segment intervals — measured
      along the bisector of the two axes for a pair that is not exactly
      parallel, so that the order of the segments does not matter
      (audit round 3 of the calendar release; on the first segment's axis
      the entries moved by up to 3.1 % of the largest one).
      Non-overlapping (e.g. staggered or end-to-end) pairs contribute
      zero. Two different conductors that overlap on one axis are
      wires lying side by side: the mutual at the distance of touching
      wires $r_i + r_j$ (they used to get none).
    - **Pairs on opposite sides of the surface** (an overhead wire
      parallel to a buried one): the field transmitted into the soil,
      :func:`~groundfield.coupling.carson.carson_mixed_mutual_correction`
      — the anti-parallel baseline of such a pair is zero (audit round 2
      of the calendar release, A2C-1; the buried wire used to be treated
      as an overhead wire at height $|z|$ on the mirrored-endpoint image:
      -36 % mutual reactance for a lead 1 m above a PEN at 0.7 m, 1 kHz).
    - **Outside Carson's domain** — oblique pairs
      (``1e-9 < |cosφ| ≤ 0.99``) and every pair and self term of a
      segment inclined by more than 8.1 deg: the exact quasi-static
      Sommerfeld correction of a homogeneous earth of the same
      conductivity (tabulated assembly), moved onto the anti-parallel
      baseline. Up to audit round 2 oblique pairs got the projected
      geometric-mean heuristic $\\sqrt{\\ell_i\\ell_j}\\,|\\cos\\varphi|$ per
      segment pair, which grows with the number of segments (a probe lead
      turning 8.1 deg against the feed lead changed the reading
      17.6-fold). At the domain boundary the result steps from the
      per-metre tiling to the Sommerfeld value, by the model error of
      the tiling there (two 1 km leads 2 m apart, 1 kHz: 13 %).
      Orthogonal pairs contribute zero by symmetry.

    Earth-conductivity sign convention
    ----------------------------------
    In ``groundfield`` the $z$-axis points *into* the soil. A wire
    above ground has $z < 0$ and ``height = -z > 0``. A wire just
    below the surface has $z > 0$ and we use ``height = z`` as the
    Sunde-equivalent depth (Carson's $h$).

    Parameters
    ----------
    seg_endpoints
        Array of shape ``(M, 2, 3)`` in m — same layout as
        :func:`build_inductance_matrix`.
    wire_radii
        Per-branch wire radii in metres (only used as a regulariser
        for a wire exactly at the surface; the Carson kernel itself
        does not depend on the radius).
    omega
        Angular frequency in rad/s.
    sigma_earth
        Earth conductivity in S/m.
    image
        Image convention of the inductance matrix the correction is
        added to: ``"antiparallel"`` (default, Carson's own baseline),
        ``"additive"`` or ``"none"``.

    Returns
    -------
    dZ : np.ndarray, shape (M, M), dtype complex
        Symmetric Carson correction matrix in $\\Omega$.
    """
    if omega <= 0.0 or sigma_earth <= 0.0:
        return np.zeros(
            (seg_endpoints.shape[0], seg_endpoints.shape[0]),
            dtype=complex,
        )
    return build_carson_correction_matrices(
        seg_endpoints,
        wire_radii,
        omegas=[omega],
        sigma_earth=sigma_earth,
        image=image,
    )[0]

docs.title: build_inductance_matrix
docs.text:
build_inductance_matrix(seg_endpoints: ndarray, wire_radii: ndarray, *, use_image: bool | None = None, image: ImageConvention | None = None, include_internal: bool | ndarray = True, touching: TouchingRule = 'exact', shields: bool | ndarray | None = None, conductors: ndarray | None = None) -> np.ndarray

Assemble the dense partial-inductance matrix over branches.

Vectorised implementation per ADR-0010 Tier 0b. Reproduces _build_inductance_matrix_loop() bit-exactly to floating- point precision but evaluates the off-diagonal entries one row at a time in batched NumPy calls — typical networks (~1000 segments) speed up by 1–2 orders of magnitude.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default seg_endpoints ndarray

Array of shape (M, 2, 3) with the start- and end-points (in m, \(z\) positive into the soil) of every distributed-conductor longitudinal-branch segment.

required wire_radii ndarray

Per-branch wire radii in metres, shape (M,): the thin-wire self terms, and the distance of touching wires \(r_i + r_j\) (or the shield radius for a wire inside a cable shield, see shields) taken where two wires lie beside each other closer than that (module docstring, "Wires lying beside each other").

required use_image bool | None

Legacy switch: True is image="additive", False is image="none". Pass either this or image, not both.

None image ImageConvention | None

Image convention of the returned matrix (see the module docstring): "none" (free space), "additive" (perfect magnetic mirror, the historic default) or "antiparallel" (perfect electric mirror — Carson's baseline). The image term is the Neumann integral against the mirrored partner (and the segment's own image on the diagonal). Defaults to "additive".

None include_internal bool | ndarray

Add the DC internal inductance \(\mu_0\ell/(8\pi)\) to the self terms (default True). A boolean applies to every segment; an array of shape (M,) selects it per segment (e.g. False for conductors whose internal impedance is supplied separately by a skin-effect model).

True touching TouchingRule

"exact" (default): closed forms for pairs that share an end point or lie on one axis; "quadrature": the 16x16 rule of 0.15.0 (see neumann_mutual()).

'exact' shields bool | ndarray | None

Segments of cable shields (a bool for all, or an array of shape (M,); None, the default, for none). A thinner wire parallel inside a shield (\(\delta + r_\text{thin} \le r_s\)) couples to it at the shield radius, at every axial offset (a core inside a cable shield; user decision Q32 of 2026.11); two unmarked wires on one axis touch. The self terms do not depend on it: pass include_internal=~shields to drop the internal inductance of a solid wire from the shields, as the solver does for conductor_type="cable_shield" (Q33). Without it a shield keeps \(\mu_0\ell/(8\pi)\) = 50 nH/m: the 100 m coax with 5 mm core and 15 mm shield reads 31.97 µH instead of 26.97 µH.

None conductors ndarray | None

Conductor label of every segment, shape (M,) (any values that can be compared for equality, e.g. conductor names; None, the default: every segment is a conductor of its own). For two conductors lying beside each other (a pair of their segments closer than touching: on one axis, tilted against each other, crossing, leaving one junction), a point lies beside the partner when its foot falls inside the partner's whole conductor — the straight run of its segments with that label — so the sub-pieces of the two conductors add up to the lumped pair (audit W1A-02 of the calendar release). For segments that are not parallel the stretches inside, beside and away from the partner are found exactly, at any angle and for pieces of any length (audits W1R2-01, W1R3-01, W1R3-02: a slightly tilted core, a core crossing its shield's axis, two wires leaving a junction add up within 3e-12; up to W1R3 the rule stopped where the lateral distance changed by more than \(r_i + r_j\) along a segment and at \(|\cos\varphi| = 0.99\), and the pieces read up to 1.6e-3 off the lumped pair). Pieces of one conductor and conductors that only meet end to end keep the filament integral. Without labels, unmarked touching pieces of one cable are not recognised as one conductor: they keep the rule of the single segments and do not add up (the 100 m pair of 5 and 15 mm wires reads 40.34 µH in 0.25 m pieces against 43.47 µH lumped); the inside reading of a marked shield (shields) needs no labels and adds up either way (audit W1R2-08). The solver passes one label per conductor.

None

def build_inductance_matrix(
    seg_endpoints: np.ndarray,  # shape (M, 2, 3): each branch's [start, end]
    wire_radii: np.ndarray,  # shape (M,)
    *,
    use_image: bool | None = None,
    image: ImageConvention | None = None,
    include_internal: bool | np.ndarray = True,
    touching: TouchingRule = "exact",
    shields: bool | np.ndarray | None = None,
    conductors: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Assemble the dense partial-inductance matrix over branches.

    Vectorised implementation per ADR-0010 Tier 0b. Reproduces
    :func:`_build_inductance_matrix_loop` bit-exactly to floating-
    point precision but evaluates the off-diagonal entries one row
    at a time in batched NumPy calls — typical networks
    (~1000 segments) speed up by 1–2 orders of magnitude.

    Parameters
    ----------
    seg_endpoints
        Array of shape ``(M, 2, 3)`` with the start- and end-points
        (in m, $z$ positive into the soil) of every
        distributed-conductor longitudinal-branch segment.
    wire_radii
        Per-branch wire radii in metres, shape ``(M,)``: the thin-wire
        self terms, and the distance of touching wires $r_i + r_j$ (or
        the shield radius for a wire inside a cable shield, see
        ``shields``) taken where two wires lie beside each other closer
        than that (module docstring, "Wires lying beside each other").
    use_image
        Legacy switch: ``True`` is ``image="additive"``, ``False`` is
        ``image="none"``. Pass either this or ``image``, not both.
    image
        Image convention of the returned matrix (see the module
        docstring): ``"none"`` (free space), ``"additive"`` (perfect
        magnetic mirror, the historic default) or ``"antiparallel"``
        (perfect electric mirror — Carson's baseline). The image term
        is the Neumann integral against the mirrored partner (and the
        segment's own image on the diagonal). Defaults to
        ``"additive"``.
    include_internal
        Add the DC internal inductance $\\mu_0\\ell/(8\\pi)$ to the
        self terms (default ``True``). A boolean applies to every
        segment; an array of shape ``(M,)`` selects it per segment
        (e.g. ``False`` for conductors whose internal impedance is
        supplied separately by a skin-effect model).
    touching
        ``"exact"`` (default): closed forms for pairs that share an end
        point or lie on one axis; ``"quadrature"``: the 16x16 rule of
        0.15.0 (see :func:`neumann_mutual`).
    shields
        Segments of cable shields (a bool for all, or an array of shape
        ``(M,)``; ``None``, the default, for none). A thinner wire
        parallel inside a shield ($\\delta + r_\\text{thin} \\le r_s$)
        couples to it at the shield radius, at every axial offset (a core
        inside a cable shield; user decision Q32 of 2026.11); two unmarked
        wires on one axis touch. **The self terms do not depend on it**:
        pass ``include_internal=~shields`` to drop the internal inductance
        of a solid wire from the shields, as the solver does for
        ``conductor_type="cable_shield"`` (Q33). Without it a shield keeps
        $\\mu_0\\ell/(8\\pi)$ = 50 nH/m: the 100 m coax with 5 mm core and
        15 mm shield reads 31.97 µH instead of 26.97 µH.
    conductors
        Conductor label of every segment, shape ``(M,)`` (any values that
        can be compared for equality, e.g. conductor names; ``None``, the
        default: every segment is a conductor of its own). For two
        conductors lying beside each other (a pair of their segments closer
        than touching: on one axis, tilted against each other, crossing,
        leaving one junction), a point lies beside the partner when its
        foot falls inside the partner's whole conductor — the straight run
        of its segments with that label — so the sub-pieces of the two
        conductors add up to the lumped pair (audit W1A-02 of the calendar
        release). For segments that are not parallel the stretches inside,
        beside and away from the partner are found exactly, at any angle and
        for pieces of any length (audits W1R2-01, W1R3-01, W1R3-02: a
        slightly tilted core, a core crossing its shield's axis, two wires
        leaving a junction add up within 3e-12; up to W1R3 the rule stopped
        where the lateral distance changed by more than $r_i + r_j$ along a
        segment and at $|\\cos\\varphi| = 0.99$, and the pieces read up to
        1.6e-3 off the lumped pair). Pieces of one
        conductor and conductors that only meet end to end keep the
        filament integral. **Without labels**, unmarked touching pieces of
        one cable are not recognised as one conductor: they keep the rule
        of the single segments and do not add up (the 100 m pair of 5 and
        15 mm wires reads 40.34 µH in 0.25 m pieces against 43.47 µH
        lumped); the inside reading of a marked shield (``shields``) needs
        no labels and adds up either way (audit W1R2-08). The solver
        passes one label per conductor.

    Returns
    -------
    L : np.ndarray, shape (M, M)
        Symmetric partial-inductance matrix in H. Entry ``L[i, j]``
        is the partial mutual inductance between branch *i* and
        branch *j* (and the diagonal is the self-inductance + image).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        With an image convention other than ``"none"``: a segment
        that crosses the soil surface (its image intersects it) or
        lies in the surface plane (its image coincides with it). A
        segment of zero length.

    Notes
    -----
    The legacy loop-based implementation is kept as
    :func:`_build_inductance_matrix_loop` for regression testing.
    See :file:`tests/test_inductance_vectorised.py` for the
    bit-exact regression suite.
    """
    mode = _resolve_image(image, use_image)
    _check_touching_rule(touching)
    M = seg_endpoints.shape[0]
    if M == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 0), dtype=float)

    p1 = seg_endpoints[:, 0, :].astype(float, copy=False)  # (M, 3)
    p2 = seg_endpoints[:, 1, :].astype(float, copy=False)  # (M, 3)
    radii = np.asarray(wire_radii, dtype=float)
    internal = _include_internal_array(include_internal, M)
    if mode != "none":
        _check_image_geometry(p1, p2, radii, where="build_inductance_matrix")
    shield = _shield_array(shields, M)
    labels = _conductor_labels(conductors, M)
    hits: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
    L_dir, L_img = _inductance_blocks(
        p1,
        p2,
        radii,
        want_direct=True,
        want_image=mode != "none",
        self_from_rows=mode == "none",
        include_internal=internal,
        touching=touching,
        shields=shield,
        beside_hits=hits,
    )
    _apply_bundles(L_dir, p1, p2, radii, shield, labels, hits)
    if mode == "none":
        return L_dir
    if mode == "additive":
        return L_dir + L_img
    L = L_dir - L_img
    # A perfect conductor screens the soil: a pair on opposite sides of
    # the surface has no anti-parallel baseline (audit A2C-1).
    L[_opposite_sides(p1, p2)] = 0.0
    return L

neumann_mutual(p1_a: ndarray, p2_a: ndarray, p1_b: ndarray, p2_b: ndarray, *, min_distance: float = 1e-06, parallel_tol: float = 1e-09, touching: TouchingRule = 'exact') -> float

Neumann mutual-inductance integral between two straight segments.

Hybrid implementation:

  1. If the two segments are parallel (or anti-parallel) within parallel_tol on distinct axes, the closed-form Grover expression in _parallel_filaments_mutual() is used — exact, no quadrature error. This fast path covers the bulk of the typical inductance assembly (parallel PEN strands).
  2. With touching="exact", pairs that share an end point (chain neighbours, bends) or lie on one axis without overlapping use their closed forms (Grover 1946; see the module docstring).
  3. Otherwise the Neumann double integral is evaluated by 16×16 Gauss–Legendre quadrature: exact to round-off for pairs separated by more than about half their length, but only to -0.3 % ... +0.8 % for touching pairs (review pass 10, finding 10.46), and up to +250 % for nearly parallel wires 1 cm apart (audit round 2 of the calendar release). With touching="exact" such close pairs — nearest quadrature nodes within half the longer segment, no shared end point, not coaxial — are integrated semi-analytically instead (inner integral in closed form, outer panels graded towards the near-singular points; _close_pair_mutual()).

Accuracy (measured against adaptive mpmath references, audit round 3 of the calendar release): closed forms to round-off; filaments from one vertex to round-off on axis-parallel geometry and to 4e-10 in a general orientation down to 3e-9 rad (the angle itself carries about 1e-16/angle); close pairs as stated in _close_pair_mutual() (5e-11 above 1e-6 rad, 1.0e-9 at 1e-8 rad). Pairs inside the parallel tolerance — directions within parallel_tol in cos (4.5e-5 rad) and a lateral offset that varies by at most parallel_tol m along the segment — use the parallel closed form at the offset of the start point, off by about the relative variation of the offset (4.2e-9 for wires 1 cm apart tilted by 1e-10 rad over 5 m, 1.7e-5 at 1 µm).

The kernel \(1/r\) is clamped at min_distance to suppress the integrable singularity for segments that touch — physically the diagonal uses thin_wire_self_inductance() instead, so this only affects pathological inputs.

def neumann_mutual(
    p1_a: np.ndarray,
    p2_a: np.ndarray,
    p1_b: np.ndarray,
    p2_b: np.ndarray,
    *,
    min_distance: float = 1e-6,
    parallel_tol: float = 1e-9,
    touching: TouchingRule = "exact",
) -> float:
    """Neumann mutual-inductance integral between two straight segments.

    Hybrid implementation:

    1. If the two segments are **parallel** (or anti-parallel) within
       ``parallel_tol`` on distinct axes, the closed-form Grover
       expression in :func:`_parallel_filaments_mutual` is used —
       exact, no quadrature error. This fast path covers the bulk of
       the typical inductance assembly (parallel PEN strands).
    2. With ``touching="exact"``, pairs that share an end point (chain
       neighbours, bends) or lie on one axis without overlapping use
       their closed forms (Grover 1946; see the module docstring).
    3. Otherwise the Neumann double integral is evaluated by 16×16
       Gauss–Legendre quadrature: exact to round-off for pairs
       separated by more than about half their length, but only
       to -0.3 % ... +0.8 % for touching pairs (review pass 10,
       finding 10.46), and up to +250 % for nearly parallel wires 1 cm
       apart (audit round 2 of the calendar release). With
       ``touching="exact"`` such close pairs — nearest quadrature nodes
       within half the longer segment, no shared end point, not coaxial
       — are integrated semi-analytically instead (inner integral in
       closed form, outer panels graded towards the near-singular
       points; :func:`_close_pair_mutual`).

    Accuracy (measured against adaptive mpmath references, audit round 3
    of the calendar release): closed forms to round-off; filaments from
    one vertex to round-off on axis-parallel geometry and to 4e-10 in a
    general orientation down to 3e-9 rad (the angle itself carries about
    1e-16/angle); close pairs as stated in :func:`_close_pair_mutual`
    (5e-11 above 1e-6 rad, 1.0e-9 at 1e-8 rad). Pairs inside the
    parallel tolerance — directions within ``parallel_tol`` in cos (4.5e-5
    rad) and a lateral offset that varies by at most ``parallel_tol`` m
    along the segment — use the parallel closed form at the offset of the
    start point, off by about the relative variation of the offset
    (4.2e-9 for wires 1 cm apart tilted by 1e-10 rad over 5 m, 1.7e-5 at
    1 µm).

    The kernel $1/r$ is clamped at ``min_distance`` to suppress the
    integrable singularity for segments that touch — physically the
    diagonal uses :func:`thin_wire_self_inductance` instead, so
    this only affects pathological inputs.

    Parameters
    ----------
    p1_a, p2_a
        Endpoints of segment *a* as ``(x, y, z)`` arrays in metres.
    p1_b, p2_b
        Endpoints of segment *b*.
    min_distance
        Numerical floor on $|r_a - r_b|$ in metres.
    parallel_tol
        Tolerance on $||\\hat{u}_a\\cdot\\hat{u}_b| - 1|$ that
        triggers the closed-form fast path.
    touching
        ``"exact"`` (default) or ``"quadrature"`` (the 16x16 rule, the
        default up to 0.15.0) — the treatment of touching and coaxial
        pairs.

    Returns
    -------
    M : float
        Partial mutual inductance in H.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``touching`` is not ``"exact"`` or ``"quadrature"``, or if a
        segment of the generic (non-parallel, non-touching) case has
        zero length.
    """
    _check_touching_rule(touching)
    p1_a = np.asarray(p1_a, dtype=float)
    p2_a = np.asarray(p2_a, dtype=float)
    p1_b = np.asarray(p1_b, dtype=float)
    p2_b = np.asarray(p2_b, dtype=float)

    if touching == "exact":
        M_touch = _touching_mutual(p1_a, p2_a, p1_b, p2_b)
        if M_touch is not None:
            return M_touch

    # Fast path: parallel filaments with closed form.
    M_par = _parallel_filaments_mutual(
        p1_a,
        p2_a,
        p1_b,
        p2_b,
        parallel_tol=parallel_tol,
    )
    if M_par is not None:
        return M_par

    # Generic 3-D case: Gauss–Legendre quadrature.
    da = p2_a - p1_a
    db = p2_b - p1_b
    la = float(np.linalg.norm(da))
    lb = float(np.linalg.norm(db))
    if la <= 0.0 or lb <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("segment lengths must be positive")
    ua = da / la
    ub = db / lb
    dot = float(ua @ ub)
    if dot == 0.0:
        return 0.0  # perpendicular — orthogonality kills the integral
    s_nodes = 0.5 * (_GL_NODES + 1.0)
    w_nodes = 0.5 * _GL_WEIGHTS
    pts_a = p1_a[None, :] + s_nodes[:, None] * da[None, :]
    pts_b = p1_b[None, :] + s_nodes[:, None] * db[None, :]
    diff = pts_a[:, None, :] - pts_b[None, :, :]
    r = np.linalg.norm(diff, axis=2)
    if touching == "exact" and _needs_close_rule(
        p1_a, p2_a, p1_b, p2_b, float(r.min())
    ):
        return _close_pair_mutual(p1_a, p2_a, p1_b, p2_b)
    np.maximum(r, min_distance, out=r)
    inv_r = 1.0 / r
    integral = float(np.einsum("i,j,ij->", w_nodes, w_nodes, inv_r))
    return MU_0 / (4.0 * math.pi) * dot * la * lb * integral

parallel_segments_mutual(length: float, distance: float) -> float

Closed-form mutual inductance of two parallel coaxial segments.

For two segments of equal length \(\ell\) that share the same axis direction and are placed at perpendicular distance \(d\),

\[ M_\parallel(\ell, d) \;=\; \frac{\mu_0\,\ell}{2\pi} \Bigl[\ln\!\Bigl(\frac{\ell + \sqrt{\ell^2 + d^2}}{d}\Bigr) - \frac{\sqrt{\ell^2 + d^2} - d}{\ell}\Bigr]. \]

Used both as an internal closed-form fast path (when the segment pair geometry matches the assumption) and as a reference in the test suite.

required distance float

Perpendicular distance \(d\) between the two parallel axes in m. Must be > 0.

def parallel_segments_mutual(length: float, distance: float) -> float:
    r"""Closed-form mutual inductance of two parallel coaxial segments.

    For two segments of equal length $\ell$ that share the same
    axis direction and are placed at perpendicular distance $d$,

    $$
    M_\parallel(\ell, d) \;=\; \frac{\mu_0\,\ell}{2\pi}
    \Bigl[\ln\!\Bigl(\frac{\ell + \sqrt{\ell^2 + d^2}}{d}\Bigr)
          - \frac{\sqrt{\ell^2 + d^2} - d}{\ell}\Bigr].
    $$

    Used both as an internal closed-form fast path (when the segment
    pair geometry matches the assumption) and as a reference in the
    test suite.

    Parameters
    ----------
    length
        Segment length $\ell$ in m (both segments have the same).
    distance
        Perpendicular distance $d$ between the two parallel axes
        in m. Must be > 0.

    Returns
    -------
    M : float
        Partial mutual inductance in H.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``length`` or ``distance`` is not positive.
    """
    if length <= 0.0 or distance <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("length and distance must be positive")
    s = math.hypot(length, distance)
    return (
        (MU_0 * length)
        / (2.0 * math.pi)
        * (math.log((length + s) / distance) - (s - distance) / length)
    )

def perfect_mirror_self_pair_inductance(
    p1: np.ndarray,
    p2: np.ndarray,
    wire_radius: float,
    *,
    include_internal: bool = True,
    touching: TouchingRule = "exact",
) -> float:
    """Self-inductance contribution of a segment plus its earth image.

    For a single segment the *partial* self-inductance against itself
    uses the thin-wire formula. The image segment (mirrored at the
    soil surface) is treated as an external segment whose Neumann
    integral with the original is added to the total (the
    ``"additive"`` image convention of ADR-0004).

    Parameters
    ----------
    p1, p2
        Endpoints in metres (with $z > 0$ pointing into the soil).
    wire_radius
        Wire radius in m (only used for the thin-wire self term).
    include_internal
        Add the DC internal inductance $\\mu_0\\ell/(8\\pi)$ (default,
        see :func:`thin_wire_self_inductance`).
    touching
        Rule for the segment–image pair when the segment touches the
        surface with one end point (see :func:`neumann_mutual`).

    Returns
    -------
    L : float
        Self-inductance plus image contribution, in henries.
    """
    p1 = np.asarray(p1, dtype=float)
    p2 = np.asarray(p2, dtype=float)
    L_self = thin_wire_self_inductance(
        float(np.linalg.norm(p2 - p1)),
        wire_radius,
        include_internal=include_internal,
    )
    p1_img = _mirror(p1)
    p2_img = _mirror(p2)
    # Image segment runs in the opposite direction (current image of a
    # vertical filament is anti-parallel; for a horizontal filament it
    # is parallel). The general rule is: image of (p1 → p2) is
    # (p1' → p2'), with the *same* tangent direction up to the
    # sign of ẑ. For Neumann the dot product ǔ_a·ǔ_b takes care of
    # the sign automatically — we just feed the mirrored endpoints.
    L_image = neumann_mutual(p1, p2, p1_img, p2_img, touching=touching)
    return L_self + L_image

thin_wire_self_inductance(length: float, wire_radius: float, *, include_internal: bool = True) -> float

Closed-form self-inductance of a straight thin-wire segment.

Decomposed into the external Grover 1946 thin-wire term and the internal contribution from the magnetic field inside the conductor (uniform DC current distribution, non-magnetic material):

\[ L_\text{ext} \;=\; \frac{\mu_0\,\ell}{2\pi} \Bigl[\ln\!\Bigl(\frac{2\ell}{a}\Bigr) - 1\Bigr], \qquad L_\text{int} \;=\; \frac{\mu_0\,\ell}{8\pi}. \]

Adding the internal term reproduces the standard Oeding/Oswald loop-inductance formula (Gl. 9.13c) when used as the diagonal contribution of a two-wire loop. This is the package-wide internal-inductance convention (see the module docstring): a per-unit-length reference consistent with include_internal=True uses \(\mathrm{GMR} = a\,e^{-1/4}\). For the frequency-dependent internal impedance (skin effect) see groundfield.conductors.Conductor.internal_impedance_per_length().

Segment length \(\ell\) in metres.

required wire_radius float

Wire radius \(a\) in metres.

required include_internal bool

True (default) — add the internal-field contribution \(\mu_0 \ell / (8\pi)\) (uniform current, the DC limit). False — the pure external-field thin-wire formula.

def thin_wire_self_inductance(
    length: float,
    wire_radius: float,
    *,
    include_internal: bool = True,
) -> float:
    r"""Closed-form self-inductance of a straight thin-wire segment.

    Decomposed into the **external** Grover 1946 thin-wire term and
    the **internal** contribution from the magnetic field inside the
    conductor (uniform DC current distribution, non-magnetic
    material):

    $$
    L_\text{ext} \;=\; \frac{\mu_0\,\ell}{2\pi}
    \Bigl[\ln\!\Bigl(\frac{2\ell}{a}\Bigr) - 1\Bigr],
    \qquad
    L_\text{int} \;=\; \frac{\mu_0\,\ell}{8\pi}.
    $$

    Adding the internal term reproduces the standard Oeding/Oswald
    loop-inductance formula (Gl. 9.13c) when used as the diagonal
    contribution of a two-wire loop. This is the package-wide
    internal-inductance convention (see the module docstring): a
    per-unit-length reference consistent with
    ``include_internal=True`` uses $\mathrm{GMR} = a\,e^{-1/4}$.
    For the frequency-dependent internal impedance (skin effect) see
    :meth:`groundfield.conductors.Conductor.internal_impedance_per_length`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    length
        Segment length $\ell$ in metres.
    wire_radius
        Wire radius $a$ in metres.
    include_internal
        ``True`` (default) — add the internal-field contribution
        $\mu_0 \ell / (8\pi)$ (uniform current, the DC limit).
        ``False`` — the pure external-field thin-wire formula.

    Returns
    -------
    L : float
        Partial self-inductance in henries.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``length`` or ``wire_radius`` is not positive.
    """
    if length <= 0.0 or wire_radius <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("length and wire_radius must be positive")
    L_ext = (
        (MU_0 * length) / (2.0 * math.pi) * (math.log(2.0 * length / wire_radius) - 1.0)
    )
    if not include_internal:
        return L_ext
    L_int = (MU_0 * length) / (8.0 * math.pi)
    return L_ext + L_int

docs.title: carson
docs.text:
Carson 1926 correction for the earth-return path.

This module implements the earth-return correction described in ADR-0005: the finite-conductivity contribution that Carson 1926 derived for a homogeneous, semi-infinite, conductive half-space. It is defined against the anti-parallel (perfect-electric-conductor) image of the Neumann inductance matrix (build_inductance_matrix(image="antiparallel") in groundfield.coupling.inductance): the complete per-metre series impedance of a wire at height \(h\) is \(j\omega(\mu_0/2\pi)\ln(2h/\mathrm{GMR}) + \Delta Z_\text{Carson}\). Up to 0.15.0 the solver added it on top of the additive ("perfect-mirror") image instead, which double-counts the image (review pass 10, finding 10.20 / F32).

Mathematical background

Carson 1926 (Bell Syst. Tech. J. 5(4)) writes the earth-return correction to the per-unit-length series impedance of a long straight wire above a homogeneous earth as

\[ \Delta Z_\text{Carson}(\omega) \;=\; \frac{\omega\,\mu_0}{\pi}\, \bigl[P(a, \theta) \,+\, j\,Q(a, \theta)\bigr], \]

with the dimensionless Carson parameter

\[ a \;=\; D\,\sqrt{\omega\,\mu_0\,\sigma_\text{earth}} \;=\; \frac{D\sqrt{2}}{\delta(\omega)}, \qquad \delta(\omega) \;=\; \sqrt{2 \,/\, (\omega\mu_0\sigma_\text{earth})} \;[\text{skin depth in soil}], \]

where \(D = 2h_i\) for the self-impedance correction (\(\theta = 0\)) and \(D = \sqrt{(h_i + h_j)^2 + d_{ij}^2}\), \(\theta = \arctan(d_{ij} / (h_i + h_j))\) for the mutual-impedance correction between two parallel wires at heights \(h_i, h_j\) with horizontal separation \(d_{ij}\).

The functions \(P, Q\) are the real and imaginary parts of Carson's infinite integral \(J(p, q)\) (Carson eq. 29, with \(p = a\cos\theta\), \(q = a\sin\theta\)):

\[ J(p, q) \;=\; \int_0^{\infty}\!\bigl(\sqrt{\mu^2 + j}-\mu\bigr)\, e^{-p\mu}\cos(q\mu)\,d\mu \;=\; P(a,\theta) + j\,Q(a,\theta). \] Three evaluation regimes

We follow Carson's own discussion in section III of the original paper:

  1. Small \(a\) (\(a \le 0.25\)) — Carson's convergent series (eqs. 34/35), summed to order \(a^{12}\) with the exact constants \(c_2 = 5/4 + \ln 2 - \gamma_E\) and \(Q_0 = \tfrac12(\tfrac12 - \gamma_E)\). Closed form, only \(\sin / \cos / \ln\).
  2. Intermediate \(a\) (\(0.25 < a \le 15\)) — direct numerical quadrature of Carson's \(J(p, q)\): a composite, geometrically graded Gauss–Legendre rule for \(\theta \approx 0\) and QUADPACK's Fourier integrator otherwise. The original Carson 1926 series in that range is technically convergent but its recurrence is numerically delicate; quadrature is robust.
  3. Large \(a\) (\(a > 15\)) — Carson eqs. 36/37, asymptotic expansion in inverse powers of \(a\) up to \(a^{-7}\) (for \(\theta \le 1.4\) rad; steeper angles stay on the quadrature).

Accuracy against mpmath (review pass 10): the series and the quadrature are accurate to round-off for \(a \le 0.25\) and \(a > 0.25\) respectively, the asymptote to \(\le 10^{-7}\) above \(a = 15\); both regime boundaries are continuous to those levels. At large \(a\) and steep angles (\(\theta > 1.4\) rad, where the asymptote is not used) QUADPACK's Fourier rule limits the quadrature: 1.5e-9 at \(a = 8.9\) and 1.2e-7 at \(a = 28\), \(\theta = 89.9°\) — two wires 1 km apart at 1 kHz in 10 Ω·m (measured in audit round 3 of the calendar release against an independent quadrature of the \(\lambda\) integral). Until the calendar release 2026.11 the small-\(a\) form kept only the leading terms (no \(a^2\) term \(-(\pi/64)\,a^2\cos 2\theta\) of \(Q\), constant rounded to \(-0.0386\), \(P\) and \(Q\) off by up to \(2.4\cdot 10^{-4}\) and \(3.0\cdot 10^{-3}\) at \(a = 0.25\)) and the \(\theta = 0\) quadrature used 64 nodes on \([0, 30/p]\) (\(6\cdot 10^{-6}\) off at \(a = 0.25\)): the boundary at \(a = 0.25\) jumped by up to \(2.9\cdot 10^{-3}\) in \(Q\) (findings 10.46, 10.20).

Implementation notes
  • All formulas use SI units throughout. Carson's CGS pre-factor \(4\omega\) becomes \(\omega\mu_0 / \pi\) in SI.
  • \(\sigma_\text{earth}\) is an explicit argument; the caller is responsible for selecting the right resistivity (homogeneous \(1/\rho\), or upper-layer \(1/\rho_1\) with a warning).
  • \(\omega = 0\) or \(\sigma = 0\) short-circuit to 0+0j: the prefactor \(\omega\mu_0/\pi\) vanishes, so the (logarithmically diverging) \(Q\)-asymptote is harmless.
  • The complex-depth Deri/Semlyen approximation is provided as an internal sanity check (deri_semlyen_correction()); it is not the production code path.
  • A wire above the surface parallel to a wire below it is not a Carson pair (both wires overhead) nor a buried pair: its mutual impedance is the field transmitted into the soil, carson_mixed_mutual_correction() (Carson's \(J\) plus a bounded remainder for the buried wire's attenuation; audit round 2 of the calendar release, A2C-1).
References
  • Carson, J. R. (1926). Wave propagation in overhead wires with ground return. Bell Syst. Tech. J. 5(4), 539–554.
  • Deri, A.; Tevan, G.; Semlyen, A.; Castanheira, A. (1981). The complex ground return plane. IEEE Trans. PAS 100(8), 3686–3693.
  • Tleis, N. D. (2008). Power Systems Modelling and Fault Analysis, Newnes, ch. 3.

docs.title: carson_mixed_mutual_correction
docs.text:
carson_mixed_mutual_correction(omega: float, height: float, depth: float, horizontal_distance: float, sigma_earth: float) -> complex

Mutual impedance of an overhead wire parallel to a buried wire.

Per-unit-length mutual impedance of two long parallel horizontal wires on opposite sides of the soil surface — one at height \(h\) above it, one at depth \(d\) below it, horizontal separation \(x\) — over a homogeneous earth (quasi-static, the regime of Carson's theory):

\[ Z_m(\omega) \;=\; \frac{j\omega\mu_0}{\pi}\int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-\lambda h - u d}}{\lambda + u}\,\cos(\lambda x)\, d\lambda \;=\; \frac{\omega\mu_0}{\pi}\,J_m(p_h, p_d, q), \qquad u = \sqrt{\lambda^2 + j\omega\mu_0\sigma}, \]

the field of the overhead wire transmitted into the soil, with Carson's variables \(\lambda = \mu\sqrt{\omega\mu_0\sigma}\), \(p_h = h\sqrt{\omega\mu_0\sigma}\), \(p_d = d\sqrt{\omega\mu_0\sigma}\), \(q = x\sqrt{\omega\mu_0\sigma}\) and

\[ J_m \;=\; \int_0^\infty \bigl(\sqrt{\mu^2 + j} - \mu\bigr)\, e^{-p_h\mu - p_d\sqrt{\mu^2 + j}}\cos(q\mu)\,d\mu . \]

For \(d \to 0\) this is Carson's \(J\) of two overhead wires at heights \(h\) and \(0\); it is evaluated as Carson's \(J(p_h + p_d, q)\) (carson_p_q(), every regime) plus the bounded remainder of the buried wire's attenuation (_mixed_remainder()). Measured remainder: \(10^{-5}\) to \(4\cdot 10^{-1}\) of \(J\) (shallow conductors at 50 Hz in resistive soil to deep ones at 5 kHz in 10 \(\Omega\)m). The remainder is accurate to round-off; the whole agrees with an independent quadrature of the \(\lambda\) integral to 4.2e-9 for x ≤ 300 m (\(q \le 8.4\); f ≤ 1 kHz, \(\rho \ge 10\,\Omega\)m, h and d from 1 mm to 10 m; 1e-10 at 50 Hz) and to 1.2e-7 at x = 1 km at 1 kHz in 10 \(\Omega\)m (\(q = 28\)), the accuracy of Carson's \(J\) there (carson_p_q(); audit round 3 of the calendar release).

Image baseline. Relative to the anti-parallel (perfect-electric-conductor) image of build_inductance_matrix(image="antiparallel") this is the whole coupling: a perfect conductor screens the soil, so the baseline of a pair on opposite sides of the surface is zero. Treating the buried wire as an overhead wire at height \(d\) (Carson's correction on the mirrored-endpoint image, as the solver did up to audit round 2 of the calendar release) gives 36 % too little mutual reactance for a lead 1 m above a PEN at 0.7 m depth at 1 kHz, 14 % at 1 m offset, 3 % for a lead 0.1 m above it.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default omega float

Angular frequency in rad/s.

required height float

Height \(h\) of the overhead wire above the surface in m (positive).

required depth float

Depth \(d\) of the buried wire below the surface in m (positive).

required horizontal_distance float

Horizontal separation \(x\) of the two wires in m.

required sigma_earth float

Earth conductivity in S/m.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description Z complex

Per-unit-length mutual impedance in \(\Omega/\text{m}\).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

For a non-positive height or depth, or a negative distance.

References
  • Ametani, A.; Yoneda, T.; Baba, Y.; Nagaoka, N. (2009). An investigation of earth-return impedance between overhead and underground conductors and its approximation. IEEE Trans. Electromagn. Compat. 51(3), 860–867, doi:10.1109/TEMC.2009.2019953.
Source code in src/groundfield/coupling/carson.py 
def carson_mixed_mutual_correction(
    omega: float,
    height: float,
    depth: float,
    horizontal_distance: float,
    sigma_earth: float,
) -> complex:
    """Mutual impedance of an overhead wire parallel to a buried wire.

    Per-unit-length mutual impedance of two long parallel horizontal
    wires on **opposite sides** of the soil surface — one at height
    $h$ above it, one at depth $d$ below it, horizontal separation
    $x$ — over a homogeneous earth (quasi-static, the regime of
    Carson's theory):

    $$
    Z_m(\\omega) \\;=\\; \\frac{j\\omega\\mu_0}{\\pi}\\int_0^\\infty
    \\frac{e^{-\\lambda h - u d}}{\\lambda + u}\\,\\cos(\\lambda x)\\,
    d\\lambda
    \\;=\\; \\frac{\\omega\\mu_0}{\\pi}\\,J_m(p_h, p_d, q),
    \\qquad u = \\sqrt{\\lambda^2 + j\\omega\\mu_0\\sigma},
    $$

    the field of the overhead wire transmitted into the soil, with
    Carson's variables $\\lambda = \\mu\\sqrt{\\omega\\mu_0\\sigma}$,
    $p_h = h\\sqrt{\\omega\\mu_0\\sigma}$,
    $p_d = d\\sqrt{\\omega\\mu_0\\sigma}$,
    $q = x\\sqrt{\\omega\\mu_0\\sigma}$ and

    $$
    J_m \\;=\\; \\int_0^\\infty \\bigl(\\sqrt{\\mu^2 + j} - \\mu\\bigr)\\,
    e^{-p_h\\mu - p_d\\sqrt{\\mu^2 + j}}\\cos(q\\mu)\\,d\\mu .
    $$

    For $d \\to 0$ this is Carson's $J$ of two overhead wires at
    heights $h$ and $0$; it is evaluated as Carson's
    $J(p_h + p_d, q)$ (:func:`carson_p_q`, every regime) plus the
    bounded remainder of the buried wire's attenuation
    (:func:`_mixed_remainder`). Measured remainder: $10^{-5}$ to
    $4\\cdot 10^{-1}$ of $J$ (shallow conductors at 50 Hz in resistive
    soil to deep ones at 5 kHz in 10 $\\Omega$m). The remainder is accurate
    to round-off; the whole agrees with an independent quadrature of the
    $\\lambda$ integral to 4.2e-9 for x ≤ 300 m ($q \\le 8.4$; f ≤ 1 kHz,
    $\\rho \\ge 10\\,\\Omega$m, h and d from 1 mm to 10 m; 1e-10 at
    50 Hz) and to 1.2e-7 at x = 1 km at 1 kHz in 10 $\\Omega$m
    ($q = 28$), the accuracy of Carson's $J$ there (:func:`carson_p_q`;
    audit round 3 of the calendar release).

    **Image baseline.** Relative to the anti-parallel
    (perfect-electric-conductor) image of
    ``build_inductance_matrix(image="antiparallel")`` this is the
    whole coupling: a perfect conductor screens the soil, so the
    baseline of a pair on opposite sides of the surface is zero.
    Treating the buried wire as an overhead wire at height $d$
    (Carson's correction on the mirrored-endpoint image, as the solver
    did up to audit round 2 of the calendar release) gives 36 % too
    little mutual reactance for a lead 1 m above a PEN at 0.7 m depth
    at 1 kHz, 14 % at 1 m offset, 3 % for a lead 0.1 m above it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    omega
        Angular frequency in rad/s.
    height
        Height $h$ of the overhead wire above the surface in m
        (positive).
    depth
        Depth $d$ of the buried wire below the surface in m
        (positive).
    horizontal_distance
        Horizontal separation $x$ of the two wires in m.
    sigma_earth
        Earth conductivity in S/m.

    Returns
    -------
    Z : complex
        Per-unit-length mutual impedance in $\\Omega/\\text{m}$.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For a non-positive height or depth, or a negative distance.

    References
    ----------
    - Ametani, A.; Yoneda, T.; Baba, Y.; Nagaoka, N. (2009). An
      investigation of earth-return impedance between overhead and
      underground conductors and its approximation. *IEEE Trans.
      Electromagn. Compat.* **51**(3), 860–867,
      doi:10.1109/TEMC.2009.2019953.
    """
    if height <= 0.0 or depth <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("height and depth must be positive")
    if horizontal_distance < 0.0:
        raise ValueError("horizontal_distance must be non-negative")
    if omega <= 0.0 or sigma_earth <= 0.0:
        return 0.0 + 0.0j
    base = carson_mutual_correction(
        omega, height, depth, horizontal_distance, sigma_earth
    )
    k = math.sqrt(omega * MU_0 * sigma_earth)
    re, im = _mixed_remainder(k * height, k * depth, k * horizontal_distance)
    pref = omega * MU_0 / math.pi
    return base + complex(pref * re, pref * im)

carson_mutual_correction(omega: float, height_i: float, height_j: float, horizontal_distance: float, sigma_earth: float) -> complex

Carson earth-return correction between two parallel horizontal wires.

Evaluates the per-unit-length mutual-impedance correction

\[ \Delta Z_\text{mutual}(\omega) \;=\; \frac{\omega\mu_0}{\pi} \bigl[P(a_m, \theta_m) \,+\, j Q(a_m, \theta_m)\bigr], \]

with

\[ a_m \;=\; D_m \sqrt{\omega\mu_0\sigma_\text{earth}}, \quad D_m \;=\; \sqrt{(h_i + h_j)^2 + d^2}, \quad \theta_m \;=\; \arctan(d / (h_i + h_j)), \]

after Carson eq. 31. The parallel-wire assumption is the same as for ADR-0004's Neumann fast path; for non-parallel segments the caller must split into projection components.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default omega float

Angular frequency in rad/s.

required height_i float

Heights above earth surface in metres (both positive).

required height_j float

Heights above earth surface in metres (both positive).

required horizontal_distance float

Horizontal separation \(d\) between the two wires in metres.

required sigma_earth float

Earth conductivity in S/m.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description Z complex

Per-unit-length mutual correction in \(\Omega/\text{m}\).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If height_i or height_j is not positive, or if horizontal_distance is negative.

Source code in src/groundfield/coupling/carson.py 
def carson_mutual_correction(
    omega: float,
    height_i: float,
    height_j: float,
    horizontal_distance: float,
    sigma_earth: float,
) -> complex:
    """Carson earth-return correction between two parallel horizontal wires.

    Evaluates the per-unit-length mutual-impedance correction

    $$
    \\Delta Z_\\text{mutual}(\\omega) \\;=\\; \\frac{\\omega\\mu_0}{\\pi}
    \\bigl[P(a_m, \\theta_m) \\,+\\, j Q(a_m, \\theta_m)\\bigr],
    $$

    with

    $$
    a_m \\;=\\; D_m \\sqrt{\\omega\\mu_0\\sigma_\\text{earth}}, \\quad
    D_m \\;=\\; \\sqrt{(h_i + h_j)^2 + d^2}, \\quad
    \\theta_m \\;=\\; \\arctan(d / (h_i + h_j)),
    $$

    after Carson eq. 31. The parallel-wire assumption is the same
    as for ADR-0004's Neumann fast path; for non-parallel segments
    the caller must split into projection components.

    Parameters
    ----------
    omega
        Angular frequency in rad/s.
    height_i, height_j
        Heights above earth surface in metres (both positive).
    horizontal_distance
        Horizontal separation $d$ between the two wires in metres.
    sigma_earth
        Earth conductivity in S/m.

    Returns
    -------
    Z : complex
        Per-unit-length mutual correction in $\\Omega/\\text{m}$.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``height_i`` or ``height_j`` is not positive, or if
        ``horizontal_distance`` is negative.
    """
    if height_i <= 0.0 or height_j <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("heights must be positive")
    if horizontal_distance < 0.0:
        raise ValueError("horizontal_distance must be non-negative")
    if omega <= 0.0 or sigma_earth <= 0.0:
        return 0.0 + 0.0j
    h_sum = height_i + height_j
    D = math.hypot(h_sum, horizontal_distance)
    theta = math.atan2(horizontal_distance, h_sum)
    a = carson_parameter(D, omega, sigma_earth)
    P, Q = carson_p_q(a, theta)
    pref = omega * MU_0 / math.pi
    return complex(pref * P, pref * Q)

carson_p_q(a: float, theta: float) -> tuple[float, float]

Evaluate Carson's \(P(a, \theta)\), \(Q(a, \theta)\).

Dispatches to the appropriate regime based on the magnitude of \(a\):

  • \(a \le 0.25\): Carson's convergent series (eqs. 34/35) to order \(a^{12}\).
  • \(0.25 < a \le 15\): direct numerical quadrature of Carson's \(J(p, q)\) (Gauss–Legendre for \(\theta \approx 0\), QUADPACK Fourier integrator otherwise — audit 2026-07-08, WP-B2).
  • \(a > 15\): asymptotic expansion (Carson eqs. 36/37, \(a^{-7}\) term of \(Q\) with the corrected sign), except for \(\theta > 1.4\) rad where the expansion degrades and the quadrature path is used instead.

The small-\(a\) boundary is continuous to round-off, the large-\(a\) boundary to \(\le 10^{-7}\) (see the module docstring). Results are memoised on (a, theta).

Name Type Description Default a float

Dimensionless Carson parameter \(a = D \sqrt{\omega \mu_0 \sigma_\text{earth}}\). Must be \(\ge 0\).

required theta float

Angle of the image-distance vector to the vertical, in radians. \(\theta = 0\) for the self-impedance correction, \(\theta = \arctan(d/(h_i+h_j))\) for the mutual.

required

def carson_p_q(a: float, theta: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Evaluate Carson's $P(a, \\theta)$, $Q(a, \\theta)$.

    Dispatches to the appropriate regime based on the magnitude of
    $a$:

    - $a \\le 0.25$: Carson's convergent series (eqs. 34/35) to
      order $a^{12}$.
    - $0.25 < a \\le 15$: direct numerical quadrature of Carson's
      $J(p, q)$ (Gauss–Legendre for $\\theta \\approx 0$, QUADPACK
      Fourier integrator otherwise — audit 2026-07-08, WP-B2).
    - $a > 15$: asymptotic expansion (Carson eqs. 36/37, $a^{-7}$
      term of $Q$ with the corrected sign), except for
      $\\theta > 1.4$ rad where the expansion degrades and the
      quadrature path is used instead.

    The small-$a$ boundary is continuous to round-off, the large-$a$
    boundary to $\\le 10^{-7}$ (see the module docstring). Results are
    memoised on ``(a, theta)``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    a : float
        Dimensionless Carson parameter $a = D \\sqrt{\\omega
        \\mu_0 \\sigma_\\text{earth}}$. Must be $\\ge 0$.
    theta : float
        Angle of the image-distance vector to the vertical, in
        radians. $\\theta = 0$ for the self-impedance correction,
        $\\theta = \\arctan(d/(h_i+h_j))$ for the mutual.

    Returns
    -------
    P, Q : tuple[float, float]
        Real and imaginary parts of Carson's integral $J$.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``a`` is negative.
    """
    if a < 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"Carson parameter a must be non-negative, got {a}")
    return _carson_p_q_cached(float(a), float(theta))

def carson_parameter(distance: float, omega: float, sigma_earth: float) -> float:
    """Dimensionless Carson parameter $a = D \\sqrt{\\omega\\mu_0\\sigma}$.

    Parameters
    ----------
    distance
        Geometric distance $D$ in metres
        ($2h$ for self-impedance, $\\sqrt{(h_i+h_j)^2 + d^2}$
        for mutual).
    omega
        Angular frequency in rad/s.
    sigma_earth
        Earth conductivity in S/m.

    Returns
    -------
    a : float
        Dimensionless Carson parameter $a$ (0 for a non-positive
        ``omega`` or ``sigma_earth``).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``distance`` is negative.
    """
    if distance < 0.0:
        raise ValueError("distance must be non-negative")
    if omega <= 0.0 or sigma_earth <= 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return distance * math.sqrt(omega * MU_0 * sigma_earth)

def carson_self_correction(
    omega: float,
    height: float,
    sigma_earth: float,
) -> complex:
    """Carson earth-return correction for a single horizontal wire.

    Evaluates the per-unit-length impedance correction

    $$
    \\Delta Z_\\text{self}(\\omega) \\;=\\; \\frac{\\omega \\mu_0}{\\pi}
    \\bigl[P(a_s, 0) + j Q(a_s, 0)\\bigr],
    $$

    with $a_s = 2h\\sqrt{\\omega\\mu_0\\sigma_\\text{earth}}$ and
    $\\theta = 0$ (Carson eq. 30, ADR-0005).

    Parameters
    ----------
    omega
        Angular frequency $\\omega = 2\\pi f$ in rad/s.
    height
        Height of the wire above the earth surface in metres
        (positive — for buried wires use the Sunde-equivalent
        height).
    sigma_earth
        Earth conductivity in S/m
        ($\\sigma = 1/\\rho$ for a homogeneous earth).

    Returns
    -------
    Z : complex
        Per-unit-length earth-return correction in $\\Omega/\\text{m}$.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``height`` is non-positive.
    """
    if height <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("height must be positive (use |z| of the wire)")
    if omega <= 0.0 or sigma_earth <= 0.0:
        return 0.0 + 0.0j
    a = carson_parameter(2.0 * height, omega, sigma_earth)
    P, Q = carson_p_q(a, 0.0)
    pref = omega * MU_0 / math.pi
    return complex(pref * P, pref * Q)

docs.text:
deri_semlyen_correction(omega: float, height_i: float, height_j: float, horizontal_distance: float, sigma_earth: float) -> complex

Deri/Semlyen 1981 complex-depth approximation.

Replaces the Carson integral by the closed-form expression

\[ \Delta Z_\text{Deri-Semlyen} \;=\; \frac{j\omega\mu_0}{2\pi} \ln\!\Bigl(\frac{D'}{D}\Bigr), \]

with \(D = \sqrt{(h_i - h_j)^2 + d^2}\) the direct distance, \(D' = \sqrt{(h_i + h_j + 2p)^2 + d^2}\) the distance to a complex-depth image, and the complex penetration depth

\[ p \;=\; 1 \big/ \sqrt{j\omega\mu_0\sigma_\text{earth}}. \]

The Deri/Semlyen approximation is not the production code path. It is provided as an alternative independent estimator that the test suite can compare against the Carson series — agreement within \(\approx 5\,\%\) over the typical parameter range confirms that neither implementation contains a sign or pre-factor bug.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default omega float

Same meaning as in carson_mutual_correction().

required height_i float

Same meaning as in carson_mutual_correction().

required height_j float

Same meaning as in carson_mutual_correction().

required horizontal_distance float

Same meaning as in carson_mutual_correction().

required sigma_earth float

Same meaning as in carson_mutual_correction().

required

Returns:

Name Type Description Z complex

Per-unit-length earth-return correction in \(\Omega/\text{m}\) according to Deri/Semlyen 1981.

Notes

The "self" version is recovered by setting height_i = height_j and horizontal_distance = 0: the direct-distance term degenerates to the wire radius, which the caller must substitute manually (the formula does not include a wire-radius regularisation by itself).

Source code in src/groundfield/coupling/carson.py 
def deri_semlyen_correction(
    omega: float,
    height_i: float,
    height_j: float,
    horizontal_distance: float,
    sigma_earth: float,
) -> complex:
    """Deri/Semlyen 1981 complex-depth approximation.

    Replaces the Carson integral by the closed-form expression

    $$
    \\Delta Z_\\text{Deri-Semlyen} \\;=\\; \\frac{j\\omega\\mu_0}{2\\pi}
    \\ln\\!\\Bigl(\\frac{D'}{D}\\Bigr),
    $$

    with $D = \\sqrt{(h_i - h_j)^2 + d^2}$ the direct distance,
    $D' = \\sqrt{(h_i + h_j + 2p)^2 + d^2}$ the distance to a
    complex-depth image, and the complex penetration depth

    $$
    p \\;=\\; 1 \\big/ \\sqrt{j\\omega\\mu_0\\sigma_\\text{earth}}.
    $$

    The Deri/Semlyen approximation is **not** the production
    code path. It is provided as an alternative independent
    estimator that the test suite can compare against the Carson
    series — agreement within $\\approx 5\\,\\%$ over the typical
    parameter range confirms that neither implementation contains
    a sign or pre-factor bug.

    Parameters
    ----------
    omega, height_i, height_j, horizontal_distance, sigma_earth
        Same meaning as in :func:`carson_mutual_correction`.

    Returns
    -------
    Z : complex
        Per-unit-length earth-return correction in $\\Omega/\\text{m}$
        according to Deri/Semlyen 1981.

    Notes
    -----
    The "self" version is recovered by setting
    ``height_i = height_j`` and ``horizontal_distance = 0``: the
    direct-distance term degenerates to the wire radius, which the
    caller must substitute manually (the formula does not include
    a wire-radius regularisation by itself).
    """
    if omega <= 0.0 or sigma_earth <= 0.0:
        return 0.0 + 0.0j
    p = 1.0 / np.sqrt(1j * omega * MU_0 * sigma_earth)
    D = math.hypot(height_i - height_j, horizontal_distance)
    if D == 0.0:
        D = 1e-9
    D_prime = np.sqrt((height_i + height_j + 2.0 * p) ** 2 + horizontal_distance**2)
    return complex(1j * omega * MU_0 / (2.0 * math.pi) * np.log(D_prime / D))

def skin_depth(omega: float, sigma_earth: float) -> float:
    """Electromagnetic skin depth in soil.

    Returns $\\delta = \\sqrt{2 / (\\omega \\mu_0 \\sigma)}$ in
    metres. Diverges at $\\omega = 0$ (purely conductive earth-
    return path); the caller must handle that case by skipping the
    Carson correction altogether.

    Parameters
    ----------
    omega
        Angular frequency $\\omega = 2\\pi f$ in rad/s.
    sigma_earth
        Earth conductivity $\\sigma$ in S/m.

    Returns
    -------
    delta : float
        Skin depth in metres. ``+inf`` when ``omega`` or
        ``sigma_earth`` is zero.
    """
    if omega <= 0.0 or sigma_earth <= 0.0:
        return math.inf
    return math.sqrt(2.0 / (omega * MU_0 * sigma_earth))

docs.title: sommerfeld_inductance
docs.text:
Geometric Sommerfeld earth-return Green function (ADR-0006).

This module implements the rigorous geometric formulation of the inductive earth-return coupling described in ADR-0006. Compared to ADR-0005's Carson per-meter scaling, it integrates the actual vector-potential Green's function over the segment-pair geometry, which correctly handles short wires, non-parallel arrangements, and layered earth.

Mathematical background

For a horizontal current element in a stratified, quasi-static medium (\(z > 0\) soil, \(z < 0\) air, layer \(k\) with \(\gamma_k^2 = j\omega\mu_0\sigma_k\) and vertical wavenumber \(u_k = \sqrt{\lambda^2 + \gamma_k^2}\), \(u_0 = \lambda\) in air; time convention \(e^{+j\omega t}\)), the vector-potential Green's function of a source at depth \(z'\) and an observer at depth \(z\) is

\[ G(\rho, z, z') \;=\; \delta_{kj}\,\frac{e^{-\gamma_k R}}{R} \;+\; \int_0^{\infty}\! \lambda\,F_{kj}(\lambda; z, z')\, J_0(\lambda\rho)\,d\lambda , \]

with \(k\) / \(j\) the layers of observer / source. The spectral amplitude \(F\) follows from the continuity of \(A\) and \(\partial A/\partial z\) at every interface. For source and observer in the same layer \(k\) (top at \(z_{k-1}\), thickness \(t\), depths \(h, h'\) measured from its top) it is the closed form

\[ F_{kk} \;=\; \frac{\tilde R_\uparrow e^{-u_k(h+h')} + \tilde R_\downarrow e^{-u_k(2t-h-h')} + \tilde R_\uparrow\tilde R_\downarrow\bigl[e^{-u_k(2t-(h-h'))} + e^{-u_k(2t+(h-h'))}\bigr]} {u_k\,\bigl(1 - \tilde R_\uparrow \tilde R_\downarrow e^{-2u_k t}\bigr)}, \]

where \(\tilde R_\uparrow\), \(\tilde R_\downarrow\) are the generalised reflection coefficients of the stack above and below layer \(k\) (bottom-up / top-down recursions over \(r_{k,m} = (u_k - u_m)/(u_k + u_m)\)). For the homogeneous half-space this is the familiar \((\lambda/u_1)\Gamma e^{-u_1(h+h')}\) with \(\Gamma = (u_1-\lambda)/(u_1+\lambda)\); for two layers it is the four-term buried-in-layer-1 amplitude validated against Tsiamitros (2005) Eq. (8) (WP-D2, 2026-07-20); for \(n \ge 3\) layers the generalised \(\tilde R_\downarrow\) makes it exact as well (review pass 10, finding 10.35 — the historic \(n \ge 3\) path used the single air-image form and was 17–25 % off in \(X'\)). Pairs in different layers (including a buried / overhead pair over a layered earth) use the transmitted amplitude, obtained from the same interface conditions by a small linear solve per \(\lambda\).

The overhead pair keeps Carson's geometry, \(\lambda F_{00} = -\Gamma_s(\lambda) e^{-\lambda(H+H')}\), with the surface reflection coefficient \(\Gamma_s\) of the whole stack.

Earth-return correction and image conventions

The functions here return the earth-return correction \(\Delta Z\) that is added to \(j\omega L\), the Neumann partial-inductance matrix of groundfield.coupling.inductance.build_inductance_matrix(). The correction depends on which image that matrix carries (image=):

  • "none" — \(\Delta G = G - 1/R\), the exact quasi-static correction to free space. At DC the soil is magnetically transparent: no image at all.
  • "additive" (historic default, ADR-0004) — the matrix carries the perfect-magnetic-mirror image \(L_\text{img}\); the correction removes it exactly: \(\Delta Z_\text{additive} = \Delta Z_\text{none} - j\omega L_\text{img}\), with \(L_\text{img}\) computed by the same routine that added it (closed form for parallel pairs, the mirrored orientation for inclined and vertical segments).
  • "antiparallel" — \(\Delta Z_\text{none} + j\omega L_\text{img}\); for a pair on opposite sides of the surface, whose anti-parallel baseline is zero (a perfect conductor screens the soil), \(\Delta Z_\text{none} + j\omega L_\text{dir}\).

Before review pass 10 the image was removed as \(-1/R'\) integrated by the 16x16 outer rule and weighted with the direct orientation: vertical segments kept twice the image in the \(\sigma \to 0\) limit, and segments much longer than twice their depth lost 0.6 % (25 m) to 5.7 % (50 m) of the image term (finding 10.46).

Numerical method

Each segment pair is integrated by 16x16 Gauss–Legendre over the two segments; the closed-form direct term \((e^{-\gamma R}-1)/R\) is evaluated at every node, the spectral part \(S(\rho) = \int \lambda F J_0(\lambda\rho)\,d\lambda\) on 24 log-spaced \(\rho\) nodes and interpolated (segments assumed approximately horizontal, mean depths per segment). Segments that cross the soil surface or a layer interface are split there first.

Along the line of closest approach of a segment with itself, or of two segments that come close (wires beside each other, a core in its shield), the integrand has a kink: the \(\gamma^2 R/2\) term of the direct part and the corresponding term of \(S\), smoothed only over the decay length of the spectral weight. The tensor rule cannot follow it: the self correction of a buried segment was 4.8e-4 off at a quarter skin depth (100 Ω·m), up to 1.5e-3 for two wires 1 mm apart in 30 over 1000 Ω·m. Since user decision Q34

  • the self term of a (sub-)segment is the exact one-dimensional reduction \(2\int_0^L (L - u)\,g(u)\,du\) of its double integral (one spectral plan per segment, so \(g\) depends on \(u = |s - s'|\) only), with graded 16-node panels (_self_values());
  • a close pair (closest distance of the Gauss nodes below half the longer segment) gets a graded rule along the line of closest approach (_close_pair_values()); for two coinciding segments it is the self rule;
  • the other pairs keep the tensor rule (16x16, composite for segments longer than a quarter skin depth).

The self correction is within 1.1e-9 of a refined rule (1024 logarithmic \(\lambda\) nodes) and of an independent reference (closed-form direct part, the \(\mathrm{Ji}_0\) kernel of the spectral part; audit W3B) from 1 m and 0.01 skin depths to 3 km at 50 Hz and 1 kHz and has no step where the rule changes (below 3e-13); close pairs are within about 4e-8 of the same two references (3.5e-8 for two 1 m wires 1 mm apart in 30 over 1000 Ω·m at 1 kHz, 2.7e-9 at a quarter skin depth). Up to audit W3B-01 the logarithmic region of the \(\lambda\) grid had 64 nodes and short segments missed the skin-scale part of \(S\): 1e-5 … 7.4e-5 at 0.01 skin depths, up to 3e-4 at 1 m (9e-9 of the input impedance of a 200 m PEN in 1 m pieces). Both rules cost at most linearly in the length: a lumped conductor of 2 km between a rod and a junction is solved in 1.1 s within 0.21 GB (audit W2B-05: 28 s, 1.6 GB, about \(L^{2.7}\)).

The \(\lambda\) quadrature (review pass 10, finding 10.36) follows the F14 policy of groundfield.coupling.layered_green: a logarithmic region on \([\epsilon, \lambda_\text{b}]\) with \(\lambda_\text{b} \le \pi/(4\rho_\text{max})\) so that it is free of \(J_0\) oscillations, followed by Gauss panels of width \(\le \pi/\rho_\text{max}\) (16 nodes per \(J_0\) period), geometrically graded near the skin and decay scales, up to \(\lambda_\text{max} = 30/z\). Before the fix the log region ended at \(\max(p_\text{skin}, 1/z)\) regardless of the distance, so \(J_0\) went unresolved for distant pairs (Re −24 % at 200 m, +274 % at 400 m), and a 4096-panel cap truncated silently. The node budget is now explicit: beyond a soft limit the density drops to 8 nodes per period, and a SommerfeldResolutionWarning is raised instead of a silent truncation when even that does not fit.

build_sommerfeld_correction_matrices() evaluates several frequencies at once (finding 10.60): geometry, \(\lambda\) grid and the Bessel table are built once per pair and reused for every frequency whose grid is identical (the common case — the grid depends on the frequency only through skin scales above \(1/z\)). Each frequency's matrix equals the single-frequency result bit for bit.

Limit checks (built into the test suite)
  • \(\sigma_e\to 0\): \(\Delta Z_\text{none} \to 0\), and with image="additive" the correction cancels the mirror exactly for every orientation.
  • \(\sigma_e\to\infty\), overhead pair: \(-\Gamma \to -1\), the net image becomes the anti-parallel PEC image (Carson's baseline).
  • \(\sigma_e\to\infty\), buried pair: \(e^{-\gamma R} \to 0\) — the conductor is screened by the surrounding medium.
  • Long parallel buried wires: the per-metre limit reproduces Pollaczek's \(\frac{j\omega\mu_0}{2\pi}\bigl[K_0(\gamma d) - K_0(\gamma D') + J_P\bigr]\).
  • A three-layer earth with \(\rho_2 = \rho_3\) reproduces the two-layer result.
References
  • Stratton, J. A. (1941). Electromagnetic Theory, McGraw-Hill, §9-10 — derivation of the half-space vector potential.
  • Sommerfeld, A. (1909). Über die Ausbreitung der Wellen in der drahtlosen Telegraphie. Ann. Phys. 28(4), 665–736.
  • Wait, J. R. (1972). Electromagnetic Waves in Stratified Media, Pergamon. Ch. 3.
  • Chew, W. C. (1995). Waves and Fields in Inhomogeneous Media, IEEE Press, §2.1 (generalised reflection coefficients).
  • Tsiamitros, D. A. et al. (2005). Earth return path impedances of underground cables for the two-layer earth case. IEEE Trans. Power Delivery 20(3), 2174–2181.
