def create_engine(
    *,
    backend: Backend = "image",
    frequencies: Sequence[float] | npt.NDArray[Any] | None = None,
    segment_length: float | None = None,
    tolerance: float | None = None,
    max_iterations: int | None = None,
    earth_inductive_model: EarthInductiveModel | None = None,
    image_max_terms: int | None = None,
    image_series_tol: float | None = None,
    kernel: KernelKind | None = None,
    image_far_field: Literal["quadrupole", "point"] | None = None,
    options: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    sommerfeld_assembly: Literal["exact", "tabulated"] | None = None,
    max_segments: int | None = None,
    warn_segments: int | None = None,
) -> Engine:
    """Create a configured :class:`~groundfield.Engine`.

    Only the arguments you pass are forwarded; every argument left at
    ``None`` takes the :class:`~groundfield.Engine` default, so the engine
    is the single source of its defaults and option-level warnings of the
    engine concern only options you actually set. Backend-specific
    settings, such as the accuracy controls of ``mom_sommerfeld``
    (``epsabs``, ``epsrel``, ``lambda_max_factor``, ``max_osc_panels``) or
    the mesh of ``fem``, go into ``options``.

    The :class:`Engine` performs an automatic backend dispatch inside
    :meth:`Engine.solve`: when ``backend="image"`` (the default) is
    combined with a :class:`TwoLayerSoil` the call is forwarded to
    ``"image_2layer"``, and with a :class:`MultiLayerSoil` to
    ``"image_nlayer"``. Notebooks written for the homogeneous case
    therefore keep working when the soil model is replaced by a
    layered one.

    Parameters
    ----------
    backend
        Numerical method (:data:`~groundfield.solver.engine.Backend`).
        Leaving the default ``"image"`` lets the engine pick the
        matching layered image backend from the world's soil model.
    frequencies
        Frequencies in Hz (order preserved). Default: ``[50.0]``.
    segment_length
        Maximum segment length used to discretise the geometry, in m.
        Default: the engine default (0.5 m).
    tolerance, max_iterations
        Convergence parameters for iterative solvers. No backend reads
        them; they are forwarded only when given.
    earth_inductive_model
        Earth model for the inductive coupling between distributed
        conductor segments, effective only when a conductor sets
        ``inductance_model="neumann"``
        (:data:`~groundfield.solver.engine.EarthInductiveModel`):
        ``"sommerfeld"`` (engine default since 0.13.0; geometric
        integration of the σ-dependent vector-potential Green's function,
        validated against Pollaczek and Carson), ``"carson_series"``
        (Carson 1926 per-metre correction × length on the anti-parallel
        image baseline) or ``"perfect_mirror"`` (frequency-independent
        Neumann baseline with an additive image).
    image_max_terms
        Maximum number of image-charge series terms of the layered
        backends; a truncated series emits a
        :class:`~groundfield.solver.image_2layer.SeriesTruncationWarning`.
    image_series_tol
        Series stop tolerance: iteration ends when the geometric tail
        bound ``|K|^(n+1)/(1-|K|)`` falls below this value.
    kernel
        Field / reaction-matrix kernel (:data:`KernelKind`):
        ``"point"`` reproduces the results of earlier releases,
        ``"line"`` integrates each segment as a uniform line source.
        ``None`` keeps the engine default.
    image_far_field
        Form of the far images of the line kernel in two-layer soil,
        ``"quadrupole"`` (engine default) or ``"point"`` (faster)
        (:attr:`Engine.image_far_field <groundfield.Engine.image_far_field>`).
    options
        Backend-specific settings, keyed by backend name, e.g.
        ``{"mom_sommerfeld": {"epsabs": 1e-8}}`` or option models such as
        :class:`~groundfield.solver.MomSommerfeldOptions`; forwarded to
        :attr:`Engine.options <groundfield.Engine.options>`.
    sommerfeld_assembly
        ``"tabulated"`` (engine default since 2026.11) or ``"exact"``
        (per segment pair, the default up to 0.15.0) assembly of the
        Sommerfeld earth-return correction of inductive conductors
        (:attr:`Engine.sommerfeld_assembly
        <groundfield.Engine.sommerfeld_assembly>`).
    max_segments
        Resource limit of the engine: the largest number of leakage
        segments and of nodal unknowns it solves (:attr:`Engine.max_segments
        <groundfield.Engine.max_segments>`). Default: the module constant
        ``groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT`` (20 000).
    warn_segments
        Size of the soft notice of the engine: at or above this number of
        leakage segments or nodal unknowns the solve warns that it may take
        minutes (:attr:`Engine.warn_segments
        <groundfield.Engine.warn_segments>`). Default: the module constant
        ``groundfield.diagnostics.SOFT_LIMIT`` (5 000).

    Returns
    -------
    Engine
        The configured engine.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        An unknown keyword argument.
    ValueError
        A value the engine rejects.
    """
    engine_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"backend": backend}
    if options is not None:
        engine_kwargs["options"] = dict(options)
    if frequencies is not None:
        # Only a numpy array is converted; anything else (list, tuple, but
        # also a mistaken str or scalar) is validated by the Engine itself.
        if isinstance(frequencies, np.ndarray):
            engine_kwargs["frequencies"] = frequencies.tolist()
        else:
            engine_kwargs["frequencies"] = frequencies
    explicit = {
        "segment_length": segment_length,
        "tolerance": tolerance,
        "max_iterations": max_iterations,
        "earth_inductive_model": earth_inductive_model,
        "image_max_terms": image_max_terms,
        "image_series_tol": image_series_tol,
        "image_far_field": image_far_field,
        "sommerfeld_assembly": sommerfeld_assembly,
        "max_segments": max_segments,
        "warn_segments": warn_segments,
    }
    engine_kwargs.update({k: v for k, v in explicit.items() if v is not None})
    if kernel is not None:
        if "kernel" in Engine.model_fields:
            engine_kwargs["kernel"] = kernel
        elif kernel != "point":
            # Transitional: an engine without the ``kernel`` option only
            # has the point kernel.
            raise ValueError(
                f"kernel={kernel!r} is not available in this build; only "
                "the point kernel is."
            )
    return Engine(**engine_kwargs)

def run_simulation(world: World, engine: Engine) -> FieldResult:
    """Solve ``world`` with ``engine``; identical to ``world.solve(engine)``.

    The call goes through :meth:`World.solve` and therefore has exactly
    its semantics, including the source snapshot: the world's sources
    are restored after the solve even if a backend changes them in
    flight, and the handles returned by :func:`create_source` stay
    attached to the world.

        The world to solve.
    engine
        The engine configuration.

    Returns
    -------

        The solution.

docs.title: Generators
docs.text:
The generators package builds complete worlds of TN low-voltage networks (Ortsnetze): a substation earth, the foundation earths of the buildings, cable distribution cabinets, the PEN network that joins them and, optionally, a fall-of-potential measurement set-up. It contains no physics of its own; it decides geometry and topology and hands a World to the solver. Design and validation programme: ADR-0009.

Two front-ends share one data model:

  • TnNetworkGenerator(config, seed=...) draws a network from population parameters (TnNetworkConfig: building counts and types, soil, placement, PEN topology), every numeric field a fixed value or a Distribution;
  • LvNetworkLayout composes one deterministic network step by step, as an engineer draws it: real building footprints (OSM), a hand-placed substation and cabinets, PEN cables routed on a Manhattan grid around the buildings, and the measurement loop.

Both produce a pure-data NetworkPlan; one materialiser, materialise_plan(plan), turns every plan into a World, so both front-ends build foundations, concrete shells, PEN junctions and measurement leads in the same way.

docs.title: Mathematical and physical context
docs.text:
The generated world is solved like any other: Laplace's equation in the layered soil with the electrodes as equipotential clusters and the PEN network as branches. What the generator controls is the parameter space of the study (AP1):

Axis Config field building mix (single-family houses, small and medium commercial) building_counts, building_types grounding system per building type (foundation, ring, rods, strips) BuildingTypeSpec.grounding (GroundingSystemSpec of ElectrodeSpec) penetration of foundation earths FoundationElectrodeSpec.presence_prob concrete encasement (moisture) FoundationElectrodeSpec.concrete_rho_ohm_m, concrete_thickness_m substation earth substation cable distribution cabinets cabinets PEN topology and cable data pen_topology, pen soil \(\rho_1\), \(\rho_2\), \(h_1\) soil (HomogeneousSoilSpec, TwoLayerSoilSpec, MultiLayerSoilSpec)

Reproducibility. All random draws come from one generator seeded by seed (or rng= of build, plan and sample_world), in a canonical order: the same configuration and seed give the same world, independent of the order in which mapping keys were written. sample_world(rng=...) also returns the resolved configuration (every distribution replaced by its drawn value); it replays the world exactly when no per-site draws remain (presence probabilities 0 or 1, no placement jitter), otherwise keep the seed or the plan / world JSON. Successive build() or plan() calls on one generator draw successive realisations from its stream; build() right after plan() (no rng= in either, nothing drawn from generator.rng since, the same configuration) gives the world of that plan — up to audit W3R2B it drew a second realisation, another world with placement jitter. The foundation penetration mask of the layout builder is a stable hash of the building ids and is nested in the penetration rate (a house equipped at 10 % is also equipped at 20 %).

Foundations and PEN cables. A mesh foundation (style="mesh") is one wire electrode per mesh line at every orientation (<name>, <name>_w<j>, bonded into one cluster), bare or encased; an encased foundation (concrete_rho_ohm_m) carries the concrete shell on every wire, its cross-braces included (DIN 18014, see concrete shells). The image family solves one uniform current per straight wire (since user decision Q30 also inside a grid, so a mesh electrode built by hand and the generated foundation of bonded wires are the same model). Against the per-segment mom solution (100 Ω·m, 1 m segments; mom uses the point kernel), one current per wire is +1.1 % with the default line kernel and +0.3 … +0.5 % with kernel="point" for 10 m 2 × 2 to 30 m 4 × 4 meshes; one current for the whole mesh was +2.4 … +3.7 % (point kernel +1.5 … +3.1 %) and depended on the orientation. A rectangle without cross-braces (style="ring", or "mesh" with n_x = n_y = 1) is one strip per side at every orientation (user decision Q38); up to that decision an axis-aligned one was one grid_mesh electrode connected at its centre, and per side its input impedance is lower by less than 1 % up to aspect ratio 4 and 2 % up to 50 for a short side of at least 1 m over the soils of the AP1 grid, equal for a square (scope and numbers on the concrete-shell page). electrode_currents[<name>] and grounding_impedance(<name>) therefore refer to the first wire (the local −y side, whose start, a corner of the rectangle, is the connection point of conductors attached to <name> by name); use cluster_impedance or the sum over the wires for the foundation. A rectangle at a multiple of 90° is rotated exactly (no round-off), so the local −y side stays the first wire. A polygon outline is one closed polyline with one owner per straight side (one current per straight wire, user decisions Q30, Q44). The deprecated concrete_model has no effect (drop the argument, see Deprecations); an outline narrower than MIN_FOUNDATION_SIDE_M (1 m) is widened to it, with a warning, for both foundation_outline="ombr" and "polygon".

Cable cabinets per building group (user decisions Q22 and Q35). In the star topology TnNetworkGenerator places one cable cabinet per building group, at the far end of the houses it feeds (CabinetConfig.placement=None, the default): the buildings are ordered by their bearing around the substation, counter-clockwise from the widest angular gap between two neighbouring bearings, and cut into as many runs of consecutive bearings as there are cabinets (count_per_100_buildings or fixed_count), of sizes that differ by at most one (StarCabinetTopology.group_buildings); the cabinet of a group stands on the ray from the substation through the group's centroid, CabinetConfig.end_clearance_m (1 m, positive) beyond the largest projection on that ray of the group's earth electrodes (horizontal wires and rods) plus the plan extent of the cabinet's own grounding — when it stands there within CabinetConfig.max_far_end_gap_m (20 m, positive, larger than end_clearance_m) of the nearest electrode of its group: a cabinet stands next to the houses it feeds. A wider group, whose centroid ray leads past its houses, has its cabinet on the ray through its far-end building (the largest projection of its position on the direction of the centroid, ties to the one nearest to that direction), end_clearance_m beyond that building's electrodes. The cabinet feeds its group (audits W1B-01, W1B-02). 10 houses and one small commercial building had their cabinet 50.4 m from the nearest building on the centroid ray (drops 527.4 m), now 1.56 m (311.8 m) on the far-end ray; with the far-end ray for every group, six houses of the 50-house grid were fed straight from the substation (up to 116.8 m). The plan records per cabinet which rule placed it, PlannedSite.cabinet_rule ("centroid_ray" / "far_end_ray"), and its distance from the group on the centroid ray, PlannedSite.centroid_ray_gap_m (None for every other site and for cabinets of a given placement or of the radial topology; materialising ignores both).

The threshold is a step, kept for 2026.11 (user decision D7, audit W1R2-02). Groups lie on both sides of it: on the centroid ray the groups of the default 50-house grid stand 8.8 … 12.8 m from their houses, those of the 100-house grid 10.05 … 23.01 m (its two groups beyond 20 m are on the far-end ray; 15 / 25 m put four / none there), and over the 80 AP1 mixes the 118 groups beyond it stand 20.21 … 53.56 m from their houses and the largest gap kept is 18.84 m (19 mixes have a group between 15 and 25 m). A group whose distance crosses the threshold moves its cabinet by up to the width of the group, and the results jump:

layout change (homogeneous 100 Ω·m) cabinet moves drops R at 50 Hz X at 1 kHz, inductive PEN (carson_series / sommerfeld) 50-house grid, house columns 32.0 → 32.2 m apart (one group 19.99 → 20.22 m) 141.8 m 1 788.9 → 1 443.0 m −0.36 % (−0.14 % beyond the smooth trend) −21.6 / −18.9 % 100-house grid, columns across 22.95 m (two groups cross 20 m) 65.6 m each +15.8 % −0.03 % +1.5 / −3.1 % 80 houses + 5 medium commercial (AP1), one group at 20.21 m: max_far_end_gap_m 20 → 20.5 m 31.4 m 1 960.6 → 1 968.2 m −0.02 % +1.5 / +1.1 %

The 100-house row is the difference of straight lines through three spacings on each side of the crossing, at the crossing; R at 50 Hz with the image backend (2 m and 1 m segments agree), Z at 1 kHz with the isolated Neumann PEN in 5 m pieces. A study that varies the layout can read where a group crosses from the plan. A cabinet whose electrodes would come closer than end_clearance_m to those of another site — a building of its own or of another group, the substation, another cabinet — raises a ValueError that names both (3 of 100 random layouts of 200 houses 12 m apart; none of the default grids and AP1 mixes). In the default grid of 30 houses (three rows of ten, 25 m × 30 m, the substation in the middle row) the groups are the western and the eastern half, with their cabinets at (−118.5, 0) m and (118.5, 0) m; each main runs along the middle row, whose houses are joined to it, and the 20 houses of the outer rows tap it with drops of 25 m (before: both cabinets west of the substation, at (−180, 0) m and (−140, 0) m on a strip along the substation row, and 25 drops of 1 140 m, the 15 eastern ones from the substation, 3.5 … 106.5 m). A single group around the substation (one cabinet for a row through it) gets its cabinet beyond its farthest house, ties to the first in bearing order. A given CabinetConfig.placement keeps the former rule — the given positions, every building fed by its nearest cabinet (Manhattan metric) — and a configuration stored before the decision carries the former strip and keeps its cabinets. In RadialTrunkTopology a building in a substation slot that no trunk crosses taps its feeder's trunk at the closest pair, like the buildings of the cabinets, instead of getting its own line from the substation (default 30 houses: drops 1 115 → 778 m, 14 → 4 from the substation, those of the two feeders without a trunk).

In TnNetworkGenerator every cable cabinet has its own PEN cable, as the topology documents: from the substation (StarCabinetTopology), or one cable per trunk segment (RadialTrunkTopology). A service drop taps the cable path that feeds its own building — the cable of its cabinet, or the trunk from the substation to its tap source, for a building in a substation slot its feeder's whole trunk — at the point nearest to the building: a leakage-free tap junction pen_tap_<k> that splits the cable into sections <cable>_s<k>, or the substation or cabinet at the end of the cable; a building in a substation slot of a feeder without a trunk is connected to the substation. The router guarantees that a drop never starts on another building's drop, never runs along a cable (the one it taps, a trunk, another cabinet's main) farther than one minimum section, and that no cable section is shorter than that minimum section, 1 cm (a tap closer to a node is that node; longer for PEN radii above 7.3 mm, so that every section stays a finite resistance). "Along" means both ends of a cable section within 1 cm of the drop's line; the one overlap left is that 1 cm, where a foundation touches the end node of its cable from beyond and is tapped 1 cm before the node. Drops that leave one tap in one direction — the drops of houses behind each other, such as the five drops of the 5-house radial network from the substation ring along −x, or the five drops of the 10-house star from the substation — lie side by side at the touching distance \(2r\) of the PEN (decision D9 of 2026.11), so that only neighbours touch: sorted by length, shortest first (equal lengths in plan order), and centred on their common axis, drop \(k\) of \(n\) at \((k - (n - 1)/2)\,2r\) along the normal \((-d_y, d_x)/|d|\) of the drop direction \(d\). The plan records the offset as PlannedBranch.axis_offset_m; the materialiser moves both ends of the conductor by it, and the drop stays attached to its tap and its building (it starts up to \((n - 1)/2 \cdot 2r\) off the tap, 2 cm in a row of five). Two drops of one node are in a row when their start points lie within \(2r\) of each other and the end of the shorter one within \(2r\) of the line of the longer one — the overlap criterion — so the rows hold under placement jitter (audit W3R2B-01): drops that are not exactly parallel are shifted along one common normal (recorded as PlannedBranch.axis_offset_normal_xy), each just far enough to lie at least \(2r\) from every shorter one, and a drop that would come closer than touching to a drop of a row — of the same tap, or of a tap 1 … 4 cm away on the same trunk — joins the row. No generated network reports an overlap (star and radial networks of 5 … 200 houses, jitter_m 0 … 0.1 m), and the input impedance is continuous in the jitter: the reactance of the 10-house radial network at 1 kHz moves by −8.5e-10 at 1 nm and −4.5e-4 at 1 mm (carson_series; up to then +2.4 % at 1 nm, where the rows fell apart). Before D9 such drops lay on one axis and the inductance matrix read them as a bundle in which every pair touches, which no cross-section of four or more equal wires realises; gf.diagnose() reported every pair (audit W3B-05). With an inductive PEN (5 m pieces, 100 Ω·m) the input reactance moves at 1 kHz by −2.3 / −2.7 % (carson_series / sommerfeld) in the 5-house radial network, −2.3 / −2.8 % with 10 houses, −1.1 / −1.3 % in the 10-house star, and by at most 1.1e-6 (30 houses) and 5e-4 (80 and 200 houses, both frequencies) in the radial networks; the star networks of 5, 30, 80 and 200 houses have no such drops and build the same world, those of 40, 60, 100, 120, 140 and 180 houses have (the 60-house star: X −1.0e-3 / −6.1e-4 at 50 Hz / 1 kHz under carson_series, −1.3e-3 / −8.1e-4 under sommerfeld; the 40-house star, all 40 drops in rows, 3e-7), and plans written before (no offsets) build the worlds they built. LvNetworkLayout draws no rows. Conductors that overlap otherwise (in a hand-made plan) are evaluated as touching wires. A drop may also pass over other buildings' foundations, 0.2 m above their wires (PEN at 0.6 m, foundations at 0.8 m): the contact of a house lies at the corner of the side facing its cable (the tie rule below), so a drop to a house behind others of its grid column runs above their side wires. In the default grids of 10 to 200 houses that is 0 … 100 % of the drops (star, 30 houses: all 20 drops, each over 5 m above a side wire of the middle-row house it passes on its way from the main, 100 m in all; star 50, 150 and 200: none; radial 150: 87 of 140 drops, 1 805 m, up to 40 m over 4 houses); drops are not routed around foundations (user decision Q42). A drop has no inductive coupling to these wires in the field model (an electrode carries no current along itself), a bare one leaks next to them through the soil; moved 1 m aside as a whole, those drops change the input impedance by at most 0.006 % with an insulated PEN and by up to −0.40 % with a bare one (default grids of 30 and 150 houses, 50 Hz and 1 kHz; see the known limitations). The layout builder merges cable nodes closer than the same length.

Where conductors meet a site (user decisions Q41 and Q43). Every conductor the generators route to a site with a horizontal earth electrode ends at the point of that electrode nearest to it, in TnNetworkGenerator and in the layout builder: at a foundation of every form (rectangles at any orientation, building outlines) since user decision Q41, at a circular ring (RingElectrodeSpec, e.g. the default substation of both generators, a 4 m ring with four rods) and a strip since user decision Q43. A site with horizontal electrodes and rods is met at the nearest point of the horizontal ones, a site with several of them (the large_industry ring, mesh and strips) at the nearest point of all; rods (vertical) keep their head. A circle is met at its exact nearest point (it is searched on an inscribed polygon with a sagitta of at most 1 mm and refined to the circle). The default mains now leave the substation ring at its point nearest to their cabinets — the western ones at (−4, 0) m instead of (4, 0) m, through the ring — and drops from the substation at the point of the ring nearest to the house.

  • a service drop is the shortest connection in plan between its feeding cable and the horizontal wires of the building (their closest pair): the tap on the cable and the end on the foundation, ring or strip, at the PEN depth (layout builder: at the wire's depth), attached to the wire that holds the point (PlannedBranch.end_contact, a PlannedContact);
  • a cable leaving a substation or cabinet with horizontal electrodes starts at their point nearest to its next node;
  • a building that a cable crosses is joined to it and fed by it: a cable of the building's feeding path that crosses or touches its foundation in plan is joined to the wire there, and the building gets no drop; every trunk of the radial topology counts as a cable of the feeding path for this rule (a building in a substation slot has no cable of its own), and in the star topology a building that a main crosses is fed by that main's cabinet (the nearest of the cabinets whose mains cross it, ties to the lower cabinet index) instead of its nearest one; a main that crosses a building it does not feed stays unjoined (no cross-tie between cabinets through a house); where the foundation touches the cable at a node (a cabinet on a wire) and the cable crosses it elsewhere, it is joined where it crosses (audit R5A-03), otherwise the joint lies 1 cm from the node (audits R4A-02, R4B-01);
  • a drop whose closest pair lies at such a joint starts there, on the cable (audit R4A-01); a drop from a node that would run along a trunk or another main (both ends of a section within 1 cm of the drop's line, audit R5A-01) starts where it leaves it, at its node at the end of the shared stretch (audit R4B-01);
  • the layout builder keeps its taps on the layout polyline, where the cable's junctions are. The leading run of waypoints inside the start site's closed electrodes (a rectangle, a building outline, a circle) and the trailing run inside the end site's are part of those sites (audit R6A-01 — a router corner inside a small cabinet ring was a node that houses tapped, 82 of 2 540 drops in 200 random layouts with a 2 m cabinet ring started inside it), and the segment that leaves (enters) the site is clipped at the projection of the site's point nearest to its far waypoint. Every other passage of the cable through the closed electrodes of the substation or a cabinet — another cabinet on its way, or its own start or end site when it comes back through it — is clipped the same way: the cable reaches the site where it enters and leaves it where it leaves, joined to it there, and the waypoints in between are part of it (audits W1B-03, W1B-04; up to then a cable to a far cabinet kept a tap inside a near cabinet's ring, and a leg that left its start site and came back through it, or overshot its cabinet, was merged into the site and lost its taps: 142.8 m instead of 30.0 m of drops in the audit's loop case). So no tap and no corner lies inside the foundation of the substation or a cabinet, also for a rotated, polygon or offset one; a tap at a clip point, or at the site's waypoint, is the site (audits R4A-03, R5A-02). A cable through a house foundation is not joined to it: the house keeps its own drop, of no length in plan where the cable crosses its foundation;
  • ties go to the lowest wire index, then to the smallest arc position along the wire: a cable parallel to the side facing it meets the side at the start of the range of equal distance, for a side it passes along its whole length the corner where that wire starts.

Sites with rods only keep the connection point of their anchor (the head of the first rod), and so does everything attached by name (site_anchor_point, create_conductor(start=<foundation>)). site_contact_wires(site) returns the wires the rule uses (named site_foundation_wires before user decision Q43, foundations only). materialise_plan rejects a PlannedContact that names no horizontal wire (foundation, ring, strip) of the branch's site (a direct materialise_branch call without foundation_wires checks only that it names a strip, polyline or ring electrode; a NetworkPlan rejects another site's electrode when it is validated) or lies farther from its wire — from the exact circle of a ring — than one minimum cable section (1 cm; a joined cable's point may lie that far off the wire it crosses; audit R4A-05). LvNetworkLayout.plot(world=...) draws the drops as built (tap to foundation contact) instead of the layout's centroid stubs.

Coordinates. Both generators build in local coordinates around the origin. SubstationConfig.position moves the substation only: the buildings, cabinets and the measurement stay around (0, 0), so a substation placed at projected coordinates builds a world that mixes projected and local coordinates (10 houses with the substation at the UTM origin: one PEN cable of 33 118 km), which diagnose() reports and the solve warns about with MixedCoordinatesWarning; RadialTrunkTopology then drops every building and fails to build (audit W2R2-07). To place a network at projected coordinates, build it around the origin and translate the whole built world — every electrode, conductor and junction by the same offset; groundfield has no public helper for that, and the solve does not need it, since every result depends on coordinate differences only (the translated network of 10 houses has the input impedance of the local one to twelve digits).

Measurement set-up. A fall-of-potential measurement is a two-terminal source between the earthing system and an auxiliary electrode; the current and probe leads end on leakage-free junctions at the instrument, and measured_impedance(result) returns the reading of the simulated earth tester, probe voltage over source current. The leads can be overhead or buried (overhead_lead, buried_lead); their inductive coupling to the PEN network is part of the solve.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import groundfield as gf

config = gf.TnNetworkConfig(
    soil=gf.TwoLayerSoilSpec(rho_1=gf.Uniform(low=80.0, high=300.0), rho_2=100.0, h_1=5.0),
    building_counts={"residential": 5},
)
world = gf.TnNetworkGenerator(config, seed=42).build()
again = gf.TnNetworkGenerator(config, seed=42).build()
assert gf.world_fingerprint(world) == gf.world_fingerprint(again)   # same seed, same world

stats = gf.world_statistics(world)
# each house has a 2 × 2 mesh foundation, one wire electrode per mesh line
assert stats["n_electrodes_by_kind"]["polyline"] == 5 * 6
result = gf.create_engine(frequencies=[50.0]).solve(world)
assert 1.0 < result.input_impedance()[0].real < 5.0       # Ω, substation with the PEN network

Tutorial T06 builds a network synthetically and from OpenStreetMap data, T07 adds the fall-of-potential measurement. The German names of releases up to 0.15.0 (OrtsnetzLayout, kvs, KvsConfig, …) keep working with a DeprecationWarning; see Deprecations and the glossary.

docs.title: generators
docs.text:
World generators for reference networks.

This subpackage hosts the factory layer that turns high-level parameter sets — for example "N single-family houses on a two-layer soil" — into a fully populated groundfield.World that the solver can consume.

The framework is organised in five composable spec layers:

  • distributions — Constant, Uniform, Normal, LogNormal, Weibull, Discrete, Categorical. Each numerical / categorical field of any spec class accepts a fixed value or a Distribution.
  • electrode_specs — single-electrode specs (rod / ring / strip / foundation) with presence_prob and offset_xy_m.
  • grounding — GroundingSystemSpec composes a list of ElectrodeSpec into one cluster.
  • placement — Manhattan-grid and explicit-coordinate placement strategies.
  • soil_specs — homogeneous / two-layer / multi-layer soil specs that resolve to the groundfield.soil.models types.
  • building — BuildingTypeSpec bundles a name with a grounding system and an optional plot size.

Two front-ends compose these layers into a TN low-voltage network: TnNetworkGenerator (stochastic population parameters) and LvNetworkLayout (real footprints and routed PEN cables). Both produce a pure-data NetworkPlan; one materialiser (materialise_plan()) turns every plan into a groundfield.World.

See docs/adr/0009-world-generators.md for the design rationale and the validation programme.

docs.title: AuxiliaryElectrodePlacement
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Auxiliary current electrode (Hilfserder) for a fall-of- potential measurement of the substation grounding.

The auxiliary electrode closes the test-current loop. It is materialised in LvNetworkLayout.to_world() via GroundingSystemSpec.build_at(), giving the user full control over its geometry (single rod, ring, mesh, foundation, or any combination). The default is a bundle of three 0.5 m rods in a 0.5 m equilateral triangle, parallel-bonded — matching real-world practice and yielding a spreading resistance roughly a third of a single rod.

In LvNetworkLayout.to_world() the substation's current source returns its current through the auxiliary electrode's anchor (Source.return_to), so the potential field develops the expected dipole pattern (positive trumpet at the substation, negative trumpet at the auxiliary electrode). Up to 0.15.0 the solver ignored return_to and a second source with phase_deg=180 on the auxiliary electrode stood in for it.

total_length_m() -> float

Route length of the stub in m.

Sums the Manhattan length abs(dx) + abs(dy) of every piece between consecutive stub_waypoints.

Type Description float

Length of the stub in m.

Source code in src/groundfield/generators/layout/routing.py 
def total_length_m(self) -> float:
    """Route length of the stub in m.

    Sums the Manhattan length ``abs(dx) + abs(dy)`` of every piece
    between consecutive ``stub_waypoints``.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Length of the stub in m.
    """
    return sum(
        abs(p1[0] - p0[0]) + abs(p1[1] - p0[1])
        for p0, p1 in zip(
            self.stub_waypoints[:-1],
            self.stub_waypoints[1:],
            strict=True,
        )
    )

docs.title: CabinetConfig
docs.text:
Bases: GeneratorConfig

Cable-cabinet block (German KVS) — placement, count, grounding.

Attributes:

Name Type Description placement Optional[PlacementSpec]

Where to place the cabinets (star topology only). None (the default since 2026.11, user decisions Q22 and Q35): one cabinet per building group, at the far end of the houses it feeds — the buildings are grouped by group_buildings() (consecutive bearings around the substation, sizes differing by at most one), and the cabinet of a group stands on the ray from the substation through the group's centroid, end_clearance_m beyond the largest projection on that ray of the group's earth electrodes (horizontal wires and, since audit W1B-02, rods) plus the plan extent of the cabinet's own grounding — when it stands there within max_far_end_gap_m of the nearest electrode of its group; otherwise (a wide group, whose centroid ray leads past its houses) on the ray through the group's far-end building, the largest projection of its position on the direction of the centroid, end_clearance_m beyond that building's electrodes (audit W1B-01). It feeds its group. A cabinet whose electrodes would come closer than end_clearance_m to those of another site (a building of its or another group, the substation, another cabinet) raises a ValueError naming both. A placement places the cabinets as up to 2026.11 (the strip along the substation row of the former default, ManhattanGridPlacement(spacing_x_m=40, spacing_y_m=1, n_per_row=10), reproduces that world bit for bit), and every building is fed by its nearest cabinet (Manhattan metric). In both cases a building that a cabinet's cable crosses is fed by that cable (user decision Q41). A configuration stored before 2026.11 carries the former default placement and keeps its cabinets.

count_per_100_buildings Union[float, AnyDistribution]

Number of cabinets per 100 buildings; the count is ceil(count_per_100_buildings * n_buildings / 100), at least 1 (with building groups at most one per building).

fixed_count Optional[Union[int, AnyDistribution]]

Optional fixed cabinet count (overrides the rate).

grounding GroundingSystemSpec

Grounding system of every cabinet.

end_clearance_m Union[_PositiveDistance, AnyDistribution]

Smallest plan distance in m between the earth electrodes of a cabinet and those of any other site (building groups only), positive, finite and smaller than max_far_end_gap_m — a cabinet on the centroid ray stands at least this far from its group, so a larger value sent every group to the far-end ray, silently (audit W1R2-09); a distribution is checked where it is drawn (audit W1B-05).

max_far_end_gap_m Union[_PositiveDistance, AnyDistribution]

Largest plan distance in m (default 20, positive, finite, larger than end_clearance_m) between a cabinet on the ray through its group's centroid and the nearest electrode of its group; a cabinet farther from the houses it feeds stands on the ray through the group's far-end building instead (building groups only; e.g. 10 houses and one small commercial building: 50.4 m on the centroid ray, 1.6 m on the far-end ray). The plan records per cabinet which rule placed it and that distance (cabinet_rule, centroid_ray_gap_m). The threshold is a step, kept for 2026.11 (user decision D7; audit W1R2-02): a group whose distance crosses it moves its cabinet by up to the width of the group, and the results jump — the 50-house grid with its house columns 32.0 / 32.2 m apart (southern group 19.99 → 20.22 m) moves one cabinet by 141.8 m, its drops by −19 %, the input resistance at 50 Hz by −0.14 % beyond the smooth trend and, with an inductive PEN, the reactance at 1 kHz by −22 / −19 % (carson_series / sommerfeld). Groups lie on both sides of it: on the centroid ray the groups of the default 50-house grid stand 8.8 … 12.8 m from their houses, those of the 100-house grid 10.05 … 23.01 m (two beyond 20 m; 15 / 25 m put four / none of its groups on the far-end ray), and over the 80 AP1 mixes the groups beyond it 20.21 … 53.56 m, the largest one kept 18.84 m.

Source code in src/groundfield/generators/distributions.py 
def sample(self, rng: np.random.Generator) -> str:
    """Draw one entry of ``values``, weighted by ``weights`` if given.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rng : numpy.random.Generator
        Random number generator that supplies the draw.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        One entry of ``values``.
    """
    if self.weights is None:
        idx = int(rng.integers(0, len(self.values)))
    else:
        p = np.asarray(self.weights, dtype=float)
        p = p / p.sum()
        idx = int(rng.choice(len(self.values), p=p))
    return str(self.values[idx])

def generate(self, n: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
    """Return the first ``n`` of the given positions.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n : int
        Number of sites.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator
        Random number generator (not used; kept for the common
        interface of the placement strategies).

    Returns
    -------
    list of tuple of float
        The first ``n`` entries of ``positions``, ``(x, y)`` in m.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``n`` exceeds the number of given positions.
    """
    if n > len(self.positions):
        raise ValueError(
            f"ExplicitPlacement: requested {n} positions but only "
            f"{len(self.positions)} provided."
        )
    return list(self.positions[:n])

docs.title: FoundationElectrodeSpec
docs.text:
Bases: _ElectrodeSpecBase

Rectangular foundation electrode (Fundamenterder).

A rectangle of side length size_m (or size_xy_m for an asymmetric footprint) at depth depth_m. The internal structure is selected by style:

  • "ring" — only the rectangle's perimeter is buried (a closed wire loop). No internal cross-bracing. n_x and n_y are ignored. Use this for the Ringerder-style foundation electrode in residential buildings where only the strip foundation is electrically connected.
  • "mesh" (default) — perimeter plus horizontal and vertical cross-braces, dividing the foundation into n_x × n_y cells. The Maschenerder-style foundation electrode found in larger buildings, transformer stations and industrial sites. With n_x = n_y = 2 (the default) the rectangle gets exactly one internal horizontal plus one internal vertical wire.

The image family solves one uniform leakage current per straight wire (an owner; user decisions Q30, Q44): an outline is one owner per straight side. The owners of a foundation depend only on its structure, never on the orientation, on whether a shell is configured (audit A2G-04) or on the deprecated concrete_model, which has no effect (user decision Q38). A "mesh" foundation is one straight wire per mesh line (a polyline split at the crossings), bonded to the first: one owner over perimeter and braces was 2.4 % (2 × 2) to 3.7 % (4 × 4) high against mom (one current per segment) with the default line kernel, one owner per wire is 1.1 % high (0.3–0.5 % with the point kernel, the kernel of mom). A rectangle without cross-braces ("ring", or "mesh" with n_x = n_y = 1) is one straight wire per side, bonded to the first, at every angle (user decision Q38). Up to then an axis-aligned one (also one turned by a multiple of 90°) was one groundfield.geometry.electrodes.GridMeshElectrode (one owner) with the default value; per side its input impedance is lower by less than 1 % up to aspect ratio 4 and 2 % up to 50 for a short side of at least 1 m, and equal for a square (see concrete_model for the scope). A polygon_xy_m outline is one closed polyline, solved as one owner per straight side (user decisions Q30/Q44).

The first wire of a rectangle (the anchor, named after the foundation) is its local \(-y\) side; its connection point, where conductors attached to the foundation by name start, is the corner at the start of that side (a building outline: its first vertex). The generators end their cables and service drops at the point of the foundation nearest to each conductor instead (user decision Q41, see groundfield.generators.materialise).

With a shell (concrete_rho_ohm_m) every wire of the foundation, the cross-braces of a mesh included, is encased (DIN 18014, user decision Q20); see ADR-0012.

For an asymmetric footprint set size_xy_m instead of size_m (when both are given, size_xy_m wins).

docs.text:
model_copy(*, update: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, deep: bool = False) -> Self

Copy of the spec; validates an update of concrete_model.

Pydantic stores update without validation, so the deprecated concrete_model (user decision Q21) is validated here like in the constructor: a value outside {"lumped", "distributed"} raises the constructor's pydantic.ValidationError (no warning, nothing stored; audit D2B-04), "distributed" emits the constructor's DeprecationWarning at the caller's line and "lumped" is silent. Only that field is validated (on a shallow copy), so the other fields, also the required fields of a subclass, are copied as they are (audit R2B-05). copy.replace (Python >= 3.13) calls this method. Copies that leave the field alone (every copy the generators make) are silent.

def model_copy(
    self, *, update: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, deep: bool = False
) -> Self:
    """Copy of the spec; validates an ``update`` of ``concrete_model``.

    Pydantic stores ``update`` without validation, so the deprecated
    :attr:`concrete_model` (user decision Q21) is validated here like
    in the constructor: a value outside ``{"lumped", "distributed"}``
    raises the constructor's :class:`pydantic.ValidationError` (no
    warning, nothing stored; audit D2B-04), ``"distributed"`` emits
    the constructor's :class:`DeprecationWarning` at the caller's line
    and ``"lumped"`` is silent. Only that field is validated (on a
    shallow copy), so the other fields, also the required fields of a
    subclass, are copied as they are (audit R2B-05).
    ``copy.replace`` (Python >= 3.13) calls this method. Copies that
    leave the field alone (every copy the generators make) are silent.

    Parameters
    ----------
    update
        Field values to change. ``concrete_model`` is validated; the
        other fields are not (as in pydantic).
    deep
        Deep copy instead of a shallow one.

    Returns
    -------
    FoundationElectrodeSpec
        The copy (the receiver is not changed).

    Raises
    ------
    pydantic.ValidationError
        If ``update`` sets ``concrete_model`` to a value other than
        ``"lumped"`` or ``"distributed"``.
    """
    if update and "concrete_model" in update:
        # Only the field is validated, on a shallow copy, so the other
        # fields of a subclass need not be rebuilt (audit R2B-05): the
        # Literal check raises, the field validator warns for the
        # deprecated value.
        probe = super().model_copy()
        type(self).__pydantic_validator__.validate_assignment(
            probe, "concrete_model", update["concrete_model"]
        )
        update = {**update, "concrete_model": probe.concrete_model}
    return super().model_copy(update=update, deep=deep)

docs.text:
Bases: PickleUpgrade, BaseModel

Base class for generator configurations.

Subclasses declare their parameters as Pydantic fields. Numerical fields are typed as T | <distribution alias> so the user can pass a fixed value or a Distribution. Categorical fields use str | Categorical.

Two introspection helpers are provided:

  • has_distributions() returns True if any field still carries a Distribution instance — useful as a guard before passing the config to WorldGenerator.build().
  • sample() returns a copy of the config with every Distribution field resolved to a concrete value via its .sample(rng) method. Nested GeneratorConfig sub-fields are recursed into; lists are processed element-wise.

A config pickled by an earlier release unpickles with its renamed fields moved to the current names (_field_renames of the subclass) and fields added since filled with their defaults (PickleUpgrade, audit A2G-07).

def has_distributions(self) -> bool:
    """Return whether any field still carries a :class:`Distribution`.

    Recursive: a nested :class:`GeneratorConfig` whose own field
    carries a distribution counts as "has distributions".
    """
    for value in self.__dict__.values():
        if _has_dist(value):
            return True
    return False

def build_at(
    self,
    world: World,
    site_xy: tuple[float, float],
    name_prefix: str,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> Optional[str]:
    """Materialise the grounding system inside ``world``.

    Equivalent to :meth:`plan_site` followed by
    :func:`groundfield.generators.materialise.materialise_site`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        The :class:`World` to populate.
    site_xy
        Centre position ``(x, y)`` of this site (substation centre,
        cabinet centre, building centre, …) in m.
    name_prefix
        Prefix of every created electrode name. The actual name is
        ``f"{name_prefix}_{kind}_{i}"`` with ``i`` the electrode's
        index in :attr:`electrodes`. Should be unique within the
        world.
    rng
        Random generator used for ``presence_prob`` and every
        distribution field.

    Returns
    -------
    str | None
        The name of the *anchor* electrode (the first present one).
        ``None`` if no electrode ended up being placed (every
        Bernoulli draw failed) — the caller may want to skip this
        site or raise.
    """
    from groundfield.generators.materialise import materialise_site

    site = PlannedSite(
        name=name_prefix,
        role="building",
        position_xy=(site_xy[0], site_xy[1]),
        electrodes=self.resolve_electrodes(rng),
        bond_conductor_type=self.bond_conductor_type,
    )
    return materialise_site(world, site)

def plan_site(
    self,
    name: str,
    *,
    role: str,
    position_xy: tuple[float, float],
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    footprint: "Optional[BuildingFootprint]" = None,
    building_type: Optional[str] = None,
    outline: FoundationOutline = "spec",
) -> PlannedSite:
    """Resolve the system into a :class:`~groundfield.generators.plan.PlannedSite`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name
        Site name (electrode-name prefix).
    role
        Site role, see :data:`groundfield.generators.plan.SiteRole`.
    position_xy
        Site reference point ``(x, y)`` in m.
    rng
        Random generator (see :meth:`resolve_electrodes`).
    footprint, building_type
        Recorded on the site for information.
    outline
        ``"spec"`` (default): the foundations keep the spec geometry.
        ``"ombr"`` / ``"polygon"``: after the random draws, the
        resolved foundations are shaped after ``footprint`` (see
        :meth:`with_footprint`). Drawing first keeps the random
        stream independent of the outline, so the same seed puts
        optional electrodes on the same sites whatever the outline
        (audit M2).

    Returns
    -------
    PlannedSite
        The concrete site.
    """
    electrodes = self.resolve_electrodes(rng)
    if footprint is not None and outline != "spec" and electrodes:
        shaped = GroundingSystemSpec(
            electrodes=[planned.spec for planned in electrodes],
            bond_conductor_type=self.bond_conductor_type,
        ).with_footprint(footprint, site_xy=position_xy, outline=outline)
        electrodes = [
            PlannedElectrode(index=planned.index, spec=spec)
            for planned, spec in zip(electrodes, shaped.electrodes, strict=True)
        ]
    return PlannedSite(
        name=name,
        role=role,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        position_xy=(float(position_xy[0]), float(position_xy[1])),
        electrodes=electrodes,
        bond_conductor_type=self.bond_conductor_type,
        footprint=footprint,
        building_type=building_type,
    )

def resolve_electrodes(self, rng: np.random.Generator) -> list[PlannedElectrode]:
    """Make every random decision of this grounding system.

    For each electrode in list order: one draw for a distributed
    ``presence_prob``, one Bernoulli draw when the probability is
    below one, and — for a present electrode — one draw per
    distribution field (see :func:`_resolve_spec` for the order).

    Parameters
    ----------
    rng
        Random generator.

    Returns
    -------
    list of PlannedElectrode
        The present electrodes with concrete values, each tagged with
        its index in :attr:`electrodes`.
    """
    out: list[PlannedElectrode] = []
    for i, spec in enumerate(self.electrodes):
        p = _to_float(spec.presence_prob, rng)
        if p < 1.0 and rng.random() >= p:
            continue
        out.append(PlannedElectrode(index=i, spec=_resolve_spec(spec, rng)))
    return out

def with_footprint(
    self,
    footprint: "BuildingFootprint",
    *,
    site_xy: Optional[tuple[float, float]] = None,
    outline: FoundationOutline = "ombr",
) -> "GroundingSystemSpec":
    r"""Return a copy whose foundation electrodes follow ``footprint``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    footprint
        Building outline in the world's local frame (m).
    site_xy
        Site position the spec will be built at, i.e. the origin of
        every ``offset_xy_m``. ``None`` uses the polygon centroid.
    outline
        ``"ombr"`` (default): every
        :class:`~groundfield.generators.electrode_specs.FoundationElectrodeSpec`
        takes the size :math:`(d_x, d_y)`, orientation
        :math:`\varphi` and centre :math:`(c_x, c_y)` of the
        outline's oriented minimum bounding rectangle; the centre
        enters as an extra offset :math:`(c_x, c_y) - \text{site}`
        on top of the spec's own ``offset_xy_m``. A side shorter than
        :data:`MIN_FOUNDATION_SIDE_M` is widened to it (with a
        :class:`UserWarning`). ``"polygon"``: every
        foundation follows the outline itself (``polygon_xy_m`` =
        exterior ring relative to ``site_xy``); only defined for
        ``style="ring"``. An outline whose OMBR is narrower than
        :data:`MIN_FOUNDATION_SIDE_M` is replaced by that OMBR widened
        to it, as a four-cornered outline (with a :class:`UserWarning`,
        as for ``"ombr"``); a polygon foundation along it would run
        along both faces of a wall, and an outline narrower than
        :data:`~groundfield.generators.materialise.MIN_POLYGON_EDGE_M`
        could not be built at all. ``"spec"``: return ``self``
        unchanged.

    Returns
    -------
    GroundingSystemSpec
        A new spec (``self`` when nothing changes). Presence
        probabilities, depths, styles, mesh counts, wire radii and
        concrete parameters are kept.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For ``outline="polygon"`` with a ``style="mesh"`` foundation
        (cross-braces are undefined on a general polygon) or an
        unknown ``outline``.
    ImportError
        ``outline="ombr"``, and ``outline="polygon"`` for an outline
        narrower than :data:`MIN_FOUNDATION_SIDE_M` on average, need
        :mod:`shapely` (``geo`` extra).
    """
    if outline not in ("spec", "ombr", "polygon"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"outline must be 'spec', 'ombr' or 'polygon', got {outline!r}."
        )
    if outline == "spec" or not any(
        isinstance(spec, FoundationElectrodeSpec) for spec in self.electrodes
    ):
        # Nothing to shape (no foundation): no OMBR, no warning.
        return self
    if site_xy is None:
        site_xy = footprint.centroid_xy_m()
    ring = [(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in footprint.polygon_xy_m]
    if outline == "ombr":
        (cx, cy), (dx, dy), orientation_deg = _widened_ombr(footprint)
        # Recentre on the OMBR centre (F25): the electrode sits at
        # ``site_xy + offset_xy_m``.
        recentre = (cx - site_xy[0], cy - site_xy[1])
    elif footprint.mean_width_m() < MIN_FOUNDATION_SIDE_M:
        # Only thin outlines can have an OMBR side below the minimum
        # (the mean width of a rectangle is below its short side), so
        # ordinary buildings need no shapely here.
        (cx, cy), (dx, dy), orientation_deg = (
            footprint.oriented_bounding_rectangle()
        )
        if min(dx, dy) < MIN_FOUNDATION_SIDE_M:
            ring = _rectangle_ring(*_widened_ombr(footprint))
    rewritten: list[ElectrodeSpec] = []
    changed = False
    for spec in self.electrodes:
        if not isinstance(spec, FoundationElectrodeSpec):
            rewritten.append(spec)
            continue
        if outline == "ombr":
            update: dict[str, object] = {
                "size_xy_m": (dx, dy),
                "orientation_deg": orientation_deg,
                "offset_xy_m": (
                    spec.offset_xy_m[0] + recentre[0],
                    spec.offset_xy_m[1] + recentre[1],
                ),
            }
        else:
            if spec.style != "ring":
                raise ValueError(
                    "outline='polygon' needs style='ring' foundations — the "
                    "cross-braces of style='mesh' are undefined on a general "
                    "polygon. Use outline='ombr' or a ring-style spec."
                )
            sx, sy = site_xy
            update = {"polygon_xy_m": tuple((x - sx, y - sy) for x, y in ring)}
        rewritten.append(spec.model_copy(update=update))
        changed = True
    if not changed:
        return self
    return self.model_copy(update={"electrodes": rewritten})

Build a LogNormal from the physical mean and std.

Solves \(\mu = \ln(\text{mean}^2/\sqrt{\text{std}^2 + \text{mean}^2})\) and \(\sigma^2 = \ln(1 + \text{std}^2/\text{mean}^2)\).

required Source code in src/groundfield/generators/distributions.py 
@classmethod
def from_moments(cls, mean: float, std: float) -> "LogNormal":
    """Build a :class:`LogNormal` from the physical mean and std.

    Solves $\\mu = \\ln(\\text{mean}^2/\\sqrt{\\text{std}^2 + \\text{mean}^2})$
    and $\\sigma^2 = \\ln(1 + \\text{std}^2/\\text{mean}^2)$.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mean
        Target physical mean $\\mathbb{E}[X] > 0$.
    std
        Target physical standard deviation $\\sqrt{\\mathrm{Var}(X)} > 0$.
    """
    if mean <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"LogNormal.from_moments: mean must be > 0 (got {mean}).")
    if std <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"LogNormal.from_moments: std must be > 0 (got {std}).")
    var = std * std
    sigma_sq = math.log(1.0 + var / (mean * mean))
    mu = math.log(mean) - 0.5 * sigma_sq
    return cls(mu=mu, sigma=math.sqrt(sigma_sq))

Place a cable cabinet at position_xy or position_lat_lon.

Exactly one of position_xy (local ENU metres) or position_lat_lon (WGS84 degrees) must be set. The lat / lon variant projects through the layout's frame_origin_lat_lon; if no frame origin is set, a RuntimeError is raised.

Returns the assigned cabinet name (auto-generated when name is None). The returned name is what callers pass to add_pen_cable() as start=....

Source code in src/groundfield/generators/layout/model.py 
def add_cabinet(
    self,
    position_xy: Optional[tuple[float, float]] = None,
    *,
    position_lat_lon: Optional[tuple[float, float]] = None,
    name: Optional[str] = None,
) -> str:
    """Place a cable cabinet at ``position_xy`` or ``position_lat_lon``.

    Exactly one of ``position_xy`` (local ENU metres) or
    ``position_lat_lon`` (WGS84 degrees) must be set. The lat /
    lon variant projects through the layout's
    :attr:`frame_origin_lat_lon`; if no frame origin is set, a
    :class:`RuntimeError` is raised.

    Returns the assigned cabinet name (auto-generated when ``name``
    is ``None``). The returned name is what callers pass to
    :meth:`add_pen_cable` as ``start=...``.
    """
    if (position_xy is None) == (position_lat_lon is None):
        raise ValueError(
            "LvNetworkLayout.add_cabinet: exactly one of "
            "``position_xy`` and ``position_lat_lon`` must be set."
        )
    if position_lat_lon is not None:
        position_xy = self.lat_lon_to_xy(*position_lat_lon)
    if name is None:
        name = f"kvs_{len(self.cabinet_placements)}"
    if any(k.name == name for k in self.cabinet_placements):
        raise ValueError(
            f"LvNetworkLayout.add_cabinet: name {name!r} is already taken."
        )
    if name == self.substation_name:
        raise ValueError(
            f"LvNetworkLayout.add_cabinet: name {name!r} clashes with "
            "the substation name."
        )
    assert position_xy is not None
    self.cabinet_placements.append(
        CabinetPlacement(name=name, position_xy=tuple(position_xy)),
    )
    return name

@classmethod
def from_osm(
    cls,
    *,
    center_lat_deg: float,
    center_lon_deg: float,
    radius_m: float,
    substation_lat_lon: Optional[tuple[float, float]] = None,
    substation_xy: Optional[tuple[float, float]] = None,
    cabinet_lat_lons: Optional[list[tuple[float, float]]] = None,
    cabinet_xys: Optional[list[tuple[float, float]]] = None,
    substation_name: str = "substation",
    obstacle_clearance_m: float = 1.0,
    min_area_m2: float = 16.0,
    cache_dir=None,
    force_refresh: bool = False,
    endpoint: Optional[str] = None,
    timeout_s: Optional[int] = None,
    max_retries: int = 1,
    exclude_building_tags: Optional[Collection[str]] = None,
    **deprecated: object,
) -> "LvNetworkLayout":
    """One-shot constructor: query OSM and pre-place anchors.

    Parameters
    ----------
    center_lat_deg, center_lon_deg
        Centre of the buildings-in-radius Overpass query. Also
        the WGS84 origin of the local ENU frame
        :attr:`frame_origin_lat_lon` so subsequent
        ``position_lat_lon`` arguments stay consistent.
    radius_m
        Search radius in metres.
    substation_lat_lon
        Optional substation location as WGS84 ``(lat, lon)``.
        Mutually exclusive with ``substation_xy``. When both
        are omitted the substation defaults to the local
        origin ``(0, 0)``.
    substation_xy
        Substation location in already-projected metres.
        Mutually exclusive with ``substation_lat_lon``.
    cabinet_lat_lons
        Optional list of cabinet locations in WGS84 ``(lat, lon)``.
        Each entry is projected and appended to
        :attr:`cabinet_placements`. Names are auto-generated.
    cabinet_xys
        Optional list of cabinet locations in already-projected
        metres. Mutually exclusive with ``cabinet_lat_lons``.
    substation_name
        Anchor id for the substation. Default ``"substation"``.
    obstacle_clearance_m, min_area_m2
        Forwarded to the layout / OSM query respectively.
    cache_dir, force_refresh, endpoint, timeout_s, max_retries
        Forwarded to :func:`groundfield.geo.osm.query_and_project`.
    exclude_building_tags
        ``building=*`` values to drop, e.g.
        :data:`groundfield.geo.osm.NON_SERVICE_BUILDING_TAGS`
        (garages, sheds, carports, ...). ``None`` (default) keeps
        every element with a ``building`` tag.

    Returns
    -------
    LvNetworkLayout
        Layout with footprints loaded, projector seeded, and
        substation / cabinets pre-placed. Routing and connections
        are still up to the caller.

    Examples
    --------
    Build the layout for Mulmke (Heudeber / Nordharz) in a
    300 m radius around the village centre, with the
    substation at a chosen lat / lon and two cabinets along the
    main road:

    >>> layout = LvNetworkLayout.from_osm(
    ...     center_lat_deg=51.9136, center_lon_deg=10.8432,
    ...     radius_m=300.0,
    ...     substation_lat_lon=(51.9138, 10.8418),
    ...     cabinet_lat_lons=[
    ...         (51.9133, 10.8445),
    ...         (51.9140, 10.8460),
    ...     ],
    ... )
    """
    from groundfield.geo.osm import query_and_project

    renamed = take_renamed_kwargs(
        "LvNetworkLayout.from_osm",
        deprecated,
        {"kvs_lat_lons": "cabinet_lat_lons", "kvs_xys": "cabinet_xys"},
    )
    cabinet_lat_lons = renamed.get("cabinet_lat_lons", cabinet_lat_lons)  # type: ignore[assignment]
    cabinet_xys = renamed.get("cabinet_xys", cabinet_xys)  # type: ignore[assignment]
    if substation_lat_lon is not None and substation_xy is not None:
        raise ValueError(
            "LvNetworkLayout.from_osm: substation_lat_lon and "
            "substation_xy are mutually exclusive."
        )
    if cabinet_lat_lons is not None and cabinet_xys is not None:
        raise ValueError(
            "LvNetworkLayout.from_osm: cabinet_lat_lons and cabinet_xys "
            "are mutually exclusive."
        )

    query_kwargs: dict = {
        "min_area_m2": min_area_m2,
        "force_refresh": force_refresh,
        "max_retries": max_retries,
    }
    if exclude_building_tags is not None:
        query_kwargs["exclude_building_tags"] = exclude_building_tags
    if cache_dir is not None:
        query_kwargs["cache_dir"] = cache_dir
    if endpoint is not None:
        query_kwargs["endpoint"] = endpoint
    if timeout_s is not None:
        query_kwargs["timeout_s"] = timeout_s

    footprints, projector = query_and_project(
        lat0_deg=center_lat_deg,
        lon0_deg=center_lon_deg,
        radius_m=radius_m,
        **query_kwargs,
    )

    if substation_lat_lon is not None:
        sub_xy = projector.to_xy_m(*substation_lat_lon)
    elif substation_xy is not None:
        sub_xy = tuple(substation_xy)
    else:
        sub_xy = (0.0, 0.0)

    layout = cls(
        footprints=footprints,
        substation_xy=sub_xy,
        substation_name=substation_name,
        obstacle_clearance_m=obstacle_clearance_m,
        frame_origin_lat_lon=(center_lat_deg, center_lon_deg),
    )

    if cabinet_lat_lons:
        for lat, lon in cabinet_lat_lons:
            layout.add_cabinet(position_lat_lon=(lat, lon))
    elif cabinet_xys:
        for xy in cabinet_xys:
            layout.add_cabinet(position_xy=xy)

    return layout

def lat_lon_to_xy(
    self,
    lat_deg: float,
    lon_deg: float,
) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Project a WGS84 ``(lat, lon)`` to the layout's local frame.

    Raises :class:`RuntimeError` when no
    :attr:`frame_origin_lat_lon` has been set (i.e. the layout
    was not built via :meth:`from_osm`).
    """
    projector = self.projector
    if projector is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "LvNetworkLayout.lat_lon_to_xy: layout has no "
            "frame_origin_lat_lon. Build via ``from_osm`` or "
            "pass ``frame_origin_lat_lon`` to ``from_footprints`` "
            "to enable lat / lon based placement."
        )
    return projector.to_xy_m(lat_deg, lon_deg)

def plan(
    self,
    *,
    name: str = "ortsnetz_layout",
    soil: Optional[SoilModel] = None,
    substation_grounding: Optional[GroundingSystemSpec] = None,
    cabinet_grounding: Optional[GroundingSystemSpec] = None,
    house_grounding: Optional[GroundingSystemSpec] = None,
    pen_wire_radius_m: float = 0.005,
    pen_segment_length_m: Optional[float] = 5.0,
    include_source: bool = True,
    source_magnitude_a: float = 1.0,
    seed: int = 0,
    foundation_mask: Optional[list[bool]] = None,
    foundation_outline: FoundationOutline = "ombr",
    **deprecated: object,
) -> NetworkPlan:
    """Resolve the layout into a :class:`~groundfield.generators.plan.NetworkPlan`.

    Parameters are those of :meth:`to_world`. Random draws (presence
    probabilities and distributions in the grounding specs) use
    ``numpy.random.default_rng(seed)`` in the order substation,
    cabinets, houses, auxiliary electrode. Each house's foundation
    electrodes are shaped after its footprint once its draws are made
    (see ``foundation_outline`` in :meth:`to_world`), so the outline
    does not change which optional electrodes a seed produces.

    Returns
    -------
    NetworkPlan
        The concrete network. Every PEN cable becomes a chain of
        branches between junctions at its corners and tap points;
        cable ends at the substation or a cabinet attach to that
        site.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``foundation_mask`` has the wrong length.
    RuntimeError
        If the substation, a cabinet or the auxiliary electrode
        grounding produces zero electrodes.
    """
    renamed = take_renamed_kwargs(
        "LvNetworkLayout.plan",
        deprecated,
        {
            "kvs_grounding": "cabinet_grounding",
            "source_magnitude_A": "source_magnitude_a",
        },
    )
    cabinet_grounding = renamed.get("cabinet_grounding", cabinet_grounding)  # type: ignore[assignment]
    source_magnitude_a = renamed.get("source_magnitude_a", source_magnitude_a)  # type: ignore[assignment]
    if foundation_mask is not None and len(foundation_mask) != len(
        self.footprints,
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            "LvNetworkLayout.to_world: foundation_mask length "
            f"{len(foundation_mask)} does not match footprints "
            f"count {len(self.footprints)}."
        )
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    # 1. Substation grounding.
    substation_spec = substation_grounding or _default_substation_grounding()
    substation = substation_spec.plan_site(
        self.substation_name,
        role="substation",
        position_xy=self.substation_xy,
        rng=rng,
    )
    if substation.anchor is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "LvNetworkLayout.to_world: substation grounding "
            "produced zero electrodes."
        )
    sites: list[PlannedSite] = [substation]

    # 2. Cable-cabinet groundings.
    cabinet_spec = cabinet_grounding or _default_cabinet_grounding()
    for k in self.cabinet_placements:
        cabinet = cabinet_spec.plan_site(
            k.name, role="cabinet", position_xy=k.position_xy, rng=rng
        )
        if cabinet.anchor is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "LvNetworkLayout.to_world: cabinet "
                f"{k.name!r} grounding produced zero electrodes."
            )
        sites.append(cabinet)

    # 3. House groundings, shaped after the footprint
    #    (``GroundingSystemSpec.with_footprint``). Houses outside
    #    ``foundation_mask`` stay in the layout (plots) but not in the
    #    network.
    house_spec = house_grounding or _default_house_grounding()
    houses: dict[int, PlannedSite] = {}
    for i, fp in enumerate(self.footprints):
        if foundation_mask is not None and not foundation_mask[i]:
            continue
        centroid = fp.centroid_xy_m()
        house = house_spec.plan_site(
            f"house_{i:03d}",
            role="building",
            position_xy=centroid,
            rng=rng,
            footprint=fp,
            outline=foundation_outline,
        )
        sites.append(house)
        houses[i] = house

    # 4. Auxiliary current electrode, if configured.
    measurement: Optional[PlannedMeasurement] = None
    if self.auxiliary_electrode is not None:
        aux = self.auxiliary_electrode
        aux_site = aux.grounding.plan_site(
            aux.name, role="auxiliary", position_xy=aux.position_xy, rng=rng
        )
        if aux_site.anchor is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "LvNetworkLayout.to_world: auxiliary electrode "
                "grounding produced zero electrodes "
                f"({aux.name!r}). Increase presence_prob."
            )
        measurement = PlannedMeasurement(auxiliary=aux_site)

    # 5. PEN cables: a junction at every interior corner and tap
    #    point, one branch between consecutive nodes. Nodes closer
    #    than the shortest cable section are merged (a tap a few
    #    millimetres from a corner or from another tap left a section
    #    the Conductor model refuses, audit A3SG-01). A cable or drop
    #    ends at the point of a site's horizontal electrodes nearest to
    #    it (user decisions Q41, Q43): a house with a foundation, ring
    #    or strip is tapped at the closest pair between its cable and
    #    their wires. Corners inside a site's foundation are part of the
    #    site (audit R6A-01), and a cable that passes through the
    #    foundation of the substation or a cabinet is joined to it there
    #    (audits W1B-03, W1B-04).
    conductor = ConductorParameters(
        conductor_type="pen",
        wire_radius_m=pen_wire_radius_m,
        cross_section="from_radius",
        coupling_to_soil="isolated",
        segment_length_m=pen_segment_length_m,
    )
    min_length = min_section_length(conductor)
    geometry = {site.name: _site_geometry(site) for site in sites}
    anchor_points = {
        site.name: geometry[site.name][0]
        for site in sites
        if site.role in ("substation", "cabinet")
    }
    wires = {name: g.wires for name, g in geometry.items() if g.wires}
    outlines = {name: g.outlines for name, g in geometry.items() if g.outlines}
    meet = _Meeting({name: g.point for name, g in geometry.items()}, wires)
    built = {
        cable.name: self._built_segments(
            cable, wires, outlines, passing=list(anchor_points)
        )
        for cable in self.pen_cables
    }
    taps = self._service_taps(houses, wires, min_length, built)
    junctions: list[PlannedJunction] = []
    branches: list[PlannedBranch] = []
    cable_nodes: dict[str, list[tuple[str, tuple[float, float]]]] = {}
    for cable in self.pen_cables:
        nodes = self._merge_close_nodes(
            cable.name,
            self._cable_nodes(
                cable,
                junctions,
                taps,
                built[cable.name].merged,
                built[cable.name].passages,
            ),
            junctions,
            anchor_points,
            min_length,
            meet,
        )
        cable_nodes[cable.name] = nodes
        meet.junctions(junctions)
        for j, ((a0, p0), (a1, p1)) in enumerate(
            zip(nodes[:-1], nodes[1:], strict=True)
        ):
            if a0 == a1:
                continue
            c0, c1 = meet.contacts(a0, p0, a1, p1)
            branches.append(
                PlannedBranch(
                    name=f"{cable.name}_seg_{j}",
                    role="pen",
                    start=a0,
                    end=a1,
                    conductor=conductor,
                    cable=cable.name,
                    start_contact=c0,
                    end_contact=c1,
                )
            )

    # 6. Service drops: tap node on the cable -> house (its foundation
    #    point nearest to the tap node, user decision Q41).
    for c in self.connections:
        house = houses.get(c.house_idx)
        if house is None or house.anchor is None:
            continue
        tap = self._tap_anchor_for(c, cable_nodes, taps.get(c.house_idx))
        if tap is None:
            continue
        tap_xy = dict(cable_nodes[c.cable_name])[tap]
        # A tap at the substation or a cabinet with a foundation leaves
        # it at its point nearest to the house (two foundations: their
        # closest pair).
        start_contact, end_contact = meet.contacts(tap, tap_xy, house.name, None)
        branches.append(
            PlannedBranch(
                name=f"service_{c.house_idx:03d}",
                role="service_drop",
                start=tap,
                end=house.name,
                conductor=conductor,
                cable=c.cable_name,
                start_contact=start_contact,
                end_contact=end_contact,
            )
        )

    # 7. Sources. With an auxiliary electrode the source takes its
    #    current back there (``Source.return_to``, honoured by the
    #    solver since 2026.11, finding 10.16).
    sources: list[PlannedSource] = []
    if include_source:
        sources.append(
            PlannedSource(
                attached_to=substation.name,
                return_to=None
                if measurement is None
                else measurement.auxiliary.name,
                magnitude=source_magnitude_a,
            )
        )

    return NetworkPlan(
        name=name,
        soil=soil or HomogeneousSoil(resistivity=100.0),
        sites=sites,
        junctions=junctions,
        branches=branches,
        measurement=measurement,
        sources=sources,
    )

to_world(*, name: str = 'ortsnetz_layout', soil: Optional[SoilModel] = None, substation_grounding: Optional[GroundingSystemSpec] = None, cabinet_grounding: Optional[GroundingSystemSpec] = None, house_grounding: Optional[GroundingSystemSpec] = None, pen_wire_radius_m: float = 0.005, pen_segment_length_m: Optional[float] = 5.0, include_source: bool = True, source_magnitude_a: float = 1.0, seed: int = 0, foundation_mask: Optional[list[bool]] = None, foundation_outline: FoundationOutline = 'ombr', **deprecated: object) -> World

Materialise the layout into a groundfield.World.

Equivalent to materialise_plan(self.plan(...)). Each PenCable becomes a chain of straight conductors between junctions at its corners and tap points, so the cable follows its Manhattan polyline; each BuildingConnection becomes one conductor from the tap junction to the house foundation. A conductor routed to a site with a horizontal earth electrode (a foundation, since user decision Q43 also a circular ring or a strip) ends at the point of that electrode nearest to it (user decision Q41): such a house is tapped at the closest pair in plan of its cable and its horizontal wires (not at the tap point of its BuildingConnection, the cable point nearest to the centroid), and its drop ends there, at the wire's depth, attached to that wire; a cable leaves a substation or a cabinet with horizontal electrodes (the default substation ring) at their point nearest to the cable's next node. Taps lie on the layout polyline where the cable is built: the leading run of its waypoints inside the start site's closed electrodes (a rectangle, a building outline, a circle) and the trailing run inside the end site's are part of those sites (audit R6A-01: a router corner inside a small cabinet ring was a node that houses tapped), and the segment that leaves (reaches) the site is clipped at the projection onto it of the site's point nearest to its far waypoint; a cable that passes through the closed electrodes of the substation or a cabinet elsewhere — another cabinet, or its own start or end site again — is clipped there the same way and joined to that site where it enters and where it leaves it (audits W1B-03, W1B-04). So no tap and no corner lies inside the foundation of the substation or a cabinet, and a rotated, polygon or offset site foundation leaves the taps of the houses on the cable (audits R4A-03, R5A-02); a tap at a clip point, or at the site's waypoint, is the site itself. A site with rods only keeps the connection point of its anchor.
