def signed_area(ring: Ring) -> float:
    r"""Signed area of a polygon ring via the shoelace formula.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ring
        Vertex list. The ring may be open (last vertex != first); the
        shoelace formula closes it implicitly.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Signed area in m². Positive for counter-clockwise rings,
        negative for clockwise rings, zero for degenerate rings.

    Notes
    -----
    Implements

    .. math::

       A \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\bigl(x_i\,y_{i+1}\;-\;
                                                x_{i+1}\,y_i\bigr)

    with indices taken modulo *n*. The orientation convention used
    here (CCW positive) matches the right-hand rule with a
    z-axis pointing *out of the ground* in the local ENU frame.
    """
    n = len(ring)
    if n < 3:
        return 0.0
    s = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        x0, y0 = ring[i]
        x1, y1 = ring[(i + 1) % n]
        s += x0 * y1 - x1 * y0
    return 0.5 * s

docs.title: Geometry
docs.text:
The geometry package describes the buried metal: parametric electrodes (rod, ring, strip, polyline, star, mesh, grid mesh), the leakage-free Junction node, and the discretisation of every electrode into straight wire segments that the solvers consume.

Kind Class Parameters (m) Typical use rod RodElectrode position (top end), length driven rod (Tiefenerder) ring RingElectrode center, radius ring earth around a building or substation strip StripElectrode start, end horizontal earth strip, counterpoise polyline PolylineElectrode vertices, closed foundation earth following a building outline star StarElectrode center, n_arms, arm_length, orientation_deg star earth (Sternerder) mesh MeshElectrode corner, size, spacing mesh with a given spacing grid_mesh GridMeshElectrode corner, size, n_x, n_y substation grid with a given number of wires

Every kind also takes wire_radius (default 5 mm) and concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m (default 0, see below).

docs.title: Mathematical and physical context
docs.text:
An electrode is a thin wire: its radius \(a\) is small against its length and against the distance to other wires, so the current leaving the surface can be represented by a current on the wire axis and the potential is evaluated on the surface (at distance \(a\)). Each geometry is cut into straight segments

\[ \Gamma_i = \{\mathbf{x}_i^{(0)} + \xi\,(\mathbf{x}_i^{(1)} - \mathbf{x}_i^{(0)}) : \xi \in [0, 1]\}, \qquad i = 1 \ldots N, \]

no longer than Engine.segment_length. Grid and mesh wires are split so that wire crossings fall on segment end points, and every wire is cut at the soil-layer interfaces so that each segment lies in one layer; every interface cut is kept, however short the piece beyond it, so a rod tip that reaches a few millimetres into a layer is in contact with it. (The thin wire has no end face, so a rod end within one wire radius of an interface is a limit of the model — up to +21 % against the solid rod — and warns with InterfaceContactWarning; see the image_2layer page.) How the current is distributed over the segments — uniform per unit length on each electrode (image family) or one unknown per segment (mom family) — is a property of the backend, see Solver and source kernels.

Concrete encasement. A foundation earth in concrete adds the radial resistance of the concrete shell. Every electrode kind carries it as a per-length coefficient

\[ C = \frac{\rho_c}{2\pi}\,\ln\frac{a + t}{a} \quad [\Omega\,\mathrm{m}], \]

for concrete resistivity \(\rho_c\), bare wire radius \(a\) and shell thickness \(t\); the electrode's wire_radius is then the outer radius \(a + t\) (the soil sees the shell surface), and every segment of length \(\Delta s\) adds the series resistance \(C/\Delta s\) of its shell to its self term. Only the image family (image, image_2layer) and solve_mutual_* represent a non-zero coefficient; the other backends reject such a world before they run. The helpers concrete_shell_coefficient, shell_resistance_from_coefficient and shell_coefficient_from_resistance convert between the coefficient and a lumped resistance; the physics is explained in concrete shells and ADR-0012.

Validity. Thin-wire approximation (\(a \ll\) segment length and wire spacing); wires must be in the soil (\(z > 0\)) — the solver rejects segments in the air and warns about leakage segments that are long compared with their depth.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import groundfield as gf
from groundfield.references import dwight1936

world = gf.create_world(soil=gf.HomogeneousSoil(rho=100.0))
star = gf.create_electrode(
    world, "star", name="star", center=(0.0, 0.0, 0.5), n_arms=4, arm_length=5.0
)
gf.create_source(world, attached_to="star", magnitude=1.0)
result = gf.create_engine(segment_length=0.5).solve(world)

assert abs(star.total_length() - 20.0) < 1e-12       # four arms of 5 m
R = result.input_impedance()[0].real                  # 10.05 Ω
R_ref = dwight1936.n_point_star(rho=100.0, arm_length=5.0, radius=0.005, depth=0.5, n_arms=4)
assert abs(R - R_ref) / R_ref < 1e-3                  # Dwight (1936), Eqs. 23-26

The geometry queries segments(ds), segment_count(ds), wire_polylines(), bounds(), total_length() and min_feature_length() are available on every electrode without a solve, for example to check a model before a long computation.

docs.title: geometry
docs.text:
Geometries of electrodes and grounding systems.

This subpackage provides the 3-D geometry of the grounding system: the standard parametric electrode geometries and their discretisation into straight wire segments (WireSegments), which every electrode produces itself through segments(ds).

Contents

RodElectrode, RingElectrode, StripElectrode, PolylineElectrode, StarElectrode, MeshElectrode, GridMeshElectrode Parametric standard electrode geometries. Each answers the geometry queries segments(ds), segment_count(ds), wire_polylines(), bounds(), total_length() and min_feature_length(). Electrode Discriminated union over all electrode types. WireSegments Midpoints, lengths and unit tangents of a discretised wire geometry.

Notes

The geometry layer is deliberately decoupled from the solver, so the same geometry can be fed into the image-charge backend, MoM, or FEM.

Defines an axis-aligned rectangle of size (dx, dy) at depth corner[2], divided into n_x × n_y internal meshes. The geometry consists of n_x + 1 longitudinal wires (running along the local \(x\) axis from corner to corner + (dx, 0)) and n_y + 1 transverse wires (running along the local \(y\) axis). All wires share the same depth.

size tuple[PositiveLength, PositiveLength]

Extent (dx, dy) of the rectangle in metres.

n_x int

Number of meshes along \(x\) (must be ≥ 1). The number of longitudinal wires is n_y + 1.

n_y int

Number of meshes along \(y\) (must be ≥ 1). The number of transverse wires is n_x + 1.

Per-length concrete-shell coefficient in Ω·m (ADR-0012, default 0: no shell); see concrete_shell_coefficient().

Notes

Naming convention: n_x × n_y is the count of meshes (cells), not of wires. A grid with n_x = n_y = 1 is therefore a single closed rectangle (the perimeter wires only).

docs.title: PolylineElectrode
docs.text:
Bases: _ElectrodeBase

Buried wire following an arbitrary horizontal polyline.

Generalises StripElectrode from a single straight wire to a chain of straight wires through vertices. With closed = True the last vertex is wired back to the first, which makes this the Ringerder along an arbitrary building outline — the DIN-18014 Streifenfundament that follows the real building perimeter instead of its bounding rectangle.

All vertices must lie at the same depth (the wire is horizontal), consistent with StripElectrode.

Attributes:

Name Type Description vertices list[Point3D]

Ordered polyline vertices (x, y, z) in metres, at least two. For closed = True do not repeat the first vertex at the end — the closing edge is implicit.

closed bool

Whether the polyline is closed into a ring (default True).

Notes

Motivation (AP1): approximating a building footprint by its oriented bounding rectangle (OMBR) overestimates the electrode perimeter for L- and U-shaped buildings and — worse — lets the rectangles of neighbouring buildings coincide or overlap, which drives distinct segments into the solver's 1 mm singularity clamp. Following the real polygon removes both artefacts by construction.

docs.title: segments
docs.text:
segments(ds: float, layer_interfaces: Sequence[float] | None = None) -> WireSegments

Horizontal ring: max(8, ceil(2πr/ds)) equal arcs (see base class).

Each arc is represented by its midpoint on the circle, its arc length and the tangent there.

Source code in src/groundfield/geometry/electrodes.py 
def segments(
    self, ds: float, layer_interfaces: Sequence[float] | None = None
) -> WireSegments:
    """Horizontal ring: ``max(8, ceil(2πr/ds))`` equal arcs (see base class).

    Each arc is represented by its midpoint on the circle, its arc
    length and the tangent there.
    """
    perimeter = 2.0 * np.pi * self.radius
    n = _segment_count(perimeter, ds, minimum=8)
    seg_len = perimeter / n
    cx, cy, cz = self.center
    mids = np.empty((n, 3))
    dirs = np.empty((n, 3))
    for k in range(n):
        # Scalar trigonometry, kept from the historic discretiser so
        # the midpoints stay bit-identical across platforms.
        phi = 2.0 * np.pi * (k + 0.5) / n
        mids[k] = (
            cx + self.radius * np.cos(phi),
            cy + self.radius * np.sin(phi),
            cz,
        )
        dirs[k] = (-np.sin(phi), np.cos(phi), 0.0)
    return WireSegments(mids, np.full(n, seg_len), dirs)

                cy + self.radius * np.sin(theta),
                np.full_like(theta, cz),

segments(ds: float, layer_interfaces: Sequence[float] | None = None) -> WireSegments

Vertical rod: equal segments per soil layer (see base class).

The rod is cut at every interface it crosses; a part beyond a cut keeps its own segment however short it is (it may be shorter than the wire radius), so a tip that reaches into a layer is in contact with it (audit round 2, A2S-01).

Source code in src/groundfield/geometry/electrodes.py 
def segments(
    self, ds: float, layer_interfaces: Sequence[float] | None = None
) -> WireSegments:
    """Vertical rod: equal segments per soil layer (see base class).

    The rod is cut at every interface it crosses; a part beyond a cut
    keeps its own segment however short it is (it may be shorter than
    the wire radius), so a tip that reaches into a layer is in contact
    with it (audit round 2, A2S-01).
    """
    x0, y0, z0 = self.position
    head = np.array([x0, y0, 0.0])
    tangent = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
    intervals = _split_interval_at_interfaces(
        z0, z0 + self.length, layer_interfaces
    )
    parts = []
    for z_lo, z_hi in intervals:
        part_len = z_hi - z_lo
        n = _segment_count(part_len, ds)
        parts.append(_straight_wire(head, tangent, z_lo, part_len / n, n))
    return WireSegments.concatenate(parts)

Buried horizontal star electrode (Sternerder).

n_arms equal-length wires radiate from a common centre node at a single depth, spaced uniformly by \(360^\circ / n\). This is the classic \(n\)-point star of Dwight (1936, Eqs. 23–26); the closed-form grounding resistance is available as groundfield.references.dwight1936.n_point_star() for validation (Dwight covers 3, 4, 6 and 8 arms).

Straight strip: equal segments along the axis (see base class).

A sloped strip whose depth range crosses a layer interface would be split there first (ADR-0007 step 1); the model validator keeps strips horizontal, so this only guards the invariant.

Source code in src/groundfield/geometry/electrodes.py 
def segments(
    self, ds: float, layer_interfaces: Sequence[float] | None = None
) -> WireSegments:
    """Straight strip: equal segments along the axis (see base class).

    A sloped strip whose depth range crosses a layer interface would
    be split there first (ADR-0007 step 1); the model validator
    keeps strips horizontal, so this only guards the invariant.
    """
    L = self.length
    p0 = np.array(self.start, dtype=float)
    p1 = np.array(self.end, dtype=float)
    direction = (p1 - p0) / L
    # Map interface depths to axis parameters t in [0, L].
    t_cuts: list[float] = []
    dz = p1[2] - p0[2]
    if layer_interfaces and abs(dz) > 1e-12:
        for h in layer_interfaces:
            t_cuts.append((h - p0[2]) / dz * L)
    intervals = _split_interval_at_interfaces(0.0, L, t_cuts)
    # The length comes from the end points: allow their round-off.
    scale = _coordinate_scale(p0, p1)
    parts = []
    for t_lo, t_hi in intervals:
        part_len = t_hi - t_lo
        n = _segment_count(part_len, ds, scale=scale)
        parts.append(_straight_wire(p0, direction, t_lo, part_len / n, n))
    return WireSegments.concatenate(parts)

docs.title: concatenate classmethod
docs.text:
concatenate(parts: Iterable[WireSegments]) -> WireSegments

Join several containers in order.

The wire indices are kept as they are (no offset): the parts of one wire cut at a layer interface stay one wire. A caller that joins different wires numbers them itself (_edge_wires()).

Source code in src/groundfield/geometry/primitives.py 
@classmethod
def concatenate(cls, parts: Iterable[WireSegments]) -> WireSegments:
    """Join several containers in order.

    The wire indices are kept as they are (no offset): the parts of
    one wire cut at a layer interface stay one wire. A caller that
    joins different wires numbers them itself (:func:`_edge_wires`).
    """
    parts = [p for p in parts if len(p)]
    if not parts:
        return cls.empty()
    wires = None
    if any(p.wires is not None for p in parts):
        wires = np.concatenate([p.wire_index for p in parts])
    return cls(
        np.concatenate([p.midpoints for p in parts], axis=0),
        np.concatenate([p.lengths for p in parts]),
        np.concatenate([p.directions for p in parts], axis=0),
        wires,
    )

docs.title: electrodes
docs.text:
Electrode geometries.

Defines the electrode primitives supported by the PDE / field model as plain data containers (Pydantic v2). Each class describes the geometric parameters (position, dimensions, wire radius). The discretisation into segments is performed inside the solver backend.

Conventions
  • Coordinate system: right-handed; the \(z\) axis points downwards into the soil. The soil surface is at \(z = 0\). A depth of 1 m therefore corresponds to \(z = 1.0\) (positive depth values).
  • Lengths in metres, wire radii in metres.
Notes

For TN distribution networks, RodElectrode (driven rod), RingElectrode (foundation / ring earth electrode) and MeshElectrode (mesh / foundation earth electrode) are the most relevant primitives.

docs.title: concrete_shell_coefficient
docs.text:
concrete_shell_coefficient(rho_c: float, wire_radius: float, thickness: float) -> float

Per-length coefficient of a cylindrical concrete shell (ADR-0012).

\[ C = \frac{\rho_c}{2\pi}\,\ln\frac{r_a + t}{r_a} \]

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rho_c float

Resistivity of the concrete in Ω·m, >= 0.

required wire_radius float

Radius \(r_a\) of the bare wire in m, > 0.

required thickness float

Radial thickness \(t\) of the shell in m, >= 0.

required

Returns:

Type Description float

\(C\) in Ω·m; 0.0 for rho_c = 0 or thickness = 0.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If an argument is negative or not finite, or wire_radius is not positive.

Notes

The electrode then carries wire_radius = r_a + t and concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m = C. For rho_c = 100 Ω·m and 5 cm of concrete around a 5 mm wire, \(C\) = 38.16 Ω·m.

Source code in src/groundfield/geometry/electrodes.py 
def concrete_shell_coefficient(
    rho_c: float, wire_radius: float, thickness: float
) -> float:
    r"""Per-length coefficient of a cylindrical concrete shell (ADR-0012).

    .. math::

        C = \frac{\rho_c}{2\pi}\,\ln\frac{r_a + t}{r_a}

    Parameters
    ----------
    rho_c
        Resistivity of the concrete in Ω·m, ``>= 0``.
    wire_radius
        Radius :math:`r_a` of the bare wire in m, ``> 0``.
    thickness
        Radial thickness :math:`t` of the shell in m, ``>= 0``.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        :math:`C` in Ω·m; ``0.0`` for ``rho_c = 0`` or ``thickness = 0``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If an argument is negative or not finite, or ``wire_radius`` is
        not positive.

    Notes
    -----
    The electrode then carries ``wire_radius = r_a + t`` and
    ``concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m = C``. For ``rho_c = 100`` Ω·m and
    5 cm of concrete around a 5 mm wire, :math:`C` = 38.16 Ω·m.
    """
    values = {"rho_c": rho_c, "wire_radius": wire_radius, "thickness": thickness}
    for name, value in values.items():
        if not math.isfinite(float(value)) or float(value) < 0.0:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite and non-negative, got {value!r}.")
    if float(wire_radius) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"wire_radius must be positive (m), got {wire_radius!r}.")
    r_a = float(wire_radius)
    return float(rho_c) / (2.0 * math.pi) * math.log((r_a + float(thickness)) / r_a)

def shell_resistance_from_coefficient(
    electrode: "_ElectrodeBase", coefficient_ohm_m: float | None = None
) -> float:
    """Lumped shell resistance of ``electrode`` for a per-length coefficient.

    Inverse of :func:`shell_coefficient_from_resistance`:
    :math:`R = C / L` in Ω with the total wire length :math:`L` in m.

    Parameters
    ----------
    electrode
        Encased electrode.
    coefficient_ohm_m
        Coefficient :math:`C` in Ω·m; ``None`` (default) takes the
        electrode's own ``concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m``.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        :math:`R` in Ω.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the coefficient is negative or not finite.
    """
    coefficient = float(
        electrode.concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m
        if coefficient_ohm_m is None
        else coefficient_ohm_m
    )
    if not math.isfinite(coefficient) or coefficient < 0.0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"coefficient_ohm_m must be finite and non-negative, got {coefficient!r}."
        )
    return coefficient / electrode.total_length()

docs.title: shell_coefficient_from_resistance
docs.text:
shell_coefficient_from_resistance(electrode: '_ElectrodeBase', resistance_ohm: float) -> float

Coefficient that gives electrode a lumped shell resistance.

The lumped shell model (ADR-0012 V1) describes the shell of one electrode by its total radial resistance \(R\) in series with the soil. Spread uniformly over the electrode's wire, it becomes the per-length coefficient \(C = R\,L\) with the total wire length \(L\) (total_length()); the image family then adds exactly \(R\) per ampere to the electrode potential. Use it when a shell is known as a lumped resistance (a measured value, or the World.concrete_shell_corrections entry of a 0.15.0 world); the generators compute \(C\) from the concrete resistivity with concrete_shell_coefficient() and put it on every wire of an encased foundation, cross-braces included.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default electrode '_ElectrodeBase'

Encased electrode (all of its wire is encased).

required resistance_ohm float

Lumped shell resistance \(R\) in Ω, >= 0.

required

Returns:

Type Description float

\(C\) in Ω·m, for concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If resistance_ohm is negative or not finite.

Source code in src/groundfield/geometry/electrodes.py 
def shell_coefficient_from_resistance(
    electrode: "_ElectrodeBase", resistance_ohm: float
) -> float:
    r"""Coefficient that gives ``electrode`` a lumped shell resistance.

    The lumped shell model (ADR-0012 V1) describes the shell of one
    electrode by its total radial resistance :math:`R` in series with the
    soil. Spread uniformly over the electrode's wire, it becomes the
    per-length coefficient :math:`C = R\,L` with the total wire length
    :math:`L` (:meth:`~_ElectrodeBase.total_length`); the image family then
    adds exactly :math:`R` per ampere to the electrode potential. Use it
    when a shell is known as a lumped resistance (a measured value, or
    the ``World.concrete_shell_corrections`` entry of a 0.15.0 world);
    the generators compute :math:`C` from the concrete resistivity with
    :func:`concrete_shell_coefficient` and put it on every wire of an
    encased foundation, cross-braces included.

    Parameters
    ----------
    electrode
        Encased electrode (all of its wire is encased).
    resistance_ohm
        Lumped shell resistance :math:`R` in Ω, ``>= 0``.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        :math:`C` in Ω·m, for ``concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``resistance_ohm`` is negative or not finite.
    """
    resistance = float(resistance_ohm)
    if not math.isfinite(resistance) or resistance < 0.0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"resistance_ohm must be finite and non-negative, got {resistance_ohm!r}."
        )
    return resistance * electrode.total_length()

docs.title: IO and groundinsight
docs.text: The io package is the boundary between groundfield and the rest of the software family: the export of reduced rho-f models as groundinsight BusType definitions (JSON file or live object, ADR-0008), CSV tables with a provenance header, and legacy VTK files for ParaView. Result files of a solve are described on Result files.

docs.title: Mathematical and physical context
docs.text:
The reduction pipeline is

\[ \text{field model} \;\longrightarrow\; Z(\rho, f) \;\longrightarrow\; \texttt{BusType.impedance\_formula} \;\longrightarrow\; \text{network model}. \]

groundinsight evaluates the formula with two free symbols, f (Hz) and rho (the Bus.specific_earth_resistance in Ω·m), and the imaginary unit j. Both fit families are projected onto that set:

  • standard form (RhoFStandardFit), fitted over a sweep of \(\rho\) and \(f\): \(Z = k_0 + k_1\rho + (k_2 + jk_3)f + (k_4 + jk_5)f\rho\), already in (rho, f);
  • vector fit (VectorFitResult) at one soil: a rational function of \(s\), exported with \(s \to j2\pi f\), so the formula depends on f only. The soil it belongs to must be given as rho_at_fit.

The rho of layered soil. A Bus carries one resistivity. For homogeneous soil it is \(\rho\); for layered soil it is the effective resistivity of the AP1 catalogue,

\[ \rho_\text{eff} = \rho_1^{\,1-w}\,\rho_2^{\,w}, \qquad w = w_0\,(h_1/10\ \mathrm{m})^{-\beta}, \]

with the weights \((w_0, \beta)\) of the electrode class: \(w_0 = 0.13\), \(\beta = 0.8\) of the LV networks by default, or a preset of the AP2 hand-over such as "station" (0.06, 1.3) or "lv_group_2_p10" (gf.effective_resistivity(soil, preset=...), see Soil). It is the value the AP2 network model gives a bus. A vector fit therefore passes rho_at_fit=gf.effective_resistivity(soil, preset=...), and a standard form is fitted over the effective resistivities of the solved soils, gf.rho_f_standard_from_results(results, [gf.effective_resistivity(r.soil, preset=...) for r in results]); both kinds of BusType then pair with a Bus whose resistivity uses the same preset. Every document records the convention as metadata["rho_definition"] = "effective_resistivity" (documents of 0.15.0 have no such entry) and the preset you name with rho_preset=... (a key of gf.soil.EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS) as metadata["rho_preset"], None when none is named (user decision Q39; documents of earlier versions load with None, spec.rho_preset). The exporter cannot check the number it is given against the preset; the paths that serve a bus can: evaluate_spec(spec, f, rho, rho_preset=...) and bustype_from_spec(spec, rho_preset=...) (the live groundinsight BusType of a loaded document) take the preset of the bus and emit RhoPresetMismatchWarning when the document names another one — a preset holds for its electrode class only (the AP1 station paired with "lv_group_4_p40" misses the field solution by 39.9 % rms). The live BusType of to_bustype, save_bustype_to_db and bustype_from_spec has no metadata; with a preset its description ends with the line groundfield rho_preset: <name> (a preset line in the given description is replaced), which the groundinsight database keeps, and gf.bustype_rho_preset(bus_type) reads it back, also from a BusType loaded with gi.load_bustypes_from_db() (audit W3B-06; None without a preset line). On load metadata["rho_preset"] must be a preset name or null, as the exporters write it (padding, line breaks and unknown names are refused); only the exact line groundfield rho_preset: <name> of a description is the record, the other lines stay as given (audit W3R2B-06). Describe the layers, and explicit weights \(w_0\), \(\beta\), in soil_summary.

Before a BusType is written, the exported formula (with its rounded coefficients) is checked for passivity, \(\operatorname{Re}Z \ge 0\) from 0 Hz to twice the highest fitted frequency; a violation warns with NonPassiveFitWarning (or raises NonPassiveFitError with require_passive=True). A formula read from a file is untrusted text: load_bustype_json and evaluate_spec parse it with an allow-list parser that builds the expression from the syntax tree and never evaluates the text (numbers, f, rho, j, pi, E, arithmetic, literal powers, sqrt / exp / log, within size bounds). Every node is built unevaluated; the parser computes the numbers itself in bounded floating point, and evaluate_spec evaluates the tree with its own numeric function instead of SymPy's lambdify, so a crafted formula cannot make SymPy expand or simplify it. Printing a parsed formula or handing it to lambdify lets SymPy evaluate parts of it again: show the formula text of an untrusted file instead. The parser collects like terms of a sum itself; a real or imaginary part that cancels below \(2^{-100}\) times the largest magnitude of that part among the terms is zero, the other part is kept. Non-finite numbers of a BusType document (an unknown rms error, a non-finite sample) are written as null, so the file is strict JSON. load_bustype_json also checks the rest of the document: name and system_type are not objects or lists, description is a string or null, and the free-form metadata nest at most MAX_METADATA_DEPTH (32) levels; anything else raises ValueError. fit_quality_summary reads only finite numbers and strings from the metadata, so a loaded document never makes it fail.

Validity. The exported model inherits the quasi-static band (\(f < 1\,\mathrm{kHz}\)) and the linearity of the field model; it is meant for fault-current, EPR and reduction studies, not for impulse or lightning transients. One BusType is the impedance of one terminal (the input impedance by default); mutual impedances (BranchType) are not exported.

docs.title: Transport
docs.text: Path Functions Needs groundinsight JSON file save_bustype_json, load_bustype_json, to_bustype_dict no Python object to_bustype (live groundinsight.BusType), save_bustype_to_db yes (pip install "groundfield[groundinsight]") Check evaluate_spec(spec, frequencies, rho), fit_quality_summary(spec) no

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A station earth (ring and rod) in two-layer soil, swept over the upper-layer resistivity \(\rho_1\) (fixed \(\rho_2 = 100\,\Omega\,\mathrm{m}\), \(h_1 = 5\,\mathrm{m}\)), fitted with the standard form over the effective resistivities of the four soils (weights of the "station" preset) and exported:

import groundfield as gf

def station(rho_1):
    world = gf.create_world(soil=gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=rho_1, rho_2=100.0, h_1=5.0))
    gf.create_electrode(world, "ring", name="station", center=(0.0, 0.0, 0.8), radius=2.0)
    gf.create_electrode(world, "rod", name="rod", position=(2.0, 0.0, 0.8), length=3.0)
    gf.create_conductor(world, name="bond", start="station", end="rod")   # ideal bond
    gf.create_source(world, attached_to="station", magnitude=1.0)
    return world

engine = gf.create_engine(frequencies=[50.0, 1000.0])
results = [engine.solve(station(rho_1)) for rho_1 in (30.0, 100.0, 300.0, 1000.0)]
rhos = [gf.effective_resistivity(r.soil, preset="station") for r in results]  # 35.8 ... 711.6 Ohm m
fit = gf.rho_f_standard_from_results(results, rhos, max_relative_tol=0.10)  # input impedance

path = gf.save_bustype_json(
    fit, "station.bustype.json", name="Station", system_type="Substation", voltage_level=20.0,
    soil_summary="TwoLayerSoil(rho_1 sweep, rho_2=100, h_1=5)", rho_preset="station",
)
spec = gf.load_bustype_json(path)
print(gf.fit_quality_summary(spec))      # ... max_rel=7.48%, quantity=input, rho_preset=station

Z_formula = gf.evaluate_spec(spec, frequencies=[50.0], rho=rhos[3], rho_preset="station")[0]
Z_field = results[3].input_impedance()[0]
assert abs(Z_formula - Z_field) / abs(Z_field) <= fit.max_relative + 1e-9
assert spec.metadata["rho_definition"] == "effective_resistivity"
assert spec.rho_preset == "station"
assert abs(rhos[3] - 711.64) < 0.01 and fit.max_relative < 0.10

A bus whose resistivity comes from another preset is reported:

import warnings

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    gf.evaluate_spec(spec, [50.0], gf.effective_resistivity(results[3].soil), rho_preset="lv_network")
assert any(issubclass(w.category, gf.RhoPresetMismatchWarning) for w in caught)

The station is compact and lies in the upper layer, so it sees less of the lower layer than an LV network: the standard form fits it to 7.5 % over \(\rho_\text{eff}\) with the station weights, against 13.4 % with the default weights of the LV networks. Over \(\rho_1\) it would fit to 3.9 %, because at fixed \(\rho_2\) the constant \(k_0\) absorbs the lower layer, but the bus the BusType is paired with carries \(\rho_\text{eff}\), here with the station preset. Check max_relative, and see Soil for the presets and the validity of \(\rho_\text{eff}\). Without inductive conductors the impedance does not depend on frequency, and the frequency coefficients \(k_2 \ldots k_5\) come out at round-off level. Tutorial T05 shows the export of a frequency-dependent system, including the vector-fit path with rho_at_fit.

docs.title: CSV and VTK
docs.text:
The CSV writers (save_potential_path_csv, save_electrode_table_csv, save_cluster_impedances_csv) write UTF-8, comma-separated files at full precision with a # header that records the package version, the backend, the frequencies and the solve provenance; read_csv_with_provenance(path) returns the table and the header. A complex quantity is written as <symbol>_re, <symbol>_im, abs_<symbol>. overwrite=False (default) refuses to replace a file.

export_geometry_vtk(world, path) writes the electrodes and conductors as legacy ASCII POLYDATA (cell scalar role: 0 electrode, 1 conductor), export_field_vtk(result, path, extent=..., z=...) the surface potential as STRUCTURED_POINTS with real and imaginary part. Coordinates are double precision; \(z\) points down, so apply a Transform with scale \((1, 1, -1)\) in ParaView for the usual view.

world = station(100.0)
result = results[1]
csv_path = gf.save_potential_path_csv(
    result, "profile.csv", start=(2.0, 0.0, 0.0), direction=(1.0, 0.0, 0.0), distance=30.0, n=31
)
table, header = gf.read_csv_with_provenance(csv_path)
gf.export_geometry_vtk(world, "station.vtk")
gf.export_field_vtk(result, "surface_potential.vtk", extent=(-10.0, 10.0, -10.0, 10.0), n=(41, 41))

assert len(table) == 2 * 31      # 31 points at each of the two frequencies
assert {"frequency_Hz", "phi_re", "phi_im", "abs_phi"} <= set(table.columns)
assert header["backend"] == "image_2layer"

docs.title: groundinsight
docs.text:
Export of reduced rho-f fits to groundinsight.

This module is the canonical bridge between the field-grade reference computation in groundfield and the reduced equivalent network model in groundinsight.

Two equally supported transports are provided:

  • JSON file — neutral, language-agnostic schema versioned via schema_version. Produce with to_bustype_dict() / save_bustype_json(); read back with load_bustype_json().
  • Python API — to_bustype() returns a live groundinsight.BusType Pydantic instance via a lazy import. groundinsight is therefore an optional dependency of groundfield (extras group [groundinsight]). The JSON path does not require groundinsight at all.
Mathematical background

groundinsight.BusType.impedance_formula is parsed with two free symbols, f (frequency in Hz) and rho (Bus.specific_earth_resistance), and the imaginary unit j. Both fit families exported here are projected onto that symbol set:

  • RhoFStandardFit is already in the canonical (rho, f) form

$$ Z(\rho, f) \;=\; k_1\rho \;+\; (k_2 + j k_3)\,f \;+\; (k_4 + j k_5)\,f\,\rho. $$

  • VectorFitResult is a rational function of the Laplace variable \(s = j\,2\pi f\). The export substitutes \(s\to j\,2\pi f\) symbolically so the resulting expression is in f only (independent of rho); the soil resistivity the fit belongs to (rho_at_fit) is recorded in the samples and metadata blocks.

A groundinsight Bus carries one specific_earth_resistance, the rho of the formula: \(\rho\) for homogeneous soil and, for layered soil, the effective resistivity

\[ \rho_\text{eff} = \rho_1^{\,1-w}\,\rho_2^{\,w}, \qquad w = w_0\,(h_1 / 10\ \mathrm{m})^{-\beta}, \]

with the weights \((w_0, \beta)\) of the electrode class: the AP1 calibration \(w_0 = 0.13\), \(\beta = 0.8\) by default, or a preset of EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS such as "station" or "lv_group_2_p10" (effective_resistivity(); ADR-0008), the value the AP2 network model gives a bus. A vector fit therefore passes rho_at_fit=effective_resistivity(soil, preset=...), and a standard-form fit over layered soils is fitted over the effective resistivities of the solved soils, rho_f_standard_from_results(results, [effective_resistivity(r.soil, preset=...) for r in results]); both kinds of BusType then pair with a Bus whose resistivity uses the same preset. Every document records this convention as metadata["rho_definition"] = "effective_resistivity" (documents of 0.15.0 have no such entry) and the preset the caller names, metadata["rho_preset"] (rho_preset=... of the exporters, None when no preset is named; user decision Q39; documents of earlier versions have no such entry and load with None). The live groundinsight BusType of to_bustype(), save_bustype_to_db() and bustype_from_spec() has no metadata; it carries the preset as the last line of its description, groundfield rho_preset: <name>, which the groundinsight database keeps, and bustype_rho_preset() reads it back (audit W3B-06). Only that exact line, with a known preset name, is the record: the rest of a given description stays as it is (audit W3R2B-06), and a document is loaded only with a known preset name (or none), as the exporters write it. The exporter cannot check the number it is given against the preset. evaluate_spec() and bustype_from_spec() take the preset of the bus they serve and emit RhoPresetMismatchWarning when the document names another one (a preset holds for its electrode class only: the AP1 station paired with "lv_group_4_p40" misses the field solution by 39.9 % rms). The layers themselves, and explicit weights \(w_0\), \(\beta\), go into soil_summary.

The exporter does not care which impedance was fitted (input impedance, cluster impedance or the impedance of one electrode); it exports the function it is given.

Formula text

The formula keeps the structure of the fit (partial fractions for a vector fit, the standard form term by term) and prints every floating-point coefficient once, rounded to decimals significant digits with Python's correctly rounded float formatting, so the text is identical on every platform. The expression comes from the same renderer as fit_to_sympy() and fit_to_sympy_standard() (one pole-pairing rule, no sympy.simplify). A coefficient therefore carries a relative rounding error of at most \(\tfrac12\,10^{1-N}\) for \(N\) = decimals; with the default \(N = 12\) the formula reproduces fit.evaluate to about \(10^{-11}\) relative.

Formula safety

A formula read from a file is untrusted text. evaluate_spec(), BusTypeSpec.from_dict() and load_bustype_json() parse it with an allow-list parser that builds the SymPy expression from the Python syntax tree and never evaluates the text: numbers, f, rho, j / I, pi, E, + - * /, ** with a literal exponent, and sqrt / exp / log, within size and magnitude bounds. Every formula written by the exporter satisfies this grammar, including those of groundfield 0.15.0 and earlier.

Passivity

A grounding impedance is the driving-point impedance of a passive one-port, so its real part is non-negative at every frequency,

\[ \operatorname{Re} Z(j\,2\pi f) \;\ge\; 0 \qquad (f \ge 0). \]

A fit can violate this between its samples (a spurious resonance) or beyond them. Before a BusType is built the exported formula (what groundinsight will evaluate, coefficients rounded) goes through check_passivity(), the one passivity check of the package, over its default band from 0 Hz to twice the highest fitted frequency: for a vector fit a dense grid (linear and logarithmic points, the samples and the midpoints between them, points around every pole) whose lowest minima are refined by a bounded scalar minimisation; for the standard form, whose real part is bilinear in \((\rho, f)\), the four corners of the fitted range of rho times the band, which is exact. The report (as_dict()) is stored in metadata["passivity"]; a violation emits NonPassiveFitWarning, or raises NonPassiveFitError with require_passive=True.

See also

docs/adr/0008-groundinsight-bridge.md — full design rationale, JSON schema, and validation programme.

docs.title: MAX_METADATA_DEPTH module-attribute
docs.text:
MAX_METADATA_DEPTH = 32

Deepest nesting of objects and lists in the metadata of a BusType document.

The exporters write at most four levels. A deeper document is refused on load (ValueError); the JSON decoder reads thousands of levels, but every consumer that walks the metadata recursively would fail with RecursionError.

docs.text:
BusTypeSpec(name: str, description: Optional[str], system_type: str, voltage_level: float, impedance_formula: str, samples: dict[str, list[float]], metadata: dict[str, Any])

Neutral, in-memory representation of an exported BusType.

The spec is what to_bustype_dict() returns under the hood and what load_bustype_json() reads back. It carries everything necessary to either build a groundinsight.BusType (via to_bustype()) or to write the on-disk JSON document.

Attributes:

Name Type Description name, description, system_type, voltage_level

The four scalar fields that the groundinsight.BusType Pydantic model carries.

impedance_formula str

The fitted Z(rho, f) expression as text. Free symbols: f (Hz) and rho (\(\Omega\,\mathrm{m}\)); imaginary unit j. Only the grammar described in the module docstring is accepted when the spec is loaded or evaluated.

samples dict[str, list[float]]

Dict with the parallel tabular representation. Keys "frequency_Hz", "rho_Ohm_m", "Z_real_Ohm", "Z_imag_Ohm" each map to a list of floats of equal length (null in the JSON document for a value that is not finite). Provided so a future tabular ingest path on the groundinsight side can be served immediately.

metadata dict[str, Any]

Free-form metadata dict; populated by the exporters with the fit method, fit quality (rms_error_Ohm, rms_relative, for the standard form max_relative; null when unknown), the impedance the fit represents ("quantity": "input", "cluster", "electrode" or null for raw samples), how rho is defined ("rho_definition": "effective_resistivity", see the module docstring), fit-method-specific details (poles/residues for vector fits, \(k_0\dots k_5\) and the "weights" for the standard form), the passivity check ("passivity"), the source groundfield version and a UTC timestamp.

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> "BusTypeSpec":
    """Build a :class:`BusTypeSpec` from a JSON-loaded ``dict``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    payload : dict
        Schema-v1 document as produced by :func:`to_bustype_dict`.

    Returns
    -------
    BusTypeSpec

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the payload is not a schema-v1 BusType document: not a
        ``dict``, a wrong schema name or version, a missing ``name``,
        ``system_type`` or ``voltage_level``, a ``name`` or
        ``system_type`` that is an object or a list, a ``description``
        that is neither a string nor ``null``, a ``voltage_level`` that
        is not a finite number, ``samples`` / ``metadata`` that are not
        objects (sample lists hold numbers or ``None``), or metadata
        nested deeper than :data:`MAX_METADATA_DEPTH`.
    EvaluateSpecError
        If ``impedance_formula`` is missing, not a string or a number,
        or outside the allowed formula grammar. The formula is parsed,
        never evaluated as code; the message names the offending
        element.
    """
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise ValueError(
            f"a BusType document is a JSON object, got {type(payload).__name__}"
        )
    if payload.get("schema") != SCHEMA_NAME:
        raise ValueError(
            f"unexpected schema name: got {payload.get('schema')!r}, "
            f"expected {SCHEMA_NAME!r}"
        )
    try:
        version = int(payload.get("schema_version", 0))
    except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError):
        raise ValueError(
            "unsupported schema_version "
            f"{str(payload.get('schema_version'))[:40]!r}; this groundfield "
            f"build only reads v{SCHEMA_VERSION}"
        ) from None
    if version != SCHEMA_VERSION:
        raise ValueError(
            f"unsupported schema_version {version}; this groundfield "
            f"build only reads v{SCHEMA_VERSION}"
        )
    for key in ("name", "system_type", "voltage_level"):
        if key not in payload:
            raise ValueError(f"BusType document has no {key!r}")
    for key in ("name", "system_type"):
        if isinstance(payload[key], (dict, list)):
            raise ValueError(
                f"BusType document: {key!r} must be a string, got a JSON "
                f"{'object' if isinstance(payload[key], dict) else 'array'}"
            )
    name = str(payload["name"])
    description = payload.get("description")
    if description is not None and not isinstance(description, str):
        raise ValueError(
            f"BusType document {name!r}: description must be a string or "
            f"null, got {type(description).__name__}"
        )
    formula = payload.get("impedance_formula")
    if formula is None:
        raise EvaluateSpecError(
            f"BusType document {name!r} has no 'impedance_formula'."
        )
    if isinstance(formula, (dict, list)):
        raise EvaluateSpecError(
            f"BusType document {name!r}: impedance_formula must be a string."
        )
    formula = formula if isinstance(formula, str) else str(formula)
    _parse_formula(formula, context=f"BusType document {name!r}")
    samples = payload.get("samples") or {}
    try:
        voltage_level = float(payload["voltage_level"])
    except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError):
        voltage_level = math.nan
    if not math.isfinite(voltage_level):
        raise ValueError(
            f"BusType document {name!r}: voltage_level must be a finite "
            f"number, got {str(payload['voltage_level'])[:40]!r}"
        )
    metadata = payload.get("metadata") or {}
    if not isinstance(samples, dict) or not isinstance(metadata, dict):
        raise ValueError(
            f"BusType document {name!r}: samples and metadata must be JSON objects"
        )
    _strict_json(metadata, context=f"BusType document {name!r}: metadata")
    # a preset name as the exporters write it (audit W3R2B-06: blank
    # names were refused, but padding, line breaks and unknown names
    # loaded, and the live BusType could not carry them)
    _check_rho_preset(
        metadata.get("rho_preset"),
        f"BusType document {name!r}: metadata['rho_preset']",
    )
    sample_lists: dict[str, list[Any]] = {}
    for key in ("frequency_Hz", "rho_Ohm_m", "Z_real_Ohm", "Z_imag_Ohm"):
        values = samples.get(key, [])
        if isinstance(values, np.ndarray):
            values = values.tolist()
        if not isinstance(values, (list, tuple)) or not all(
            value is None
            or (isinstance(value, numbers.Real) and not isinstance(value, bool))
            for value in values
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                f"BusType document {name!r}: samples[{key!r}] must be a list "
                "of numbers (null for a value that is not finite)"
            )
        sample_lists[key] = list(values)
    return cls(
        name=name,
        description=description,
        system_type=str(payload["system_type"]),
        voltage_level=voltage_level,
        impedance_formula=formula,
        samples=sample_lists,
        metadata=dict(metadata),
    )

def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return a JSON-ready ``dict`` matching schema v1.

    The result is strict JSON: every number that is not finite (a
    sample, a fit-quality figure of a hand-built fit, a description
    that is not a string, ...) is written as ``None`` (JSON ``null``).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the metadata nest deeper than :data:`MAX_METADATA_DEPTH`.
    """
    return {
        "schema": SCHEMA_NAME,
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "name": self.name,
        "description": _strict_json(self.description),
        "system_type": self.system_type,
        "voltage_level": float(self.voltage_level),
        "impedance_formula": self.impedance_formula,
        "samples": {
            key: [_finite_or_none(x) for x in self.samples.get(key, [])]
            for key in ("frequency_Hz", "rho_Ohm_m", "Z_real_Ohm", "Z_imag_Ohm")
        },
        "metadata": _strict_json(dict(self.metadata)),
    }

The exported impedance formula has Re Z < 0 somewhere.

A passive grounding impedance satisfies \(\operatorname{Re} Z \ge 0\) at every frequency. def bustype_from_spec(spec: BusTypeSpec, *, rho_preset: Optional[str] = None):
    """Build a live :class:`groundinsight.BusType` from a loaded document.

    The ``groundinsight`` model of a spec built by the exporters or read
    with :func:`load_bustype_json` (its four scalar fields and the
    formula; the metadata is not carried over, as with :func:`to_bustype`,
    except the preset the document records: the description ends with
    ``groundfield rho_preset: <name>``, audit W3B-06).

    Parameters
    ----------
    spec : BusTypeSpec
        The document.
    rho_preset : str, optional
        The preset of :func:`~groundfield.soil.effective_resistivity` that
        the bus of this BusType uses for its ``specific_earth_resistance``.
        A different preset recorded in the document emits
        :class:`RhoPresetMismatchWarning` (user decision Q39); ``None``
        (default) checks nothing.

    Returns
    -------
    groundinsight.models.core_models.BusType

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If ``spec`` is not a :class:`BusTypeSpec`.
    ValueError
        If ``rho_preset`` is not a preset name.
    ImportError
        If ``groundinsight`` is not installed.

    Warns
    -----
    RhoPresetMismatchWarning
        If ``rho_preset`` differs from the preset the document records.
    """
    if not isinstance(spec, BusTypeSpec):
        raise TypeError(
            f"bustype_from_spec: expected a BusTypeSpec, got {type(spec).__name__}"
        )
    _warn_on_preset_mismatch(spec, rho_preset, "bustype_from_spec")
    return _to_live_bustype(spec)

def bustype_rho_preset(bus_type: Any) -> Optional[str]:
    """Effective-resistivity preset recorded on a BusType (audit W3B-06).

    A live ``groundinsight.BusType`` built by :func:`to_bustype`,
    :func:`save_bustype_to_db` or :func:`bustype_from_spec` from a fit or a
    document with a preset carries it as the last line of its description,
    ``groundfield rho_preset: <name>``; the ``groundinsight`` database keeps
    the description, so the preset of a BusType loaded from it
    (``gi.load_bustypes_from_db()``) is read the same way. Compare it with
    the preset of the bus's ``specific_earth_resistance``
    (:func:`~groundfield.soil.effective_resistivity`); for a document use
    :attr:`BusTypeSpec.rho_preset` or the check of :func:`evaluate_spec`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    bus_type : groundinsight.BusType, BusTypeSpec or any object with a ``description``
        The BusType. For a :class:`BusTypeSpec` the preset its metadata
        records (:attr:`BusTypeSpec.rho_preset`).

    Returns
    -------
    str or None
        The preset name, or ``None`` when the last line of the description
        is not exactly ``groundfield rho_preset: <name>`` with a name of
        :data:`~groundfield.soil.EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS` (no preset
        was named, the BusType was not built by groundfield 2026.11 or
        later, or the line is the user's own text; audit W3R2B-06).

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If ``bus_type`` has no ``description`` or a description that is
        neither a string nor ``None``.
    """
    if isinstance(bus_type, BusTypeSpec):
        return bus_type.rho_preset
    try:
        text = bus_type.description
    except AttributeError:
        raise TypeError(
            "bustype_rho_preset: expected a groundinsight BusType (an object "
            f"with a description), got {type(bus_type).__name__}"
        ) from None
    if text is None:
        return None
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise TypeError(
            "bustype_rho_preset: the description must be a string or None, got "
            f"{type(text).__name__}"
        )
    lines = text.splitlines()
    return _preset_of_line(lines[-1]) if lines else None

def evaluate_spec(
    spec: BusTypeSpec,
    frequencies: Sequence[float],
    rho: float,
    *,
    rho_preset: Optional[str] = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Evaluate a :class:`BusTypeSpec` at arbitrary frequencies.

    Parses the stored ``impedance_formula`` with the allow-list parser
    (see the module docstring; the text is never evaluated as code) and
    evaluates the resulting expression with NumPy at the provided
    ``rho`` and ``f`` values, node by node through
    :func:`~groundfield.io._formula.formula_function` (complex
    arithmetic, principal branch for roots and logarithms; SymPy's code
    generation is not used). Useful for cheap sanity checks that do not
    require ``groundinsight`` to be installed.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spec : BusTypeSpec
        Loaded spec (e.g. from :func:`load_bustype_json`).
    frequencies : sequence of float
        Frequencies in Hz.
    rho : float
        Soil resistivity in $\\Omega\\,\\mathrm{m}$. Ignored if the
        formula does not depend on ``rho`` (vector-fit case).
    rho_preset : str, optional
        The preset of :func:`~groundfield.soil.effective_resistivity` that
        gave ``rho`` (the bus's preset). When the document records another
        one (:attr:`BusTypeSpec.rho_preset`), a
        :class:`RhoPresetMismatchWarning` is emitted (user decision Q39);
        ``None`` (default), or a document without a recorded preset, checks
        nothing.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Complex-valued $Z$ in $\\Omega$ at every requested frequency.

    Raises
    ------
    EvaluateSpecError
        Subclass of :class:`ValueError`; raised when ``spec`` is not a
        :class:`BusTypeSpec` instance, ``impedance_formula`` is empty
        / missing on the spec, or the formula is outside the allowed
        grammar or its size and magnitude bounds (including unknown
        free symbols — anything other than ``f``, ``rho``, ``j`` /
        ``I``, ``pi`` and ``E``). The exception is typed so downstream
        consumers (notably ``groundinsight``) can catch it without
        substring matching on the message. Existing ``except
        ValueError`` blocks keep working because
        :class:`EvaluateSpecError` inherits from :class:`ValueError`.
        A ``rho_preset`` that is not a preset name raises
        :class:`ValueError`.

    Warns
    -----
    RhoPresetMismatchWarning
        If ``rho_preset`` differs from the preset the document records.
    """
    from groundfield.io._formula import formula_function

    # Defensive entry-point validation. Hand-rolled BusTypeSpec-like
    # dicts (e.g. constructed in a CLI helper from a YAML campaign
    # config) routinely miss the impedance_formula; surface the real
    # problem here instead of an opaque error deep in SymPy.
    if not isinstance(spec, BusTypeSpec):
        raise EvaluateSpecError(
            "evaluate_spec: expected a BusTypeSpec instance, got "
            f"{type(spec).__name__}. Build one via load_bustype_json "
            "or BusTypeSpec.from_dict before calling evaluate_spec."
        )
    formula = getattr(spec, "impedance_formula", None)
    if formula is None or not str(formula).strip():
        raise EvaluateSpecError(
            "evaluate_spec: spec.impedance_formula is missing or "
            "empty. A BusTypeSpec must carry a non-empty "
            "impedance_formula string with free symbols in "
            "{f, rho, j}."
        )
    expr = _parse_formula(
        formula if isinstance(formula, str) else str(formula),
        context="evaluate_spec: spec.impedance_formula",
    )
    _warn_on_preset_mismatch(spec, rho_preset, "evaluate_spec")
    func = formula_function(expr, ("f", "rho"))
    f_arr = np.asarray(frequencies, dtype=float)
    out = func(f_arr, float(rho))
    return np.broadcast_to(out, f_arr.shape).copy()

def fit_quality_summary(spec: BusTypeSpec) -> str:
    """One-line human-readable summary of fit quality / kind.

    Names the fit method, the rms error, the relative rms and worst
    pointwise relative error when the document records them, and the
    impedance the fit represents (``quantity``: ``input``,
    ``cluster`` or ``electrode``) when known.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spec
        Exported or loaded BusType document.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        ``BusTypeSpec(name=..., method=..., rms=..., ...)``; a figure the
        document does not record is left out (the rms reads ``unknown``).
    """
    md = spec.metadata if isinstance(spec.metadata, dict) else {}
    fq = md.get("fit_quality")
    if not isinstance(fq, dict):
        fq = {}
    method = _summary_label(md.get("fit_method")) or "unknown"
    rms = _summary_figure(fq.get("rms_error_Ohm"))
    rms_text = "unknown" if rms is None else f"{rms:.3e} Ω"
    parts = [f"name={spec.name!r}", f"method={method}", f"rms={rms_text}"]
    rms_relative = _summary_figure(fq.get("rms_relative"))
    if rms_relative is not None:
        parts.append(f"rms_rel={rms_relative:.2%}")
    max_relative = _summary_figure(fq.get("max_relative"))
    if max_relative is not None:
        parts.append(f"max_rel={max_relative:.2%}")
    quantity = _summary_label(md.get("quantity"))
    if quantity is not None:
        parts.append(f"quantity={quantity}")
    preset = spec.rho_preset if isinstance(spec, BusTypeSpec) else None
    if preset is not None:
        parts.append(f"rho_preset={preset}")
    return f"BusTypeSpec({', '.join(parts)})"

def load_bustype_json(path: Union[str, Path]) -> BusTypeSpec:
    """Load a ``BusType`` JSON document into a :class:`BusTypeSpec`.

    Validates the schema name and version and parses the formula with
    the allow-list parser (it is never evaluated as code).
    Forward-compatibility for future schema versions is the explicit
    responsibility of this function: when ``schema_version`` differs
    from :data:`SCHEMA_VERSION`, dispatch to the appropriate loader.
    Today only v1 exists.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : str or pathlib.Path
        JSON file written by :func:`save_bustype_json`.

    Returns
    -------
    BusTypeSpec

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the file is not valid JSON (also: nested too deeply to be
        read) or not a schema-v1 BusType document, see
        :meth:`BusTypeSpec.from_dict`.
    EvaluateSpecError
        If ``impedance_formula`` is missing or outside the allowed
        formula grammar.
    """
    p = Path(path)
    with p.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        try:
            payload = json.load(fh)
        except RecursionError:
            raise ValueError(
                f"BusType document {p.name!r} is nested too deeply to be read"
            ) from None
    return BusTypeSpec.from_dict(payload)

def save_bustype_json(
    fit: FitLike,
    path: Union[str, Path],
    *,
    name: str,
    system_type: str,
    voltage_level: float,
    description: Optional[str] = None,
    decimals: int = 12,
    rho_at_fit: Optional[float] = None,
    electrode_name: Optional[str] = None,
    soil_summary: Optional[str] = None,
    indent: int = 2,
    require_passive: bool = False,
    rho_preset: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Path:
    """Write the schema-v1 JSON file to disk.

    Performs the conversion and checks of :func:`to_bustype_dict`.
    Nothing is written when the export is refused (missing
    ``rho_at_fit`` for a vector fit, ``require_passive=True`` with a
    failed passivity check).

    Parameters
    ----------
    fit : RhoFStandardFit or VectorFitResult
        The fitted rho-f model.
    path : str or pathlib.Path
        Target file; parent directories are created.
    name, system_type, voltage_level, description
        The ``BusType`` fields, see :func:`to_bustype_dict`.
    decimals : int, optional
        Significant digits per coefficient (default 12), see
        :func:`to_bustype_dict`.
    rho_at_fit : float, optional
        Soil resistivity in $\\Omega\\,\\mathrm{m}$ of a
        :class:`VectorFitResult`; required for vector fits, ignored for
        standard-form fits. For layered soil the convention is the
        effective resistivity ``effective_resistivity(soil, preset=...)``
        (see :func:`to_bustype_dict`).
    electrode_name, soil_summary : str, optional
        Free-form metadata entries.
    indent : int, optional
        JSON indentation. Default 2.
    require_passive : bool, optional
        Raise :class:`NonPassiveFitError` instead of warning when the
        passivity check fails. Default False.
    rho_preset : str, optional
        The preset of :func:`~groundfield.soil.effective_resistivity` behind
        the ``rho`` of the fit, recorded as ``metadata["rho_preset"]``
        (default ``None``: none named), see :func:`to_bustype_dict`.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The path the file was actually written to, for chaining.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``rho_at_fit`` is missing for a vector fit or invalid.
    NonPassiveFitError
        With ``require_passive=True``, if the passivity check fails.

    Warns
    -----
    NonPassiveFitWarning
        If the passivity check fails and ``require_passive`` is False.
    """
    payload = _build_spec(
        fit,
        name=name,
        system_type=system_type,
        voltage_level=voltage_level,
        description=description,
        decimals=decimals,
        rho_at_fit=rho_at_fit,
        electrode_name=electrode_name,
        soil_summary=soil_summary,
        require_passive=require_passive,
        caller="save_bustype_json",
        rho_preset=rho_preset,
    ).to_dict()
    text = json.dumps(payload, indent=indent, sort_keys=False, allow_nan=False)
    p = Path(path)
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with p.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(text + "\n")
    return p

docs.text:
CSV exports for groundfield results.

This module provides three convenience writers that turn a FieldResult (and optionally its companion World) into machine-readable, tool-agnostic CSV files. They wrap the existing postprocess helpers — no new science here, just a clean disk format for sharing typical results across notebooks, spreadsheets, and downstream pipelines.

Column-name convention

All complex-valued quantities follow the same <symbol>_re, <symbol>_im, abs_<symbol> triple where symbol is the physical symbol of the quantity:

  • potential — phi_re / phi_im / abs_phi;
  • current — I_re / I_im / abs_I;
  • impedance — Z_re / Z_im / abs_Z.

The three writers therefore deliberately use different magnitude columns (abs_phi for the potential path, abs_I for the electrode table, abs_Z for the cluster table). They are not intended to be concat/merge-ed on the magnitude column without an explicit rename; the column constants below (POTENTIAL_PATH_COLUMNS, etc.) lock the schema for downstream consumers.

The identifier columns follow the postprocess tables the writers wrap: an electrode row is keyed by name, a cluster row by cluster_root (the canonical member of the galvanic cluster). There is no electrode or cluster column.

All writers use UTF-8, comma-separated, with a header row; floating-point values are written at full precision so the files round-trip without loss of accuracy.

Frequency and provenance (review pass 10, 10.73)

Every table records its frequency in Hz: the electrode and cluster tables in a frequency_hz column (lower-case unit suffix, the convention of the spec layer and of FieldResult.to_dataframe(), 10.69), the potential path in its frequency_Hz column of v0.15.0. Every file starts with # comment lines that record where it came from::

# groundfield csv: electrode_table
# groundfield_version: 2026.11.0
# written_utc: 2026-11-07T19:30:00Z
# backend: image
# frequency_hz: 50
# frequency_index: 0

followed by the provenance block of the solve (solve.* keys) when the result carries one. Read such a file with read_csv_with_provenance(), which skips exactly the leading comment lines and returns the metadata as a dict, or with pandas.read_csv(path, comment="#") when no value contains #. Pass provenance=False for a plain CSV. The writers refuse to replace an existing file unless overwrite=True.

def read_csv_with_provenance(path: str | Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict[str, str]]:
    """Read a CSV written by this module, with its provenance header.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path
        File written by one of the ``save_*_csv`` writers (with or
        without provenance header).

    Returns
    -------
    df : pandas.DataFrame
        The table. Only the leading ``#`` lines are skipped, so values
        that contain ``#`` (electrode names) stay intact.
    provenance : dict[str, str]
        ``key -> value`` of the header lines (the first line's
        ``groundfield csv: <table>`` appears as key ``groundfield csv``);
        empty for a plain CSV.
    """
    p = Path(path)
    meta: dict[str, str] = {}
    n_comment = 0
    with p.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            if not line.startswith("#"):
                break
            n_comment += 1
            key, sep, value = line[1:].strip().partition(":")
            if sep:
                meta[key.strip()] = value.strip()
    return pd.read_csv(p, skiprows=n_comment), meta

def save_cluster_impedances_csv(
    result: "FieldResult",
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    frequency_index: int = 0,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    provenance: bool = True,
) -> Path:
    """Wrap :func:`cluster_current_balance` and write to CSV.

    Note that the ``members`` column of
    :func:`cluster_current_balance` carries Python lists; CSV is
    a flat format, so the lists are joined into ``';'``-separated
    strings before writing.

    Parameters
    ----------
    result
        Solver output.
    path
        Destination CSV path.
    frequency_index
        Index into :attr:`FieldResult.frequencies`. Default 0. The
        frequency is written to the ``frequency_hz`` column.
    overwrite
        Replace an existing file (default ``False``: raise).
    provenance
        Write the ``#`` provenance header (default ``True``).

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path

    Raises
    ------
    FileExistsError
        If ``path`` exists and ``overwrite`` is ``False``.

    Notes
    -----
    The ``Z`` columns are cluster impedances (a cluster's potential over
    its own soil leakage), not the input impedance a source sees.
    """
    from groundfield.postprocess.current_balance import cluster_current_balance

    out = _ensure_path(path, overwrite)
    df = cluster_current_balance(result, frequency_index=frequency_index)
    if "members" in df.columns:
        df = df.copy()
        df["members"] = df["members"].apply(lambda lst: ";".join(lst))
    f_hz = float(result.frequencies[frequency_index])
    df.insert(min(1, len(df.columns)), "frequency_hz", f_hz)
    header = None
    if provenance:
        header = _provenance_lines(
            result,
            "cluster_impedances",
            {"frequency_hz": _fmt_number(f_hz), "frequency_index": frequency_index},
        )
    return _write(df, out, header)

def save_potential_path_csv(
    result: "FieldResult",
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    start: tuple[float, float, float],
    direction: tuple[float, float, float] = (1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
    distance: float = 30.0,
    n: int = 200,
    frequency_indices: Sequence[int] | None = None,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    provenance: bool = True,
) -> Path:
    """Sample the potential along a line and write to CSV.

    Builds an evenly spaced set of ``n`` field points starting at
    ``start`` and walking ``distance`` metres along the unit
    vector of ``direction``, evaluates
    :meth:`FieldResult.potential` at every selected frequency
    index, and writes the result to ``path``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    result
        Solver output. Must carry ``point_sources`` (i.e. not a
        stub backend).
    path
        Destination CSV path. Parent directories are created
        automatically.
    start
        Path start point ``(x, y, z)`` in metres.
    direction
        Direction vector. Will be normalised to unit length.
        Default ``(1, 0, 0)``.
    distance
        Path length in metres. Default 30.
    n
        Number of sample points along the path. Default 200.
    frequency_indices
        Iterable of integer indices into
        :attr:`FieldResult.frequencies`. ``None`` (default)
        uses every available frequency.
    overwrite
        Replace an existing file (default ``False``: raise).
    provenance
        Write the ``#`` provenance header (default ``True``, see the
        module docstring).

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The path the file was written to.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``distance <= 0``, ``n < 2``, ``direction`` is the zero
        vector, or any ``frequency_indices`` value is out of range.
    FileExistsError
        If ``path`` exists and ``overwrite`` is ``False``.
    """
    if distance <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"distance must be > 0, got {distance!r}.")
    if n < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"n must be >= 2, got {n!r}.")
    direction_arr = np.asarray(direction, dtype=float)
    norm = float(np.linalg.norm(direction_arr))
    if norm == 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"direction must be non-zero, got {tuple(direction)}.")
    direction_arr = direction_arr / norm

    if frequency_indices is None:
        f_idx = list(range(len(result.frequencies)))
    else:
        f_idx = list(frequency_indices)
        for k in f_idx:
            if not (0 <= k < len(result.frequencies)):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"frequency index {k} out of range [0, {len(result.frequencies)})."
                )

    out = _ensure_path(path, overwrite)
    s = np.linspace(0.0, float(distance), int(n))
    pts = np.column_stack(
        [
            start[0] + s * direction_arr[0],
            start[1] + s * direction_arr[1],
            start[2] + s * direction_arr[2],
        ]
    )

    rows = []
    for k in f_idx:
        f_hz = float(result.frequencies[k])
        phi = result.potential(pts, frequency_index=k)
        for i in range(len(s)):
            rows.append(
                {
                    "s": float(s[i]),
                    "x": float(pts[i, 0]),
                    "y": float(pts[i, 1]),
                    "z": float(pts[i, 2]),
                    "frequency_Hz": f_hz,
                    "phi_re": float(phi[i].real),
                    "phi_im": float(phi[i].imag),
                    "abs_phi": float(abs(phi[i])),
                }
            )

    header = None
    if provenance:
        header = _provenance_lines(
            result,
            "potential_path",
            {
                "frequencies_hz": ", ".join(
                    _fmt_number(result.frequencies[k]) for k in f_idx
                ),
                "frequency_indices": ", ".join(str(k) for k in f_idx),
            },
        )
    return _write(pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=list(POTENTIAL_PATH_COLUMNS)), out, header)

docs.title: vtk
docs.text:
Legacy ASCII VTK exports for ParaView / VisIt / Mayavi.

This module writes two flavours of the legacy ASCII VTK file format (.vtk), keeping the dependency surface zero — no pyvista or vtk Python bindings are required:

  • export_geometry_vtk() — POLYDATA with the electrode wires (rod, ring, strip, mesh, grid_mesh) and the conductor line segments. Useful for "drag the world into ParaView and rotate it" inspections of large typical networks.
  • export_field_vtk() — STRUCTURED_POINTS with the soil surface (or any horizontal slice) sampled on a regular (N_x, N_y) grid. The potential is exported as a single scalar field; ParaView's contour / colour-map filters take it from there.
Why legacy ASCII VTK?

The legacy format is the smallest common denominator: every VTK reader since the 90s opens it, the on-disk layout is plain text (diff-able, version-controllable), and the writer is ~30 lines of pure-Python without any external library. For large research runs prefer pyvista once you need binary I/O and unstructured grids; for production-grade networks at notebook scale this format is fast enough.

Format details (review pass 10, 10.10)
  • Coordinates and scalars are declared double: float makes readers store 32-bit values, which quantises UTM-scale coordinates (northings of 5.2e6–6.2e6 m) by up to 0.25 m.
  • The free-text header line is sanitised: control and line-separator characters in world.name become spaces, and the line is limited to 256 bytes as the legacy format requires. A newline in the name used to corrupt the file.
  • groundfield measures \(z\) downwards (depth below the soil surface). ParaView shows the world upside down; apply a Transform filter with scale (1, 1, -1) for a conventional view.
References
  • Schroeder, W., Martin, K., Lorensen, B. (2006). The Visualization Toolkit, 4th ed., Kitware. Section 19.5 (Legacy file format).
  • VTK File Formats reference: https://vtk.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/file-formats.pdf

def export_field_vtk(
    result: "FieldResult",
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    extent: tuple[float, float, float, float],
    z: float = 0.0,
    n: tuple[int, int] = (120, 120),
    frequency_index: int = 0,
) -> Path:
    """Sample the potential on a horizontal grid and write a VTK file.

    Evaluates :meth:`FieldResult.potential` on a regular
    :math:`N_x \\times N_y` grid in the plane :math:`z = z_0` and
    writes a ``DATASET STRUCTURED_POINTS`` (a.k.a. uniform grid)
    with a single scalar field ``potential_re``. The imaginary
    part is included as a second scalar ``potential_im`` for
    above-DC typical studies.

    Parameters
    ----------
    result
        Solver output. Must carry ``point_sources`` (not a stub).
    path
        Destination ``.vtk`` path.
    extent
        Plot extent ``(x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max)`` in metres.
    z
        Slice depth in metres (default ``0.0`` — soil surface).
        Positive ``z`` is below ground.
    n
        Grid resolution ``(n_x, n_y)``. Default ``(120, 120)``.
    frequency_index
        Index into :attr:`FieldResult.frequencies`. Default 0.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        On bad extent or non-positive grid sizes.
    """
    x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max = extent
    if x_max <= x_min or y_max <= y_min:
        raise ValueError(
            f"extent must satisfy x_max > x_min and y_max > y_min, got {extent!r}."
        )
    n_x, n_y = n
    if n_x < 2 or n_y < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"n must be >= (2, 2), got {n!r}.")

    xs = np.linspace(float(x_min), float(x_max), int(n_x))
    ys = np.linspace(float(y_min), float(y_max), int(n_y))
    X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys, indexing="xy")
    pts = np.column_stack([X.ravel(), Y.ravel(), np.full(X.size, float(z))])
    phi = result.potential(pts, frequency_index=frequency_index)
    phi = phi.reshape(X.shape)

    dx = (x_max - x_min) / (n_x - 1)
    dy = (y_max - y_min) / (n_y - 1)

    out = _ensure_path(path)
    buf = StringIO()
    buf.write("# vtk DataFile Version 3.0\n")
    buf.write(
        _header_line(
            f"groundfield potential @ z={z} m, "
            f"f={result.frequencies[frequency_index]} Hz"
        )
        + "\n"
    )
    buf.write("ASCII\n")
    buf.write("DATASET STRUCTURED_POINTS\n")
    buf.write(f"DIMENSIONS {n_x} {n_y} 1\n")
    buf.write(f"ORIGIN {x_min:.17g} {y_min:.17g} {z:.17g}\n")
    buf.write(f"SPACING {dx:.17g} {dy:.17g} 1\n")

    n_pts = n_x * n_y
    buf.write(f"POINT_DATA {n_pts}\n")
    buf.write("SCALARS potential_re double 1\n")
    buf.write("LOOKUP_TABLE default\n")
    # The order in STRUCTURED_POINTS is x fastest, then y, then z.
    # numpy meshgrid with indexing='xy' gives Y[i, j], X[i, j];
    # ravel() with C-order then walks j (x) before i (y) — exactly
    # what VTK expects.
    for v in phi.real.ravel():
        buf.write(f"{float(v):.17g}\n")

    buf.write("SCALARS potential_im double 1\n")
    buf.write("LOOKUP_TABLE default\n")
    for v in phi.imag.ravel():
        buf.write(f"{float(v):.17g}\n")

    out.write_text(buf.getvalue(), encoding="utf-8")
    return out
