def export_geometry_vtk(world: "World", path: str | Path) -> Path:
    """Export the world geometry as a legacy ASCII VTK PolyData file.

    Writes electrodes (rods, rings, strips, mesh / grid_mesh
    perimeters) **and** conductors as 3-D polylines. The on-disk
    layout uses VTK's ``DATASET POLYDATA`` with a ``LINES`` block;
    cell data carries an integer ``role`` field (0 = electrode,
    1 = conductor) so colour-by-role works directly in ParaView.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        World to export. May be empty (the writer still produces
        a syntactically valid header-only file). Its ``name`` goes into
        the (sanitised) header line.
    path
        Destination ``.vtk`` path. Parent directories are created
        automatically.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The path the file was written to.

    Notes
    -----
    POINTS are written as ``double``; :math:`z` is the depth below the
    surface (positive downwards), see the module docstring.
    """
    polylines: list[np.ndarray] = []
    roles: list[int] = []

    for e in world.electrodes:
        for poly in _polylines_for_electrode(e):
            polylines.append(poly)
            roles.append(0)

    for c in world.conductors:
        seg = np.array([list(c.start), list(c.end)], dtype=float)
        polylines.append(seg)
        roles.append(1)

    out = _ensure_path(path)
    buf = StringIO()
    buf.write("# vtk DataFile Version 3.0\n")
    buf.write(_header_line(f"groundfield geometry: {world.name}") + "\n")
    buf.write("ASCII\n")
    buf.write("DATASET POLYDATA\n")

    if not polylines:
        buf.write("POINTS 0 double\n")
        out.write_text(buf.getvalue(), encoding="utf-8")
        return out

    n_points = sum(p.shape[0] for p in polylines)
    n_lines = len(polylines)
    n_line_data = n_lines + n_points  # one count + entries per line

    buf.write(f"POINTS {n_points} double\n")
    for poly in polylines:
        for x, y, z in poly:
            buf.write(f"{x:.17g} {y:.17g} {z:.17g}\n")

    buf.write(f"LINES {n_lines} {n_line_data}\n")
    offset = 0
    for poly in polylines:
        n = poly.shape[0]
        idx_list = " ".join(str(offset + k) for k in range(n))
        buf.write(f"{n} {idx_list}\n")
        offset += n

    # Cell data: role per polyline (0 = electrode, 1 = conductor).
    buf.write(f"CELL_DATA {n_lines}\n")
    buf.write("SCALARS role int 1\n")
    buf.write("LOOKUP_TABLE default\n")
    for r in roles:
        buf.write(f"{r}\n")

    out.write_text(buf.getvalue(), encoding="utf-8")
    return out

docs.title: Postprocess
docs.text: The postprocess package turns a FieldResult into engineering quantities: potentials and their plots, touch and step voltages with the EN 50522 limits, the current sharing between electrodes and conductors, parameter sweeps and convergence studies, and the reduced rho-f models that are exported to groundinsight. Every function is available at the top level (gf.touch_voltage) and in the namespaces gf.plot, gf.safety and gf.fit.

docs.title: Mathematical and physical context
docs.text:
Potentials. After the solve the leakage currents \(I_k\) of the segments are known, and the potential anywhere in or on the soil is the superposition \(\varphi(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_k G(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{r}_k)\,I_k\) with the Green's function of the soil (homogeneous or two-layer).

Touch and step voltage (EN 50522:2022, IEC 61936-1). A person touches an accessible conductive part at the potential \(U_\text{part}\) of the earthing system it is bonded to and stands on the surface 1 m away from it (EN 50522's conventional position):

\[ U_T = U_\text{part} - \varphi(\mathbf{r}_\text{feet}), \qquad U_S = \varphi(\mathbf{r}_1) - \varphi(\mathbf{r}_1 + d_\text{step}\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}). \]

touch_voltage_at_part evaluates \(U_T\) at a touch point, an accessible metal part above ground (a station housing or door, a mast, a fence post, a service connection box): the feet stand on the circle of radius \(d\) (default 1 m) around the part, optionally only in given directions or outside the outlines where nobody can stand, and \(U_\text{part}\) is the potential of the electrode or junction the part is bonded to — a PEN junction at a house gives the transferred potential. Where the parts are not known, touch_voltage and touch_voltage_envelope take the electrode itself as the touched part, \(U_\text{part} = U_E = \varphi_\text{cluster}\), with the feet at distance \(d\) from its footprint, the horizontal projection of its wires; the envelope walks all around it. It samples nothing inside the footprint by default (there stands the station, the house, the steel structure or the mast); for open-air grids such as a substation yard, interior="meshes" adds the centres of the meshes (the analogue of the IEEE 80 mesh voltage) and of a ring, interior=True also the inside of closed polylines. permissible_touch_voltage_en50522(t_f) follows Figure 8 / Table B.4 of EN 50522:2022 up to 10 s and returns 80 V for every \(t_f > 10\) s, including an uncleared fault (math.inf), the value the standard allows for current-flow durations considerably longer than 10 s; permissible_prospective_touch_voltage_en50522 adds the body and footwear resistances of Annex B.4. For a fault current with harmonics, touch_voltage_spectrum returns the true-RMS value \(U_{T,\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\sum_k \lvert U_{T,k}\rvert^2}\) over the frequencies of the spectrum.

Current sharing. cluster_current_balance and electrode_current_table list the current every cluster and electrode leaks into the soil; split_factor is the share of a source current that leaves through the soil at the feeding cluster (the rest flows away through conductors). The inductive reduction factor of cable screens is not computed here.

Reduced models. The quantity a reduced model describes is selected with quantity= ("input", the default, "cluster" or "electrode", see the quickstart). Two families:

  • vector fitting (Gustavsen and Semlyen 1999) of a rational function in \(s = j\omega\) at a fixed soil, \(Z(s) \approx R_\infty + sL_\infty + \sum_k r_k/(s - p_k)\), with a passivity check (\(\operatorname{Re}Z \ge 0\)) before export;
  • the standard form fitted over a \(\rho\) and \(f\) sweep (for layered soil \(\rho\) is the effective resistivity of each solved soil, see Soil),

$$ Z(\rho, f) = k_0 + k_1\rho + (k_2 + jk_3)\,f + (k_4 + jk_5)\,f\rho , $$

with relative weights by default; max_relative is the quality figure to check (a fit above 5 % warns with RhoFStandardQualityWarning).

Validity. Quasi-static range \(f < 1\,\mathrm{kHz}\). The image family assumes a uniform current per unit length on each straight wire of an electrode (user decision Q30): near grids, meshes, stars, strip ends and bonded multi-electrode clusters its surface potentials are impedance-grade, not field-grade, and the safety helpers warn with UniformCurrentFieldWarning (re-solve with backend="mom" for field-grade values). FieldResult.potential and everything built on it support homogeneous and two-layer soil only.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A ring earth carrying a fault current of 100 A at 50 Hz, the touch voltage 1 m outside its footprint, checked against a second backend and against the EN 50522 limit for a fault cleared in 0.5 s:

import groundfield as gf

world = gf.create_world(soil=gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=100.0, rho_2=300.0, h_1=2.0))
gf.create_electrode(world, "ring", name="g1", center=(0.0, 0.0, 0.8), radius=3.0)
gf.create_source(world, attached_to="g1", magnitude=100.0)
result = gf.create_engine(frequencies=[50.0]).solve(world)

U_E = result.electrode_potentials["g1"][0]                       # 1381 V
U_T = gf.touch_voltage(result, world, electrode="g1", distance=1.0)   # 525 V
U_S = gf.step_voltage(result, position=(3.0, 0.0, 0.0), direction=(1.0, 0.0, 0.0), world=world)
U_Tp = gf.permissible_touch_voltage_en50522(0.5)                  # 225 V (Table B.4)

mom = gf.create_engine(backend="mom", frequencies=[50.0]).solve(world)
U_T_mom = gf.touch_voltage(mom, world, electrode="g1", distance=1.0)  # 517 V

assert abs(U_E - 1380.9) < 0.5 and abs(U_T - 525.3) < 0.5
assert abs(U_T - U_T_mom) / abs(U_T) < 0.02     # ring: both current ansätze agree
assert U_Tp == 225.0 and abs(U_T) > U_Tp        # this earth needs a closer look
assert 0 < U_S.real < U_T.real

The how-to guide Assess touch voltages and tutorial T08 show the complete assessment (touch points, transferred potential, envelope, prospective touch voltage, spectrum); tutorial T04 the frequency response and the rho-f fits.

docs.title: safety
docs.text:
Touch and step voltages for grounding-system safety assessment.

This module turns a groundfield.solver.result.FieldResult into the engineering quantities used in the grounding-system safety verification according to EN 50522:2022 (DIN EN 50522 (VDE 0101-2): 2023-10) / IEC 61936-1: the touch voltage \(U_T\) and the step voltage \(U_S\). It also provides the permissible values \(U_{Tp}(t_f)\) of EN 50522:2022, Table B.4 (the curve of Figure 8), the permissible prospective (open-circuit) touch voltage \(U_{vTp}\) of Annex B.4, and the true-RMS touch voltage over a fault-current spectrum.

Mathematical / physical content

A grounding cluster at earth potential rise

\[ U_E \;=\; \varphi_\text{cluster}, \]

is connected — through any galvanically bonded metallic part — to whatever a person can touch. Standing on the soil surface 1 m away from the touched part (the conventional position of EN 50522), the person's feet sit at the surface potential \(\varphi(\mathbf{r}_\text{feet})\). The prospective touch voltage is

\[ U_T \;=\; U_E \;-\; \varphi(\mathbf{r}_\text{feet}). \]

The touched parts are the accessible metal parts above ground: a station housing or its door, a mast, a fence, a service connection box. touch_voltage_at_part() takes such a part as a touch point — its horizontal position and the electrode or junction it is bonded to — and puts the feet on the circle of radius distance around it, optionally only in given directions or outside the outlines where nobody can stand (the housing or building itself). A part bonded to a node far from the faulted earth, for example to a PEN junction at a house, carries a transferred potential.

Where the parts are not known, touch_voltage() and touch_voltage_envelope() use the electrode itself: since review pass 10 (10.21) the metre is measured from its footprint — the horizontal projection of its wires — not from its connection point; the feet stand distance metres from the nearest wire, on the side given by direction (seen from the length-weighted centroid of the wires). The envelope does not sample the inside of the footprint by default, because there stands the station, the house, the steel structure or the mast. Over an open-air grid such as a substation yard people do walk inside the loops, where the surface potential sags: interior="meshes" adds the mesh centres of grids and the centre of a ring, the analogue of the IEEE Std 80 mesh voltage, and interior=True also the inside of a closed polyline.

For a step voltage the body bridges two surface points at the typical step distance \(d_\text{step} = 1\,\mathrm{m}\):

\[ U_S \;=\; \varphi(\mathbf{r}_1) \;-\; \varphi(\mathbf{r}_1 + d_\text{step}\,\hat{\mathbf e}). \]

Both quantities are returned as complex phasors per frequency index — consistent with the rest of groundfield — so that inductive- and resistive-coupling effects above DC remain visible.

Validity envelope
  • Frequency: quasi-static envelope \(f \le 1\,\mathrm{kHz}\), inherited from the underlying Green's function.
  • Current ansatz: the image family (image, image_2layer, image_nlayer, cim) solves one uniform current per straight wire of an electrode (a wire line of a grid, an arm of a star, a straight run of a polyline, user decision Q30 of 2026.11; a rod, a strip or a ring is one wire). Impedances are fine, but near grids, meshes, stars, strip ends and bonded multi-electrode clusters the surface potential is impedance-grade, not field-grade. Measured against the per-segment mom backend (homogeneous 100 Ω·m, segment_length 0.5 m) with the default line kernel, touch voltage with the feet 1 m outside the footprint and step voltage from 1 m to 2 m outside it: 20 m × 20 m grid with 4 × 4 meshes at the corner, touch +6 %, step −8 % (non-conservative; the step from the point above the corner 1 m outwards is −11 %; one current per grid, up to then, gave +20 % / −21 % / −28 %); 4-arm star (5 m arms) beyond a tip touch +8 %, step −9 %; 10 m strip beyond its end step −6 %; single rings, rods and closed rectangular loops within 2 %. A bonded cluster of a foundation mesh and a bare ring 1 m outside it reads +5 … +16 % with the feet right above the ring (example E02; the warning below fires for it, use mom). The point kernel, which mom shares, isolates the ansatz: grid +5 % / −8 % (−11 % from above the corner), star +7 % / −10 %, strip −7 %, rings, rods and loops within 1 %. The helpers emit UniformCurrentFieldWarning once per call when a uniform-current result is evaluated within NEAR_FIELD_DISTANCE_M of such an electrode; re-solve with backend="mom" for field-grade values.
  • Coordinate convention: the soil surface is at \(z = 0\), positive \(z\) points downwards into the soil (see groundfield.geometry.electrodes). The default surface_z = 0.0 therefore models bare-foot contact at the ground surface.
  • permissible_touch_voltage_en50522() interpolates EN 50522:2022, Table B.4 (the curve of Figure 8) for fault durations \(50\,\mathrm{ms} \le t_f \le 10\,\mathrm{s}\), clamps to 725 V below 50 ms and returns 80 V for every \(t_f > 10\,\mathrm{s}\) including an uncleared fault (the value the standard allows for current-flow durations considerably longer than 10 s).
References
  • EN 50522:2022 — Earthing of power installations exceeding 1 kV a.c., Annex B (Table B.1 body current, Table B.4 permissible touch voltage, B.4 prospective touch voltage). German edition DIN EN 50522 (VDE 0101-2):2023-10.
  • IEC 60479-1:2018 — Effects of current on human beings and livestock (curve c2, body impedance).
  • IEC 61936-1:2021 — Power installations exceeding 1 kV a.c.
  • IEEE Std 80-2013 — Guide for safety in AC substation grounding.

docs.title: NEAR_FIELD_DISTANCE_M module-attribute
docs.text:
NEAR_FIELD_DISTANCE_M: float = 5.0

Distance in m within which the safety helpers warn about uniform currents.

Horizontal distance from a crowding electrode within which the safety helpers warn about uniform-current results (10.22). At 5 m from the footprint the measured touch / step deviations of the uniform ansatz against mom are at most 4 % for strips, bonded clusters and grids (2.5 % for a 20 m grid with 4 × 4 meshes since user decision Q30, 8 % with one current per grid before) and 6.5 % for a 4-arm star (default line kernel; with the point kernel 5 % for the star).

docs.title: UniformCurrentFieldWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Field quantity from a uniform-current backend near a crowding geometry.

The image family assigns one uniform current density to every straight wire of an electrode (user decision Q30 of 2026.11). Near grids, meshes, stars, strip ends and bonded multi-electrode clusters the true current crowds to edges, corners and tips, so touch and step voltages computed there are impedance-grade (review pass 10, 10.22; see the module docstring for measured deviations). Re-solve with backend="mom" for field-grade values, or silence the category with warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UniformCurrentFieldWarning).

docs.title: permissible_prospective_touch_voltage_en50522
docs.text:
permissible_prospective_touch_voltage_en50522(t_f: float, *, R_H: float = 0.0, R_F1: float = 0.0, rho_s: float | None = None, HF: float = 1.0) -> float

Permissible prospective touch voltage \(U_{vTp}\) (EN 50522:2022, B.4).

The prospective (open-circuit) touch voltage may exceed the permissible touch voltage across the body by the drop of the body current over the additional resistances (equivalent circuit of Figure B.2, Equation (A.3) of the standard):

\[ U_{vTp}(t_f) \;=\; U_{Tp}(t_f) \;+\; \frac{I_B(t_f)}{HF}\,R_A, \qquad R_A = R_H + R_{F1} + R_{F2}, \qquad R_{F2} = 1.5\,\mathrm{m}^{-1}\cdot\rho_s, \]

with \(U_{Tp}\) from permissible_touch_voltage_en50522() (Table B.4 up to 10 s, 80 V beyond) and the permissible body current \(I_B(t_f)\) of Table B.1 (0.05 s: 900 mA, 0.1 s: 800 mA, 0.2 s: 600 mA, 0.5 s: 200 mA, 1 s: 80 mA, 2 s: 60 mA, 5 s: 51 mA, 10 s: 50 mA; interpolated log-log, 900 mA below 50 ms, and held at 50 mA beyond 10 s).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default t_f float

Fault duration in s, > 0; math.inf for an earth fault that is not cleared.

required R_H float

Hand resistance (e.g. gloves) in Ω, >= 0.

0.0 R_F1 float

Resistance of the footwear in Ω, >= 0 (EN 50522 quotes 1000 Ω as an average for worn, damp shoes).

0.0 rho_s float | None

Resistivity of the surface layer at the standing position in Ω·m; None (default) omits the standing-position resistance \(R_{F2}\).

None HF float

Heart-current factor of the current path, > 0; 1 for left hand to feet, the path the standard uses here.

1.0

Returns:

Type Description float

Permissible prospective touch voltage \(U_{vTp}\) in V.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If a resistance or rho_s is negative or not finite, HF is not positive, or t_f is invalid (see permissible_touch_voltage_en50522()).

Examples:

Figure B.3 of the standard, 0.5 s, no footwear, 500 Ω·m gravel (\(R_F = 750\,\Omega\)): 225 V + 0.2 A · 750 Ω = 375 V.

>>> permissible_prospective_touch_voltage_en50522(0.5, rho_s=500.0)
375.0

An earth fault that is not cleared, 1000 Ω shoes: 80 V + 0.05 A · 1000 Ω = 130 V.

>>> permissible_prospective_touch_voltage_en50522(math.inf, R_F1=1000.0)
130.0
Source code in src/groundfield/postprocess/safety.py 
def permissible_prospective_touch_voltage_en50522(
    t_f: float,
    *,
    R_H: float = 0.0,
    R_F1: float = 0.0,
    rho_s: float | None = None,
    HF: float = 1.0,
) -> float:
    """Permissible prospective touch voltage :math:`U_{vTp}` (EN 50522:2022, B.4).

    The prospective (open-circuit) touch voltage may exceed the
    permissible touch voltage across the body by the drop of the body
    current over the additional resistances (equivalent circuit of
    Figure B.2, Equation (A.3) of the standard):

    .. math::

        U_{vTp}(t_f) \\;=\\; U_{Tp}(t_f) \\;+\\;
        \\frac{I_B(t_f)}{HF}\\,R_A,
        \\qquad
        R_A = R_H + R_{F1} + R_{F2},
        \\qquad
        R_{F2} = 1.5\\,\\mathrm{m}^{-1}\\cdot\\rho_s,

    with :math:`U_{Tp}` from :func:`permissible_touch_voltage_en50522`
    (Table B.4 up to 10 s, 80 V beyond) and the permissible body current
    :math:`I_B(t_f)` of Table B.1 (0.05 s: 900 mA, 0.1 s: 800 mA,
    0.2 s: 600 mA, 0.5 s: 200 mA, 1 s: 80 mA, 2 s: 60 mA, 5 s: 51 mA,
    10 s: 50 mA; interpolated log-log, 900 mA below 50 ms, and held at
    50 mA beyond 10 s).

    Parameters
    ----------
    t_f
        Fault duration in s, ``> 0``; ``math.inf`` for an earth fault
        that is not cleared.
    R_H
        Hand resistance (e.g. gloves) in Ω, ``>= 0``.
    R_F1
        Resistance of the footwear in Ω, ``>= 0`` (EN 50522 quotes
        1000 Ω as an average for worn, damp shoes).
    rho_s
        Resistivity of the surface layer at the standing position in
        Ω·m; ``None`` (default) omits the standing-position resistance
        :math:`R_{F2}`.
    HF
        Heart-current factor of the current path, ``> 0``; 1 for left
        hand to feet, the path the standard uses here.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Permissible prospective touch voltage :math:`U_{vTp}` in V.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a resistance or ``rho_s`` is negative or not finite, ``HF`` is
        not positive, or ``t_f`` is invalid (see
        :func:`permissible_touch_voltage_en50522`).

    Examples
    --------
    Figure B.3 of the standard, 0.5 s, no footwear, 500 Ω·m gravel
    (:math:`R_F = 750\\,\\Omega`): 225 V + 0.2 A · 750 Ω = 375 V.

    >>> permissible_prospective_touch_voltage_en50522(0.5, rho_s=500.0)
    375.0

    An earth fault that is not cleared, 1000 Ω shoes:
    80 V + 0.05 A · 1000 Ω = 130 V.

    >>> permissible_prospective_touch_voltage_en50522(math.inf, R_F1=1000.0)
    130.0
    """
    for name, value in (("R_H", R_H), ("R_F1", R_F1)):
        if not math.isfinite(value) or value < 0.0:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite and >= 0 Ohm, got {value!r}.")
    if rho_s is not None and (not math.isfinite(rho_s) or rho_s < 0.0):
        raise ValueError(f"rho_s must be finite and >= 0 Ohm m, got {rho_s!r}.")
    if not math.isfinite(HF) or HF <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"HF must be finite and > 0, got {HF!r}.")
    u_tp = permissible_touch_voltage_en50522(t_f)
    i_b = _loglog(
        min(float(t_f), _EN50522_CURVE_END_S), _EN50522_IB_GRID, exact_anchors=True
    )
    r_a = R_H + R_F1 + (0.0 if rho_s is None else 1.5 * float(rho_s))
    return u_tp + i_b / HF * r_a

docs.title: permissible_touch_voltage_en50522
docs.text:
permissible_touch_voltage_en50522(t_clear_s: float) -> float

Permissible touch voltage \(U_{Tp}(t_f)\) per EN 50522:2022.

Returns the maximum admissible touch voltage as a function of the fault duration \(t_f\). Up to 10 s it follows the curve of Figure 8 in its tabulated form, Table B.4 (DIN EN 50522 (VDE 0101-2):2023-10),

\[ \{(t_k, U_{Tp,k})\} \;=\; \{(0.05, 725),\ (0.10, 655),\ (0.20, 525),\ (0.50, 225),\ (1.00, 115),\ (2.00, 95),\ (5.00, 85),\ (10.0, 85)\}, \]

in s and V (rounded to 5 V in the standard), interpolated linearly in \(\log t\)–\(\log U\) between the anchors and clamped to 725 V below 50 ms. Beyond the end of the curve,

\[ U_{Tp}(t_f) \;=\; 80\,\mathrm{V} \qquad \text{for } t_f > 10\,\mathrm{s}, \]

including an earth fault that is not cleared (math.inf).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default t_clear_s float

Fault duration \(t_f\) in s, > 0; math.inf for an earth fault that is not cleared.

required

Returns:

Type Description float

Permissible touch voltage \(U_{Tp}\) in V.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If t_clear_s is NaN or not strictly positive.

Notes

Where the values come from in EN 50522:2022:

  • 5.4.1, Figure 8: \(U_{Tp}\) as a function of the fault duration; Annex B, B.3, Table B.4: the values of that curve from 0.05 s to 10 s. The curve is not defined beyond 10 s.
  • The note to Figure 8 (5.4.1) and the paragraph after Table B.4 (B.3): for a current-flow duration considerably longer than 10 s, 80 V may be used as the permissible touch voltage.
  • 5.4.1 assumes that every earth fault is cleared, automatically or by hand, so that no touch voltage of very long or unlimited duration occurs. A resonant-earthed network can carry its earth fault for hours, which is where the 80 V value matters.

The helper uses 80 V for every \(t_f > 10\,\mathrm{s}\) instead of continuing the 85 V end value of Table B.4: 80 V is below 85 V, on the safe side where the curve gives no value. Hence the step from 85 V at 10 s to 80 V just above. Up to the 2026.11 development snapshots an opt-in keyword selected the 80 V and the default returned 85 V; v0.15.0 returned 85 V and rejected math.inf.

Review pass 10 (10.42) checked the anchors against the standard text: they are the published values. A secondary reproduction quoted in the review (716 / 654 / 537 / 220 / 117 / 96 / 86 / 85 V) does not match EN 50522:2022. Compare the value with touch_voltage(), touch_voltage_at_part() or touch_voltage_envelope() (or, with additional resistances, use permissible_prospective_touch_voltage_en50522()).

Source code in src/groundfield/postprocess/safety.py 
def permissible_touch_voltage_en50522(t_clear_s: float) -> float:
    """Permissible touch voltage :math:`U_{Tp}(t_f)` per EN 50522:2022.

    Returns the maximum admissible touch voltage as a function of the
    fault duration :math:`t_f`. Up to 10 s it follows the curve of
    Figure 8 in its tabulated form, Table B.4 (DIN EN 50522
    (VDE 0101-2):2023-10),

    .. math::

        \\{(t_k, U_{Tp,k})\\} \\;=\\;
        \\{(0.05, 725),\\ (0.10, 655),\\ (0.20, 525),\\
        (0.50, 225),\\ (1.00, 115),\\ (2.00, 95),\\
        (5.00, 85),\\ (10.0, 85)\\},

    in s and V (rounded to 5 V in the standard), interpolated linearly in
    :math:`\\log t`–:math:`\\log U` between the anchors and clamped to
    725 V below 50 ms. Beyond the end of the curve,

    .. math::

        U_{Tp}(t_f) \\;=\\; 80\\,\\mathrm{V}
        \\qquad \\text{for } t_f > 10\\,\\mathrm{s},

    including an earth fault that is not cleared (``math.inf``).

    Parameters
    ----------
    t_clear_s
        Fault duration :math:`t_f` in s, ``> 0``; ``math.inf`` for an
        earth fault that is not cleared.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Permissible touch voltage :math:`U_{Tp}` in V.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``t_clear_s`` is NaN or not strictly positive.

    Notes
    -----
    Where the values come from in EN 50522:2022:

    * 5.4.1, Figure 8: :math:`U_{Tp}` as a function of the fault
      duration; Annex B, B.3, Table B.4: the values of that curve from
      0.05 s to 10 s. The curve is not defined beyond 10 s.
    * The note to Figure 8 (5.4.1) and the paragraph after Table B.4
      (B.3): for a current-flow duration considerably longer than 10 s,
      80 V may be used as the permissible touch voltage.
    * 5.4.1 assumes that every earth fault is cleared, automatically or
      by hand, so that no touch voltage of very long or unlimited
      duration occurs. A resonant-earthed network can carry its earth
      fault for hours, which is where the 80 V value matters.

    The helper uses 80 V for every :math:`t_f > 10\\,\\mathrm{s}` instead
    of continuing the 85 V end value of Table B.4: 80 V is below 85 V,
    on the safe side where the curve gives no value. Hence the step from
    85 V at 10 s to 80 V just above. Up to the 2026.11 development
    snapshots an opt-in keyword selected the 80 V and the default
    returned 85 V; v0.15.0 returned 85 V and rejected ``math.inf``.

    Review pass 10 (10.42) checked the anchors against the standard
    text: they are the published values. A secondary reproduction quoted
    in the review (716 / 654 / 537 / 220 / 117 / 96 / 86 / 85 V) does not
    match EN 50522:2022. Compare the value with :func:`touch_voltage`,
    :func:`touch_voltage_at_part` or :func:`touch_voltage_envelope`
    (or, with additional resistances, use
    :func:`permissible_prospective_touch_voltage_en50522`).
    """
    # math.isnan rejects text (TypeError) before float() could parse it.
    if math.isnan(t_clear_s) or t_clear_s <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"t_clear_s must be > 0 (s), got {t_clear_s!r}.")
    t = float(t_clear_s)
    # user decision Q4: 80 V beyond the end of Figure 8 / Table B.4.
    if t > _EN50522_CURVE_END_S:
        return _EN50522_TP_LONG_DURATION
    return _loglog(t, _EN50522_TP_GRID)

def step_voltage(
    result: "FieldResult",
    *,
    position: tuple[float, float, float],
    direction: tuple[float, float, float] = (1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
    step: float = 1.0,
    surface_z: float | None = None,
    frequency_index: int = 0,
    world: "World | None" = None,
) -> complex:
    """Step voltage between two surface points.

    Evaluates :math:`U_S = \\varphi(\\mathbf{r}_1) -
    \\varphi(\\mathbf{r}_1 + d_\\text{step}\\,\\hat{\\mathbf{e}})`
    on the soil surface.

    Parameters
    ----------
    result
        Solver output.
    position
        First foot position :math:`(x, y, z)` in m. The :math:`z`
        coordinate is overridden by ``surface_z`` if the latter is
        given; the default keeps ``z`` as supplied so callers can use
        the helper for buried-step studies if desired.
    direction
        Step direction in world coordinates. The horizontal
        projection is used (the :math:`z` component is ignored —
        both feet stay on the same surface).
    step
        Step length :math:`d_\\text{step}` in m. EN 50522 uses ``1.0``.
    surface_z
        Optional explicit surface :math:`z` in m. ``None`` keeps the
        :math:`z` of ``position`` (typical for bare-foot contact
        at the ground surface, ``position = (x, y, 0.0)``).
    frequency_index
        Index into :attr:`FieldResult.frequencies`.
    world
        Optional companion world. Only used to decide whether to emit
        :class:`UniformCurrentFieldWarning`: with the world the warning
        is restricted to the electrode shapes with measured ansatz
        errors; without it any wire within
        :data:`NEAR_FIELD_DISTANCE_M` of a uniform-current result
        triggers it.

    Returns
    -------
    complex
        Phasor :math:`U_S(f)` in V.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``step`` is not strictly positive or ``direction`` has
        no horizontal component.

    Warns
    -----
    UniformCurrentFieldWarning
        Once per call, see the module docstring. At the corner of a
        20 m × 20 m grid the uniform-current ansatz under-estimates the
        step voltage by 21 % (feet 1 m and 2 m outside the corner) to 28 %
        (feet above the corner and 1 m outside), with either kernel.
    """
    if not math.isfinite(step) or step <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"step must be > 0, got {step!r}.")

    e_h = _horizontal(direction)
    z0 = float(position[2]) if surface_z is None else float(surface_z)
    p1 = np.array([float(position[0]), float(position[1]), z0])
    p2 = p1 + step * e_h
    pts = np.stack([p1, p2])
    _uniform_current_caveat(result, world, pts, caller="step_voltage")

    phi = result.potential(pts, frequency_index=frequency_index)
    return complex(phi[0] - phi[1])

touch_voltage(result: 'FieldResult', world: 'World', *, electrode: str, distance: float = 1.0, direction: tuple[float, float, float] = (1.0, 0.0, 0.0), surface_z: float = 0.0, frequency_index: int = 0, anchor: Anchor = 'footprint') -> complex

Touch voltage at a single point on the soil surface.

Evaluates \(U_T = U_E - \varphi(\mathbf{r}_\text{feet})\), where \(U_E\) is the cluster potential of the touched electrode. With the default anchor="footprint" the feet stand distance metres (horizontally) from the nearest wire of the electrode, on the ray that leaves the electrode's footprint in the horizontal projection of direction: 1 m outside the edge of a grid, 1 m beyond the tip of a star arm, 1 m outside a ring on either side. This is a proxy for an unknown touched part; for a known accessible metal part use touch_voltage_at_part().

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default result 'FieldResult'

Solver output from Engine.solve().

required world 'World'

Companion world used to resolve the electrode geometry.

required electrode str

Name of the touched electrode. Its cluster potential is the EPR seen by the hand.

required distance float

Horizontal distance between the touched part and the feet, in m. EN 50522 uses 1.0.

1.0 direction tuple[float, float, float]

Side of the electrode on which the person stands, in world coordinates, seen from the length-weighted centroid of the wires. Only the horizontal projection is used (the feet stay on the surface). Defaults to +x.

(1.0, 0.0, 0.0) surface_z float

\(z\) coordinate of the soil surface in m. Default 0.0 (groundfield convention; positive z is below ground).

0.0 frequency_index int

Index into FieldResult.frequencies. Default 0.

0 anchor Anchor

"footprint" (default since review pass 10, 10.21) measures distance from the nearest wire; "connection_point" measures it from connection_point of electrode, the rule of v0.15.0. For a hand-built grid mesh or star that is its centre, as in v0.15.0. A rectangular foundation of the generators is since 2026.11 several bonded wires — one per mesh line (audit A2G-04), one per side without cross-braces (user decision Q38) — and the electrode named after it is its local \(-y\) side, whose connection point is a corner of the rectangle (in 0.15.0 one grid mesh connected at its centre): the feet then stand around that corner. For 100 A into a generated ring at 0.8 m in 100 Ω·m the largest value on the circle (default engine, 0.5 m segments; touch_voltage_at_part() on the same circle gives the same) is 270.89 V round the corner of a 10 m × 10 m ring against 245.22 V round its centre, 229.71 against 161.76 V for 20 m × 5 m, 91.10 against 111.38 V for 30 m × 30 m and, in 5 cm of 150 Ω·m concrete, 134.24 against 120.12 V for 40 m × 10 m (audit D3A-03; with the point kernel at 0.25 m segments 1.3 … 2.2 % lower). 0.15.0, whose circle went round the centre of one grid mesh, gave 240.82, 156.07 and 109.87 V for the bare rings, and 60.30 V for the encased one, whose shell it did not model (audit R4B-09). Use the default "footprint" for generated foundations; it takes the whole foundation and does not depend on the connection point.

'footprint'

Returns:

Type Description complex

Phasor \(U_T(f) = U_E(f) - \varphi(\mathbf{r}_\text{feet}, f)\) in V.

Raises:

Type Description KeyError

If electrode is unknown to world or result.

ValueError

If distance is not strictly positive, direction has no horizontal component, or anchor is unknown.

Warns:

Type Description UniformCurrentFieldWarning

Once per call, for a uniform-current result evaluated near a crowding geometry (see the module docstring).

Notes

Up to v0.15.0 the metre was measured from the connection point, so for a 20 m × 20 m grid (4 × 4 meshes, 100 A, 100 Ω·m) the feet stood above the grid and the helper reported 9.92 V where 1 m outside the edge has 61.3 V (default line kernel; 60.0 V with the point kernel, 61.6 V per segment with mom; 69.6 V with one current over the whole grid, before user decision Q30; F13 / 10.21).

def touch_voltage(
    result: "FieldResult",
    world: "World",
    *,
    electrode: str,
    distance: float = 1.0,
    direction: tuple[float, float, float] = (1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
    surface_z: float = 0.0,
    frequency_index: int = 0,
    anchor: Anchor = "footprint",
) -> complex:
    """Touch voltage at a single point on the soil surface.

    Evaluates :math:`U_T = U_E - \\varphi(\\mathbf{r}_\\text{feet})`,
    where :math:`U_E` is the cluster potential of the touched electrode.
    With the default ``anchor="footprint"`` the feet stand ``distance``
    metres (horizontally) from the nearest wire of the electrode, on the
    ray that leaves the electrode's footprint in the horizontal
    projection of ``direction``: 1 m outside the edge of a grid, 1 m
    beyond the tip of a star arm, 1 m outside a ring on either side.
    This is a proxy for an unknown touched part; for a known accessible
    metal part use :func:`touch_voltage_at_part`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    result
        Solver output from :meth:`Engine.solve`.
    world
        Companion world used to resolve the electrode geometry.
    electrode
        Name of the touched electrode. Its cluster potential is the
        EPR seen by the hand.
    distance
        Horizontal distance between the touched part and the feet,
        in m. EN 50522 uses ``1.0``.
    direction
        Side of the electrode on which the person stands, in world
        coordinates, seen from the length-weighted centroid of the wires.
        Only the horizontal projection is used (the feet stay on the
        surface). Defaults to ``+x``.
    surface_z
        :math:`z` coordinate of the soil surface in m. Default ``0.0``
        (groundfield convention; positive ``z`` is below ground).
    frequency_index
        Index into :attr:`FieldResult.frequencies`. Default 0.
    anchor
        ``"footprint"`` (default since review pass 10, 10.21) measures
        ``distance`` from the nearest wire; ``"connection_point"``
        measures it from :attr:`connection_point` of ``electrode``, the
        rule of v0.15.0. For a hand-built grid mesh or star that is its
        centre, as in v0.15.0. A rectangular foundation of the generators
        is since 2026.11 several bonded wires — one per mesh line (audit
        A2G-04), one per side without cross-braces (user decision Q38) —
        and the electrode named after it is its local :math:`-y` side,
        whose connection point is a corner of the rectangle (in 0.15.0 one
        grid mesh connected at its centre): the feet then stand around that
        corner. For 100 A into a generated ring at 0.8 m in 100 Ω·m the
        largest value on the circle (default engine, 0.5 m segments;
        :func:`touch_voltage_at_part` on the same circle gives the same) is
        270.89 V round the corner of a 10 m × 10 m ring against 245.22 V
        round its centre, 229.71 against 161.76 V for 20 m × 5 m, 91.10
        against 111.38 V for 30 m × 30 m and, in 5 cm of 150 Ω·m concrete,
        134.24 against 120.12 V for 40 m × 10 m (audit D3A-03; with the
        point kernel at 0.25 m segments 1.3 … 2.2 % lower). 0.15.0, whose
        circle went round the centre of one grid mesh, gave 240.82, 156.07
        and 109.87 V for the bare rings, and 60.30 V for the encased one,
        whose shell it did not model (audit R4B-09). Use the default
        ``"footprint"`` for generated foundations;
        it takes the whole foundation and does not depend on the
        connection point.

    Returns
    -------
    complex
        Phasor :math:`U_T(f) = U_E(f) - \\varphi(\\mathbf{r}_\\text{feet}, f)`
        in V.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If ``electrode`` is unknown to ``world`` or ``result``.
    ValueError
        If ``distance`` is not strictly positive, ``direction`` has no
        horizontal component, or ``anchor`` is unknown.

    Warns
    -----
    UniformCurrentFieldWarning
        Once per call, for a uniform-current result evaluated near a
        crowding geometry (see the module docstring).

    Notes
    -----
    Up to v0.15.0 the metre was measured from the connection point, so
    for a 20 m × 20 m grid (4 × 4 meshes, 100 A, 100 Ω·m) the feet stood
    above the grid and the helper reported 9.92 V where 1 m outside the
    edge has 61.3 V (default line kernel; 60.0 V with the point kernel,
    61.6 V per segment with ``mom``; 69.6 V with one current over the
    whole grid, before user decision Q30; F13 / 10.21).
    """
    _check_distance(distance)
    _check_anchor(anchor)
    e_h = _horizontal(direction)
    feet_xy = _feet_xy(world, electrode, e_h[None, :2], distance, anchor, result)[0]
    feet = np.array([[feet_xy[0], feet_xy[1], surface_z]])
    _uniform_current_caveat(result, world, feet, caller="touch_voltage")
    phi_feet = complex(result.potential(feet, frequency_index=frequency_index)[0])
    U_E = _cluster_potential(result, electrode, frequency_index)
    return U_E - phi_feet

docs.title: touch_voltage_at_part
docs.text:
touch_voltage_at_part(result: 'FieldResult', world: 'World | None' = None, *, position: Sequence[float], bonded_to: str, distance: float = 1.0, n_angles: int | None = None, directions: 'Sequence[Sequence[float]] | None' = None, exclude: 'Sequence[Sequence[Sequence[float]]] | None' = None, surface_z: float = 0.0, frequency_index: int = 0, return_points: bool = False) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

Touch voltage of an accessible metal part, feet distance around it.

EN 50522 defines the touch voltage between a conductive part that a person touches and the person's feet, standing 1 m away from the part. The touch points of an installation are its accessible metal parts above ground — a station housing or its door, a mast, a fence post, a cable cabinet, a service connection box — not the buried electrode. This helper takes one such part: its horizontal position \(\mathbf p\) and the electrode or junction it is bonded to, whose potential \(U_\text{part}\) it carries. The feet stand on the circle of radius \(d\) = distance around the part,

\[ \mathbf r_k = \mathbf p + d\,(\cos\theta_k, \sin\theta_k), \qquad U_{T,k} = U_\text{part} - \varphi(\mathbf r_k), \]

at n_angles equally spaced azimuths \(\theta_k = 2\pi k / n\), or only in the given directions; foot positions inside an outline of exclude (the housing or the building itself, where nobody can stand) are dropped. A part bonded to a node far from the faulted earth — a service connection box on the PEN junction of a house, a cable screen led out of a station — carries a transferred potential; U_T is then most of the earth potential rise.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default result 'FieldResult'

Solver output from Engine.solve().

required world 'World | None'

Optional companion world. Only used to decide whether to emit UniformCurrentFieldWarning, as in step_voltage().

None position Sequence[float]

Horizontal position (x, y) of the touched part in m. A third coordinate is accepted and ignored: the part stands above ground, the feet on the surface.

required bonded_to str

Name of the electrode or junction (create_junction()) whose potential the part carries: the station earth for its housing, the PEN junction of a house for its connection box.

required distance float

Horizontal distance between the part and the feet in m, > 0 (1.0 by EN 50522).

1.0 n_angles int | None

Number of equally spaced foot positions on the circle, >= 3; 24 when neither n_angles nor directions is given.

None directions 'Sequence[Sequence[float]] | None'

Only these horizontal directions (2- or 3-vectors, the z component is ignored), seen from the part: for example the outside of a fence. Not together with n_angles.

None exclude 'Sequence[Sequence[Sequence[float]]] | None'

Outlines where nobody can stand, each a polygon of vertices (x, y) or (x, y, z) in m (z ignored), e.g. the housing of a station or a building. Foot positions strictly inside an outline are dropped; positions on it (against the wall) are kept.

None surface_z float

\(z\) coordinate of the soil surface in m. Default 0.0.

0.0 frequency_index int

Index into FieldResult.frequencies. Default 0.

0 return_points bool

Also return the foot positions.

False

Returns:

Name Type Description angles (ndarray, shape(n))

Azimuth in radians in \([0, 2\pi)\) of each remaining foot position, seen from the part and measured from +x.

voltages np.ndarray, shape (n,), dtype complex

Touch-voltage phasor \(U_T\) in V at every foot position.

points (ndarray, shape(n, 3))

Foot positions in m; only with return_points=True.

Raises:

Type Description KeyError

If bonded_to is neither an electrode nor a junction with a potential in result.

IndexError

If frequency_index is out of range.

ValueError

If distance is not a positive finite number, position is not a finite 2- or 3-vector, n_angles < 3, both n_angles and directions are given, a direction has no horizontal component, an outline is not a polygon, or every foot position lies inside an outline.

Warns:

Type Description UniformCurrentFieldWarning

Once per call, for a uniform-current result evaluated near a crowding geometry (see the module docstring).

Notes

For a part on a wire of the electrode with the feet pointing away from it, the foot position is the one of touch_voltage() and so is the value. The voltage is the prospective (open-circuit) touch voltage; compare its magnitude with permissible_touch_voltage_en50522(), or with permissible_prospective_touch_voltage_en50522() when footwear or a surface layer adds resistance.

def touch_voltage_at_part(
    result: "FieldResult",
    world: "World | None" = None,
    *,
    position: Sequence[float],
    bonded_to: str,
    distance: float = 1.0,
    n_angles: int | None = None,
    directions: "Sequence[Sequence[float]] | None" = None,
    exclude: "Sequence[Sequence[Sequence[float]]] | None" = None,
    surface_z: float = 0.0,
    frequency_index: int = 0,
    return_points: bool = False,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Touch voltage of an accessible metal part, feet ``distance`` around it.

    EN 50522 defines the touch voltage between a conductive part that a
    person touches and the person's feet, standing 1 m away from the
    part. The touch points of an installation are its accessible metal
    parts above ground — a station housing or its door, a mast, a fence
    post, a cable cabinet, a service connection box — not the buried
    electrode. This helper takes one such part: its horizontal position
    :math:`\\mathbf p` and the electrode or junction it is bonded to,
    whose potential :math:`U_\\text{part}` it carries. The feet stand on
    the circle of radius :math:`d` = ``distance`` around the part,

    .. math::

        \\mathbf r_k = \\mathbf p + d\\,(\\cos\\theta_k, \\sin\\theta_k),
        \\qquad
        U_{T,k} = U_\\text{part} - \\varphi(\\mathbf r_k),

    at ``n_angles`` equally spaced azimuths
    :math:`\\theta_k = 2\\pi k / n`, or only in the given ``directions``;
    foot positions inside an outline of ``exclude`` (the housing or the
    building itself, where nobody can stand) are dropped. A part bonded
    to a node far from the faulted earth — a service connection box on the
    PEN junction of a house, a cable screen led out of a station —
    carries a transferred potential; ``U_T`` is then most of the earth
    potential rise.

    Parameters
    ----------
    result
        Solver output from :meth:`Engine.solve`.
    world
        Optional companion world. Only used to decide whether to emit
        :class:`UniformCurrentFieldWarning`, as in :func:`step_voltage`.
    position
        Horizontal position ``(x, y)`` of the touched part in m. A third
        coordinate is accepted and ignored: the part stands above ground,
        the feet on the surface.
    bonded_to
        Name of the electrode or junction (:func:`~groundfield.create_junction`)
        whose potential the part carries: the station earth for its
        housing, the PEN junction of a house for its connection box.
    distance
        Horizontal distance between the part and the feet in m, ``> 0``
        (1.0 by EN 50522).
    n_angles
        Number of equally spaced foot positions on the circle, ``>= 3``;
        24 when neither ``n_angles`` nor ``directions`` is given.
    directions
        Only these horizontal directions (2- or 3-vectors, the ``z``
        component is ignored), seen from the part: for example the outside
        of a fence. Not together with ``n_angles``.
    exclude
        Outlines where nobody can stand, each a polygon of vertices
        ``(x, y)`` or ``(x, y, z)`` in m (``z`` ignored), e.g. the housing
        of a station or a building. Foot positions strictly inside an
        outline are dropped; positions on it (against the wall) are kept.
    surface_z
        :math:`z` coordinate of the soil surface in m. Default ``0.0``.
    frequency_index
        Index into :attr:`FieldResult.frequencies`. Default 0.
    return_points
        Also return the foot positions.

    Returns
    -------
    angles : np.ndarray, shape (n,)
        Azimuth in radians in :math:`[0, 2\\pi)` of each remaining foot
        position, seen from the part and measured from ``+x``.
    voltages : np.ndarray, shape (n,), dtype complex
        Touch-voltage phasor :math:`U_T` in V at every foot position.
    points : np.ndarray, shape (n, 3)
        Foot positions in m; only with ``return_points=True``.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If ``bonded_to`` is neither an electrode nor a junction with a
        potential in ``result``.
    IndexError
        If ``frequency_index`` is out of range.
    ValueError
        If ``distance`` is not a positive finite number, ``position`` is
        not a finite 2- or 3-vector, ``n_angles < 3``, both ``n_angles``
        and ``directions`` are given, a direction has no horizontal
        component, an outline is not a polygon, or every foot position
        lies inside an outline.

    Warns
    -----
    UniformCurrentFieldWarning
        Once per call, for a uniform-current result evaluated near a
        crowding geometry (see the module docstring).

    Notes
    -----
    For a part on a wire of the electrode with the feet pointing away
    from it, the foot position is the one of :func:`touch_voltage` and so
    is the value. The voltage is the prospective (open-circuit) touch
    voltage; compare its magnitude with
    :func:`permissible_touch_voltage_en50522`, or with
    :func:`permissible_prospective_touch_voltage_en50522` when footwear or
    a surface layer adds resistance.
    """
    # user decision Q3: touch points are the accessible metal parts.
    _check_distance(distance)
    origin = _horizontal_xy(position, "position")
    angles, unit = _part_directions(n_angles, directions)
    keep = _accessible(distance * unit, exclude, origin, distance)
    if not keep.any():
        raise ValueError(
            "every foot position around the part lies inside an outline of "
            "exclude; there is no accessible standing position."
        )
    angles, feet_xy = angles[keep], origin + distance * unit[keep]
    u_part = _node_potential(result, bonded_to, frequency_index)
    feet = np.column_stack([feet_xy, np.full(len(feet_xy), surface_z, dtype=float)])
    _uniform_current_caveat(result, world, feet, caller="touch_voltage_at_part")
    voltages = u_part - result.potential(feet, frequency_index=frequency_index)
    if return_points:
        return angles, voltages, feet
    return angles, voltages

docs.text:
touch_voltage_envelope(result: 'FieldResult', world: 'World', *, electrode: str, distance: float = 1.0, n_angles: int = 24, surface_z: float = 0.0, frequency_index: int = 0, anchor: Anchor = 'footprint', interior: Interior = False, corners: bool = True, return_points: bool = False) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

Touch voltages around an electrode, on request also inside its loops.

Walks n_angles equally spaced directions and places the feet as in touch_voltage(): with anchor="footprint" this traces the curve at distance from the electrode's wires (rounded around corners and arm tips). Equally spaced directions hit the rounded corners only by chance, and the touch voltage is largest there: the corners of a 60 m × 40 m grid lie at 33.7° from its centre, between the 30° and 45° rays of the default 24, and that envelope read 12 … 28 % low in two-layer soil (case study E03). With corners=True (the default) the feet also stand on the arc around every corner of the convex hull of the wires, nine per corner. The maximum of |U_T| is the conservative envelope used in safety verification when the touched parts are not known; where they are, touch_voltage_at_part() puts the feet around each part.

By default nothing inside the footprint is sampled: there stands the station, the house, the steel structure or the mast. Over an open-air grid such as a substation yard people walk inside the loops, and the surface potential sags there, so the touch voltage can exceed every value on the offset curve (a 20 m × 20 m perimeter loop at 0.5 m depth, 100 Ω·m, 100 A: 158 V in the centre against at most 141 V 1 m outside). For such grids interior="meshes" also evaluates the centre of every closed mesh, the analogue of the mesh voltage of IEEE Std 80 (the worst touch voltage inside a mesh of a grid, near the mesh centre).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default result 'FieldResult'

See touch_voltage().

required world 'FieldResult'

See touch_voltage().

required electrode str

Name of the touched electrode.

required distance float

Horizontal distance from the wires in m (1.0 by EN 50522).

1.0 n_angles int

Number of equally spaced directions \(\theta_k = 2\pi k / n\) with \(k = 0, \dots, n - 1\). Must be >= 3.

24 surface_z float

See touch_voltage().

0.0 frequency_index float

See touch_voltage().

0.0 anchor float

See touch_voltage().

0.0 interior Interior

Which closed loops are also sampled inside (review pass 10, 10.21). False (default): none, the offset curve only, for every electrode kind. "meshes": the centre of every mesh of a mesh / grid_mesh electrode, the centre of a ring, and the centre of every cell of a foundation built from bonded wires (foundation_wires(); the generators build every mesh foundation as one open polyline per wire line and every rectangle without cross-braces as one wire per side, user decision Q38), but not the inside of a closed polyline, the building-outline foundation of the generators. Use it where the inside of the loops is accessible open ground: a substation yard or another open-air grid, a ring around an open area. True: also a closed polyline, at the point inside it farthest from its wires. The modes cannot see buildings: a mesh foundation's cells lie under the house, a ring may surround a station housing or a mast foot.

False corners bool

With anchor="footprint", also place nine feet on the arc of the offset curve around every corner of the convex hull of the wires, from one edge normal to the next (a half circle at each end of a single straight wire; none for one rod or a ring). False reproduces the equally spaced directions alone (the behaviour up to the final documentation pass of 2026.11.0). Ignored with anchor="connection_point".

True return_points bool

Also return the foot positions.

False

Returns:

Name Type Description angles (ndarray, shape(n))

Azimuth in radians of each foot position, measured from +x. The first n_angles entries are \(\theta_k\). The corner points follow (they lie on the offset curve too), then the interior points; both carry their azimuth seen from the centroid of the wires (0 for an interior point that coincides with it). To read the interior points alone, call once more with corners=False: they then start at index n_angles.

voltages np.ndarray, shape (n,), dtype complex

Touch-voltage phasor \(U_T\) in V at every foot position.

points (ndarray, shape(n, 3))

Foot positions in m; only with return_points=True.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

For n_angles < 3, a non-positive distance, an unknown anchor or an interior other than False, "meshes" and True.

Warns:

Type Description UniformCurrentFieldWarning

Once per call, for a uniform-current result evaluated near a crowding geometry (see the module docstring).

Notes

n = n_angles plus the number of interior points and of corner points. The rule of v0.15.0 (circle around the connection point) is anchor="connection_point"; for a generated rectangular foundation that connection point is a corner since 2026.11, no longer the centre (see anchor in touch_voltage()). During the 2026.11 development the mesh sampling was the default (interior=None); it is now the explicit interior="meshes".

def touch_voltage_envelope(
    result: "FieldResult",
    world: "World",
    *,
    electrode: str,
    distance: float = 1.0,
    n_angles: int = 24,
    surface_z: float = 0.0,
    frequency_index: int = 0,
    anchor: Anchor = "footprint",
    interior: Interior = False,
    corners: bool = True,
    return_points: bool = False,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Touch voltages around an electrode, on request also inside its loops.

    Walks ``n_angles`` equally spaced directions and places the feet as
    in :func:`touch_voltage`: with ``anchor="footprint"`` this traces
    the curve at ``distance`` from the electrode's wires (rounded around
    corners and arm tips). Equally spaced directions hit the rounded
    corners only by chance, and the touch voltage is largest there: the
    corners of a 60 m × 40 m grid lie at 33.7° from its centre, between
    the 30° and 45° rays of the default 24, and that envelope read 12 …
    28 % low in two-layer soil (case study E03). With ``corners=True``
    (the default) the feet also stand on the arc around every corner of
    the convex hull of the wires, nine per corner. The maximum of ``|U_T|`` is the conservative
    envelope used in safety verification when the touched parts are not
    known; where they are, :func:`touch_voltage_at_part` puts the feet
    around each part.

    By default nothing inside the footprint is sampled: there stands the
    station, the house, the steel structure or the mast. Over an open-air
    grid such as a substation yard people walk inside the loops, and the
    surface potential sags there, so the touch voltage can exceed every
    value on the offset curve (a 20 m × 20 m perimeter loop at 0.5 m
    depth, 100 Ω·m, 100 A: 158 V in the centre against at most 141 V
    1 m outside). For such grids ``interior="meshes"`` also evaluates the
    centre of every closed mesh, the analogue of the *mesh voltage* of
    IEEE Std 80 (the worst touch voltage inside a mesh of a grid, near
    the mesh centre).

    Parameters
    ----------
    result, world
        See :func:`touch_voltage`.
    electrode
        Name of the touched electrode.
    distance
        Horizontal distance from the wires in m (1.0 by EN 50522).
    n_angles
        Number of equally spaced directions
        :math:`\\theta_k = 2\\pi k / n` with :math:`k = 0, \\dots, n - 1`.
        Must be ``>= 3``.
    surface_z, frequency_index, anchor
        See :func:`touch_voltage`.
    interior
        Which closed loops are also sampled inside (review pass 10, 10.21).
        ``False`` (default): none, the offset curve only, for every
        electrode kind. ``"meshes"``: the centre of every mesh of a
        ``mesh`` / ``grid_mesh`` electrode, the centre of a ``ring``, and
        the centre of every cell of a foundation built from bonded wires
        (:func:`~groundfield.postprocess._footprint.foundation_wires`; the
        generators build every mesh foundation as one open polyline per
        wire line and every rectangle without cross-braces as one wire per
        side, user decision Q38), but not the inside of a closed
        ``polyline``, the
        building-outline foundation of the generators. Use it where the
        inside of the loops is accessible open ground: a substation yard
        or another open-air grid, a ring around an open area. ``True``:
        also a closed polyline, at the point inside it farthest from its
        wires. The modes cannot see buildings: a mesh foundation's cells
        lie under the house, a ring may surround a station housing or a
        mast foot.
    corners
        With ``anchor="footprint"``, also place nine feet on the arc of
        the offset curve around every corner of the convex hull of the
        wires, from one edge normal to the next (a half circle at each end
        of a single straight wire; none for one rod or a ring). ``False``
        reproduces the equally spaced directions alone (the behaviour up to
        the final documentation pass of 2026.11.0). Ignored with
        ``anchor="connection_point"``.
    return_points
        Also return the foot positions.

    Returns
    -------
    angles : np.ndarray, shape (n,)
        Azimuth in radians of each foot position, measured from ``+x``.
        The first ``n_angles`` entries are :math:`\\theta_k`. The corner
        points follow (they lie on the offset curve too), then the
        interior points; both carry their azimuth seen from the centroid of
        the wires (0 for an interior point that coincides with it). To
        read the interior points alone, call once more with
        ``corners=False``: they then start at index ``n_angles``.
    voltages : np.ndarray, shape (n,), dtype complex
        Touch-voltage phasor :math:`U_T` in V at every foot position.
    points : np.ndarray, shape (n, 3)
        Foot positions in m; only with ``return_points=True``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For ``n_angles < 3``, a non-positive ``distance``, an unknown
        ``anchor`` or an ``interior`` other than ``False``, ``"meshes"``
        and ``True``.

    Warns
    -----
    UniformCurrentFieldWarning
        Once per call, for a uniform-current result evaluated near a
        crowding geometry (see the module docstring).

    Notes
    -----
    ``n = n_angles`` plus the number of interior points and of corner
    points. The rule of
    v0.15.0 (circle around the connection point) is
    ``anchor="connection_point"``; for a generated rectangular foundation
    that connection point is a corner since 2026.11, no longer the centre
    (see ``anchor`` in :func:`touch_voltage`). During the 2026.11 development the
    mesh sampling was the default (``interior=None``); it is now the
    explicit ``interior="meshes"``.
    """
    if n_angles < 3:
        raise ValueError(f"n_angles must be >= 3, got {n_angles}.")
    _check_distance(distance)
    _check_anchor(anchor)
    # user decision Q3: no interior sampling unless asked for.
    interior = _check_interior(interior)

    angles = np.linspace(0.0, 2.0 * np.pi, n_angles, endpoint=False)
    dirs = np.column_stack([np.cos(angles), np.sin(angles)])
    feet_xy = _feet_xy(world, electrode, dirs, distance, anchor, result)
    if corners and anchor == "footprint":
        fp = footprint_of(
            foundation_wires(world, electrode, getattr(result, "clusters", None))
        )
        corner = fp.corner_feet(distance)
        if len(corner):
            ref = fp.reference_point
            az = np.mod(
                np.arctan2(corner[:, 1] - ref[1], corner[:, 0] - ref[0]), 2 * np.pi
            )
            angles = np.concatenate([angles, az])
            feet_xy = np.vstack([feet_xy, corner])
    if interior is not False:
        wires = foundation_wires(world, electrode, getattr(result, "clusters", None))
        inner = interior_points_of(wires, outlines=interior is True)
        if len(inner):
            ref = footprint_of(wires).reference_point
            az = np.mod(
                np.arctan2(inner[:, 1] - ref[1], inner[:, 0] - ref[0]), 2 * np.pi
            )
            az[np.hypot(*(inner - ref).T) <= 1e-12] = 0.0
            angles = np.concatenate([angles, az])
            feet_xy = np.vstack([feet_xy, inner])
    feet = np.column_stack([feet_xy, np.full(len(feet_xy), surface_z, dtype=float)])
    _uniform_current_caveat(result, world, feet, caller="touch_voltage_envelope")
    phi_feet = result.potential(feet, frequency_index=frequency_index)
    U_E = _cluster_potential(result, electrode, frequency_index)
    voltages = U_E - phi_feet
    if return_points:
        return angles, voltages, feet
    return angles, voltages

touch_voltage_spectrum(result: 'FieldResult | Sequence[FieldResult]', world: 'World', *, electrode: str, currents: 'Sequence[complex] | Mapping[float, complex]', distance: float = 1.0, direction: tuple[float, float, float] = (1.0, 0.0, 0.0), surface_z: float = 0.0, anchor: Anchor = 'footprint', source: str | None = None) -> float

True-RMS touch voltage of a fault-current spectrum at one position.

The field problem is linear, so the touch voltage of harmonic \(k\) scales with the fault current \(I_k\) of that harmonic. With \(U_T(f_k)\) from a solve with source current \(I_\text{src}(f_k)\), the touch voltage at the fixed foot position of touch_voltage() is

\[ U_{T,\text{rms}} \;=\; \sqrt{\sum_k \left|U_T(f_k)\,\frac{I_k}{I_\text{src}(f_k)}\right|^2}, \]

the RMS value of the superposed harmonics (they are orthogonal over a period).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default result 'FieldResult | Sequence[FieldResult]'

One multi-frequency result, or a sequence of results whose frequencies are taken in order (for example one result per harmonic).

required world 'World'

Companion world (geometry of the touched electrode).

required electrode str

Name of the touched electrode.

required currents 'Sequence[complex] | Mapping[float, complex]'

Fault current per frequency as RMS phasors (or RMS magnitudes) in A: either a sequence aligned with the frequencies of result, or a mapping {frequency_Hz: current} that covers every frequency exactly once.

required distance float

Foot position, see touch_voltage(); the same position is used for every frequency.

1.0 direction float

Foot position, see touch_voltage(); the same position is used for every frequency.

1.0 surface_z float

Foot position, see touch_voltage(); the same position is used for every frequency.

1.0 anchor float

Foot position, see touch_voltage(); the same position is used for every frequency.

1.0 source str | None

Name of the current or voltage source the results were solved with (the denominator is its impressed or solved current); may be omitted when there is exactly one.

None

Returns:

Type Description float

RMS touch voltage \(U_{T,\text{rms}}\) in V.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the currents do not match the frequencies, are not finite, a frequency appears in more than one result (it would be counted twice), a result carries no source snapshot or no source current per frequency (a voltage record without its solved current), or the source current is zero at some frequency.

Notes

EN 50522's permissible touch voltage is a 50 Hz curve; comparing a spectrum RMS with \(U_{Tp}\) ignores the frequency factors of IEC 60479-2 (the body tolerates more current at higher frequencies), which is conservative.

def touch_voltage_spectrum(
    result: "FieldResult | Sequence[FieldResult]",
    world: "World",
    *,
    electrode: str,
    currents: "Sequence[complex] | Mapping[float, complex]",
    distance: float = 1.0,
    direction: tuple[float, float, float] = (1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
    surface_z: float = 0.0,
    anchor: Anchor = "footprint",
    source: str | None = None,
) -> float:
    """True-RMS touch voltage of a fault-current spectrum at one position.

    The field problem is linear, so the touch voltage of harmonic
    :math:`k` scales with the fault current :math:`I_k` of that
    harmonic. With :math:`U_T(f_k)` from a solve with source current
    :math:`I_\\text{src}(f_k)`, the touch voltage at the fixed foot
    position of :func:`touch_voltage` is

    .. math::

        U_{T,\\text{rms}} \\;=\\; \\sqrt{\\sum_k
        \\left|U_T(f_k)\\,\\frac{I_k}{I_\\text{src}(f_k)}\\right|^2},

    the RMS value of the superposed harmonics (they are orthogonal over
    a period).

    Parameters
    ----------
    result
        One multi-frequency result, or a sequence of results whose
        frequencies are taken in order (for example one result per
        harmonic).
    world
        Companion world (geometry of the touched electrode).
    electrode
        Name of the touched electrode.
    currents
        Fault current per frequency as RMS phasors (or RMS magnitudes)
        in A: either a sequence aligned with the frequencies of
        ``result``, or a mapping ``{frequency_Hz: current}`` that covers
        every frequency exactly once.
    distance, direction, surface_z, anchor
        Foot position, see :func:`touch_voltage`; the same position is
        used for every frequency.
    source
        Name of the current or voltage source the results were solved
        with (the denominator is its impressed or solved current); may be
        omitted when there is exactly one.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        RMS touch voltage :math:`U_{T,\\text{rms}}` in V.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the currents do not match the frequencies, are not finite, a
        frequency appears in more than one result (it would be counted
        twice), a result carries no source snapshot or no source current
        per frequency (a voltage record without its solved current), or
        the source current is zero at some frequency.

    Notes
    -----
    EN 50522's permissible touch voltage is a 50 Hz curve; comparing a
    spectrum RMS with :math:`U_{Tp}` ignores the frequency factors of
    IEC 60479-2 (the body tolerates more current at higher frequencies),
    which is conservative.
    """
    results = [result] if hasattr(result, "frequencies") else list(result)
    pairs = [
        (res, k, float(f)) for res in results for k, f in enumerate(res.frequencies)
    ]
    freqs = [f for _, _, f in pairs]
    # The harmonics of a spectrum are orthogonal only at distinct
    # frequencies; a frequency carried by two results was counted twice
    # (audit 1, L4).
    ordered = sorted(freqs)
    for lo, hi in zip(ordered, ordered[1:], strict=False):
        if math.isclose(lo, hi, rel_tol=1e-9, abs_tol=1e-9):
            raise ValueError(
                f"touch_voltage_spectrum: {lo:g} Hz appears more than once among "
                "the results; give every harmonic once."
            )
    if isinstance(currents, Mapping):
        keys = [float(f) for f in currents]
        values = []
        used: set[int] = set()
        for f in freqs:
            hit = [
                i
                for i, key in enumerate(keys)
                if math.isclose(key, f, rel_tol=1e-9, abs_tol=1e-9)
            ]
            if len(hit) != 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"currents must give exactly one value for {f:g} Hz; "
                    f"keys: {sorted(keys)}."
                )
            used.add(hit[0])
            values.append(list(currents.values())[hit[0]])
        extra = [keys[i] for i in range(len(keys)) if i not in used]
        if extra:
            raise ValueError(f"currents has no result for frequencies {extra} Hz.")
    else:
        values = list(currents)
        if len(values) != len(pairs):
            raise ValueError(
                f"currents has {len(values)} entries but the results carry "
                f"{len(pairs)} frequencies."
            )
    i_k = np.asarray(values, dtype=complex)
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(i_k)):
        raise ValueError("currents must be finite.")

    _check_distance(distance)
    _check_anchor(anchor)
    e_h = _horizontal(direction)
    feet_xy = _feet_xy(world, electrode, e_h[None, :2], distance, anchor, results[0])[0]
    feet = np.array([[feet_xy[0], feet_xy[1], surface_z]])
    warned = set()
    total = 0.0
    for (res, k, _), i_fault in zip(pairs, i_k, strict=True):
        if res.backend not in warned:
            _uniform_current_caveat(res, world, feet, caller="touch_voltage_spectrum")
            warned.add(res.backend)
        u_t = _cluster_potential(res, electrode, k) - complex(
            res.potential(feet, frequency_index=k)[0]
        )
        total += abs(u_t * i_fault / _source_current(res, source, k)) ** 2
    return math.sqrt(total)

docs.title: current_balance
docs.text:
Current sharing and split-factor analysis for a FieldResult.

This module turns the per-electrode currents stored in groundfield.solver.result.FieldResult into the engineering quantities that answer "where does the injected source current actually return?". In a TN-Ortsnetz with hundreds of houses, dozens of cable cabinets and one or more metallic return paths (PEN trunk, measurement leads, cable shields), the soil-leakage current of every cluster matters and cannot be read off electrode_currents directly without aggregation.

Quantities
  • Per-cluster soil leakage \(I_{c} = \sum_{e \in c} I_e\). With ideal galvanic bonds (cross_section=None) the cluster members share a potential \(U_c\); the cluster impedance is then \(Z_c = U_c / I_c\). Returned as a tabular summary by cluster_current_balance().
  • Per-electrode share of cluster current — what fraction of the cluster's net soil leakage flows through this specific electrode: \(s_{e \mid c} = I_e / I_c\) (complex). Returned alongside the per-electrode potential / impedance by electrode_current_table().
  • Split factor \(s = I_{c_\text{src}} / I_\text{src} = \sum_{e \in c_\text{src}} I_e / I_\text{src}\), with \(c_\text{src}\) the cluster of the source's attached_to electrode. s = 1 means the injected current leaves the source cluster entirely through the soil (no metallic short-cut to the return-path cluster). s < 1 means a metallic conductor (PEN trunk, parallel measurement lead, cable shield) carries part of the current as a parallel resistive path.

This is the galvanic current-split between parallel paths. It is not the Reduktionsfaktor in the German EVU / Schirmtechnik sense (Oeding & Oswald 2016): that latter quantity is the additional transformatorische / inductive coupling correction between a current-carrying conductor and a parallel grounding / shield conductor. The Reduktionsfaktor vanishes when the two conductors are perpendicular (no flux linkage) but the split factor still applies — the current always splits among parallel resistive paths irrespective of the geometric angle. A future helper may add the proper Reduktionsfaktor based on the Neumann mutual-inductance / Carson / Sommerfeld backends already present in groundfield.coupling.

Validity envelope
  • Frequency: quasi-static envelope \(f \le 1\,\mathrm{kHz}\).
  • Conventions: FieldResult.electrode_currents carries the per-electrode soil-leakage current in A (complex phasor), with positive sign in the direction electrode → soil. All quantities here are complex per frequency_index.
  • Cluster discovery uses FieldResult.clusters — the same map produced by every backend.
Which impedance (review pass 10, 10.18)

The Z columns of cluster_current_balance() are cluster impedances — a cluster's potential over its own soil leakage — and those of electrode_current_table() are electrode impedances \(U_e / I_e\). Neither is the input impedance a source sees (FieldResult.input_impedance(), the default quantity of groundfield.postprocess.sweep.sweep() and of the rho-f exporters). For one current source returning through remote earth the split factor links them: \(Z_\text{in} = s\,Z_c\).

def cluster_current_balance(
    result: "FieldResult",
    *,
    frequency_index: int = 0,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-cluster soil leakage, potential and impedance.

    Returns one row per *unique* galvanic cluster present in the
    result. The cluster impedance is computed as
    :math:`Z_c = U_c / I_c` with :math:`I_c = \\sum_{e \\in c} I_e`
    — the cluster's potential over its **own soil leakage**, not the
    input impedance a source sees when conductors carry current out of
    the cluster (see the module docstring). Where :math:`I_c = 0`
    (purely passive observer cluster) the impedance columns are ``NaN``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    result
        Solver output.
    frequency_index
        Index into :attr:`FieldResult.frequencies`. Default 0.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns
        ``cluster_root``,
        ``n_members``,
        ``members`` (list of strings),
        ``U_re``, ``U_im``, ``abs_U``,
        ``sum_I_re``, ``sum_I_im``, ``abs_sum_I``,
        ``Z_re``, ``Z_im``, ``abs_Z``, ``arg_Z_deg``.
        Rows are sorted by descending ``abs_sum_I`` so the
        dominant clusters surface first — the typical
        debugging order.
    """
    rows = []
    for root, members in _unique_clusters(result).items():
        # Cluster potential = potential of any member (ideal cluster
        # bond -> shared phi). Use the canonical root.
        U = complex(result.electrode_potentials[root][frequency_index])
        sum_I = 0.0 + 0j
        for m in members:
            if m not in result.electrode_currents:
                continue
            sum_I += complex(result.electrode_currents[m][frequency_index])
        if sum_I != 0:
            Z = U / sum_I
        else:
            Z = complex("nan")
        rows.append(
            {
                "cluster_root": root,
                "n_members": len(members),
                "members": list(members),
                "U_re": U.real,
                "U_im": U.imag,
                "abs_U": abs(U),
                "sum_I_re": sum_I.real,
                "sum_I_im": sum_I.imag,
                "abs_sum_I": abs(sum_I),
                "Z_re": Z.real if np.isfinite(Z.real) else float("nan"),
                "Z_im": Z.imag if np.isfinite(Z.imag) else float("nan"),
                "abs_Z": (
                    abs(Z)
                    if (np.isfinite(Z.real) and np.isfinite(Z.imag))
                    else float("nan")
                ),
                "arg_Z_deg": (
                    math.degrees(cmath.phase(Z))
                    if (np.isfinite(Z.real) and np.isfinite(Z.imag))
                    else float("nan")
                ),
            }
        )
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    if not df.empty:
        df = df.sort_values("abs_sum_I", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
    return df

Per-electrode potential, current and share of cluster current.

For each electrode in the result the table reports the potential \(U_e\) (= cluster potential), the soil-leakage current \(I_e\), the implied two-terminal impedance \(Z_e = U_e / I_e\) (the electrode's own leakage impedance, quantity="electrode" in the sweep / rho-f helpers), and the fractional share of the cluster total \(s_{e \mid c} = I_e / I_c\). The latter is the engineering key indicator for "of all the soil current leaving cluster c, how much physically flows through this specific electrode" — useful when looking at a single transformer station with a ring + several rods, or a building cluster with multiple foundation parts.

None frequency_index int

Index into FieldResult.frequencies. Default 0.
