Implements Oeding/Oswald 2016 Eq. (9.13c):

\[ L'_S \;=\; \frac{\mu_0}{\pi} \Bigl[\ln\!\Bigl(\frac{d}{r}\Bigr) + \frac{1}{4}\Bigr], \]

valid for two long, straight, parallel wires of radius \(r\) at centre-to-centre distance \(d\), with \(d \gg r\).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default distance float

Centre-to-centre distance \(d\) between the two wires (m).

required wire_radius float

Wire radius \(r\) (m).

required include_internal bool

True (default) — include the internal-field contribution \(\mu_0 / (4\pi)\) per loop. False — return the external-field expression \(L'_{S,\text{ext}} = (\mu_0 / \pi) \ln(d/r)\) that applies in the high-frequency skin-effect limit.

True

Name Type Description L_per_length float

Loop self-inductance per unit length in H/m.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If distance or wire_radius is not positive, or if distance does not exceed wire_radius.

def loop_self_inductance_per_length(
    distance: float,
    wire_radius: float,
    *,
    include_internal: bool = True,
) -> float:
    """Self-inductance per unit length of a two-wire loop.

    Implements Oeding/Oswald 2016 Eq. (9.13c):

    $$
    L'_S \\;=\\; \\frac{\\mu_0}{\\pi}
    \\Bigl[\\ln\\!\\Bigl(\\frac{d}{r}\\Bigr) + \\frac{1}{4}\\Bigr],
    $$

    valid for two long, straight, parallel wires of radius $r$ at
    centre-to-centre distance $d$, with $d \\gg r$.

    Parameters
    ----------
    distance
        Centre-to-centre distance $d$ between the two wires (m).
    wire_radius
        Wire radius $r$ (m).
    include_internal
        ``True`` (default) — include the internal-field
        contribution $\\mu_0 / (4\\pi)$ per loop. ``False`` —
        return the external-field expression
        $L'_{S,\\text{ext}} = (\\mu_0 / \\pi) \\ln(d/r)$ that
        applies in the high-frequency skin-effect limit.

    Returns
    -------
    L_per_length : float
        Loop self-inductance per unit length in H/m.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``distance`` or ``wire_radius`` is not positive, or if
        ``distance`` does not exceed ``wire_radius``.
    """
    if distance <= 0.0 or wire_radius <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("distance and wire_radius must be positive")
    if distance <= wire_radius:
        raise ValueError("distance must exceed wire_radius (d >> r assumed)")
    r_eff = two_wire_loop_radius(wire_radius, include_internal=include_internal)
    return (MU_0 / math.pi) * math.log(distance / r_eff)

docs.title: two_wire_loop_radius
docs.text:
two_wire_loop_radius(wire_radius: float, *, include_internal: bool = True) -> float

Effective wire radius \(r' = r \cdot e^{-1/4}\) used in the Oeding loop-inductance formulas.

The factor \(e^{-1/4}\) is the mean geometric distance of a circular cross section from itself (Anhang A.7, case 1) and folds the internal-field contribution \(\mu_0 / (8\pi)\) into a purely geometric expression. With \(r' = r \cdot e^{-1/4}\) the loop self-inductance becomes \(L'_S = (\mu_0 / \pi) \ln(d/r')\), which equals \((\mu_0 / \pi)(\ln(d/r) + 1/4)\) — Eq. (9.13c).

Pass include_internal=False to suppress the substitution and obtain the pure external-field expression.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default wire_radius float

Wire radius \(r\) in m.

required include_internal bool

True returns \(r' = r \cdot e^{-1/4}\) (internal field folded in); False returns \(r\) unchanged.

True

Returns:

Type Description float

Effective wire radius in m.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If wire_radius is not positive.

Source code in src/groundfield/references/oeding.py 
def two_wire_loop_radius(wire_radius: float, *, include_internal: bool = True) -> float:
    """Effective wire radius $r' = r \\cdot e^{-1/4}$ used in the
    Oeding loop-inductance formulas.

    The factor $e^{-1/4}$ is the **mean geometric distance** of a
    circular cross section from itself (Anhang A.7, case 1) and
    folds the internal-field contribution
    $\\mu_0 / (8\\pi)$ into a purely geometric expression. With
    $r' = r \\cdot e^{-1/4}$ the loop self-inductance becomes
    $L'_S = (\\mu_0 / \\pi) \\ln(d/r')$, which equals
    $(\\mu_0 / \\pi)(\\ln(d/r) + 1/4)$ — Eq. (9.13c).

    Pass ``include_internal=False`` to suppress the substitution and
    obtain the pure external-field expression.

    Parameters
    ----------
    wire_radius : float
        Wire radius $r$ in m.
    include_internal : bool, default True
        ``True`` returns $r' = r \\cdot e^{-1/4}$ (internal field
        folded in); ``False`` returns $r$ unchanged.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Effective wire radius in m.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``wire_radius`` is not positive.
    """
    if wire_radius <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("wire_radius must be positive")
    if include_internal:
        return wire_radius * math.exp(-0.25)
    return wire_radius

docs.title: carson
docs.text:
Closed-form Carson 1926 reference values for the test suite.

This module collects the worked examples and tabulated values from Carson's original paper (Bell Syst. Tech. J. 5(4), 1926, pp. 539–554) plus a small set of textbook reference cases from Tleis 2008 and Oeding/Oswald 2016. They are the ground truth that the implementation in groundfield.coupling.carson must reproduce.

All values are returned in the dimensionless form \(J(p, q) = P(a, \theta) + j Q(a, \theta)\) — the bare Carson integral, without the \((\omega \mu_0 / \pi)\) pre-factor. The production code applies that pre-factor in carson_self_correction() and carson_mutual_correction().

References
  • Carson, J. R. (1926). Wave propagation in overhead wires with ground return. Bell Syst. Tech. J. 5(4), 539–554. Section V worked examples are reproduced verbatim.
  • Tleis, N. D. (2008). Power Systems Modelling and Fault Analysis, Newnes, Tab. 3.2 (P, Q values for the intermediate-\(a\) regime).
  • Oeding, D. & Oswald, B. R. (2016). Elektrische Kraftwerke und Netze, 8. Aufl., Springer, §9.4.

docs.title: earth_return
docs.text:
Carson earth-return line-impedance reference (per unit length).

Closed-form series impedance of a conductor with earth return, as derived by Carson (1926) and reproduced in every power-system textbook. It is the engineering-level (Ω/km) companion to the dimensionless Carson integral tabulated in groundfield.references.carson, and the reference against which the assembled Sommerfeld/Pollaczek earth-return stack (earth_inductive_model="sommerfeld") is benchmarked in tests/test_earth_return_benchmark.py and notebooks/45_earth_return_line_impedance.ipynb.

Mathematical background

For a thin conductor of geometric mean radius \(\mathrm{GMR}\) above or below a homogeneous earth of resistivity \(\rho\), carrying a current that returns through the earth, Carson's series impedance per unit length at angular frequency \(\omega = 2\pi f\) is

\[ Z'_\text{self} = \underbrace{\frac{\omega\mu_0}{8}}_{R'_\text{earth}} + j\,\frac{\omega\mu_0}{2\pi}\,\ln\!\frac{D_e}{\mathrm{GMR}}, \qquad Z'_\text{mutual} = \frac{\omega\mu_0}{8} + j\,\frac{\omega\mu_0}{2\pi}\,\ln\!\frac{D_e}{d_{ij}}, \]

where \(d_{ij}\) is the conductor–conductor separation and

\[ D_e = 658.87\,\sqrt{\rho / f}\ \text{[m]} \]

is Carson's equivalent earth-return depth — the depth of the fictitious return conductor that reproduces the earth's inductive effect. Two features carry the physics:

  • the earth-return resistance \(R'_\text{earth} = \omega\mu_0/8\) (\(\approx 0.0493\) Ω/km at 50 Hz) is independent of the soil resistivity — it is the loss of the return current spreading through the earth;
  • the equivalent depth \(D_e \propto \sqrt{\rho/f}\) shrinks with frequency and grows with soil resistivity — a more resistive or lower-frequency earth lets the return current spread deeper and wider. The earth-return reactance \(X' = (\omega\mu_0/2\pi)\ln(D_e/\mathrm{GMR})\) therefore increases with soil resistivity and also increases with frequency: the \(\omega\) prefactor dominates the shrinking logarithm, so \(X'\) rises almost linearly with \(f\) (1000 Ω·m, GMR = 7 mm: 0.814 mΩ/m at 50 Hz → 14.39 mΩ/m at 1 kHz, a 17.7× rise over a 20× frequency step).

Internal-inductance convention (review pass 10, finding 10.46). The formulas here are external to the conductor for a given \(\mathrm{GMR}\). The assembled inductive stack of groundfield adds the DC internal inductance \(\mu_0/(8\pi)\) per metre of a solid round conductor to every self term by default (groundfield.coupling.inductance.thin_wire_self_inductance(), include_internal=True), so a like-for-like comparison uses \(\mathrm{GMR} = a\,e^{-1/4} = 0.7788\,a\); with GMR = a the stack sits 2.0–2.5 % above Carson's reactance (100 Ω·m at 50 Hz to 30 Ω·m at 1 kHz, 4 mm wire) for that reason alone. Use GMR = a together with include_internal=False. The frequency dependence of the internal impedance (skin effect) is groundfield.conductors.Conductor.internal_impedance_per_length().

References
  • Carson, J. R. (1926). Wave propagation in overhead wires with ground return. Bell Syst. Tech. J. 5(4), 539–554.
  • Tleis, N. D. (2008). Power Systems Modelling and Fault Analysis, Newnes, §3.2 (earth-return impedance, equivalent depth \(D_e\)).
  • Oeding, D. & Oswald, B. R. (2016). Elektrische Kraftwerke und Netze,
  • Aufl., Springer, §9.4.

def carson_earth_return_resistance(frequency: float) -> float:
    r"""Carson earth-return resistance per unit length :math:`\omega\mu_0/8`.

    Independent of the soil resistivity. Returns Ω/m.

    Parameters
    ----------

        Frequency in Hz. Must be positive.

        Earth-return resistance in Ω/m (:math:`\approx 4.93\times10^{-5}`
        at 50 Hz, i.e. 0.0493 Ω/km).
    """

docs.text:
carson_mutual_impedance(rho: float, frequency: float, *, separation: float) -> complex

Carson earth-return mutual impedance per unit length (Ω/m).

\(Z' = \omega\mu_0/8 + j\,(\omega\mu_0/2\pi)\ln(D_e/d)\), the per-unit-length coupling between two parallel conductors a horizontal distance separation apart, both closing through the earth. This is the impedance behind an induced voltage on a parallel measurement / pilot line — Carson's original railway-induction problem.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rho float

Soil resistivity in Ω·m. Must be positive.

required frequency float

Frequency in Hz. Must be positive.

required separation float

Conductor–conductor distance in m. Must be positive.

required

Returns:

Type Description complex

Mutual impedance \(R' + jX'\) in Ω/m.

Source code in src/groundfield/references/earth_return.py 
def carson_mutual_impedance(
    rho: float, frequency: float, *, separation: float
) -> complex:
    r"""Carson earth-return **mutual** impedance per unit length (Ω/m).

    :math:`Z' = \omega\mu_0/8 + j\,(\omega\mu_0/2\pi)\ln(D_e/d)`, the
    per-unit-length coupling between two parallel conductors a horizontal
    distance ``separation`` apart, both closing through the earth. This is
    the impedance behind an induced voltage on a parallel measurement /
    pilot line — Carson's original railway-induction problem.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rho
        Soil resistivity in Ω·m. Must be positive.
    frequency
        Frequency in Hz. Must be positive.
    separation
        Conductor–conductor distance in m. Must be positive.

    Returns
    -------
    complex
        Mutual impedance :math:`R' + jX'` in Ω/m.
    """
    _check_positive(rho=rho, frequency=frequency, separation=separation)
    omega = 2.0 * math.pi * frequency
    r_earth = omega * MU_0 / 8.0
    d_e = carson_equivalent_depth(rho, frequency)
    x = omega * MU_0 / (2.0 * math.pi) * math.log(d_e / separation)
    return complex(r_earth, x)

def carson_self_impedance(rho: float, frequency: float, *, gmr: float) -> complex:
    r"""Carson earth-return **self** impedance per unit length (Ω/m).

    :math:`Z' = \omega\mu_0/8 + j\,(\omega\mu_0/2\pi)\ln(D_e/\mathrm{GMR})`,
    the external earth-return series impedance of a single conductor (no
    internal-conductor resistance or inductance).

    Parameters
    ----------
    rho

    frequency
        Frequency in Hz. Must be positive.

        Geometric mean radius of the conductor in m: the physical wire
        radius :math:`a` for an external-inductance model, ``0.7788·a``
        to include the internal inductance of a solid round conductor
        (the convention of the assembled stack, see the module
        docstring). Must be positive.

    Returns
    -------
    complex
        Series impedance :math:`R' + jX'` in Ω/m.
    """
    _check_positive(rho=rho, frequency=frequency, gmr=gmr)

    x = omega * MU_0 / (2.0 * math.pi) * math.log(d_e / gmr)
    return complex(r_earth, x)

docs.title: pollaczek
docs.text:
Layered (Pollaczek/Sunde) earth-return line impedance reference.

The per-unit-length self and mutual impedances of conductors buried in a two-layer earth, as exact quasi-static spectral integrals. This is the layered, buried-conductor companion to groundfield.references.earth_return.carson_self_impedance(): where Carson gives the homogeneous equivalent-depth closed form, this gives the spectral integral over a stratified earth, and reduces to Pollaczek's homogeneous form for rho_1 == rho_2.

It is the analytic per-unit-length quantity that the assembled Sommerfeld/Pollaczek stack (earth_inductive_model="sommerfeld") does not expose directly — the assembled stack builds a PEEC segment inductance matrix, from which a single per-unit-length line impedance cannot be read back without an ill-defined return-path assumption. This closed integral form therefore both (a) serves callers that need a frequency- and layer-dependent series impedance belag z'(f) (e.g. a reduced nodal network of a distribution earthing system) and (b) gives groundfield an independent per-unit-length reference against which the assembled stack's earth-return reactance can be benchmarked.

Mathematical background

A line current at depth \(h\) in a two-layer earth (layer 1 of thickness \(h_1\) and resistivity \(\rho_1\) over a half-space \(\rho_2\), air above) has the quasi-static vector potential

\[ A(y, z) \propto K_0(\gamma_k R) + \int_0^\infty F(\lambda; z, h)\,\cos(\lambda y)\,d\lambda , \]

with \(\gamma_k^2 = j\omega\mu_0/\rho_k\) of the conductor's layer and \(u_k = \sqrt{\lambda^2 + \gamma_k^2}\). The spectral amplitude \(F\) follows exactly from the continuity of \(A\) and \(\partial A/\partial z\) at the soil surface and at the layer interface (Tsiamitros et al. 2005, Eq. 8). For a conductor in layer 1, with \(r_0 = (u_1-\lambda)/(u_1+\lambda)\) and \(K = (u_1-u_2)/(u_1+u_2)\),

\[ F = \frac{r_0 e^{-u_1(h+h')} + K e^{-u_1(2h_1-h-h')} + r_0 K\bigl[e^{-u_1(2h_1-h+h')} + e^{-u_1(2h_1+h-h')}\bigr]} {u_1\,\bigl(1 - r_0 K e^{-2u_1 h_1}\bigr)} , \]

and the per-unit-length self impedance is

\[ Z'_\text{self} = j\,\frac{\omega\mu_0}{2\pi}\left[ K_0(\gamma_1\,\mathrm{GMR}) + \int_0^\infty F(\lambda; h, h)\,d\lambda \right]. \]

Conductors in layer 2 and pairs in different layers use the corresponding generalised-reflection and transmission amplitudes (see _two_layer_amplitude()). For \(\rho_1 = \rho_2\) the form reduces to the homogeneous Pollaczek integral \(K_0(\gamma\,\mathrm{GMR}) - K_0(2\gamma h) + 2\int_0^\infty e^{-2hu}/(\lambda+u)\,d\lambda\).

Review pass 10 (finding 10.45) replaced two approximations of earlier releases:

  • the two-layer kernel used the surface wavenumber \(u_\text{eff}\) of the layered earth (Tagg/Sunde/Wait recursion, layered_effective_wavenumber()) in the buried exponent, \(e^{-2h u_\text{eff}}/(\lambda + u_\text{eff})\) — exact only for \(h \to 0\) or \(\rho_1 = \rho_2\); it missed the lower-interface term \(K e^{-2u_1(h_1-h)}\): \(R'\) −0.13…−0.5 % in band near an interface, −28.5 % at 1 MHz;
  • the head term was the small-argument form \(\ln(2h/\mathrm{GMR})\) of \(K_0(\gamma\,\mathrm{GMR}) - K_0(2\gamma h)\): \(R'\) −0.15 % (1 m) and −0.99 % (3 m) at 30 Ω·m, 1 kHz — more than the documented "< 0.05 %".

Both are now exact at every frequency (quasi-static) for the same cost.

Note the exponent: for a conductor buried in the earth the vertical decay of the reflected field is governed by \(u_1\), not by \(\lambda\). The Laplace kernel \(e^{-2h\lambda}\) is Carson's air kernel, valid only for a conductor above the interface; using it below the interface under-counts \(R'\) and inverts the sign of its depth dependence (fixed in 0.15.0, pass-9 F09).

Internal-inductance convention. Like groundfield.references.earth_return, this returns the earth-return series impedance, external to the conductor, for the geometric mean radius gmr: pass gmr equal to the physical wire radius \(a\) for a pure external model, or \(a\,e^{-1/4} = 0.7788\,a\) to include the DC internal inductance \(\mu_0/(8\pi)\) of a solid round conductor — the convention of the assembled inductive stack (include_internal=True, the default of groundfield.coupling.inductance.thin_wire_self_inductance()).

Limiting cases (all covered by the regression tests):

  • rho_1 == rho_2 — homogeneous Pollaczek, which matches carson_self_impedance() to well under 1 % in the reactance across 50 Hz – 1 kHz; the earth-return resistance sits slightly above \(\omega\mu_0/8\) (Carson's low-frequency, surface-return limit) and rises with burial depth and with frequency.
  • h_1 → ∞ — upper layer only; h_1 → 0 (conductor in layer 2) — lower layer only.
  • two-layer — the reactance lies within the [carson(rho_1), carson(rho_2)] bracket, weighted toward the deeper, more conductive layer at low frequency.
References
  • Pollaczek, F. (1926). Über das Feld einer unendlich langen wechselstromdurchflossenen Einfachleitung. Elektr. Nachr.-Techn. 3, 339–359.
  • Sunde, E. D. (1949). Earth Conduction Effects in Transmission Systems, Van Nostrand, §§ 3–4 (buried-conductor earth-return, layered surface impedance).
  • Wait, J. R. (1970). Electromagnetic Waves in Stratified Media, §2.
  • Tsiamitros, D. A. et al. (2005). Earth return path impedances of underground cables for the two-layer earth case. IEEE Trans. Power Delivery 20(3), 2174–2181 (Eq. 8).

docs.title: layered_effective_wavenumber
docs.text:
layered_effective_wavenumber(lam: float, rho_1: float, rho_2: float, h_1: float, omega: float) -> complex

Effective vertical wavenumber \(u_\text{eff}(\lambda)\) of a two-layer earth.

The Tagg/Sunde/Wait tanh-recursion surface term: the input wavenumber of the layered earth seen from the surface (it sets the surface reflection coefficient \((u_\text{eff}-\lambda)/ (u_\text{eff}+\lambda)\) of an overhead conductor). It is not the exponent of a buried conductor's kernel — the self and mutual impedances of this module use the exact buried amplitude since review pass 10 (finding 10.45). Reduces to the homogeneous half-space value \(u_1\) when rho_1 == rho_2, to \(u_1\) as h_1 → ∞ and to \(u_2\) as h_1 → 0. Units: 1/m.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default lam float

Spectral (Hankel) variable, 1/m.

required rho_1 float

Upper / lower layer resistivity in Ω·m.

required rho_2 float

Upper / lower layer resistivity in Ω·m.

required h_1 float

Upper-layer thickness in m.

required omega float

Angular frequency in rad/s.

required

Returns:

Type Description complex

Effective wavenumber \(u_\text{eff}\) in 1/m.

Source code in src/groundfield/references/pollaczek.py 
def layered_effective_wavenumber(
    lam: float, rho_1: float, rho_2: float, h_1: float, omega: float
) -> complex:
    r"""Effective vertical wavenumber :math:`u_\text{eff}(\lambda)` of a two-layer earth.

    The Tagg/Sunde/Wait tanh-recursion surface term: the input
    wavenumber of the layered earth seen from the **surface** (it sets the
    surface reflection coefficient :math:`(u_\text{eff}-\lambda)/
    (u_\text{eff}+\lambda)` of an overhead conductor). It is not the
    exponent of a buried conductor's kernel — the self and mutual
    impedances of this module use the exact buried amplitude since review
    pass 10 (finding 10.45). Reduces to the homogeneous half-space value :math:`u_1` when
    ``rho_1 == rho_2``, to :math:`u_1` as ``h_1 → ∞`` and to :math:`u_2`
    as ``h_1 → 0``. Units: 1/m.

    Parameters
    ----------
    lam
        Spectral (Hankel) variable, 1/m.
    rho_1, rho_2
        Upper / lower layer resistivity in Ω·m.
    h_1
        Upper-layer thickness in m.
    omega
        Angular frequency in rad/s.

    Returns
    -------
    complex
        Effective wavenumber :math:`u_\text{eff}` in 1/m.
    """
    u1 = cmath.sqrt(lam * lam + 1j * omega * MU_0 / rho_1)
    if rho_1 == rho_2:
        return u1
    u2 = cmath.sqrt(lam * lam + 1j * omega * MU_0 / rho_2)
    t = cmath.tanh(u1 * h_1)
    return u1 * (u2 + u1 * t) / (u1 + u2 * t)

docs.title: loop_impedance_conductor_earth
docs.text:
loop_impedance_conductor_earth(rho_1: float, rho_2: float, h_1: float, frequency: float, *, depth: float, gmr: float, r_internal: float) -> complex

Conductor–earth loop impedance per unit length (Ω/m), ideal termination.

The series impedance seen by a current that flows out along a buried earthing conductor — a cable PEN, a cable screen — and returns through the earth, with the earthing electrodes at both ends idealised as \(\approx 0\,\Omega\):

\[ z'_\text{loop} = \underbrace{R'_\text{internal}}_{\text{conductor}} + \underbrace{Z'_\text{earth-return}}_{\text{Pollaczek self}} = R'_\text{internal} + Z'_\text{self}(\rho_1, \rho_2, h_1, f;\, \text{depth}, \text{gmr}). \]

This is the "go along the conductor, return through the soil" loop that governs earth-fault current sharing and the reach of an earthing system connected through cable PENs / screens — the quantity a bare earth-return impedance (pollaczek_self_impedance()) does not give on its own, because it omits the conductor's own series resistance.

Convention. The earth-return term carries the external inductance and, through gmr, the conductor's internal inductance: for a solid round conductor pass gmr = 0.7788·a = a·e^{-1/4} (a the physical radius), which already includes the internal inductance \(\mu_0/(8\pi)\); for a thin tubular / wire screen pass gmr equal to the screen radius (negligible internal inductance). r_internal is the conductor's series resistance per unit length — its DC / IEC 60228 value, or a skin-corrected AC value near the top of the band. With the ideal (\(\approx 0\,\Omega\)) earthing at both ends the loop impedance of a line of length \(\ell\) is simply \(z'_\text{loop}\,\ell\); a real earthing resistance \(R_E\) at the terminations adds in series on top of that.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rho_1 float

Two-layer earth resistivities (Ω·m), upper-layer thickness (m) and frequency (Hz), exactly as in pollaczek_self_impedance(). Set rho_1 == rho_2 for a homogeneous earth.

required rho_2 float

Two-layer earth resistivities (Ω·m), upper-layer thickness (m) and frequency (Hz), exactly as in pollaczek_self_impedance(). Set rho_1 == rho_2 for a homogeneous earth.

required h_1 float

Two-layer earth resistivities (Ω·m), upper-layer thickness (m) and frequency (Hz), exactly as in pollaczek_self_impedance(). Set rho_1 == rho_2 for a homogeneous earth.

required frequency float

Two-layer earth resistivities (Ω·m), upper-layer thickness (m) and frequency (Hz), exactly as in pollaczek_self_impedance(). Set rho_1 == rho_2 for a homogeneous earth.

required depth float

Burial depth of the conductor in m. Must be positive.

required gmr float

Geometric mean radius in m — 0.7788·a for a solid round conductor, the screen radius for a tubular / wire screen. Must be positive.

required r_internal float

Conductor series resistance per unit length in Ω/m. Must be non-negative.

required

Returns:

Type Description complex

Loop series impedance \(R'_\text{loop} + jX'_\text{loop}\) in Ω/m. Multiply by the line length for the terminated loop impedance.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If rho_1, rho_2, h_1, frequency, depth or gmr is not positive and finite, or if r_internal is negative.

Notes

Earth-return path only: no mutual coupling to a parallel conductor, and no internal skin-effect model (pass a skin-corrected r_internal if that matters at the top of the band). A conductor–conductor loop (e.g. line–PEN at a fixed spacing) has its return-path reactance set by that spacing, not by the earth-return depth, and is much smaller — this function is specifically the conductor–earth loop.

Examples:

>>> import math
>>> a = math.sqrt(150e-6 / math.pi)          # 150 mm^2 solid-round radius
>>> z = loop_impedance_conductor_earth(       # NAYY PEN, 100 Ohm.m, 50 Hz
...     100.0, 100.0, 10.0, 50.0,
...     depth=0.7, gmr=0.7788 * a, r_internal=0.206e-3)
>>> round(z.real * 1e3, 3), round(z.imag * 1e3, 3)  # mOhm/m -> Ohm/km
(0.255, 0.758)
Source code in src/groundfield/references/pollaczek.py 
def loop_impedance_conductor_earth(
    rho_1: float,
    rho_2: float,
    h_1: float,
    frequency: float,
    *,
    depth: float,
    gmr: float,
    r_internal: float,
) -> complex:
    r"""Conductor–earth loop impedance per unit length (Ω/m), ideal termination.

    The series impedance seen by a current that flows out along a buried
    earthing conductor — a cable PEN, a cable screen — and returns through
    the earth, with the earthing electrodes at both ends idealised as
    :math:`\approx 0\,\Omega`:

    .. math::

        z'_\text{loop}
        = \underbrace{R'_\text{internal}}_{\text{conductor}}
          + \underbrace{Z'_\text{earth-return}}_{\text{Pollaczek self}}
        = R'_\text{internal}
          + Z'_\text{self}(\rho_1, \rho_2, h_1, f;\, \text{depth}, \text{gmr}).

    This is the "go along the conductor, return through the soil" loop that
    governs earth-fault current sharing and the reach of an earthing system
    connected through cable PENs / screens — the quantity a bare
    earth-return impedance (:func:`pollaczek_self_impedance`) does not give
    on its own, because it omits the conductor's own series resistance.

    Convention. The earth-return term carries the external inductance and,
    **through** ``gmr``, the conductor's internal inductance: for a solid
    round conductor pass ``gmr = 0.7788·a = a·e^{-1/4}`` (``a`` the physical
    radius), which already includes the internal inductance
    :math:`\mu_0/(8\pi)`; for a thin tubular / wire screen pass ``gmr`` equal
    to the screen radius (negligible internal inductance). ``r_internal`` is
    the conductor's series resistance per unit length — its DC / IEC 60228
    value, or a skin-corrected AC value near the top of the band. With the
    ideal (:math:`\approx 0\,\Omega`) earthing at both ends the loop
    impedance of a line of length :math:`\ell` is simply
    :math:`z'_\text{loop}\,\ell`; a real earthing resistance :math:`R_E` at
    the terminations adds in series on top of that.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rho_1, rho_2, h_1, frequency
        Two-layer earth resistivities (Ω·m), upper-layer thickness (m) and
        frequency (Hz), exactly as in :func:`pollaczek_self_impedance`.
        Set ``rho_1 == rho_2`` for a homogeneous earth.
    depth
        Burial depth of the conductor in m. Must be positive.
    gmr
        Geometric mean radius in m — ``0.7788·a`` for a solid round
        conductor, the screen radius for a tubular / wire screen. Must be
        positive.
    r_internal
        Conductor series resistance per unit length in Ω/m. Must be
        non-negative.

    Returns
    -------
    complex
        Loop series impedance :math:`R'_\text{loop} + jX'_\text{loop}` in
        Ω/m. Multiply by the line length for the terminated loop impedance.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``rho_1``, ``rho_2``, ``h_1``, ``frequency``, ``depth`` or
        ``gmr`` is not positive and finite, or if ``r_internal`` is
        negative.

    Notes
    -----
    Earth-return path only: no mutual coupling to a parallel conductor, and
    no internal skin-effect model (pass a skin-corrected ``r_internal`` if
    that matters at the top of the band). A conductor–conductor loop (e.g.
    line–PEN at a fixed spacing) has its return-path reactance set by that
    spacing, not by the earth-return depth, and is much smaller — this
    function is specifically the conductor–*earth* loop.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import math
    >>> a = math.sqrt(150e-6 / math.pi)          # 150 mm^2 solid-round radius
    >>> z = loop_impedance_conductor_earth(       # NAYY PEN, 100 Ohm.m, 50 Hz
    ...     100.0, 100.0, 10.0, 50.0,
    ...     depth=0.7, gmr=0.7788 * a, r_internal=0.206e-3)
    >>> round(z.real * 1e3, 3), round(z.imag * 1e3, 3)  # mOhm/m -> Ohm/km
    (0.255, 0.758)
    """
    _check_positive(
        rho_1=rho_1,
        rho_2=rho_2,
        h_1=h_1,
        frequency=frequency,
        depth=depth,
        gmr=gmr,
    )
    if r_internal < 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"r_internal must be non-negative, got {r_internal}")
    z_earth = pollaczek_self_impedance(
        rho_1,
        rho_2,
        h_1,
        frequency,
        depth=depth,
        gmr=gmr,
    )
    return complex(r_internal, 0.0) + z_earth

docs.title: pollaczek_mutual_impedance
docs.text:
pollaczek_mutual_impedance(rho_1: float, rho_2: float, h_1: float, frequency: float, *, depth_i: float, depth_j: float, separation: float) -> complex

Layered Pollaczek earth-return mutual impedance per unit length (Ω/m).

The per-unit-length coupling impedance between two parallel buried conductors — each closing its current through the earth — over a two-layer earth, in the same exact spectral form as pollaczek_self_impedance():

\[ Z'_\text{M} = j\,\frac{\omega\mu_0}{2\pi}\left[ K_0(\gamma_k d) + \int_0^\infty F(\lambda; h_i, h_j)\cos(\lambda x)\,d\lambda \right], \]

with the horizontal separation \(x\), the direct distance \(d = \sqrt{x^2 + (h_i - h_j)^2}\), \(\gamma_k\) of the common layer and the exact two-layer amplitude \(F\) (module docstring). For two conductors in different layers there is no direct \(K_0\) term and \(F\) is the transmitted amplitude. In the homogeneous case the bracket is \(K_0(\gamma d) - K_0(\gamma D) + 2\int_0^\infty e^{-(h_i+h_j)u}/(\lambda + u)\cos(\lambda x)\,d\lambda\) with \(D = \sqrt{x^2 + (h_i + h_j)^2}\).

This is the mutual (off-diagonal) counterpart of pollaczek_self_impedance(): the coupling that induces a voltage on a parallel earthing conductor / cable through the shared earth-return path — the term a self impedance alone omits. It carries no internal-conductor term (the two conductors are galvanically separate; the coupling is purely inductive through the soil), so with ideal (\(\approx 0\,\Omega\)) earthing at both ends the coupling impedance of a parallel run of length \(\ell\) is \(Z'_\text{M}\,\ell\). Together with two self impedances it forms the \(2\times2\) loop impedance matrix of the coupled pair.

Limiting behaviour (covered by the tests): it reduces to the homogeneous Carson mutual impedance (carson_mutual_impedance()) when \(\rho_1 = \rho_2\) (reactance to well under 1 % at low frequency), its magnitude is below the self impedance and decays monotonically with the separation \(x\), and its two-layer reactance lies within the two homogeneous Carson bounds, deep-layer dominated at low frequency.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rho_1 float

Two-layer earth resistivities (Ω·m), upper-layer thickness (m) and frequency (Hz), as in pollaczek_self_impedance(). Set rho_1 == rho_2 for a homogeneous earth.

required rho_2 float

Two-layer earth resistivities (Ω·m), upper-layer thickness (m) and frequency (Hz), as in pollaczek_self_impedance(). Set rho_1 == rho_2 for a homogeneous earth.

required h_1 float

Two-layer earth resistivities (Ω·m), upper-layer thickness (m) and frequency (Hz), as in pollaczek_self_impedance(). Set rho_1 == rho_2 for a homogeneous earth.

required frequency float

Two-layer earth resistivities (Ω·m), upper-layer thickness (m) and frequency (Hz), as in pollaczek_self_impedance(). Set rho_1 == rho_2 for a homogeneous earth.

required depth_i float

Burial depths of the two conductors in m. Must be positive.

required depth_j float

Burial depths of the two conductors in m. Must be positive.

required separation float

Horizontal centre-to-centre distance \(x\) between the conductors in m. Must be non-negative; separation == 0 is allowed only when depth_i != depth_j (one conductor directly above the other). Coincident conductors (separation == 0 and depth_i == depth_j) are the self case — use pollaczek_self_impedance().

Returns:

Mutual series impedance \(R'_\text{M} + jX'_\text{M}\) in Ω/m.

Notes

Earth-return coupling only: quasi-static, no displacement current. The vertical decay in the soil is governed by \(u_1\), not by Carson's air kernel \(e^{-(h_i+h_j)\lambda}\). As \(x \to \mathrm{GMR}\) with \(depth_i = depth_j\) it recovers pollaczek_self_impedance().

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If rho_1, rho_2, h_1, frequency, depth_i or depth_j is not positive and finite, if separation is negative, or if the two conductors coincide (separation == 0 and depth_i == depth_j).

def pollaczek_mutual_impedance(
    rho_1: float,
    rho_2: float,
    h_1: float,
    frequency: float,
    *,
    depth_i: float,
    depth_j: float,
    separation: float,
) -> complex:
    r"""Layered Pollaczek earth-return **mutual** impedance per unit length (Ω/m).

    The per-unit-length coupling impedance between two parallel buried
    conductors — each closing its current through the earth — over a
    two-layer earth, in the same exact spectral form as
    :func:`pollaczek_self_impedance`:

    .. math::

        Z'_\text{M} = j\,\frac{\omega\mu_0}{2\pi}\left[
            K_0(\gamma_k d)
            + \int_0^\infty F(\lambda; h_i, h_j)\cos(\lambda x)\,d\lambda
        \right],

    with the horizontal separation :math:`x`, the direct distance
    :math:`d = \sqrt{x^2 + (h_i - h_j)^2}`, :math:`\gamma_k` of the common
    layer and the exact two-layer amplitude :math:`F` (module docstring).
    For two conductors in different layers there is no direct
    :math:`K_0` term and :math:`F` is the transmitted amplitude. In the
    homogeneous case the bracket is
    :math:`K_0(\gamma d) - K_0(\gamma D) + 2\int_0^\infty
    e^{-(h_i+h_j)u}/(\lambda + u)\cos(\lambda x)\,d\lambda` with
    :math:`D = \sqrt{x^2 + (h_i + h_j)^2}`.

    This is the mutual (off-diagonal) counterpart of
    :func:`pollaczek_self_impedance`: the coupling that induces a voltage on
    a parallel earthing conductor / cable through the shared earth-return
    path — the term a self impedance alone omits. It carries **no
    internal-conductor term** (the two conductors are galvanically separate;
    the coupling is purely inductive through the soil), so with ideal
    (:math:`\approx 0\,\Omega`) earthing at both ends the coupling impedance
    of a parallel run of length :math:`\ell` is :math:`Z'_\text{M}\,\ell`.
    Together with two self impedances it forms the :math:`2\times2` loop
    impedance matrix of the coupled pair.

    Limiting behaviour (covered by the tests): it reduces to the homogeneous
    Carson mutual impedance
    (:func:`~groundfield.references.earth_return.carson_mutual_impedance`)
    when :math:`\rho_1 = \rho_2` (reactance to well under 1 % at low
    frequency), its magnitude is below the self impedance and decays
    monotonically with the separation :math:`x`, and its two-layer reactance
    lies within the two homogeneous Carson bounds, deep-layer dominated at
    low frequency.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rho_1, rho_2, h_1, frequency
        Two-layer earth resistivities (Ω·m), upper-layer thickness (m) and
        frequency (Hz), as in :func:`pollaczek_self_impedance`. Set
        ``rho_1 == rho_2`` for a homogeneous earth.
    depth_i, depth_j
        Burial depths of the two conductors in m. Must be positive.
    separation
        Horizontal centre-to-centre distance :math:`x` between the
        conductors in m. Must be non-negative; ``separation == 0`` is
        allowed only when ``depth_i != depth_j`` (one conductor directly
        above the other). Coincident conductors (``separation == 0`` and
        ``depth_i == depth_j``) are the self case — use
        :func:`pollaczek_self_impedance`.

    Returns
    -------
    complex
        Mutual series impedance :math:`R'_\text{M} + jX'_\text{M}` in Ω/m.

    Notes
    -----
    Earth-return coupling only: quasi-static, no displacement current. The
    vertical decay in the soil is governed by :math:`u_1`, not by Carson's
    air kernel :math:`e^{-(h_i+h_j)\lambda}`. As :math:`x \to \mathrm{GMR}`
    with :math:`depth_i = depth_j` it recovers
    :func:`pollaczek_self_impedance`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``rho_1``, ``rho_2``, ``h_1``, ``frequency``, ``depth_i`` or
        ``depth_j`` is not positive and finite, if ``separation`` is
        negative, or if the two conductors coincide (``separation == 0``
        and ``depth_i == depth_j``).
    """
    _check_positive(
        rho_1=rho_1,
        rho_2=rho_2,
        h_1=h_1,
        frequency=frequency,
        depth_i=depth_i,
        depth_j=depth_j,
    )
    if separation < 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"separation must be non-negative, got {separation}")
    omega = 2.0 * math.pi * frequency
    x = separation
    d = math.hypot(x, depth_i - depth_j)
    if d <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(
            "coincident conductors (separation == 0 and depth_i == depth_j); "
            "use pollaczek_self_impedance for the self case"
        )
    if rho_1 == rho_2:
        rho_2, h_1 = rho_1, max(h_1, 1e3 * max(depth_i, depth_j))
    same_layer = (depth_i < h_1) == (depth_j < h_1)
    head = 0.0j
    if same_layer:
        rho_k = rho_1 if depth_i < h_1 else rho_2
        gamma = cmath.sqrt(1j * omega * MU_0 / rho_k)
        head = complex(kv(0, gamma * d))
    integral = _spectral_integral(rho_1, rho_2, h_1, omega, depth_i, depth_j, x)
    return 1j * omega * MU_0 / (2.0 * math.pi) * (head + integral)

pollaczek_self_impedance(rho_1: float, rho_2: float, h_1: float, frequency: float, *, depth: float, gmr: float) -> complex

Layered Pollaczek earth-return self impedance per unit length (Ω/m).

Exact two-layer, buried-conductor series impedance \(Z' = R' + jX'\) (quasi-static), earth-return only — no internal conductor resistance; the internal inductance is included only through gmr (see the module docstring). Reduces to Pollaczek's homogeneous form for rho_1 == rho_2 and agrees with carson_self_impedance() in the reactance.

Parameters:

Upper / lower layer resistivity in Ω·m. Must be positive. Set equal for a homogeneous earth.

required rho_2 float

required h_1 float

Upper-layer thickness in m. Must be positive (ignored when rho_1 == rho_2).

required frequency float

Frequency in Hz. Must be positive.

required depth float

Burial depth of the conductor in m. Must be positive; a depth >= h_1 places the conductor in the lower layer.

required gmr float

Geometric mean radius of the conductor in m: the physical wire radius for an external-inductance model, 0.7788·a to include the internal inductance of a solid round conductor. Must be positive.

def pollaczek_self_impedance(
    rho_1: float,
    rho_2: float,
    h_1: float,
    frequency: float,
    *,
    depth: float,
    gmr: float,
) -> complex:
    r"""Layered Pollaczek earth-return **self** impedance per unit length (Ω/m).

    Exact two-layer, buried-conductor series impedance
    :math:`Z' = R' + jX'` (quasi-static), earth-return only — no internal
    conductor resistance; the internal inductance is included only through
    ``gmr`` (see the module docstring). Reduces to Pollaczek's homogeneous
    form for ``rho_1 == rho_2`` and agrees with
    :func:`carson_self_impedance` in the reactance.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rho_1, rho_2
        Upper / lower layer resistivity in Ω·m. Must be positive. Set
        equal for a homogeneous earth.
    h_1
        Upper-layer thickness in m. Must be positive (ignored when
        ``rho_1 == rho_2``).
    frequency
        Frequency in Hz. Must be positive.
    depth
        Burial depth of the conductor in m. Must be positive; a depth
        ``>= h_1`` places the conductor in the lower layer.
    gmr
        Geometric mean radius of the conductor in m: the physical wire
        radius for an external-inductance model, ``0.7788·a`` to include
        the internal inductance of a solid round conductor. Must be
        positive.

    Returns
    -------
    complex
        Earth-return series impedance :math:`R' + jX'` in Ω/m.
    """
    _check_positive(
        rho_1=rho_1,
        rho_2=rho_2,
        h_1=h_1,
        frequency=frequency,
        depth=depth,
        gmr=gmr,
    )
    omega = 2.0 * math.pi * frequency
    if rho_1 == rho_2:
        rho_2, h_1 = rho_1, max(h_1, 1e3 * depth)  # one layer: no interface term
    rho_k = rho_1 if depth < h_1 else rho_2
    gamma = cmath.sqrt(1j * omega * MU_0 / rho_k)
    head = complex(kv(0, gamma * gmr))
    integral = _spectral_integral(rho_1, rho_2, h_1, omega, depth, depth, 0.0)
    return 1j * omega * MU_0 / (2.0 * math.pi) * (head + integral)

docs.title: Backend registry
docs.text: Every numerical backend of Engine is a registered backend (groundfield.solver.registry, ADR-0014). A registration ties a name to its solve function, its declared capabilities, an optional options model for Engine.options, and flags for deprecated aliases, experimental status and the automatic forwarding by soil model. Engine.solve resolves the name, applies the forwarding, checks the capabilities against the world before any backend code runs, calls the solve function and fills the common metadata of the result.

docs.title: Built-in backends
What the capability check does
docs.text:
A world that a backend cannot represent raises BackendCapabilityError (a subclass of ValueError and NotImplementedError) naming the backends that can: an unsupported layer count, electrodes with a concrete-shell coefficient, junction nodes, voltage sources, or an explicitly requested kernel the backend does not have. Adjacent layers of equal resistivity count as one layer.

A world that a backend solves with a documented simplification warns with BackendCapabilityWarning and solves: conductor models the backend reduces (no built-in backend since 2026.11), or a return_to terminal on a backend that returns the current through remote earth.

Solving with a deprecated alias warns with DeprecationWarning; the first solve with an experimental backend in a process warns once with ExperimentalBackendWarning. Options for a backend that will not run warn with BackendOptionsWarning.

docs.title: Registering a backend
docs.text: register_backend(name, solve_fn, capabilities=..., options_model=...) adds a backend without changing Engine.solve; the solve function has the signature solve_fn(world, engine, **options) -> FieldResult. A registered name is accepted by Engine(backend=...) and listed by available_backends().

docs.title: registry
docs.text:
Backend registry: names, capabilities, options and the solve contract.

Every numerical backend of Engine is a registered backend. A registration ties a name to

  • a solve function solve_fn(world, engine, **options) -> FieldResult;
  • the capabilities of the backend (BackendCapabilities): which soil models, conductor models and source kinds it can represent;
  • an optional options model (a BackendOptions subclass) that validates the backend-specific settings in Engine.options; the validated options are passed to the solve function as keyword arguments;
  • optional aliases, a deprecated-alias target, an experimental flag and an auto-forwarding rule by soil model.

Engine.solve resolves the requested name, applies the auto-forwarding, checks the capabilities against the world before any backend code runs, calls the solve function and fills the common metadata core of the result. Adding a backend therefore needs one register_backend() call and no change to Engine.solve.

Capability checks

A world that a backend cannot represent raises BackendCapabilityError naming the backends that can solve it:

  • the soil: homogeneous (one layer), two-layer, or n-layer (\(n \ge 3\)). Adjacent layers of equal resistivity are one layer physically, so a stack is acceptable to a backend that supports any layer count between the merged and the declared one (the check is conservative: it never rejects a world the backend could solve);
  • electrodes with a concrete-shell correction (ADR-0012);
  • leakage-free junction nodes (World.junctions) on a backend that does not build its nodal system through the shared pipeline;
  • a source kernel requested explicitly that the backend does not implement.

A world that a backend solves with a documented simplification emits BackendCapabilityWarning and solves:

  • conductor models the backend reduces (no built-in backend since 2026.11; fem treated distributed conductors as lumped branches and ignored inductance and the skin effect up to its conforming model, user decision Q37);
  • sources with a return_to electrode on a backend that returns the current through remote earth instead.
Backend options

The validated options of the backend that runs are passed as keyword arguments. Settings that several backends and the post-solve layer share are common Engine fields, not backend options: segment_length, earth_inductive_model and the Tagg / Sunde image-series controls image_max_terms / image_series_tol (consumed by image_2layer, image_nlayer, mom, mom_sommerfeld on its delegated two-layer path and solve_mutual_*, and recorded in FieldResult.metadata["series"], from which FieldResult.potential() takes them for the post-solve field evaluation; the deprecated names cim and bem run image and mom). Their single documented defaults are DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_TERMS and DEFAULT_IMAGE_SERIES_TOL. image_far_field (the form of the far images of the line kernel, "quadrupole" or "point") is read by the image family in two-layer soil and solve_mutual_* and recorded in the same place.

Deprecated aliases and experimental backends

Solving with a deprecated alias emits a DeprecationWarning that names the replacement and the earliest removal (DEPRECATION_REMOVAL). The first solve with an experimental backend in a process emits ExperimentalBackendWarning once. Neither is emitted for the internal auto-forwarding.

Since review pass 10 (10.76) cim and bem are pure deprecated aliases of image and mom (both assembled the same system as their target), image_nlayer is a deprecated name of the image auto-dispatch that keeps its own solve function, so the forwarding of image to it stays silent, and fem is experimental.

docs.title: DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_TERMS module-attribute
docs.text:
DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_TERMS = 300

Default cap on the number of Tagg / Sunde image-series terms.

One value for the engine, every layered backend and the post-solve field evaluation. The geometric tail bound |K|^(n+1)/(1-|K|) falls below the default tolerance after 277 terms for the AP1 corner soil rho_1 = 1000, rho_2 = 30 Ohm m (|K| = 0.9417), so the cap stays unused there.

docs.text:
DEFAULT_IMAGE_SERIES_TOL = 1e-06

Default stop tolerance of the Tagg / Sunde image series.

Summation ends when the geometric tail bound |K|^(n+1)/(1-|K|) falls below this value.

docs.title: BackendCapabilities dataclass
docs.text:
BackendCapabilities(soils: Set[str], conductors: Set[str] = frozenset(_CONDUCTOR_FEATURES), concrete_shells: bool = False, two_terminal_sources: bool = False, kernels: Set[str] = frozenset({'point'}), junctions: bool = False, voltage_sources: bool = False)

What a backend can represent.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default soils Set[str]

Soil layer counts the backend solves: "homogeneous" (one layer), "two_layer", "multi_layer" (three or more). Any set of names is accepted ({"homogeneous"}); the collections are stored as frozenset.

required conductors Set[str]

Conductor models the backend honours: "lumped" (a single series branch), "distributed" (discretize_segment_length set), "inductive" (inductance_model set) and "skin" (resistance_model="skin", the frequency-dependent resistance of review pass 10, 10.37; audit round 2, A2C-4). A world using a model outside this set solves with a BackendCapabilityWarning.

frozenset(_CONDUCTOR_FEATURES) concrete_shells bool

Whether the backend consumes the per-electrode concrete-shell coefficient concrete_shell_coefficient_ohm_m (ADR-0012).

False two_terminal_sources bool

Whether the backend returns a source current through Source.return_to. If not, a world with a return electrode solves with a BackendCapabilityWarning and the current returns through remote earth.

False junctions bool

Whether the backend represents leakage-free junction nodes (World.junctions): conductors ending on them and sources attached to them. A world with junctions is rejected by a backend without this capability.

Whether the backend solves impressed voltage sources (VoltageSource, modified nodal analysis; 2026.11). A world with a voltage source is rejected by a backend without this capability.

Source kernels the backend implements ("point", "line"). Empty for backends without a source kernel (volume methods); those accept any kernel setting.

docs.title: BackendCapabilityError
docs.text:
Bases: ValueError, NotImplementedError

The selected backend cannot represent the world.

Raised by Engine.solve() before any backend code runs. The message names the missing capability and the registered backends that can solve the world. The backend functions raise it as well when they are called directly with a soil model they cannot solve (solve_image with a layered soil, solve_image_2layer with a homogeneous soil, solve_image_nlayer and solve_mom with three or more distinct layers), and so does the concrete-shell guard of the backends without the shell correction: one error type for one situation (audit A1-08). TypeError is left for a world.soil that is no soil model at all.

Subclasses both ValueError and NotImplementedError, the types image_nlayer, cim, bem and the concrete-shell guard raised for the same situations in 0.15.0. Changed in 2026.11: image_2layer (homogeneous soil, layer stack) and mom (three or more layers) raised TypeError, which does not catch this error; catch BackendCapabilityError (or ValueError).

def resolve_solve_fn(self) -> SolveFunction:
    """Return the callable solve function (imports lazy references).

    Returns
    -------
    Callable
        ``solve_fn(world, engine, **options) -> FieldResult``.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        For a pure alias, which has no solve function of its own.
    """
    fn = self.solve_fn
    if fn is None:
        raise TypeError(f"Backend '{self.name}' is a pure alias.")
    if isinstance(fn, str):
        module_name, _, attr = fn.partition(":")
        return getattr(importlib.import_module(module_name), attr)
    return fn

def check_capabilities(
    resolved: ResolvedBackend,
    world: World,
    *,
    kernel: str | None = None,
    kernel_explicit: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Check that the resolved backend can represent ``world``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    resolved
        Outcome of :func:`resolve_backend`.
    world
        World to be solved.
    kernel
        Source kernel requested by the engine, if the engine has one.
    kernel_explicit
        Whether the kernel was set explicitly (a default kernel that the
        backend does not implement is replaced by the backend's own).

    Raises
    ------
    BackendCapabilityError
        If the backend cannot represent the world.

    Warns
    -----
    BackendCapabilityWarning
        If the backend solves the world with a documented
        simplification (reduced conductor model, ignored
        ``return_to``).
    """
    spec = resolved.spec
    caps = _capabilities(spec)
    label = f"'{resolved.requested}'"
    if resolved.requested != spec.name:
        label += f" (running '{spec.name}')"
    problems = _hard_problems(spec, world, kernel, kernel_explicit)
    if problems:
        capable = _capable_backends(world, kernel, kernel_explicit)
        alternatives = (
            f"Backends that can: {', '.join(capable)}."
            if capable
            else "No registered backend supports this combination."
        )
        raise BackendCapabilityError(
            f"Backend {label} cannot solve this world: "
            f"{'; '.join(problems)}. {alternatives}"
        )

    reduced = sorted(_conductor_features(world) - caps.conductors)
    if reduced:
        able = [
            f"'{n}'"
            for n in available_backends()
            if set(reduced) <= _capabilities(_REGISTRY[n]).conductors
        ]
        dc = (
            " at their DC resistance (the skin effect of resistance_model="
            "'skin' is ignored)"
            if "skin" in reduced
            else ""
        )
        warn_external(
            f"Backend '{spec.name}' does not implement the {', '.join(reduced)} "
            "conductor model(s) of this world and solves them as lumped, "
            f"purely resistive branches{dc}. Backends that implement them: "
            f"{', '.join(able)}.",
            BackendCapabilityWarning,
        )
    two_terminal = [s.name for s in world.sources if getattr(s, "return_to", None)]
    if two_terminal and not caps.two_terminal_sources:
        warn_external(
            f"Backend '{spec.name}' ignores Source.return_to (source(s) "
            f"{two_terminal}): the current returns through remote earth, not "
            "through the return electrode.",
            BackendCapabilityWarning,
        )

def effective_kernel(spec: BackendSpec, requested: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Kernel a backend uses when the engine requests ``requested``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spec
        Record of the backend that runs.
    requested
        Kernel requested by the engine, or ``None``.

    Returns
    -------
    str or None
        ``None`` for backends without a source kernel; otherwise the
        requested kernel if implemented, else the backend's own
        (``"point"`` when available).
    """
    kernels = spec.capabilities.kernels if spec.capabilities else frozenset()
    if not kernels:
        return None
    if requested in kernels:
        return requested
    return "point" if "point" in kernels else sorted(kernels)[0]

def emit_resolution_warnings(resolved: ResolvedBackend) -> None:
    """Deprecation warning for a requested alias; experimental warning once."""
    if resolved.deprecated is not None:
        warn_external(
            f"Backend name '{resolved.deprecated.name}' is deprecated; use "
            f"'{resolved.deprecated.deprecated_alias_of}' instead. The alias "
            f"will be removed no earlier than {DEPRECATION_REMOVAL}.",
            DeprecationWarning,
        )
    spec = resolved.spec
    if spec.experimental and spec.name not in _EXPERIMENTAL_WARNED:
        warn_external(
            f"Backend '{spec.name}' is experimental: its results are not "
            "validated as a cross-check and may change between releases.",
            ExperimentalBackendWarning,
        )
        # Marked after the warning, so an "error" filter raises on every
        # solve instead of only the first one.
        _EXPERIMENTAL_WARNED.add(spec.name)

def get_backend(name: str) -> BackendSpec:
    """Look up a backend by name or alias.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name
        Backend name or alias.

    Returns
    -------
    BackendSpec
        The registration record (for a deprecated alias: the alias's
        own record, whose :attr:`BackendSpec.deprecated_alias_of` names
        the replacement).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the name is unknown; the message suggests the closest
        registered name.
    """
    key = _ALIASES.get(name, name)
    spec = _REGISTRY.get(key)
    if spec is None:
        known = list(_REGISTRY) + list(_ALIASES)
        close = difflib.get_close_matches(str(name), known, n=1)
        hint = f" Did you mean '{close[0]}'?" if close else ""
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown backend '{name}'.{hint} Registered backends: "
            f"{', '.join(available_backends())}."
        )
    return spec

def register_backend(
    name: str,
    solve_fn: SolveFunction | str | None,
    *,
    capabilities: BackendCapabilities | None = None,
    options_model: type[BackendOptions] | None = None,
    aliases: Iterable[str] = (),
    deprecated_alias_of: str | None = None,
    experimental: bool = False,
    forward: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    summary: str = "",
    replace: bool = False,
) -> BackendSpec:
    """Register a backend name.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name
        Backend name as used in ``Engine(backend=name)``.
    solve_fn
        ``solve_fn(world, engine, **options) -> FieldResult``, or a lazy
        ``"package.module:function"`` reference. ``None`` registers a
        pure deprecated alias that runs ``deprecated_alias_of``.
    capabilities
        What the backend can represent. Required unless ``solve_fn`` is
        ``None`` (a pure alias inherits its target's capabilities).
    options_model
        :class:`BackendOptions` subclass for ``Engine.options[name]``.
        Its fields must be keyword arguments of ``solve_fn``.
    aliases
        Further accepted names, resolved without a warning.
    deprecated_alias_of
        Registered replacement name. Solving with ``name`` then emits a
        :class:`DeprecationWarning` naming the replacement and
        :data:`DEPRECATION_REMOVAL`. With a ``solve_fn`` the old
        implementation keeps running; without, the replacement runs.
    experimental
        Emit :class:`ExperimentalBackendWarning` on the first solve in a
        process.
    forward
        Auto-forwarding by soil model kind, e.g. ``{"two_layer":
        "image_2layer"}``. Targets are resolved at solve time.
    summary
        One-line description.
    replace
        Allow replacing an existing registration of ``name``; the name
        keeps its position in :func:`available_backends`.

    Returns
    -------
    BackendSpec
        The stored registration record.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the name is taken (and ``replace`` is false), the alias
        target is unknown or itself deprecated, or the arguments are
        inconsistent.
    """
    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or name != name.strip():
        raise ValueError(f"Backend name must be a non-empty string, got {name!r}.")
    alias_names = tuple(aliases)
    taken = [n for n in (name, *alias_names) if n in _REGISTRY or n in _ALIASES]
    if replace and name in _REGISTRY:
        own = {name, *_REGISTRY[name].aliases}
        taken = [n for n in taken if n not in own]
    if taken:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Backend name(s) {taken} already registered; pass replace=True "
            "to replace a registration."
        )
    if deprecated_alias_of is not None:
        target = _REGISTRY.get(deprecated_alias_of)
        if target is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"deprecated_alias_of={deprecated_alias_of!r} is not a "
                "registered backend."
            )
        if target.deprecated_alias_of is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Backend '{deprecated_alias_of}' is itself deprecated; "
                "point the alias at its replacement."
            )
    if solve_fn is None:
        if deprecated_alias_of is None:
            raise ValueError("solve_fn=None is only allowed for a deprecated alias.")
        if capabilities is not None or options_model is not None or forward:
            raise ValueError(
                "A pure deprecated alias inherits capabilities, options and "
                "forwarding from its target; do not pass them."
            )
    elif capabilities is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Backend '{name}' needs capabilities.")
    if options_model is not None and not (
        isinstance(options_model, type) and issubclass(options_model, BackendOptions)
    ):
        raise TypeError("options_model must be a BackendOptions subclass.")
    forward_pairs = tuple((forward or {}).items())
    bad_kinds = sorted({k for k, _ in forward_pairs} - set(_SOIL_KINDS))
    if bad_kinds:
        raise ValueError(f"forward: unknown soil model kind(s) {bad_kinds}.")

    if deprecated_alias_of is not None:
        dependants = [
            s.name for s in _REGISTRY.values() if s.deprecated_alias_of == name
        ]
        if dependants:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Backend(s) {dependants} are deprecated aliases of '{name}'; it "
                "cannot become a deprecated alias itself."
            )
    if replace and name in _REGISTRY:
        # Re-assigning the key below keeps the registration order.
        for alias in _REGISTRY[name].aliases:
            _ALIASES.pop(alias, None)
        _EXPERIMENTAL_WARNED.discard(name)
    spec = BackendSpec(
        name=name,
        solve_fn=solve_fn,
        capabilities=capabilities,
        options_model=options_model,
        aliases=alias_names,
        deprecated_alias_of=deprecated_alias_of,
        experimental=bool(experimental),
        forward=forward_pairs,
        summary=summary,
    )
    _REGISTRY[name] = spec
    for alias in alias_names:
        _ALIASES[alias] = name
    return spec

def resolve_backend(requested: str, world: World) -> ResolvedBackend:
    """Resolve aliases and the auto-forwarding for ``world``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    requested
        Backend name as given in ``Engine.backend``.
    world
        World to be solved (its soil model kind drives the forwarding).

    Returns
    -------
    ResolvedBackend
        The backend that runs; emits no warning.
    """
    first = get_backend(requested)
    deprecated = first if first.deprecated_alias_of is not None else None
    spec = _implementation(first)
    soil_kind = getattr(world.soil, "kind", None)
    target = spec.forward_target(soil_kind) if soil_kind else None
    if target is not None:
        spec = _implementation(get_backend(target))
    return ResolvedBackend(requested=requested, spec=spec, deprecated=deprecated)

def validate_options_entry(key: str, value: Any) -> tuple[str, BackendOptions]:
    """Validate one ``Engine.options`` entry.

    Parameters
    ----------
    key
        Backend name or alias.
    value
        Options model instance or mapping of option values.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple
        ``(canonical backend name, options model instance)``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For an unknown backend, a backend without options, an unknown
        option name (with a suggestion) or a wrong value type.
    """
    canonical = options_key(key)
    model = _REGISTRY[canonical].options_model
    if model is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Backend '{canonical}' has no backend-specific options. Settings "
            "shared by several backends are Engine fields: segment_length, "
            "earth_inductive_model, image_max_terms, image_series_tol."
        )
    if isinstance(value, model):
        return canonical, value
    if isinstance(value, BackendOptions):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Engine.options['{canonical}'] must be a {model.__name__}, got "
            f"{type(value).__name__}."
        )
    if not isinstance(value, Mapping):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Engine.options['{canonical}'] must be a {model.__name__} or a "
            f"mapping, got {type(value).__name__}."
        )
    unknown = [k for k in value if k not in model.model_fields]
    if unknown:
        hints = []
        for k in unknown:
            close = difflib.get_close_matches(str(k), list(model.model_fields), n=1)
            hints.append(f"'{k}'" + (f" (did you mean '{close[0]}'?)" if close else ""))
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown option(s) {', '.join(hints)} for backend '{canonical}'. "
            f"Valid options: {_describe_options(model)}."
        )
    return canonical, model.model_validate(dict(value))

This matters most for DeprecationWarning, which Python only shows by default when it is attributed to __main__.

def warn_external(message: str, category: type[Warning]) -> None:
    """Emit a warning attributed to the first frame outside the package.

    Frames inside ``groundfield`` and ``pydantic`` (model validators) and
    in the standard library's :mod:`copy` module (``copy.replace`` on
    Python >= 3.13 calls pydantic's ``__replace__``; audit R2B-06) are
    skipped, so the warning points at the user's line. This matters most
    for :class:`DeprecationWarning`, which Python only shows by default
    when it is attributed to ``__main__``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    message
        Warning text.
    category
        Warning class.
    """
    warnings.warn(
        message,
        category,
        skip_file_prefixes=(_PACKAGE_DIR, _PYDANTIC_DIR, _COPY_STEM),
    )

docs.title: Result files
docs.text: save_result(result, path) writes a FieldResult to a versioned JSON file and load_result(path) reads it back; world_fingerprint(world) is the hash of a world that every solve records in its provenance. A parameter study can therefore store each solve and later check which world, engine and package versions produced it.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
One UTF-8 JSON document (standard JSON: no NaN / Infinity tokens, no pickle) with an envelope:

{
  "format": "groundfield.result",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "written_by": "groundfield <version>",
  "provenance": {"groundfield_version": "...", "engine": {...}, "world_fingerprint": "...", "solved_at_utc": "..."},
  "result": {...}
}

result is the lossless JSON of the FieldResult: complex numbers are strings, non-finite floats of typed fields are "Infinity" / "NaN" strings, and metadata values JSON cannot express are tagged objects (arrays with dtype and shape, tuples, complex numbers). provenance repeats the solve provenance (groundfield, numpy, scipy, pydantic and Python versions, platform, engine configuration, world fingerprint, UTC time stamp) so it can be read without parsing the result.

Compatibility. load_result reads every schema version up to RESULT_SCHEMA_VERSION and raises ResultFormatError for a newer one instead of guessing. The loader reads only what the writer writes (plain numeric and string arrays with bounded size and nesting), so a file from an untrusted source cannot make it allocate arbitrary memory or construct objects. Files are written atomically; overwrite=False (default) refuses to replace an existing file.

The world is not part of the file. Save it alongside with world.model_dump_json() (exact round trip) and compare it with world_fingerprint(world) against provenance["world_fingerprint"].

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import groundfield as gf

world = gf.create_world(soil=gf.HomogeneousSoil(rho=100.0))
gf.create_electrode(world, "rod", name="g1", position=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), length=3.0)
gf.create_source(world, attached_to="g1", magnitude=1.0)
result = gf.create_engine(frequencies=[50.0, 1000.0]).solve(world)

path = gf.save_result(result, "rod.result.json")
loaded = gf.load_result(path)

assert loaded.input_impedance() == result.input_impedance()        # bit-identical
assert loaded.metadata["provenance"]["world_fingerprint"] == gf.world_fingerprint(world)

docs.title: results
docs.text:
Versioned on-disk format of a FieldResult.

A result file is one UTF-8 JSON document (standard JSON, no NaN / Infinity tokens, no pickle) with an envelope::

{
  "format": "groundfield.result",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "written_by": "groundfield <version>",
  "provenance": {...},        # FieldResult.metadata["provenance"] or null
  "result": {...}             # FieldResult JSON (lossless, see below)
}

provenance repeats the solve provenance of the result (groundfield / numpy / scipy / Python versions, platform, engine configuration, world_fingerprint and the UTC timestamp), so it can be read without parsing the result. It is null for results that were not produced by Engine.solve (hand-built results).

The result body is FieldResult.model_dump_json(), which round-trips losslessly: complex numbers are strings, non-finite floats of typed fields are "Infinity" / "NaN" strings, and the metadata uses tagged objects for values JSON cannot express (see groundfield.solver.result).

Schema versions

schema_version increases whenever a reader of the previous version could misread a file. load_result() reads every version up to RESULT_SCHEMA_VERSION and raises ResultFormatError for a newer one, instead of guessing.

The world itself is not part of the file; save it alongside with world.model_dump_json() (exact round trip) and compare it with world_fingerprint() against provenance["world_fingerprint"].

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str | PathLike[str]

required

Returns:

Raises:

Type Description ResultFormatError

If the file is not UTF-8 JSON (or nests too deeply for the JSON parser), not a groundfield result file, uses a schema version newer than RESULT_SCHEMA_VERSION, or lacks the result body.

ValidationError

If the result body does not validate as a FieldResult, including malformed tagged metadata (see groundfield.solver.result). Both error types subclass ValueError.

Notes

The reader accepts only what save_result() writes, so a file from an untrusted source cannot make it allocate more than a small multiple of the file size or create object, datetime or void arrays. No pickle is involved at any point.

Source code in src/groundfield/io/results.py 
def load_result(path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> FieldResult:
    """Read a result file written by :func:`save_result`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path
        File to read.

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        The stored result, equal to the one that was saved.

    Raises
    ------
    ResultFormatError
        If the file is not UTF-8 JSON (or nests too deeply for the JSON
        parser), not a groundfield result file, uses a schema version
        newer than :data:`RESULT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, or lacks the
        ``result`` body.
    pydantic.ValidationError
        If the ``result`` body does not validate as a
        :class:`FieldResult`, including malformed tagged metadata (see
        :mod:`groundfield.solver.result`). Both error types subclass
        :class:`ValueError`.

    Notes
    -----
    The reader accepts only what :func:`save_result` writes, so a file
    from an untrusted source cannot make it allocate more than a small
    multiple of the file size or create object, datetime or void
    arrays. No pickle is involved at any point.
    """
    source = Path(path)
    try:
        text = source.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise ResultFormatError(f"{source} is not UTF-8 text: {exc}") from exc
    try:
        payload = json.loads(text)
    except RecursionError as exc:
        raise ResultFormatError(
            f"{source} nests JSON values too deeply to be a result file."
        ) from exc
    except ValueError as exc:  # json.JSONDecodeError and over-long integers
        raise ResultFormatError(f"{source} is not a JSON file: {exc}") from exc
    if not isinstance(payload, dict) or "format" not in payload:
        raise ResultFormatError(
            f"{source} is not a groundfield result file (no 'format' key, "
            f"expected '{RESULT_FORMAT}'). Result files are written by "
            "groundfield.io.save_result; a bare FieldResult JSON loads with "
            "FieldResult.model_validate_json."
        )
    if payload["format"] != RESULT_FORMAT:
        raise ResultFormatError(
            f"{source}: format {payload['format']!r} is not {RESULT_FORMAT!r}."
        )
    version = payload.get("schema_version")
    if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool) or version < 1:
        raise ResultFormatError(
            f"{source}: invalid schema_version {version!r} (expected an integer >= 1)."
        )
    if version > RESULT_SCHEMA_VERSION:
        writer = payload.get("written_by", "a newer groundfield")
        raise ResultFormatError(
            f"{source} uses schema_version {version}, newer than the "
            f"supported {RESULT_SCHEMA_VERSION} (written by {writer}); "
            "upgrade groundfield to read it."
        )
    if "result" not in payload:
        raise ResultFormatError(f"{source} has no 'result' body.")
    return FieldResult.model_validate(payload["result"])

Write a result to a versioned JSON file.

required overwrite bool

False indent int | None

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

ValueError

Notes

Its permissions are those of a plain open(path, "w"): a new file gets 0o666 reduced by the process umask (0o644 under the usual 022), a replaced file keeps its mode.

def save_result(
    result: FieldResult,
    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    indent: int | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Write a result to a versioned JSON file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    result
        The result to store.
    path
        Target file. The parent directory must exist.
    overwrite
        Replace an existing file. Default ``False``: an existing file
        raises :class:`FileExistsError`.
    indent
        Indentation of the JSON text; ``None`` (default) writes it
        compactly.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The written path.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If ``result`` is not a :class:`FieldResult`.
    FileExistsError
        If ``path`` exists and ``overwrite`` is false.
    ValueError
        If the result holds values that cannot be stored (the message
        names the metadata key).

    Notes
    -----
    The file is written to a temporary file in the target directory and
    moved into place with :func:`os.replace`, so an interrupted write
    never leaves a truncated result file behind. Its permissions are
    those of a plain ``open(path, "w")``: a new file gets ``0o666``
    reduced by the process umask (``0o644`` under the usual ``022``), a
    replaced file keeps its mode.
    """
    if not isinstance(result, FieldResult):
        raise TypeError(
            f"save_result expects a FieldResult, got {type(result).__name__}."
        )
    target = Path(path)
    if target.exists() and not overwrite:
        raise FileExistsError(f"{target} exists; pass overwrite=True to replace it.")
    from groundfield import __version__

    body: dict[str, Any] = json.loads(result.model_dump_json())
    envelope = {
        "format": RESULT_FORMAT,
        "schema_version": RESULT_SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "written_by": f"groundfield {__version__}",
        "provenance": body.get("metadata", {}).get("provenance"),
        "result": body,
    }
    text = json.dumps(envelope, allow_nan=False, indent=indent, ensure_ascii=False)
    directory = target.parent if str(target.parent) else Path(".")
    fd, tmp_name = _create_temporary(directory, target.name)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            if target.exists():  # overwrite: keep the mode of the replaced file
                os.chmod(tmp_name, stat.S_IMODE(target.stat().st_mode))
            handle.write(text)
            handle.write("\n")
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_name, target)
    except BaseException:
        if os.path.exists(tmp_name):
            os.unlink(tmp_name)
        raise
    return target
