docs.text:
world_fingerprint(world: World) -> str

SHA-256 fingerprint of the canonical JSON of a world.

The canonical form is json.dumps(world.model_dump(mode="json"), sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")). Pydantic writes floats in their shortest round-trip form, so equal worlds give equal fingerprints, also after a JSON round trip of the world. The fingerprint depends on the world schema of the installed version: renamed or added model fields change it.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default world World

The world to fingerprint.

required

Returns:

Type Description str

"sha256:" followed by 64 hexadecimal digits.

Source code in src/groundfield/solver/result.py 
def world_fingerprint(world: World) -> str:
    """SHA-256 fingerprint of the canonical JSON of a world.

    The canonical form is ``json.dumps(world.model_dump(mode="json"),
    sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))``. Pydantic writes floats in
    their shortest round-trip form, so equal worlds give equal
    fingerprints, also after a JSON round trip of the world. The
    fingerprint depends on the world schema of the installed version:
    renamed or added model fields change it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        The world to fingerprint.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        ``"sha256:"`` followed by 64 hexadecimal digits.
    """
    canonical = json.dumps(
        world.model_dump(mode="json"), sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
    )
    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

docs.title: Soil
docs.text: Soil models describe the conducting half-space: horizontal layers with a resistivity \(\rho_i\) in Ω·m and a thickness \(h_i\) in m, below non-conducting air. Three models share one interface: HomogeneousSoil(rho=...), TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=..., rho_2=..., h_1=...) and MultiLayerSoil(layers=[SoilLayer(rho=..., h=...), ...]) with h=None for the bottom half-space.

docs.title: Mathematical and physical context
docs.text:
Below 1 kHz the soil is a quasi-static conductor. The potential obeys

\[ \nabla\cdot\bigl(\rho^{-1}(z)\,\nabla\varphi\bigr) = 0 \quad (z > 0), \qquad \partial_z\varphi = 0 \ \text{at}\ z = 0, \]

with \(\varphi\) and the normal current density \(\rho^{-1}\partial_z\varphi\) continuous at every layer interface and \(\varphi \to 0\) at remote earth. For two layers the image-series coefficient is the reflection coefficient

\[ K = \frac{\rho_2 - \rho_1}{\rho_2 + \rho_1}, \qquad |K| < 1, \]

the source is reflected into a series of images spaced \(2h_1\) apart whose strengths decay like \(K^n\) (slowly for high contrast; the AP1 corner soil \(\rho_1 = 1000\), \(\rho_2 = 30\,\Omega\,\mathrm{m}\) has \(|K| = 0.94\)). Three or more layers are solved by quadrature of the layered Green's function (mom_sommerfeld) or by the experimental fem backend; see Explanation → Engines.

Validity. Linear, isotropic, horizontally layered soil; the displacement current is neglected against the conduction current. Their ratio is \(\omega\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_r\rho\):

import math

eps_0 = 8.8541878128e-12                         # F/m
ratio = {rho: 2 * math.pi * 1e3 * eps_0 * 81 * rho for rho in (100.0, 1e3, 1e4)}
assert ratio[100.0] < 1e-3 and ratio[1e3] < 1e-2 and ratio[1e4] < 5e-2

At 1 kHz and \(\varepsilon_r = 81\) it is \(4.5\cdot10^{-4}\) for 100 Ω·m and \(4.5\cdot10^{-3}\) for 1000 Ω·m; only very resistive rock (10 kΩ·m) reaches \(4.5\cdot10^{-2}\), a limit of the quasi-static model itself. No backend reads relative_permittivity; a non-default value warns with InertConfigurationWarning.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import groundfield as gf

homogeneous = gf.HomogeneousSoil(rho=100.0)
two_layer = gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=100.0, rho_2=500.0, h_1=1.0)  # 1 m topsoil over rock
three_layer = gf.MultiLayerSoil(
    layers=[
        gf.SoilLayer(rho=80.0, h=0.5),
        gf.SoilLayer(rho=300.0, h=2.0),
        gf.SoilLayer(rho=50.0),          # bottom half-space: h=None
    ]
)

K = (two_layer.rho_2 - two_layer.rho_1) / (two_layer.rho_2 + two_layer.rho_1)
assert abs(K - 2 / 3) < 1e-12
assert three_layer.kind == "multi_layer"     # discriminator for JSON round trips

Parameters are validated on construction and on assignment: a resistivity or thickness must be finite and positive. The names resistivity and thickness of releases up to 0.15.0 still work with a DeprecationWarning (see Deprecations).

docs.title: Effective resistivity
docs.text:
A groundinsight bus carries one resistivity, its specific_earth_resistance. The AP1 catalogue of real LV networks describes a two-layer soil for that purpose by its effective resistivity, a weighted geometric mean of the two layers,

\[ \rho_\text{eff} = \rho_1^{\,1-w}\,\rho_2^{\,w} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \ln\rho_\text{eff} = (1 - w)\ln\rho_1 + w\ln\rho_2, \qquad w = w_0\left(\frac{h_1}{h_\text{ref}}\right)^{-\beta}, \]

with \(h_\text{ref} = 10\) m and weights \((w_0, \beta)\) of the electrode class (presets). The default is the AP1 calibration over all LV networks, \(w_0 = 0.13\), \(\beta = 0.8\): the weight of the lower layer falls with the thickness of the upper layer, \(w\) = 0.47, 0.23, 0.13 and 0.054 for \(h_1\) = 2, 5, 10 and 30 m. AP2 gives a bus \(\rho_\text{eff}\), so the rho of a BusType fitted in layered soil is \(\rho_\text{eff}\) of the soil it was fitted in (IO and groundinsight).

gf.effective_resistivity(soil) (or with the keywords rho_1, rho_2, h_1)

  • returns \(\rho\) itself for homogeneous soil and for a stack of equal layers, without round-off (the plain formula gives 200.00000000000003 Ω·m for \(\rho_1 = \rho_2 = 200\ \Omega\,\mathrm{m}\), \(h_1 = 10\) m);
  • reduces a MultiLayerSoil to its canonical stack (adjacent layers of equal resistivity merged, as every layered backend does) and raises ValueError for three or more distinct layers;
  • limits \(w\) to \([0, 1]\), so \(\rho_\text{eff}\) lies between \(\rho_1\) and \(\rho_2\). Without the limit \(w > 1\) for \(h_1 < h_\text{ref}\,w_0^{1/\beta}\) (0.78 m with the default weights, 0.28 … 1.34 m over the presets) and \(\rho_\text{eff}\) leaves the interval (17.9 Ω·m for \(\rho_1 = 100\), \(\rho_2 = 30\ \Omega\,\mathrm{m}\), \(h_1 = 0.5\) m); with the limit such a thin upper layer gives \(\rho_2\);
  • is bit-identical, inside the calibration range, to r1 ** (1 - w) * r2 ** w of the AP1 / AP2 scripts with the same weights.
soil = gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=1000.0, rho_2=30.0, h_1=10.0)
rho_eff = gf.effective_resistivity(soil)               # w = w0 = 0.13 at h_1 = 10 m
assert abs(rho_eff - 1000.0**0.87 * 30.0**0.13) < 1e-9 and abs(rho_eff - 633.907) < 1e-3

assert gf.effective_resistivity(gf.HomogeneousSoil(rho=200.0)) == 200.0
assert gf.effective_resistivity(rho_1=200.0, rho_2=200.0, h_1=10.0) == 200.0
assert gf.effective_resistivity(rho_1=100.0, rho_2=30.0, h_1=0.5) == 30.0  # w limited to 1
assert gf.effective_resistivity(soil, w0=0.0) == 1000.0  # w0 = 0: the upper layer

stack = gf.MultiLayerSoil(    # two-layer after merging: rho_1 = 100, h_1 = 2 + 3 m
    layers=[gf.SoilLayer(rho=100.0, h=2.0), gf.SoilLayer(rho=100.0, h=3.0), gf.SoilLayer(rho=30.0)]
)
assert gf.effective_resistivity(stack) == gf.effective_resistivity(rho_1=100.0, rho_2=30.0, h_1=5.0)

try:
    gf.effective_resistivity(three_layer)    # 80 / 300 / 50 Ohm m from the example above
except ValueError as error:
    print(error)    # effective_resistivity: the soil has 3 distinct layers (rho = 80, 300, 50 Ohm m); ...

docs.title: Presets per electrode class
docs.text:
The weights depend on the extent of the earthing system: a compact electrode in the upper layer sees less of the lower layer than an LV network with its foundation electrodes. gf.soil.EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS is a read-only mapping from a name to the weights (w0, beta) of one electrode class, all at \(h_\text{ref} = 10\) m; gf.effective_resistivity(soil, preset=...) uses them, and an explicit w0 or beta replaces that weight only.

Preset Electrode class \(w_0\) \(\beta\) "lv_network" (default) all LV networks of the AP1 catalogue (global calibration, the hand-over's method A0) 0.13 0.8 "station" the station electrode alone: 4 m × 4 m ring with three 4 m rods, no foundation electrodes, purely resistive 0.06 1.3 "lv_group_<g>_p<pp>" LV network of group \(g\) with \(pp\) % foundation electrodes table below

\((w_0, \beta)\) of "lv_group_<g>_p<pp>", fitted per group and penetration (method A, the values of the group's median network, q50):

Group p = 5 % p = 10 % p = 20 % p = 40 % 1 single objects, hamlets 0.06, 1.1 0.04, 1.6 0.04, 1.6 0.06, 1.3 2 villages 0.06, 1.4 0.10, 0.9 0.16, 0.9 0.24, 0.5 3 large villages, districts 0.12, 0.9 0.16, 0.6 0.20, 0.5 0.24, 0.4 4 dense built-up areas 0.12, 0.8 0.18, 0.6 0.28, 0.4 0.36, 0.3

An LV network belongs to a group by its perimeter equivalent \(n_U = \sum_i U_i / 40\ \mathrm{m}\) (\(U_i\) the perimeter of building \(i\)) with the thresholds 20, 100 and 250, so "lv_group_2_p10" is a village with 10 % foundation electrodes.

Provenance. The values are those of the author's AP2 hand-over (gruppen_bustypes.json and bericht_gruppen.md, generated on 2026-10-20 by gruppenbildung.py from the AP1 catalogue computed with groundfield 0.14.0). Their calibration range is that of the catalogue: \(h_1\) = 5 … 30 m, \(\rho_1\) = 30 … 1000 Ω·m, \(\rho_2\) = 30 … 200 Ω·m. They belong to that catalogue and are re-derived when it is recomputed (the author re-runs it with groundfield 2026.11). The hand-over's q10 and q90 BusTypes carry weights of their own, which are not presets.

presets = gf.soil.EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS
assert presets["lv_network"] == (0.13, 0.8) and presets["station"] == (0.06, 1.3)

soil = gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=100.0, rho_2=30.0, h_1=5.0)
network = gf.effective_resistivity(soil)                         # "lv_network": w = 0.226
station = gf.effective_resistivity(soil, preset="station")       # w = 0.06 * 0.5**-1.3 = 0.148
village = gf.effective_resistivity(soil, preset="lv_group_2_p10")  # w = 0.10 * 0.5**-0.9 = 0.187
assert abs(network - 76.1465) < 1e-4 and abs(station - 83.7050) < 1e-4 and abs(village - 79.8780) < 1e-4
assert gf.effective_resistivity(soil, preset="station", beta=0.8) == gf.effective_resistivity(soil, w0=0.06)

try:
    gf.effective_resistivity(soil, preset="statoin")
except ValueError as error:
    print(error)    # effective_resistivity: unknown preset 'statoin'. Did you mean 'station'? ...

A BusType and the bus it is paired with must use the same weights: fit the BusType of a station over \(\rho_\text{eff}\) with "station" and give its bus the same \(\rho_\text{eff}\). The exporters record the preset you name (rho_preset="station", metadata["rho_preset"]), and evaluate_spec / bustype_from_spec warn when the bus uses another one (user decision Q39, IO and groundinsight).

Validity. An empirical one-parameter description of a two-layer soil, calibrated on the AP1 catalogue; outside the calibration range it is an extrapolation, and a preset belongs to its electrode class. For the AP1 station (the ring and rods above, at 0.6 m) solved in the 39 soils of the AP1 grid, \(R = c\,\rho_\text{eff}\) with \(c\) from homogeneous soil misses the field solution by a median of 2.1 % over the 36 two-layer soils and at most 15.7 % with "station", by 5.5 % and 35.9 % with "lv_network" and by 12.4 % and 41.9 % over \(\rho_1\) (rms 5.5, 11.8 and 18.9 %); counting the three homogeneous soils, where the relation is exact, the median over all 39 soils is 1.8 % with "station" (5.0 % with "lv_network", 11.9 % over \(\rho_1\)). The LV network presets give an rms error of 5.5 % (group 1) up to 39.9 % (group 4, 40 %) there. The hand-over quotes a median of 1.7 % and a maximum of 15.7 % for the station without naming its metric; they appear to be this error over all 39 soils, computed with the point kernel at 1.5 m segments (the kernel of groundfield up to 0.15.0 and the segment length of the AP1 pipeline), which gives 1.71 % and 15.69 %. The point kernel alone changes the 36-soil median by 0.01 percentage points; the three exact soils lower the median by 0.26 (default engine) to 0.37 points. An independent thin-wire boundary-element solution of the station (audit D2B) gives the same medians to 0.01 points. For the station of the IO example (a 2 m ring and a 3 m rod at 0.8 m) swept over \(\rho_1\) at \(\rho_2 = 100\ \Omega\,\mathrm{m}\), the standard form fits to 7.5 / 2.9 / 0.6 % over \(\rho_\text{eff}\) with "station", 13.4 / 8.3 / 3.6 % with "lv_network" and 3.9 / 1.9 / 0.6 % over \(\rho_1\) for \(h_1\) = 5 / 10 / 30 m: at fixed \(\rho_2\) the constant \(k_0\) absorbs the lower layer, which favours \(\rho_1\), but a bus carries \(\rho_\text{eff}\). Check max_relative, and calibrate \((w_0, \beta)\) for systems unlike the hand-over's classes. \(\rho_\text{eff}\) is not FieldResult.soil_resistivity, which holds \(\rho_1\) of a layered soil.

docs.title: Penetration depth
docs.text:
The earth-return impedance of a cable or an overhead line is commonly written with a complex penetration depth \(p = \sqrt{\rho/(j\omega\mu_0)}\) (Dubanton; Deri et al. 1981): the earth is replaced by a perfectly conducting plane at the depth \(p\), and two parallel wires at the distances \(h_i\), \(h_j\) from the surface and the horizontal distance \(x\) couple by

\[ Z'_{ij} = \frac{j\omega\mu_0}{2\pi}\, \ln\frac{\sqrt{(h_i + h_j + 2p)^2 + x^2}}{\sqrt{(h_i - h_j)^2 + x^2}} \]

per metre (the self impedance with \(x\) the wire radius). For a layered soil, gf.penetration_depth(soil, frequencies) returns per frequency the depth \(p\) for which these homogeneous formulas reproduce the layered earth-return impedance, and the equivalent homogeneous resistivity \(\rho_\text{eq} = j\omega\mu_0 p^2\) with the same depth (complex; its modulus is the magnetotelluric apparent resistivity). \(p\) is the plane-wave surface impedance of the stack over \(j\omega\mu_0\) (transmission-line recursion from the bottom layer up), so \(e^{-2p\lambda}\) agrees with the layered surface reflection coefficient to second order in the horizontal wavenumber \(\lambda\). It is exact for homogeneous soil (\(p = 1/\gamma\), \(\rho_\text{eq} = \rho\)), tends to the layer values for thin and thick top layers, and the error vanishes at large separations; any number of layers is accepted.

import groundfield as gf

soil = gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=1000.0, rho_2=30.0, h_1=5.0)
pd = gf.penetration_depth(soil, [50.0, 1000.0])
print(pd.depth)                        # complex depth p in m, per frequency
print(abs(pd.resistivity))             # apparent resistivity in Ohm m: 30.8 / 33.5
z = pd.mutual_impedance(0.7, 0.7, 10.0)  # two cables at 0.7 m, 10 m apart, Ohm/m
hom = gf.penetration_depth(gf.HomogeneousSoil(rho=100.0), [50.0])
assert hom.resistivity[0] == 100.0

Accuracy (stream w3perf; two methods: the exact layered earth-return integral coupling.sommerfeld_inductance.per_metre_mutual_impedance, any number of layers, against the formula with the equivalent depth; the integral is within 6e-8 of the earth-return correction of an independent reference integral up to 300 m and 7e-7 at 1 km for buried pairs, 4e-8 overhead, audit W3B-08, and agrees with Carson and the two-layer Pollaczek integral). Over the 39 soils of the AP1 grid (\(\rho_1\) = 30 … 1000, \(\rho_2\) = 30 … 200 Ω·m, \(h_1\) = 5 / 10 / 30 m), 50 Hz … 1 kHz and separations of 0.1 … 1000 m, the earth-return correction (Carson's quantity, relative to the perfectly conducting image) of two wires overhead at 10 m / buried at 0.7 m is reproduced within a median of 2.2 % and at most 28.4 % / 33.4 %; the same formula in homogeneous soil, against Carson's and Pollaczek's integrals, has a median error of 2.4 % and a maximum of 12.3 % / 13.0 %. The homogeneous depth of \(\rho_1\) is off by a median of 31 % / 23 % (up to 2255 % / 2797 %), that of \(\rho_\text{eff}\) by 27 % / 20 %. The error grows with the separation and the frequency (overhead: at most 6.3 % up to 10 m, 12.7 % at 100 m and 28.4 % at 300 m at 1 kHz; 3.1 / 4.7 / 6.5 % at 50 Hz) and is largest for a conductive top layer over a resistive one (30 over 200 Ω·m, \(h_1\) = 30 m) where \(x\) approaches \(|p|\); it falls again beyond (the worst soil at 1 kHz: 15 % at 1 km, 0.05 % at 10 km) and slowly towards low frequency (12.7 % at 1 kHz, 1.4 % at 0.1 Hz for 100 m). The equivalence of the soils alone — the exact homogeneous integral at the complex \(\rho_\text{eq}\) against the layered one — is within a median of 0.4 % (at most 26 % / 29 %). Beyond two layers the error is larger (audit W3B-08; both references agree to 3e-5 %): in 300 / 50 / 2000 Ω·m (\(h\) = 2 / 20 m) at 1 kHz 8.1 / 8.4 / 14 / 44 % overhead and 5.1 / 7.8 / 16 / 46 % buried at 0.1 / 10 / 100 / 1000 m, in 50 / 500 / 20 / 1000 Ω·m (\(h\) = 2 / 3 / 50 m) 7.2 / 7.6 / 20 / 54 % and 3.9 / 7.0 / 28 / 77 %, at 50 Hz up to 9 % and 37 %. penetration_depth is a modelling aid for line-impedance formulas; the solver's earth-return models do not use it.

Frequencies are finite, positive real numbers of at least numpy.finfo(float).tiny: bool, str and complex values and subnormal numbers raise ValueError (audit W3B-11). A PenetrationDepth is a value: its arrays are read-only copies, two results with equal arrays compare equal and have equal hashes.

docs.title: soil
docs.text:
Soil models for groundfield.

This subpackage describes the propagation medium "soil": a horizontally stratified half-space below a non-conducting air half-space, described by the layer resistivities \(\rho_i\) (Ω·m) and thicknesses \(h_i\) (m). Below 1 kHz the formulation is quasi-static (conduction currents only), so the resistivities and thicknesses are the only parameters any backend reads. The solver turns them into Green's functions or image-charge coefficients.

Contents

HomogeneousSoil Uniform half-space with a single resistivity rho. TwoLayerSoil Upper layer (rho_1, thickness h_1) over a semi-infinite lower layer (rho_2). MultiLayerSoil Generic multi-layer model with arbitrarily many horizontal layers. SoilLayer Single layer (rho, thickness h; h=None for the bottom half-space) used by MultiLayerSoil. SoilModel Discriminated union of all supported soil types (kind). effective_resistivity Effective resistivity \(\rho_\text{eff} = \rho_1^{1-w}\rho_2^{w}\) of a homogeneous or two-layer soil (AP1 calibration): the rho of a groundinsight bus and of a BusType fitted in layered soil. EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS Read-only mapping of named weight presets (w0, beta) of effective_resistivity per electrode class ("lv_network", the default; "station"; "lv_group_<g>_p<pp>" of the AP2 hand-over). penetration_depth, PenetrationDepth Complex penetration depth \(p\) and equivalent resistivity of a soil with any number of layers, per frequency, for the complex-depth (Dubanton / Deri) earth-return formulas of cables and overhead lines.

Notes

The two-layer model is the primary case (parameter space: varying resistivities and layer thicknesses). Names follow the literature symbols; the pre-2026.11 names resistivity and thickness are deprecated aliases (see groundfield.soil.models).

docs.title: EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS module-attribute
docs.text:
EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS: Mapping[str, tuple[float, float]] = MappingProxyType({'lv_network': (0.13, 0.8), 'station': (0.06, 1.3), 'lv_group_1_p05': (0.06, 1.1), 'lv_group_1_p10': (0.04, 1.6), 'lv_group_1_p20': (0.04, 1.6), 'lv_group_1_p40': (0.06, 1.3), 'lv_group_2_p05': (0.06, 1.4), 'lv_group_2_p10': (0.1, 0.9), 'lv_group_2_p20': (0.16, 0.9), 'lv_group_2_p40': (0.24, 0.5), 'lv_group_3_p05': (0.12, 0.9), 'lv_group_3_p10': (0.16, 0.6), 'lv_group_3_p20': (0.2, 0.5), 'lv_group_3_p40': (0.24, 0.4), 'lv_group_4_p05': (0.12, 0.8), 'lv_group_4_p10': (0.18, 0.6), 'lv_group_4_p20': (0.28, 0.4), 'lv_group_4_p40': (0.36, 0.3)})

Weight presets name -> (w0, beta) of effective_resistivity().

A read-only mapping; the weights are dimensionless, at \(h_\text{ref} = 10\) m. "lv_network" (0.13, 0.8) is the default, the global calibration over all LV networks of the AP1 catalogue (method A0 of the AP2 hand-over). "station" (0.06, 1.3) is the station electrode alone: a 4 m × 4 m ring with three 4 m rods, no foundation electrodes, purely resistive (the hand-over quotes a median error of 1.7 % and a maximum of 15.7 %; they appear to be the error of \(R = c\,\rho_\text{eff}\) over all 39 soils of the AP1 grid, the three homogeneous ones at zero, with the point kernel at 1.5 m segments: 2.1 % median over the 36 two-layer soils with the default engine). "lv_group_<g>_p<pp>" holds the weights fitted per LV network group g and penetration pp % of foundation electrodes (method A, the values of each group's median network, q50):

group p = 5 % p = 10 % p = 20 % p = 40 % 1 0.06, 1.1 0.04, 1.6 0.04, 1.6 0.06, 1.3 2 0.06, 1.4 0.10, 0.9 0.16, 0.9 0.24, 0.5 3 0.12, 0.9 0.16, 0.6 0.20, 0.5 0.24, 0.4 4 0.12, 0.8 0.18, 0.6 0.28, 0.4 0.36, 0.3

The groups are formed by the perimeter equivalent \(n_U = \sum\) building perimeter / 40 m of an LV network, thresholds 20, 100 and 250: 1 single objects and hamlets, 2 villages, 3 large villages and districts, 4 dense built-up areas.

Provenance: the author's AP2 hand-over (gruppen_bustypes.json and bericht_gruppen.md, generated 2026-10-20 by gruppenbildung.py from the AP1 catalogue computed with groundfield 0.14.0). Calibration range of every preset: \(h_1\) = 5 … 30 m, \(\rho_1\) = 30 … 1000 Ω·m, \(\rho_2\) = 30 … 200 Ω·m. The values belong to that catalogue and are re-derived when the catalogue is recomputed; the hand-over's q10 and q90 BusTypes carry weights of their own, which are not presets.

docs.text:
Bases: _SoilBase

Homogeneous soil: a half-space of uniform resistivity.

The potential of a point current source I at depth d is the source term plus its image above the surface, \(\varphi = \frac{\rho I}{4\pi}\left(\frac{1}{r} + \frac{1}{r'}\right)\).

Name Type Description rho float

Resistivity \(\rho\) in \(\Omega\,\mathrm{m}\); finite and positive. Deprecated alias: resistivity.

relative_permittivity float

Relative permittivity \(\varepsilon_r\) (dimensionless). Default 10. Not read by any backend (quasi-static formulation); a non-default value warns.

Horizontally stratified soil with an arbitrary number of layers.

layers runs from the surface downwards. Every layer but the last has a finite thickness h; the last one is the semi-infinite bottom half-space (h=None). A single-layer stack is a valid, if roundabout, homogeneous half-space.

docs.title: PenetrationDepth dataclass
docs.text:
PenetrationDepth(frequencies: ndarray, depth: ndarray, resistivity: ndarray)

Complex penetration depth of a soil, per frequency.

A value: the three arrays are read-only copies of the given ones, two results compare equal when their arrays are equal (==), and a result is hashable (by its frequency values, so equal results have equal hashes), so it can key a dictionary or join a set (audit W3B-11). A result built directly is validated as penetration_depth() builds it: finite, positive frequencies, no NaN in the depth or the resistivity (audit W3R2B-05: f = +0.0 and -0.0 compared equal but hashed differently, and a NaN depth made x == x False).

Attributes:

Name Type Description frequencies ndarray

Frequencies in Hz, shape (n_f,).

depth ndarray

Complex penetration depth \(p\) in m, shape (n_f,): \(\sqrt{\rho/(j\omega\mu_0)}\) for homogeneous soil, the surface impedance of the stack over \(j\omega\mu_0\) for layered soil.

resistivity ndarray

Equivalent homogeneous resistivity \(\rho_\text{eq} = j\omega\mu_0 p^2\) in Ω·m, shape (n_f,), complex: real and equal to \(\rho\) for homogeneous soil; its modulus is the magnetotelluric apparent resistivity of a layered soil.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the three arrays are not one-dimensional of one length, a frequency is not finite and positive, or the depth or the resistivity holds a NaN.

docs.title: mutual_impedance
docs.text:
mutual_impedance(z_i: float, z_j: float, distance: float) -> np.ndarray

Per-metre impedance of the complex-depth formula, every frequency.

\(Z' = \frac{j\omega\mu_0}{2\pi}\ln(D'/D)\) with \(D = \sqrt{(z_i - z_j)^2 + x^2}\) and \(D' = \sqrt{(|z_i| + |z_j| + 2p)^2 + x^2}\) (see the module docstring): the mutual impedance of two parallel wires, or the self impedance of one wire with z_i == z_j and distance its radius (or GMR). Earth return and external inductance only (no internal impedance of the wire).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default z_i float

Depths of the wires in m, the groundfield convention (> 0 buried, < 0 overhead); both on one side of the surface.

required z_j float

Depths of the wires in m, the groundfield convention (> 0 buried, < 0 overhead); both on one side of the surface.

required distance float

Horizontal distance in m (> 0; the radius for a self impedance).

required

Returns:

Complex impedance in Ω/m, shape (n_f,).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

For wires on opposite sides of the surface, a non-finite input or a distance that is not positive.

def mutual_impedance(self, z_i: float, z_j: float, distance: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Per-metre impedance of the complex-depth formula, every frequency.

    $Z' = \\frac{j\\omega\\mu_0}{2\\pi}\\ln(D'/D)$ with
    $D = \\sqrt{(z_i - z_j)^2 + x^2}$ and
    $D' = \\sqrt{(|z_i| + |z_j| + 2p)^2 + x^2}$ (see the module
    docstring): the mutual impedance of two parallel wires, or the self
    impedance of one wire with ``z_i == z_j`` and ``distance`` its radius
    (or GMR). Earth return and external inductance only (no internal
    impedance of the wire).

    Parameters
    ----------
    z_i, z_j : float
        Depths of the wires in m, the groundfield convention (``> 0``
        buried, ``< 0`` overhead); both on one side of the surface.
    distance : float
        Horizontal distance in m (``> 0``; the radius for a self
        impedance).

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Complex impedance in Ω/m, shape ``(n_f,)``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For wires on opposite sides of the surface, a non-finite input
        or a distance that is not positive.
    """
    values = (float(z_i), float(z_j), float(distance))
    if not all(math.isfinite(v) for v in values) or not values[2] > 0.0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{_CALLER}: z_i, z_j must be finite and distance positive, got "
            f"{z_i!r}, {z_j!r}, {distance!r}."
        )
    if values[0] * values[1] < 0.0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{_CALLER}: the complex-depth formula needs both wires on one "
            f"side of the surface, got z_i = {z_i}, z_j = {z_j}."
        )
    a, b, x = abs(values[0]), abs(values[1]), values[2]
    direct = math.hypot(a - b, x)
    image = np.sqrt((a + b + 2.0 * self.depth) ** 2 + x * x)
    omega = 2.0 * math.pi * self.frequencies
    return 1j * omega * MU_0 / (2.0 * math.pi) * np.log(image / direct)

docs.title: effective_resistivity
docs.text:
effective_resistivity(soil: SoilModel | None = None, *, rho_1: float | None = None, rho_2: float | None = None, h_1: float | None = None, preset: str = 'lv_network', w0: float | None = None, beta: float | None = None, h_ref: float = 10.0) -> float

Effective resistivity of a homogeneous or two-layer soil in Ω·m.

\(\rho_\text{eff} = \rho_1^{\,1-w}\,\rho_2^{\,w}\) with \(w = w_0\,(h_1/h_\text{ref})^{-\beta}\) limited to \([0, 1]\); the resistivity itself for homogeneous soil. This is the rho of a BusType fitted in layered soil and the specific_earth_resistance of the matching groundinsight bus (see groundfield.soil.effective for the derivation, the limit of \(w\) and the calibration range). The weights \((w_0, \beta)\) come from a named preset of EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS; w0 or beta given explicitly replace that weight.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default soil (HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil or MultiLayerSoil)

The soil. A MultiLayerSoil is reduced to its canonical stack (adjacent layers of equal resistivity merged) and must have at most two distinct layers. Give either soil or all of rho_1, rho_2 and h_1.

None rho_1 float

Resistivity of the upper layer in Ω·m, finite and positive (keyword, instead of soil).

None rho_2 float

Resistivity of the lower half-space in Ω·m, finite and positive (keyword, instead of soil). rho_2 == rho_1 is homogeneous soil.

None h_1 float

Thickness of the upper layer in m, finite and positive (keyword, instead of soil).

None preset str

Name of the weight preset, a key of EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS: "lv_network" (default, \(w_0 = 0.13\), \(\beta = 0.8\), the AP1 calibration over all LV networks), "station" (0.06, 1.3, a station electrode alone) or "lv_group_<g>_p<pp>" (LV network group g = 1 … 4, penetration pp = 05, 10, 20, 40 % of foundation electrodes; AP2 hand-over). It supplies every weight that is not given explicitly.

'lv_network' w0 float

Weight of the lower layer at \(h_1 = h_\text{ref}\) (dimensionless, finite, \(\ge 0\)). Default None: the value of the preset (0.13 for "lv_network"). w0=0 gives the upper-layer resistivity.

None beta float

Exponent of the thickness dependence (dimensionless, finite, \(\ge 0\), so that the weight does not grow with \(h_1\)). Default None: the value of the preset (0.8 for "lv_network").

None h_ref float

Reference thickness in m, finite and positive. Default 10 m, the reference of every preset (a different h_ref changes what a preset's \(w_0\) means).

10.0

Returns:

Type Description float

\(\rho_\text{eff}\) in Ω·m, between \(\rho_1\) and \(\rho_2\).

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If both soil and numbers, or neither, are given, if a number is missing, or if soil is not a soil model.

ValueError

If preset is not a preset name (the message names the closest ones), if a number is not finite or out of range, or if the soil has three or more distinct layers.

Notes

Inside the calibration range the value is bit-identical to the AP1 / AP2 scripts' r1 ** (1 - w) * r2 ** w with the same weights; the default preset reproduces every call made before the presets existed. For a thin upper layer (\(h_1 < h_\text{ref}\,w_0^{1/\beta}\): 0.78 m for "lv_network", 1.15 m for "station") the limit \(w = 1\) gives \(\rho_2\), where the unlimited formula would leave the interval \([\rho_1, \rho_2]\).

Examples:

>>> import groundfield as gf
>>> soil = gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=100.0, rho_2=30.0, h_1=5.0)
>>> round(gf.effective_resistivity(soil), 4)  # w = 0.13 * 0.5**-0.8 = 0.226
76.1465
>>> gf.effective_resistivity(gf.HomogeneousSoil(rho=100.0))
100.0
>>> gf.effective_resistivity(rho_1=100.0, rho_2=30.0, h_1=0.5)  # w limited to 1
30.0
>>> round(gf.effective_resistivity(soil, preset="station"), 4)  # w = 0.148
83.705
Source code in src/groundfield/soil/effective.py 
def effective_resistivity(
    soil: SoilModel | None = None,
    *,
    rho_1: float | None = None,
    rho_2: float | None = None,
    h_1: float | None = None,
    preset: str = "lv_network",
    w0: float | None = None,
    beta: float | None = None,
    h_ref: float = 10.0,
) -> float:
    r"""Effective resistivity of a homogeneous or two-layer soil in Ω·m.

    $\rho_\text{eff} = \rho_1^{\,1-w}\,\rho_2^{\,w}$ with
    $w = w_0\,(h_1/h_\text{ref})^{-\beta}$ limited to $[0, 1]$; the
    resistivity itself for homogeneous soil. This is the ``rho`` of a
    BusType fitted in layered soil and the ``specific_earth_resistance`` of
    the matching groundinsight bus (see :mod:`groundfield.soil.effective`
    for the derivation, the limit of $w$ and the calibration range). The
    weights $(w_0, \beta)$ come from a named ``preset`` of
    :data:`EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS`; ``w0`` or ``beta`` given
    explicitly replace that weight.

    Parameters
    ----------
    soil : HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil or MultiLayerSoil, optional
        The soil. A :class:`~groundfield.soil.MultiLayerSoil` is reduced
        to its canonical stack (adjacent layers of equal resistivity
        merged) and must have at most two distinct layers. Give either
        ``soil`` or all of ``rho_1``, ``rho_2`` and ``h_1``.
    rho_1 : float, optional
        Resistivity of the upper layer in Ω·m, finite and positive
        (keyword, instead of ``soil``).
    rho_2 : float, optional
        Resistivity of the lower half-space in Ω·m, finite and positive
        (keyword, instead of ``soil``). ``rho_2 == rho_1`` is homogeneous
        soil.
    h_1 : float, optional
        Thickness of the upper layer in m, finite and positive (keyword,
        instead of ``soil``).
    preset : str, optional
        Name of the weight preset, a key of
        :data:`EFFECTIVE_RESISTIVITY_PRESETS`: ``"lv_network"`` (default,
        $w_0 = 0.13$, $\beta = 0.8$, the AP1 calibration over all LV
        networks), ``"station"`` (0.06, 1.3, a station electrode alone) or
        ``"lv_group_<g>_p<pp>"`` (LV network group ``g`` = 1 … 4,
        penetration ``pp`` = 05, 10, 20, 40 % of foundation electrodes;
        AP2 hand-over). It supplies every weight that is not given
        explicitly.
    w0 : float, optional
        Weight of the lower layer at $h_1 = h_\text{ref}$
        (dimensionless, finite, $\ge 0$). Default ``None``: the value of
        the preset (0.13 for ``"lv_network"``). ``w0=0`` gives the
        upper-layer resistivity.
    beta : float, optional
        Exponent of the thickness dependence (dimensionless, finite,
        $\ge 0$, so that the weight does not grow with $h_1$). Default
        ``None``: the value of the preset (0.8 for ``"lv_network"``).
    h_ref : float, optional
        Reference thickness in m, finite and positive. Default 10 m, the
        reference of every preset (a different ``h_ref`` changes what a
        preset's $w_0$ means).

    Returns
    -------
    float
        $\rho_\text{eff}$ in Ω·m, between $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If both ``soil`` and numbers, or neither, are given, if a number
        is missing, or if ``soil`` is not a soil model.
    ValueError
        If ``preset`` is not a preset name (the message names the closest
        ones), if a number is not finite or out of range, or if the soil
        has three or more distinct layers.

    Notes
    -----
    Inside the calibration range the value is bit-identical to the
    AP1 / AP2 scripts' ``r1 ** (1 - w) * r2 ** w`` with the same weights;
    the default preset reproduces every call made before the presets
    existed. For a thin upper layer
    ($h_1 < h_\text{ref}\,w_0^{1/\beta}$: 0.78 m for ``"lv_network"``,
    1.15 m for ``"station"``) the limit $w = 1$ gives $\rho_2$, where the
    unlimited formula would leave the interval $[\rho_1, \rho_2]$.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import groundfield as gf
    >>> soil = gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=100.0, rho_2=30.0, h_1=5.0)
    >>> round(gf.effective_resistivity(soil), 4)  # w = 0.13 * 0.5**-0.8 = 0.226
    76.1465
    >>> gf.effective_resistivity(gf.HomogeneousSoil(rho=100.0))
    100.0
    >>> gf.effective_resistivity(rho_1=100.0, rho_2=30.0, h_1=0.5)  # w limited to 1
    30.0
    >>> round(gf.effective_resistivity(soil, preset="station"), 4)  # w = 0.148
    83.705
    """
    # user decision Q36: the preset supplies each weight not given explicitly
    preset_w0, preset_beta = _preset_weights(preset)
    w0 = _number(preset_w0 if w0 is None else w0, "w0", positive=False, unit="")
    beta = _number(
        preset_beta if beta is None else beta, "beta", positive=False, unit=""
    )
    h_ref = _number(h_ref, "h_ref", positive=True, unit=" in m")
    numbers_given = {"rho_1": rho_1, "rho_2": rho_2, "h_1": h_1}
    if soil is None:
        missing = [name for name, value in numbers_given.items() if value is None]
        if missing:
            raise TypeError(
                f"{_CALLER}: pass either a soil model or rho_1, rho_2 and h_1; "
                f"missing {', '.join(missing)}."
            )
        soil = TwoLayerSoil(
            rho_1=_number(rho_1, "rho_1", positive=True, unit=" in Ohm m"),
            rho_2=_number(rho_2, "rho_2", positive=True, unit=" in Ohm m"),
            h_1=_number(h_1, "h_1", positive=True, unit=" in m"),
        )
    elif any(value is not None for value in numbers_given.values()):
        raise TypeError(
            f"{_CALLER}: pass either a soil model or rho_1, rho_2 and h_1, not both."
        )
    elif not isinstance(soil, (HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil, MultiLayerSoil)):
        raise TypeError(
            f"{_CALLER}: soil must be a HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil or "
            f"MultiLayerSoil, got {type(soil).__name__}; for numbers pass "
            "rho_1=..., rho_2=..., h_1=... as keywords."
        )

    # The canonical stack of the layered backends (equal layers merged, 10.48).
    from groundfield.solver._layered import as_layer_stack

    stack = as_layer_stack(soil)
    if stack.n_layers == 1:
        return float(stack.rhos[0])
    if stack.n_layers > 2:
        rhos = ", ".join(f"{float(rho):g}" for rho in stack.rhos)
        raise ValueError(
            f"{_CALLER}: the soil has {stack.n_layers} distinct layers "
            f"(rho = {rhos} Ohm m); the effective resistivity is defined for "
            "homogeneous and two-layer soil (AP1 calibration). Describe the "
            "soil by an equivalent two-layer model, or pass rho_1, rho_2 and "
            "h_1 of one explicitly."
        )
    return _two_layer_value(
        float(stack.rhos[0]), float(stack.rhos[1]), float(stack.h[0]), w0, beta, h_ref
    )

docs.title: penetration_depth
docs.text:
penetration_depth(soil: SoilModel, frequencies: float | ndarray) -> PenetrationDepth

Complex penetration depth and equivalent resistivity of a soil.

Per frequency, the complex depth \(p\) for which the homogeneous complex-depth formulas of Dubanton and Deri reproduce the earth-return impedance of the (layered) soil, and the equivalent homogeneous resistivity \(\rho_\text{eq} = j\omega\mu_0 p^2\) with the same \(p\) (see groundfield.soil.penetration for the matching, where it is exact and its accuracy). Homogeneous soil gives \(p = \sqrt{\rho/(j\omega\mu_0)}\) and \(\rho_\text{eq} = \rho\); any number of layers is accepted.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default soil (HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil or MultiLayerSoil)

The soil (reduced to its canonical stack: adjacent layers of equal resistivity merged, as in every layered backend).

required frequencies float or array_like

Frequencies in Hz: finite, positive real numbers, at least numpy.finfo(float).tiny (not bool, str or complex).

required

Returns:

Type Description PenetrationDepth

frequencies (Hz), depth \(p\) (m, complex) and resistivity \(\rho_\text{eq}\) (Ω·m, complex), one entry per frequency; PenetrationDepth.mutual_impedance() evaluates the complex-depth formula.

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If soil is not a soil model.

ValueError

If a frequency is not a finite, positive real number (bool, str and complex values are refused, not converted) or is subnormal (below numpy.finfo(float).tiny).

Notes

The recursion is the transmission-line transformation of the plane-wave surface impedance from the bottom half-space up through the layers; it is the \(\lambda \to 0\) value of the input admittance of the stack, which makes \(e^{-2p\lambda}\) agree with the layered surface reflection coefficient to second order in the horizontal wavenumber.

Examples:

>>> import groundfield as gf
>>> pd = gf.penetration_depth(gf.HomogeneousSoil(rho=100.0), [50.0])
>>> complex(pd.resistivity[0])
(100+0j)
>>> pd = gf.penetration_depth(gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=1000.0, rho_2=30.0, h_1=5.0), [50.0])
>>> round(float(abs(pd.resistivity[0])), 3)  # the lower layer dominates at 50 Hz
30.756
Source code in src/groundfield/soil/penetration.py 
def penetration_depth(
    soil: SoilModel, frequencies: float | np.ndarray
) -> PenetrationDepth:
    r"""Complex penetration depth and equivalent resistivity of a soil.

    Per frequency, the complex depth $p$ for which the homogeneous
    complex-depth formulas of Dubanton and Deri reproduce the earth-return
    impedance of the (layered) soil, and the equivalent homogeneous
    resistivity $\rho_\text{eq} = j\omega\mu_0 p^2$ with the same $p$ (see
    :mod:`groundfield.soil.penetration` for the matching, where it is exact
    and its accuracy). Homogeneous soil gives $p = \sqrt{\rho/(j\omega\mu_0)}$
    and $\rho_\text{eq} = \rho$; any number of layers is accepted.

    Parameters
    ----------
    soil : HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil or MultiLayerSoil
        The soil (reduced to its canonical stack: adjacent layers of equal
        resistivity merged, as in every layered backend).
    frequencies : float or array_like
        Frequencies in Hz: finite, positive real numbers, at least
        ``numpy.finfo(float).tiny`` (not ``bool``, ``str`` or complex).

    Returns
    -------
    PenetrationDepth
        ``frequencies`` (Hz), ``depth`` $p$ (m, complex) and ``resistivity``
        $\rho_\text{eq}$ (Ω·m, complex), one entry per frequency;
        :meth:`PenetrationDepth.mutual_impedance` evaluates the complex-depth
        formula.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If ``soil`` is not a soil model.
    ValueError
        If a frequency is not a finite, positive real number (``bool``,
        ``str`` and complex values are refused, not converted) or is
        subnormal (below ``numpy.finfo(float).tiny``).

    Notes
    -----
    The recursion is the transmission-line transformation of the plane-wave
    surface impedance from the bottom half-space up through the layers; it
    is the $\lambda \to 0$ value of the input admittance of the stack, which
    makes $e^{-2p\lambda}$ agree with the layered surface reflection
    coefficient to second order in the horizontal wavenumber.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import groundfield as gf
    >>> pd = gf.penetration_depth(gf.HomogeneousSoil(rho=100.0), [50.0])
    >>> complex(pd.resistivity[0])
    (100+0j)
    >>> pd = gf.penetration_depth(gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=1000.0, rho_2=30.0, h_1=5.0), [50.0])
    >>> round(float(abs(pd.resistivity[0])), 3)  # the lower layer dominates at 50 Hz
    30.756
    """
    if not isinstance(soil, (HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil, MultiLayerSoil)):
        raise TypeError(
            f"{_CALLER}: soil must be a HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil or "
            f"MultiLayerSoil, got {type(soil).__name__}."
        )
    f = _frequencies(frequencies)
    from groundfield.solver._layered import as_layer_stack

    stack = as_layer_stack(soil)
    rhos = [float(r) for r in stack.rhos]
    thicknesses = [float(h) for h in stack.h]
    depth = np.empty(f.size, dtype=complex)
    resistivity = np.empty(f.size, dtype=complex)
    for k, freq in enumerate(f.tolist()):
        # sqrt(j w mu0) and gamma_k = sqrt(j w mu0 / rho_k) as products of
        # square roots: j w mu0 itself is subnormal near the smallest normal
        # frequency, and sqrt(rho / (j w mu0)) overflowed to inf below about
        # 1e-303 Hz (audit W3B-11, own attack)
        root = _SQRT_J * math.sqrt(2.0 * math.pi * freq) * math.sqrt(MU_0)
        gammas = [root / math.sqrt(rho) for rho in rhos]
        p = 1.0 / gammas[-1]
        if len(rhos) == 1:
            depth[k] = p
            resistivity[k] = rhos[0]
            continue
        for g, h in zip(reversed(gammas[:-1]), reversed(thicknesses), strict=True):
            e = cmath.exp(-2.0 * g * h)
            t = (1.0 - e) / (1.0 + e)  # tanh(g h), stable for Re(g h) > 0
            p = (p + t / g) / (1.0 + g * p * t)
        depth[k] = p
        resistivity[k] = (root * p) ** 2
    return PenetrationDepth(frequencies=f, depth=depth, resistivity=resistivity)

docs.title: Solver
docs.text: The solver layer holds the numerics: the Engine (configuration and solve), the FieldResult (potentials, currents, impedances, metadata) and the multi-port functions solve_mutual_matrix / solve_mutual_field. The backends themselves are registered in the backend registry; their theory is on the engine pages.

docs.title: Mathematical and physical context
docs.text:
Every backend solves the same problem — the quasi-static potential of the electrodes in layered soil, coupled to the conductor network — for each frequency of Engine.frequencies. The electrodes are cut into \(N\) segments (length at most segment_length) carrying leakage currents \(I_k\); the potential of segment \(i\) is

\[ \varphi_i = \sum_{k=1}^{N} G_{ik}\, I_k , \]

with \(G_{ik}\) the potential at segment \(i\) per unit current on segment \(k\) (the Green's function of the layered half-space integrated over the segments). The galvanic clusters are equipotential, the conductor branches add Kirchhoff's laws, and the source currents are the right-hand side of the augmented system. The backends differ in how they evaluate \(G\) and which current ansatz they use:

Backend Green's function Current ansatz image free space + surface image, closed form uniform current per unit length on each straight wire of an electrode (one unknown per wire line of a grid, arm of a star, straight run of a polyline, and soil layer; user decision Q30); exact line-source kernel by default image_2layer Tagg/Sunde image series, closed form; layered Sommerfeld correction for wires through the interface as image mom the same closed-form kernels point matching: one unknown current per segment, midpoint point sources mom_sommerfeld numerical Sommerfeld quadrature of the layered Green's function, any number of layers as mom fem (experimental) none: conforming finite elements of the soil, axisymmetric for coaxial rods and rings, three-dimensional otherwise (fem3d extra) volume solution (axisymmetric: the electrodes as solid bodies; 3-D: smoothed line sources)

The uniform-current ansatz gives accurate impedances at low cost; near grids, stars, strip ends and bonded multi-electrode clusters its surface potentials are impedance-grade, not field-grade (see Known limitations).

Engine(backend="image"), the default, forwards a TwoLayerSoil to image_2layer and a MultiLayerSoil with at most two distinct layers to the image dispatcher; three or more layers need mom_sommerfeld. FieldResult.metadata["effective_backend"] and ["kernel"] record what ran.

docs.title: Engine settings
docs.text:
Field Default Meaning backend "image" registered backend name (see registry) frequencies [50.0] Hz; the given order is kept (a non-monotonic list warns with EngineFrequencyOrderWarning, with_frequencies(..., preserve_order=True) silences it) segment_length 0.5 maximum segment length in m kernel None None: the backend's preferred kernel ("line" for the image family); "line" or "point" explicitly; "point" reproduces the numbers of releases up to 0.15.0 earth_inductive_model "sommerfeld" earth return of inductive conductors: "sommerfeld", "carson_series", "perfect_mirror" (see Coupling) sommerfeld_assembly "tabulated" assembly of the Sommerfeld correction of inductive conductors: "tabulated" (one table of the spectral integral per pair of depth groups and frequency; default since 2026.11) or "exact" (one quadrature per segment pair, the default up to 0.15.0) max_segments None resource limit of this engine: the largest number of leakage segments and of nodal unknowns it solves, ResourceLimitError above it before anything is allocated; None takes groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT (20 000); recorded in metadata["max_segments"] warn_segments None size of the soft notice of this engine, counted like max_segments: at or above it the solve warns that it may take minutes (an info finding of diagnose); None takes groundfield.diagnostics.SOFT_LIMIT (5 000); not checked against max_segments (a notice above the hard limit never appears) image_max_terms, image_series_tol 300, 10⁻⁶ cap and stop tolerance of the Tagg/Sunde series (tail bound \(\lvert K\rvert^{n+1}/(1-\lvert K\rvert)\)) image_far_field "quadrupole" form of the far images of the line kernel in two-layer soil (Tagg/Sunde images and images of the cross-layer correction): "quadrupole" (point value plus the quadrupole term of the segment average) or "point" (point sources beyond the near-pair reach: the dense far term is left out, the near image pairs stay Galerkin integrals on both paths, audit W3R2A-01; faster; networks move by 3 · 10⁻⁶ … 4.3 · 10⁻⁴, not the result before wave 3 of the 2026.11 work); any other value raises ValueError; recorded in metadata["series"], used by FieldResult.potential and solve_mutual_*; no effect with kernel="point" or in homogeneous soil (the author's decision of 2026-11-15) options {} backend-specific settings, e.g. {"mom_sommerfeld": {"epsrel": 1e-9}} (see the backend pages for the options of each backend)

tolerance and max_iterations have no effect and are deprecated (see Deprecations).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import groundfield as gf

world = gf.create_world(soil=gf.TwoLayerSoil(rho_1=100.0, rho_2=300.0, h_1=2.0))
gf.create_electrode(world, "rod", name="a", position=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), length=3.0)
gf.create_electrode(world, "ring", name="b", center=(20.0, 0.0, 0.8), radius=2.0)
engine = gf.create_engine(frequencies=[50.0])

# Mutual grounding-impedance matrix of the two earths in one assembly:
# Z[i, j] = potential of cluster i per ampere leaking from cluster j.
Z = gf.solve_mutual_matrix(world, engine, anchors=["a", "b"])   # Ω

# The same entries from an ordinary solve with 1 A at "a":
gf.create_source(world, attached_to="a", magnitude=1.0)
result = engine.solve(world)
assert abs(Z[0, 0] - result.cluster_impedance("a")[0]) < 1e-9    # 51.40 Ω
assert abs(Z[1, 0] - result.electrode_potentials["b"][0]) < 1e-9  # 2.26 Ω
assert result.metadata["effective_backend"] == "image_2layer"

solve_mutual_matrix returns the galerkin off-diagonal (the reaction of the leakage distributions: reciprocal, and the matrix that reproduces a solve of the clusters joined by branches) for every call since 2026.11. offdiag="probe" with probe_points samples the potential at one point per cluster instead, the definition up to 0.15.0; probe points passed without it are ignored with a ProbePointsIgnoredWarning.

FieldResult.potential(points, frequency_index=0) evaluates the potential in V at arbitrary points of shape (M, 3) (homogeneous and two-layer soil), to_dataframe() returns the per-electrode table, to_dataframe("sources") the per-source table (impressed or solved current, the voltage and internal impedance of a voltage source, the input impedance), and metadata["provenance"] records the package and library versions, the engine configuration, a fingerprint of the world and the solve time stamp. Results are saved and loaded with save_result / load_result.

docs.title: engine
docs.text:
Numerical computation core (Engine).

An Engine bundles everything that is purely numerical: the chosen backend (image, MoM, FEM, ...), the frequency list, the discretisation and the backend settings. It is deliberately separated from the World, so that the same physical configuration can be run against different backends.

Backends are registered in groundfield.solver.registry, which records for each name the solve function, the declared capabilities (soil layer counts, conductor models, concrete shells, two-terminal sources, source kernels) and the backend-specific options model. The built-in backends fall into three families:

Closed-form / image-charge. image is the homogeneous-soil image-charge sum (closed form, uniform current per unit length, cheapest backend). image_2layer implements the Tagg / Sunde geometric series for two-layer soil with convergence \(|K|^n\). Both use the exact line-source kernel by default (Engine.kernel). image_nlayer (deprecated name) routes a layered soil with one or two distinct layers to image / image_2layer and rejects three or more; cim is a deprecated name of the image auto-dispatch.

Integral equation. mom solves for the segment currents by point matching (collocation) with the closed-form kernels above; mom_sommerfeld does the same with direct numerical Sommerfeld quadrature of the layered Green's function and is the only integral backend for \(n \ge 3\) layers. bem is a deprecated name of mom.

Volume PDE. fem (experimental) solves the field in the soil by conforming finite elements: an axisymmetric model for rods on one axis and rings around it, a three-dimensional one for every other world (the optional fem3d extra), described in groundfield.solver.fem.

Notes

Engine.solve() performs an automatic dispatch when backend="image" is requested: the call is forwarded to "image_2layer" if the world holds a TwoLayerSoil, and to "image_nlayer" if it holds a MultiLayerSoil. Notebooks written for the homogeneous case therefore keep working when the soil is replaced by a layered one.

Every result carries the metadata core CORE_METADATA_KEYS, filled here for all backends, next to the backend-specific keys.

docs.title: Backend module-attribute
docs.text:
Backend = Literal['image', 'image_2layer', 'image_nlayer', 'cim', 'mom', 'mom_sommerfeld', 'bem', 'fem']

Names of the built-in backends, for type hints.

The registry is the authority at runtime and also accepts registered third-party names (available_backends()). "cim", "bem" and "image_nlayer" are deprecated aliases of "image" and "mom".

docs.title: CORE_METADATA_KEYS module-attribute
docs.text:
CORE_METADATA_KEYS: tuple[str, ...] = ('backend', 'effective_backend', 'kernel', 'groundfield_version', 'frequencies', 'n_segments', 'soil_kind', 'earth_inductive_model', 'solve_time_s', 'series', 'max_segments', 'provenance')

Metadata keys that Engine.solve() writes into every result.

  • backend: Backend name as requested (Engine.backend).
  • effective_backend: Registered backend that ran, after alias resolution and the auto-forwarding by soil model.
  • kernel: Source kernel used ("point" / "line"); fem reports the kernel of the point sources of its result (the engine's, default "line"), which the field evaluation uses.
  • groundfield_version: Version of the package that solved.
  • frequencies: Frequencies in Hz, in solve order.
  • n_segments: Number of current-carrying source segments (for fem the display segments that carry the point sources of its result).
  • soil_kind: kind of the soil model ("homogeneous", "two_layer", "multi_layer").
  • earth_inductive_model: Earth model of the inductive coupling.
  • solve_time_s: Wall time of the backend call in s.
  • series: Image-series controls of the engine, {"max_terms", "tol", "far_field"}, for the post-solve field evaluation.
  • max_segments: Problem-size limit the solve was checked against (Engine.max_segments, or groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT when the engine leaves it at None); fem checks its display segments against it and limits its mesh by FemOptions.max_nodes / max_nodes_3d.
  • provenance: Versions, platform, engine configuration, world fingerprint and UTC timestamp (see groundfield.solver.result.solve_provenance()).

docs.title: DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_TERMS module-attribute
docs.text:
DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_TERMS = 300

Default cap on the number of Tagg / Sunde image-series terms.

One value for the engine, every layered backend and the post-solve field evaluation. The geometric tail bound |K|^(n+1)/(1-|K|) falls below the default tolerance after 277 terms for the AP1 corner soil rho_1 = 1000, rho_2 = 30 Ohm m (|K| = 0.9417), so the cap stays unused there.

docs.title: DEFAULT_IMAGE_SERIES_TOL module-attribute
docs.text:
DEFAULT_IMAGE_SERIES_TOL = 1e-06

Default stop tolerance of the Tagg / Sunde image series.

Summation ends when the geometric tail bound |K|^(n+1)/(1-|K|) falls below this value.

docs.title: DEFAULT_KERNEL module-attribute
docs.text:
DEFAULT_KERNEL = 'line'

Kernel an engine requests when it leaves the choice to the backend.

Applies to Engine.kernel = None, the default since 2026.11 (review pass 10, 10.28): the exact line-source kernel wherever a backend implements it (the image family), the backend's own kernel elsewhere.

docs.title: EarthInductiveModel module-attribute
docs.text:
EarthInductiveModel = Literal['perfect_mirror', 'carson_series', 'sommerfeld']

Earth-return models of the inductive coupling.

The values of Engine.earth_inductive_model:

  • "perfect_mirror": the earth as a perfect magnetic mirror (ADR-0004), a fast diagnostic baseline;
  • "carson_series": Carson's (1926) per-metre series correction for long parallel wires over homogeneous earth (ADR-0005);
  • "sommerfeld": the geometric Sommerfeld / Pollaczek integral for any geometry and any number of layers (ADR-0006), the engine's default.

docs.title: Engine
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Configuration of the numerical kernel.

Attributes:

Name Type Description backend str

Numerical method, a name registered in groundfield.solver.registry. Built in: image, image_2layer, image_nlayer, cim, mom, mom_sommerfeld, bem, fem. See the module docstring above for the family overview, and ADR-0002 for the selection heuristic. An unknown name raises with the closest registered one as suggestion.

frequencies list[float]

Frequency list in Hz. Default [50.0].

segment_length float

Maximum segment length used to discretise the geometry, in m.

max_segments int | None

Resource limit of this engine: the largest problem size it solves, counted as the number of leakage segments and as the number of unknowns of the dense nodal system (current owners, nodes and branches, every conductor sub-piece included). A world above it raises ResourceLimitError before anything of that size is allocated, in every segment backend and in solve_mutual_matrix() / solve_mutual_field. None (default) takes groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT (20 000), read at solve time; a positive integer raises or lowers the limit for this engine only (user decision Q17 of 2026.11, finding 10.06). The dense reaction matrix of \(N\) segments takes \(8N^2\) bytes (3.0 GiB at 20 000), the nodal system of \(n\) unknowns \(16n^2\) bytes; expected_segments() predicts both. The limit is recorded in FieldResult.metadata ["max_segments"]; fem checks the display segments of its result against it and limits its volume mesh by FemOptions.max_nodes / max_nodes_3d.

warn_segments int | None

Size of the soft notice of this engine, counted like max_segments: at or above it every solve emits a UserWarning that the solve time may run from seconds to minutes ("budget: ..."), and diagnose() reports it as an info finding. None (default) takes groundfield.diagnostics.SOFT_LIMIT (5 000), read at solve time; a positive integer moves the notice for this engine only, for instance up to the size a workstation solves in seconds (user decision Q31 of 2026.11). It is not checked against max_segments: a notice above the hard limit never appears, because such a world is refused first. Kept by JSON round trips, with_frequencies() and model_copy(); the provenance block of a result records the request.

tolerance, max_iterations

Deprecated, no effect (no backend reads them). A non-default value warns; both fields will be removed no earlier than 2027.5.

earth_inductive_model EarthInductiveModel

How the earth contributes to the inductive coupling between distributed-conductor segments (only effective when at least one conductor sets inductance_model = "neumann"):

  • "perfect_mirror" (ADR-0004, the pre-0.13 default) — the earth is a perfect magnetic mirror. Cheap, frequency-independent inductance assembly, but its additive image is far from the f < 1 kHz physics of buried conductors (audit finding F5); kept as a fast diagnostic baseline.
  • "carson_series" (ADR-0005) — the earth has finite conductivity. Carson 1926's per-metre earth-return correction \(\Delta Z'_\text{Carson}(\omega)\) is added to the Neumann matrix built on Carson's own baseline, the anti-parallel image (since 2026.11; up to 0.15.0 it was added to the additive perfect-mirror matrix, which roughly doubled the reactance, review pass 10, 10.20). It is tiled per metre of axial overlap, and only inside its validity domain: near-parallel pairs (\(|\cos\varphi| > 0.99\)) of near-horizontal segments (inclination below 8.1°) on one side of the surface; two conductors overlapping on one axis get the correction of touching wires. A pair across the surface has no anti-parallel baseline and couples through the field transmitted into the soil (carson_mixed_mutual_correction()). Oblique pairs and every pair and self term of a segment inclined by more than 8.1° get the Sommerfeld correction of a homogeneous earth of the same conductivity; at that boundary the result steps by the error of the per-metre model (13 % for two 1 km leads 2 m apart at 1 kHz; audit rounds 2 and 3). Asymptotically correct for long parallel wires over homogeneous earth; an approximation for short wires and for layered soil (the top layer's conductivity is used).
  • "sommerfeld" (ADR-0006, Pollaczek kernel since the 2026-07-08 audit, WP-C1) — geometric integration of the σ-dependent vector-potential Green's function over the actual segment-pair geometry, dispatched by conductor side: buried pairs carry the in-soil attenuation \(e^{-\gamma R}\) (and with it the positive earth-return resistance \(\approx \omega\mu_0/8\) per metre in the long-wire limit), overhead pairs use the air-side reflection (Carson's geometry). The Neumann matrix carries no image: the correction holds the whole earth effect, so conductors in or crossing the surface plane are solved too (since 2026.11). Supports layered earth; see sommerfeld_assembly for the assembly (tabulated by default). Limits: \(\sigma \to 0\) → free space (no image); \(\sigma \to \infty\) → screened (buried) / anti-parallel PEC image (overhead). Validated against Pollaczek's analytic \(K_0\) mutual and Carson's line impedance (tests/test_earth_return_benchmark.py). The default since 0.13.0 — the rigorous choice whenever a quantitative Z(f) matters.
image_max_terms, image_series_tol

Controls of the Tagg / Sunde image-charge series (maximum number of terms; stop tolerance on the geometric tail bound \(|K|^{n+1}/(1-|K|)\), dimensionless). Common to every layered backend that evaluates the series (image_2layer, mom, the delegated two-layer path of mom_sommerfeld; the deprecated names run these) and to solve_mutual_*; recorded in FieldResult.metadata["series"], which FieldResult.potential() uses for the post-solve field evaluation. Defaults: DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_TERMS (300) and DEFAULT_IMAGE_SERIES_TOL (1e-6).

image_far_field Literal['quadrupole', 'point']

Form of the far images of the line kernel in two-layer soil — the Tagg/Sunde images (n >= 1) and the images of the cross-layer correction beyond the near-pair reach (the author's decision of 2026-11-15):

  • "quadrupole" (default) — the far form of direct pairs: the point value plus the quadrupole term of the segment average, tapered off between 60 and 120 segment lengths of vertical distance (wave 3 of the 2026.11 work, finding 10.28).
  • "point" — point sources: the dense far term is left out. The near image pairs (within 7.5 segment lengths, a segment's own images included) stay Galerkin integrals blended into the point form, on the series and the cross-layer path alike, and so do the continuous switch (user decision D2) and the transverse distance of near image pairs. It is therefore not the result before wave 3: within the upper layer it differs from it by up to 2.3e-4 (16 house grids in 1000 / 30 Ω·m with \(h_1\) = 1.5 m, the blend of D2). Up to audit W3R2A-01 the cross-layer path kept the line form of the interface image only, so a long segment below the interface saw its own images as point sources: a 75 m strip below a 0.5 m top layer read -1.0e-3 at a segment length of 2.5 m and -58 % at 37.5 m; it is now within 1.1e-5 of its exact value at every segment length (500 / 100 and 1000 / 30 Ω·m).

Against the default, "point" moves networks by 3e-6 … 4.3e-4 (16 house grids 0.4 m above a 1000 / 10 Ω·m interface: 4.3e-4), a straight wire 0.5 m above the interface by 4e-4 and the surface potential above it by up to 0.8 %. With numba it takes 1.1 … 1.3 times the solve before wave 3 on house grids within the upper layer. On the cross-layer path it takes 0.49 … 0.94 of the default's time (0.25 … 0.54 without numba), because the Galerkin near image pairs stay: 1.5 … 2.4 times the solve before wave 3 below thin top layers, 4.3 … 4.5 times with long pieces there, and 0.91 times (0.90 without numba) on a 40-house network in 1000 / 30 Ω·m with \(h_1\) = 1.5 m, whose transformer rods reach below \(h_1\) (performance page). Any other value raises ValueError (audit W3R2A-02). No effect with kernel="point", in homogeneous soil or on backends without the line kernel. Read by the image family and solve_mutual_*, recorded in FieldResult.metadata["series"] ("far_field") and used by FieldResult.potential(); kept by JSON round trips, with_frequencies(), model_copy() and the provenance block. The name follows image_max_terms / image_series_tol, the other controls of how the image series is evaluated.

options Mapping[str, SerializeAsAny[BackendOptions] | Mapping[str, Any]]

Backend-specific settings, keyed by backend name and validated against the backend's options model: {"mom_sommerfeld": MomSommerfeldOptions(...)} (quadrature accuracy) and {"fem": FemOptions(...)} (mesh and truncation). Plain mappings are accepted and validated into the options models; unknown option names raise with a suggestion. Options for a backend other than the selected one (or one it forwards to) emit BackendOptionsWarning. Entries put into the mapping in place (engine.options["fem"] = {...}) bypass that validation; they are validated when they are read (backend_options(), solve()). The 0.15.0 flat fields sommerfeld_lambda_max_factor, sommerfeld_epsabs, sommerfeld_epsrel and sommerfeld_max_osc_panels are still accepted (constructor, JSON, attribute access and model_copy()) and mapped onto options["mom_sommerfeld"] with a DeprecationWarning (the constructor drops a value equal to the default silently, so engine JSON of 0.15.0 loads without warnings).

sommerfeld_assembly Literal['exact', 'tabulated']

Assembly of the Sommerfeld earth-return correction of inductive conductors (earth_inductive_model="sommerfeld"):

  • "tabulated" (default since 2026.11, user decision Q16) — one table of the spectral integral \(S(\rho)\) per pair of depth groups and frequency (cubic spline, 100 nodes), the outer quadrature of all segment pairs vectorised. Blocks of fewer than 64 sub-segment pairs and blocks whose \(\lambda\) grid cannot resolve their largest distance (conductors in the surface plane) keep the per-pair rule.
  • "exact" — every segment pair with its own quadrature and 24 interpolation nodes of \(S(\rho)\); the default up to 0.15.0.

On a TN network of 8 houses with an inductive PEN (78 inductive branches, four frequencies) the tabulated solve took 1.0 s CPU instead of 16.6 s, and its input impedance is within 2e-10 of two independent refined references (per-pair rule with 200 nodes, tables of 400 nodes, both with a refined \(\lambda\) grid; they agree to 2e-10), the per-pair rule within 1.2e-8. Read by every backend that assembles the inductive branches through the shared pipeline (the image family, mom, mom_sommerfeld) and by solve_mutual_*; see build_sommerfeld_correction_matrices(), method. The Sommerfeld fallback of carson_series for oblique pairs is always tabulated.

kernel Literal['point', 'line'] | None

Green's-function kernel of the image family (image, image_2layer and image_nlayer for one or two layers), also used by FieldResult.potential() and solve_mutual_matrix() / solve_mutual_field:

  • None (default since 2026.11) — the backend's preferred kernel: "line" for the image family, the backend's own kernel ("point") for every other backend. FieldResult.metadata["kernel"] records the kernel that ran.
  • "line" — every segment is a uniform line current (Galerkin form of the exact line-source potential, see groundfield.solver._line_kernel). In homogeneous soil it is exact for straight wires at any segment length. In two-layer soil the Tagg/Sunde images and the images of the cross-layer correction get the same treatment: near image pairs exact (with the transverse distance of the wire from the image, audit W3A-02), blended into the far form between six and 7.5 segment lengths, far images with the quadrupole term (image_far_field). A straight 10 m strip is within 3.6e-6 of its uniform-current resistance for ds = 0.125–2 m, not monotonically (point kernel: up to 22 %), a ring 1 cm above a 1000 / 30 Ω·m interface within 0.004 % of its exact thin-ring value, and a rod through the layer interface within 1.4e-6 of its exact two-owner value. Cost: a solve of 16 house grids (N = 1920 segments) takes 3.8 times as long as with "point" in homogeneous soil and 1.6 times in two-layer soil (\(h_1\) = 5 m) when numba is installed (it is used automatically), 5.8 and 1.4 times without it; the extra time grows with \(N^2\). The far images of a high contrast cost more: a 40-house network in 1000 / 30 Ω·m with \(h_1\) = 1.5 m takes 1.8 times the solve before wave 3 of the 2026.11 work with numba, 3.6 times without (image_far_field="point": 0.8 times).
  • "point" — each segment's current sits at its midpoint; reproduces the results of releases up to 0.15.0. Its row sums carry an error of about \(-0.23/L\), so the grounding resistance converges to a value 0.9–1.9 % below the exact uniform-current solution (review pass 10, 10.28).

An explicit "line" on a backend without the line kernel raises BackendCapabilityError. The request is carried in the value: an engine rebuilt from its JSON, from with_frequencies or from a result's provenance block runs exactly like the original.

Notes

Every field is validated on construction, on assignment (engine.frequencies = [] raises) and in model_copy() (unlike pydantic's default model_copy, which stores update unchecked). Lists mutated in place are checked when the engine solves.

Examples:

>>> eng = Engine(backend="mom_sommerfeld", options={"mom_sommerfeld": {"epsabs": 1e-8}})
>>> eng.backend_options().epsabs
1e-08

def backend_options(self, name: str | None = None) -> BackendOptions | None:
    """Options a backend runs with: the stored entry or the defaults.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name
        Backend name or alias. Default: :attr:`backend`.

    Returns
    -------
    BackendOptions or None
        The validated options model of the backend, or ``None`` for
        a backend without backend-specific options.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If an entry put into :attr:`options` in place does not
        validate (unknown backend or option name, wrong value).
    """
    key = _registry.options_key(self.backend if name is None else name)
    model = _registry.get_backend(key).options_model
    if model is None:
        return None
    stored = self._checked_options().get(key)
    return stored if stored is not None else model()

def model_copy(
    self, *, update: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, deep: bool = False
) -> Self:
    """Copy of the engine with ``update`` validated like the constructor.

    pydantic's ``model_copy`` stores ``update`` without validation; a
    deprecated flat name such as ``sommerfeld_epsrel`` was then
    shadowed by its property and silently ignored (audit A1-02), and
    an empty frequency list or a raw option mapping went through
    (A1-04).

    Parameters
    ----------
    update
        Field values to change. Validated together with the unchanged
        fields; the deprecated flat ``sommerfeld_*`` names are mapped
        onto ``options["mom_sommerfeld"]`` with a
        :class:`DeprecationWarning`.
    deep
        Deep copy instead of a shallow one.

    Returns
    -------
    Engine
        The copy (the receiver is not changed).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a key of ``update`` is not a field (with a suggestion), a
        value does not validate, or a flat name contradicts
        ``update["options"]``.

    Notes
    -----
    Only warnings that the update introduces are emitted; those of
    the unchanged fields (e.g. a non-monotonic frequency list) were
    emitted when the engine was built.
    """
    if not update:
        return super().model_copy(deep=deep)
    fields = type(self).model_fields
    unknown = [
        k for k in update if k not in fields and k not in _LEGACY_SOMMERFELD_FIELDS
    ]
    if unknown:
        key = str(unknown[0])
        raise ValueError(
            f"Engine.model_copy: {key!r} is not a field."
            f"{did_you_mean(key, fields)} Fields: {', '.join(fields)}."
        )
    changes = dict(update)
    flat = {
        _LEGACY_SOMMERFELD_FIELDS[k]: changes.pop(k)
        for k in list(changes)
        if k in _LEGACY_SOMMERFELD_FIELDS
    }
    if flat:
        changes["options"] = self._options_with_flat(
            changes.get("options", self.options), flat, explicit="options" in update
        )
    # The unchanged fields as set on this engine (not the defaults), so
    # the copy keeps pydantic's ``model_fields_set`` semantics.
    base = {name: self.__dict__[name] for name in self.model_fields_set}
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as before:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        type(self).model_validate(base)
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as after:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        copy = type(self).model_validate({**base, **changes})
    seen = {(w.category, str(w.message)) for w in before}
    for w in after:
        if (w.category, str(w.message)) not in seen:
            warn_external(str(w.message), w.category)
    return super(Engine, copy).model_copy(deep=True) if deep else copy

def solve(self, world: "World") -> FieldResult:
    """Run the simulation with the configured backend.

    Resolves :attr:`backend` in the registry, checks the backend's
    declared capabilities against ``world`` and runs it. When
    ``backend == "image"`` the backend is auto-forwarded to
    ``"image_2layer"`` for a
    :class:`~groundfield.soil.models.TwoLayerSoil` and to
    ``"image_nlayer"`` for a
    :class:`~groundfield.soil.models.MultiLayerSoil`, so notebooks
    written for the homogeneous case keep working when the soil
    model is replaced.

    The sources of ``world`` are snapshotted before the backend runs
    and restored afterwards onto the caller's objects, exactly as in
    :meth:`World.solve <groundfield.world.World.solve>`: solving
    never rewrites the input world, whichever entry point is used.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world : World
        The assembled world (soil, electrodes, conductors and at
        least one source) the backend should solve.

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        Container with per-frequency potentials, currents, cluster
        impedances, the source snapshot and metadata: the core keys
        :data:`CORE_METADATA_KEYS` (including the provenance block)
        plus the backend-specific keys.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``world.soil`` is unset, ``world`` contains no electrodes,
        fails :meth:`World.check <groundfield.world.World.check>`
        (no current source, short-circuited source, zero or non-finite
        magnitude; the same for every backend and for
        :meth:`World.solve <groundfield.world.World.solve>`),
        :attr:`backend` is not registered, :attr:`frequencies` was
        emptied or given a non-finite or negative entry in place, or
        an entry put into :attr:`options` in place does not validate.
    KeyError
        If a source terminal or conductor end names no node of
        ``world`` (:meth:`World.check <groundfield.world.World.check>`).
    BackendCapabilityError
        If the backend cannot represent the world (soil layer count,
        concrete-shell electrodes, explicitly requested kernel). The
        message names the registered backends that can.
    ResourceLimitError
        If the predicted number of segments or of nodal unknowns
        exceeds :attr:`max_segments` (default
        :data:`groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT`); raised before
        anything of that size is allocated (subclass of
        ``ValueError``).

    Warns
    -----
    BackendCapabilityWarning
        If the backend solves the world with a documented
        simplification (reduced conductor model, ignored
        ``return_to``).
    DeprecationWarning
        If :attr:`backend` is a deprecated alias.
    ExperimentalBackendWarning
        On the first solve with an experimental backend in a process.
    """
    if world.soil is None:
        raise ValueError("World has no soil model. Set one before calling solve().")
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")
    # Assignments are validated; a list mutated in place is not (A1-04).
    _check_frequency_values(self.frequencies)
    # Central validation of references and excitation (10.66) for
    # every backend and entry point, a current source included: a world
    # without one solved to zeros in fem only and raised in every other
    # backend (audit round 2, A2S-05).
    world.check()

    resolved = _registry.resolve_backend(self.backend, world)
    _log.info(
        "Engine.solve: backend=%s (running %s), n_electrodes=%d, n_freq=%d",
        self.backend,
        resolved.spec.name,
        len(world.electrodes),
        len(self.frequencies),
    )
    with _guarded_sources(world):
        return self._run(world, resolved)
