def with_frequencies(
    self,
    *frequencies: float,
    preserve_order: bool = False,
) -> "Engine":
    """Return a copy of this engine with a new ``frequencies`` list.

    Parameters
    ----------
    *frequencies
        One or more frequencies in Hz. Variadic to make the
        common case readable: ``engine.with_frequencies(50, 5000)``.
    preserve_order
        If ``True``, the frequencies are stored verbatim and no
        non-monotonic warning is raised even for a decreasing or
        duplicate-bearing list. This is the explicit opt-in for
        sweeps that require a specific iteration order. If ``False``
        (default) the standard :func:`_validate_frequencies` checks
        run.

    Returns
    -------
    Engine
        A new :class:`Engine` instance — the receiver is **not**
        mutated.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> eng = Engine(backend="image").with_frequencies(50, 5000,
    ...                                                preserve_order=True)
    >>> eng.frequencies
    [50.0, 5000.0]
    """
    freqs = [float(f) for f in frequencies]
    # The scalar contract holds for *both* paths. Checking it here
    # as well as in the validator keeps the error attributable to
    # ``with_frequencies()`` rather than to a nested model rebuild.
    _check_frequency_values(freqs)
    data = self.model_dump()
    data["frequencies"] = freqs
    if preserve_order:
        # Re-validate the rest, but suppress the field validator's
        # monotone warning — a deliberately ordered sweep is the
        # documented opt-in.
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", EngineFrequencyOrderWarning)
            return self.__class__.model_validate(data)
    # Default path: run the full field validation, including the
    # monotone-order warning. ``model_copy(update=...)`` would skip
    # every validator (pydantic v2 semantics), which is the
    # pre-0.14.1 defect. Re-emit any warning at the caller's frame
    # so the notebook line that built the engine is the one shown.
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        engine = self.__class__.model_validate(data)
    for entry in caught:
        warnings.warn(entry.message, entry.category, stacklevel=2)
    return engine

docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Engine.frequencies is not strictly monotonically increasing.

A dedicated category for the monotonic-order warning emitted by Engine._validate_frequencies(). Using a dedicated class lets notebook authors silence the diagnostic with a stable warnings.simplefilter("once", EngineFrequencyOrderWarning) — the default UserWarning filter deduplicates by message text, and because the message embeds the offending list literal, every distinct non-monotonic list triggers a fresh warning even when the underlying convention is the same.

docs.title: result
docs.text:
Result object of a simulation run.

A FieldResult is the unified return value of Engine.solve() and World.solve(). It contains:

  • electrode_potentials / electrode_currents — node values per frequency, used to derive input and transfer impedances.
  • point_sources — the discretised current distribution. The post-processing layer can use these to evaluate the potential at arbitrary field points (contour plots, profiles, touch and step voltages).
  • soil_resistivity and soil — provide the parameters needed to evaluate the appropriate Green's function (homogeneous or 2-layer) inside potential().
  • sources — the source snapshot of the solve, read by FieldResult.input_impedance(): the impressed current of every current source; the impressed voltage and the solved current of every voltage source.
  • metadata — the core keys every backend reports (see groundfield.solver.engine.CORE_METADATA_KEYS), including the provenance block, plus backend-specific keys.
Serialisation

model_dump_json / model_validate_json round-trip a result losslessly and produce standard JSON (no NaN / Infinity tokens). Values that JSON cannot express in metadata are written as single-key tagged objects and restored on validation:

  • {"$float": "inf" | "-inf" | "nan"} — non-finite float;
  • {"$complex": [re, im]} — complex number;
  • {"$tuple": [...]} — tuple;
  • {"$dict": [[key, value], ...]} — mapping with non-string keys (e.g. penetration_depth keyed by frequency) or with a key that looks like a tag;
  • {"$ndarray": {"dtype": ..., "shape": [...], "data": [...]}} — numpy array (bool, integer, float, complex or string dtype).

numpy scalars are stored as the equal Python scalar. The tag names are reserved: a metadata value that is a single-key mapping with one of the keys above is decoded on validation. The versioned file format around this JSON is groundfield.io.save_result() / groundfield.io.load_result().

The decoder reads only what the encoder writes, so a result file from an untrusted source cannot allocate more memory than a small multiple of its own size: $ndarray dtypes are limited to bool, integer, float16 … float64, complex64 / complex128 and unicode strings (no object, datetime, void, structured or sub-array dtypes); the shape must match the number of items before anything is allocated; every item must be a scalar of the dtype's kind; a string array may take at most 64 bytes per character of its items (plus 4 KiB); and metadata may nest at most MAX_METADATA_DEPTH levels. A tag that breaks these rules raises ValueError naming the metadata key (a pydantic.ValidationError when it is read through validation). The encoder applies the same limits, so every file it writes loads.

docs.title: cluster_impedance
docs.text:
cluster_impedance(electrode_name: str) -> list[complex]

Grounding impedance of the galvanic cluster containing an electrode.

Definition: \(Z_{\text{cluster}}(f) = \varphi_{\text{cluster}}/\sum_{e \in c} I_e\). For a stand-alone electrode this is identical to grounding_impedance(). For connected electrodes it corresponds to the parallel combination of the individual grounding admittances.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default electrode_name str

Name of any electrode in the target cluster. The cluster members are looked up in clusters; if the electrode does not appear there it is treated as a stand-alone cluster [electrode_name].

required

Returns:

Type Description list[complex]

Complex cluster impedance per frequency in ohms, one entry per entry in frequencies. Frequencies for which the summed cluster current is exactly zero return nan.

Raises:

Type Description KeyError

If the resolved cluster is empty, or if none of its members carries potential and current data.

Notes

The cluster potential is the length-weighted (Galerkin) average over all members,

\[ \varphi_c \;=\; \frac{\sum_{e \in c} L_e\, \varphi_e} {\sum_{e \in c} L_e}, \qquad L_e = \sum_{k \in e} L_k , \]

with the per-electrode lengths taken from point_sources. Since every member potential \(\varphi_e\) is itself the length-weighted average over that electrode's segments, \(\varphi_c\) is exactly the length-weighted average over the whole cluster surface — the quantity the augmented system constrains to one value (see solver/image.py, block 1 of the multi-port system).

Up to 0.14.1 this method read members[0], i.e. the alphabetically first member name. Because the reported member potentials were unweighted segment means they did not agree with each other, so renaming an electrode changed the reported cluster impedance of an unchanged geometry (19.4393 Ω → 19.2314 Ω in the audit case, 2026-07-28, F11). With the weighted reduction the members agree to round-off for the image family and the result is invariant under renaming for every backend.

Numerator and denominator run over different member sets, deliberately:

  • \(\varphi_c\) averages over members that carry both potential and current data — a member with no potential cannot contribute a term to the average.
  • \(\sum_e I_e\) sums over every member that carries current data, whether or not its potential was stored, because its injected current is part of the cluster total regardless.

Every backend in this package populates both mappings for every member, so the two sets coincide in practice. They differ only for hand-built FieldResult instances, where restricting the current sum to the potential-carrying members would silently under-count the cluster current (audit 2026-07-29).

def cluster_impedance(self, electrode_name: str) -> list[complex]:
    """Grounding impedance of the galvanic cluster containing an electrode.

    Definition: $Z_{\\text{cluster}}(f) =
    \\varphi_{\\text{cluster}}/\\sum_{e \\in c} I_e$. For a
    stand-alone electrode this is identical to
    :meth:`grounding_impedance`. For connected electrodes it
    corresponds to the parallel combination of the individual
    grounding admittances.

    Parameters
    ----------
    electrode_name : str
        Name of any electrode in the target cluster. The cluster
        members are looked up in :attr:`clusters`; if the
        electrode does not appear there it is treated as a
        stand-alone cluster ``[electrode_name]``.

    Returns
    -------
    list[complex]
        Complex cluster impedance per frequency in ohms, one entry
        per entry in :attr:`frequencies`. Frequencies for which
        the summed cluster current is exactly zero return ``nan``.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If the resolved cluster is empty, or if none of its members
        carries potential *and* current data.

    Notes
    -----
    The cluster potential is the **length-weighted (Galerkin)
    average** over all members,

    .. math::
        \\varphi_c \\;=\\;
        \\frac{\\sum_{e \\in c} L_e\\, \\varphi_e}
              {\\sum_{e \\in c} L_e},
        \\qquad
        L_e = \\sum_{k \\in e} L_k ,

    with the per-electrode lengths taken from
    :attr:`point_sources`. Since every member potential
    :math:`\\varphi_e` is itself the length-weighted average over
    that electrode's segments, :math:`\\varphi_c` is exactly the
    length-weighted average over the whole cluster surface — the
    quantity the augmented system constrains to one value (see
    ``solver/image.py``, block 1 of the multi-port system).

    Up to 0.14.1 this method read ``members[0]``, i.e. the
    *alphabetically first* member name. Because the reported
    member potentials were unweighted segment means they did not
    agree with each other, so renaming an electrode changed the
    reported cluster impedance of an unchanged geometry (19.4393 Ω
    → 19.2314 Ω in the audit case, 2026-07-28, F11). With the
    weighted reduction the members agree to round-off for the
    image family and the result is invariant under renaming for
    every backend.

    Numerator and denominator run over **different** member sets,
    deliberately:

    * :math:`\\varphi_c` averages over members that carry *both*
      potential and current data — a member with no potential
      cannot contribute a term to the average.
    * :math:`\\sum_e I_e` sums over every member that carries
      current data, whether or not its potential was stored,
      because its injected current is part of the cluster total
      regardless.

    Every backend in this package populates both mappings for
    every member, so the two sets coincide in practice. They
    differ only for hand-built :class:`FieldResult` instances,
    where restricting the current sum to the potential-carrying
    members would silently under-count the cluster current
    (audit 2026-07-29).
    """
    members, u = self._cluster_potential(electrode_name)
    n_freq = len(u)
    # The *denominator* runs over every member that has current
    # data, not over ``usable``: a member without potential data
    # cannot contribute to the weighted average, but its injected
    # current is still part of the cluster's total. Restricting the
    # sum to ``usable`` (0.15.0 development state) silently dropped
    # it and returned a too-large impedance instead of the
    # ``KeyError`` v0.14.1 raised — e.g. potentials {"a"} with
    # currents {"a": 1 A, "b": 1 A} and cluster ["a", "b"] gave
    # 10 V / 1 A = 10 Ω where 10 V / 2 A = 5 Ω is meant
    # (audit 2026-07-29). Not reachable through any shipped
    # backend, but ``FieldResult`` is public and user-constructible.
    current_members = [
        m
        for m in members
        if m in self.electrode_currents
        and len(self.electrode_currents[m]) >= n_freq
    ]
    i_sum = [
        sum(self.electrode_currents[m][k] for m in current_members)
        for k in range(n_freq)
    ]
    return [
        (uk / ik) if ik != 0 else complex("nan")
        for uk, ik in zip(u, i_sum, strict=False)
    ]

def grounding_impedance(self, electrode_name: str) -> list[complex]:
    """Input impedance $Z(f) = U/I$ of an electrode.

    Parameters
    ----------
    electrode_name : str
        Name of the electrode whose input impedance is requested.
        Must be present in both :attr:`electrode_potentials` and
        :attr:`electrode_currents`.

    Returns
    -------
    list[complex]
        Complex impedance per frequency in ohms, one entry per
        entry in :attr:`frequencies`. Frequencies for which the
        electrode current is exactly zero return ``nan``.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If ``electrode_name`` is unknown to the result.

    Notes
    -----
    For galvanically connected electrodes (cluster with more than
    one member) this quantity is the cluster potential divided by
    the electrode's share of the total current. The physically
    meaningful quantity is the **cluster impedance** (see
    :meth:`cluster_impedance`).
    """
    if electrode_name not in self.electrode_potentials:
        raise KeyError(f"No potential data for '{electrode_name}'.")
    if electrode_name not in self.electrode_currents:
        raise KeyError(f"No current data for '{electrode_name}'.")
    u = self.electrode_potentials[electrode_name]
    i = self.electrode_currents[electrode_name]
    return [
        (uk / ik) if ik != 0 else complex("nan")
        for uk, ik in zip(u, i, strict=False)
    ]

docs.text:
input_impedance(source: str | None = None) -> list[complex]

Driving-point impedance seen by a source.

Definition:

\[ Z_\text{in}(f) \;=\; \frac{\varphi_a(f) - \varphi_r(f)}{I_s(f)}, \]

with \(\varphi_a\) the potential of the galvanic cluster the source feeds (attached_to), \(\varphi_r\) the potential of the return cluster (return_to; zero for a return through remote earth) and \(I_s\) the source current. Cluster potentials are the length-weighted averages used by cluster_impedance().

  • Current source: \(I_s\) is the impressed current.
  • Voltage source (since 2026.11): the solve fixes \(\varphi_a - \varphi_r = U - Z_q I_s\), so \(Z_\text{in} = U / I_s - Z_q\) with the impressed voltage \(U\), the solved source current \(I_s\) and the internal impedance \(Z_q = R + j\omega L\) of the source (SourceRecord.voltage, SourceRecord.current, SourceRecord.internal_impedance()). It is the impedance the source sees at its terminals, without its own \(Z_q\) (the current is \(U / (Z_q + Z_\text{in})\)). For a world with this one source it equals the impedance a 1 A current source at the same terminals reports, to round-off; with several sources it is an apparent impedance (see Notes).

This is the impedance a measurement instrument or a fault sees at the feeding point. It differs from cluster_impedance() (cluster potential over the cluster's own leakage current) as soon as part of the injected current leaves the cluster through conductors (PEN, cable shields, measurement leads): then the cluster impedance describes the local electrode only, the input impedance the whole connected system.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default source str | None

Name of the source. May be omitted when the result carries exactly one source.

None

Returns:

Type Description list[complex]

Complex input impedance per frequency in ohms. Frequencies with zero source current return nan.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the result carries no source snapshot (hand-built results), no source, or several sources and source is omitted; if the record of a voltage source carries no solved current (a backend that does not report it).

KeyError

If source is unknown, or the feeding / return electrode has no potential data in this result.

Notes

With several simultaneous sources the potential difference includes the contribution of the other sources, so the ratio is an apparent impedance of the named source. Two 230 V sources on two 3 m rods 5 m apart (100 Ω·m, image) report 38.90 Ω each, against 35.99 Ω of the 1 A solve of one rod (+8.1 %).

Source code in src/groundfield/solver/result.py 
def input_impedance(self, source: str | None = None) -> list[complex]:
    """Driving-point impedance seen by a source.

    Definition:

    $$
    Z_\\text{in}(f) \\;=\\;
    \\frac{\\varphi_a(f) - \\varphi_r(f)}{I_s(f)},
    $$

    with $\\varphi_a$ the potential of the galvanic cluster the
    source feeds (``attached_to``), $\\varphi_r$ the potential of
    the return cluster (``return_to``; zero for a return through
    remote earth) and $I_s$ the source current. Cluster potentials
    are the length-weighted averages used by
    :meth:`cluster_impedance`.

    * **Current source:** $I_s$ is the impressed current.
    * **Voltage source** (since 2026.11): the solve fixes
      $\\varphi_a - \\varphi_r = U - Z_q I_s$, so
      $Z_\\text{in} = U / I_s - Z_q$ with the impressed voltage $U$,
      the solved source current $I_s$ and the internal impedance
      $Z_q = R + j\\omega L$ of the source
      (:attr:`SourceRecord.voltage`, :attr:`SourceRecord.current`,
      :meth:`SourceRecord.internal_impedance`). It is the impedance
      the source sees at its terminals, **without** its own $Z_q$
      (the current is $U / (Z_q + Z_\\text{in})$). For a world with
      this one source it equals the impedance a 1 A current source
      at the same terminals reports, to round-off; with several
      sources it is an apparent impedance (see *Notes*).

    This is the impedance a measurement instrument or a fault sees
    at the feeding point. It differs from :meth:`cluster_impedance`
    (cluster potential over the cluster's own *leakage* current)
    as soon as part of the injected current leaves the cluster
    through conductors (PEN, cable shields, measurement leads):
    then the cluster impedance describes the local electrode only,
    the input impedance the whole connected system.

    Parameters
    ----------
    source
        Name of the source. May be omitted when the result carries
        exactly one source.

    Returns
    -------
    list[complex]
        Complex input impedance per frequency in ohms. Frequencies
        with zero source current return ``nan``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the result carries no source snapshot (hand-built
        results), no source, or several sources and ``source`` is
        omitted; if the record of a voltage source carries no solved
        current (a backend that does not report it).
    KeyError
        If ``source`` is unknown, or the feeding / return electrode
        has no potential data in this result.

    Notes
    -----
    With several simultaneous sources the potential difference
    includes the contribution of the other sources, so the ratio is
    an *apparent* impedance of the named source. Two 230 V sources
    on two 3 m rods 5 m apart (100 Ω·m, ``image``) report 38.90 Ω
    each, against 35.99 Ω of the 1 A solve of one rod (+8.1 %).
    """
    if not self.sources:
        raise ValueError(
            "input_impedance needs the source snapshot of the solve; "
            "this result carries none (hand-built FieldResult?)."
        )
    candidates = [s for s in self.sources if s.kind in _SOURCE_KINDS]
    if source is None:
        if not candidates:
            raise ValueError("The result carries no current source.")
        if len(candidates) > 1:
            kinds = {s.kind for s in candidates}
            label = f"{kinds.pop()} sources" if len(kinds) == 1 else "sources"
            names = ", ".join(s.name for s in candidates)
            raise ValueError(
                f"The result carries several {label} ({names}); pass source=<name>."
            )
        record = candidates[0]
    else:
        by_name = {s.name: s for s in self.sources}
        if source not in by_name:
            known = ", ".join(sorted(by_name)) or "none"
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown source {source!r} (known: {known}).")
        record = by_name[source]
        if record.kind not in _SOURCE_KINDS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Source {source!r} is a {record.kind!r} source; the input "
                "impedance is defined for current and voltage sources."
            )
    if record.kind == "voltage":
        n_freq = len(self.frequencies)
        if len(record.current) != n_freq or len(record.voltage) != n_freq:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Voltage source {record.name!r}: the result carries no "
                "solved source current (the backend did not report it), "
                f"or not one per frequency ({len(record.current)} currents, "
                f"{len(record.voltage)} voltages, {n_freq} frequencies)."
            )
        z_in = [
            u / i if i != 0 else complex("nan")
            for u, i in zip(record.voltage, record.current, strict=True)
        ]
        if record.internal_resistance_ohm or record.internal_inductance_h:
            # The impedance seen by the source, without its own Z_q.
            z_in = [
                z - record.internal_impedance(f)
                for z, f in zip(z_in, self.frequencies, strict=True)
            ]
        return z_in
    u_a = self._terminal_potential(record.name, "feeds", record.attached_to)
    if record.return_to is None:
        u_r = [0j] * len(u_a)
    else:
        u_r = self._terminal_potential(record.name, "returns to", record.return_to)
    return [
        (ua - ur) / ik if ik != 0 else complex("nan")
        for ua, ur, ik in zip(u_a, u_r, record.current, strict=False)
    ]

potential(points: ndarray, frequency_index: int = 0, min_distance: float = 0.001) -> np.ndarray

Evaluate the potential at field points (image-charge sum).

Picks the appropriate Green's-function kernel automatically:

  • homogeneous (HomogeneousSoil or no self.soil set but soil_resistivity available): classic image-charge sum \(1/r + 1/r_{\text{img}}\).
  • 2-layer (TwoLayerSoil, or MultiLayerSoil with exactly two layers): Tagg/Sunde series truncated with the controls of the solve, metadata["series"] (the engine's image_max_terms and image_series_tol; defaults 300 and 1e-6 for results without the record).
  • 1-layer (MultiLayerSoil with a single layer): degenerate case, dispatched to the homogeneous kernel.

The dispatch reads the canonical layer stack of self.soil (adjacent layers of one resistivity merged, review pass 10, 10.48): TwoLayerSoil(rho, rho, h) and a MultiLayerSoil of one resistivity are evaluated like homogeneous soil, exactly as they are solved (before audit A3S-04 their sources below h took the point form of the two-layer kernel, +2.7 % next to a rod), and a MultiLayerSoil with at most two distinct layers like the two-layer soil.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default points ndarray

Field points, array of shape (M, 3) in metres.

required frequency_index int

Index into frequencies. Default 0.

0 min_distance float

Numerical cutoff for 1/r singularities, in metres.

0.001

Returns:

Name Type Description phi (ndarray, shape(M))

Complex potential in V.

Warns:

Type Description SeriesTruncationWarning

If the two-layer series reaches max_terms before its tail bound falls below tol.

Raises:

Type Description NotImplementedError

If self.soil is a MultiLayerSoil with three or more distinct layers. The post-solve potential path does not yet carry an n-layer Green's-function kernel. The solve itself is still correct via the cim / mom_sommerfeld / bem backends — only the explicit potential() evaluation is unavailable for n ≥ 3. Cluster impedances, electrode currents and potentials stored in electrode_potentials / cluster_impedance remain accessible.

Notes

Prior to 0.2.0 a MultiLayerSoil with n ≥ 3 silently fell through to the homogeneous kernel, returning incorrect potentials, profiles, touch / step voltages and VTK exports. The error is now raised explicitly so the regime is visible rather than silent.

Point sources at projected (UTM) coordinates, beyond 10 km from the origin, are evaluated in a local frame: points and sources are shifted by the rounded centre of the sources' bounding box (exact for nearby doubles) before the kernel runs (since 2026.11; see Units and conventions in the reference).

Source code in src/groundfield/solver/result.py 
def potential(
    self,
    points: np.ndarray,
    frequency_index: int = 0,
    min_distance: float = 1e-3,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Evaluate the potential at field points (image-charge sum).

    Picks the appropriate Green's-function kernel automatically:

    - **homogeneous** (:class:`HomogeneousSoil` or no ``self.soil``
      set but ``soil_resistivity`` available): classic image-charge
      sum $1/r + 1/r_{\\text{img}}$.
    - **2-layer** (:class:`TwoLayerSoil`, or :class:`MultiLayerSoil`
      with exactly two layers): Tagg/Sunde series truncated with the
      controls of the solve, ``metadata["series"]`` (the engine's
      ``image_max_terms`` and ``image_series_tol``; defaults 300 and
      ``1e-6`` for results without the record).
    - **1-layer** (:class:`MultiLayerSoil` with a single layer):
      degenerate case, dispatched to the homogeneous kernel.

    The dispatch reads the canonical layer stack of ``self.soil``
    (adjacent layers of one resistivity merged, review pass 10,
    10.48): ``TwoLayerSoil(rho, rho, h)`` and a ``MultiLayerSoil`` of
    one resistivity are evaluated like homogeneous soil, exactly as
    they are solved (before audit A3S-04 their sources below ``h``
    took the point form of the two-layer kernel, +2.7 % next to a
    rod), and a ``MultiLayerSoil`` with at most two distinct layers
    like the two-layer soil.

    Parameters
    ----------
    points
        Field points, array of shape ``(M, 3)`` in metres.
    frequency_index
        Index into :attr:`frequencies`. Default 0.
    min_distance
        Numerical cutoff for 1/r singularities, in metres.

    Returns
    -------
    phi : np.ndarray, shape (M,)
        Complex potential in V.

    Warns
    -----
    SeriesTruncationWarning
        If the two-layer series reaches ``max_terms`` before its tail
        bound falls below ``tol``.

    Raises
    ------
    NotImplementedError
        If ``self.soil`` is a :class:`MultiLayerSoil` with three or
        more distinct layers. The post-solve potential path does not yet
        carry an n-layer Green's-function kernel. The solve itself
        is still correct via the ``cim`` / ``mom_sommerfeld`` /
        ``bem`` backends — only the explicit
        :meth:`potential` evaluation is unavailable for n ≥ 3.
        Cluster impedances, electrode currents and potentials
        stored in :attr:`electrode_potentials` /
        :attr:`cluster_impedance` remain accessible.

    Notes
    -----
    Prior to 0.2.0 a :class:`MultiLayerSoil` with n ≥ 3 silently
    fell through to the homogeneous kernel, returning incorrect
    potentials, profiles, touch / step voltages and VTK exports.
    The error is now raised explicitly so the regime is visible
    rather than silent.

    Point sources at projected (UTM) coordinates, beyond 10 km from
    the origin, are evaluated in a local frame: points and sources are
    shifted by the rounded centre of the sources' bounding box (exact
    for nearby doubles) before the kernel runs (since 2026.11; see
    *Units and conventions* in the reference).
    """
    if not self.point_sources:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "FieldResult has no point_sources — the backend did not "
            "populate the post-processing data (stub?)."
        )

    pts = np.asarray(points, dtype=float)
    if pts.ndim == 1:
        pts = pts[None, :]
    if pts.shape[1] != 3:
        raise ValueError(f"points must have shape (M, 3), got {pts.shape}.")

    sources, all_currents = self._point_source_arrays()
    # Contiguous, as before the cache: the real/imaginary views then
    # have the stride the BLAS calls of v0.15.0 saw.
    currents = np.ascontiguousarray(all_currents[:, frequency_index])
    line = self._line_sources()
    # Sources at projected (UTM) coordinates: evaluate in a local frame
    # of the sources, exactly shifted (2026.11, see solver._frame); a
    # result within 10 km of the origin is evaluated as before.
    from groundfield.solver._frame import points_origin

    origin = points_origin(sources)
    if origin is not None:
        pts = pts - origin
        sources = sources - origin
        if line is not None:
            from groundfield.solver._line_kernel import LineSegments

            line = LineSegments(
                line.mid - origin, line.length, line.tangent, line.radius
            )

    # Dispatch to the kernel that matches the effective number of
    # soil layers: that of the canonical layer stack, the soil the
    # backends actually solve (review pass 10, 10.48). A
    # ``TwoLayerSoil(rho, rho, h)`` or a ``MultiLayerSoil`` of one
    # resistivity is homogeneous soil — its sources below h took the
    # point form of the two-layer spectral kernel here instead of the
    # line sources of the homogeneous result (+2.7 % next to a rod,
    # audit A3S-04); a ``MultiLayerSoil`` with one or two distinct
    # layers is cast on the fly. For n ≥ 3 there is no closed-form
    # image-charge series (Γ_1(λ) is no longer constant in λ — see
    # ``solver/image_nlayer.py``), so the call is rejected explicitly
    # rather than silently falling back to the homogeneous kernel.
    soil = self.soil
    if soil is not None and not isinstance(soil, HomogeneousSoil):
        from groundfield.solver._layered import canonical_soil

        soil = canonical_soil(soil)
    if isinstance(soil, TwoLayerSoil):
        return self._potential_two_layer(
            pts, sources, currents, soil, min_distance, line=line
        )
    if isinstance(soil, MultiLayerSoil):
        n = len(soil.layers)
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"FieldResult.potential: MultiLayerSoil with n={n} ≥ 3 "
            "layers is not supported on the post-solve potential "
            "path. The solve itself is correct (use the "
            "'mom_sommerfeld' or 'fem' backend), but a closed-form "
            "n-layer Green's-function kernel is not yet wired into "
            "FieldResult.potential. Access cluster impedances and "
            "electrode potentials directly via "
            "result.electrode_potentials / result.cluster_impedance "
            "instead, or reduce the soil model to "
            "TwoLayerSoil / HomogeneousSoil for explicit field "
            "evaluation."
        )
    if isinstance(soil, HomogeneousSoil) and soil is not self.soil:
        # A layered declaration of one resistivity (see above).
        return self._potential_homogeneous(
            pts,
            sources,
            currents,
            min_distance,
            rho_override=float(soil.rho),
            line=line,
        )
    return self._potential_homogeneous(
        pts, sources, currents, min_distance, line=line
    )

def summary(self) -> str:
    """Compact one-line description of the result.

def to_dataframe(self, table: str = "electrodes") -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tidy table of the result, one row per frequency and object.

    Parameters
    ----------
    table
        ``"electrodes"`` (default): one row per frequency and
        electrode with the columns

        * ``frequency_hz`` — frequency in Hz;
        * ``electrode`` — electrode name;
        * ``cluster`` — galvanic cluster, labelled by its
          alphabetically first member (see :attr:`clusters`);
        * ``potential_v`` — electrode potential in V (complex);
        * ``current_a`` — leakage current of the electrode into the
          soil in A (complex);
        * ``cluster_impedance_ohm`` — :meth:`cluster_impedance` of
          the electrode's cluster in Ω (complex), the cluster
          potential over the cluster's own leakage current.

        ``"sources"``: one row per frequency and recorded source
        with ``frequency_hz``, ``source``, ``kind``,
        ``attached_to``, ``return_to``, ``current_a`` (source
        current in A, complex: impressed, or solved for a voltage
        source), ``voltage_v`` (impressed voltage in V of a voltage
        source, complex; ``nan`` for a current source),
        ``internal_resistance_ohm`` and ``internal_inductance_h``
        (internal impedance of a voltage source in Ω and H, float;
        ``nan`` for a current source) and ``input_impedance_ohm``
        (:meth:`input_impedance` in Ω, complex), the impedance seen
        at the feeding point (without the internal impedance).

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        The table; rows ordered by frequency, then by electrode /
        source in result order. Values that the result does not
        carry (hand-built results) are ``nan``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``table`` is not ``"electrodes"`` or ``"sources"``.
    ImportError
        If pandas is not installed (it is imported on first use).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> df = result.to_dataframe()                       # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> df.pivot(index="frequency_hz", columns="electrode",
    ...          values="potential_v").abs()             # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    if table not in ("electrodes", "sources"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown table {table!r}; choose 'electrodes' or 'sources'."
        )
    try:
        import pandas as pd
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - pandas is a dependency
        raise ImportError(
            "FieldResult.to_dataframe needs pandas (pip install pandas)."
        ) from exc
    if table == "sources":
        return self._source_frame(pd)
    return self._electrode_frame(pd)

docs.title: SourceRecord
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Snapshot of one source as it was solved.

Filled by Engine.solve() (and, for a world with voltage sources, by the backend); not instantiated directly by the user. FieldResult.input_impedance() reads it, so the result stays self-contained after the world has changed.

For a current source current is the impressed current and voltage is empty. For a voltage source voltage is the impressed voltage \(U\) and current the source current \(I\) the solve returned — the current the source drives into attached_to (and takes back from return_to), the same sign convention as a current source; internal_resistance_ohm and internal_inductance_h are its internal impedance \(Z_q = R + j\omega L\) (0 for an ideal source and for current sources), so the terminal voltage is \(U - Z_q I\).

A record pickled before 2026.11 lacks the two fields of the internal impedance and unpickles with 0 / 0, as its JSON loads (audit W2R2-01).

def internal_impedance(self, frequency: float) -> complex:
    """Internal impedance $Z_q = R + j\\omega L$ in Ω at ``frequency`` (Hz).

    ``0j`` for a current source and an ideal voltage source.
    """
    return _internal_impedance(
        self.internal_resistance_ohm,
        self.internal_inductance_h,
        2.0 * np.pi * float(frequency),
    )

def solve_provenance(world: World, engine: Engine) -> dict[str, Any]:

    :meth:`Engine.solve <groundfield.solver.engine.Engine.solve>` calls

def world_fingerprint(world: World) -> str:
    """SHA-256 fingerprint of the canonical JSON of a world.

    The canonical form is ``json.dumps(world.model_dump(mode="json"),
    sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))``. Pydantic writes floats in
    their shortest round-trip form, so equal worlds give equal
    fingerprints, also after a JSON round trip of the world. The
    fingerprint depends on the world schema of the installed version:
    renamed or added model fields change it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        The world to fingerprint.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        ``"sha256:"`` followed by 64 hexadecimal digits.
    """
    canonical = json.dumps(
        world.model_dump(mode="json"), sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
    )
    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

docs.title: mutual
docs.text:
Mutual grounding-impedance matrix and field matrix in one assembly.

solve_mutual_matrix() computes the full nG × nG mutual grounding-impedance matrix Z_G of a set of grounding clusters ("gnodes"), solve_mutual_field() the potential at arbitrary points per unit excitation, each in one matrix assembly instead of one Engine.solve per excitation.

Motivation

The AP1 catalogue builds Z_G for every site and soil. The historic loop (one world per excitation, cluster_impedance on the diagonal, FieldResult.potential at a probe point off the diagonal) assembled the N × N segment reaction matrix nG times. Here:

  1. The segment reaction matrix is assembled once, directly (the kernel operators' matrix method; v0.15.0 applied the kernel to an N × N identity, one O(N³) product per image term — review pass 10, 10.59), including the ADR-0012 V2 concrete shell.
  2. The leakage distribution of every excitation is a solve of the same augmented nodal system as Engine.solve(), with one owner per straight wire of an electrode (a wire line of a grid, an arm of a star, an edge of a polyline; user decision Q30) and per soil layer for electrodes through the layer interface (10.15).
  3. The off-diagonal entries are either the reaction of the leakage columns (offdiag="galerkin", the default, no further kernel evaluation) or the probe-point potentials (offdiag="probe", one probe kernel for all columns).

Discretisation, topology and the branch block come from the shared image-family pipeline (groundfield.solver._pipeline); only the image family is accepted (10.34).

Consistency with Engine.solve

The diagonal equals FieldResult.cluster_impedance() of a per-excitation solve with the same engine to round-off (10.26), probe off-diagonals equal FieldResult.potential() at the probe point, and the columns of solve_mutual_field() equal FieldResult.potential at the field points (tests/test_mutual_matrix.py, tests/test_mutual_field.py).

Since the user decision Q15 of 2026.11 the off-diagonal of solve_mutual_matrix() is offdiag="galerkin" whatever the call. Up to 0.15.0 passing probe_points selected the potential at those points as the off-diagonal; such a call now returns the galerkin matrix, ignores the points and emits this warning. Pass offdiag="probe" to keep the 0.15.0 definition, or drop the probe points.

solve_mutual_field(world: 'World', engine: 'Engine', anchors: list[str], field_points: ndarray, *, frequency_index: int = 0, matrix_min_distance: float = 0.001, matrix_max_terms: int | None = None, matrix_tol: float | None = None) -> np.ndarray

Galvanic Green-function matrix: potential at arbitrary field points per node.

Returns R of shape (M, nG) with R[i, j] = potential at field_points[i] (x, y, depth) under unit current (1 A) injected into anchors[j] while all other clusters stay floating. This is the off-diagonal field evaluation of solve_mutual_matrix(), generalised to an arbitrary number of field points (decoupled from nG) and without the self/diagonal term — the building block for the frequency-dependent surface-potential distribution by superposition::

phi(field_points, f) = R @ I_leak(f)

with I_leak(f) = Y_G @ u(f) from the reduced network (Y_L(f) + Y_G) u = i. Uses the same one-shot assembly as solve_mutual_matrix() (reaction matrix and per-excitation leakage columns built once); only the field-point evaluation is generalised. The expensive 3D part is therefore frequency-independent and computed once, so a frequency sweep over I_leak(f) is cheap.

world must already carry all nG grounding clusters (every anchor in anchors must be a real electrode in world) and the soil model. Any current source is ignored — the excitations are applied internally, one cluster at a time, exactly as the historic per-excitation loop did.

def solve_mutual_field(
    world: "World",
    engine: "Engine",
    anchors: list[str],
    field_points: np.ndarray,
    *,
    frequency_index: int = 0,
    matrix_min_distance: float = 1e-3,
    matrix_max_terms: int | None = None,
    matrix_tol: float | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Galvanic Green-function matrix: potential at arbitrary field points per node.

    Returns ``R`` of shape ``(M, nG)`` with ``R[i, j]`` = potential at
    ``field_points[i]`` (``x, y, depth``) under unit current (1 A) injected
    into ``anchors[j]`` while all other clusters stay floating. This is the
    off-diagonal field evaluation of :func:`solve_mutual_matrix`, generalised
    to an **arbitrary** number of field points (decoupled from ``nG``) and
    without the self/diagonal term — the building block for the
    frequency-dependent surface-potential distribution by superposition::

        phi(field_points, f) = R @ I_leak(f)

    with ``I_leak(f) = Y_G @ u(f)`` from the reduced network
    ``(Y_L(f) + Y_G) u = i``. Uses the same one-shot assembly as
    :func:`solve_mutual_matrix` (reaction matrix and per-excitation leakage
    columns built once); only the field-point evaluation is generalised. The
    expensive 3D part is therefore frequency-independent and computed once, so
    a frequency sweep over ``I_leak(f)`` is cheap.

    ``world`` must already carry **all** ``nG`` grounding clusters (every
    anchor in ``anchors`` must be a real electrode in ``world``) and the soil
    model. Any current source is ignored — the excitations are applied
    internally, one cluster at a time, exactly as the historic per-excitation
    loop did.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        Assembled world holding all ``nG`` grounding clusters and the soil
        model. Sources, if any, are ignored.
    engine
        Engine configuration. ``segment_length`` controls the
        discretisation; ``frequencies`` selects the solved frequency via
        ``frequency_index``; ``image_max_terms`` / ``image_series_tol`` feed
        the 2-layer **self**-kernel (the reaction-matrix assembly), exactly
        as ``Engine.solve`` would.
    anchors
        Length-``nG`` list of electrode names, one per node. Anchor ``j``
        receives the unit current of excitation ``j`` and fills column ``j``
        of ``R``.
    field_points
        ``(M, 3)`` array of ``(x, y, depth)`` evaluation points, decoupled
        from ``nG``: ``M`` may differ from ``nG`` and the points are
        arbitrary (surface or buried). Row ``i`` becomes row ``i`` of ``R``.
    frequency_index
        Index into ``engine.frequencies``. Default 0. Only relevant when
        distributed conductors make the assembled system
        frequency-dependent.
    matrix_min_distance, matrix_max_terms, matrix_tol
        Clamp distance in m and series controls of the field evaluation.
        ``None`` (default) for the series controls takes
        ``engine.image_max_terms`` / ``engine.image_series_tol``, the
        controls :meth:`FieldResult.potential` uses after a solve with the
        same engine (before 2026.11 they were hard-coded to 100 /
        ``1e-6``, review pass 10, 10.25).

    Returns
    -------
    R : np.ndarray, shape (M, nG), complex
        Galvanic Green-function matrix; ``R[i, j]`` is the potential at
        ``field_points[i]`` under unit excitation of cluster ``j``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``world`` has no soil model, holds no electrodes, or
        ``field_points`` does not have shape ``(M, 3)``.
    KeyError
        If an entry of ``anchors`` is not an electrode in ``world``.
    NotImplementedError
        If the soil is a ``MultiLayerSoil`` with three or more layers
        (only homogeneous and 2-layer soils are supported).
    TypeError
        If the soil model type is not supported.

    See Also
    --------
    solve_mutual_matrix : Full ``nG × nG`` mutual grounding-impedance matrix.
    """
    if world.soil is None:
        raise ValueError("World has no soil model.")
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")

    nG = len(anchors)
    field_points = np.asarray(field_points, dtype=float)
    if field_points.ndim != 2 or field_points.shape[1] != 3:
        raise ValueError(
            f"field_points must have shape (M, 3), got {field_points.shape}."
        )

    problem = _prepare(world, engine, frequency_index, where="solve_mutual_field")
    n_segments = len(problem.disc.segments)

    # Per-excitation leakage columns T (no diagonal/self term needed).
    T = np.zeros((n_segments, nG), dtype=complex)
    for j, (_, sc) in enumerate(_unit_excitations(world, problem, list(anchors))):
        T[:, j] = sc

    # Potential at the M field points per excitation (nG) — one kernel pass.
    return _field_of_columns(
        problem,
        field_points,
        T,
        min_distance=matrix_min_distance,
        max_terms=matrix_max_terms,
        tol=matrix_tol,
    )

solve_mutual_matrix(world: 'World', engine: 'Engine', anchors: list[str], probe_points: ndarray | None = None, *, frequency_index: int = 0, symmetrize: bool = True, offdiag: OffDiagonal = 'galerkin', matrix_min_distance: float = 0.001, matrix_max_terms: int | None = None, matrix_tol: float | None = None) -> np.ndarray

Full mutual grounding-impedance matrix Z_G in one assembly.

Column j belongs to 1 A injected into anchors[j]; the other clusters float (zero net current, review pass 10, 10.29), exactly as in Engine.solve() with one source. The segment reaction matrix and the leakage distribution of every excitation are computed once and reused for all entries.

  • Diagonal. Z[j, j] is the cluster impedance of anchors[j], the length-weighted (Galerkin) potential average over every member of its cluster divided by the cluster current — the same reduction as FieldResult.cluster_impedance() after a per-excitation Engine.solve() (equal to round-off). Up to 2026.11 the diagonal was the unweighted mean over the alphabetically first member: +0.150 % for an L-shaped footprint at ds = 2 m, -3.8 … -9.1 % for a rod split at the layer interface (review pass 10, 10.26).
  • Off-diagonal, offdiag="galerkin" (default): the reaction Z[i, j] = T_iᵀ (K + S) T_j of the leakage columns T with the reaction matrix K and the concrete-shell diagonal S. It is the current-weighted potential of cluster i under excitation j — the off-diagonal counterpart of the diagonal, reciprocal to round-off, and the matrix that reproduces a solve of the clusters joined by branches (see Notes).
  • Off-diagonal, offdiag="probe": the potential at probe_points[i] under excitation j, as FieldResult.potential() returns it after a per-excitation solve — the definition of releases up to 0.15.0. A point potential is not the potential of cluster i: the matrix is not reciprocal (Z[i, j] and Z[j, i] differ by up to 35 % in two-layer soil, review pass 10, 10.34), and symmetrize=True averages that asymmetry away. On an AP1-like site (a station and twelve house foundations, ds = 2 m, five soils) the symmetrised probe matrix misses the input impedance of the joined network by -0.15 … -0.88 %, and its off-diagonal entries differ from the galerkin ones by 0.15 … 1.1 % (median) and up to 41 %; the galerkin matrix reproduces the network solve to 1e-12.

The galerkin off-diagonal is the default of every call since the user decision Q15 of 2026.11. Up to 0.15.0 passing probe_points selected the probe definition; such a call now returns the galerkin matrix and ignores the points with a ProbePointsIgnoredWarning — pass offdiag="probe" to keep the 0.15.0 definition.

        layers). Sources, if any, are ignored.
    engine
        Engine of the image family (``backend="image"`` and its
        aliases); ``segment_length``, ``kernel``, ``image_max_terms`` and
        ``image_series_tol`` act exactly as in :meth:`Engine.solve`.
        ``frequencies[frequency_index]`` is the solved frequency.
    anchors
        Length-``nG`` list of electrode names, one per cluster ("gnode").
    probe_points
        ``(nG, 3)`` array of ``(x, y, depth)`` points in m, one per
        anchor, used by ``offdiag="probe"`` only (required there). With
        ``offdiag="galerkin"`` they are ignored, not validated, with a
        :class:`ProbePointsIgnoredWarning`.
    frequency_index
        Index into ``engine.frequencies``. Default 0.
    symmetrize
        If ``True`` (default) return ``0.5 · (Z + Zᵀ)``.
    offdiag
        ``"galerkin"`` (default) or ``"probe"``, see above.
    matrix_min_distance, matrix_max_terms, matrix_tol
        Clamp distance in m and series controls of the probe-point
        evaluation (``offdiag="probe"`` only; the galerkin off-diagonal
        evaluates no field). ``None`` (default) for the series controls
        takes ``engine.image_max_terms`` / ``engine.image_series_tol``,
        the controls :meth:`FieldResult.potential` uses after a solve with
        the same engine (before 2026.11 they were hard-coded to 100 /
        ``1e-6``, review pass 10, 10.25).

    Returns
    -------
    Z : np.ndarray, shape (nG, nG), complex
        Mutual grounding-impedance matrix in Ω.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``world`` has no soil model or no electrodes, if
        ``offdiag="probe"`` comes without ``probe_points`` of shape
        ``(nG, 3)``, or if ``offdiag`` is unknown.
    BackendCapabilityError
        If the engine's backend is not the image family (a subclass of
        ``ValueError``; up to 2026.11 the backend was ignored, 10.34).
    ResourceLimitError
        If the problem exceeds ``engine.max_segments`` (default
        :data:`groundfield.diagnostics.HARD_LIMIT`).
    KeyError
        If an entry of ``anchors`` is not an electrode in ``world``.

    Warns
    -----
    ProbePointsIgnoredWarning
        If ``probe_points`` are given with ``offdiag="galerkin"`` (the
        default), the call of releases up to 0.15.0.

    Notes
    -----
    With the uniform current per owner of the image family, the
    potential of a cluster is the current-weighted average of its
    segment potentials. With every other cluster floating,
    ``T_iᵀ (K + S) T_j`` therefore equals the potential of cluster ``i``
    under excitation ``j`` exactly (reciprocity of the reaction matrix),
    bonded groups and rods through the layer interface included, and
    ``(Y_L + Z_G⁻¹) u = i`` reproduces the solve of the clusters joined
    by the branches ``Y_L``. With probe off-diagonals it does not
    (evidence in the 2026.11 changelog).
    """
    if world.soil is None:
        raise ValueError("World has no soil model.")
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")
    if offdiag not in _OFFDIAG_CHOICES:
        raise ValueError(f"offdiag must be 'probe' or 'galerkin', got {offdiag!r}.")

    nG = len(anchors)
    if offdiag == "probe":
        if probe_points is None:
            raise ValueError("offdiag='probe' needs probe_points of shape (nG, 3).")
        probe_points = np.asarray(probe_points, dtype=float)
        if probe_points.shape != (nG, 3):
            raise ValueError(
                f"probe_points must have shape ({nG}, 3), got {probe_points.shape}."
            )
    elif probe_points is not None:
        # user decision Q15 (2026-11-08): the galerkin off-diagonal is the
        # default whatever the call; the probe points of a 0.15.0 call are
        # ignored, not rejected, so the call keeps running.
        from groundfield.solver.registry import warn_external

        warn_external(
            "solve_mutual_matrix: probe_points are ignored. The off-diagonal "
            "is offdiag='galerkin' (the default since 2026.11): the reaction "
            "of the leakage distributions, reciprocal, the matrix that "
            "reproduces a solve of the clusters joined by branches. Up to "
            "0.15.0 probe points selected the potential at them instead; "
            "pass offdiag='probe' to keep that definition, or drop "
            "probe_points.",
            ProbePointsIgnoredWarning,
        )
        probe_points = None

    problem = _prepare(world, engine, frequency_index, where="solve_mutual_matrix")
    disc, topo, arrays = problem.disc, problem.topo, problem.arrays
    n_segments = len(disc.segments)
    seg_lengths = arrays.lengths
    Z_seg_full = problem.Z_seg_full

    # ADR-0012 V2 shell augmentation (added to the *diagonal* of the
    # reaction matrix exactly as in ``_solve_cluster_currents`` and the
    # post-solve ``ph`` step).
    shell_diag: np.ndarray | None = None
    if np.any(arrays.shell_coefficients > 0.0):
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            shell_diag = np.where(
                seg_lengths > 0.0,
                arrays.shell_coefficients / seg_lengths,
                0.0,
            )

    # Cluster members per real electrode (== FieldResult.clusters).
    real_set = {e.name for e in world.electrodes}
    cluster_id = topo.cluster_id
    cluster_members: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for ename in (e.name for e in world.electrodes):
        cluster_members[ename] = sorted(
            n
            for n in cluster_id
            if cluster_id[n] == cluster_id[ename] and n in real_set
        )

    T = np.zeros((n_segments, nG), dtype=complex)  # leakage column per excitation
    PH = np.zeros((n_segments, nG), dtype=complex)  # segment potentials per excitation
    Z = np.zeros((nG, nG), dtype=complex)
    excitations = _unit_excitations(world, problem, list(anchors))
    for j, anchor_j in enumerate(anchors):
        elec_total, sc = excitations[j]
        T[:, j] = sc
        if sc.any():
            # Segment potentials as in the post-solve step of the live
            # solver: bulk reaction matrix on the real and imaginary
            # leakage, then the shell augmentation.
            phi_re = Z_seg_full @ sc.real
            phi_im = Z_seg_full @ sc.imag
            if shell_diag is not None:
                phi_re = phi_re + shell_diag * sc.real
                phi_im = phi_im + shell_diag * sc.imag
            PH[:, j] = phi_re + 1j * phi_im
        members = cluster_members.get(anchor_j, [anchor_j])
        Z[j, j] = _cluster_impedance(problem, members, elec_total, PH[:, j])

    if offdiag == "galerkin":
        # Reaction of every pair of leakage columns (bilinear, no
        # conjugation: reciprocity holds for the complex system too).
        Phi = T.T @ PH
    else:
        Phi = _field_of_columns(
            problem,
            probe_points,
            T,
            min_distance=matrix_min_distance,
            max_terms=matrix_max_terms,
            tol=matrix_tol,
        )  # (nG, nG): row i = probe i, column j = excitation j
    off = ~np.eye(nG, dtype=bool)
    Z[off] = Phi[off]

    if symmetrize:
        return 0.5 * (Z + Z.T)
    return Z

docs.title: Backend solve functions
docs.text: Each built-in backend is one solve function, solve_<name>(world, engine), registered in the backend registry. Engine.solve resolves the backend name, checks the capabilities against the world, calls the function and fills the common metadata of the result (CORE_METADATA_KEYS); call the functions directly only to bypass that dispatch, for example in a test. The theory of each backend is on its engine page.

def solve_image(world: "World", engine: "Engine") -> FieldResult:
    """Image-charge solver for homogeneous soil.

    Runs the shared image-family pipeline
    (:mod:`groundfield.solver._pipeline`) with the half-space Green's
    function.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        World whose ``soil`` must be a :class:`HomogeneousSoil`.
    engine
        Engine configuration; relevant fields are ``segment_length``,
        ``frequencies`` and ``earth_inductive_model``.

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        Node potentials and leakage currents per frequency, point
        sources and metadata.

    Raises
    ------
    BackendCapabilityError
        If the soil is a layered model (:meth:`Engine.solve
        <groundfield.solver.engine.Engine.solve>` forwards those to
        ``image_2layer``). Before 2026.11 this was a :class:`TypeError`.
    TypeError
        If ``world.soil`` is no soil model.
    ValueError
        If the world has no electrodes, or the geometry fails a
        discretisation guard (thin wire, burial depth).
    """
    if isinstance(world.soil, (TwoLayerSoil, MultiLayerSoil)):
        from groundfield.solver.registry import BackendCapabilityError

        raise BackendCapabilityError(
            f"Backend 'image' solves homogeneous soil; got a "
            f"{type(world.soil).__name__}. Engine(backend='image').solve "
            "forwards layered soils to image_2layer (at most two distinct "
            "layers); use backend='mom_sommerfeld' for three or more."
        )
    if not isinstance(world.soil, HomogeneousSoil):
        raise TypeError(
            "Backend 'image' requires a HomogeneousSoil. "
            f"Got: {type(world.soil).__name__}."
        )
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")
    if engine.kernel is None:
        # A direct call resolves the default like Engine.solve (10.28).
        engine = engine._with(kernel=DEFAULT_KERNEL)
    green = _HalfSpaceGreen(world.soil.rho, engine.kernel)
    return solve_image_family(world, engine, green, stacklevel=3)

def solve_image_2layer(
    world: "World",
    engine: "Engine",
    *,
    max_terms: int | None = None,
    tol: float | None = None,
    far_field: str | None = None,
) -> FieldResult:
    """Image-charge solver for 2-layer soil (Tagg / Sunde).

    Runs the shared image-family pipeline
    (:mod:`groundfield.solver._pipeline`) with the two-layer Green's
    function.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        World whose ``soil`` is a :class:`TwoLayerSoil`. Electrodes in
        the upper layer use the Tagg/Sunde series; geometries reaching
        the interface use the ADR-0007 Sommerfeld path.
    engine
        Engine configuration. ``engine.segment_length`` controls the
        discretisation as in the homogeneous backend.
    max_terms
        Maximum number of series terms; ``None`` (default) takes
        ``engine.image_max_terms``.
    tol
        Series truncation: stop as soon as the geometric tail bound
        $|K|^{n+1}/(1-|K|)$ falls below ``tol`` (dimensionless);
        ``None`` (default) takes ``engine.image_series_tol``.
    far_field
        Form of the far images with the line kernel, ``"quadrupole"`` or
        ``"point"``; ``None`` (default) takes ``engine.image_far_field``.

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        Result object. :attr:`FieldResult.metadata` exposes diagnostic
        fields (``K``, ``rho_1``, ``rho_2``, ``h_1``, ``n_terms_used``,
        ``converged``, ``series_used``, ``series``).

    Raises
    ------
    BackendCapabilityError
        If the soil is a :class:`HomogeneousSoil` or a
        :class:`~groundfield.soil.models.MultiLayerSoil` with three or
        more distinct layers (a stack with at most two is solved as the
        equivalent two-layer soil). Before 2026.11 both raised
        :class:`TypeError`.
    TypeError
        If ``world.soil`` is no soil model.
    ValueError
        If the world has no electrodes, if ``far_field`` is not one of
        ``"quadrupole"`` and ``"point"`` (audit W3R2A-02; before, every other
        value ran the point form and was recorded as given), or if the
        geometry fails a discretisation guard (thin wire, burial depth).

    Warns
    -----
    SeriesTruncationWarning
        If the series is used and reaches ``max_terms`` before ``tol``.
    """
    if isinstance(world.soil, MultiLayerSoil):
        # Audit round 1, A1-numerics F09: the registry accepts a layer
        # stack that merges to at most two layers; solve it as the
        # equivalent TwoLayerSoil instead of raising a bare TypeError.
        world = world.model_copy(update={"soil": _as_two_layer(world.soil)})
    if isinstance(world.soil, HomogeneousSoil):
        from groundfield.solver.registry import BackendCapabilityError

        raise BackendCapabilityError(
            "Backend 'image_2layer' solves two-layer soil; got a "
            "HomogeneousSoil. Use backend='image' (Engine(backend='image')"
            ".solve dispatches by soil model)."
        )
    if not isinstance(world.soil, TwoLayerSoil):
        raise TypeError(
            "Backend 'image_2layer' requires a TwoLayerSoil. "
            f"Got: {type(world.soil).__name__}."
        )
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")

    soil: TwoLayerSoil = world.soil
    _log.info(
        "image_2layer: rho_1=%.1f, rho_2=%.1f, h_1=%.2f, K=%.4f",
        soil.rho_1,
        soil.rho_2,
        soil.h_1,
        soil.reflection_coefficient,
    )
    if max_terms is None:
        max_terms = engine.image_max_terms
    if tol is None:
        tol = engine.image_series_tol
    if far_field is None:
        far_field = engine.image_far_field
    if engine.kernel is None:
        # The backend's preferred kernel (Engine.kernel = None, 10.28).
        engine = engine._with(kernel=DEFAULT_KERNEL)
    green = _TwoLayerGreen(
        soil, max_terms, tol, engine.segment_length, engine.kernel, far_field
    )
    owner_interfaces = None
    if _crosses_interface(world, _owner_interfaces(soil)):
        # One owner per (electrode, layer) for rods through h_1 (10.15), on
        # top of the one owner per straight wire of every world (Q30).
        owner_interfaces = _owner_interfaces(soil)
    return solve_image_family(
        world, engine, green, stacklevel=3, owner_interfaces=owner_interfaces
    )

solve_mom(world: World, engine: Engine, *, two_layer_max_terms: int | None = None, two_layer_tol: float | None = None) -> FieldResult

Point-matching method-of-moments backend.

Supports HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil and a MultiLayerSoil whose canonical stack has at most two layers (10.48). The Green's-function kernel is taken from the matching image backend; only the resolution scheme (one current per segment, point matching at the segment midpoints, instead of one uniform current per straight wire of an electrode) differs. Clusters without a source float (zero net current, 10.29). Concrete-encased electrodes carry the per-segment shell term of ADR-0012 (since 2026.11). See the module docstring for the accuracy of the scheme and the shared solve flow.

required engine Engine

None two_layer_tol int | None

Truncation parameters for the Tagg/Sunde series (term count, dimensionless tail bound), only used for two-layer soil. None (default) takes engine.image_max_terms / engine.image_series_tol, so the engine knob reaches this backend consistently with image_2layer.

def solve_mom(
    world: World,
    engine: Engine,
    *,
    two_layer_max_terms: int | None = None,
    two_layer_tol: float | None = None,
) -> FieldResult:
    """Point-matching method-of-moments backend.

    Supports :class:`HomogeneousSoil`, :class:`TwoLayerSoil` and a
    :class:`MultiLayerSoil` whose canonical stack has at most two layers
    (10.48). The Green's-function kernel is taken from the matching
    image backend; only the resolution scheme (one current per segment,
    point matching at the segment midpoints, instead of one uniform
    current per straight wire of an electrode) differs. Clusters without a source float
    (zero net current, 10.29). Concrete-encased electrodes carry the
    per-segment shell term of ADR-0012 (since 2026.11). See the module
    docstring for the accuracy of the scheme and the shared solve flow.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        World to evaluate.
    engine
        Engine configuration; ``engine.segment_length`` (m) controls the
        discretisation.
    two_layer_max_terms, two_layer_tol
        Truncation parameters for the Tagg/Sunde series (term count,
        dimensionless tail bound), only used for two-layer soil.
        ``None`` (default) takes ``engine.image_max_terms`` /
        ``engine.image_series_tol``, so the engine knob reaches this
        backend consistently with ``image_2layer``.

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        Result object compatible with :class:`FieldResult` from the
        image backends. ``metadata['solver']`` is ``'point_matching'``
        (``'galerkin'`` up to 0.15.0, although the scheme was the
        same).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the world has no electrodes, or a segment lies partly above
        the soil surface.
    BackendCapabilityError
        For a :class:`MultiLayerSoil` with three or more distinct layers
        (a :class:`TypeError` before 2026.11).
    TypeError
        If ``world.soil`` is no soil model.
    """
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")
    if not isinstance(world.soil, (HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil, MultiLayerSoil)):
        raise TypeError(
            "Backend 'mom' supports HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil and "
            "MultiLayerSoil stacks with at most two distinct layers. "
            f"Got: {type(world.soil).__name__}."
        )
    # Review pass 10, 10.48: solve the canonical soil — a MultiLayerSoil
    # whose adjacent layers share a resistivity is a two-layer (or
    # homogeneous) soil, and a TwoLayerSoil without contrast is
    # homogeneous.
    soil = canonical_soil(world.soil)
    if isinstance(soil, MultiLayerSoil):
        from groundfield.solver.registry import BackendCapabilityError

        raise BackendCapabilityError(
            "Backend 'mom' supports at most two distinct soil layers; this "
            f"MultiLayerSoil has {len(soil.layers)}. Use "
            "backend='mom_sommerfeld' for n >= 3 soils."
        )
    if two_layer_max_terms is None:
        two_layer_max_terms = engine.image_max_terms
    if two_layer_tol is None:
        two_layer_tol = engine.image_series_tol
    _log.info(
        "mom: soil=%s, segment_length=%.3f",
        type(soil).__name__,
        engine.segment_length,
    )
    green = _MomGreen(soil, two_layer_max_terms, two_layer_tol)
    return solve_point_matching(world, engine, green, stacklevel=3)

docs.text:
solve_mom_sommerfeld(world: World, engine: Engine, *, lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0, epsabs: float = 1e-09, epsrel: float = 1e-07, max_osc_panels: int = _MAX_OSC_PANELS, tabulate: bool = True) -> FieldResult

Point-matching MoM with direct Sommerfeld quadrature for layered soil.

The discretisation and the linear solve are those of mom (point matching at the segment midpoints, point-source near field, source-free clusters floating), run through the shared solve pipeline (10.75). Every off-diagonal reaction-matrix entry is the Sommerfeld kernel of sommerfeld_kernel_value(), i.e. the closed-form direct pair plus a numerically integrated reflected remainder; no image series and no fit enter the off-diagonal kernel. For \(n = 2\) the diagonal is the Tagg/Sunde series diagonal of mom, so on two-layer soil this backend reproduces mom and checks the kernel, not the scheme; for \(n \ge 3\) distinct layers it is the only integral-equation backend.

Cost (review pass 10, 10.61): pairs that share a depth pair and a horizontal distance share one quadrature, which halves the work of every world and collapses it for regular geometries. For \(n \ge 3\) the reflected remainder of a depth group with many distinct distances is tabulated on log-spaced nodes and interpolated (tabulate=True, the default): about \(10^{-7}\) relative error of the kernel at the verification points and below \(10^{-6}\) on the reaction matrix of the benchmark grid B12, for a cost that no longer grows with the number of pairs. tabulate=False evaluates every distinct pair by quadrature (the kernel reference). For \(n = 2\) every pair is evaluated by quadrature: this backend is the kernel check of the closed-form series there.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default world World

World to evaluate.

required engine Engine

Engine configuration.

required lambda_max_factor float

Truncation of the remainder quadrature in units of the remainder decay length \(1 / d_{\text{rem}}\); saturates at 60. See sommerfeld_kernel_value() for the delegated \(n = 2\) cross-layer path.

200.0 epsabs float

Convergence thresholds of the remainder quadrature (absolute in 1/m, relative).

1e-09 epsrel float

Convergence thresholds of the remainder quadrature (absolute in 1/m, relative).

1e-09 max_osc_panels int

Budget for the \(J_0\) half-period panel family.

_MAX_OSC_PANELS tabulate bool

Depth-group tabulation of the reflected kernel for \(n \ge 3\) (see above).

True

Returns:

Type Description FieldResult

metadata['converged'] (one bool) and metadata['converged_per_frequency'] report the quadrature and series convergence (10.47); metadata['kernel_tabulation'] the tabulation counters and the largest relative error at its verification points.

Warns:

Type Description SommerfeldConvergenceWarning

Once per solve, if any reaction-matrix entry's remainder quadrature failed to converge.

Notes

The quadrature keywords are reachable through Engine.options["mom_sommerfeld"] (MomSommerfeldOptions); the signature defaults equal the option defaults, so a direct call without keywords behaves exactly like solve().

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If the soil is not a HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil or MultiLayerSoil.

ValueError

If the world has no electrodes.

def solve_mom_sommerfeld(
    world: World,
    engine: Engine,
    *,
    lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0,
    epsabs: float = 1e-9,
    epsrel: float = 1e-7,
    max_osc_panels: int = _MAX_OSC_PANELS,
    tabulate: bool = True,
) -> FieldResult:
    """Point-matching MoM with direct Sommerfeld quadrature for layered soil.

    The discretisation and the linear solve are those of ``mom`` (point
    matching at the segment midpoints, point-source near field,
    source-free clusters floating), run through the shared solve
    pipeline (10.75). Every off-diagonal reaction-matrix entry is the
    Sommerfeld kernel of :func:`sommerfeld_kernel_value`, i.e. the
    closed-form direct pair plus a numerically integrated reflected
    remainder; no image series and no fit enter the off-diagonal
    kernel. For $n = 2$ the diagonal is the Tagg/Sunde series diagonal
    of ``mom``, so on two-layer soil this backend reproduces ``mom`` and
    checks the kernel, not the scheme; for $n \\ge 3$ distinct layers it
    is the only integral-equation backend.

    Cost (review pass 10, 10.61): pairs that share a depth pair and a
    horizontal distance share one quadrature, which halves the work of
    every world and collapses it for regular geometries. For
    $n \\ge 3$ the reflected remainder of a depth group with many
    distinct distances is tabulated on log-spaced nodes and interpolated
    (``tabulate=True``, the default): about $10^{-7}$ relative error of
    the kernel at the verification points and below $10^{-6}$ on the
    reaction matrix of the benchmark grid B12, for a cost that no longer
    grows with the number of pairs. ``tabulate=False`` evaluates every
    distinct pair by quadrature (the kernel reference). For $n = 2$
    every pair is evaluated by quadrature: this backend is the kernel
    check of the closed-form series there.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        World to evaluate.
    engine
        Engine configuration.
    lambda_max_factor
        Truncation of the remainder quadrature in units of the
        remainder decay length $1 / d_{\\text{rem}}$; saturates at
        60. See :func:`sommerfeld_kernel_value` for the delegated
        $n = 2$ cross-layer path.
    epsabs, epsrel
        Convergence thresholds of the remainder quadrature (absolute
        in 1/m, relative).
    max_osc_panels
        Budget for the $J_0$ half-period panel family.
    tabulate
        Depth-group tabulation of the reflected kernel for $n \\ge 3$
        (see above).

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        ``metadata['converged']`` (one bool) and
        ``metadata['converged_per_frequency']`` report the quadrature
        and series convergence (10.47);
        ``metadata['kernel_tabulation']`` the tabulation counters and
        the largest relative error at its verification points.

    Warns
    -----
    SommerfeldConvergenceWarning
        Once per solve, if any reaction-matrix entry's remainder
        quadrature failed to converge.

    Notes
    -----
    The quadrature keywords are reachable through
    ``Engine.options["mom_sommerfeld"]``
    (:class:`~groundfield.solver.registry.MomSommerfeldOptions`); the
    signature defaults equal the option defaults, so a direct call
    without keywords behaves exactly like
    :meth:`~groundfield.solver.engine.Engine.solve`.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If the soil is not a :class:`HomogeneousSoil`,
        :class:`TwoLayerSoil` or :class:`MultiLayerSoil`.
    ValueError
        If the world has no electrodes.
    """
    if not isinstance(world.soil, (HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil, MultiLayerSoil)):
        raise TypeError(
            "Backend 'mom_sommerfeld' supports HomogeneousSoil, "
            "TwoLayerSoil, and MultiLayerSoil. "
            f"Got: {type(world.soil).__name__}."
        )
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")
    green = _SommerfeldGreen(
        world.soil,
        lambda_max_factor=lambda_max_factor,
        epsabs=epsabs,
        epsrel=epsrel,
        max_osc_panels=max_osc_panels,
        max_terms=engine.image_max_terms,
        tol=engine.image_series_tol,
        tabulate=tabulate,
    )
    _log.info(
        "mom_sommerfeld: n_layers=%d, segment_length=%.3f, lam_max_fac=%.1f",
        green.stack.n_layers,
        engine.segment_length,
        lambda_max_factor,
    )
    return solve_point_matching(world, engine, green, stacklevel=3)
