docs.text:
sommerfeld_kernel_value(stack: LayerStack, s: float, z: float, z_s: float, *, lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0, epsabs: float = 1e-09, epsrel: float = 1e-07, max_osc_panels: int = _MAX_OSC_PANELS, issues: list[_QuadratureIssue] | None = None) -> float

Evaluate the layered-soil Sommerfeld kernel at one point.

Returns the full top-layer kernel $$ G(s, z, z_s) \;=\; \int_0^{\infty} \frac{e^{-\lambda |z - z_s|} + \Gamma_1 e^{-\lambda (2 h_1 - |z - z_s|)} + e^{-\lambda (z + z_s)} + \Gamma_1 e^{-\lambda (2 h_1 - z - z_s)}} {1 - \Gamma_1(\lambda)\, e^{-2 \lambda h_1}} J_0(\lambda s)\, d\lambda , $$ i.e. both image families plus the full multiple-reflection multiplier between the free surface (\(R_{\text{air}} = +1\)) and the layer interface. The potential of a point source \(I\) is then ρ_1 · I · G / (4 π).

The integral is not evaluated by a bare real-axis quadrature: the two \(\Gamma_1 \to 0\) terms (which converge only through the oscillation of \(J_0\) and are the reason the pre-0.15.0 implementation could return a negative value) are taken from Lipschitz' integral \(\int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda d} J_0(\lambda s) d\lambda = (s^2 + d^2)^{-1/2}\), so that $$ G = \frac{1}{\sqrt{s^2 + (z - z_s)^2}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{s^2 + (z + z_s)^2}} + G_{\text{refl}}, $$ and only the exponentially decaying reflected remainder \(G_{\text{refl}}\) is integrated numerically — see _reflected_integral().

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default stack LayerStack

Layer stack.

required s float

Cylindrical radius \(s = \sqrt{(x - x_s)^2 + (y - y_s)^2}\) in metres.

required z float

Field-point depth and source depth (positive into the soil).

required z_s float

Field-point depth and source depth (positive into the soil).

required lambda_max_factor float

Truncation of the remainder quadrature, in units of \(1 / d_{\text{rem}}\), where \(d_{\text{rem}}\) is the decay length of the remainder (not, as before 0.15.0, a characteristic length of the geometry). The discarded tail is bounded by \(e^{-\texttt{lambda\_max\_factor}}\); the factor saturates at 60 (\(\sim 10^{-26}\)), so raising it beyond the default cannot change the result.

On the delegated \(n = 2\) cross-layer path (\(z > h_1\) or \(z_s > h_1\), forwarded to groundfield.coupling.layered_green.two_layer_real_space_kernel()) the keyword is measured in units of a geometric characteristic length instead. Since the F14 fix of 0.15.0 that kernel adds every image term it does not resolve back in closed form, so the factor is only an upper bound there as well: values from 30 to 20 000 change the delegated kernel by at most 1.3e-8 and raise no warning (review pass 10; the pre-0.15.0 advice to lower the factor on that path is obsolete).

200.0 epsabs float

Absolute / relative thresholds of the grid-refinement convergence test of the remainder quadrature. epsrel is measured against the magnitude of the whole kernel. They are not forwarded to the delegated \(n = 2\) cross-layer path, which carries its own fixed-order grid.

1e-09 epsrel float

Absolute / relative thresholds of the grid-refinement convergence test of the remainder quadrature. epsrel is measured against the magnitude of the whole kernel. They are not forwarded to the delegated \(n = 2\) cross-layer path, which carries its own fixed-order grid.

1e-09 max_osc_panels int

Budget for the half-period panel family that resolves the \(J_0(\lambda s)\) oscillation, default 200 000 panels (× 12 Gauss nodes). Only binds for \(s / d_{\text{rem}} \gtrsim 1.9 \cdot 10^{4}\), i.e. a centimetre-thin intermediate layer combined with a kilometre-scale horizontal separation; there the coverage is incomplete, a SommerfeldConvergenceWarning is raised and raising this budget is the remedy (cost grows linearly).

_MAX_OSC_PANELS issues list[_QuadratureIssue] | None

Optional collector for non-convergence diagnostics; see _reflected_integral(). Used by _build_Z_sommerfeld() to aggregate \(O(N^2)\) warnings into one.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description G float

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

For \(n \ge 3\) with \(z > h_1\) or \(z_s > h_1\): the expression above is a top-layer form, so the kernel refuses instead of silently returning a diverging number (before 0.15.0 it returned \(\approx -2 \cdot 10^{127}\) there).

Warns:

Type Description SommerfeldConvergenceWarning

If the remainder quadrature does not reach the requested tolerance. The returned value is then not converged and its sign may be wrong.

Notes

Limits and special cases:

  • stack.n_layers == 1 (homogeneous, \(\Gamma_1 \equiv 0\)): short-circuited to \(1/r + 1/r_{\text{img}}\), bit-exact.
  • \(\rho_1 = \rho_2\) in a declared 2-layer stack (\(K_1 = 0\), hence \(\Gamma_1 \equiv 0\)): the reflected remainder is identically zero, so the same closed form is returned bit-exact. This is the strongest available accuracy test of the backend.
  • stack.n_layers == 2 with \(z > h_1\) or \(z_s > h_1\): delegated to groundfield.coupling.layered_green.two_layer_real_space_kernel(), which solves the cross-layer spectral matching.

Distances are floored at 1 mm (_MIN_DISTANCE), consistently with the homogeneous image backend, so the coincident-point limit stays finite.

def sommerfeld_kernel_value(
    stack: LayerStack,
    s: float,
    z: float,
    z_s: float,
    *,
    lambda_max_factor: float = 200.0,
    epsabs: float = 1e-9,
    epsrel: float = 1e-7,
    max_osc_panels: int = _MAX_OSC_PANELS,
    issues: list[_QuadratureIssue] | None = None,
) -> float:
    """Evaluate the layered-soil Sommerfeld kernel at one point.

    Returns the full top-layer kernel
    $$
    G(s, z, z_s) \\;=\\; \\int_0^{\\infty}
    \\frac{e^{-\\lambda |z - z_s|}
         + \\Gamma_1 e^{-\\lambda (2 h_1 - |z - z_s|)}
         + e^{-\\lambda (z + z_s)}
         + \\Gamma_1 e^{-\\lambda (2 h_1 - z - z_s)}}
         {1 - \\Gamma_1(\\lambda)\\, e^{-2 \\lambda h_1}}
    J_0(\\lambda s)\\, d\\lambda ,
    $$
    i.e. both image families plus the full multiple-reflection
    multiplier between the free surface ($R_{\\text{air}} = +1$)
    and the layer interface. The potential of a point source $I$
    is then ``ρ_1 · I · G / (4 π)``.

    The integral is **not** evaluated by a bare real-axis quadrature:
    the two $\\Gamma_1 \\to 0$ terms (which converge only through
    the oscillation of $J_0$ and are the reason the pre-0.15.0
    implementation could return a negative value) are taken from
    Lipschitz' integral
    $\\int_0^\\infty e^{-\\lambda d} J_0(\\lambda s) d\\lambda
    = (s^2 + d^2)^{-1/2}$, so that
    $$
    G = \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{s^2 + (z - z_s)^2}}
      + \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{s^2 + (z + z_s)^2}}
      + G_{\\text{refl}},
    $$
    and only the exponentially decaying reflected remainder
    $G_{\\text{refl}}$ is integrated numerically — see
    :func:`_reflected_integral`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    stack
        Layer stack.
    s
        Cylindrical radius $s = \\sqrt{(x - x_s)^2 + (y - y_s)^2}$
        in metres.
    z, z_s
        Field-point depth and source depth (positive into the soil).
    lambda_max_factor
        Truncation of the *remainder* quadrature, in units of
        $1 / d_{\\text{rem}}$, where $d_{\\text{rem}}$ is the
        decay length of the remainder (not, as before 0.15.0, a
        characteristic length of the geometry). The discarded tail is
        bounded by $e^{-\\texttt{lambda\\_max\\_factor}}$; the factor
        saturates at 60 ($\\sim 10^{-26}$), so raising it beyond
        the default cannot change the result.

        On the delegated $n = 2$ cross-layer path ($z > h_1$ or
        $z_s > h_1$, forwarded to
        :func:`groundfield.coupling.layered_green.two_layer_real_space_kernel`)
        the keyword is measured in units of a *geometric*
        characteristic length instead. Since the F14 fix of 0.15.0
        that kernel adds every image term it does not resolve back in
        closed form, so the factor is only an upper bound there as
        well: values from 30 to 20 000 change the delegated kernel by
        at most 1.3e-8 and raise no warning (review pass 10; the
        pre-0.15.0 advice to *lower* the factor on that path is
        obsolete).
    epsabs, epsrel
        Absolute / relative thresholds of the grid-refinement
        convergence test of the remainder quadrature. ``epsrel`` is
        measured against the magnitude of the *whole* kernel. They are
        **not** forwarded to the delegated $n = 2$ cross-layer path,
        which carries its own fixed-order grid.
    max_osc_panels
        Budget for the half-period panel family that resolves the
        $J_0(\\lambda s)$ oscillation, default 200 000 panels
        (× 12 Gauss nodes). Only binds for
        $s / d_{\\text{rem}} \\gtrsim 1.9 \\cdot 10^{4}$, i.e. a
        centimetre-thin intermediate layer combined with a
        kilometre-scale horizontal separation; there the coverage is
        incomplete, a :class:`SommerfeldConvergenceWarning` is raised
        and raising this budget is the remedy (cost grows linearly).
    issues
        Optional collector for non-convergence diagnostics; see
        :func:`_reflected_integral`. Used by
        :func:`_build_Z_sommerfeld` to aggregate $O(N^2)$ warnings
        into one.

    Returns
    -------
    G : float

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For $n \\ge 3$ with $z > h_1$ or $z_s > h_1$: the
        expression above is a top-layer form, so the kernel refuses
        instead of silently returning a diverging number (before
        0.15.0 it returned $\\approx -2 \\cdot 10^{127}$ there).

    Warns
    -----
    SommerfeldConvergenceWarning
        If the remainder quadrature does not reach the requested
        tolerance. The returned value is then not converged and its
        sign may be wrong.

    Notes
    -----
    Limits and special cases:

    - ``stack.n_layers == 1`` (homogeneous, $\\Gamma_1 \\equiv 0$):
      short-circuited to $1/r + 1/r_{\\text{img}}$, bit-exact.
    - $\\rho_1 = \\rho_2$ in a declared 2-layer stack
      ($K_1 = 0$, hence $\\Gamma_1 \\equiv 0$): the reflected
      remainder is identically zero, so the same closed form is
      returned bit-exact. This is the strongest available accuracy
      test of the backend.
    - ``stack.n_layers == 2`` with $z > h_1$ or $z_s > h_1$:
      delegated to
      :func:`groundfield.coupling.layered_green.two_layer_real_space_kernel`,
      which solves the cross-layer spectral matching.

    Distances are floored at 1 mm (``_MIN_DISTANCE``), consistently
    with the homogeneous ``image`` backend, so the coincident-point
    limit stays finite.
    """
    # Homogeneous shortcut.
    if stack.n_layers <= 1:
        r = np.sqrt(s**2 + (z - z_s) ** 2)
        r_img = np.sqrt(s**2 + (z + z_s) ** 2)
        return float(1.0 / max(r, _MIN_DISTANCE) + 1.0 / max(r_img, _MIN_DISTANCE))

    # ADR-0006 Phase B: 2-layer soil with cross-layer source/observer.
    # Delegate to coupling.layered_green which solves the full 2-layer
    # spectral matching for any (z_layer, z_s_layer) combination. The
    # caller multiplies by rho_1/(4π); the layered_green kernel
    # internally carries the source-layer rho factor, so we divide
    # out rho_1 here to match the existing convention.
    if stack.n_layers == 2 and (z > stack.h[0] or z_s > stack.h[0]):
        from groundfield.coupling.layered_green import (
            two_layer_real_space_kernel,
        )

        # ``lambda_max_factor`` is measured in units of a geometric
        # length here (1/d_rem on the top-layer path below). It is
        # forwarded verbatim: since F14 (0.15.0) the delegated kernel
        # adds the unresolved image terms back in closed form, so the
        # factor is an upper bound only (30 ... 20 000 change the
        # kernel by <= 1.3e-8, review pass 10).
        rho_1_local = float(stack.rhos[0])
        rho_2_local = float(stack.rhos[1])
        h_1_local = float(stack.h[0])
        # Distances floored at 1 mm like every other branch here: the
        # closed-form 1/R terms of the delegated kernel are clamped at
        # min(h_1/200, 1 mm) instead of h_1/200 (audit A3S-01).
        G_phys = two_layer_real_space_kernel(
            s=s,
            z=z,
            z_s=z_s,
            rho_1=rho_1_local,
            rho_2=rho_2_local,
            h_1=h_1_local,
            lambda_max_factor=lambda_max_factor,
            min_distance=_MIN_DISTANCE,
        )
        # G_phys has rho/2·(1/r + ...) structure; the existing caller
        # forms Z = rho_1/(4π)·G_old, so we want G_old = 2·G_phys/rho_1.
        return float(2.0 * G_phys / rho_1_local)

    # Layered case — full top-layer Sommerfeld form.
    #
    # The complete Green's function of a top-layer source observed in the
    # top layer combines four exponentials, each propagated through the
    # multiple-reflection multiplier 1/(1 - Γ_1(λ)·e^{-2λh_1}):
    #
    #   ξ(λ) = (e^{-λ|z-z_s|} + Γ_1·e^{-λ(2h_1-|z-z_s|)}
    #         + e^{-λ(z+z_s)}  + Γ_1·e^{-λ(2h_1-z-z_s)})
    #          / (1 - Γ_1(λ)·e^{-2λh_1})
    #
    # In the limits Γ_1 → 0 this reduces to the homogeneous form
    # e^{-λ|z-z_s|} + e^{-λ(z+z_s)}; for Γ_1 = K_1 = const it expands
    # into the classical Tagg/Sunde geometric series in K_1^n at images
    # ±2nh_1 ± z_s.
    #
    # The two Γ_1 → 0 terms are the conditionally convergent part of
    # the integral and are taken from Lipschitz' integral in closed
    # form; only the decaying reflected remainder is quadratured.
    h_top = float(stack.h[0])
    z_tol = 1e-9 * max(h_top, 1.0)
    if z > h_top + z_tol or z_s > h_top + z_tol:
        # Only reachable for n >= 3 (n == 2 is handled above). The
        # top-layer form is not valid below the interface; before
        # 0.15.0 it silently returned a diverging number (≈ -2e127).
        raise ValueError(
            "mom_sommerfeld: the n>=3 top-layer Sommerfeld kernel "
            "requires both the field point and the source inside the "
            f"upper layer (got z = {z:.4f} m, z_s = {z_s:.4f} m, "
            f"h_1 = {h_top:.4f} m). Use backend='image_2layer' for "
            "cross-layer geometries on a 2-layer soil."
        )
    abs_dz = abs(z - z_s)
    z_plus = z + z_s
    r = float(np.hypot(s, abs_dz))
    r_img = float(np.hypot(s, z_plus))
    G_direct = 1.0 / max(r, _MIN_DISTANCE) + 1.0 / max(r_img, _MIN_DISTANCE)

    G_refl = _reflected_integral(
        stack,
        s,
        abs_dz,
        z_plus,
        lambda_max_factor=lambda_max_factor,
        epsabs=epsabs,
        epsrel=epsrel,
        reference=G_direct,
        max_osc_panels=max_osc_panels,
        issues=issues,
    )
    return float(G_direct + G_refl)

docs.title: solve_fem
docs.text:
solve_fem(world: 'World', engine: 'Engine', *, refinement: int = 0, extrapolate: bool = True, r_far_factor: float = 1000.0, far_field: str = 'robin', max_nodes: int = 2000000, max_nodes_3d: int = 2000000, max_ports_3d: int = 100, model: str = 'auto', source_radius: float | None = None, growth: float = 0.5, concrete_resistivity: float | None = None, _concrete_mesh: float | None = None, n_radial: int | None = None, n_axial: int | None = None, z_far_factor: float | None = None) -> FieldResult

Conforming finite-element solve (see the module docstring).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default world 'World'

World to solve, any horizontally layered soil, bare or encased electrodes (see model).

required engine 'Engine'

Engine; its frequencies, earth_inductive_model (conductor branches) and segment_length (the display segments that carry the leakage distribution of the result) are used.

required refinement int

Refinement level of the coarser of the two meshes (axisymmetric model: each level bisects every interval of the graded mesh lines, about four times the nodes; 3-D model: about eight times). 0 (default) gives a port resistance within about 1e-4 of the converged value for coaxial rods and rings. A ring wire that an interface cuts or comes within 1.05 radii of: within 5.1e-5 of an independent boundary-element model of the solid torus at layer contrasts of 3 ... 1000, on either side, cut or touching (60 cases of audit W4R2A's sweep, estimates 3.9e-4 ... 1.5e-3), and -8.5e-4 touching a layer 10 000 times more conductive (estimate 5.3e-3); refinement=1 within 1.9e-5 and 3.3e-4 (evidence fw4r2a/e05, e08).

0 extrapolate bool

Solve at refinement and refinement + 1 and extrapolate the port conductance matrix with the second order (default). False solves the level refinement alone; its resistance usually lies below the converged value (see Notes) and metadata["fem_error_estimate"] is NaN (one level has no estimate).

True r_far_factor float

Size of the truncation box in characteristic lengths (the electrodes' size, or the depth of the deepest interface times the layer contrast if larger); dimensionless, default 1000.

1000.0 far_field str

"robin" (default): the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of the monopole far field on the box. "dirichlet": the box grounded, which biases the resistance low by about \(\rho_n/(2\pi R)\) (for truncation studies).

'robin' max_nodes int

Resource limit of the axisymmetric model: the node count of the finer mesh, estimated before anything is assembled (the estimate errs high). Default 2 million: the solve needs about 4 GB per million nodes of the finer mesh, so about 8 GB at the limit.

2000000 max_nodes_3d int

Resource limit of the three-dimensional model: the node count of its finer mesh, predicted before meshing and counted before the finer level is built. The solve adds about 2.9 GB per million nodes to the peak memory of the process (3.0 ... 3.1 GB with the process itself).

2000000 max_ports_3d int

Resource limit of the three-dimensional model: the number of ports (every electrode and every leaking piece of a galvanic distributed conductor), checked before meshing. Default 100: every port costs one conjugate-gradient solve per mesh level, about 0.9 s per port and level at 600 000 nodes of the finer mesh.

100 model str

"auto" (default): the axisymmetric model where it applies (rods on one axis, rings around it, no galvanic distributed conductor), the three-dimensional model otherwise; "axisymmetric" refuses every other world; "3d" forces the three-dimensional model.

'auto' source_radius float | None

3-D model: radius in m of the disc over which each wire's leakage is smoothed; None (default) takes 0.06 m (at least 2.2 bare wire radii, at most what the depth of the wires, their gap to the interfaces and the distance of wires that run beside each other — kept 1.5 source radii apart — allow).

None growth float

3-D model: growth of the element size per metre away from the wires (default 0.5; smaller is finer and slower).

0.5 concrete_resistivity float | None

3-D model: None (default) applies every encased wire's own shell coefficient; a resistivity in Ω·m resolves the concrete as square prisms of conformal radius wire_radius around the encased (axis-aligned, straight) wires, shared where they meet (user decision Q40).

None _concrete_mesh float | None

Private, for the overlap study of user decision Q40 (see solid_earth()).

None n_radial int | None

Deprecated: the mesh controls of the equivalent-hemisphere mesh (0.15.0); a value has no effect and warns.

None n_axial int | None

Deprecated: the mesh controls of the equivalent-hemisphere mesh (0.15.0); a value has no effect and warns.

None z_far_factor int | None

Deprecated: the mesh controls of the equivalent-hemisphere mesh (0.15.0); a value has no effect and warns.

None

Returns:

Type Description FieldResult

Electrode potentials and currents (every electrode an equipotential port), point sources with the leakage distribution of the model, and metadata with fem_port_resistance (the extrapolated port resistance matrix in Ω, ports in world order, fem_ports), fem_port_resistance_levels (per mesh level), fem_error_estimate (largest relative difference of a diagonal entry between the extrapolated and the finer level; NaN with extrapolate=False), fem_error_estimate_transfer (3-D model: the same for the transfer entries; NaN for one port or one level), fem_model ("axisymmetric" or "3d": the model that ran), fem_mesh (size and time per level) and fem_r_far (box size in m).

Raises:

Type Description BackendCapabilityError

With model="axisymmetric": if the world is not axisymmetric (an electrode other than a rod or a ring, a rod or ring off the common axis by more than 1e-3 of the smallest wire radius or gap, a galvanic distributed conductor), its electrodes touch, a ring wire reaches within 5 % of its radius to the soil surface, or a ring has no room for its mesh block (within about a wire radius, diagonally, of a rod's end edge); model="auto" solves these worlds with the three-dimensional model. 3-D model, before meshing: a wire too close to the soil surface or an interface for its smoothed source; wires that do not meet but run beside each other (side by side within 30° of parallel, a folded arm, a small ring around a rod head, two wires that meet at less than 10° or touch along their length) closer than 1.5 times the smallest source radius, and wires end to end in line with a gap, such as stacked rods, closer than 5 times it (the smallest source radius is 2.2 radii of the thickest bare wire of the world, so 3.3 and 11 such radii, axis to axis); wires that meet at 10° or more are left alone; resolved concrete around a wire that is not straight along x, y or z, or whose cover is so thin that the smoothed source does not reach beyond the metal. After meshing: conjugate gradients that do not converge (layer contrasts above about 300). The message names the backends that solve the world. A subclass of ValueError and NotImplementedError.

ImportError

If the world needs the three-dimensional model and the fem3d extra (scikit-fem, pyamg) is not installed.

ValueError

If an electrode or a galvanic distributed conductor lies at or above the soil surface (as every backend), or the world fails World.check.

ResourceLimitError

If the finer mesh would exceed max_nodes nodes (the 3-D model: max_nodes_3d, a prediction before meshing and the exact count before the finer level), or the 3-D model would solve more than max_ports_3d ports; where wires that run beside each other limited the source radius, the message says so.

TypeError

If world.soil is no soil model.

Warns:

Type Description MixedCoordinatesWarning

For a world that mixes local and projected coordinates (user decision D5), as every backend.

InterfaceContactWarning

3-D model: for a rod end within one wire radius of a layer interface (audit W4R2A-03: a rod tip on 1000/30 Ohm m read +43 % against the solid rod, with an estimate of 6e-3) and for a horizontal wire within the reach of a contrasting one (audits W4A-07, W4B-02), where the smoothed line source shares the thin-wire error of the integral engines; once per rule and solve, as there. The axisymmetric model resolves rod end faces and ring wires and does not warn.

DeprecationWarning

For n_radial, n_axial or z_far_factor.

Notes

Without extrapolation the resistance of the axisymmetric model converges at second order and, in every case tested away from interfaces, from below; this is not guaranteed (the O-grid of a ring is not nested between levels), and next to an interface cut into a ring's mesh block it did not hold before that block was refined (audit W4A-01) and graded towards the points where the interface meets the wire (audit W4R2A-02: touching a 1000 times more conductive layer the levels converged at about first order, the default read -1.6e-2 with an estimate of 1.1e-2). The error estimate bounds the error of the extrapolated value while both levels lie on the same side of the converged value and the finer level's error is at most 1/2.5 of the coarser level's (about 1/3.9 is observed for rods and rings, 1/3.9 ... 1/4.0 for a ring touching a 100 or 1000 times more conductive layer).

def solve_fem(
    world: "World",
    engine: "Engine",
    *,
    refinement: int = 0,
    extrapolate: bool = True,
    r_far_factor: float = 1000.0,
    far_field: str = "robin",
    max_nodes: int = 2_000_000,
    max_nodes_3d: int = 2_000_000,
    max_ports_3d: int = 100,
    model: str = "auto",
    source_radius: float | None = None,
    growth: float = 0.5,
    concrete_resistivity: float | None = None,
    _concrete_mesh: float | None = None,
    n_radial: int | None = None,
    n_axial: int | None = None,
    z_far_factor: float | None = None,
) -> FieldResult:
    """Conforming finite-element solve (see the module docstring).

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        World to solve, any horizontally layered soil, bare or encased
        electrodes (see ``model``).
    engine
        Engine; its ``frequencies``, ``earth_inductive_model`` (conductor
        branches) and ``segment_length`` (the display segments that carry
        the leakage distribution of the result) are used.
    refinement
        Refinement level of the coarser of the two meshes (axisymmetric
        model: each level bisects every interval of the graded mesh lines,
        about four times the nodes; 3-D model: about eight times). ``0``
        (default) gives a port resistance within about 1e-4 of the
        converged value for coaxial rods and rings. A ring wire that an
        interface cuts or comes within 1.05 radii of: within 5.1e-5 of an
        independent boundary-element model of the solid torus at layer
        contrasts of 3 ... 1000, on either side, cut or touching (60 cases
        of audit W4R2A's sweep, estimates 3.9e-4 ... 1.5e-3), and -8.5e-4
        touching a layer 10 000 times more conductive (estimate 5.3e-3);
        ``refinement=1`` within 1.9e-5 and 3.3e-4 (evidence ``fw4r2a/e05``,
        ``e08``).
    extrapolate
        Solve at ``refinement`` and ``refinement + 1`` and extrapolate the
        port conductance matrix with the second order (default). ``False``
        solves the level ``refinement`` alone; its resistance usually lies
        below the converged value (see *Notes*) and
        ``metadata["fem_error_estimate"]`` is ``NaN`` (one level has no
        estimate).
    r_far_factor
        Size of the truncation box in characteristic lengths (the
        electrodes' size, or the depth of the deepest interface times the
        layer contrast if larger); dimensionless, default 1000.
    far_field
        ``"robin"`` (default): the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of the
        monopole far field on the box. ``"dirichlet"``: the box grounded,
        which biases the resistance low by about $\\rho_n/(2\\pi R)$ (for
        truncation studies).
    max_nodes
        Resource limit of the axisymmetric model: the node count of the
        finer mesh, estimated before anything is assembled (the estimate
        errs high). Default 2 million: the solve needs about 4 GB per
        million nodes of the finer mesh, so about 8 GB at the limit.
    max_nodes_3d
        Resource limit of the three-dimensional model: the node count of
        its finer mesh, predicted before meshing and counted before the
        finer level is built. The solve adds about 2.9 GB per million nodes
        to the peak memory of the process (3.0 ... 3.1 GB with the process
        itself).
    max_ports_3d
        Resource limit of the three-dimensional model: the number of ports
        (every electrode and every leaking piece of a galvanic distributed
        conductor), checked before meshing. Default 100: every port costs
        one conjugate-gradient solve per mesh level, about 0.9 s per port
        and level at 600 000 nodes of the finer mesh.
    model
        ``"auto"`` (default): the axisymmetric model where it applies (rods
        on one axis, rings around it, no galvanic distributed conductor),
        the three-dimensional model otherwise; ``"axisymmetric"`` refuses
        every other world; ``"3d"`` forces the three-dimensional model.
    source_radius
        3-D model: radius in m of the disc over which each wire's leakage
        is smoothed; ``None`` (default) takes 0.06 m (at least 2.2 bare

    concrete_resistivity

        shell coefficient; a resistivity in Ω·m resolves the concrete as

    -------
    FieldResult
        Electrode potentials and currents (every electrode an
        equipotential port), point sources with the leakage distribution of
        the model, and ``metadata`` with ``fem_port_resistance`` (the
        extrapolated port resistance matrix in Ω, ports in world order,

        ``fem_error_estimate`` (largest relative difference of a diagonal

        ``extrapolate=False``), ``fem_error_estimate_transfer`` (3-D model:

        level), ``fem_model`` (``"axisymmetric"`` or
        ``"3d"``: the model that ran), ``fem_mesh`` (size and time per
        level) and ``fem_r_far`` (box size in m).

    Raises
    ------
    BackendCapabilityError
        With ``model="axisymmetric"``: if the world is not axisymmetric (an
        electrode other than a rod or a ring, a rod or ring off the common
        axis by more than 1e-3 of the smallest wire radius or gap, a
        galvanic distributed conductor), its electrodes touch, a ring wire
        reaches within 5 % of its radius to the soil surface, or a ring has
        no room for its mesh block (within about a wire radius, diagonally,
        of a rod's end edge); ``model="auto"`` solves these worlds with the
        three-dimensional model.
        3-D model, before meshing: a wire too close to the soil surface or
        an interface for its smoothed source; wires that do not meet but
        run beside each other (side by side within 30° of parallel, a
        folded arm, a small ring around a rod head, two wires that meet at
        less than 10° or touch along their length) closer than 1.5 times
        the smallest source radius, and wires end to end in line with a
        gap, such as stacked rods, closer than 5 times it (the smallest
        source radius is 2.2 radii of the thickest bare wire of the world,
        so 3.3 and 11 such radii, axis to axis); wires that meet at 10° or
        more are left alone; resolved concrete around a wire that is not straight along x, y or
        z, or whose cover is so thin that the smoothed source does not
        reach beyond the metal. After meshing: conjugate gradients that do
        not converge (layer contrasts above about 300). The message names
        the backends that solve the world. A subclass of ``ValueError`` and
        ``NotImplementedError``.
    ImportError
        If the world needs the three-dimensional model and the ``fem3d``
        extra (scikit-fem, pyamg) is not installed.
    ValueError
        If an electrode or a galvanic distributed conductor lies at or
        above the soil surface (as every backend), or the world fails
        :meth:`World.check <groundfield.world.World.check>`.
    groundfield.diagnostics.ResourceLimitError
        If the finer mesh would exceed ``max_nodes`` nodes (the 3-D model:
        ``max_nodes_3d``, a prediction before meshing and the exact count
        before the finer level), or the 3-D model would solve more than
        ``max_ports_3d`` ports; where wires that run beside each other
        limited the source radius, the message says so.
    TypeError
        If ``world.soil`` is no soil model.

    Warns
    -----
    MixedCoordinatesWarning
        For a world that mixes local and projected coordinates (user
        decision D5), as every backend.
    InterfaceContactWarning
        3-D model: for a rod end within one wire radius of a layer
        interface (audit W4R2A-03: a rod tip on 1000/30 Ohm m read +43 %
        against the solid rod, with an estimate of 6e-3) and for a
        horizontal wire within the reach of a contrasting one (audits
        W4A-07, W4B-02), where the smoothed line source shares the
        thin-wire error of the integral engines; once per rule and solve,
        as there. The axisymmetric model resolves rod end faces and ring
        wires and does not warn.
    DeprecationWarning
        For ``n_radial``, ``n_axial`` or ``z_far_factor``.

    Notes
    -----
    Without extrapolation the resistance of the axisymmetric model
    converges at second order and, in every case tested away from
    interfaces, from below; this is not guaranteed (the O-grid of a ring
    is not nested between levels), and next to an interface cut into a
    ring's mesh block it did not hold before that block was refined (audit
    W4A-01) and graded towards the points where the interface meets the
    wire (audit W4R2A-02: touching a 1000 times more conductive layer the
    levels converged at about first order, the default read -1.6e-2 with
    an estimate of 1.1e-2). The error estimate bounds the error of the
    extrapolated value while both levels lie on the same side of the
    converged value and the finer level's error is at most 1/2.5 of the
    coarser level's (about 1/3.9 is observed for rods and rings, 1/3.9 ...
    1/4.0 for a ring touching a 100 or 1000 times more conductive layer).
    """
    from groundfield.soil.models import HomogeneousSoil, MultiLayerSoil, TwoLayerSoil
    from groundfield.solver import _frame

    _warn_deprecated_mesh_arguments(
        n_radial=n_radial, n_axial=n_axial, z_far_factor=z_far_factor
    )
    if far_field not in _FAR_FIELDS:
        raise ValueError(
            "far_field must be 'robin' (monopole DtN) or 'dirichlet' "
            f"(grounded truncation box), got {far_field!r}."
        )
    if int(refinement) != refinement or refinement < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"refinement must be an integer >= 0, got {refinement!r}.")
    if not r_far_factor > 1.0:
        raise ValueError(f"r_far_factor must be > 1, got {r_far_factor!r}.")
    if not isinstance(world.soil, (HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil, MultiLayerSoil)):
        raise TypeError(
            "Backend 'fem' supports HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil, "
            f"and MultiLayerSoil. Got: {type(world.soil).__name__}."
        )
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")
    if model not in _MODELS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"model must be one of {', '.join(repr(m) for m in _MODELS)}, got {model!r}."
        )
    if source_radius is not None and not (
        math.isfinite(float(source_radius)) and float(source_radius) > 0.0
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"source_radius must be a positive length in m, got {source_radius!r}."
        )
    if not (math.isfinite(float(growth)) and 0.05 <= float(growth) <= 2.0):
        raise ValueError(f"growth must lie in [0.05, 2], got {growth!r}.")
    if concrete_resistivity is not None and not (
        math.isfinite(float(concrete_resistivity)) and float(concrete_resistivity) > 0.0
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            "concrete_resistivity must be a positive resistivity in Ohm m or None, "
            f"got {concrete_resistivity!r}."
        )
    frame = _frame.LocalFrame.of(world)
    with frame.active():
        result = _solve(
            frame.world,
            engine,
            refinement=int(refinement),
            extrapolate=bool(extrapolate),
            r_far_factor=float(r_far_factor),
            far_field=far_field,
            max_nodes=int(max_nodes),
            model=model,
            solid={
                "source_radius_m": None
                if source_radius is None
                else float(source_radius),
                "growth": float(growth),
                "concrete_resistivity": None
                if concrete_resistivity is None
                else float(concrete_resistivity),
                "concrete_mesh": _concrete_mesh,
                "max_nodes_3d": int(max_nodes_3d),
                "max_ports_3d": int(max_ports_3d),
            },
        )
    return frame.to_user(result)

docs.title: Deprecated backend names
docs.text: cim, bem and image_nlayer are deprecated names of image and mom (see Deprecations); their solve functions forward to the current backends. The complex-image fit of the cim module (fit_complex_images, ComplexImageFit) is a stand-alone tool that no backend evaluates. equivalent_hemisphere_radius is deprecated: it belongs to the hemisphere reduction that fem no longer uses.

def solve_cim(world: World, engine: Engine) -> FieldResult:
    """Run the image auto-dispatch under the deprecated backend name ``cim``.

    ``cim`` never evaluated a complex-image fit on a reachable path: for
    $n = 1$ it used the homogeneous image kernel and for $n = 2$ the
    exact Tagg/Sunde series, i.e. it reproduced ``image`` and
    ``image_2layer`` (bit for bit since the length-weighted read-back of
    10.30). Since review pass 10 (10.76) the name is a deprecated alias:
    this function runs the backend ``image`` would run for the soil
    model — :func:`~groundfield.solver.image.solve_image` for a
    :class:`HomogeneousSoil`,
    :func:`~groundfield.solver.image_2layer.solve_image_2layer` for a
    :class:`TwoLayerSoil` and the layered router for a
    :class:`MultiLayerSoil` — with the engine's series controls, so a
    two-layer world also gets the cross-layer treatment of
    ``image_2layer``. :func:`fit_complex_images` stays available as a
    spectral helper.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        World to evaluate.
    engine
        Engine configuration; ``engine.segment_length`` (m) controls the
        discretisation, ``engine.image_max_terms`` /
        ``engine.image_series_tol`` the Tagg/Sunde truncation at
        $n = 2$.

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        The result of the image backend, labelled ``backend="cim"`` with
        ``metadata['dispatched_to']`` naming the backend that ran.

    Raises
    ------
    NotImplementedError
        For three or more distinct soil layers (use ``mom_sommerfeld``).

    Warns
    -----
    DeprecationWarning
        Always: use ``backend="image"`` (``image_2layer`` for two-layer
        soil) instead; the alias is removed no earlier than groundfield
        2027.5.
    """
    from groundfield.solver.image import solve_image
    from groundfield.solver.image_2layer import solve_image_2layer
    from groundfield.solver.image_nlayer import solve_image_nlayer
    from groundfield.solver.registry import DEPRECATION_REMOVAL, warn_external

    warn_external(
        "Backend name 'cim' (groundfield.solver.cim.solve_cim) is deprecated; "
        "use 'image' instead, which runs 'image_2layer' for two-layer soil "
        "(the series 'cim' evaluated). The alias will be removed no earlier "
        f"than {DEPRECATION_REMOVAL}.",
        DeprecationWarning,
    )
    soil = world.soil
    if not isinstance(soil, (HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil, MultiLayerSoil)):
        raise TypeError(
            "Backend 'cim' supports HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil, "
            f"and MultiLayerSoil. Got: {type(soil).__name__}."
        )
    n_layers = as_layer_stack(soil).n_layers
    if n_layers >= 3:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"cim: n_layers = {n_layers} >= 3 is not supported — the "
            "historic complex-image kernel was structurally incomplete "
            "(audit 2026-07-08). Use backend='mom_sommerfeld' (full layered "
            "Green's function) for n >= 3 soils."
        )
    # The forwarding rules of backend 'image' (registry): by soil model.
    if isinstance(soil, HomogeneousSoil):
        res = solve_image(world, engine)
    elif isinstance(soil, TwoLayerSoil):
        res = solve_image_2layer(
            world, engine, max_terms=engine.image_max_terms, tol=engine.image_series_tol
        )
    else:
        res = solve_image_nlayer(
            world, engine, max_terms=engine.image_max_terms, tol=engine.image_series_tol
        )
    return res.model_copy(
        update={
            "backend": "cim",
            "metadata": {**res.metadata, "dispatched_to": res.backend},
        }
    )

fit_complex_images(stack: LayerStack, *, n_images: int = 8, n_samples: int = 64, lambda_min_factor: float = 0.001, lambda_max_factor: float = 50.0, rms_tol: float = _DEFAULT_RMS_TOL, warn: bool = True) -> ComplexImageFit

Fit Γ_1(λ) of an n-layer stack by n_images complex exponentials.

Physical / mathematical context

The upward-looking reflection coefficient of a stratified half-space (see groundfield.solver._layered.reflection_gamma()) is a rational function of the interface attenuations \(e^{-2 \lambda h_i}\). It is not a decaying function: it tends to the top-interface Fresnel coefficient

\[ \lim_{\lambda \to \infty} \Gamma_1(\lambda) \;=\; K_1 \;=\; \frac{\rho_2 - \rho_1}{\rho_2 + \rho_1}, \]

while a sum \(\sum_k a_k e^{-2\lambda\beta_k}\) with \(\Re\{\beta_k\} > 0\) tends to 0. The asymptote is hence split off analytically and carried by an image at \(\beta_0 = 0\) (weight \(K_1\); in the spatial domain an image at the air-mirror position \(z = -z_s\), integrable through the Sommerfeld identity because \(d = z + z_s > 0\)), and the matrix pencil only sees the genuinely decaying remainder \(\Gamma_1(\lambda) - K_1\).

Steps:

  1. Build a uniform sampling grid \(\lambda_j = \lambda_{\min} + j \Delta\). Only the thicknesses \(h_2, \dots, h_{n-1}\) enter \(\Gamma_1\) (the recursion never uses \(h_1\)), so the structure scale is \(h_{\max} = \max_i h_{i\ge2}\) and the decay scale is \(h_{\min} = \min_i h_{i\ge2}\): the step is capped at \(\Delta \le 1/(8 h_{\max})\) so the slowest exponential is resolved, and the window reaches up to \(\lambda_{\max} = \lambda_{\max,\text{factor}}/h_{\min}\) where the fastest one has died.
  2. Sample \(g_j = \Gamma_1(\lambda_j)\) and subtract \(K_1\).
  3. Apply the matrix-pencil method to the remainder to recover the poles \(p_k = e^{-2 \Delta \beta_k}\), filtered to \(|p_k| < 0.999\) and \(\Re\{\beta_k\} > 0\).
  4. Re-solve the least-squares coefficients \(a_k\) for the surviving \(\{\beta_k\} \cup \{0\}\) on the original samples of \(\Gamma_1\) — the filtered model is therefore self-consistent (up to 0.14.1 the coefficients were solved before the filter and then merely sliced, so the reported weights belonged to a different model).

Special cases:

  • stack.n_layers <= 1 → empty fit (\(\Gamma_1 \equiv 0\)).
  • stack.n_layers == 2 → \(\Gamma_1 \equiv K_1\) exactly; the single \(\beta = 0\) image reproduces it with rms = 0 (up to 0.14.1 this returned P = 0 and rms = nan).
  • \(\rho_1 = \dots = \rho_n\) → empty fit.
Notes

No solver path calls this function: the backend name cim is a deprecated alias of the closed-form image backends (see the module docstring). It is kept public as the spectral building block for a future complete \(n \ge 3\) complex-image kernel, and it reports failure instead of hiding it.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default stack LayerStack

Layer stack to fit.

required n_images int

Target number of decaying complex images. Sensible range 4–12; the returned \(P\) is one larger when the asymptote image is present, and may be smaller when the SVD truncates poles.

8 n_samples int

Number of samples drawn from Γ_1(λ).

64 lambda_min_factor float

Lower grid bound as a multiple of \(1/h_{\max}\).

0.001 lambda_max_factor float

Upper grid bound as a multiple of \(1/h_{\min}\) (an upper bound only — the step cap of item 1 above may stop the grid earlier).

50.0 rms_tol float

Error bound (dimensionless, \(|\Gamma_1| \le 1\)): the RMS residual on the fitting grid, the RMS residual on the verification grid and the maximum error on the verification grid including \(\lambda = 0\) must not exceed it, otherwise the fit counts as failed (converged=False plus a ComplexImageFitWarning). The maximum-error gate was added in review pass 10 (10.49).

_DEFAULT_RMS_TOL warn bool

Set to False to suppress the warning in bulk sweeps; converged / rms / rms_extrapolated / max_error still report the failure.

True

Returns:

Type Description ComplexImageFit

Warns:

Type Description ComplexImageFitWarning

If rms or rms_extrapolated exceeds rms_tol, or the pencil produced no usable pole for a non-flat remainder.

       $h_{\\max} = \\max_i h_{i\\ge2}$ and the *decay* scale is
       $h_{\\min} = \\min_i h_{i\\ge2}$: the step is capped at

       $\\lambda_{\\max} = \\lambda_{\\max,\\text{factor}}/h_{\\min}$

       *surviving* $\\{\\beta_k\\} \\cup \\{0\\}$ on the original
       samples of $\\Gamma_1$ — the filtered model is therefore
       self-consistent (up to 0.14.1 the coefficients were solved

    - ``stack.n_layers <= 1`` → empty fit ($\\Gamma_1 \\equiv 0$).
    - ``stack.n_layers == 2`` → $\\Gamma_1 \\equiv K_1$ exactly;

    Notes
    -----

    deprecated alias of the closed-form image backends (see the module
    docstring). It is kept public as the spectral building block for a
    future complete $n \\ge 3$ complex-image kernel, and it reports
    failure instead of hiding it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    stack
        Layer stack to fit.
    n_images
        Target number of *decaying* complex images. Sensible range
        4–12; the returned $P$ is one larger when the asymptote
        image is present, and may be smaller when the SVD truncates
        poles.
    n_samples
        Number of samples drawn from Γ_1(λ).
    lambda_min_factor
        Lower grid bound as a multiple of $1/h_{\\max}$.
    lambda_max_factor
        Upper grid bound as a multiple of $1/h_{\\min}$ (an upper
        bound only — the step cap of item 1 above may stop the grid
        earlier).
    rms_tol
        Error bound (dimensionless, $|\\Gamma_1| \\le 1$): the RMS
        residual on the fitting grid, the RMS residual on the
        verification grid *and* the maximum error on the verification
        grid including $\\lambda = 0$ must not exceed it, otherwise the
        fit counts as failed (``converged=False`` plus a
        :class:`ComplexImageFitWarning`). The maximum-error gate was
        added in review pass 10 (10.49).
    warn
        Set to ``False`` to suppress the warning in bulk sweeps;
        ``converged`` / ``rms`` / ``rms_extrapolated`` / ``max_error``
        still report the
        failure.

    Returns
    -------
    ComplexImageFit

    Warns
    -----
    ComplexImageFitWarning
        If ``rms`` or ``rms_extrapolated`` exceeds ``rms_tol``, or the
        pencil produced no usable pole for a non-flat remainder.
    """
    if stack.n_layers <= 1:
        return _empty_fit()

    k_inf = float(stack.K[0])

    # Only h_2 … h_{n-1} enter Γ_1 — the recursion in
    # `reflection_gamma` never touches h_1.
    h_rel = np.asarray(stack.h[1:], dtype=float)

    if h_rel.size == 0:
        # n == 2: Γ_1 ≡ K_1, a constant. Exactly one image, at β = 0.
        if abs(k_inf) < _FLAT_TOL:
            return _empty_fit()
        return ComplexImageFit(
            a=np.array([k_inf + 0j]),
            beta=np.zeros(1, dtype=complex),
            rms=0.0,
            k_inf=k_inf,
            converged=True,
        )

    h_struct = float(np.max(h_rel))
    h_decay = float(np.min(h_rel))
    lam_min = lambda_min_factor / h_struct
    lam_max = lambda_max_factor / h_decay

    # Uniform spacing required by the matrix-pencil method; capped so
    # the slowest exponential (scale 1/(2 h_struct)) is resolved.
    delta = min(
        (lam_max - lam_min) / (n_samples - 1),
        1.0 / (_SAMPLES_PER_STRUCTURE_SCALE * h_struct),
    )
    lam = lam_min + delta * np.arange(n_samples)
    g = reflection_gamma(stack, lam).astype(complex)

    # Degenerate case ρ_1 = ρ_2 = … = ρ_n: nothing to fit.
    if np.max(np.abs(g)) < _FLAT_TOL:
        return _empty_fit()

    resid = g - k_inf
    if np.max(np.abs(resid)) < _FLAT_TOL:
        # Γ_1 is constant on the whole window (e.g. ρ_2 = … = ρ_n).
        return ComplexImageFit(
            a=np.array([k_inf + 0j]),
            beta=np.zeros(1, dtype=complex),
            rms=float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.abs(resid) ** 2))),
            k_inf=k_inf,
            converged=True,
        )

    beta_decay = _matrix_pencil_beta(resid, delta, n_images)
    pencil_failed = beta_decay.size == 0

    # β = 0 (the analytic asymptote) plus the decaying images.
    beta = np.concatenate([np.zeros(1, dtype=complex), beta_decay])

    # Coefficients a_k by linear least squares on the original samples
    # of Γ_1 — solved *after* all pole filtering.
    A = np.exp(-2.0 * lam[:, None] * beta[None, :])  # (n_samples, P)
    a, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, g, rcond=None)
    rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.abs(A @ a - g) ** 2)))

    # Independent verification on a log-spaced grid over the *full*
    # requested λ range: the uniform fitting window may stop well
    # below λ_max when the thickness spread is large, and a residual
    # measured on the fitting grid alone cannot see that.
    lam_v = np.logspace(np.log10(lam_min), np.log10(lam_max), _N_VERIFY)
    g_v = reflection_gamma(stack, lam_v).astype(complex)
    model_v = np.exp(-2.0 * lam_v[:, None] * beta[None, :]) @ a
    rms_wide = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.abs(model_v - g_v) ** 2)))
    # Max-norm on the same grid plus lambda = 0, where the static
    # Green's function is most sensitive (review pass 10, 10.49): an RMS
    # gate let localised misses between the fitting samples through.
    err_0 = abs(complex(np.sum(a)) - complex(reflection_gamma(stack, np.zeros(1))[0]))
    max_err = float(max(np.max(np.abs(model_v - g_v)), err_0))

    converged = (
        bool(rms <= rms_tol)
        and bool(rms_wide <= rms_tol)
        and bool(max_err <= rms_tol)
        and not pencil_failed
    )

    _log.info(
        "cim.fit: n_images_used=%d (P_decay=%d), rms=%.2e, "
        "rms_extrapolated=%.2e, K_1=%.4f, n_layers=%d, "
        "lam=[%.3g, %.3g], delta=%.3g",
        beta.size,
        beta_decay.size,
        rms,
        rms_wide,
        k_inf,
        stack.n_layers,
        lam[0],
        lam[-1],
        delta,
    )
    if not converged and warn:
        if pencil_failed:
            reason = (
                "the matrix pencil returned no usable pole for a "
                "non-flat remainder Γ_1 - K_1"
            )
        elif rms > rms_tol:
            reason = f"RMS residual {rms:.3e} > rms_tol {rms_tol:.3e}"
        elif rms_wide > rms_tol:
            reason = (
                f"RMS residual on the verification grid "
                f"{rms_wide:.3e} > rms_tol {rms_tol:.3e}"
            )
        else:
            reason = (
                f"maximum error on the verification grid incl. lambda = 0 "
                f"{max_err:.3e} > rms_tol {rms_tol:.3e}"
            )
        warnings.warn(
            f"fit_complex_images: unreliable fit for an "
            f"{stack.n_layers}-layer stack ({reason}). Grid: "
            f"lambda in [{lam[0]:.3g}, {lam[-1]:.3g}], delta="
            f"{delta:.3g}, structure scale 1/(2*h_max)="
            f"{1.0 / (2.0 * h_struct):.3g}, decay scale "
            f"1/(2*h_min)={1.0 / (2.0 * h_decay):.3g}. Raise "
            "n_samples / n_images, or widen lambda_max_factor when the "
            "thickness spread h_max/h_min is large. Do not use these "
            "images in a Green's function.",
            ComplexImageFitWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    return ComplexImageFit(
        a=a,
        beta=beta,
        rms=rms,
        k_inf=k_inf,
        rms_extrapolated=rms_wide,
        converged=converged,
        max_error=max_err,
    )

docs.title: ComplexImageFit dataclass
docs.text:
ComplexImageFit(a: ndarray, beta: ndarray, rms: float, k_inf: float = 0.0, rms_extrapolated: float = 0.0, converged: bool = True, max_error: float = 0.0)

Result of fit_complex_images().

The fit represents \(\Gamma_1(\lambda) \approx \sum_k a_k e^{-2 \lambda \beta_k}\). Index 0 is the analytic asymptote image (\(\beta_0 = 0\), \(a_0 \approx K_1\)) whenever the stack has one; the remaining entries are the decaying images recovered by the matrix pencil.

Attributes:

Name Type Description a (ndarray, shape(P), complex)

Image weights \(a_k\).

beta (ndarray, shape(P), complex)

Image depths \(\beta_k\) (units of metres).

rms float

RMS of the residual \(|\text{fit} - \Gamma_1|\) on the sample grid. Always finite: a failed fit reports the residual it actually achieved (and warns) instead of nan.

k_inf float

The \(\lambda \to \infty\) asymptote \(K_1 = (\rho_2 - \rho_1)/(\rho_2 + \rho_1)\) that the \(\beta = 0\) image carries. 0.0 for a homogeneous stack.

rms_extrapolated float

RMS of the same residual on an independent log-spaced verification grid covering the full requested \(\lambda\) range. Larger than rms when the uniform fitting window did not reach the decay band of the thinnest layer (large thickness spread) or when the pencil overfitted.

converged bool

Both residuals and max_error are <= rms_tol, and the decaying remainder was either numerically flat or successfully fitted. False means a ComplexImageFitWarning was emitted.

max_error float

Maximum of \(|\text{fit} - \Gamma_1|\) over \(\lambda = 0\) and the verification grid. The RMS values average a localised miss away: between the uniform fitting samples the model can be off by more than rms_tol while both RMS values stay below it (review pass 10, 10.49: 2.4e-3 against an RMS of 9.3e-4).

def solve_bem(world: World, engine: Engine) -> FieldResult:
    """Run the point-matching ``mom`` solver under the deprecated name ``bem``.

    Runs :func:`groundfield.solver.mom.solve_mom` (review pass 10,
    10.76); ``bem`` assembled the identical point-matching system, see
    the module docstring.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        World to evaluate.
    engine
        Engine configuration; ``engine.segment_length`` (m) controls the
        discretisation, ``engine.image_max_terms`` /
        ``engine.image_series_tol`` the Tagg/Sunde truncation for two
        layers.

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        The ``mom`` result, labelled ``backend="bem"`` with
        ``metadata['dispatched_to'] = 'mom'``.

    Warns
    -----
    DeprecationWarning
        Always: use ``backend="mom"`` (:func:`solve_mom`) instead; the
        alias is removed no earlier than groundfield 2027.5.
    """
    warn_external(
        "Backend name 'bem' (groundfield.solver.bem.solve_bem) is deprecated; "
        "use 'mom' (solve_mom) instead — it assembles the identical "
        "point-matching system. The alias will be removed no earlier than "
        f"{DEPRECATION_REMOVAL}.",
        DeprecationWarning,
    )
    res = solve_mom(world, engine)
    return res.model_copy(
        update={
            "backend": "bem",
            "metadata": {**res.metadata, "dispatched_to": res.backend},
        }
    )

def solve_image_nlayer(
    world: "World",
    engine: "Engine",
    *,
    max_terms: int | None = None,
    tol: float | None = None,
) -> FieldResult:
    """Image-charge dispatcher for n-layer soil.

    Routes to ``image`` for ``n = 1`` and to ``image_2layer`` for
    ``n = 2``. For ``n \\ge 3`` raises a clear :class:`ValueError`
    pointing the caller to the engines that actually support that
    regime.

    Parameters
    ----------
    world
        World whose soil is any layered soil model.
    engine
        Engine configuration; ``engine.segment_length`` controls the
        discretisation.
    max_terms, tol
        Series controls forwarded to :func:`solve_image_2layer` for
        ``n = 2`` (``None``, the default, takes ``engine.image_max_terms``
        / ``engine.image_series_tol``); ignored otherwise.

    Returns
    -------
    FieldResult
        ``backend`` is rewritten to ``"image_nlayer"`` so that
        cross-engine reports use one unified label.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If the soil is not a :class:`HomogeneousSoil`,
        :class:`TwoLayerSoil` or :class:`MultiLayerSoil`.
    ValueError
        If the world has no electrodes.
    BackendCapabilityError
        If the soil has three or more layers (a :class:`ValueError`
        subclass).
    """
    if not isinstance(world.soil, (HomogeneousSoil, TwoLayerSoil, MultiLayerSoil)):
        raise TypeError(
            "Backend 'image_nlayer' supports HomogeneousSoil, "
            "TwoLayerSoil, and MultiLayerSoil. "
            f"Got: {type(world.soil).__name__}."
        )
    if not world.electrodes:
        raise ValueError("World contains no electrodes.")

    stack = as_layer_stack(world.soil)
    n = stack.n_layers
    _log.info("image_nlayer: dispatching for n_layers=%d", n)

    if n == 1:
        # Forward to the homogeneous backend; HomogeneousSoil is the
        # only soil it accepts. If the user supplied a degenerate
        # MultiLayerSoil with one layer, build an equivalent
        # HomogeneousSoil on the fly.
        if isinstance(world.soil, HomogeneousSoil):
            res = solve_image(world, engine)
        else:
            # A copy keeps every other field of the world (junctions too).
            tmp = world.model_copy(
                update={"soil": HomogeneousSoil(rho=float(stack.rhos[0]))}
            )
            res = solve_image(tmp, engine)
    elif n == 2:
        # Forward to the closed-form Tagg/Sunde series.
        if isinstance(world.soil, TwoLayerSoil):
            res = solve_image_2layer(world, engine, max_terms=max_terms, tol=tol)
        else:
            # MultiLayerSoil with exactly two layers: cast to TwoLayerSoil.
            two = TwoLayerSoil(
                rho_1=float(stack.rhos[0]),
                rho_2=float(stack.rhos[1]),
                h_1=float(stack.h[0]),
            )
            tmp = world.model_copy(update={"soil": two})
            res = solve_image_2layer(tmp, engine, max_terms=max_terms, tol=tol)
    else:
        from groundfield.solver.registry import BackendCapabilityError

        raise BackendCapabilityError(
            f"image_nlayer: layer count {n} ≥ 3 is not supported by "
            "the real image-charge series (Γ_1(λ) is no longer "
            "constant in λ). Use 'mom_sommerfeld' (direct Sommerfeld "
            "quadrature of the full layered Green's function) or "
            "'fem' — the 'cim'/'bem' n ≥ 3 kernels were found "
            "structurally incomplete in the 2026-07-08 audit and "
            "are rejected as well."
        )

    # Rewrite backend tag so that cross-engine reports use the unified label.
    res = res.model_copy(
        update={
            "backend": "image_nlayer",
            "metadata": {
                **res.metadata,
                "n_layers": int(n),
                "dispatched_to": res.backend,
            },
        }
    )
    return res
